title: bug: make global-skill validation cleanup transactional and non-destructive
description:
## PROBLEM
Validation runs have repeatedly damaged ~/.xtrm/skills. The xtrm-gg02y worker ran host-global `xt update --apply`, then manually pruned managed skills to an assumed three-entry baseline without a full skill-root backup or ownership manifest. Receipt cleanup checks accepted a count-based claim rather than verifying the expected managed registry. This recurrence can silently remove runtime capabilities.

## SUCCESS
Validation cannot delete or prune host global skills. All artifact/live smokes use isolated HOME/prefix by default. Any explicitly approved host-global swap snapshots the complete skill root and restores it transactionally from a hash-bound archive. Cleanup verification compares registry/manifest ownership and representative runtime resolution, not a guessed count.

## SCOPE
Core validation/update/bootstrap safety seams, smoke scripts/contracts, global skill bootstrap/restore behavior, receipt cleanup requirements, and regression tests for a populated ~/.xtrm/skills tree.

## NON_GOALS
No npm publication. No redesign of skill content. No deletion of current user/optional/reconciled skill state.

## CONSTRAINTS
P0 recurring data-loss class. Impact analysis before code edits. Fail before mutation if backup/archive verification cannot be completed. Never use broad rm/prune against real HOME in tests. Preserve user packs and unmanaged entries. `xt update` failures must not leave partial global config/skill mutations without rollback evidence.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Regression fixture seeds default, optional, user, and unmanaged sentinel skills.
- [ ] Validation setup/cleanup leaves the complete tree byte-identical.
- [ ] Crash/timeout path restores from a verified archive.
- [ ] Missing/corrupt backup fails closed before host mutation.
- [ ] Receipt gate verifies manifest identity and representative runtime resolution.
- [ ] `xt update --apply` preflight/transaction behavior covers GlobalPromptSyncError without partial mutation.
- [ ] Security auditor and reviewer PASS.

## LIBRARIES
Reuse Node filesystem/tar/hash and existing backup primitives; no new dependency unless existing primitives cannot create atomic recovery.

## OUTPUT
Root-cause report, production/test changes, regression counts, crash-recovery proof, GitNexus impact/detect output, and audit verdicts.

title: bug: restore global skills removed by ISSUE-127 cleanup
description:
## PROBLEM
The post-PR595 validation worker ran `xt update --apply`, populated ~/.xtrm/skills/default, then treated a three-entry snapshot as the desired baseline and removed the other default skills during cleanup. The orchestrator accepted that assumption and additionally removed two audit skills. The operator reports the root global skill installation is wiped.

## SUCCESS
The full expected xtrm-managed global skill tree is restored from a verified local Core package/source without losing user state. The exact causal timeline, before/after inventory, recovery source hashes, and prevention follow-up are recorded.

## SCOPE
~/.xtrm/skills inventory and recovery, installed Core package .xtrm/skills payload, xt update behavior/logs, ISSUE-127 evidence, and durable incident report.

## NON_GOALS
No Core/Specialists integration, npm publication, unrelated home cleanup, or replacement of user-owned skill content.

## CONSTRAINTS
P0. Snapshot current ~/.xtrm/skills before recovery. Preserve user/, optional/, reconciled-out*, skills-lock.json, and unrelated state. Prefer the native `xt update --apply` registry mechanism over manual broad copying. Verify exact resulting inventory and required skills. Do not delete anything further during investigation.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Current damaged inventory captured.
- [ ] Recovery source is identified and hash-bound.
- [ ] Native update restores expected default skills.
- [ ] User/optional/reconciled-out and lock state remain present.
- [ ] Representative critical skills load from ~/.xtrm/skills/default.
- [ ] Root cause and prevention issue are recorded.

## LIBRARIES
N/A — use existing xt update and filesystem/hash tools.

## OUTPUT
Incident cause, recovery command, backup path/hash, before/after counts, representative skill checks, preserved user-state checks, and prevention bead.
notes:

Topology now exactly matches captured 58-entry pre-cleanup list; xt skills list reports 55 default active skills for Claude/Pi/Codex and 7 packs. User and reconciled-out trees preserved; skills-lock unchanged. Prevention implementation completed at Core commit b0321a8f4f423d6c562f4c132af9cb89fb080895; PR #608 open with CI watch. Recovery remains verified: 55 default skills active for Claude/Pi/Codex, 7 packs, 58-entry expected topology, custom multiplexing-native-test and lock/user/reconciled state preserved.
close_reason: Recovered operator global skills from verified sources without losing user/reconciled state; captured full backup and before/after hashes; restored exact expected topology; identified false-baseline cleanup root cause; shipped audited prevention fix as Core PR #608. title: executor: preserve operator blocks in Pi global-prompt sync
description:
## PROBLEM
~/.pi/agent/APPEND_SYSTEM.md contains four xtrm:global-prompt pairs, but Core global-prompt-sync supports exactly one unnamed pair and xt update --apply will throw. The command-chaining block is Core-owned; ast-grep, probe/kernel, and repo-knowledge blocks are operator-owned and must survive byte-identical.
## SUCCESS
Prompt sync identifies its owned command-chaining block, updates only that block, preserves unmatched blocks and all outside bytes, supports migration from the current four unnamed pairs, and remains idempotent.
## SCOPE
cli/src/core/global-prompt-sync.ts, cli/src/tests/global-prompt-sync.test.ts, packaged command-chaining asset, update/pi-install integration tests if required.
## NON_GOALS
Do not package or rewrite the three operator-owned blocks. Do not implement tool-routing enforcement here.
## CONSTRAINTS
SCRUTINY: critical. renderManagedGlobalPrompt impact LOW/5, two processes; readCanonicalGlobalPromptBody path HIGH/11 and must remain compatible. Follow claude-sync named/versioned unknown-fragment-preservation precedent. Fail closed only on malformed ownership of the Core-owned block, not on unknown blocks.
## VALIDATION
- [ ] Current four-block APPEND_SYSTEM.md dry-run/apply succeeds.
- [ ] Core-owned body updates; other three blocks remain byte-identical.
- [ ] Single legacy unnamed block migrates safely.
- [ ] Duplicate owned names/nesting fail visibly.
- [ ] Repeated sync is idempotent and CRLF/outside bytes preserved.
- [ ] update and pi-install prompt tests pass.
## LIBRARIES
Reuse claude-sync parser/sentinel patterns and Node stdlib; no dependency.
## OUTPUT
Committed fix, migration examples, tests, impact/detect_changes, residual compatibility risks.
notes:
Code complete. Rewrote renderManagedGlobalPrompt to a named marker owner model: Core-owned command-chaining block identified by <!-- xtrm:global-prompt:command-chaining:start|end -->; operator-owned blocks (unnamed/other-named) preserved byte-identical. Migration: unnamed block whose first line matches canonical command-chaining heading converts to named owned form (handles current four-uncnamed layout). Fail closed only on malformed owned markers (duplicate/orphan/out-of-order) or ambiguous candidates. Verified: tsc clean; global-prompt-sync.test.ts 30/30; update.test.ts + pi-install-global-prompt.test.ts 22/22; real ~/.pi/agent/APPEND_SYSTEM.md probe -> replace-block, 3 operator blocks byte-identical, idempotent on rerun.
SECONDER FAIL: (1) shipped cli/dist/index.cjs remains stale old single-block implementation; package bin executes dist, so source-only fix does not ship. Rebuild and add package-bin smoke. (2) source normalizes mixed EOL across whole file, violating byte-identical outside owned span; replace by original string offsets. (3) unnamed marker pairing lacks structural validation for nested/overlap; refuse ambiguity before replacement. Add mixed-EOL byte assertions and malformed unnamed nesting/overlap regressions. Re-run source+dist/package-bin tests. Operator decision on monitor sentence remains pending; do not resolve it silently.
SECURITY REQUEST CHANGES adds: migrate unnamed block only on complete normalized body equality against explicit canonical/legacy allowlist, never first-line heading alone; customized same-heading block must remain byte-identical and named Core block is prepended or actionable ambiguity returned. Also preflight/render BOTH Pi and Claude targets before writing either, so malformed second target leaves both unchanged. Where practical surface preflight before install/update side effects; at minimum make prompt sync atomic across targets with regression. Existing seconder findings cover stack/interval validation and mixed-EOL offsets.
Seconder+security round applied: (1) render now splices by original string offsets (mixed-EOL outside bytes byte-identical, no whole-file re-EOL). (2) Migration claims an unnamed block ONLY on exact complete normalized-body equality to canonical/legacy allowlist (never first-line heading); customized same-heading block stays byte-identical and Core named block is prepended — the operator monitor line in the real block1 is neither dropped nor promoted (decision left pending). (3) Structural validation (pairBlocks) refuses nested/orphan/mismatched unnamed markers before any claim. (4) syncGlobalPrompts plans BOTH Pi+Claude targets before writing either; malformed second target leaves both unchanged. Rebuilt tracked cli/dist/index.cjs (+.map) so the shipped bin carries the fix; added hidden _global-prompt-sync diagnostic command + package-bin smoke against a four-block fixture (prepend + byte-identical operator preservation + idempotent rerun). Tests: global-prompt-sync 38/38, update+pi-install 56/..., auto_commit: checkpoint_on_waiting.
ROUND-2 SECONDER FAIL on 14331fb2: owned-block fast path replaces before global pairBlocks validation; nested/crossing operator marker inside/across owned span can be deleted/orphaned. Validate complete marker structure before every replacement. Concurrent creation race: planned original=null is not checked; a target created after plan can be overwritten. Before commit, assert still absent (exclusive create/appropriate fail) and abort preserving new file; add deterministic regression. Remove production _global-prompt-sync command and index wiring; it is visible and unjustified API surface. Exercise existing production update/pi-install route if feasible; otherwise retain source test plus deterministic dist rebuild/stale-dist assertion without adding runtime API. Rebuild dist and tests.
SECURITY round-2 confirms SEC-01..04 closed but adds second-target commit failure atomicity: planning preflight alone is insufficient. Stage both writes, then if second replacement fails, roll back first target to exact original state (including restore absence for originally absent target). Add injected deterministic second-commit failure regression asserting both targets unchanged. Production diagnostic command removal already required, so SEC-05 resolves by deletion rather than hide/apply gate.
ROUND-2 fixes: (1) hoisted global structural validation (pairBlocks) BEFORE the owned fast path so a nested/crossing marker intersecting the owned span refuses (regression added); duplicate-owned still fails closed explicitly. (2) commit phase is now transactional: stage (guards+backup+temp) THEN rename both; if second rename fails, first is rolled back to exact original bytes (or absence). Exclusive-create guard: a target absent at plan must still be absent before create, else refuse and preserve the concurrent file (regression, deterministic via _beforeWrite). Added injected second-commit-failure regressions for both original-exists restore and absence restore. (3) DELETED _global-prompt-sync command + index wiring entirely (not hidden). Package-bin smoke now a deterministic rebuild + stale-dist guard (asserts new literals present, command absent; CI git-diff dist check enforces freshness). Rebuilt dist. auto_commit: checkpoint_on_waiting.
FINAL SECONDER FAIL on 08dd2d5b: absent-target lstat guard catches every error as absence; catch ONLY ENOENT and propagate EACCES/EIO. Rollback currently suppresses unlink/write failures; collect rollback failures and throw GlobalPromptSyncError containing original commit error plus exact rollback failures/possibly inconsistent targets. Add deterministic EACCES lstat and rollback-failure regressions. Rebuild dist.
FINAL gaps closed: (1) exclusive-create guard now treats ONLY ENOENT as absence; EACCES/EIO and other lstat errors propagate (regression injects EACCES at the guard lstat — target not created, sibling untouched). (2) rollback/temp-cleanup failures are no longer swallowed; the thrown GlobalPromptSyncError aggregates the original commit failure + each rollback failure (label+path) + affected target paths + cleanup count (regression injects commit-fail then rollback-fail and asserts all surfaced). Rebuilt dist. Testing: global-prompt-sync 43/43, integration 56/56; full suite running.
FINAL DELTA RECHECK FAIL d74fe5de: rollbackTarget still swallows fs.remove failure for originally-absent target at source ~421. Remove catch; propagate so collector reports it. Cleanup failures are only a count; collect target label + temp path + message for each and include all in GlobalPromptSyncError. Add regressions for absent-target rollback removal failure and target-qualified cleanup failure reporting. Rebuild dist.
Delta recheck: rollbackTarget no longer suppresses fs.remove for originally-absent targets (remove failure propagates to the collector and surfaces under rollback failure(s)); temp-cleanup failures are now collected individually with target label + temp path + error (temp cleanup failure(s)) instead of a bare count. Regressions: absent-target rollback-remove failure surfacing; target-qualified cleanup failure. Rebuilt dist. 45/45 sync, 56/56 integration; full suite running.

title: Archon workflow hooks lost on ~/.xtrm/hooks bootstrap rebuild (pre-merge-codex-gate, post-merge-orch-hygiene)
description:
## PROBLEM
`~/.xtrm/hooks/pre-merge-codex-gate.mjs` and `~/.xtrm/hooks/post-merge-orch-hygiene.mjs` — the two Archon-workflow-connector hooks that gate `gh pr merge` on unresolved Codex blockers and trigger post-merge orch_hygiene classification — vanished. Wiring in `~/.claude/settings.json:233,398` still points at those paths. Neither file has a source tree: not in git of core/xtmux/specialists, not in `~/.archon/*`, not tracked by any bd bead. Data they consumed still exists (`~/.archon/state/codex-blockers-active.jsonl` — 7 recent entries, `~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/orch_hygiene.py`).

Same class as **xtrm-d3qud** (P0, resolved for service-skills only): `ensureGlobalHooksBootstrapped` wipes+rebuilds `~/.xtrm/hooks/` from the `@jaggerxtrm/xtrm-tools` npm payload on every `xt update --apply` / `xt claude` first-run. Hooks installed outside the payload (like these two, dropped in by an Archon workflow install script that never re-runs) are treated as garbage and deleted.

Discovered 2026-07-25 by operator; unblocked with `chmod 0755` stub for pre-, `touch` stub for post-. Stubs disable the gates: **`gh pr merge` no longer blocks on unresolved Codex blockers, post-merge orch_hygiene classification no longer fires.**

## SUCCESS
Both hooks re-live in a location the bootstrap does NOT wipe, AND their sources are tracked. Wiring in `~/.claude/settings.json` points at the new stable path. Both gates enforce their contracts again.

## SCOPE
Two independent surfaces:
1. **Structural fix (relocation)**: the `.mjs` files land under `~/.archon/hooks/` (not touched by xtrm-tools bootstrap) OR are added to the xtrm-tools payload as canonical (`.xtrm/hooks/*.mjs` in this repo). Ponytail leans toward the former — they're Archon-specific, Archon-installed, keeps xtrm-tools payload lean.
2. **Source reconstruction**: rebuild the two .mjs bodies from spec.
   - `pre-merge-codex-gate.mjs`: reads `~/.archon/state/codex-blockers-active.jsonl`, filters by the target PR from the intercepted `gh pr merge` args (or by the current branch's PR), exits non-zero if any unacked blocker matches. See `xtrm-checks` skill Archon-workflow section and bd `xtrm-99dcc` for design context.
   - `post-merge-orch-hygiene.mjs`: on a Bash exit that matches a successful `gh pr merge` OR `xt merge` invocation, spawns `~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/orch_hygiene.py` in the background. See bd `xtrm-z62qt` for the classifier body it wraps.
3. **Preventive**: add a manifest under `~/.archon/hooks/registry.json` (or similar) that survives xtrm bootstrap and is re-linked into `~/.claude/settings.json` by an idempotent Archon install script — so any future `xt update --apply` can't wipe them silently.

## NON_GOALS
- Adding these hooks to the xtrm-tools npm payload unless Archon is considered a first-party xtrm subsystem (currently it isn't — see xtrm-99dcc which is still open)
- Restoring pre-2026-07-25 exact content bit-for-bit (unrecoverable — no source)
- Fixing the general "bootstrap wipes user-owned files" pattern for `.xtrm/hooks/` (that's the class-fix, would be a separate bead extending xtrm-d3qud's scope)

## CONSTRAINTS
- Codex-blocker gate MUST NOT block on beads-only edits — matcher should be tight enough to only catch `gh pr merge` / `xt merge` invocations
- orch_hygiene wrapper MUST NOT block Claude Code exit; run detached, log to `~/.archon/logs/`
- Stubs currently in place MUST be replaced (not deleted) so no window of missing file re-triggers the block
- If relocating to `~/.archon/hooks/`, add a defensive `[ -f "$p" ] && node "$p"; exit 0` wrapper in settings.json (per xtrm-d3qud pattern) so a future missing-file doesn't brick sessions

## VALIDATION
- [ ] `~/.claude/settings.json` PreToolUse Bash matcher wraps the new pre-merge-codex-gate path with fail-open guard
- [ ] Same for PostToolUse orch_hygiene
- [ ] `gh pr merge N` on a PR with an entry in `codex-blockers-active.jsonl` → blocked with clear reason; without entry → passes
- [ ] `gh pr merge N` succeeds → orch_hygiene runs in background within 5s, entry appears in `~/.archon/logs/`
- [ ] `xt update --apply` — hooks survive (regression test for the bootstrap leak)
- [ ] Sources tracked (either in git via `~/.archon/hooks/` repo or in an Archon workspace)

## OUTPUT
PR link (if the fix lands in xtrm-tools) OR patch summary + new source location for the two `.mjs` files + confirmation `xt update --apply` no longer wipes them.

## REFERENCES
- Related P0: xtrm-d3qud (service-skills hooks fail-open pattern — same class)
- Main Archon epic: xtrm-99dcc (open)
- Consumer of pre-merge gate data: `~/.archon/state/codex-blockers-active.jsonl`
- Consumer of post-merge gate: `~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/orch_hygiene.py` (bd `xtrm-z62qt`)
- Wiring: `~/.claude/settings.json:233` (pre) and `:398` (post)
notes: FINAL REPORT (2026-07-25): Phase 1 y — reconstructed hooks at ~/.archon/hooks/pre-merge-codex-gate.mjs and ~/.archon/hooks/post-merge-orch-hygiene.mjs; settings.json now uses guarded Archon paths. Phase 2 y — option b, source repo /home/dawid/dev/core-archon-workspace commit 1ad752d; ~/.archon/hooks and ~/.archon/scripts/install-hooks.sh symlink into it. Manifest: ~/.archon/hooks/registry.json. Installer: ~/.archon/scripts/install-hooks.sh; rerunnable after xt update --apply. Validation: test-hooks.sh passes; live xtrm-dev/core#493 blocker was blocked with URL; non-merge passes; post hook spawned fresh ~/.archon/logs/orch-hygiene-*.log; installer rerun preserved settings hash and exactly one registration per hook. Phase 3 y — bead closed with memory ack. No blockers.
close_reason: Restored and reconstructed both Archon hooks under source-tracked /home/dawid/dev/core-archon-workspace; installer and guarded settings wiring are live. Tests and live blocker evidence pass; ~/.xtrm stubs removed.

title: PreToolUse hook drift: service-skills skill_activator.py removed but hook config still registered
description:

PR #493 (`c2c7edca refactor(skills): retire vendored service-skills from core [xtrm-56flm.6]`) deleted `.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/skill_activator.py` but left the corresponding PreToolUse hook wiring in `.claude/settings.json` / `.xtrm/config/hooks.json` / `.xtrm/registry.json`.

PreToolUse hook error: [python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/skill_activator.py"]:
python3: can't open file '...skill_activator.py': [Errno 2] No such file or directory

- (a) hook wiring is removed from `.claude/settings.json` + `.xtrm/config/hooks.json` + `.xtrm/registry.json`, OR
- (b) the script is restored (undo `c2c7edca` intent), OR
- (c) `plugin-era-cleanup` / `xt update --apply` prunes stale hook entries whose script path no longer exists

## SCOPE

- `.xtrm/config/hooks.json` — same

title: P0: first-class xtmux coordination tools in Pi
description:
## PROBLEM

xtmux now has a mature JSON CLI surface for durable agent coordination, observation, delegation, and last-turn retrieval. Pi currently exposes only the xtmux inbox/status extension; agents still reach the rest of the surface through shell commands, which loses typed arguments, rich result rendering, CLI semantics, validation, and discoverability. The `expectsReply` distinction is also currently overloaded: ordinary status messages are stored correctly but are ignored by the reply-obligation notifier, while only reply-required messages can wake an agent.

Recent mainline work expanded the surface substantially: PR #55 added identity/coordinator/bridge capabilities, PR #56 added canonical event streaming, and PR #57 added `message-get`, `agent-last`, full-turn capture, and retrieval. This P0 must make the shipped command surface first-class in Pi rather than requiring agents to rediscover it through `bash` and `xtmux help`.

## SUCCESS

Every normal agent-facing xtmux command has a typed Pi tool with a CLI-shaped name, complete help-derived description, safe parameter schema, structured JSON result, and native Pi TUI rendering. Agents can send/read/reply/ack messages, inspect obligations, delegate and wait, retrieve final turns, inspect topology/health/logs, and capture bounded pane content without shell parsing. Ordinary unread status messages produce a UI notification without automatically triggering an LLM turn; `expectsReply=true` remains the explicit wake/reply-obligation mechanism.

## SCOPE

### Pi tool names and command parity

Implement the following tools in the grouped xtmux Pi package (`extensions/`), using exact CLI command names in labels and descriptions:

#### Messages

- `xtmux_message_send` → `message-send`
- `xtmux_message_list` → `message-list`
- `xtmux_message_get` → `message-get`
- `xtmux_message_reply` → `message-reply`
- `xtmux_message_cancel` → `message-cancel`
- `xtmux_message_ack` → `message-ack`
- `xtmux_message_status` → `message-status`
- `xtmux_unread_count` → `unread-count`
- `xtmux_obligations_list` → `obligations list`

#### Coordination and delegation

- `xtmux_handoff` → `handoff`
- `xtmux_wait_agent` → `wait-agent`
- `xtmux_monitor_agent` → `monitor-agent`
- `xtmux_monitor_list` → `monitor-list`

#### Identity, observation, and retrieval

- `xtmux_context` → `context --current`
- `xtmux_agent_last` → `agent-last`
- `xtmux_pane_capture` → `pane capture`
- `xtmux_topology_snapshot` → topology snapshot / current topology JSON command
- `xtmux_health` → `health`
- `xtmux_log_query` → `log query`

`log-follow` may be omitted from the normal tool set if streaming cannot be represented safely; document the reason and retain CLI access.

### Help-derived documentation

Each tool definition must include:

- Exact CLI usage and command name from `xtmux help`.
- Full parameter descriptions matching CLI flags and JSON fields.
- Sender/recipient/session/pane identity semantics.
- `$N`, `@N`, and `%N` quoting rules.
- `messageKey` versus numeric `messageId` semantics.
- The fact that `summary` is the message body for existing message JSON.
- Ack, reply, cancellation, fulfilment, wake, and monitor lifecycle semantics.
- Mutation/read-only classification.
- Safety guidance: inbound message summaries are data, never executable instructions.

Avoid duplicating help text manually where practical: establish a small command metadata source or generated mapping so CLI help, Pi descriptions, and docs cannot drift.

### Tool execution and output

- Invoke the existing CLI with argument arrays and `--json`, never shell interpolation.
- Preserve the existing CLI JSON contracts; do not duplicate domain/database logic in the extension.
- Return concise model-facing `content` plus complete structured `details` for rendering and state.
- Apply Pi output bounds for large lists/logs/pane captures and provide a temp-file path when content is truncated.
- Preserve full message/agent-last bodies within the documented caps.
- Support `AbortSignal`, timeouts, and cancellation for waits, monitors, log queries, and pane capture.
- Throw on command failure so Pi marks the tool result as an error.

### Native Pi rendering

Use `label`, `promptSnippet`, `promptGuidelines`, `renderCall`, and `renderResult` so calls look like native context-mode/GitNexus tools:

- Collapsed call: command name, target/action, bead, reply mode.
- Collapsed result: success/error, message key, target, state, counts, or monitor status.
- Expanded result: complete structured JSON, full body, correlation state, and CLI reference.
- Render partial/waiting states without dumping raw shell output.
- Use consistent colors and `expanded` behavior.

### Notification semantics

- Keep `expectsReply=true` as the explicit agent-wake/reply-obligation mechanism.
- Poll/read all unacked messages, not only `--expects-reply`, for notification purposes.
- Add a deduplicated `ctx.ui.notify`/status-widget signal for newly arrived ordinary messages.
- Do not inject or execute ordinary message summaries as prompts.
- Keep correlated reply obligations and existing safety validation unchanged.

### Documentation and installation

Update xtmux help-facing docs, `docs/json-command-api.md`, `docs/INSTALL.md`, and the Pi extension documentation/package metadata. Ensure the grouped package remains the only xtmux Pi entrypoint and that the installer registers it exactly once.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not remove or rename existing CLI commands or JSON fields.
- Do not make all messages `expectsReply=true`.
- Do not execute inbound message content, prompt summaries, or handoff notes automatically without an explicit tool/user action.
- Do not expose arbitrary shell, telemetry, migration, retention, audit, or destructive monitor-kill commands as unrestricted normal LLM tools.
- Do not replace the SQLite/domain command implementation with a second extension-only database implementation.
- Do not make `capture-pane` the default way to retrieve completed agent answers; use `agent-last`.
- Do not add a new npm dependency unless the existing Pi/TUI/TypeBox APIs cannot provide the required behavior.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve exact stable IDs and quoting rules; never infer pane/session identity from names or indexes when stable IDs are available.
- `message-send --bead` continues to imply `expectsReply=true` unless explicitly disabled.
- Read-only tools must not ack messages or mutate coordination state implicitly.
- Mutating tools must expose the resulting key/state clearly and remain idempotent where the CLI is idempotent.
- Wait/monitor tools must not prompt working panes; preserve existing monitor semantics and timeouts.
- Handoff remains durable/bead-backed and must report that send-keys success is only an attempt, not acceptance.
- Keep output secrets-safe: never log API keys, credentials, or unredacted sensitive environment data.
- Add structured tool telemetry for start/end/error with tool name, command, target, outcome, duration_ms, and correlation/message/monitor key where applicable; do not log full message bodies by default.
- Scope changes to xtmux and its grouped Pi package. Do not modify core's unrelated extension runtime.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Every scoped tool appears in Pi `Available tools` with a CLI-shaped label and complete help-derived description.
- [ ] Tool schemas reject invalid targets/IDs and preserve CLI-compatible defaults.

title: P0-05: canonical --subordinate coordinator launch verb
description:
## PROBLEM

Inside $TMUX an interactive role launch defaults to the CURRENT pane
(worktree-session.ts:1466 `currentPaneMode`). That is right when the operator
wants this pane to become the role; it is wrong for spawning a subordinate
coordinator, because it overwrites the orchestrator's own @agent_* metadata and
replaces the orchestrator process. The safe shape today is three flags the
operator must remember and compose correctly: `--new-session --no-attach
--parent "$(tmux display-message -p '#{session_id}')"`. Audit P0-05 asks for one
verb.

## SUCCESS

`xt pi <slug> --role chain-coordinator --bead <id> --subordinate` is equivalent
to the three-flag form. It never runs in the current pane, always prints
`session_name:pane_id`, and always gets its own worktree + branch. `xt claude`
has parity.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts — `WorktreeSessionOptions.subordinate`, resolution in `launchWorktreeSession`/`launchTmuxSession`.
- cli/src/commands/pi.ts, cli/src/commands/claude.ts — `--subordinate` option + help text + example.
- cli/src/tests/worktree-session-role.test.ts (or a new subordinate test file).

## NON_GOALS

- Coordinator-specific launch validation (P1-05) — separate child.
- Changing the current-pane default for non-subordinate role launches.
- Any new worktree/branch behavior — --subordinate must NOT imply "no worktree" or "shared branch".

## CONSTRAINTS

- `--subordinate` implies exactly: newSession=true, attach=false, parent=<current #{session_id}>.
- An explicit `--parent <target>` still wins (operator is being deliberate); an explicit `--attach`-ish contradiction is an error, not a silent override.
- Requires `--role`; requires being inside $TMUX (no parent session id otherwise). Both fail fast with a remediation line, before worktree creation.
- Must not change the stdout contract, session-name shape, or existing pane options.
- Reuse the existing `resolveParentSession` / `currentTmuxSessionId` helpers — no new tmux plumbing.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit test: subordinate option set produces newSession/attach/parent triple.
- [ ] Unit test: `--subordinate` without `--role` is rejected with the audit's suggested error text shape.
- [ ] Unit test: `--subordinate` outside $TMUX is rejected.
- [ ] Unit test: `--subordinate --parent X` honours X.
- [ ] `xt pi --help` and `xt claude --help` both contain `--subordinate` (this is Suite C's probe).
- [ ] `npm run build` clean, `npm test --workspace cli` green.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** `resolveParentSession` (worktree-session.ts:1385), `currentTmuxSessionId` (:833) — both already do exactly the parent resolution this needs.
- **Installed deps:** commander — the option surface is a plain `.option()`.
- **Stdlib:** none needed.
- **New dep candidate:** none — tiers 1-2 cover it.
- **Roll it:** no.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, the flag-implication table, test output, and the exact
`xt pi --help` line Suite C will probe for.
notes: IMPLEMENTED. resolveSubordinateLaunch() (worktree-session.ts) is a pure validator expanding --subordinate to {newSession:true, attach:false, child:!parent}; launchWorktreeSession applies it before anything else so the rest of the launcher only ever sees ordinary flags — no third launch mode. Rejections (both before worktree creation): no --role; outside $TMUX without --parent. Both print the audit's canonical long-form command as remediation, runtime-parameterized. --parent still wins. --subordinate exposed on xt pi and xt claude with help text + example. 5 unit tests. Verified end-to-end live in Suite C step 3 against the packed artifact.

title: P0: Restore Serena as code-navigation-only; never proxy shell or file commands
description:
## Problem
Pi currently prefers Serena MCP wrappers for generic operations such as execute_shell_command and file access because those tools advertise themselves as preferred over direct equivalents. This regresses the previously established boundary: Serena is code-navigation intelligence, not the command/file execution substrate.

The coupling is availability-critical. During live xtmux coordination on 2026-07-13, two ordinary execute_shell_command calls failed with `Serena MCP error: fetch failed` / `Connection closed`; the same read-only commands succeeded immediately through the direct bash tool. An urgent coordination reply was delayed while an unrelated language-server/MCP connection sat on the shell path.

## Expected boundary
Serena may provide semantic code navigation (symbol overview/search, definitions/references, type hierarchy and related read-only code-intelligence queries). Generic shell execution, test/build runners, process management, file reads/writes/edits, directory listing, filename search and ordinary text search must use the direct Pi tools and must not depend on Serena availability.

## Investigation
Find where core generates/registers Serena tool descriptions and the `Preferred over other tools with similar functionality` policy, and why the former code-navigation-only filter/default blocked-tool set regressed. Audit global/project settings generation as well as pi-serena-tools package wiring.
design: Prefer an allowlist of read-only semantic navigation tools over an expanding denylist. Do not solve this by adding runtime fallback after a Serena failure: generic operations should never enter Serena. Keep structured_return/process routing unchanged for tests and long-running commands.
acceptance_criteria:
1. A fresh core-managed Pi session exposes/prefers Serena only for semantic code-navigation operations.
2. Shell commands route to direct bash/structured_return/process; file and filesystem operations route to direct read/write/edit/find/grep/ls tools.
3. With Serena disconnected, ordinary shell and file operations continue without Serena errors or fallback retries.
4. A regression test asserts the allowed Serena tool set and prevents generic execution/file tools from being reintroduced or marked preferred.
5. Existing generated/global settings are migrated or repaired, not only new installs.
6. Documentation states the ownership boundary and the verification command/smoke.
notes: Recurrence root cause fixed: pi-serena-tools reads only current project .pi/settings.json; settings-less xtmux worktree fell back to built-in native blocklist. Patch now rewrites defaultBlockedToolNames to [] in installed extension. Seeded affected worktree .pi/settings.json, hot-patched installed package copies, added regression assertion/docs/changelog. Verified targeted tests/typecheck/docs and fresh xtmux worktree smoke with Serena unavailable: native read+bash called, no Serena generic proxies.
close_reason: Done: PR rebased by merge onto v0.10.5 main after resolving changelog; fail-open Serena fix remains verified.

title: Eliminate Pi package startup conflicts and move beads shortcut to Alt+G
description:
PROBLEM
The Pi package starts with user-visible extension/theme conflict diagnostics. The published custom-footer still registers Ctrl+B, which collides with Pi cursor-left and tmux. The merged follow-up changed it to Alt+B, but Alt+B also collides with Pi word-left. Separately, all four xtrm themes are loaded both from ~/.pi/agent/themes and @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions/themes/xtrm-ui, producing duplicate-name warnings and skipping one copy.

DECISION
Use Alt+G for the custom-footer beads expansion shortcut. Ctrl+B and Alt+B must remain available to Pi's native editor behavior. Establish one canonical loading source for xtrm-dark, xtrm-dark-flattools, xtrm-light, and xtrm-light-flattools so normal startup emits no duplicate-theme diagnostics.

SCOPE
Update source, tests, package/install/update/migration behavior as needed. The fix must work both when loading merged development source with `pi --no-extensions -e <local package>` and when loading the installed npm package. Prefer a generic package/settings ownership fix over suppressing diagnostics.

ACCEPTANCE
1. `/beads` and Alt+G toggle active bead details.
2. The xtrm package registers neither Ctrl+B nor Alt+B.
3. Pi verbose startup emits no xtrm shortcut conflict.
4. Pi verbose startup emits no xtrm theme-name collision; all four themes remain available exactly once.
5. Existing users upgrading from copied ~/.pi/agent/themes assets converge automatically to the canonical ownership model.
6. Unit/package migration coverage protects the shortcut and theme ownership contracts.
7. A real local-source Pi TUI smoke passes before any npm release.

VALIDATION
Use a detached worktree at the exact merged SHA. Launch `PI_OFFLINE=1 pi --no-extensions -e <worktree>/packages/pi-extensions --no-skills --no-prompt-templates --no-context-files --no-tools --approve --verbose`. Capture startup, exercise `/beads`, collapse, then send Alt+G and capture expansion. Also validate the installed-package path after staging the package locally. Record exact SHA and pane evidence; do not release on warnings or unverified package ownership.
notes: Post-close runtime correction: fresh Pi was still loading stale npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions because both ~/.pi/settings.json and ~/.pi/agent/settings.json retained that entry; the local package path was not active. Replaced only those two entries with ~/.pi/agent/local/pi-extensions. Fresh full-Pi Alt+G smoke now loads ~/.pi/agent/local/pi-extensions/src, has no shortcut/theme/extension conflicts, and renders the parent-child footer group. This is a local development override until the package version is published; future runtime sync may intentionally restore the canonical npm package.
close_reason: Corrected package/theme ownership and updated both global/project installs; final fresh-session and external-tool smoke are clean.

title: Make xtrm-ui external tool headers stable across running and completed states
description:
PROBLEM
External-tool rows change visual grammar when execution completes. While running, the row includes the disclosure arrow and bracketed provider badge (for example `› [Serena] execute_shell_command`). After completion, the arrow and brackets disappear (for example `serena execute_shell_command tmux ...`), creating visible flicker and inconsistency with native-tool rendering.

EXPECTED
Preserve the same external-tool header structure before, during, and after execution: disclosure arrow, bracketed provider label, and action/tool name must not disappear or change casing when the result arrives. Render the external tool/action name in bold (for example **execute_shell_command**). Bold treatment applies only to external tools; native Pi tool names retain their existing typography.

SCOPE
Implement this in the generic xtrm-ui external-tool renderer so it covers Serena, MCP, LSP, GitNexus, and any future external provider without provider-specific branches. Keep running/completed/error states visually consistent while retaining their state-specific metadata and colors.

NON_GOALS
Do not change model-facing tool_call/tool_result payloads. Do not bold native tool names. Do not redesign result bodies, footer metadata, expansion behavior, or native-tool rendering beyond what is necessary for parity.

ACCEPTANCE
1. A running external tool shows `› [Provider]` plus a bold tool/action name.
2. Completed and failed renderings preserve that same arrow, brackets, provider casing, and bold tool/action name.
3. Native tool names are not made bold.
4. The behavior is provider-agnostic and applies automatically to future external tools.
5. Transitioning from pending to completed produces no header-shape flicker.
6. Existing Ctrl+O/result expansion and completion metadata remain unchanged.

VALIDATION
Add renderer regression fixtures/snapshots for at least one Serena/MCP external command in running, success, and failure states; assert identical header chrome across states and assert native-tool typography remains unchanged. Manually smoke in a real Pi TUI with an external `execute_shell_command` call.
notes: Implemented generic xtrm-ui external header normalization: running/success/error all render › [Provider] action, provider badge is stable, action is ANSI-bold, native tools remain unchanged, and patch version bumped to 18 for reload. Added Serena/GitNexus/MCP lifecycle regression coverage. Evidence: xtrm-ui parity suite passes (26/26), targeted changed-file suite 54/54, cli typecheck pass, packed installed package contains the renderer change. Live external-provider execution was unavailable in the isolated no-tools TUI smoke; renderer fixtures cover running/success/failure and native typography remains covered by existing tests.
close_reason: Implemented and verified stable provider/action external-tool headers with regression coverage.

title: Service-skills hook paths use CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR — dead after xt migrate skills
description:
## PROBLEM
`policies/service-skills-claude.json` wires the SessionStart cataloger, PreToolUse skill_activator, and PostToolUse drift_detector at `\$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/`. Post-v2 migration (`xt migrate skills --apply`), `.xtrm/skills/default/` is REMOVED from every consumer repo — so every one of those hooks fires `python3: can't open file` on next PreToolUse/PostToolUse/SessionStart. Bash tool BLOCKED in every migrated repo until the hook path is fixed.

Reproduced 2026-07-13 on xtmux repo after fleet migration; sed'd 18/18 fleet repos as immediate unblock. Source repo (core) still ships the broken path.

## SUCCESS
- Hooks resolve regardless of whether the repo is on v1 (default/ present) or v2 (default/ removed).
- Fix: replace `\$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` with `\$HOME` in all three hook commands. Global `~/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/` is present via `ensureGlobalHooksBootstrapped` on any machine with xtrm-tools installed, independent of per-repo state.
- Regenerated hooks.json + registry.
- Consumers pick up the fix via `xt update --apply`.

## SCOPE
- policies/service-skills-claude.json
- .xtrm/config/hooks.json (regenerated)
- .xtrm/registry.json (regenerated)

## NON_GOALS
- No script-side changes (cataloger/skill_activator/drift_detector unchanged).
- No policy schema changes beyond the path substitution.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Match the existing pattern of statusline global-path resolution (already $HOME-based).
- claude-runtime-sync propagates the compiled hooks.json to `.claude/settings.json` on next install/update — no separate consumer-side patch needed after release.

## VALIDATION
- `npm run compile-policies` idempotent (no drift after edit).
- `.xtrm/config/hooks.json` shows $HOME paths for the 3 service-skills hooks.
- Local smoke on core: PreToolUse Bash succeeds (hook doesn't crash).
- Fleet smoke: after xt update --apply, all 18 consumer settings.json switch to $HOME automatically.
close_reason: v0.10.4 published to npm. Service-skills hooks now use $HOME/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/ — verified locally + on fleet. Bash tool unblocked in migrated repos.

title: Reusable workflow parser reads top-level services[] instead of parsed_json.services[]
description:

ROOT CAUSE: parser in step 10 reads from top-level of result JSON:
  r = json.load(open('/tmp/reconcile-result.json'))
  services = r.get('services') or []

But result JSON shape (returned by sp script service-skills-sync) is:
  {success, output (raw str), parsed_json: {summary, services[], actions[]}, meta}

Services + actions are NESTED under parsed_json, not at top level.

Fix: read r['parsed_json'].get('services') or [] (with fallback to top-level for backward compat).

Without this fix, even successful Phase C reconciliations never trigger peter-evans → no auto-PR opens → operator never sees the proposed registry/SKILL.md changes.

Evidence: artifact /tmp/v14/reconcile-result.json from mercury-infra action 28100725859. Parsed_json shows 8 services all 'synced (audited-and-unchanged)' but reconciled_count emerged as empty string.

Tracks final Phase C functionality gate. With this fixed + v14 already proving gitnexus works, Phase C is fully shipped.

title: xt update --apply bakes worktree cwd into .claude/settings.json hook paths
description:
When xt update --apply runs from inside a git worktree (cwd matches .xtrm/worktrees/<name>/), it materializes the **main repo's** .claude/settings.json with literal worktree-nested hook paths like:

  node "/home/dawid/projects/mercury/infra/.xtrm/worktrees/infra-xt-pi-zo58/.xtrm/hooks/beads-memory-gate.mjs"

Those paths break every Stop / PreToolUse / PostToolUse hook when Claude is later opened from the main repo (not the worktree) — node throws MODULE_NOT_FOUND because the literal path doesn't resolve from that session's cwd. Worktrees are ephemeral; baking their path into a tracked config is structurally wrong.

## Repro
1. cd into any xtrm-equipped project (saw it in mercury-infra).
2. Create a worktree: `git worktree add .xtrm/worktrees/<name> main`.
3. cd .xtrm/worktrees/<name>; xt update --apply
4. cd back to the main repo root.
5. Open Claude Code. Every hook crashes with MODULE_NOT_FOUND on the worktree path.

## Observed downstream
- mercury-infra hit this on 2026-06-13 after running xt update --apply for the sre-triage materialization (PR mercuryintelligence/infra#99).
- Hotfix: in-place sed rewrote 16 occurrences (mercuryintelligence/infra#102, commit 5228b38).
- Pattern logged in beads memory `xtrm-worktree-settings-path-drift` (mercury-infra).

## Expected
xt update --apply detects worktree cwd and writes **top-level** .xtrm/hooks/<name>.mjs paths into the main repo's .claude/settings.json — never worktree-nested ones. Or, equivalently: resolve hook paths relative to the main repo root, not cwd.

## Severity
P0 — silently corrupts hook wiring on every worktree-based xt update. Every project using worktrees + xt update is at risk on next sync. Hook crashes are user-facing (visible in Claude UI) and block the bd gate enforcement (memory-gate, edit-gate, etc.) from running.

## Fix sketch
In the materializer, when generating hook command strings:
- Resolve the project root via `git rev-parse --show-toplevel` from a known-stable ancestor (or `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), not from cwd.
- Always emit `<project_root>/.xtrm/hooks/<name>.mjs` regardless of where xt was invoked from.
close_reason: Fix landed: resolveMainProjectRoot(cwd) helper in cli/src/utils/repo-root.ts, applied at xt install (getProjectRoot) + xt update (resolveTargetRepos default). 4 regression tests added; 278/278 cli tests green; cli/dist rebuilt. PR pending.

title: P0: rebuild CLI dist — claude-runtime-sync fix not active until compiled
description:
## Problem

The fix to `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts` (early return when `isGlobal=true` to prevent global hook clobber) exists only in TypeScript source. The compiled output at `cli/dist/` has NOT been rebuilt and is therefore still running the broken behaviour.

Until rebuilt, any `xt install --global` invocation will:
1. Replace the entire `hooks` section of `~/.claude/settings.json` with project-scoped paths hardcoded to the current repo's `.xtrm/hooks/`
2. Wipe hand-configured global hooks (PreCompact `bd prime`, SessionStart `bd prime` + `context-mode-cache-heal.mjs`)
3. Duplicate every hook already owned by the project-level `.claude/settings.json`, causing all hooks to fire twice
4. Hardcode the current project path — any future `xt install --global` from a different repo would re-break the global settings

## What was fixed

`cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts` — inserted early return block at line ~85:

```typescript
if (isGlobal) {
    console.log(t.muted('  ↻ Global install: skipping hook sync (project .claude/settings.json owns hooks)'));
    console.log(t.label(`  • global settings preserved: ${settingsPath}`));
    await ensureGlobalStatusLine();
    return {
        settingsPath,
        hooksEventsWritten: 0,
        hooksEntriesWritten: 0,
        wroteSettings: false,
    };
}
```

Rationale: all hooks reference `<projectRoot>/.xtrm/hooks/` — they are project-scoped by definition. The global `~/.claude/settings.json` must not own them. `ensureGlobalStatusLine()` still runs to keep the statusLine wiring current.

## Fix

```bash
cd ~/dev/xtrm-tools
npm run build        # or: pnpm build / npx tsup
# verify dist is updated:
grep -n 'skipping hook sync' cli/dist/commands/install.js || grep -rn 'skipping hook sync' cli/dist/
```

## Acceptance criteria

- `xt install --global` runs without touching the `hooks` section of `~/.claude/settings.json`
- `xt install --global` still updates the `statusLine` field via `ensureGlobalStatusLine()`
- `~/.claude/settings.json` PreCompact and SessionStart hooks remain intact after a global install

title: P0: auto-apply bd auto-stage patch on xt init/update + verify dependency upgrades
description:
PROBLEM:
Every xtrm-managed repo currently inherits bd's default `export.git-add: true`, which causes persistent dirty-state pain:
- `.beads/issues.jsonl` re-stages after every bd write op (create/update/close/kv-set), blocking `git checkout` mid-orchestration
- Concurrent bd auto-export races with the orchestrator's git operations on `.git/index.lock`
- Sessions accumulate 5-10 throwaway "chore(beads): export state" commits per logical change
- The pain is project-wide: every clone of every repo with bd, on every machine

The fix is two small changes that, once applied, eliminate this class of bug across the orchestration loop:
1. `bd config set export.git-add false`   # bd still auto-exports JSONL on every write, just doesn't stage
2. Append a stage shim to `.git/hooks/pre-commit` AFTER the bd-managed markers — `git add -f .beads/issues.jsonl 2>/dev/null || true`

End-state: mid-work bd ops silent from git's perspective; commits naturally include the fresh JSONL snapshot via the pre-commit hook chain; zero chore commits.

SCRUTINY: high (touches every xtrm-managed repo's git hooks)

SUCCESS:
- `xt init` on a fresh repo: after bd hooks install, automatically applies both the config flip and the pre-commit shim addition
- `xt update` on an existing repo: detects unpatched repos (export.git-add still true OR pre-commit lacks the custom stage block) and applies the patch idempotently
- Patch script must be idempotent — running twice is a no-op
- Patch lives OUTSIDE bd's BEGIN/END markers in .git/hooks/pre-commit so bd's own hooks install/upgrade doesn't clobber it
- Sweep across ~/dev/* and ~/projects/* applying the patch — repo inventory + dry-run report + apply
- Verified end-to-end in specialists repo on 2026-05-25 (see memory: bd-auto-export-pain-fix-set-export-git, commit 63ac83f6)

EXTRA SCOPE — dependency + migration verification:
xt init and xt update must also:
- Detect installed bd version vs latest; suggest or auto-upgrade (with operator confirm for major bumps)
- Detect installed gitnexus version vs latest; same pattern
- Run any pending bd migrations (`bd doctor` may surface these; check + apply)
- Run gitnexus reindex if `.gitnexus/meta.json` schema version drifted
- Report what was upgraded/migrated/patched in a single summary at the end of init/update
- Idempotent: re-running doesn't re-trigger already-applied migrations

SCOPE:
- ~/dev/xtrm-tools/cli/src/commands/init.ts (or equivalent — wherever `xt init` lives)
- ~/dev/xtrm-tools/cli/src/commands/update.ts
- New module: bd-config-patch (apply config flip + hook shim idempotently)
- New module: dependency-checker (bd version, gitnexus version, migrations status)
- Sweep script: applies patch across ~/dev/* and ~/projects/* (one-off, ship as `xt update --all-repos` or similar)

NON_GOALS:
- Not changing bd's defaults upstream (separate upstream issue)
- Not modifying the bd-managed hook section itself
- Not touching repos outside ~/dev and ~/projects
- Not auto-confirming destructive upgrades (operator confirms major version bumps)

CONSTRAINTS:
- Patch must survive `bd hooks install` / bd version upgrades — sits outside bd's markers
- Sweep must be a dry-run by default; --apply flag commits the change
- Each patched repo gets its own atomic commit: "chore: apply bd auto-stage patch (xtrm-tools auto-applied)"
- Migration steps must report what they did, not silently mutate

VALIDATION:
- Test repo gauntlet: create 3 fresh repos, run xt init, verify all three have export.git-add=false + custom hook block + working pre-commit stage behavior
- Test xt update idempotency: run twice on the same repo, second run reports "no changes needed"
- Dependency check: stub a stale bd version, verify update detects + offers upgrade
- Migration check: bd doctor passes after xt update

OUTPUT:
- Updated xt init + xt update commands
- Repo sweep tool
- Inline acceptance evidence (gauntlet runs) in bead notes
- Migration summary format documented in update output

REFERENCES:
- Working recipe verified in /home/dawid/dev/specialists: commit 63ac83f6
- Pre-commit shim addition pattern: lines 26-33 of /home/dawid/dev/specialists/.git/hooks/pre-commit
- Memory: bd-auto-export-pain-fix-set-export-git (full context)

Fresh temp repo using cli/dist/index.cjs and bd init: dry-run detected patch needed; apply wrote export.git-add:false and appended shim to .beads/hooks/pre-commit; second apply was idempotent (already-disabled/already-present, shim_count=1). Smoke exposed and fixed core.hooksPath=.beads/hooks handling for bd v1.0.3 fresh init.

title: P0: installer should add ~/.xtrm/skills/default as second pi skills search path
description:
## PROBLEM
When xtrm-tools installer scaffolds .pi/settings.json into a project, it currently sets:
  "skills": ["../.xtrm/skills/active"]

Specialist configs that reference skills by canonical name (e.g. `.xtrm/skills/active/clean-code/SKILL.md`) fail to resolve in projects that don't have those skills under .xtrm/skills/active/. Symptom: `validateBeforeRun` (src/specialist/runner.ts:255 in specialists repo) emits warnings for missing skill paths; specialists run without their declared skills.

Installer scaffolds .pi/settings.json with two entries:

    "../.xtrm/skills/active",
    "~/.xtrm/skills/default"
  ]

Project-local active skills win; user-level default skills resolve as fallback. No specialist config needs to change.

## SCOPE
xtrm-tools installer code that writes .pi/settings.json during `xt init` / `xt update`.

## NON_GOALS
- No change to skill resolution semantics in pi itself.
- No vendoring skills into projects.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Preserve user-customized .pi/settings.json on `xt update` (don't overwrite if user added their own paths).
- Honor any existing entries the user added.

## VALIDATION
- Fresh `xt init` produces a .pi/settings.json with both paths.
- `xt update` on a project with a single-path .pi/settings.json appends the second path without clobbering other settings.

## OUTPUT
Diff + test.

## REFERENCES
Discovered in specialists repo Phase 0 routing analysis (2026-05-14). Manual fix already applied in /home/dawid/dev/specialists/.pi/settings.json for smoke.

title: fix(deps): declare yaml in cli/package.json — unblock PR 206 CI build
description:
PR 206 (fix/xtrm-krk0-osv-dependencies) CI fails at the bundling step:

  Could not resolve 'yaml' in src/core/beads-shared-server.ts:3

Root cause: cli/src/core/beads-shared-server.ts imports yaml (added 2026-05-12 for xtrm-16ec) but yaml was never declared as a direct dependency in cli/package.json or the root package.json. On main, the build coincidentally works because yaml is hoisted from a transitive dep of tdd-guard (which PR 206 removes as part of the security pruning). On PR 206 with tdd-guard gone, the transitive yaml disappears from node_modules/yaml top-level → bundler cannot resolve.

Fix: add 'yaml': '^2.4.2' to cli/package.json dependencies. Regenerate lockfile. Push to PR branch.

Acceptance:
- CI test (22.x, 3.11) workflow flips to green.
- cli/dist build completes locally.
- No other side effects on the security baseline.
close_reason: Added 'yaml': '^2.4.2' to cli/package.json dependencies. Regenerated cli/package-lock.json + root package-lock.json so node_modules/yaml is top-level. Local cli build clean; full test suite 525/0/98. Unblocks PR 206 CI.

title: P0: xtrm worktree creation propagates contaminated .beads state — pre-merge guard needed against 120000 mode
description:
PROBLEM: Real incident in mercury-market-data 2026-05-11: PR #103 (cvyg STIR cluster) committed .beads as a 120000 self-symlink mode change. squash-merge through gh pr merge --admin accepted it; master ended up with .beads broken; bd died on clone until recovery via PR #107 + bd init --force. Proximate cause is executor's blanket git add (filed in specialists as unitAI-dmu9q), but xtrm-tools should harden at the framework level. Three prongs requested in the original bead; prong 1 (worktree provisioning .beads index match) is ALREADY COVERED by xtrm-nsca (just shipped — cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts suppressBeadsWorktreeNoise via skip-worktree + info/exclude). This bead now scopes ONLY prong 2 — pre-push guard in xt end. Prong 3 (worktree-removal cleanup) is deferred to a follow-up bead if needed; xtrm-nsca's skip-worktree may already render it moot.

SUCCESS: xt end refuses to push/create-PR if the cumulative diff vs upstream introduces a 120000 (symlink) mode for any path under .beads/. Failure must include actionable message naming the offending paths and how to recover. Existing successful flows (no .beads/* in diff at all, or .beads/* changes that are not symlink-mode introductions) MUST NOT regress.

SCOPE: cli/src/commands/end.ts (insert the guard between branch-up-to-date check and the git push call, around line 414), cli/dist/* rebuild, a new regression test under cli/test/ or cli/src/tests/.

NON_GOALS: do not touch the worktree provisioning code (xtrm-nsca covers that prong); do not add the guard as a separate git pre-push hook (out of scope — that'd be a separate bead for defense-in-depth at the git layer); do not change the symlink behavior in worktree-session.ts at all.

CONSTRAINTS: preserve all existing xt end behavior (dry-run, --force-with-lease, PR creation via gh, worktree cleanup); the new guard runs ONLY before push; on dirty .beads/* with NORMAL file modes (100644 → 100644), the guard MUST NOT fire (only 120000 introductions are blocked). Implementation plan: (a) before the push call, run `git -C <cwd> diff <upstream>..HEAD --raw -- .beads/` (the --raw format shows mode bits like ':000000 120000 ... A path'), (b) parse output for any line where the destination mode is '120000' on a .beads/ path, (c) if any match, abort with kleur.red error listing the offending paths + recovery hint ('git restore --source=<upstream> -- .beads/' or similar). Wrap in try/catch — if the diff command fails for any reason, fail SAFE (allow the push, log a warning).

CRITICAL — worktree hygiene per memory specialist-worktree-provisioning-in-xtrm-tools-replaces-trac and the fix that just shipped (cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts suppressBeadsWorktreeNoise): your worktree's checkpoint commits should now naturally exclude .beads/* paths. But STILL: use 'git add' with explicit source/test paths; after bd close, run 'git restore --staged .beads/issues.jsonl' if it auto-exports.

VALIDATION: (1) new test file (cli/src/tests/end-beads-symlink-guard.test.ts or similar) covering: (a) clean diff (no .beads) → allow, (b) normal .beads changes (mode 100644 → 100644) → allow, (c) .beads/* symlink introduction (mode → 120000) → block with descriptive error; (2) targeted vitest run shows test passes; (3) full 'npm test --workspace cli' shows 0 fails (must match current 508 baseline); (4) manual smoke step the executor should document: create a feature branch, stage a fake symlink under .beads/test-symlink, attempt xt end --dry-run, observe the guard fire.

READ_ONLY audit complete: xtrm-tools ships Category B specialists skills via vendored package payload; specialists package ships Category A runtime and requires xt/.xtrm for init skill sync. Recommended order: install xtrm-tools and run xt init/install before specialists init; install sp anytime for CLI, but Category B still requires xt.
### Specialist Output — overthinker (job 91accf) [WAITING — more output may follow]

## Summary

Fresh-machine order: install `xtrm-tools` first, run `xt init` or `xt install`, then install `@jaggerxtrm/specialists`, then run `sp init`.

## Status

Audit done. Read-only. No source edits. Bead closed.

## Phase 1 — Initial Analysis

### Evidence

- `xtrm-tools@0.7.17`
  - bins: `xt`, `xtrm`, `ghgrep`
  - package includes `.xtrm/skills/default`, `.xtrm/hooks`, `.xtrm/registry.json`
  - package includes specialists-facing Cat B skills:
    - `update-specialists`
    - `specialists-creator`
    - `using-specialists`
    - `using-specialists-v2`
    - `using-specialists-v3`
    - `using-nodes`
    - `using-kpi`
    - `using-script-specialists`
- `@jaggerxtrm/specialists@3.13.0`
  - bins: `specialists`, `sp`, `install`
  - package includes Cat A runtime:
    - `config/specialists/*.specialist.json`
    - `config/mandatory-rules/*`
    - `config/hooks/*`
    - `config/skills/*`
  - dependencies do **not** include `xtrm-tools`
- `sp init --help` says prerequisite:
  - `.claude/skills` and `.pi/skills` symlinks must already exist
  - created by `xt install`
  - `--no-xtrm-check` only for CI/testing
- `using-specialists` docs say:
  - `specialists init` requires xtrm
  - `xt` must be installed first
  - failure fix: `npm install -g xtrm-tools && xt install`

### Current split

- Category A = specialists runtime/npm-live assets. Owned by `sp`.
- Category B = xtrm-managed filesystem assets. Owned by `xt`.
- `xt update` can deliver specialists-facing skills without `sp` installed because payload ships inside `xtrm-tools`.
- `sp init/update` cannot own Cat B without `xt`; it can only sync/check specialists-owned parts and needs existing `.xtrm` runtime wiring.

## Phase 2 — Devil's Advocate

### Risk: docs imply specialists “upcoming”

README still says Specialists “upcoming”, while package already ships `using-specialists*` skills and hooks. Docs stale. Fresh user may not know install order.

### Risk: `xt install` does not install `sp`

`xt` machine bootstrap installs `bd`, `dolt`, `bv`, `pi`, `pnpm`, optional `gitnexus`, `deepwiki`, `ctx7`. No `sp`. User can get specialists-facing skills but command examples fail until `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` installed.

### Risk: hard dependency creates release coupling

Making `xtrm-tools` hard-depend on `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` makes every `xt` install pull specialist runtime even for users who never use it. Also creates split-release pressure.

### Risk: peer dependency weak for global CLIs

`peerDependencies` on global CLI packages provide poor UX. npm global peer warnings do not guarantee `sp` command exists. Better: explicit doctor/init checks.

### Risk: source vendoring still dev-path based

`scripts/vendor-specialists-skills.mjs` needs sibling `../specialists`, fallback path, or `SPECIALISTS_REPO_PATH`. Good for dev. Bad for deterministic CI. Existing bead `xtrm-lait` covers immutable package/SHA source.

## Phase 3 — Synthesis

### Correct dependency model

- `xtrm-tools` owns Category B and should remain primary installer for repo runtime.
- `specialists` owns Category A and should remain separate runtime package.
- No hard npm dependency either way.
- `sp init` should keep hard runtime prerequisite check for `xt`/`.xtrm`, not package dependency.
- `xt doctor` should not fail because `sp` missing unless checking specialists workflow explicitly.
- `using-specialists` skill activation should check command availability and give install command.

### Recommended order

```bash
npm install -g xtrm-tools@latest
xt init   # or xt install in existing repo

npm install -g @jaggerxtrm/specialists@latest
sp init
sp doctor
```

### Optional improvement

`xt install --specialists` or `xt install all` may install `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` as optional managed dependency. Not default hard dependency.

## Phase 4 — Final Refined Output

## Fresh-machine smoke matrix

| Scenario | Expected result | Current audit result |
|---|---|---|
| `npm install -g xtrm-tools` only → `xt install/update/doctor` | Works. Cat B installed. `sp` commands unavailable but not required. | Supported. |
| `npm install -g @jaggerxtrm/specialists` only → `sp list` | Works from package/runtime defaults. | Supported by package evidence. |
| `sp doctor` without `xt` | Should report missing xtrm-tools/.xtrm with fix hint. | Help confirms xtrm check. |
| `sp init` without `xt` | Should fail clearly unless `--no-xtrm-check`. | Help confirms prerequisite. |
| install `xt` first then `sp` | Best path. `xt` creates Cat B, `sp init` wires Cat A. | Recommended. |
| install `sp` first then `xt` | `sp list` okay; `sp init` blocked until `xt install/init`; after `xt`, rerun `sp init`. | Acceptable but docs should warn. |
| fresh repo no clones/symlinks/env | `xt init` creates `.xtrm` and skill symlinks. `sp init` follows. | Intended path. |
| `xt update` without `sp` | Cat B refresh works because xtrm package includes vendored skills. | Supported. |
| `sp init --sync-skills` without `xt` | Should fail or require `--no-xtrm-check`; cannot safely own Cat B. | Correct behavior. |

## What must be hard vs optional

| Relationship | Model |
|---|---|
| `sp init` → `xt` | Hard runtime prerequisite check, not npm dependency |
| `xt` → `sp` | Optional command check only |
| Cat B skills | Hard dependency on xtrm package payload |
| Cat A runtime | Hard dependency on specialists package payload |
| Shared package | Not needed now; consider later only for schemas/constants |

title: Orchestrate hard fix for recurring pi-core + pi-mcp-adapter extension load failures
description: User still gets extension load failures in ~/projects/claw-code: missing @xtrm/pi-core for project extensions and ~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-mcp-adapter missing commands.js. Need robust end-to-end solution: reproduce, identify why safeguards didn\'t prevent recurrence, implement durable fix in xtrm-tools, and provide remediation steps that make claw-code healthy immediately.
notes:
Implemented. I wired launch-time self-heal into the **actual Pi startup paths**, added recurrence regression tests, and verified behavior.

### What was failing repeatedly (root cause)
Safeguards from prior fix existed, but were mostly reached via maintenance flows (`xt pi doctor` / `xt pi reload` / install sync), not guaranteed on runtime entrypoints.  
So users could still hit runtime load failures when launching/resuming Pi sessions with broken state:

- broken/missing `.xtrm/extensions/node_modules/@xtrm/pi-core`
- stale `~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-mcp-adapter` override missing `commands.js`

---

## Code changes made

### 1) Launch preflight utility added
**File:** `cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts`

- Added `runPiLaunchPreflight(projectRoot, dryRun, log?)`
- It runs:
  - `remediateStalePiMcpAdapterOverride(...)`
  - `ensureCorePackageSymlink(... .xtrm/extensions/core ...)`

Also reused this preflight inside `runPiRuntimeSync` to keep existing flows intact and avoid drift.

---

### 2) `xt pi` launch path now always pre-heals before Pi starts
**File:** `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts`

- Replaced direct `ensureCorePackageSymlink(...)` call with `runPiLaunchPreflight(worktreePath, false)`
- This now heals both:
  - core symlink
  - stale pi-mcp-adapter override
- Runs before `spawnSync('pi', ...)`

---

### 3) Direct resume helper path covered (`xt attach` for Pi)
**File:** `cli/src/commands/attach.ts`

- Added preflight before runtime spawn when `runtime === 'pi'`:
  - `await runPiLaunchPreflight(target.path, false)`

So both main entrypoints now self-heal at runtime startup.

---

### 4) Regression/integration tests added for recurrence scenario
**New file:** `cli/src/tests/pi-launch-self-heal-regression.test.ts`

Covers both startup paths:

- `xt pi` worktree launch heals:
  - broken `@xtrm/pi-core` symlink
  - stale `pi-mcp-adapter` override
- `xt attach` (Pi resume) heals same broken state before launching Pi

Existing safeguard tests remain and pass:
- `cli/src/tests/pi-runtime-safeguards.test.ts`

---

### 5) Docs update
**File:** `docs/pi-extensions.md`

- Added note that `xt pi` and Pi-mode `xt attach` now run launch-time self-heal before startup.

---

## Exact verification commands + outputs

### A) Regression tests
```bash
cd /home/dawid/projects/xtrm-tools/cli
npm run test -- --run src/tests/pi-runtime-safeguards.test.ts src/tests/pi-launch-self-heal-regression.test.ts
```

Result:
- `2 test files passed`
- `4 tests passed`
- includes:
  - `heals broken core symlink + stale pi-mcp-adapter override on xt pi launch path`
  - `heals broken state on xt attach pi resume path before launching runtime`

---

### B) Immediate health check in `claw-code`
```bash
cd /home/dawid/projects/claw-code
xt pi doctor
```

Observed output:
- `✓ pi-mcp-adapter override check passed`
- `✓ @xtrm/pi-core symlink is healthy`
- `✓ project runtime points to .xtrm/extensions`
- `✓ All checks passed`

---

## Immediate remediation for user (if recurrence appears before upgraded xt build is installed)

Run in `~/projects/claw-code`:

```bash
cd ~/projects/claw-code
rm -rf ~/.pi/agent/extensions/pi-mcp-adapter
mkdir -p .xtrm/extensions/node_modules/@xtrm
rm -f .xtrm/extensions/node_modules/@xtrm/pi-core
ln -s ../../core .xtrm/extensions/node_modules/@xtrm/pi-core
xt pi doctor
```

Expected doctor output includes:
- `✓ pi-mcp-adapter override check passed`
- `✓ @xtrm/pi-core symlink is healthy`

title: Investigate broken xtrm extension session gating and migrate memory gate from file marker to session KV
description:
## Problem

In a live specialists session using currently installed xtrm extensions/hooks, bead gates and memory workflow appear active but not behaving correctly. The session repeatedly hit gate errors like 'No active claim for session ... bd update <id> --claim' even after issues had already been claimed. This suggests the gate/runtime is loaded, but the claim/session identity path is inconsistent or stale.

## Observed symptoms

- Bead edit gating is active in-session
- Claimed issues were not consistently recognized by the current session
- Tooling behaved as if there was no active claim for the session even after successful bd claim operations
- Memory workflow artifacts still showed file-based behavior (for example `.beads/.memory-gate-done`)

## Required investigation

1. Reproduce the session-level claim/gate mismatch in a real xtrm-equipped session
2. Verify which extensions/hooks are actually active and in what order
3. Trace how `claimed:<sessionId>` and related KV entries are written and read
4. Confirm whether Claude/Pi/session IDs diverge across the installed gate path
5. Determine whether hook registration, KV writes, or extension session identity is the root cause

## Required fix direction

The memory gate should no longer rely on the file marker `.beads/.memory-gate-done`. It should use the session KV / issue identity path instead. Update the design so memory acknowledgment and gating are keyed off KV state (for example session-scoped or issue-scoped KV), not a filesystem sentinel file.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Claimed issue is consistently recognized by bead gates throughout a live session
- [ ] No false 'No active claim for session' errors after a valid claim
- [ ] Root cause documented (hook mismatch, session ID mismatch, KV bug, or extension load bug)
- [ ] Memory gate no longer depends on `.beads/.memory-gate-done`
- [ ] Memory acknowledgment uses KV-backed state instead
- [ ] Regression test or reproducible verification steps documented

## Notes

This is a P0 because it undermines trust in the active xtrm workflow during normal issue-driven sessions: the gates are loaded, but they may block legitimate work incorrectly, and the memory gate still uses a file-based mechanism that should be replaced.
notes: PR: https://github.com/Jaggerxtrm/xtrm-tools/pull/164
close_reason: Fix memory gate ack: remove stale file-marker instruction from claim-sync, drop file-marker fallback in messages, remove dead isMemoryGatePending/isMemoryAckCommand; clean 27 stale claimed KV entries

title: Re-enter worktree session after Claude/Pi closes
description:
## Problem

When working with `xt claude` or worktrees in general, if Claude/Pi session closes unexpectedly, there's no easy way to re-enter the worktree and resume work.

## Proposed Solution

1. **CLI command to re-enter latest worktree**
   - `xt attach` or `xt resume` — re-enters most recent worktree
   - `xt tree list` shows worktrees with timestamps for easy selection

2. **Session persistence**
   - Ability to resume the same Claude/Pi session from the worktree
   - Evaluate tmux integration for session persistence
   - Session state saved to worktree metadata

3. **Enhanced `xt tree list`**
   - Show date/time of last activity
   - Show branch name, issue ID, session status
   - Easy reattach/resume commands

## Acceptance

- `xt attach` re-enters latest worktree
- `xt tree list` shows timestamps and session state
- Session resume works (via tmux or session file)
- Works for both Claude and Pi runtimes

title: Repurpose session-flow policy: remove xtrm-finish refs, align with xt end + worktree flow
description:
## Context
`policies/session-flow.json` currently describes:
> 'Worktree auto-creation on claim and session closure enforcement via xtrm finish'

`xtrm finish` is deprecated and removed. `.xtrm-session-state.json` is gone. The policy's Claude hooks (`beads-claim-sync.mjs` PostToolUse + `beads-stop-gate.mjs` Stop) are still valid and correct. The Pi extension `config/pi/extensions/session-flow.ts` needs investigation.

The policy should be repurposed to reflect the ACTUAL current behavior: claim sync auto-commits on `bd close`, the stop gate blocks stop when an issue is still in_progress, and `xt end` is the closure command.

## Step 1: Read the actual Pi extension
Read `config/pi/extensions/session-flow/index.ts` (or wherever the session-flow Pi extension lives). Identify every reference to:
- `xtrm finish`
- `.xtrm-session-state.json`
- Session phases (`waiting-merge`, `conflicting`, `pending-cleanup`, `cleanup-done`)
- Any mention of worktree auto-creation via `--claim`

## Step 2: Determine what to keep vs rewrite
The Pi extension should either:
- (a) Be simplified to match the Claude side: stop gate (block if in_progress claim) + claim sync (auto-commit on bd close)
- (b) Be extended to know about `xt end` — when a worktree session ends (`agent_end`), if there is an open in_progress claim, remind the agent to run `xt end` and close the issue

Option (b) is preferred and aligns with the new `xt-end` skill.

## Step 3: Update policy description
Update `session-flow.json` description to:
> 'Claim sync (auto-commit on bd close), stop gate (blocks stop with unclosed in_progress claim), xt end reminder on session close in worktree context.'

## Step 4: Update session-flow Pi extension
Rewrite `config/pi/extensions/session-flow/index.ts` to:
- Remove all `xtrm finish` command references
- Remove all `.xtrm-session-state.json` file reads/writes
- Remove all session phase tracking (`waiting-merge`, etc.)
- Keep: stop gate logic (if in_progress claim, block agent_end with message to close issue first)
- Add: on `agent_end`, if in a worktree (detect: cwd contains `.xtrm/worktrees/`), remind to run `xt end` to create PR and clean up

## Step 5: Verify Pi extension still compiles
Run `pi check` or equivalent to verify the updated extension has no TypeScript errors.

## Step 6: Update `docs/pi-extensions.md`
Update the `session-flow` row in the Extension Catalog table.

## Expected Outcome
- `session-flow.json` description is accurate
- Pi extension has no references to deprecated commands
- Stop gate still works: agent_end is blocked when there is an active in_progress claim
- New behavior: xt end reminder fires when session ends in a worktree context
- No TypeScript errors in the extension

## Required Close Message
1. What was found in the original Pi extension (exact deprecated references)
2. Every function/handler modified or removed, with brief description
3. The exact new behavior of each event handler that was changed
4. Whether the stop-gate behavior is confirmed unchanged
5. Whether the xt-end reminder was implemented and what it says
6. Result of Pi extension compilation check
7. Updated `docs/pi-extensions.md` row content
close_reason: session-flow extension rewritten: removed all xtrm-finish/session-state/worktree-auto-creation dead code. Now has claim sync, stop gate (blocks on in_progress), and xt end reminder in worktrees. PR #129 merged.

title: Migrate worktree path from sibling dirs to .xtrm/worktrees/ inside repo
description:
## Context
Currently `xt claude` / `xt pi` create worktrees as siblings of the main checkout (e.g. `../xtrm-tools-xt-claude-ab3k`). This clutters the user's projects root and makes worktrees hard to find. They should live inside the repo under `.xtrm/worktrees/<name>`.

## Required Changes

### 1. `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts`
Change `worktreePath` from:
```ts
path.join(path.dirname(cwd), worktreeName)
```
To:
```ts
path.join(repoRoot, '.xtrm', 'worktrees', worktreeName)
```
The rest of the Dolt bootstrap (port file redirect) is already correct — it writes to `worktreePath/.beads/dolt-server.port` which is relative to the new location. Verify this still works with the new path.

### 2. `cli/src/commands/worktree.ts`
`listXtWorktrees` discovers worktrees from `git worktree list`. Since git worktree list returns absolute paths, it will automatically pick up the new location — verify this. The branch filter (`xt/*`) remains the same.

`xt worktree remove` matches by path or branch name — verify path matching still works.

### 3. `.gitignore`
Add `.xtrm/worktrees/` to ensure the worktree dirs themselves are gitignored (they are git worktrees so git knows about them, but the directory content should not be tracked by the main repo).

### 4. `docs/worktrees.md`
Update every path reference: naming convention table, the launch flow diagram, troubleshooting section.

### 5. Rebuild
`cd cli && npm run build` — update `cli/dist/`

### 6. Version bump + publish
Bump patch version, run `node scripts/sync-cli-version.mjs`, publish `npm publish --tag latest`.

## Expected Outcome
- `xt claude` creates worktree at `<repo>/.xtrm/worktrees/xtrm-tools-xt-claude-<slug>`
- `xt worktree list` shows the new path correctly
- `xt worktree clean` removes merged worktrees from the new location
- `.xtrm/worktrees/` is gitignored
- `docs/worktrees.md` is accurate

## Required Close Message
State exactly:
1. The exact new path pattern (with example)
2. Every file changed with brief description of each change
3. Confirmation that Dolt bootstrap still works (port redirect written before claude launch)
4. Confirmation `xt worktree list` and `xt worktree clean` work with the new paths
5. npm version published and confirmed
6. Any edge cases discovered (e.g. what happens if .xtrm/worktrees/ doesn't exist yet)
