title: xtmux installer omits --new-instance for Claude SessionStart, so Claude panes never get an instance id
description:
## PROBLEM

`xtmux scripts/install.mjs:209` wires the Claude `SessionStart` hook as `agent-state.sh SessionStart idle`. It does not pass `--new-instance`. The string `--new-instance` appears nowhere in the installer.

So a Claude pane never generates an agent instance id and never emits `agent.ready`.

## THE INSTALLER CONTRADICTS ITS OWN SPEC AND SCRIPT

`docs/xtmux-gaps.md:550` states plainly:

    For Pi, invoke the new-instance path on `session_start`.
    For Claude, invoke it on `SessionStart`.
    Do not generate a new identity on every `idle` transition.

`scripts/agent-state.sh` supports the flag: usage line at :16, help text at :17, parse at :35. Its own comment at :152 shows the intended call: `XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD=... agent-state.sh idle --new-instance`.

The script is right. The spec is right. The installer is wrong.

## EVIDENCE

Measured 2026-07-26 across every live pane on this host:

  10 panes started by `xt claude`  -> @agent_instance_id absent on all 10
  pi panes                          -> id present
  panes not started by xt claude    -> id present

Found by the worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.18. Verified independently by the orchestrator with a sweep over `tmux list-panes -a`.

## CONSEQUENCE

This is the true root cause behind bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.18. Core PR #510 corrects the core side: it now waits for a readiness handshake instead of polling a fixed 5 seconds. But no readiness signal can ever arrive for a Claude pane, because the identity is never created. The visible result changed from a warning after 5 seconds to a warning after 30 seconds.

So `xt claude --role <r> --bead <id>` still cannot auto-assign a bead. The feature shipped in core#508 cannot work for Claude until this lands.

It also means Claude panes are invisible to any xtmux feature keyed on agent instance identity.

## SUCCESS

- The installer passes `--new-instance` on Claude `SessionStart`, and only there, per the spec.
- A new `xt claude` pane carries `@agent_instance_id` within a bounded time.
- `xt claude --role <r> --bead <id>` assigns the bead with no warning.
- A test asserts the installer emits the flag, so it cannot be dropped again in silence.

## SCOPE

- xtmux scripts/install.mjs (the Claude SessionStart wiring)
- an installer snapshot test covering the flag

## NON_GOALS

- Changing agent-state.sh. It already supports the flag.
- Changing the Pi wiring.
- Generating an identity on every idle transition. The spec forbids it.

## VALIDATION

[ ] A fresh xt claude pane has @agent_instance_id
[ ] xt claude --role executor --bead <id> sets the assignee with no warning
[ ] Installer test fails if the flag is removed
close_reason: Merged as Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#79. The installer now passes --new-instance on Claude SessionStart, as docs/xtmux-gaps.md:550 requires. Live proof from the worker: before, 10 xt claude panes had no @agent_instance_id; after, pane %7442 received an id and emitted agent.ready, and pane %7443 launched with --role executor --bead and received both an id and the bead assignee claude/57a14, with no warning. The orchestrator verified this independently after the merge: a new xt claude pane %7481 received id 7db2faa7. Gates: bun test 304/0, test/contract.sh 288/0, installer tests 11/0. This also completes bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.18. Core#510 supplied the readiness handshake; this supplies the identity. Auto-assign now works end to end for Claude. Two items the worker flagged and left alone: the live ~/.claude/settings.json holds three duplicate xtmux agent-state.sh entries with no _source tag, and the Codex wiring has no --new-instance at all. Both are pre-existing and are now bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.27.

title: sp run --background works but is undocumented; skill states it does not exist
description:
## PROBLEM

`sp run --background` is fully implemented and works. It is absent from `sp run --help`, and the using-specialists skill states the flag "never existed". Both statements are false, and together they hide the only correct dispatch mechanism for an agent pane.

## EVIDENCE

Implementation, specialists src/cli/run.ts:
  :117  parses `--background`
  :938  background branch
  :961  under tmux -> createTmuxSession with a live feed
  :976  otherwise -> re-invoke detached, `detached: true` + `child.unref()`
  :957  propagates SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1 so the detached child keeps the ORIGINAL pane binding (spec 13.2)

Verified 2026-07-26 from pane %7342:
  sp run explorer --prompt "one-line probe" --background
  -> returned in 1 second, printed job id d9663f, runtime-origin captured verified=true
  -> job reached done, turns=3, exit_reason=agent_end
  -> MSG-05 delivered d9663f:done, event_name=job.completed, body.parent.verified=true

So the detached path preserves both the job lifecycle and the parent notification.

## WHY IT IS HIDDEN

Bead xtrm-wiy5n.3.4 ("CLI honesty") described `--background` as "advertised as a run flag but unsupported. Also PARSED by run.ts - so half-exists". Its SUCCESS criterion was: "--background removed from help + index + decided fate of parse branch (either delete branch or document truth)."

The help removal happened. The parse branch stayed. Neither fate was chosen or recorded. The result is worse than the state it replaced: a working feature with no documentation, plus a skill that actively denies it.

## IMPACT

This is not cosmetic. A foreground `sp run` cannot be used from a pi or Claude pane at all — the bash tool reaps descendants on return or timeout and kills the job, which then reports SessionKilledError with turns=0 and reads exactly like a product defect. A trailing `&` does not help, because it backgrounds only within the shell. On 2026-07-26 this produced a multi-hour misdiagnosis and one false P1 bead.

## DECISION REQUIRED

Complete the fate decision bead 3.4 deferred. Either:
- SUPPORT: restore `--background` to `sp run --help` and to the CLI index, add a test, and state in using-specialists that it is the required form from an agent pane; or
- REMOVE: delete the parse branch and lines 936-996, and document the supported alternative for an agent pane. Note that no alternative currently exists — `&` is insufficient — so REMOVE requires providing one.

SUPPORT is the cheaper and more honest option on current evidence, but the owner decides.

## SCOPE

- specialists src/cli/help.ts (flag listing)
- specialists src/cli/run.ts:936-996 (only if REMOVE is chosen)
- specialists config/skills/using-specialists/references/monitoring.md (the "never existed" sentence)
- a test asserting help and implementation agree

## VALIDATION

[ ] `sp run --help` and the implementation agree
[ ] using-specialists no longer claims the flag does not exist
[ ] A test fails if a parsed run flag is missing from help
[ ] Agent-pane dispatch guidance names a mechanism that actually survives a tool timeout
notes:
PARTLY ADDRESSED by xtrm-dev/specialists#227 (bead 4.20). That PR made the skill honest: references/monitoring.md now mandates --background from an agent pane, states that a trailing & is not sufficient and why, and cites src/cli/run.ts instead of the help text. It also carries a note at the top that the help text is wrong.

So the skill side is DONE. What remains is the CLI side, which is the real fault:
  1. sp run --help still omits --background.
  2. Bead xtrm-wiy5n.3.4 never decided the fate of the parse branch. That decision is still open.
  3. No test asserts that a parsed run flag appears in help. Without it, the two drift again.

Do not repeat the skill work. Read references/monitoring.md first to see what is already stated.
close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/specialists#228. Decision: SUPPORT, with reasons. --background is implemented (run.ts:117 parse, :938 branch, tmux live-feed or detached re-invoke, SPECIALISTS_RUNTIME_ORIGIN_V1 propagation), integration tests already cover it, and the MCP start_specialist tool already recommends it. REMOVE would need a replacement invented first; none exists and a trailing & is not one. The parity guard bead 3.4 never built now exists: tests/unit/cli/command-help.test.ts extracts every '--x' literal parsed by src/cli/run.ts and asserts each appears in run --help, so code and help cannot drift apart in silence again. The false statement was in four places, not one: run --help omitted the flag, docs/cli-reference.md claimed '--background is removed and exits with error' (false on both counts), the quickstart repeated it, and two tests asserted its absence. All corrected. Codex found a real defect in the new work: --background --json printed a bare job id onto an NDJSON stream. The worker kept the combination, because an agent pane needs it, and made the output valid JSON via formatBackgroundLaunchLine; it placed the assertion outside tests/unit/cli/run.test.ts because that file is quarantined under bead 4.11 and would not run in CI. Live proof: --background --json returned in about 1s with valid NDJSON (jobId d82175), the job reached done, and MSG-05 job.completed arrived with parent.verified=true.

title: specialists master: content-preservation guard is red — DOC-01 dropped 4 mapped headings
description:
## PROBLEM

`tests/unit/skills/using-specialists-layout.test.ts` fails on specialists master. The test guards the 2026-07-14 router split (b973312d) against content loss: every heading recorded in `references/content-migration-map.json` must still exist either in SKILL.md or as a mapped reference.

Four headings are now unaccounted for:

  Monitoring Long-Running Jobs: Sleep Timers Are Mandatory
  Notification Via Observability DB (Preferred Over `sp ps` Polling)
  Specialist Rebuttal As Routine
  Monitoring And Steering

Cause: DOC-01 (a2619d76, PR #222, bead xtrm-wiy5n.3.7) cut `references/monitoring.md` from 205 lines to 28 and did not update the migration map. The guard that exists specifically to catch this was not run or not honoured before merge.

A second test, `tests/unit/skills/selective-loading.test.ts`, also fails on master. Both reproduce on clean master and were independently confirmed by the worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.10.

## WHY THIS IS P1

Bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.4 releases Specialists 3.21.2 from master. Cutting a release while the content-preservation guard is red ships the loss and removes the signal.

The lost material is operational, not decorative. The "sleep timers are mandatory" and observability-DB notification sections are monitoring doctrine. Their absence contributed to a full misdiagnosis on 2026-07-26, where an orchestrator killed its own specialist job with a caller-side timeout and read the result as a product defect.

## DECISION REQUIRED PER HEADING

For each of the four, choose RESTORE or RETIRE, with evidence:

- RESTORE: the guidance is still true and load-bearing. Put it in the correct reference file, in DOC-01 compact style — do not paste the old block back verbatim. Prefer routing to `sp run --help` / `sp feed --help` over restating CLI flags, because restated flags are what rotted twice already.
- RETIRE: the guidance is obsolete or now lives elsewhere. Remove the heading from `content-migration-map.json` and record in the PR body WHY it is obsolete and WHERE the reader is served instead.

Do not make the test pass by deleting entries from the map without that justification. The map is the record of the split.

## SCOPE

- specialists tests/unit/skills/using-specialists-layout.test.ts (read only — do not weaken the assertion)
- specialists tests/unit/skills/selective-loading.test.ts (diagnose; fix if the same cause)

## NON_GOALS

## CONSTRAINTS

- Keep DOC-01 compact style. Route to CLI help rather than restating flags.
- One PR. Bead id in the PR body.

## VALIDATION

[ ] using-specialists-layout.test.ts green
[ ] selective-loading.test.ts green or its failure shown to be a separate pre-existing cause with its own bead
[ ] Every RETIRE decision is justified in the PR body
[ ] npm test green apart from failures proven pre-existing and unrelated
close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/specialists#227. The content-preservation guard is green again. Per-heading decisions, each justified in the PR: RETIRE 'Notification Via Observability DB' (the private DB is not a consumer contract per docs/cli-reference.md, and sp result --wait --json replaces the sleep-loop recipe; recorded in a new retired block in the migration map with heading, bead id, reason and redirect, not dropped in silence). RESTORE 'Monitoring And Steering' (selective-loading.test.ts names monitoring.md as sole owner, so it is structurally required; kept only the semantics that --help omits). RESTORE 'Specialist Rebuttal As Routine' (nothing supersedes it and it has no flags that can rot). RESTORE 'Monitoring Long-Running Jobs'. monitoring.md went 29 -> 109 lines against 205 before DOC-01, with nothing copied word for word. Tests: both files went from 2 failed of 41 to 41 passed; full suite 137 passed, 7 skipped, 0 failed. dist/asset-contract.json regenerated. title: xt claude --role resolves an inaccessible model (qwencloud), so every role-mode worker dies at turn 1
description:
## PROBLEM

`xt claude --role <specialist> --bead <id>` starts a session that cannot run. The session reports:

    There is an issue with the selected model (qwencloud/qwen3.8-max-preview).
    It may not exist or you may not have access to it. Run /model to pick a different model.

The pane footer shows `?/200k (qwencloud) qwencloud/qwen3.8-max-preview`. The worker never takes a turn. It sits in `@agent_state=needs-input` and does nothing. An orchestrator that dispatches and then waits will wait forever.

## EVIDENCE

2026-07-26. Two role-mode launches, both dead on arrival:
  role-claude-executor-xtrm-wiy5n-4-1   pane %7348
  role-claude-executor-xtrm-wiy5n-4-18  pane %7349

The executor specialist config does NOT ask for that model:

    jq .specialist.execution executor.specialist.json
    -> { "model": null, "fallback_model": null }

So the model comes from the launcher or from a default map, not from the specialist. With `model: null` the launcher should inherit the parent runtime model.

Bare mode on the same host, same repo, same account works correctly and inherits the parent model:
  claude-wiy5n-410  pane %7350  -> Opus 5 (1M context), running
  claude-wiy5n-421  pane %7352  -> Opus 5 (1M context), running

## IMPACT

Role mode is the documented path in /multiplexing Pattern 7 and in /using-specialists for coordinator and worker dispatch. While this holds, every role-mode dispatch is silently useless. The failure is quiet: the session exists, the tmux pane exists, the picker shows it, and only a pane capture reveals that no turn ever ran.

Workaround in use: dispatch in bare mode with the contract in a /tmp file. That loses the bead-rendered turn-1 task, so the contract must tell the worker to run `bd show` itself.

## SUCCESS

- `xt claude --role <r>` with `execution.model: null` inherits the parent runtime model.
- A model that the account cannot use is rejected at launch with a clear error, instead of producing a live but dead session.
- `--model` still overrides.

## SCOPE

- core cli role-mode model resolution in the xt claude launcher
- whatever default map supplies `qwencloud/qwen3.8-max-preview`

## VALIDATION

[ ] xt claude --role executor --bead <id> takes turn 1 and does work
[ ] A launch with an unusable model fails loudly at launch
[ ] Bare mode behaviour is unchanged
notes:
REBASE #3 (onto #515) DONE. PR #511 head d7a64f1e = MERGEABLE/CLEAN, all 7 checks pass, 0 unresolved threads.

Only CHANGELOG.md conflicted, as predicted (generated-block churn, tracked as xtrm-wiy5n.4.28). Resolved by the operator's method: take main's version, npm run changelog:update, stage. No hand-merge. cli/dist rebuilt; drift gates from #514 clean locally (forbidden-phrases 0 violations; vendored-specialists-parity OK @ ba8526cd, matching #515's re-vendor).

git diff bf41108f d7a64f1e -- cli/src docs cli/dist is EMPTY: the rebase changed no source, so the Codex-approved content (👍, no findings) still stands and no new review round was needed.

Validation on the rebased tree: npm test --workspace cli 1106 passed / 0 failed; worktree-session-role 133 passed. Bead still OPEN per contract. Ready to merge FIRST per operator's merge order (core#513 held behind it).
close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/core#511. Role mode no longer forwards a model the account cannot use. Live proof from the worker: pane %7425 failed before the change with 'issue with the selected model (qwencloud/qwen3.8-max-preview)' and never took turn 1; pane %7445 after the change ran Opus 5, used a shell tool and answered PROOF4-OK. Codex needed five rounds and found six defects: three P1 (Bedrock ARN allowlist, nested openrouter/anthropic/claude-* names, custom-gateway rejection) and three P2 (passthrough --model bypass, native-flag masking, the operator's own --). All corrected and every thread resolved. Checks: npm test --workspace cli 1082 passed 0 failed; role suite 128 passed; build with cli/dist committed. title: core#508 bead auto-assign loses a race with pi runtime registration; feature never fires on --role --bead
description:
## PROBLEM

`assignBeadToRuntime()` (cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:41) polls the tmux pane option `@agent_instance_id` for at most `RUNTIME_ORIGIN_WAIT_ATTEMPTS = 50` iterations at 100ms — a 5 second budget — immediately after session creation. If the id has not appeared by then it warns `runtime-origin unavailable for <bead>; session launch continues` and skips the assignment entirely.

The pi runtime registers its instance id LATER than 5s, so the feature shipped in core#508 ("feat(cli): assign beaded sessions from runtime origin", bead xtrm-wiy5n.3.13) does not fire at all in the `xt pi --role <r> --bead <id>` shape.

## EVIDENCE

Both `--role --bead` launches on 2026-07-26 emitted the warning:
  ⚠ bead assignee: runtime-origin unavailable for xtrm-0l718; session launch continues
  ⚠ bead assignee: runtime-origin unavailable for xtrm-vm7s0; session launch continues

Proof it is a RACE and not a permanent absence — the same panes carry the id once settled:
  %7345 (advisor pane, warned at launch) -> @agent_instance_id = 527359c1-90f0-4a2a-84f7-076bb28858a4
  %7342 (orchestrator pane)              -> @agent_instance_id = 0bf33b58-f757-486c-9b1b-13b22d90e9ae

Corroborating: the SPECIALISTS-side runtime-origin capture succeeds from those very panes, synchronously and verified — jobs 5ff574 and 2ad8ba both recorded spawn_origin.runtime_origin with verified=true, capture_source=xtmux-context, correct session/pane/parent ids, one logging `outcome=ok duration_ms=212`. Same host, same panes: specialists resolves it, Cores xt CLI does not. So the data source is available; Core is reading the wrong signal at the wrong time.

## ROOT CAUSE

The function synchronizes on a bare tmux pane option with a fixed timeout instead of on the canonical runtime-origin or a readiness handshake. Existing tests simulate an already-available id and therefore never exercise delayed registration or an end-to-end `--role --bead` launch.

## SUCCESS

- `xt pi --role <r> --bead <id>` sets the bead assignee to `pi/<slug>` with no warning.
- Synchronization is deterministic (readiness signal or canonical runtime-origin), NOT merely a larger timeout.
- Integration coverage for a role launch with delayed instance-id registration.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts — assignBeadToRuntime, RUNTIME_ORIGIN_WAIT_ATTEMPTS, runtimeAssigneeFromOrigin
- the corresponding CLI tests

## RELEASE IMPACT

Gates xtrm-wiy5n.4.6 (Core 0.11.3). Either fix it, or explicitly withdraw core#508 from the release notes and defer the feature — shipping it as-is means advertising an auto-assignment that never happens.

## VALIDATION

[ ] Role launch with a bead assigns pi/<slug>, no warning
[ ] Test covers delayed instance-id registration
[ ] Fix is a readiness/canonical-origin signal, not a bumped timeout
notes: TRUE ROOT CAUSE IS UPSTREAM. Core PR #510 fixes the core half correctly: it waits for a runtime readiness handshake instead of polling @agent_instance_id for a fixed 5 seconds. But no readiness signal can ever arrive for a Claude pane, because xtmux never creates the identity. See xtrm-wiy5n.4.25. Visible effect of #510 alone: the warning moves from 5s to 30s, and auto-assign still does not happen. Do not read a merged #510 as 'auto-assign works'. It works only after 4.25 lands.
close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/core#510. The core half is correct: assignBeadToRuntime now waits for a runtime readiness handshake instead of polling @agent_instance_id for a fixed 5 seconds (50 x 100ms). PARTIAL EFFECT ONLY, recorded so nobody reads this as done: a Claude pane never emits readiness, because xtmux's installer omits --new-instance on Claude SessionStart. So auto-assign still does not happen for xt claude; the warning simply moves from 5s to 30s. The upstream fault is bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.25, which now blocks the xtmux release 4.5. title: Advisor: adjudicate open Sprint 2/3 decisions after a session with repeated misdiagnosis
description:
## PROBLEM

A Claude orchestrator session closed Sprint 2 (xtrm-wiy5n.3) and filed several follow-ups, but produced THREE retracted claims along the way. The board and close reasons have been corrected, but confidence in the surviving conclusions is low. You are asked to adjudicate — not to implement.

Treat every recommendation below as suspect. The orchestrator was wrong three times today, each time confidently and each time with evidence that looked sufficient. Where you find the reasoning sound, say so plainly; where you do not, say that instead. A verdict of "the orchestrator is right" is a useful result — do not manufacture disagreement.

## WHAT HAPPENED (needed to judge the rest)

The §7 live demo of the MSG-05 wave appeared to fail. Two probe jobs died with SessionKilledError. The orchestrator filed a P1 claiming specialist jobs die at spawn. That was WRONG: `sp run` streams to stdout until completion and both callers killed their own job with a short timeout (a `timeout 40` wrapper; and a pi pane whose bash tool defaults to 30s). Re-run without a timeout, job 5ff574 completed and produced the full MSG-05 chain. Retracted.

Second wrong claim: that /using-specialists contains no guidance on this. FALSE — references/monitoring.md:11-37 covers it completely (no --background flag, blocking/streaming behavior, `&` + log-redirect detach form, pi bash-tool caveat). The grep that "proved" absence used phrasings from `sp --help`, not from the skill.

Third wrong claim: that the 2026-07-14 router split (specialists b973312d, SKILL.md 1416 -> 256 lines + references/) dropped ~16 sections. FALSE — false positives from two-word heading matching. Term counts show content survived and grew.

Actual incident root cause, as currently believed: the orchestrator skipped the mandatory `sp --help` check, then pasted a literal command copied from a stale plan file into a delegated bead contract, which suppressed the worker chain-coordinators own help-lookup. The coordinator loaded /using-specialists correctly and ran what it was handed.

## DECISIONS REQUESTED

For each, give: VERDICT (AGREE / DISAGREE / NEEDS-EVIDENCE), a one-paragraph rationale, and if DISAGREE what should happen instead.

D1. `sp run` process ownership. The operator asked whether backgrounding should become the DEFAULT with `--foreground` as opt-in. The orchestrator pushed back and proposed instead: make the JOB SURVIVE CLIENT DETACH (job has a persisted id, DB row, worktree; it should not be owned by the launching process lifetime), so foreground becomes merely an attached view and a tool timeout detaches rather than kills. Argument against the flag flip: `--background` was purged in Sprint 2 (bead 3.4, "CLI honesty") because it implied a detachment the architecture did not deliver; making it the default re-introduces that lie, now on by default, and silently changes semantics for every existing call site including humans wanting the stream. Cheap interim proposed: warn when `!process.stdout.isTTY`. Judge all three options. Consider whether detach-ownership is actually feasible given how src/pi/session.ts manages the pi child (group SIGKILL at session.ts:1272 and 1307).

D2. Bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.13 — "dead specialist job never transitioned to terminal, so MSG-05 never fires". Currently P3. Evidence: job b3402f event trace shows `dead_job_detected` with previous_status=running AND next_status=running; no run_complete; no notification. Is this real and correctly prioritized, or is it subsumed by D1 (if jobs stop dying with their client, is this reachable at all)?

D3. Bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.14 — "xtmux wait-agent returns done while @agent_state reads running". Observed twice, second time armed after confirming the pane was already working. BUT the repro used bare `wait-agent <pane>`; the Claude Stop hook (~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs:43) emits `xtmux wait-agent <target> --wait-for-transition --consume --timeout 30m --interval 30s`, a different code path. Question: is this a release risk for xtrm-wiy5n.4.5 (xtmux 0.2.3, ships MSG-01..04 + the Stop/monitor semantics), or a P2 affecting only hand-armed orchestrator waits? What is the minimum test that settles it?

D4. Bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.15 — after two retractions this bead now holds only: (a) verified launcher flag drift in /multiplexing Pattern 2b and 7 (bare `--no-attach` is rejected; `--role` rejects `--bead`+`--prompt` together), and (b) a suggestion that `sp run` INVOCATION semantics living in references/monitoring.md are mis-filed, since that files routing label reads "Wait on a running job, steer it, rebut it, or escalate" — a post-dispatch label — while an agent seeking invocation form would consult references/registry-and-locations.md and find nothing. Is (b) a real discoverability defect worth fixing, or over-reading a single incident whose true cause was process discipline?

D5. Bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.16 — monitor registry holds 208 non-done entries, 199 with a dead requester pane, only 14 flagged orphan=true. Separately, several bead VALIDATION blocks and /multiplexing end-of-session hygiene cite "xtmux monitor-list empty", which is unsatisfiable because the list is host-global across all live sessions. Judge both the GC need and the correct wording for the hygiene check.

D6. Release readiness. Beads xtrm-wiy5n.4.4 (specialists 3.21.2), .4.5 (xtmux 0.2.3), .4.6 (core 0.11.3) are the coordinated release. MSG-05 is now verified end-to-end on BOTH terminal paths (5ff574:done -> job.completed; 2ad8ba:error -> job.failed, both parent.verified=true). Local ~/dev/core main is 1 commit behind origin (missing 75ee080e / core#509). Is anything above an actual release blocker, or does the release proceed once core main is synced?

D7. The §7 PASS verdict itself. Given the orchestrators error rate today, is the PASS sound? Payloads claimed: A event_name=job.completed transition=done parent.verified=true; B inbox row messageKey=5ff574:done expectsReply=false; C message-get returns the forensic-v1 terminal snapshot; D sp result --json -> status=done turns=8 tool_calls=14 exit=agent_end. Is that sufficient to call VALIDATION checkbox 2 passed, or is something still unproven?

## SCOPE

Read-only investigation. Relevant material:
- Beads: xtrm-wiy5n.3 (notes contain the full corrected §7 transcript), xtrm-wiy5n.4 and its children .4, .5, .6, .13, .14, .15, .16
- specialists: src/pi/session.ts, src/specialist/supervisor.ts (emitParentNotification ~line 201), src/specialist/runtime-origin.ts, config/skills/using-specialists/
- core: ~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs
- bd memories: sp-run-is-foreground-long-running, dont-paste-unverified-commands-into-contracts, msg05-requires-terminal-job, wait-agent-premature-done

## NON_GOALS

- Do not modify any file, open any PR, or change any bead status.
- Do not dispatch other specialists.
- Do not run the release.
- Do not re-run the §7 demo. If you believe it must be re-run to settle D7, say so and specify exactly what to run; the operator decides.

## CONSTRAINTS

- `sp run` blocks and streams; if you dispatch anything at all you will hang. Do not.
- Verify any command against its `--help` before citing it. That failure is what caused this whole situation.
- Where evidence is insufficient for a verdict, return NEEDS-EVIDENCE and name the exact check. Do not guess.

## VALIDATION

[ ] All seven decisions carry a verdict and rationale
[ ] Every DISAGREE names a concrete alternative
[ ] Any NEEDS-EVIDENCE names the specific command or file that would settle it

## OUTPUT

A decision memo: D1..D7, each with VERDICT + rationale + action. Then a short list of anything the orchestrator still has wrong that was not in the docket.
notes:
D8 (added after dispatch — please include in the memo).

Both `xt pi --role ... --bead <id>` launches in this session printed:
    ⚠ bead assignee: runtime-origin unavailable for <bead-id>; session launch continues

That is the core-side feature from PR core#508 ("feat(cli): assign beaded sessions from runtime origin", bead xtrm-wiy5n.3.13), which ships in the coordinated release xtrm-wiy5n.4.6 (Core 0.11.3).

What makes it worth judging: the SPECIALISTS-side runtime-origin capture works perfectly from the same panes — job 5ff574 and 2ad8ba both recorded spawn_origin.runtime_origin with verified=true, capture_source=xtmux-context, correct tmux_session_id / tmux_pane_id / parent_session_id, and the direct run logged `component=runtime-origin event=capture outcome=ok verified=true duration_ms=212`. So the same host, same panes, same underlying data — specialists resolves it, cores xt CLI does not.

Questions: is core#508s bead-assignee path broken, or is "runtime-origin unavailable" an expected soft-degrade in this launch shape (e.g. it queries a source that is only populated later, or only for --role sessions started differently)? Does it block or reduce the value of releasing Core 0.11.3 (xtrm-wiy5n.4.6)? The orchestrator observed the warning twice, did not investigate, and has no opinion — treat this as genuinely open rather than as a claim to check.
close_reason: Advisor memo delivered, D1-D8. Verdicts: D1 NEEDS-EVIDENCE (reject flag flip, detach-ownership feasibility unproven, non-TTY warning rejected as too broad), D2 DISAGREE (4.13 raised P3->P2), D3 NEEDS-EVIDENCE -> since RESOLVED by test: Stop-hook form correct, not a 4.5 blocker, D4 AGREE (raised P2, found invalid --bead+--prompt example in monitoring.md:15), D5 AGREE (hygiene wording replaced), D6 DISAGREE (release gated by 4.1 smoke container, not just core sync), D7 AGREE (§7 PASS sound), D8 AGREE (core#508 race, filed as 4.18 P1 gating 4.6). Three orchestrator errors caught beyond the docket. All actions applied to the board.

title: Phase 1a — Enable pr-review-gate branch protection + live demo verification
description:
## PROBLEM
Split from xtrm-54zwl.1: after the workflow lands on main, the required-check
must be enabled manually and a live demo must confirm it blocks/unblocks
correctly. Neither step can happen pre-merge.

## SUCCESS
`pr-review-gate / gate` is required on main. One PR observed flipping red
when a bot review thread is unresolved and green when it's resolved.

## SCOPE
- Settings → Branches → main → Require status checks → add `pr-review-gate / gate`.
- Pick or spin an open PR; simulate a bot review comment (or wait for Codex);
  observe the check flip red; resolve the thread; observe green.
- Record PR link + timestamps in bead notes.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Check appears in required checks list (screenshot/URL in notes).
- [ ] Red-on-unresolved observed.
- [ ] Green-on-resolved observed.
notes:
## 2026-07-24 — actual completion story (much messier than planned)

Ended up needing 4 rounds of fixes before the workflow was actually usable:
1. Original file: unpinned github-script action → semgrep pre-push blocked; pinned to SHA
2. Job had no explicit name → check-run was called `gate`, not `pr-review-gate` → renamed via job-level `name:`
3. `pull_request_review_thread` trigger caused every workflow run to fail at startup with 0 jobs (actionlint confirmed: GitHub Actions doesn't accept this event despite the docs listing it) → removed
4. `(?i)codex|coderabbit|claude` regex used Perl-style inline flag which JS doesn't support → moved to RegExp constructor's `'i'` flag with defensive strip of any `(?i)` prefix
5. Added `workflow_dispatch` with a `pr:` input as the resolve-refresh path (Codex flagged this gap correctly — without `pull_request_review_thread`, resolving a thread emits no event; check stays failing until push/comment/manual dispatch)

Fix PRs merged: core#492, specialists#212, infra#248.

Branch protection state:
- xtrm-dev/core main: required checks = OSV scan, Semgrep scan, Gitleaks scan, pr-review-gate ✅
- xtrm-dev/specialists master: required checks = OSV scan, Semgrep scan, Gitleaks scan, pr-review-gate ✅
- mercuryintelligence/infra main: NOT PROTECTED (never was — operator decision needed on whether to enable from scratch)

Manual demo verification: implicitly done — Codex left real review threads on specialists#212 and infra#248, the gate blocked as expected, resolving the threads (via GraphQL) + rerun let them pass.
## 2026-07-24 — infra was using rulesets (newer API), not classic protection

My earlier "NOT PROTECTED" call on infra was wrong — I only queried the
classic /branches/{b}/protection endpoint, which 404s when protection is
via the newer rulesets API. Both infra and market-data (added below)
have an active "Protect master" ruleset that targets ~DEFAULT_BRANCH.
Neither had any required_status_checks configured; both do now.

## 2026-07-24 — added fourth mirror: mercuryintelligence/market-data#399
- Same workflow as the other three (post-fix version).
- Merged UNSTABLE (checks still pending, ruleset allows it since no required
  checks were configured yet). Would prefer to have waited for green but the
  workflow file is a pure YAML add and can't break existing CI. Noted for
  future rollouts: wait for CLEAN before merging in ruleset-protected repos
  that don't require checks yet.

## 2026-07-24 — final required-check state (all four repos)
- xtrm-dev/core:main (classic) → [OSV scan, Semgrep scan, Gitleaks scan, pr-review-gate]
- xtrm-dev/specialists:master (classic) → [OSV scan, Semgrep scan, Gitleaks scan, pr-review-gate]
- mercuryintelligence/infra:main (ruleset "Protect master") → [pr-review-gate]
- mercuryintelligence/market-data:master (ruleset "Protect master") → [pr-review-gate]

Infra + market-data intentionally have only pr-review-gate as required (their
other CI — gitleaks, semgrep, osv-scanner, otel-drift, etc — is present but
not required-to-merge by owner choice). If that should change, adding to the
same ruleset takes one API call each. Not doing it silently.
close_reason: All four repos have pr-review-gate as a required check (2× classic protection, 2× rulesets). Live demo confirmed via Codex leaving real blocking threads on specialists#212 and infra#248, gate blocking, thread resolve + rerun letting them merge.

title: Phase 1 — Land pr-review-gate workflow in xtrm-tools + enable branch protection
description:
## PROBLEM
The custom Codex-blocker gate lives in Archon and only fires when a merge
goes through `xtrm-merge-fifo`. `gh pr merge` bypasses it. This repo has no
required status check for LLM-bot review verdicts.

## SUCCESS
`.github/workflows/pr-review-gate.yml` is on main. Branch protection on main
requires the `pr-review-gate / gate` check. One live PR demonstrates
block-on-unresolved-thread and unblock-on-resolve.

## SCOPE
- Author `.github/workflows/pr-review-gate.yml` — single `actions/github-script`
  job, ~60 lines. Triggers: `pull_request` [opened, synchronize, reopened],
  `pull_request_review` [submitted, dismissed], `pull_request_review_thread`
  [resolved, unresolved], `issue_comment` [created, edited, deleted].
- Gate logic (both must pass):
  (a) Zero unresolved-and-not-outdated review threads whose first-comment
      author matches `PR_REVIEW_GATE_BOT_RE` (default `(?i)codex|coderabbit|claude`).
  (b) No allowlisted bot has latest review `state == CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
      For bots with `submittedAt: null` (Codex), skip (b) — (a) covers it.
- Land as its own PR.
- After merge: Settings → Branches → main → Require status checks → add
  `pr-review-gate / gate`. Manual step, record completion in bead notes.
- Verify by leaving a review comment as any LLM-shaped bot login on an open
  PR, observing the check flip red, resolving the thread, observing green.

## NON_GOALS
- No new required checks for gitleaks/osv/semgrep (already in place).
- No changes to Archon or any skill in this bead — pure CI insertion.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Use `github-script@v7`; no non-official actions.
- No external HTTP; permissions block: `pull-requests: read`.
- Must work for PRs from forks (read-only permissions).
- Fail closed if the GraphQL query errors.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Workflow file present and passes `actionlint` if installed locally.
- [ ] PR opened, `pr-review-gate / gate` appears in checks list.
- [ ] Simulated bot-authored unresolved thread → check red.
- [ ] Thread resolved → check re-runs green within one event.
- [ ] Branch protection UI shows the check as required.

## OUTPUT
- `.github/workflows/pr-review-gate.yml`
- Bead notes: PR link, branch-protection settings screenshot/URL, the demo
  PR used for verification.

title: pr-review-gate: canonical CI-enforced LLM-bot PR review gate
description:
## PROBLEM
Codex/LLM-bot PR review blocking is currently done client-side inside the
Archon `xtrm-merge-fifo` workflow (~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/codex_blocker_check.py).
That gate only fires when the operator drives the merge through Archon; a
plain `gh pr merge` bypasses it. It also re-computes the same signal in every
repo and duplicates the responsibility of a required CI check.

## SUCCESS
- A GitHub Actions workflow `pr-review-gate` becomes a required status check
  on `main`, blocking merges while any LLM-bot-authored review thread is
  unresolved OR any allowlisted bot has an active `CHANGES_REQUESTED`.
- The workflow ships as a template in `skills/security-pipeline/` and is
  installable in any xtrm-managed repo via the existing `security-bootstrap.sh`.
- Archon's `xtrm-merge-fifo` stops re-computing the signal and instead reads
  the CI check status.
- Docs in `judge-with-codex` / `pr-reviewer` / `xt-merge` reflect the split:
  merge blocking = CI; per-finding weighing = the skills.

## SCOPE
- Phase 1: author + land the workflow in xtrm-tools.
- Phase 2: canonicalize as a template in security-pipeline.
- Phase 3: simplify the Archon workflow to consume the CI check (after ≥1 week live).
- Phase 4: fix stale bot-login docs in review skills.
- Phase 5: propagate to other xtrm-managed repos.

## NON_GOALS
- No reusable GitHub Action / composite workflow — one 60-line YAML per repo.
- Do not promote Socket Security to a required check (false-positive rate).
- Do not automate branch protection setup — manual toggle per repo.
- Do not build a PreToolUse hook to guard `gh pr merge` — that would be a
  separate epic if we ever want it.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Codex bot login on this repo is `chatgpt-codex-connector[bot]`. Regex
  `(?i)codex|coderabbit|claude` (default), overridable via repo variable
  `PR_REVIEW_GATE_BOT_RE`. Do NOT hardcode a single login.
- Codex reviews are always `state: COMMENTED, submittedAt: null` — the
  unresolved-threads path is the primary gate; the CHANGES_REQUESTED branch
  is kept for CodeRabbit-style bots.

## VALIDATION
- All five phase beads closed with their own VALIDATION checkboxes green.
- One live PR in xtrm-tools with the gate blocking + a bot review thread
  demonstrated as the block source, then a resolve-thread → unblock cycle.

## OUTPUT
- `.github/workflows/pr-review-gate.yml` in every xtrm-managed repo.
- `skills/security-pipeline/templates/.github/workflows/pr-review-gate.yml`.
- Updated `security-bootstrap.sh`, `security-pipeline/SKILL.md`.
- Simplified `~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-merge-fifo.yaml`.
- Corrected review-skill docs.
notes:
## 2026-07-24 — epic conclusion

All five phases closed. Total 8 PRs across 4 repos:

Original mirrors (Phase 1 → Phase 5 first wave):
- xtrm-dev/core#491 (initial workflow, 2026-07-24 12:12 UTC)
- xtrm-dev/specialists#210 (mirror)
- mercuryintelligence/infra#244 (mirror)

In-flight fixes (Phase 1 hardening):
- xtrm-dev/core#492 — job-level name + regex (?i) → 'i' flag + workflow_dispatch
- xtrm-dev/specialists#212 — trigger + regex + dispatch
- mercuryintelligence/infra#248 — trigger + regex + dispatch
- mercuryintelligence/market-data#399 (fourth repo mirrored ad-hoc)

Canonicalization (Phase 2 + Phase 4):
- xtrm-dev/core#495 — template + bootstrap patch + SKILL.md + review-skill doc refresh

Adversarial-review fixes (Codex P2s on #495 → mirrored across all 4):
- xtrm-dev/core#495 (rolled into same PR before merge)
- xtrm-dev/specialists#214
- mercuryintelligence/infra#249
- mercuryintelligence/market-data#400

Archon-side (Phase 3):
- ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/pr_review_gate_check.py (new, replaces codex_blocker_check.py inside merge-fifo)
- xtrm-merge-fifo.yaml + xtrm-merge-fifo-dry-run.yaml simplified

Final gate state (all 4 required-status-check contexts named 'pr-review-gate'):
- xtrm-dev/core:main (classic) → required
- xtrm-dev/specialists:master (classic) → required
- mercuryintelligence/infra:main (ruleset "Protect master") → required
- mercuryintelligence/market-data:master (ruleset "Protect master") → required

Template in security-pipeline is now the source of truth for future adopters.

Meta observations worth preserving:
- Codex genuinely caught real defects on this epic that I missed: resolve-refresh gap (led to workflow_dispatch), Bot-typename restriction (prevents human false-positives), pagination (prevents silent >100-thread miss). The gate blocked its own author's PRs and made them better.
- GitHub Actions rejects `pull_request_review_thread` despite the docs listing it — actionlint agrees. Workaround: workflow_dispatch + "re-request check-suite" button + push-empty-commit are the three refresh paths.
- Never trust a Perl-style regex flag prefix in JavaScript (`(?i)` throws).
- `.claude/settings.json` hard-referencing scripts under `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/**` breaks every tool call if those scripts get removed. That class of drift was independently filed as P0 xtrm-igx6a. Session-local workaround: symlink from ~/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/.

title: PR0: lift-and-shift service-skills → ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge (invert vendor pipeline)
description:
## PROBLEM

Machinery today at ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/service-skills/ is vendored INTO consumer repos as .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/, driven by `xt update --apply`. Given the reframe scale (verifier + FTS5 index + MCP tools + activator + eval + telemetry — spec ~/dev/xtrm/docs/research/kb-knowledge-base-svc.md), this must elevate to a first-class xtrm package with **independent lifecycle**: own CLI, own versioning, own release, own CHANGELOG. Not routed through `xt update --apply`. Rename service-skills → service-knowledge to reflect the reframe target (knowledge, not just skills) with room for docs/playbooks/runbooks later.

Two more corrections vs the pre-review plan:
1. **~/dev/core and ~/dev/specialists are NOT consumers**. They are xtrm tooling repos, not service hosts. Installing service-knowledge there is pointless — nothing to index. Consumer set is service-hosting mercury repos only.
2. **No forced-wave migration**. Wave-1 = mercury-infra only (PoC). 6 other mercury service-host repos adopt when operator triggers each install. Backward-compat window keeps old service-skills paths recognized for one release cycle.

This PR is lift-and-shift + rename + CLI scaffolding. No behavior changes, no reframe machinery — that lands in PR1-5.

## SUCCESS

- Package at ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/ with independent CLI (`service-knowledge install|update|status|migrate|remove`).
- pyproject.toml declares `[project.scripts] service-knowledge = "service_knowledge.cli:main"` — installable via pip, runnable standalone.
- vaultctl added as declared package dependency (PR3 uses it; declared here so the package boundary is right from v0.1.0).
- All 11 Python machinery scripts moved from ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/ → ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/scripts/ via git mv (history preserved).
- service_skill_contract.json v1.0.0 → contracts/.
- Reference SKILLs (creating, using, updating, routing, system-guide, script_quality_standards) → skills/.
- Package released as v0.1.0. Byte-equivalent machinery behavior vs current ~/dev/core state (regression: pre/post diff on cataloger/drift_detector/activator/umbrella_generator outputs against mercury-infra).
- mercury-infra runs `service-knowledge install`; picks up v0.1.0; SessionStart catalog + PostToolUse drift + PreToolUse activator all fire cleanly with the renamed paths.
- 6 other mercury service-host repos NOT touched in this PR — each installs on operator trigger post-PR0-merge.
- ~/dev/core stops vendoring service-skills; layout_migrator entry added so any operator running `xt migrate` picks up the retirement.
- ~/dev/specialists stops vendoring service-skills. Only the service-skills-sync specialist definition stays (relocates to reference the new package path in PR2).
- ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json created (user-scoped, schema locked); empty by default. Future federated-query populates it.
- Stub ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md points at package + research doc + install command.

## SCOPE

**NEW package**: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/
- package.json OR pyproject.toml (Python package; entry point exposes the CLI)
- src/service_knowledge/cli/  (install, update, status, migrate, remove commands)
- src/service_knowledge/scripts/  (all 11 .py files moved via git mv)

- src/service_knowledge/mcp/  (empty scaffold; PR3 lands 3 knowledge_* tools here)
- tests/  (fixture shells; real fixtures land in PR1)
- README.md, CHANGELOG.md
- pyproject.toml declares dep: vaultctl (constraint pinned per vaultctl current release)

**RETIREMENT**: ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/service-skills/ deleted. Any references in ~/dev/core to the old path replaced with either (a) removal (if core doesn't need it) or (b) a deprecation-only shim pointing at 'install service-knowledge via its own CLI'.

**RETIREMENT**: ~/dev/specialists/config/skills/service-skills-*/ deleted (if any). The service-skills-sync specialist definition stays in specialists but its task_template updates to reference the new package.

**MODIFY**: mercury-infra only in this PR:
- `service-knowledge install` from mercury-infra root
- Creates .xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/ (vendored subset the consumer needs)
- Creates .xtrm/cache/service-knowledge.sqlite (empty; PR3 populates schema)
- Migration commit: renames the old service-skills umbrella to service-knowledge; updates registry filename references if any

**NEW**: ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json — user-scoped, empty, schema locked ({schema_version: 1, sibling_stacks: []})

**NEW**: ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md — stub with install/update/status one-liners + research-doc link + package version pointer

## NON_GOALS

- Not routed through `xt update --apply`. Full stop. Own CLI, own lifecycle.
- ~/dev/core is NOT a consumer of service-knowledge. Deleted, not shimmed.
- ~/dev/specialists is NOT a consumer. Only the service-skills-sync specialist definition stays there (it's tooling, not a service).
- ~/dev/xtrm, ~/dev/xtmux, ~/dev/vaultctl are NOT consumers.
- No behavior changes, no verifier, no FTS5 index, no MCP tools, no activator upgrade — PR1-5.
- No docs/ inside the package — deferred.
- 6 other mercury service-host repos NOT migrated in this PR. Each on operator trigger post-merge.
- No new dep besides vaultctl.

## CONSTRAINTS

- git mv used for every moved file (history follows).
- Package must be byte-equivalent in machinery behavior vs current ~/dev/core state (regression fixture: cataloger + drift + activator + umbrella outputs pre/post).
- `service-knowledge install` idempotent on mercury-infra: running twice produces no diff.
- `service-knowledge update` idempotent: pulls latest, no diff if already at latest.
- Backward-compat: for one release cycle, activator + drift_detector recognize BOTH .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/ AND .xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/. Next cycle drops old name.

- Package CLI must NOT depend on xtrm/bd/sp/xt/xtmux being installed. Standalone Python package with vaultctl as its only cross-package dep.
- Logging/telemetry: install/update/migrate emit per-invocation {timestamp, component=sk-cli, event, consumer_path, from_version, to_version, files_touched, duration_ms} to .xtrm/state/service-knowledge/install.jsonl. Grep by component. No secrets.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] git log --follow works on every moved script (history preserved)
- [ ] Regression: cataloger/drift/activator/umbrella outputs against mercury-infra pre-move == post-move (byte-identical modulo install-path strings)
- [ ] `service-knowledge install` in mercury-infra succeeds; running twice = no diff
- [ ] mercury-infra CI green post-install (all existing service-skills hooks still fire; cataloger emits the catalog; drift detector runs)

notes:
POST-RELEASE GATE — the exact commands, so the last step is turnkey.

The README states the contract: run it twice around a coordinated release, once before publishing
against the current latest, and once after, still latest but now the new versions. BOTH must PASS.

Read the sequencing note earlier on this bead first: the PRE-release run against @latest FAILS on
the --new-instance assertion by design, because published xtmux@0.2.2 carries the bead
xtrm-wiy5n.4.25 regression. That is the gate reporting the very thing this release fixes.

  # build once
  docker build -t xtrm-smoke scripts/smoke-container/

  # PRE-release, expected to FAIL on --new-instance only. Read it, do not fix it.
  docker run --rm xtrm-smoke ./verify.sh --skip-live

  # POST-release, after all three packages reach latest. THIS ONE MUST PASS.
  docker run --rm xtrm-smoke ./verify.sh --skip-live

  # optional, exercises the live tmux + sp scenario as well
  docker run --rm -e ANTHROPIC_API_KEY=... xtrm-smoke ./verify.sh

  # to test an unreleased branch in every stage rather than the published tag
  docker run --rm xtrm-smoke ./verify.sh --branch core=<ref> --branch xtmux=<ref>

--branch <repo>=<ref> packs and installs that repo's branch globally, so the run tests the
branch's CODE, not only its files. A repo without the ref is reported SKIP. As of PR core#522 the
drift-repair stage no longer overwrites a --branch build with the published tag, so a --branch run
is now trustworthy through stage 5.

exit 0 is PASS. Nonzero is FAIL with the failing stage named in the summary.

title: xtmux P1 lane: test-session-events cursor fix + xtmux-events filter widening
description:
## PROBLEM
`scripts/test-session-events.sh` has two P1 bugs and a broad rendering gap surfaced by the user's extra ask.

**Beads cursor bug**: text comparison `WHERE created_at > '<cursor>'` where startup cursor is `date '+%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S'` (space) and stored rows are `2026-07-24T12:34:56Z` (T). Because ASCII `T`(0x54) > space(0x20), every polled row appears greater than cursor and re-emits every 2s. Also missing TZ conversion loses events for operators east of UTC until wall-clock catches up.

**Startup cursor timing**: cursor captured at line 316–319, after dashboard/follower setup work — leaves an event-loss window.

**`xtmux-events` rendering gaps**: jq filter drops `agents.turn.done`, `agent.ready` (singular vs plural regex), `messages.cancelled`/`reply.linked`/`reply.rejected`/`send.rejected`, `monitor.started`/`state`, `wait.wake.orphan`, `audit.*`, `bd.commented`, and — crucially — every `sp job.*` lifecycle event except `job.started`. So you never see a job finish.

## SUCCESS
Cursor comparison normalized. Startup cursor captured before setup. jq filter widened to cover all named event kinds with detail-branch coverage.

## SCOPE
- `scripts/test-session-events.sh:148` (SQL predicate)
- `scripts/test-session-events.sh:157` (advance-cursor jq)
- `scripts/test-session-events.sh:238-239,316-319` (startup cursor capture)
- `scripts/test-session-events.sh:260` (xtmux event regex)
- `scripts/test-session-events.sh:270` (dashboard snapshot select — comment stays)
- `scripts/test-session-events.sh:293` (sp event filter)
- `scripts/test-session-events.sh:111-120` (detail_obj branches — extend for reply/rejection variants)

## NON_GOALS
- Rewriting the script into a compiled CLI (bash+jq is fine per ponytail)
- Fixing the "dashboard never refreshes" limitation (ok per operator restart comment)

## CONSTRAINTS
- One PR
- Preserve existing 2s poll cadence
- Normalize cursor: either advance-cursor writes the raw DB format, or the SQL side converts — pick one and be consistent
- Widen filter conservatively — only render event kinds that emit stable detail; add empty detail_obj branch for cancelled/reply variants

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Reproduction: emit any bd row, verify it renders once and does NOT re-emit every 2s
- [ ] Startup: create bd event just after script starts but before dashboard setup completes — event surfaces
- [ ] Live: `sp run any-agent` → `xtmux-events` shows `job.started` AND terminal (`job.completed`/`job.failed`/`job.cancelled`)

- [ ] Live: `agent.ready` (singular) appears
- [ ] Live: `bd close` → `bd closed` row rendered

## OUTPUT

A. sp job.completed event

title: PR4: dispatch integration + PreToolUse activator upgrade (retrieval + narrow blocking)
description:
## PROBLEM

The retrieval surface (PR3) exists but nothing DEMANDS it. Beads still ship without evidence bundles; specialist dispatch still hands prompts without service context; skill_activator.py still injects reminders after the tool call. Result: the FTS5 index is a passive library, not the operational gate the reframe requires. Research §3.7 firing-points table: dispatch is the most important gate — a bead touching api-gateway/** must contain or reference the api-gateway evidence bundle, regardless of whether the model 'remembers' to read the SKILL.

Blocking must be narrow (§3.7): Read/Glob/Grep never block; Write/Edit in registered territory blocks only when retrieval CAN'T build a bundle; high-risk mutating Bash blocks with conflict-check; everything else advisory. Overblocking pushes agents around the system.

## SUCCESS

- Bead contract validator (using-specialists rule #15 promotion gate, or wherever the equivalent lives in ~/dev/core) attaches on promotion: matched_services, evidence_bundle_id, evidence_hash, unresolved_conflicts. A bead touching a registered territory without a bundle CANNOT be promoted from contract:draft.
- Specialist dispatch pipeline attaches the evidence bundle to the specialist's prompt at job start — via bead body (specialist reads via bd show) rather than injected env, so the specialist sees it in the same surface as the rest of the contract.
- skill_activator.py upgraded: matcher unchanged (already correctly uses registry + territory); behavior replaced. Instead of injecting 'please read SKILL.md', it invokes knowledge_evidence_for_files with the file path being touched, receives an evidence bundle, and injects the bundle into the PreToolUse context. Session cache keyed by (service, source_ref) avoids re-fetch within the same session.
- PreToolUse block matrix per §3.7:
  - Read/Glob/Grep: evidence-inject, never block
  - Write/Edit on registered territory: block only if retrieval fails (index broken, no bundle constructible)
  - Bash read-only: evidence-inject, don't block
  - Bash mutating (rm/mv/docker rm/systemctl/kubectl apply/gh pr merge etc.): bundle + conflict-check; block on conflicted-high-risk claim marked as prerequisite
- PostToolUse: telemetry only (consumption, drift, reindex queue). No blocking.
- Session-cache lifecycle: cache invalidates on git HEAD change; bounded ≤ 20 bundles per session.

## SCOPE

- ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/skill_activator.py — upgrade behavior (matcher stays, output replaced)
- ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/using-specialists/ — extend bead promotion check for evidence_bundle_id + evidence_hash + matched_services
- ~/dev/core/mcp-tools/knowledge/ — extend query.py to accept session-cache-key + return cache metadata (no new tool, but the surface must support caching)
- ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/dispatch/  (NEW small module) — evidence-bundle-to-bead-body renderer
- ~/dev/specialists/config/specialists/*.specialist.json — orchestrator/coordinator specialists get updated task_template referencing the evidence_bundle_id field
- ~/.xtrm/hooks/ — if session-cache lives here or in a companion .mjs, update; else keep everything Python-side
- Post-merge hook: wire index rebuild (if PR3 didn't already)
- Bead validator: possibly a bd hook or a separate script invoked from bd create / bd set-state contract=ready — pick the smallest surface

## NON_GOALS

- No auto-remediation, no auto-merge behavior change (PR5)
- No new MCP tools (PR3 already shipped them; this PR only calls them)
- No embedding integration
- No cross-repo query
- No override-per-agent ACL (deferred; today all specialists get all bundles from their bead)
- No 'read SKILL.md' fallback for backward-compat — the reminder is deleted in favor of real evidence injection
- No blocking on Read/Glob/Grep — ever
- No blocking on Bash read-only — ever

## CONSTRAINTS

- Blocking must fail LOUDLY with a specific message: which service, which territory, which bundle expected, why retrieval failed. Silent blocks train agents to ignore hooks.
- Every block has an operator override path: OVERRIDE_KNOWLEDGE_BUNDLE=1 env, recorded in telemetry as an override event with reason (matches --allow-unready pattern in using-specialists rule #15).
- Session cache: memory-only, per-Claude-Code session; do NOT persist to disk. Cache miss = fresh knowledge_evidence_for_files call.
- Bundle attachment to bead body: use a well-defined marker block (e.g. <!-- knowledge:evidence:BUNDLE_ID -->…<!-- /knowledge:evidence -->) so downstream tooling can find, replace, or strip it.
- Cache invalidation: on git HEAD change (post-commit / post-merge) OR on manual 'python3 -m index rebuild' — both signal knowledge_evidence_for_files to bypass cache next call.
- Bead validator refuses promotion when: bead SCOPE references a registered territory AND no matched_services attached. Advisory warning when: matched_services attached but no evidence_bundle_id (index not yet built for this service).
- Backward compat: existing beads (currently open) are NOT retroactively refused — the promotion gate applies to draft → ready transitions from the moment this PR merges. In-flight beads carry over.
- Logging/telemetry: {timestamp, component=activator|dispatch|bead-validator, event, tool_name, service_ids, bundle_id, decision=inject|block|allow|override, override_reason?, duration_ms}. Grep by component. Override events extra-labeled for review.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests for the block matrix: every (tool, territory-match, index-state) combination has an expected decision, tested
- [ ] Activator integration test: PreToolUse on Write in api-gateway/** → bundle injected, no block, cache populated
- [ ] Activator integration test: PreToolUse on Write in api-gateway/** with broken index → block with clear message
- [ ] Bead promotion test: bd create with SCOPE touching a registered territory but no matched_services → bd set-state contract=ready refused with reason
- [ ] Specialist dispatch smoke: create a bead with SCOPE api-gateway/**, promote (with matched_services attached), dispatch service-skills-sync → specialist sees the evidence bundle marker in bd show
- [ ] Override path: OVERRIDE_KNOWLEDGE_BUNDLE=1 + Write → warns but proceeds; override event in telemetry
- [ ] Session cache: 2× knowledge_evidence_for_files on same (service, source_ref) → second call hits cache, telemetry shows cache_hit=true
- [ ] Cache invalidation: after git commit that touches the territory → next call bypasses cache
- [ ] Regression: Read/Glob/Grep never block, even on broken index (only advisory)
- [ ] Regression: existing in-flight beads (created before this PR) are not refused on promotion (backward compat)
- [ ] Structured telemetry: grep 'decision=block' finds only Write/Edit/mutating-Bash; never finds Read/Glob/Grep

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: skill_activator.py (matcher stays), scripts/index/query.py (from PR3), using-specialists SKILL.md contract-promotion machinery
- Installed deps: none new
- Stdlib: os (env override), time (session TTL), functools.lru_cache-style bounded cache — actually use a plain dict + FIFO cap since lru_cache doesn't play well with per-session lifecycle
- New dep candidate: none
- Roll it: cache implementation is 20 LOC — roll it

## OUTPUT

- Diff on skill_activator.py (behavior replaced)
- Diff on using-specialists promotion gate
- New scripts/dispatch/ module for evidence-bundle-to-bead-body rendering
- Diff on specialist task_templates
- pytest output
- Integration transcript: create → promote → dispatch → specialist reads bundle from bd show
- Sample block message (proves it's actionable, not silent)
- Sample override telemetry line

## APPROACH NOTES

- Session cache lifecycle: Claude Code hooks fire in short-lived Python processes, so the cache must span the process lifetime OR persist per-session-id. Simplest: per-invocation cache (no persistence) + rely on PR3's index being fast enough that a repeat call within seconds is cheap. Only build real persistence if measured latency demands.
- Bead validator hook: check whether bd create / bd set-state fire pre-write hooks in this repo. If not, extend the validator invoked from bd promote (or add a wrapper). Do NOT retrofit every bd invocation.
- The 'evidence bundle marker in bd body' pattern is analogous to how PR templates already work in this repo — reuse the marker pattern from CHANGELOG or PR body handling if one exists.
- Specialist task_template updates should be minimal — just a line that says 'if the bead body contains an evidence bundle marker, treat it as authoritative context; do not re-fetch'.
- Blocking must never fire on the bead-validator itself accidentally. Bead validator changes trigger a PreToolUse Write on bd-tracking files (.beads/*) — those must be exempt or the validator locks itself out.
notes: CORRECTION to prior review note: missing command literals are (1) sp run or specialists run with --bead must attach the marker before job start, and (2) bd set-state BEAD contract=ready must be refused by a real installed/PreToolUse gate. Required tests must exercise those actual Bash command paths, not only the manual dispatch CLI.

title: PR3: per-repo FTS5 evidence index + 5 read-only MCP tools + cataloger reframe
description:
## PROBLEM

Retrieval today = 'read the whole SKILL if you happen to notice the catalog'. Activator fires a reminder AFTER the tool call. Nothing at bead-validation, dispatch, incident routing, or PreToolUse actually surfaces service knowledge. SKILLs are barely used, wrong SKILLs slip through, agents rediscover the same context every session.

Research §3 recommends a per-repo SQLite FTS5 index + 5 narrow read-only MCP tools + interpretable ranking. But — **vaultctl already ships the SQLite/FTS5/BM25 substrate** (~/dev/vaultctl, 897 LOC in store/, proven, in production for the Obsidian vault). Rebuilding it from scratch is 90% of PR3's proposed scope AND already exists as a working library. Depend on it, don't rewrite it.

**Ponytail cuts vs original PR3**:
- Vaultctl provides: schema DDL scaffolding, FTS5 tokenization (unicode61), BM25 ranking, indexer, search, link-resolution graph, in-degree stats, CLI-JSON scaffolding — reuse via package dep, do not reimplement
- Ship 3 MCP tools not 5: knowledge_search, knowledge_get, knowledge_evidence_for_files. Defer knowledge_probes + knowledge_conflicts as follow-ups (advisory extras, low value at MVP)

## SUCCESS

- vaultctl is a package dep of service-knowledge (declared in PR0).
- service-knowledge extends vaultctl's schema with 5 domain tables: items(kind=service|section|claim|probe|conflict), citations, conflicts, retrieval_events, index_state. Attached via SQLite ATTACH DATABASE OR vaultctl migration extension (whichever vaultctl already supports — inspect first, else ATTACH).
- Index builder ingests: registry entries → items rows; SKILL sections (parsed via Markdown AST) → items rows; claim manifests from PR1 (when present) → claims rows; extracted citations → citations rows; probe metadata from Cross-Service Health Check sections → items rows with kind=probe.
- 3 read-only MCP tools registered: knowledge_search, knowledge_get, knowledge_evidence_for_files. Each returns evidence bundles per §3.2 (routing header + 3-7 top items + citations + verification/freshness + link to full skill). No answer() endpoint.
- Ranking implemented per §3.5 as a Python wrapper over vaultctl.store.search: score = 0.40 T + 0.30 L + 0.15 I + 0.10 A + 0.05 F. L pulls BM25 rank from vaultctl. T/I/A/F computed on top. Post-rank penalties (conflicted-high-risk excluded, invalidated excluded, stale-high-risk −0.25, insufficient-evidence-high-risk −0.15, unverified −0.10).
- Freshness F = exp(−ln(2) × changed_commits_since_ref / 20). Commits computed via drift_detector helpers.
- Provenance: current_view mutable via status field on items rows; append-only history via retrieval_events. Claims flip to superseded/invalidated on source change; default retrieval excludes.
- Cataloger reframed: 'Available operational knowledge sources' with per-service last_sync_ref + index_health + item count + verification coverage. Replaces 'Available expert personas'.
- umbrella_generator emits index_state hash + generator_version + OKF-compatible per-item descriptions.
- Index rebuild ≤ 60s on mercury-infra (17 services).

## SCOPE

- src/service_knowledge/index/  (NEW module)
  - schema.py — 5-table domain extension (items/citations/conflicts/retrieval_events/index_state); ATTACH-based or migration-based
  - builder.py — ingest registry + SKILL sections + claim manifests + citations + probes into vaultctl DB
  - query.py — ranking wrapper over vaultctl.store.search: applies T/I/A/F/penalties on top of vaultctl's BM25 (L)
  - bundle.py — evidence-bundle assembly per §3.2 (routing header + top items + freshness + citations + full-skill link)
  - freshness.py — commit-based F signal via drift_detector helpers

title: PR2: deterministic gate in reconcile.py + specialist parity
description:
## PROBLEM

Even with a working claim verifier (PR1), the auto-reconcile pipeline still ships whatever LLM output arrives — the verifier is advisory-only. The blast-radius fix requires the gate: reconcile.py must write to a candidate path FIRST, invoke the verifier, then act on the verdict. Only PASS and PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES may reach the canonical atomic_write. Same rule applies to the service-skills-sync specialist so local runs cannot bypass what CI enforces.

Research §2.7 rejects a naive 3-tier lattice (CONFLICT/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE/PASS→auto-merge) as too aggressive for the first rollout. The recommended 6-tier lattice (INVALID/CONFLICT/EVIDENCE_RACE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK/PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES/PASS) treats PASS as 'open PR, no auto-merge' by default; auto-merge is a separate later decision (PR5).

Research §2.8 rejects LLM-panel majority as a gate arbiter and recommends deterministic-first + LLM critic ONLY on residuals the deterministic verifier returned UNKNOWN on. The critic sees only the residual claim + type + relevant diff + small evidence bundle + reason UNKNOWN was returned; its verdict is advisory.

## SUCCESS

- reconcile.py generates candidate to a temp path (worktree or /tmp), invokes the PR1 verifier CLI, receives the manifest, computes gate per §2.7 lattice, and ONLY on PASS/PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES calls atomic_write.
- Same entry point invoked from service-skills-sync specialist — no bypass path.
- INVALID / CONFLICT: no write, no PR; report emitted.
- EVIDENCE_RACE (source SHA changed mid-run): invalidate + retry the whole run.
- INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK: produce a draft PR clearly not-mergeable, or (local flow) refuse the write with an explicit override flag.
- PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES: normal PR, no auto-merge, advisories rendered in the PR description.
- PASS: normal PR, no auto-merge.
- Residual critic pass: for claims the deterministic verifier returned UNKNOWN on and where risk >= medium, an LLM critic call runs with a bounded evidence bundle; its verdict is stored as advisory in the manifest and rendered in the PR description. Never used as a gate arbiter.
- Verification report published as GHA artifact and check on every auto-reconcile PR; visible to human reviewers alongside the diff.

## SCOPE

- ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py
  - New helper: run_verifier(candidate_path, current_path, territory, refs) → manifest
  - New helper: compute_gate(manifest) → GateVerdict enum
  - New helper: run_residual_critic(unknown_claims, evidence_bundles, provider_client) → advisory annotations
  - atomic_write is only called from the PASS/PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES branch
- ~/dev/specialists/config/specialists/service-skills-sync.specialist.json
  - task_template mandates invoking the same verifier entry point before any write
  - specialist may not use --allow-unverified without an operator-recorded override reason (matches using-specialists rule #15 style)
- ~/dev/core/.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/verifier/__main__.py
  - Add --gate-mode flag that returns the gate verdict + non-zero exit code on INVALID/CONFLICT (so CI can gate cleanly)
- ~/dev/core/.github/workflows/service-skills-drift-sweep.yml
  - Run verifier BEFORE peter-evans/create-pull-request; publish manifest.json as artifact; add a status check ('service-skills-verify')
  - On INVALID/CONFLICT: fail the job (sticky comment only, no PR)
  - On INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK: open draft PR with 'do-not-merge' label
- New: docs/service-skills-verifier-gate.md documenting the lattice + operator override path

## NON_GOALS

- No changes to the PR1 verifier module itself (extend via flags, not schema changes)
- No FTS5 index integration (PR3)
- No auto-merge enable — even PASS opens a normal PR
- No changes to bead validator (PR4)
- No new hook wiring
- No security-auditor integration
- No panel/multi-LLM vote

## CONSTRAINTS

- Verifier gate must run BEFORE atomic_write in every code path (auto-reconcile + specialist + manual CLI)
- Residual critic call is bounded: max evidence bundle ≤ 4000 tokens per claim, max claims per run ≤ 12, hard cap 8000 tokens total per run (research §2.9)
- Critic timeout: 60s per claim, 300s per run; on timeout the residual stays UNKNOWN and is rendered as caveat, not blocker
- EVIDENCE_RACE detection: recompute source SHAs at start + end of verifier run; if changed → invalidate + retry once, then fail
- Draft-PR path for INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK: use 'draft: true' + 'do-not-merge' label; PR body prominently lists unverifiable claims
- The specialist path may not fall back to writing without the verifier — no override flag exists in this PR; operator override is a follow-up bead if needed
- Logging/telemetry: every gate decision emits one structured line: {timestamp, component=reconcile-gate, event=gate_decision, verdict, service_id, invalid_count, conflict_count, unknown_count, critic_calls, critic_tokens, duration_ms}. Grep 'component=reconcile-gate' finds all decisions in the audit trail.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests for compute_gate() covering every lattice cell (INVALID/CONFLICT/EVIDENCE_RACE/INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK/PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES/PASS)
- [ ] Integration test: reconcile.py invoked on api-gateway regression fixture → gate=CONFLICT → no atomic_write called (mock filesystem or tmp dir)
- [ ] Integration test: reconcile.py on a clean fixture → gate=PASS → atomic_write called exactly once with the candidate content
- [ ] EVIDENCE_RACE test: simulate source SHA change mid-run → gate returns EVIDENCE_RACE → run retries → second run completes cleanly
- [ ] service-skills-sync specialist smoke: dispatch against a synthetic bead + fixture, observe verifier invocation in the specialist log, verify no write on CONFLICT
- [ ] GHA workflow smoke via workflow_dispatch: manifest.json published as artifact, 'service-skills-verify' check appears on the PR
- [ ] Residual critic test: force UNKNOWN on one claim, mock the provider, verify the critic call is bounded (evidence tokens < 4000) and advisory-only (does not change verdict)
- [ ] Reviewer sees on the PR: candidate diff, per-claim verdict, evidence path + line range, complete-set comparison for set_claims, residuals + critic advisory
- [ ] Structured telemetry: grep 'component=reconcile-gate' in the artifact log returns one line per gate decision with correct fields

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: reconcile.py itself (extend, don't rewrite), verifier module from PR1, drift_detector.py refs helper
- Installed deps: httpx (already in reconcile.py for the LLM provider call), tenacity if retry policy is needed (verify presence before adding)
- Stdlib: hashlib for SHA re-check, tempfile for candidate path, subprocess if invoking verifier via CLI (prefer in-process import if module structure allows)
- New dep candidate: none — critic uses the same provider client reconcile.py already has
- Roll it: reuse existing tenacity if present, else stdlib retry loop with capped attempts

## OUTPUT

- Diff on reconcile.py (helper functions + gate branch)
- Diff on service-skills-sync specialist definition
- Diff on service-skills-drift-sweep.yml
- New docs/service-skills-verifier-gate.md
- pytest output (all green)
- workflow_dispatch smoke transcript (or link to a test-branch run) showing manifest.json artifact + check
- Sample PR description on a CONFLICT fixture (proves reviewer sees the residuals)
- Sample telemetry lines from a passing + failing run

## APPROACH NOTES

- Prefer in-process import of the verifier module over subprocess where possible (avoids IPC + JSON round-trip); fall back to CLI only when the CI/hook context can't import the module.
- The critic call MUST come from the same provider adapter reconcile.py already uses (nano-gpt / openrouter / etc.) — do not hard-code Anthropic or OpenAI.
- The 'don't self-merge, keep bead open, escalate to operator' pattern from the successful infra-wtd1 dispatch applies here. Both PRs (core + specialists) open, linked to xtrm-56flm.2, wait for operator merge.
- Cross-repo: specialist edit lives in ~/dev/specialists; open two PRs, link them in bead notes, ship the core PR first (verifier lives there).

title: PR1: claim verifier foundations (advisory only, no behavior change)
description:
## PROBLEM

The current auto-reconcile + service-skills-sync pipelines have no way to distinguish 'the LLM wrote something plausible' from 'the LLM wrote something true'. A recent specialist run shipped 3 factual errors in one SKILL section (invented redaction-key set, wrong redaction literal, mis-labeled metric-label set) — the only reason they were caught was manual operator review. Every future SKILL rewrite carries the same blast radius until a deterministic verifier exists.
