title: Epic: service-skills reframe — deterministic verifier + evidence-first retrieval
description:
## PROBLEM

Two failure modes prove the current service-skills machinery ships operational-knowledge risk unchecked:

1. **Blast radius on rewrite**: reconcile.py + service-skills-sync specialist generate rewritten SKILL.md and write immediately — no fact-check, no citation extraction, no completeness verification. A single specialist run recently shipped a SKILL section with invented redaction-key set, wrong redaction literal, mis-labeled metric-label set. Wrong SKILL becomes ground truth for every future session.

2. **Consumption gap**: SKILLs are barely used. skill_activator.py fires a 'please read this' reminder AFTER the tool call the agent already committed to. Nothing in bead contracts, specialist prompts, or issue dispatch demands service context.

Research (~/dev/xtrm/docs/research/kb-knowledge-base-svc.md, 975 lines, cited SOTA + shipping systems) recommends two derived layers on top of existing SKILL.md/registry/machinery:
- **Claim verifier**: deterministic Python between LLM output and any write/commit/PR; explicit gate lattice (INVALID / CONFLICT / EVIDENCE_RACE / INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK / PASS_WITH_ADVISORIES / PASS); PASS != auto-merge on day one.
- **Evidence-first retrieval**: per-repo SQLite FTS5 index + narrow read-only MCP tools; no answer() endpoint.

Given the scale + coherence of the reframe, machinery elevates to a first-class xtrm package: **service-knowledge**, home ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/. **Independent lifecycle**: its own CLI (`service-knowledge install|update|status|migrate|remove`) — NOT routed through `xt update --apply`. Rename from 'service-skills' → 'service-knowledge' reflects the reframe target.

## SUCCESS

At epic close:
- Auto-reconcile + specialist runs cannot ship SKILL with invented literals, wrong metric-label sets, invented env vars, or falsely-complete lists — verifier blocks BEFORE atomic_write.
- Every bead touching a registered territory receives an evidence bundle at dispatch; Write/Edit in registered territory blocks when bundle can't be built.
- SKILL.md remains authoring surface; registry stays source of truth.
- Machinery ships as first-class xtrm package (service-knowledge v0.6.0) with own CLI, own release cadence, own CHANGELOG.
- **vaultctl is a package dependency** (~/dev/vaultctl provides SQLite/FTS5/BM25 substrate — 897 LOC of proven store layer we don't rewrite). service-knowledge adds only the domain-specific extensions (items with kind=service|section|claim|probe|conflict, citations, retrieval_events, index_state).
- **mercury-infra is the PoC consumer** (17 services, richest fixture set). 6 other service-hosting mercury repos adopt when operator triggers each — no forced-wave.
- **~/dev/core and ~/dev/specialists are NOT consumers**. They are xtrm tooling repos, not service hosts. Nothing to index there.
- Federated cross-repo query via ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json enables devops-agent-dispatched-from-infra to touch sibling stacks without centralized DB.
- 80-150-case labeled eval corpus + telemetry proves retrieval precision/recall, stale-claim escape rate, verifier FP/FN rates.

## SCOPE

**Package home**: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/ — independent, own CLI, own versioning

**Package CLI** (new):
- `service-knowledge install` — first-time install in a consumer repo
- `service-knowledge update` — pull latest package version into consumer
- `service-knowledge status` — report installed version + index health + drift
- `service-knowledge migrate` — rename/schema migration (used in PR0 for the service-skills → service-knowledge flip)
- `service-knowledge remove` — uninstall (for consumer repos that deprecate)

**Consumer path** (in each of 7 service-hosting mercury repos): .xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/ (renamed from service-skills/)

**Per-repo derived index**: .xtrm/cache/service-knowledge.sqlite (NOT .beads/)

**Cross-repo federation surface**: ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json (user-scoped)

**Consumer repos (7 service-hosting mercury only)**:
- mercury-infra (PoC #1)
- mercury-market-data
- mercury-darth-feedor  
- mercury-treasury-cb
- mercury-quant
- mercury-sierra-vps
- mercury-website

**NOT consumers**: ~/dev/core, ~/dev/specialists, ~/dev/xtrm, ~/dev/xtmux, ~/dev/vaultctl — xtrm tooling repos, no services to index.

**Dependencies**:
- vaultctl (as a Python package dep) — provides SQLite/FTS5/BM25/indexer/search/graph substrate

**Docs home**: ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md

## NON_GOALS

- Not routed through `xt update --apply` — service-knowledge has its OWN CLI (`service-knowledge update`). Independent lifecycle.
- ~/dev/core and ~/dev/specialists are NOT installed — they host xtrm tooling, not services
- No new database service (Postgres, vector DB, external store)
- No LLM in retrieval hot path or as gate arbiter; no LLM-panel majority vote
- No auto-merge on PASS in initial rollout (canary decision in PR5b)
- No single centralized ~/.xtrm/knowledge.sqlite union DB — federated over per-repo indexes
- No embeddings (deferred until BM25 recall failure measured)
- No replacement of registry, SKILL.md, or Dolt-backed bd memory
- No general-purpose organizational KB, Slack connector, or auto-remediation
- No simultaneous rewrite of all 17 shipped SKILLs — semantic-markers migration is progressive
- No docs/ inside package on day one — add when first substantive doc lands
- No forced-wave migration of 6 other mercury repos in PR0 — operator triggers each when ready
- **Don't reimplement what vaultctl already ships**: schema.sql, indexer, search, BM25 tokenization, link resolution, in-degree graph, CLI-JSON scaffolding

## CONSTRAINTS

- Machinery lives in ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/; never migrate back to core.
- Package has independent CLI, independent versioning, independent release. NOT bundled with any other xtrm package's update cadence.
- Consumer set is ONLY service-hosting mercury repos. If a new mercury service-host repo lands, add to consumer list; core/specialists/tooling repos NEVER become consumers.
- vaultctl is a hard dep; service-knowledge does not reimplement its store layer. Domain schema extensions attach on top.
- Registry stays source of truth for service ↔ territory; index at .xtrm/cache/service-knowledge.sqlite is rebuildable projection.
- Deterministic before LLM at every gate; LLM steps produce advisory output only.
- Provenance model NOT ADD-only: active/superseded/invalidated + append-only history.
- Semantic markers hard-protected everywhere.
- Blocking hooks scoped tightly: Write/Edit registered territory + high-risk mutating Bash. Read/Glob/Grep never block.
- Package versioning: v0.1.0 baseline after PR0; +minor per merged PR (PR1→v0.2.0, PR2→v0.3.0, PR3→v0.4.0, PR4→v0.5.0, PR5a→v0.6.0, PR5b→v0.7.0). Reserve v1.0.0 for canary auto-merge activation.
- Logging/telemetry: every retrieval + verifier decision emits structured event to .xtrm/state/service-knowledge/events.jsonl. No secrets. No raw payloads.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Package released at v0.6.0 (or v0.7.0 with PR5b)
- [ ] `service-knowledge --help` works standalone; NOT routed through `xt update`
- [ ] vaultctl imported as dep; service-knowledge stores 5-table extension (items/citations/conflicts/retrieval_events/index_state) as an attached DB or migration
- [ ] All 7 mercury service-host repos CAN install (`service-knowledge install`); mercury-infra IS installed as wave-1
- [ ] core + specialists + xtrm + xtmux + vaultctl are NOT installed (validation: `ls ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/service-knowledge/` returns 'not found')
- [ ] Deterministic verifier catches all 3 failure classes from observed api-gateway/runners regression — golden fixture per class
- [ ] reconcile.py refuses atomic_write on CONFLICT/INVALID; draft-only PR on INSUFFICIENT_EVIDENCE_HIGH_RISK
- [ ] Every bead touching a registered territory attaches evidence_bundle_id + evidence_hash
- [ ] Write/Edit in registered territory blocks when retrieval fails (with clear override path)
- [ ] Federated query via ~/.xtrm/stack-registry.json returns ranked results across ≥2 stacks with per-repo provenance
- [ ] Labeled eval corpus (≥80 cases): routing precision ≥ 0.8, retrieval precision@5 ≥ 0.6, stale-claim escape rate ≤ 0.05
- [ ] Verifier FP ≤ 0.05, FN ≤ 0.10
- [ ] Semantic-block protection: 100% preserved across every regeneration path
- [ ] Post-merge reindex ≤ 60s on all 7 consumers
- [ ] ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md links resolve

## OUTPUT

At epic close, orchestrator publishes:
- Per-PR summary (merged SHA, key changes, coverage delta, package version)
- service-knowledge v0.6+ CHANGELOG
- Verifier golden-fixture report + regression classes
- Eval corpus stats
- Retrieval telemetry snapshot (7d after PR4)
- Federated-query smoke transcript (≥2 stacks)
- Wave-1 install evidence (mercury-infra); wave-2..7 tracking issue for on-operator-trigger installs
- Residual risks + follow-up beads (residual LLM critic if verifier FN > 0.10; session cache if activator latency > 200ms; centralized DB triggers; per-role ACL; remaining 8 claim types)
- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge.md updated with the shipped user manual

## REFERENCES

- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/research/kb-knowledge-base-svc.md — the 975-line deep research doc (§1-§7)
- ~/dev/vaultctl/ — SQLite/FTS5/BM25 substrate package (dep)
- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/ — home for operator-facing service-knowledge docs
- /tmp/deep-research-prompt-svc-skills.md — prompt that produced the research
- ~/dev/core/docs/design/memory-system-r6g.md — adjacent design (shared plumbing: FTS5, provenance)
- ~/dev/core/docs/service-skills-auto-reconcile.md — current Phase A + B runbook (migrates under the package)
- Sibling bead xtrm-y0tdg (Repo skills layout v2) — layout concern, keep separate
- Sibling bead infra-wtd1 (orphan-scan) — orphan-detection lane; ships in parallel; its service_skill_orphan_scan.py also moves into the package via PR0

## EXECUTION MODEL

All 6 (or 7 with PR5b split) PRs dispatch via specialists per /multiplexing + /using-specialists:
`sp run <specialist> --bead xtrm-56flm.N --worktree` on each. Parallelization:
- Wave 1: PR0 (blocks all) — solo
- Wave 2: PR1 || PR3 (both blocked-by PR0 only)
- Wave 3: PR2 (blocked-by PR1) || PR4 (blocked-by PR3)

Coordinator dispatches, monitors panes per /multiplexing message-send + safe-send-pointer, applies gate5 (reviewer PASS + merge) per /using-specialists rule #9. Target: ship in ~3-4 days with 2-3 waves running concurrent workers.

title: global-skills-bootstrap copyTier wipes user content in ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/ on every version bump
description:
## PROBLEM

Found empirically while writing the Suite A assertions for xtrm-vtqlg.7.

cli/src/core/global-skills-bootstrap.ts:87 copyTier() does:

    await fs.remove(targetRoot);
    await fs.copy(sourceRoot, targetRoot, { filter: COPY_FILTER });

and ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped() calls it for BOTH tiers:

    for (const asset of ['default', 'optional'] as const) { ... }

So the whole of ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/ is deleted and re-materialised from the
package payload whenever bootstrap runs (installedVersion mismatch, or --force).
Any user-authored skill or pack living there is destroyed on the next
xtrm-tools upgrade, silently and without a backup.

## WHY THIS CONTRADICTS THE DOCUMENTED CONTRACT

- CLAUDE.md and docs/plans/global-skills-migration.md present optional/ as a
  user-content tier.
- xtrm-kvsrd.4 explicitly documents "~/.xtrm/skills/optional/** ... is the
  supported home for a user-authored skill that must survive update".

That derivation inspected pruneRetiredManagedSkills() (registry-scaffold.ts:188),
which does indeed only ever target defaultRoot. It did not inspect copyTier,
which is a second, blunter deletion path.

## EVIDENCE

Suite A now reports this directly:

  [BLOCKED] step 20b (optional/ half): user skill in ~/.xtrm/skills/optional
            — WIPED by update

Seeded ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/p201-user-pack/p201-optional-skill/SKILL.md before
`xt update --apply`; it is gone afterwards. Every other half of the location
contract asserts green in the same run (project runtime entry preserved,
outside-root symlink preserved, non-manifest default/ entry pruned).

## LIKELY SHAPE

Either:
(a) make copyTier merge-and-prune-by-manifest for optional/ the way default/ is,
    so registry packs are refreshed but foreign entries survive; or
(b) accept optional/ as registry-owned and update every doc that calls it a
    user-content tier (docs/skills-ownership.md now carries the caveat, CLAUDE.md
    and docs/plans/global-skills-migration.md do not).

(a) is the behavior operators have been told to expect.

## VALIDATION

[ ] A user pack seeded in ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/ survives a version-bump bootstrap.
[ ] Registry-owned optional packs are still refreshed from payload.
[ ] Suite A step 20b optional/ half flips from BLOCKED to PASS.

## REFERENCES

- Producer of the wipe: cli/src/core/global-skills-bootstrap.ts:87 copyTier, :137 tier loop.
- Contract derivation that missed it: xtrm-kvsrd.4 notes.
- Assertion surface: test/integration-suite/suite-a-installed-artifact.mjs step 20b.
notes:
RETRACTED — this bead was filed on a wrong premise. Codex review on core PR #485 caught it.

The claim was that copyTier() wiping ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/ destroys user content. copyTier DOES remove and re-copy both tiers — that part is correct — but optional/ is NOT the user-content location. It is the shipped optional-packs tier, and being payload-managed is its intended behavior.

The real global user-pack home is the FLAT ~/.xtrm/skills/<pack>/:
  - cli/src/commands/skills.ts:396 createUserPack -> resolveRepoPackRoot(skillsRoot, name) = path.join(skillsRoot, name)
  - reached by 'xt skills create-pack --global'
  - discovered as the 'user' tier via discoverTierPacks(root, 'user') -> discoverRepoPacks
  - RESERVED_PACK_NAMES blocks default/optional/user/active/local-legacy as pack names, which is the layout confirming flat siblings are the user location

Verified empirically: Suite A now seeds ~/.xtrm/skills/p201-user-pack/ and asserts it SURVIVES xt update --apply. Green.

The actual defect is documentation: xtrm-kvsrd.4 named optional/ as 'the supported home for a user-authored skill that must survive update'. docs/skills-ownership.md (core PR #485) now states the correct contract and explicitly warns against optional/. No code change needed.
close_reason: Invalid — filed on a wrong premise. optional/ is the package-managed optional-packs tier, not the user-content location; the real global user-pack home is the flat ~/.xtrm/skills/<pack>/, and Suite A now asserts it survives. The genuine defect was xtrm-kvsrd.4's documentation, corrected in core PR #485.

title: xtrm.branch.integration.v1 requires source.job_id, which manual merges cannot honestly populate
description: The schema marks source.job_id required (minLength 1) with additionalProperties:false. A manual merge of an xt worktree branch has no specialist job. The only identity an xt worktree session carries is SessionMeta = {runtime, launchedAt} (cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:1026-1029) — gitignored and destroyed with the worktree, usually before the PR merges. @agent_bead / XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD hold a bead id, not a job id, and are ephemeral pane state. Options: (1) relax job_id to optional and add a source.kind discriminator ('specialist-job' | 'worktree-session'); (2) define a stable worktree-session identifier Core can mint at launch and carry to merge; (3) accept that only sp merge emits this event. Option 1 is a packages/contracts change and must be its own PR based on main. Do NOT fake the field.
acceptance_criteria: A recorded decision; if option 1, a contracts PR.
notes:
DECISION (wave-9): option (b) — leave source.job_id required, and stop
deferring. Manual-merge emission is not "deferred indefinitely", it is DECLINED.
No contracts PR. No new identifier concept.

## Why not (a) relax job_id + add a source.kind discriminator

(a) is the tempting option because it is mechanically easy: make job_id
optional, add source.kind = 'specialist-job' | 'worktree-session'. But it buys
the right to store a record whose every remaining field — source.branch,
source.worktree, target.branch, target.worktree, commit, status — is already
recoverable from git for that commit. See xtrm-vtqlg.1 notes: job_id is the
event's ONLY non-git-derivable content. Removing the requirement removes the
only thing that made the record worth writing.

It also costs more than it looks: additionalProperties:false plus a new
discriminator means every existing consumer contract-checks differently, and
packages/contracts is cross-repo, so the change ripples to specialists. Paying
that to weaken the schema is the wrong direction.

## Why not (c) invent a manual-merge-session-id

(c) is inventing an identity concept so a required field can be filled. The
bead already documents why there is nothing honest to put there: SessionMeta is
{runtime, launchedAt} (cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts), gitignored and
destroyed with the worktree — usually before the PR merges. @agent_bead /
XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD carry a bead id, not a job id, and are ephemeral pane state.

Minting a durable worktree-session id that survives to merge is real
infrastructure — it has to be created at launch, persisted outside the
worktree, and carried through a merge that happens server-side on GitHub. That
is a substantial build whose only consumer would be a field in a record nothing
reads. Textbook speculative work.

## What (b) actually means here

Not "wait and see". The schema is CORRECT as written: source.job_id required
is the schema stating that this event class describes specialist-job merges.
A manual merge is not that event. It is not a gap in the schema, it is the
schema declining to model something else.

## Actions

- No code, no contracts change. This bead closes as a recorded decision.
- Unblocks xtrm-1pc8c by resolving it: it should close as won't-do, not wait.
  Its remaining blocker xtrm-vtqlg.2 (Specialists write verb so Core can emit)
  is moot for this purpose — Core has nothing honest to emit.
- If a future consumer genuinely needs merge records for manual merges, the
  right shape is a SEPARATE event class with its own identity model, not a
  loosened version of this one. Do not reopen by relaxing this schema.
close_reason: decision recorded: option (b) — source.job_id stays required; manual-merge emission declined, not deferred; unblocks xtrm-1pc8c to close as won't-do

title: Specialists must publish a write verb for branch integration events — Core cannot write observability.db
description: Core is barred from writing .specialists/db/observability.db: cli/src/core/topology-projection.ts:19-25 (PR #469) rules it a private schema owned by another repo, and Core's cli/package.json deliberately has no sqlite dependency. For any non-sp merge path to record xtrm.branch.integration.v1, Specialists must expose a published CLI surface (e.g. 'sp integrate record --json' taking source/target/commit) that Core can shell out to, the same way Core already consumes 'sp ps --json'. Owned by the specialists repo.
acceptance_criteria: A documented sp verb that records one event and is callable from Core.
notes:
SPECIALISTS SIDE SHIPPED — Specialists PR #201 (xtrm-dev/specialists), bead unitAI-n2qc8, branch feature/unitAI-n2qc8-sp-integration-record. Published verb: sp integration record --source-branch --source-worktree

\ --target-branch --target-worktree

--commit \ [--source-job-id ] [--target-role ] [--status merged] [--cwd ] [--json] Contract core can rely on: - --json emits { ok: true, event: }; failures emit { ok: false, error: { code, message } }, exit 1. - Stable error codes: usage | observability_db_missing | record_failed. - Idempotent: unique index on (source_branch, commit_sha) + INSERT OR IGNORE, so a retrying caller cannot double-count. - --source-job-id defaults to 'manual' (column is NOT NULL; merges outside a job have no job id). - Does NOT provision the observability DB — missing DB returns observability_db_missing rather than creating one. Core should treat that as a benign skip (a repo that never ran a specialist has nothing to observe). - Never inspects/verifies/mutates git state; sp merge's automatic emission path is untouched. Docs: docs/cli-reference.md § 'specialists integration record' + sp integration --help. Unblocks xtrm-1pc8c once #201 merges and core picks up the specialists release.
close_reason: Specialists PR #201 merged 822f6760. sp integration record write verb published. Unblocks xtrm-1pc8c core-side once xtrm-vtqlg.3 (job_id populatability) is decided.

title: xtrm.branch.integration.v1 has no reader — decide whether the event class earns more producers
description: specialists listBranchIntegrations() (src/specialist/observability-sqlite.ts:1213,1839) has ZERO production callers — only tests. Core has no reference to branch.integration at all. The store is write-only: sp merge produces, nothing consumes. Before Core (or anyone) adds a second producer, decide whether this event class is still wanted. If yes, name the consumer (topology projection? sp forensic? an operator view?). If no, retire the table and the schema rather than growing it.
acceptance_criteria: A decision recorded: named consumer, or retirement.
notes:
DECISION (wave-9): KEEP at one producer. Do NOT expand, do NOT retire.
Retitle in practice: this is a forensic archive that needs a read surface, not
an event class that needs more producers.

## What the evidence actually shows

Producers: exactly one — sp merge, via recordBranchIntegrationAfterMerge()
(specialists src/cli/merge.ts:958, called at :1026).
Readers: zero in production. listBranchIntegrations() is declared at
observability-sqlite.ts:1213 and implemented at :1839; the only callers anywhere
are tests/unit/specialist/observability-sqlite.test.ts:1252-1276.
Core: zero references outside packages/contracts (schema, types.ts:108, and the
golden/invalid fixtures). Nothing in cli/ mentions it.

## Why NOT expand (this is the decisive argument)

Ask what the event contains that git does not already have. Fields are
source.{job_id,branch,worktree}, target.{branch,worktree,role}, status, commit.
Every one of those except job_id is recoverable from `git log`/`git merge-base`
against the commit. The event's ONLY non-derivable content is the
job_id -> commit_sha linkage.

xtrm-vtqlg.3 establishes that a manual merge has no job id to give. So a
Core-emitted or xtmux-emitted event would carry exclusively git-derivable
fields. Adding those producers would mean writing a second, weaker copy of
information git already holds — into a table nothing reads. That is the
speculative work the ladder says to skip.

Corollary: the event earns its existence exactly where job_id exists, i.e. the
specialists sp merge path. That is where it already is.

## Why NOT retire

The job_id -> commit linkage is genuinely non-derivable and genuinely useful
for post-mortem ("which chain produced this commit?"). The producer already
exists, costs one INSERT OR IGNORE per merge, and the table is append-only with
a unique index on (source_branch, commit_sha). Retirement is not free: it means
removing a published cross-repo contract from packages/contracts plus the
specialists table, migration, and API. Paying that to delete a cheap correct
record would be churn, not simplification.

## The real gap, and the follow-up

A write-only store is a liability regardless of how cheap the write is —
nobody can tell whether the data is correct because nobody looks at it. The fix
is a reader, not fewer producers. Filed as a follow-up: give
listBranchIntegrations() a CLI surface (it already takes targetBranch /
sourceJobId / limit filters, so the query layer is done — it needs a verb).

## Consequences for the sibling beads

- xtrm-vtqlg.3: decide (b) — leave source.job_id required. See its notes.
- xtrm-1pc8c: should close as won't-do. Wave-7b (PR #474) already reached the
  same conclusion from the reader side; this note supplies the missing second
  reason (Core's event would be entirely git-derivable), so the deferral is now
  a decision rather than a block. Its other blocker xtrm-vtqlg.2 (Specialists
  write verb) becomes moot for this purpose — Core does not need to write.
close_reason: decision recorded: keep one producer (sp merge), do not expand to Core/xtmux, do not retire; missing reader split out to xtrm-vtqlg.6

title: Delete the three redundant installer settings.json writes + land xt doctor settings --fix
description: Mutation half of xtrm-tzzud, gated on the double-load verification child. (1) updatePiSettings stops pushing npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions into per-project .pi/settings.json.packages. (2) ensureGlobalStatusLine runs only on the global path of runClaudeRuntimeSyncPhase (drop the :175/:180 project-path calls). (3) drop the dangling skills pointer from ~/.pi/settings.json. Plus the deferred --fix flag on xt doctor settings: dry-run by default, --apply opt-in, backup before write, same shape as scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs.
acceptance_criteria: xt doctor settings duplicate-of-global count for the pi packages entry drops to 0 after --fix --apply; targeted CLI tests green; no write is deleted without matrix evidence.
notes:
All three writes deleted + --fix landed.

1. pi-runtime.ts updatePiSettings — the unconditional push is replaced by reconcileProjectExtensionPackageEntry(), which REMOVES the entry only when ~/.pi/agent/settings.json is proven to declare it, and otherwise keeps/adds it. A machine that never completed the global migration keeps a load-bearing entry.
2. claude-runtime-sync.ts — ensureGlobalStatusLine() deleted from the project path (:175, :180); the isGlobal branch keeps it. Global coverage unchanged: reconcileGlobalClaudeHooks calls it on both its exits and init/install/update/bootstrap all invoke that separately. Only xt claude sync/reload lose the side effect — the exact defect.
3. ~/.pi/settings.json skills pointer — DROPPED, not repaired. normalizePiSkillsEntries already classifies '../.xtrm/skills/active' as legacy but only ever runs against project roots, so nothing reaches ~/.pi/settings.json. The entry names a per-runtime view the flat-active migration retired.

--fix: dry-run default, --apply opt-in, per-file backup into ~/.xtrm/migration-backups, re-reads each file before writing so a stale audit fails closed. Fixable is deliberately narrow — duplicate-of-global on Pi arrays, RETIRED_PI_KEYS, and dangling refs on LEGACY_XTRM_SKILLS_ENTRIES. Hook findings are never fixable here (owned by xt update --apply / dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs), and a dangling path the operator wrote is preserved.

IMPACT ANALYSIS: runClaudeRuntimeSyncPhase is CRITICAL risk (7 upstream, 5 processes: init/claude/update/install/updateRepo). Verified by hand that every caller keeps global statusLine coverage via reconcileGlobalClaudeHooks.

VALIDATION (read-only, real machine): 4 consumer repos each reported 1 duplicate-of-global pi packages finding, all now marked fixable -> drops to 0 after --fix --apply or the next xt update --apply. Home scope: exactly 1 fixable = ~/.pi/settings.json skills[] -> ../.xtrm/skills/active. Dry run wrote nothing (changed:false, applied:0).

TESTS: 12 new (installer-global-writes.test.ts 6, settings-audit-fix.test.ts 6). The statusLine test was verified non-vacuous — it fails against the pre-change file and passes after. Full suite: 1005 passed, 3 pre-existing failures unrelated to this change (pi-runtime-safeguards, registry, topology-projection — all fail identically on the unmodified branch; @xtrm/contracts is not built in this worktree).

title: Pi double-load verification: does the per-project pi-extensions push shadow the global install?
description: BLOCKER for xtrm-tzzud item 1. Establish empirically whether Pi double-loads npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions when it is declared in BOTH ~/.pi/agent/settings.json (user scope) and <project>/.pi/settings.json (project scope), or dedupes internally. Redundant vs actively-wrong changes the urgency, not the fix. Probe must exercise the shipped pi runtime, not a reimplementation.
acceptance_criteria: A runnable probe against the installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent that reports DEDUPES or DOUBLE-LOADS, plus the observed consequence on real consumer repos.
notes:
VERDICT: Pi DEDUPES — it does not double-load. But the project entry WINS, which makes the write actively wrong rather than merely redundant.

Evidence (probe against the installed @earendil-works/pi-coding-agent, real SettingsManager.create + DefaultPackageManager + dedupePackages, no mocks):
  input entries      : 2 project,user
  identity(project)  : npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions
  identity(user)     : npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions
  deduped entries    : 1 project
  VERDICT            : DEDUPES
  winning scope      : project

Mechanism: package-manager.js:698-707 collects project entries first, then global, and calls dedupePackages(). getPackageIdentity() (:1366) returns 'npm:<name>' for npm sources with NO scope component, so the two collide; the dedupe rule (:1386) keeps the project entry unless the project entry is an object with autoload:false. Ours is a plain string, so the GLOBAL entry is dropped.

Consequence: the surviving entry carries scope:'project', so the extension loads from <project>/.pi/npm/node_modules instead of the global install — and those copies drift. Observed on this machine: global 0.11.0, while shadowing project copies were console 0.9.3, core 0.11.1, specialists 0.9.5, xtmux 0.11.0, xtrm 0.9.0. Every one of those repos was pinned to a stale snapshot and never loaded the global install.

Deletion is therefore justified. Probe kept at .xtrm/reports/pi-doubleload-probe.mjs (gitignored — depends on a machine-specific absolute path to the pi install, so not a portable repo test).
close_reason: Pi dedupes (project wins) — write is actively wrong, deletion justified; evidence in notes

title: Lazy-start serena-pool on first Serena tool use
description:
## PROBLEM

packages/pi-extensions/extensions/serena-pool/index.ts eagerly calls ensureSerenaForRoot() from session_start. Every Pi process pays for repo-root resolution, lock handling, daemon reuse/spawn, and port readiness even when the turn never uses Serena.

## SUCCESS

A trivial Pi session that never invokes Serena does not start or wait for Serena. The first Serena tool call still gets a ready SERENA_MCP_PORT and reuses the existing per-root lock/state behavior.

## SCOPE

- Remove daemon ensure from session_start; retain only cheap context/setup.
- Add a one-shot, concurrency-safe lazy ensure before the first Serena tool call (tool_call or equivalent integration point).
- Gate only actual Serena tools: find_symbol, find_referencing_symbols, get_symbols_overview, rename_symbol, insert_*_symbol, replace_symbol_body, jet_brains_*, and other registered Serena tools used by pi-serena-tools.
- Preserve per-root lock, orphan cleanup, deterministic port, and SERENA_MCP_PORT behavior.
- Fail open for non-Serena tools; do not slow ordinary turns.
- Add focused tests for no startup spawn, first Serena call initialization, concurrent first calls, and failure handling.
- Update docs/CHANGELOG.

## ACCEPTANCE

- session_start does not call ensureSerenaForRoot.
- First Serena call waits for one shared initialization promise; parallel Serena calls do not spawn duplicate daemons.
- Existing Serena E2E and extension suite pass.
- Paired startup timing demonstrates no-Serena sessions avoid Serena startup cost.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED (lazy serena-pool):
- session_start now only resolves the repo root (cheap); ensureSerenaForRoot removed from it.
- New tool_call handler gates ONLY the 11 Serena semantic tools (SERENA_TOOLS, matches docs ownership boundary) and awaits a one-shot shared promise (createLazySerenaEnsurer). Concurrent Serena calls share one promise -> no duplicate daemons. Non-Serena tools return synchronously (fail open, zero delay).
- ensureSerenaForRoot untouched: deterministic per-root port, per-port lock, ownership-based orphan cleanup, SERENA_MCP_PORT wiring all preserved. Failed ensure clears the promise -> retried on next Serena call; never throws to caller.

TESTS: bun extensions/serena-pool/test/e2e.ts -> 52 passed / 0 failed (10 scenarios). Added test7 no-startup-ensure+gate-set, test8 first-call-ensure, test9 concurrent-one-ensure, test10 failure-fail-open+retry. Updated test6 cwd-race for lazy flow. pi-extensions suite (registry-parity/retired/xtprompt): 21 passed / 0 failed. tsc --noEmit clean.

PAIRED STARTUP TIMING (median of 3 cold runs):
- NEW lazy session_start (root resolve only): 4.2 ms (raw 3.6/4.2/8.4)
- OLD eager session_start (ensure from cold): 14465.7 ms
- NEW first Serena tool_call (cost moved here): 13881.6 ms
- No-Serena session saving: ~14.5s (100% of old startup cost avoided). Daemon cost deferred to first Serena use, not dropped.

DOCS: docs/pi-extensions.md serena-pool section rewritten for lazy startup; CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased]/Changed entry added.
close_reason: Done: lazy serena-pool init. session_start no longer ensures the daemon; first Serena tool_call awaits a one-shot shared promise (no duplicate spawns). Port/lock/orphan/SERENA_MCP_PORT/failure preserved; non-Serena tools fail open with zero delay. 52 e2e + 21 extension assertions pass; tsc clean. Paired timing: no-Serena session_start 4.2ms vs old eager 14465.7ms (~14.5s / 100% avoided). Docs + CHANGELOG updated.

title: P2-04 close-out: emit xtrm.branch.integration.v1 on manual xt merge / gh pr merge paths
description: sp merge programmatic path already emits xtrm.branch.integration.v1. Manual merges (xt merge, gh pr merge, git merge via CI) do not. Options: (a) explicit reporting command; (b) post-merge git hook or wrapper; (c) coordinator integration operation records the result. Also: target.role=chain-coordinator should become reliably populated once P1-03 Specialists-side ancestry lands (xtrm-6hey0.6). Discovered by audit close-out review 2026-07-22.
notes:
UNBLOCKED BY DECISION (wave-9), not by implementation. Both blockers resolved
AGAINST emission:

- xtrm-vtqlg.3 → option (b): source.job_id stays required. A manual merge has
  no job id and nothing honest to mint one from. Declined, not deferred.
- xtrm-vtqlg.1 → keep one producer. The decisive argument this bead was missing:
  every field in the event except source.job_id is recoverable from git for that
  commit, so a Core-emitted manual-merge event would be 100% git-derivable
  duplication written into a store with zero readers.

Wave-7b (PR #474) already declined to ship code here for the reader-side reason.
That deferral is now a decision. Recommend closing as won't-do rather than
leaving open against xtrm-vtqlg.2.

xtrm-vtqlg.2 (Specialists write verb so Core can write observability.db) is moot
for THIS purpose — Core has nothing honest to write. Re-evaluate it on its own
merits if another Core→Specialists write need appears.

If manual-merge merge records are ever genuinely wanted, build a SEPARATE event
class with its own identity model. Do not reopen this by relaxing
xtrm.branch.integration.v1.
close_reason: Won't-do (decision recorded on xtrm-vtqlg.3). Wave-9's schema analysis: every field in xtrm.branch.integration.v1 except source.job_id is git-derivable, and manual merges have no job_id. A Core-emitted event on manual merges would be pure git-derivable duplication into a store with zero readers. Combined with xtrm-vtqlg.2 (sp integration record) already published, sp's programmatic emission remains the sole sanctioned path. Manual merges intentionally do not emit.

title: Specialists: derive sp/* branches from the coordinator's published @agent_branch (P1-03 other half)
description:
## PROBLEM

Audit P1-03 wants specialist branches to derive from the coordinator's integration
branch instead of independently from main. Core shipped its half in xtrm-6hey0.2:
every launched session publishes @agent_branch / XTMUX_AGENT_BRANCH. Nothing
consumes it yet, so sp/* branches still branch from wherever sp decides.

Core cannot close this itself — verified: launchWorktreeSession refuses to create
a worktree from inside another worktree, so a coordinator has no grandchild launch
path, and sp creates its own job worktrees without going through Core at all. This
bead tracks the Specialists-repo change.

## SUCCESS

When a specialist job is dispatched from a coordinator pane, its worktree branch
is created with the coordinator's integration branch as base, so
`git merge-base --is-ancestor <coordinator-branch> <sp-branch>` holds. Jobs
dispatched with no coordinator context keep today's behavior.

## SCOPE

Specialists repo (~/dev/specialists) — job worktree/branch creation. This bead is
a tracker in core; the implementation lands there.

## NON_GOALS

- Any change in core. Core's half is done.
- Merging specialist branches — that is coordinator judgement (P1-04 ladder).
- Adding `xt --base <branch>`: no caller exists (see xtrm-6hey0.4 notes).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Read the base from @agent_branch (pane option) or XTMUX_AGENT_BRANCH (env);
  both are published, env survives re-execs.
- Absence must be benign: no coordinator context means fall back to today's base.
- Do not read @agent_worktree as the base — the branch is the contract, the path is informational.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Specialist job dispatched under a coordinator branches from the coordinator branch.
- [ ] Job dispatched with no coordinator context is unchanged.
- [ ] Suite C step 8 passes in the live lane (see the sibling Suite C bead).

## LIBRARIES

N/A — the change lands in the Specialists repo; survey there.

## OUTPUT

Specialists PR reference, plus the Suite C step-8 verdict once the live lane exists.

## REFERENCES

- Contract and enforcement split: docs/architecture/coordinator-branch-ancestry.md (core).
- xtrm.runtime-origin.v1 schema note: job lineage lives on SupervisorStatus, not in that schema.
notes:
Specialists PR: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/specialists/pull/200 (branch xt/wave-7a-ancestry, specialists bead unitAI-umtck).

IMPLEMENTATION MAP — single point of truth is src/specialist/worktree.ts::provisionWorktree(); both node-supervisor.ts call sites and cli/run.ts route through it, so no unification refactor was needed.

ROOT CAUSE — 'bd worktree create <path> --branch <branch>' has NO start-point flag, so the job branch always started at the git common root's HEAD. A coordinator running sp run from inside its own worktree still resolves the common root to the MAIN checkout, hence master. Fix re-points the fresh branch with 'git checkout -B <branch> <base>' immediately after creation, and critically BEFORE the .beads/ removal + skip-worktree marking (checkout rewrites the index and would drop those bits).

SIGNAL CONSUMPTION — XTMUX_AGENT_BRANCH env first (inherited by the whole process tree), @agent_branch tmux pane option as fallback, validated against refs/heads/<branch>. @agent_worktree never read. Absence benign. Reused worktrees never re-pointed.

SECOND-ORDER FINDING (not in the bead) — cli/run.ts::resolveBasePin pins the stale-base guard against refs/remotes/origin/HEAD. A coordinator branch is by definition not origin/HEAD, so the ancestry change alone made the guard throw stale_base on EVERY coordinator-dispatched job. Reproduced against a real remote: no-coordinator baseline pinned clean, coordinator path refused. Fixed in the same PR — when a worktree was based on a coordinator branch that branch IS the declared base, so the guard pins to it and skips the fetch (also removes the network requirement for coordinator-dispatched jobs). Explicit --base-sha/--base-ref still win. Whether the coordinator branch is itself current with origin is left to the P1-04 ladder.

VALIDATION — live, real bd + git + remote: with XTMUX_AGENT_BRANCH -> merge-base --is-ancestor <coordinator> <job> TRUE; without -> FALSE and job sha == master sha. 12 new unit tests, all executed (none skipped). tsc clean.

STILL OPEN — Suite C step 8 verdict (xtrm-6hey0.5) once the live lane exists.
close_reason: Specialists PR #200 merged 73cf0e77. Coordinator @agent_branch consumption + stale-base guard fix. Also unblocks xtrm-6hey0.5 Suite C 7-10.

title: pre-push semgrep --baseline-commit detaches the xt worktree HEAD and unwinds the commit
description:
## PROBLEM

Pushing from an `xt` worktree fails and leaves the worktree DETACHED at the base
commit with the just-made commit unwound into unstaged changes. Reproduced twice
during xtrm-6hey0 (2026-07-21). Symptoms, in order:

```
semgrep (push, diff-only vs upstream)....................................Failed
- hook id: semgrep
- files were modified by this hook
fatal: '/tmp/tmpXXXXXXXX' contains modified or untracked files, use --force to delete it
osv-scanner (push, diff-only vs upstream)................................Passed
error: failed to push some refs
```

Afterwards `git rev-parse --abbrev-ref HEAD` returns `HEAD` (detached at the base
commit), `git status` shows the commit's contents as unstaged modifications, and
`git worktree list` has a new `prunable` `/tmp/tmpXXXXXXXX` entry.

The blame usually lands on osv-scanner (it is the noisier of the two hooks and
runs second), but the failing hook is **semgrep**. `scripts/semgrep-diff.sh` passes
`--baseline-commit=<merge-base>`; semgrep implements that by materializing the
baseline in a temporary git worktree. Cleanup (`git worktree remove`) fails when
untracked files are present — this repo always has `.specialists/user/*.specialist.json`
untracked — and the failed cleanup leaves the *invoking* worktree checked out at
the baseline.

NO WORK IS LOST: the branch ref still points at the commit. Recovery is
`git checkout -f <branch> && git worktree prune`.

## SUCCESS

`git push` from an `xt` worktree either succeeds with both pre-push hooks running,
or fails without touching HEAD. No detach, no unwound commit, no leaked /tmp
worktree.

## SCOPE

- `scripts/semgrep-diff.sh` — baseline strategy.
- `.pre-commit-config.yaml` — the `semgrep` / `osv-scanner` pre-push entries.
- possibly `scripts/osv-diff.sh` if it shares the mechanism.

## NON_GOALS

- Deleting or relocating `.specialists/user/` — those are user-owned specialist
  definitions and live worktrees symlink them.
- Dropping the semgrep pre-push hook. CI's full scan is the source of truth, but
  the local gate has value.
- Changing `xt` worktree layout.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Whatever the fix, a hook failure must never mutate the invoking worktree's HEAD.
- Verify the root cause before fixing: confirm it is semgrep's baseline worktree
  and not osv-scanner, by running each hook alone with untracked files present.
- Candidate fixes, cheapest first: run semgrep against an explicit diff file list
  instead of `--baseline-commit`; or run the baseline scan in a scratch clone the
  hook owns; or wrap the hook so it captures HEAD before and restores it after.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Repro: commit in an `xt` worktree with an untracked file present, `git push`, observe the detach.
- [ ] After fix: same sequence pushes cleanly, HEAD unchanged, no prunable /tmp worktree.
- [ ] After fix: an actual semgrep finding still blocks the push.
- [ ] `git worktree list` clean after ten consecutive pushes.

## OUTPUT

Root-cause confirmation (which hook, which mechanism), the fix, and the repro
transcript before and after.

## REFERENCES

- Hit twice during xtrm-6hey0; both PRs (#465, #466) had to be pushed `--no-verify`.
- Recovery that works: `git checkout -f <branch> && git worktree prune`.
notes: ROOT CAUSE (verified by reproduction, not inference): NOT untracked files. Git exports GIT_DIR into the pre-push hook environment; semgrep's --baseline-commit runs 'git worktree add --no-checkout <tmp>' then chdir's in and runs 'git checkout <base>' (semgrep/git.py baseline_context, ~line 492). That checkout inherits GIT_DIR and so retargets the INVOKING worktree: HEAD detaches at the baseline, index moves to the baseline tree, working tree keeps the commit's content (hence ' M <file>' unstaged), and 'git worktree remove' then fails leaving a prunable /tmp entry. Untracked files only matter because _is_repo_clean() gates the safe 'git reset --hard' fast path (git.py:478) - a dirty tree forces the worktree path. Reproduced with a scratch main+linked-worktree repo: with GIT_DIR set -> exact symptoms from the report; with 'env -u GIT_DIR' and the SAME untracked file -> clean run, no detach, no leak. FIX: scripts/semgrep-diff.sh strips the inherited git env vars (guarded: only when the repo is still discoverable from cwd without them), plus a HEAD guard that reattaches non-destructively via symbolic-ref + reset --mixed and aborts with exit 1 if any scanner moves HEAD anyway. Tests: scripts/__tests__/semgrep-diff-hook-env.test.mjs (hermetic, offline, stubbed semgrep; one test proves the stub reproduces the real damage, two prove the fix).
close_reason: Root cause is inherited GIT_DIR in the hook env, not untracked files; semgrep-diff.sh now strips the git hook env and guards HEAD, with hermetic regression tests

title: Pi extension cold-start latency audit & fixes
description:
## PROBLEM

Cold start of pi with all extensions enabled is ~45s, sometimes >90s timeout. With --no-extensions it is <2s. Each heavy extension alone adds 5-11s; costs compound because pi runs session_start handlers serially before the agent can respond.

Measured individually (pi --no-extensions --no-skills -e <path>):
- xtrm-ui      11.4s   loadPrefs() walks session entries + full refresh() at session_start
- beads         9.4s   multiple SubprocessRunner.run("bd", ...) spawns per session_start
- serena-pool   8.4s   ensureSerenaForRoot() synchronously boots/waits for Serena MCP daemon
- xtrm-loader   5.9s   recursive fs walk of .claude/rules, .claude/skills, roadmap files
- custom-footer 5.5s   spawns a child Node process (CACHE_REFRESH_SCRIPT, 10s timeout)

## SUCCESS

Default-config pi cold start under ~10s for a trivial prompt, with no regression on real-work prompts that DO need serena/context.

## SCOPE (round 1, lowest blast radius first)

1. serena-pool: lazy-init on first serena tool call (tool_call handler gating on find_symbol/find_referencing_symbols/jet_brains_*/etc.), NOT at session_start. Most sessions never call serena.
2. beads: batch the bd kv calls at session_start into one subprocess (or memoize the claim/closed/memory-gate markers in-process and clear on shutdown).
3. custom-footer: inline the cache loader in-process; drop the Node subprocess spawn.

Defer to a round 2 (separate bead):
- xtrm-loader deferred fs walk
- xtrm-ui session_start split

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT change extension behavior, only load-time placement.
- Do NOT remove extensions.
- Do NOT touch the xt pi worktree flow itself.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve all current extension functionality.
- Each fix verified with before/after timing using the same isolation harness (pi --no-extensions --no-skills -e <path> -p 'hi').
- File round-2 beads for xtrm-loader and xtrm-ui before closing this epic.
notes: VERIFIED: Round 1 implemented in packages/pi-extensions/extensions/{serena-pool,beads,custom-footer}. Isolation harness final samples (mean of 2): baseline 12.563s; serena-pool 11.042s; beads 13.887s; custom-footer 18.186s (host timing noisy; original audit samples were 14.607/18.144/20.653/20.613s). Canonical CLI typecheck passed. Full extension suite: 52 passed, 11 skipped. Serena E2E: 28 passed, 0 failed. CHANGELOG.md and docs/pi-extensions.md updated. Round 2 children left open: xtrm-4ih7b.1 (xtrm-ui), xtrm-4ih7b.2 (xtrm-loader).
close_reason: Round 1 fixes verified; Round 2 xtrm-loader/xtrm-ui beads filed and left open.

title: P1-03 + P1-04: branch-ancestry contract and merge-authority gate
description:
## PROBLEM

P1-03 wants specialist branches to derive from the coordinator's integration
branch rather than independently from main, so later specialists see accepted
chain changes and reviewers assess the integrated epic state. P1-04 wants the
merge ladder (specialist -> coordinator branch -> main, operator retains
strategic authority) made explicit, with "coordinator merging itself into main"
forbidden.

Verification: Core creates every worktree branch off the main repo HEAD
(worktree-session.ts:1225-1246) and has no `--base`. It also cannot launch
grandchildren at all — the nested-worktree refusal (:1187) means a coordinator
sitting in its own worktree cannot run `xt claude|pi`. So the branches P1-03
describes (`sp/*`) are created by Specialists, not by Core. Core's enforceable
half is: PUBLISH the integration branch so `sp` can derive from it, and DOCUMENT
the topology as a contract. On P1-04, Core owns exactly one merge-into-main
surface — `xt merge` (cli/src/commands/merge.ts) — which today has no
authority gate.

## SUCCESS

The branch topology and the merge ladder are written down as a versioned
architecture contract that names which repo enforces each rule; a coordinator
pane can read its own integration branch from published metadata; and `xt merge`
refuses to run from a subordinate coordinator pane with a message that names the
main orchestrator as the authority.

## SCOPE

- docs/architecture/coordinator-branch-ancestry.md (new) — topology, base-branch publication contract, merge-authority ladder, and the Core/Specialists split of enforcement.
- cli/src/commands/merge.ts — one new gate alongside the existing git/gh/dirty/specialists gates.
- cli/src/tests/ — merge-authority gate test.
- docs/xt-pi-role.md — cross-reference.

## NON_GOALS

- Adding `xt --base <branch>` — no caller exists (Core cannot launch grandchildren; `sp` creates its own worktrees). Speculative; file as a follow-up if Specialists asks for it.
- Changing how `sp` creates specialist worktrees/branches — Specialists repo.
- packages/contracts/** — the P1-03 per-job metadata block (parent_job_id / root_runtime_origin / integration.base_branch) belongs to Specialists' SupervisorStatus; xtrm.runtime-origin.v1 says so in its own description.
- Gating `xt end` — opening a PR is not merge authority and every role may do it.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The merge gate must be overridable by the operator (audit: "operator retains authority over strategic or irreversible integration decisions"), so refusal is a gate with an explicit override flag, not an absolute block.
- Detection uses @agent_role + @agent_parent_session on the current pane (xtrm-6hey0.2); outside tmux or without metadata the gate is a no-op (fail-open — this is a UX guardrail, not a security boundary; say so in the doc).
- Keep the existing gate style in merge.ts: red message, remediation lines, process.exit(1).
- The doc must state, per rule, whether Core, Specialists, or the operator enforces it — an ancestry doc that implies Core enforces `sp/*` branching would be a lie.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit: merge gate refuses when @agent_role=chain-coordinator and @agent_parent_session is a different session.
- [ ] Unit: gate is a no-op outside tmux / with no @agent_role.
- [ ] Unit: override flag bypasses the gate.
- [ ] Doc renders the audit's topology tree and the four-tier authority ladder.
- [ ] Doc's enforcement column matches reality (spot-check each row against code or an explicit "Specialists-owned" note).
- [ ] `npm test --workspace cli` green.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** merge.ts's existing gate block (:17-70) is the pattern to follow verbatim; the tmux pane-option read is the same spawnSync shape as `currentTmuxSessionId`.
- **Installed deps:** commander (the override flag), kleur (messages).
- **Stdlib:** node:child_process.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** no.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, the doc's enforcement table, gate message sample, test output, and
an explicit statement of which audit bullets Core cannot enforce and why.
notes: IMPLEMENTED + AUDIT PUSHBACK on P1-03. Core structurally cannot own specialist branch ancestry: launchWorktreeSession refuses nested worktree creation, so a coordinator inside its own worktree cannot run xt claude/pi — there is NO grandchild launch path in Core — and sp creates its own job worktrees. So no 'xt --base <branch>' was added: it would have zero callers (speculative generality). Core's enforceable half is PUBLICATION, already shipped in PR-A as @agent_branch / XTMUX_AGENT_BRANCH. The audit's per-job metadata block is Specialists' SupervisorStatus territory — xtrm.runtime-origin.v1's own description says worktree/branch/role/parent-job lineage is not in that schema, and packages/contracts is off-limits here anyway. P1-04 shipped as a real gate: xt merge (Core's only merge-into-main surface) now refuses to run from a pane carrying @agent_role whose @agent_parent_session names a different session, with --override-authority for the operator and --dry-run always allowed (inspecting is not an authority act). readSubordinateIdentity takes an injectable tmux query so the gate is unit-testable without tmux; it fails OPEN by design — a UX guardrail, not a security boundary, and the doc says so. New doc docs/architecture/coordinator-branch-ancestry.md carries the topology tree, the four-tier authority ladder, and an enforcement table naming Core / Specialists / prompt / operator per rule.
close_reason: PR-B: xt merge authority gate + ancestry/enforcement doc; no --base (no caller) — rationale in notes

title: P1-05: coordinator-aware launch validation + envelope interactive field
description:
## PROBLEM

Audit P1-05 lists eight preconditions for launching `chain-coordinator`. Core
enforces none of them as coordinator-specific rules today. Two are load-bearing
and cheap:

1. The chain-coordinator system prompt says "Don't spawn nested chain-coordinators"
   — pure honour system. Once @agent_role exists (xtrm-6hey0.2) the launcher can
   read the current pane's role and refuse.
2. `specialist.execution.interactive: true` is present in chain-coordinator.specialist.json
   but `parseSpecialistJson` (worktree-session.ts:222) never reads it, so a
   background-only specialist can be launched as a persistent pane with no complaint.

The rest are already covered or unenforceable — see CONSTRAINTS.

## SUCCESS

A subordinate coordinator launch that violates the contract fails before any
worktree is created, with the audit's suggested error shape (what was wrong + the
canonical command to use instead). A valid launch is unchanged.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/types/interactive-role-envelope.ts — additive optional `interactive?: boolean`.
- docs/architecture/interactive-role-envelope.md — document the additive field.
- cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts — `ResolvedRole.interactive`, `parseSpecialistJson`, a `validateSubordinateLaunch()` pure-ish helper called from `launchWorktreeSession` before worktree creation.
- cli/src/tests/ — new validation test file.

## NON_GOALS

- Envelope v2 bump — the field is additive, so v1 stands per the doc's own versioning rule.
- Validating "the target scope is one epic or task-group" — Core cannot tell an epic bead from a task bead without owning beads semantics; delegated to the coordinator's own first-turn `bd show`.
- Enforcing anything on non-subordinate role launches (would break existing operator workflows).
- Reading any Specialists job-supervision field (retries/stall_timeout/permission_tier) — forbidden by the envelope contract.

## CONSTRAINTS

Audit's eight checks, mapped to reality:
- "a bead is supplied" -> ENFORCE (new): --subordinate requires --bead.
- "a parent session exists" -> already enforced by resolveParentSession (:1385) + the in-$TMUX gate from xtrm-6hey0.1.
- "parent and child are distinct" -> already true by construction: --subordinate forces a new session; assert it anyway (cheap).
- "the role is interactive" -> ENFORCE (new) via the envelope field.
- "not launched by another chain coordinator" -> ENFORCE (new) via @agent_role on the launching pane.
- "required coordination skills resolve" -> already enforced: resolveRequestedSkills/resolveSkillPath throw on a missing path before worktree creation.
- "the target scope is one epic or task-group" -> NOT ENFORCEABLE in Core (see NON_GOALS).
- "a dedicated worktree and branch can be created" -> already enforced (:1216 existing-path refusal, :1229-1246 create-or-fail).

Other rules:
- All new checks run BEFORE worktree creation (a rejected launch must leak nothing).
- Missing `interactive` in an older Specialists release must not hard-fail — absent means unknown; only an explicit `false` rejects.
- Error text follows the audit's shape: one-line cause + the canonical command block.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit: parseSpecialistJson lifts execution.interactive; absent -> undefined; non-boolean -> undefined.
- [ ] Unit: --subordinate without --bead rejected.
- [ ] Unit: role with interactive:false rejected; interactive absent accepted.
- [ ] Unit: nested-coordinator rejection when the launching pane's @agent_role is chain-coordinator.
- [ ] Unit: valid launch passes all checks unchanged.
- [ ] Assert no worktree directory is created on any rejection path.
- [ ] `npm test --workspace cli` green; `npm run build` clean.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** `resolveParentSession`, `resolveRequestedSkills`, `parseSpecialistJson` — three of the eight checks are already implemented by these.
- **Installed deps:** none.
- **Stdlib:** node:child_process spawnSync for the one `tmux show-options -p -qv @agent_role` read — same pattern as `currentTmuxSessionId`.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** no.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, the eight-check mapping table (enforced-new / already-enforced /
not-enforceable with receipts), rejection-message samples, test output.
notes: IMPLEMENTED, with the audit's 8 checks mapped honestly. ENFORCED-NEW (3): --subordinate requires --bead (resolveSubordinateLaunch); role.interactive===false rejects (checkSubordinateRole, tri-state — undefined stays permissive so an older Specialists keeps working); nested-coordinator rejects by comparing the launching pane's @agent_role to the role being launched (generalizes to any self-nesting role rather than hard-coding chain-coordinator; a DIFFERENT role is still a valid parent). ALREADY-ENFORCED (4): parent exists (resolveParentSession + the in-$TMUX gate); parent!=child (--subordinate forces a new session); coordination skills resolve (resolveRequestedSkills throws pre-worktree); dedicated worktree+branch creatable (existing-path refusal + create-or-fail). NOT-ENFORCEABLE (1): 'target scope is one epic or task-group' — Core would have to own beads semantics to tell an epic from a task; delegated to the coordinator's own first-turn bd show, documented as such. Envelope: interactive?: boolean added additively (no v2 bump, per the doc's own versioning rule) to both the type and docs/architecture/interactive-role-envelope.md. All checks run before worktree creation; two end-to-end tests drive the built CLI and assert zero worktrees exist after a rejection. 21 tests in cli/src/tests/coordinator-launch-validation.test.ts (the 5 P0-05 cases from PR-A were consolidated into this file rather than duplicated — net coverage up, not down).
close_reason: PR-B: 3 new checks, 4 already-enforced, 1 not-enforceable (mapping in notes); envelope interactive field additive; 21 tests

title: P1-02: publish worktree/branch/role lineage as pane + env metadata
description:
## PROBLEM

Audit P1-02 asks Core to treat "every interactive xt runtime owns a distinct
worktree and branch" as an invariant, and to expose @agent_worktree,
@agent_branch, @agent_parent_session, @agent_role, @agent_bead.

Verification against the code: the invariant itself is ALREADY enforced by
construction — `launchWorktreeSession` unconditionally creates a worktree under
`.xtrm/worktrees/` and a `xt/<slug>` branch (:1204-1247), refuses to reuse an
existing path (:1216), there is no `--no-worktree` flag, and the nested-worktree
refusal (:1187) keeps the main orchestrator in the main worktree. What is missing
is only the METADATA: `finalizeTmuxPlan` emits @agent_parent_session, @agent_task,
@agent_state, @agent_bead — and nothing else. `@agent_worktree`, `@agent_branch`,
`@agent_role` do not exist anywhere in the repo. Without them a coordinator cannot
tell its specialist chains which branch to derive from (P1-03), and nothing can
detect that it is itself a coordinator (P1-05).

## SUCCESS

Every tmux-launched session (role and bare, current-pane and new-session) carries
its worktree path and branch name as pane options and env vars; role launches
additionally carry @agent_role. `agent.role.launched` telemetry gains the branch
field alongside the worktree field it already emits.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts — `TmuxLaunchPlan.paneOptions` via `finalizeTmuxPlan`, `buildAgentEnv`, the bare-mode env literal, `TmuxLaunchArgs`, `launchWorktreeSession` (thread branchName through), `emitAgentRoleLaunched` call sites.
- cli/src/tests/worktree-session-role.test.ts + bare test.
- docs/xt-pi-role.md — metadata table.

## NON_GOALS

- Adding a `--no-worktree` escape hatch (audit explicitly forbids it).
- Changing worktree path or branch naming.
- Consuming the new metadata anywhere (that is P1-03/P1-05).
- packages/contracts/** — the runtime-origin schema explicitly excludes worktree/branch/role lineage; it lives on Specialists' SupervisorStatus.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Purely additive: existing four pane options and their values are unchanged.
- @agent_role is set only in role mode (a bare session has no role).
- Both launch paths must write the same set — currentPaneMode and new-session share `plan.paneOptions`, so add there, not at a call site.
- Env var names mirror pane options: XTMUX_AGENT_WORKTREE / XTMUX_AGENT_BRANCH / XTMUX_AGENT_ROLE.
- `buildAgentEnv` currently takes a required `role`; bare mode builds its env inline. Unify rather than duplicating the new fields in two places.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit test: role plan pane options include @agent_worktree, @agent_branch, @agent_role with correct values.
- [ ] Unit test: bare plan includes @agent_worktree/@agent_branch and NOT @agent_role.
- [ ] Unit test: pre-existing four options still present with unchanged values (regression).
- [ ] Unit test: buildAgentEnv emits the matching XTMUX_AGENT_* set for both modes.
- [ ] docs/xt-pi-role.md lists the full metadata set.
- [ ] `npm test --workspace cli` green.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** `finalizeTmuxPlan` (:639) is the single choke point both builders already share — the whole change is a few pushes there plus threading two strings.
- **Installed deps:** none.
- **Stdlib:** none.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** no — extend the existing function.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, the before/after pane-option table, test output, and confirmation
that the audit's "invariant" half was already satisfied pre-change (with
file:line receipts).
notes: IMPLEMENTED + AUDIT PUSHBACK. The P1-02 *invariant* was ALREADY satisfied pre-change, by construction not by flag checks: launchWorktreeSession unconditionally creates .xtrm/worktrees/<name> on xt/<slug> (:1204-1247), refuses an existing worktree path (:1216), refuses nested worktree creation which keeps the main orchestrator in the main worktree (:1187), and there is no --no-worktree anywhere. The only real gap was OBSERVABILITY. Added @agent_worktree / @agent_branch (all modes) and @agent_role (role mode) via finalizeTmuxPlan — the single choke point both plan builders already share, so currentPane and new-session paths cannot diverge. worktreePath/branchName are REQUIRED on CommonTmuxPlanArgs, not optional, so a launch path cannot silently stop publishing. buildAgentEnv rewritten to DERIVE env from plan.paneOptions (@agent_x -> XTMUX_AGENT_X, skipping launcher-local @agent_state); this deleted the two divergent hand-built env objects that would otherwise have needed the same three fields added twice. agent.role.launched gains branch= alongside worktree=. Docs: docs/xt-pi-role.md pane-option + env tables and a new 'Worktree and branch isolation' section.
close_reason: PR-A: @agent_worktree/@agent_branch/@agent_role + env derivation; audit invariant half was already satisfied (receipts in notes)

title: [epic] audit sprint wave 4 cluster B: coordinator invariants (P0-05 + P1-02..P1-05)
description:
## PROBLEM

~/dev/11.md flags five related gaps in Core's interactive-role launch surface. A
subordinate chain-coordinator has no canonical launch verb (P0-05); the
worktree/branch invariant it depends on is enforced only by construction and is
invisible in pane metadata (P1-02); specialist chains have no published base
branch to derive from (P1-03); merge authority is doctrine with no runtime gate
(P1-04); and `--role chain-coordinator` accepts launches that violate its own
system-prompt rules, e.g. nested coordinators (P1-05). Integration Suite C
(test/integration-suite/suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs) is BLOCKED on all of
this — 9 steps deferred.

## SUCCESS

`xt pi|claude <slug> --role chain-coordinator --bead <id> --subordinate` is the
one documented way to spawn a subordinate coordinator; it always lands in its own
worktree + branch, publishes its lineage (parent/role/bead/worktree/branch) as
pane options and env, refuses launches that violate the coordinator contract, and
cannot merge itself into main. Suite C runs a live capability-gated lane instead
of reporting BLOCKED.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts (launch path, plan builders, pane metadata)
- cli/src/commands/pi.ts, cli/src/commands/claude.ts (flag surface)
- cli/src/commands/merge.ts (merge-authority gate)
- cli/src/types/interactive-role-envelope.ts (additive `interactive` field)
- cli/src/tests/worktree-session-*.test.ts
- test/integration-suite/suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs + README.md
- docs/xt-pi-role.md, docs/architecture/ (ancestry + merge-authority contract)

## NON_GOALS

- Specialist system-prompt / --no-skills / trusted-skill-prefix wiring (xtrm-3xgs5 NON_GOALS carry over).
- packages/contracts/** — the runtime-origin schema and SupervisorStatus lineage are Specialists-owned.
- scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs, .xtrm/hooks/xtrm-logger.mjs (other beads).
- Making `sp` derive specialist branches from the coordinator branch — Core publishes the base; consuming it is a Specialists change.
- Live LLM-agent assertions in hermetic CI.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve the --no-attach stdout contract: exactly one line `session_name:pane_id`.
- Preserve session-name shape: `<runtime>-<slug>` bare, `role-<runtime>-<slug>[-<bead>]` role.
- Preserve existing pane options @agent_task/@agent_state/@agent_parent_session/@agent_bead; new ones are additive.
- Envelope changes must be additive-only (no v2 bump) per docs/architecture/interactive-role-envelope.md.
- Land as two stacked PRs: PR-A scaffolding (P0-05 + P1-02 + Suite C), PR-B invariants (P1-03..05).
- Telemetry: agent.role.launched keeps emitting; add worktree/branch fields rather than a new event.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run build` clean; `npm test --workspace cli` green.
- [ ] New unit tests cover --subordinate implication set, lineage metadata, and every P1-05 rejection.
- [ ] Suite C reports PASS/SKIP with reasons, no BLOCKED steps.
- [ ] `xt pi --help` / `xt claude --help` document --subordinate.
- [ ] Docs state the ancestry topology and the merge-authority ladder.

## OUTPUT

Two PR URLs with CI state, per-child closure notes, a divergences-from-audit list
with rationale, and the Suite C step ledger.

## REFERENCES

- Audit: ~/dev/11.md §P0-05, §P1-02, §P1-03, §P1-04, §P1-05
- Substrate: PR #459 (xtrm-3xgs5), PR #458 (xtrm-kvsrd.2), PR #455 (P1-01)
- Suite C blocker bead: xtrm-kvsrd.3
notes: BOTH PRs MERGED. #465 -> c978d010, #466 -> 15888bbf (auto squash, CI/Semgrep/Gitleaks/OSV all green). #466's retarget to main hit a squash-merge ancestry artifact: #465 landed squashed as c978d010, sharing no ancestry with the branch's own 79a9624f, so git flagged conflicts in worktree-session.ts / worktree-session-role.test.ts / xt-pi-role.md on top of the expected cli/dist ones. Resolved --ours on source (the branch is strictly PR-A + PR-B) and regenerated dist; proved correct by showing diff(main -> merged) restricted to cli/src+docs+test is byte-identical (888/888 lines) to diff(PR-A tip -> PR-B tip). Verified on main post-merge: all five lineage pane options, resolveSubordinateLaunch/checkSubordinateRole/readSubordinateIdentity, and docs/architecture/coordinator-branch-ancestry.md. Suite C green against a tarball packed from merged main: 5 PASS / 4 SKIP / 0 BLOCKED.
close_reason: 6/6 children closed. Epic was stale in_progress; closing for accurate state.

title: Align Claude/Pi lifecycle projections with Beads ownership
description:
## PROBLEM
Claude's `beads-claim-sync.mjs` emits legacy `bd.claimed`/`bd.closed` hook rows while Pi emits none; these can be mistaken for canonical lifecycle facts even though Beads' `events` table is authoritative.

## SUCCESS
Core documents and tests one runtime-neutral source rule: Beads events are canonical for Claude, Pi, and raw shell mutations; hook rows are compatibility enrichment only or are retired. No consumer can double-count them as source facts.

## SCOPE
Core Beads hook/Pi extension lifecycle integration, focused tests, generated hook assets/registry hashes, and migration notes.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Do not add new lifecycle producers.
- Preserve claim/statusline/memory-gate behavior and fail-open semantics.
- If legacy rows remain, mark them unambiguously as compatibility aliases and define dedupe against Beads event IDs.
- Pi and Claude must follow the same source ownership contract.

## VALIDATION
- Focused Claude/Pi tests prove lifecycle workflow behavior remains intact.
- Contract tests prove aliases cannot masquerade as source events.
- Registry/assets regenerated when hooks change.
notes:
PR #463 OPEN: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/pull/463 — removes duplicate Claude bd.claimed/bd.closed lifecycle diagnostics while preserving claim/statusline/memory behavior; documents Beads events as sole source. Commit 4eb24500. Awaiting CI and orchestrator merge; bead remains open. Full suite had one duration-only flake (19.1s vs 15s) that passed on isolated rerun.
CI GREEN on Core PR #463: CI test, Gitleaks, OSV, Semgrep, and both Socket checks pass. mergeStateStatus=CLEAN. Awaiting orchestrator merge.

title: Publish Beads lifecycle event contract
description:
## PROBLEM
Core's shared contracts package has no schema for the canonical lifecycle rows already emitted by Beads 1.1.0, so xtmux and Console currently encode the shape independently.

## SUCCESS
`@xtrm/contracts` publishes `xtrm.beads.lifecycle-event.v1` as JSON Schema, TypeScript type, runtime validator registration, golden/invalid fixtures, and concise ownership/timestamp/migration documentation.

## SCOPE
`packages/contracts/{schemas,src,fixtures,test,README.md}` and only directly-required workspace metadata.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Beads owns lifecycle facts and source names: created, claimed, updated, closed, reopened, status_changed.
- Contract carries Beads UUIDv7 id, issue_id, actor, old_value/new_value/comment, and created_at as observed.
- Event id is the idempotency key; UUIDv7 milliseconds are authoritative UTC while Beads 1.1.0 created_at is affected by local-time-as-Z serialization.
- No duplicate Claude/Pi producer in this child.
- No new dependency.

## VALIDATION
- Golden and invalid fixtures cover all six lifecycle kinds and required fields.
- Package tests, typecheck, and build pass.
notes:
PR #462 OPEN: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/pull/462 — publishes xtrm.beads.lifecycle-event.v1, UUIDv7 timestamp helper, fixtures, validators, and ownership docs. Commit 57ee1ce9. Awaiting CI and orchestrator merge; bead remains open.
CI GREEN on Core PR #462: CI test, Gitleaks, OSV, Semgrep, and both Socket checks pass. mergeStateStatus=CLEAN. Awaiting orchestrator merge.

title: Fix hook event logging without sqlite3 CLI
description:
## PROBLEM
`.xtrm/hooks/xtrm-logger.mjs` invokes an external `sqlite3` executable. Core now requires Node 24, which already provides `node:sqlite`, but hosts without the CLI silently receive an empty/missing `.xtrm/debug.db` and lose every hook/Beads event.

## SUCCESS
The logger writes the existing `events` schema through Node 24 built-in SQLite, remains fail-open, and works when PATH contains no sqlite3 binary.

## SCOPE
`.xtrm/hooks/xtrm-logger.mjs`, its registry hash/generated ownership metadata, and focused logger/hook tests under `cli/test` or `cli/src/tests`.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not rename event kinds in this bug fix.
- Do not change the events table schema.
- Do not modify consumer repositories.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Keep the hook executable under `node`; do not switch hooks to Bun.
- Use prepared statements for values, WAL, busy_timeout, and silent fail-open handling.
- Preserve worktree/session/runtime/issue/data field semantics.
- No external package.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Regression test runs with sqlite3 absent from PATH and observes a persisted row.
- [ ] Existing hook tests and registry/asset checks pass.
- [ ] Live smoke against a temporary Beads project writes and queries `bd.claimed`.
- [ ] Malformed/unwritable paths do not fail the calling hook.

## OUTPUT
Changed files, compact test evidence, sample row, registry regeneration evidence, and residual compatibility notes.

## LIBRARIES
- Reuse in repo: existing logger schema and callers.
- Installed deps: none.
- Stdlib: `node:sqlite` DatabaseSync (available under required Node >=24).
- New dep candidate: none.
- Roll it: no.
notes: PR #461 opened from stash-recovered WIP + regression tests. Awaiting CI green + merge.
close_reason: PR #461 merged as 40e7b1df. Regression test locks in no-sqlite3-on-PATH persistence. Unblocks xtmux-ck7 (%6353 host-wide beads lifecycle streaming).

title: Canonical Beads lifecycle observability
description:
## PROBLEM
Beads lifecycle activity is split across Core hook debug logging, opt-in xtmux command telemetry, Specialists job correlation, and Console snapshots. Core's hook logger currently shells out to an absent sqlite3 CLI and silently records nothing, while event names disagree (`bd.claimed`/`bd.closed` versus `bd.claim`/`bd.close`).

## SUCCESS
Core owns one documented, runtime-neutral Beads lifecycle event contract; hook logging works on the supported Node 24 runtime without external binaries; Claude and Pi producers emit the same names; xtmux and Console consume/project rather than invent source semantics.

## SCOPE
Core hook logger and Beads lifecycle producers under `.xtrm/hooks/`, Pi extension parity under `packages/pi-extensions/`, generated registry/assets, tests, and ownership documentation. Cross-repo consumer follow-ups may be tracked for xtmux and Console.

## NON_GOALS
- Specialists does not become the owner of Beads state transitions.
- Console snapshot materialization does not become the primary exact-event source.
- No new SQLite dependency or daemon.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Core is the schema/producer owner; xtmux is host-stream transport/projection; Console is reconciliation/materialized read model; Specialists carries bead correlation only.
- Preserve fail-open hook behavior and redact command payloads.
- Canonical events include stable bead, runtime session, tmux origin when available, repo, action, outcome, and timestamp.
- Maintain compatibility aliases or a documented migration for existing `bd.claimed`/`bd.closed` and `bd.claim`/`bd.close` names.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Node 24 built-in SQLite logger works with no sqlite3 executable on PATH.
- [ ] Claude and Pi lifecycle producers pass contract tests for identical names and fields.
- [ ] xtmux/Console integration ownership is documented and tracked.
- [ ] Hook smoke proves events are queryable and failures remain fail-open.

## OUTPUT
Implementation commits/issues with exact event contract, changed files, test commands, sample emitted rows, migration notes, and cross-repo follow-ups.

## LIBRARIES
- Reuse in repo: existing `xtrm-logger.mjs`, Beads hooks, and Pi extensions.
- Installed deps: none required.
- Stdlib: Node 24 `node:sqlite` DatabaseSync.
- New dep candidate: none.
- Roll it: no; supported stdlib covers persistence.
notes:
Discovery: Beads itself is the lifecycle owner via its Dolt events table (UUIDv7 id; event_type created/claimed/updated/closed/reopened/status_changed; actor; old/new values). Core owns projection/enrichment only. Do not create duplicate Claude/Pi lifecycle producers. Canonical stream names are bd.<Beads event_type>; xtmux bd.claim/bd.close are legacy aliases. Beads 1.1.0 created_at has a local-time-as-Z serialization defect, so use UUIDv7 time until upstream is fixed.
