title: cleanSettingsJsonEntries removes only provenance-tagged entries, so legacy per-project hooks survive migration
description:
Root cause of the duplicate-hook symptom investigated in xtrm-1ehjo.

cli/src/commands/migrate.ts:623 cleanSettingsJsonEntries() is the step that is supposed to strip xtrm-owned hook entries from <repo>/.claude/settings.json during the hooks half of 'xt migrate'. Its removal predicate (lines 653-673) drops an entry only when:
  entry._source === 'xtrm-global'   (:662)
  or entry._xtrm has a 'hash' key   (:667)

Both markers are written by the GLOBAL installer. The legacy per-project entries this function needs to remove predate provenance tagging and carry NEITHER. Measured across all 8 consumer projects: every one of the 12-14 hook entries in <repo>/.claude/settings.json has no _source and no _xtrm. So the predicate matches nothing, 'changed' stays false, and the function is a no-op on exactly the input it exists to clean.

Compounding this: ~/.xtrm/known-repos.json shows skillsMigrated:true / hooksMigrated:false for all 8 projects (stamped 2026-07-13), so the hooks phase never ran at all. Fixing the flag without fixing the predicate would still leave the duplication in place.

Suggested ownership proof that does work (implemented in scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs and validated against all 8 projects — 152 registrations, zero false positives):
  an entry is xt-owned-and-redundant iff the same (event, matcher, command) exists in ~/.claude/settings.json after normalising <repo>/.xtrm/hooks -> ~/.xtrm/hooks, AND (when the command names a project hook file) that file is byte-identical to its global counterpart.
Everything else -> preserve. Drift and uncovered entries are explicitly kept.

Durable home for the fix is xt update phase 6 'Claude hook state' per docs/architecture/repair-transaction.md, not a new verb.
notes:
FIX (xtrm-v1yck): ownership proof ported from scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs into
cli/src/core/legacy-hook-dedupe.ts (planLegacyHookDedupe), shared by two call sites:
  - cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts reconcileProjectClaudeHooks() = xt update --apply phase 6
  - cli/src/commands/migrate.ts cleanSettingsJsonEntries() (claude settings only; pi settings keep the provenance predicate)
Predicate: (event, matcher, command) covered by ~/.claude/settings.json after normalising
<repo>/.xtrm/hooks -> ~/.xtrm/hooks, AND byte-identity of the referenced project hook file.
Everything else preserved (xt-owned-drift / xt-owned-uncovered / foreign). Fail-open: unreadable
global settings or missing ~/.xtrm/hooks returns the input map untouched with `skipped` set; never throws.
ReconciliationOutcome shape and phase 6 API unchanged. scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs untouched.

CROSS-VALIDATION vs dedupe script (all 8 consumer projects, real machine state):
  per-project parity exact — console 19/19, core 18/18, specialists 19/19, transcriptoz 19/19,
  vaultctl 19/19, xtmux 19/19, xtmux-release 19/19, xtrm 19/19. TOTAL 151 = 151.
  Divergence vs the 152/2 recorded in xtrm-1ehjo: the script itself now reports 151 planned / 3 preserved.
  ~/dev/core/.xtrm/hooks/beads-claim-sync.mjs drifted from the global copy since PR #460 (PRs #461/#463
  touched the beads/logger hooks), so it is correctly reclassified xt-owned-drift and preserved.
  Nothing to do with this change — both implementations agree on it.

TESTS: cli/src/tests/legacy-hook-dedupe.test.ts (10) covers remove/drift/uncovered/foreign,
matcher sensitivity, partial-wrapper prune, both fail-open paths, and missing project hook file.
claude-runtime-sync-reconcile.test.ts now isolates $HOME — it was implicitly reading the developer's
real ~/.claude/settings.json, which the new prune made load-bearing.
close_reason: phase 6 + xt migrate hooks now use the coverage+byte-identity ownership proof; 151/151 parity with scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs across 8 projects

title: guard: make position-0 slash check provenance-based, not path-based
description: Keep checkPositionZeroSlash on bead-derived (sp render-task) bodies in the role path; keep it off operator --prompt + launcher-generated skill prefixes. Bare has no untrusted composition source (see child .2 — bare --bead is a tag, not a body source), so the guard stays off there permanently and by construction, not by accident.
close_reason: Guard reframed as provenance: fires on bead-derived bodies only. Overruled the epic — PR #439's security argument holds (bead titles are mutable by any beads-store writer). Net gain: role+--prompt '/skill:x' now works, matching bare; bead-title impersonation still rejected.

title: C2: Build identity — xt version --json
description:
## PROBLEM

`xt --version` (commander's -V flag) prints only the semver. Audit
P1-07 asks for structured build identity so operators (and downstream
compatibility checks) can see commit sha, dirty flag, install source
(npm vs local), and node runtime.

## SUCCESS

- `xt version` (new subcommand) prints human-readable identity.
- `xt version --json` prints JSON: {package, version, commit,
  dirty, source, built_at, runtime.node}.
- commander's `xt --version` stays untouched (backcompat).
- Unit test covers both human and JSON output.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/version.ts` (new)
- `cli/src/index.ts` (one `addCommand(createVersionCommand())` line)
- `cli/src/tests/version-command.test.ts` (new)

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT deprecate commander's `-V`/`--version`. It stays.
- Do NOT wire this into a doctor refactor or aggregated diagnostic
  (P1-07 later suggests `xt doctor --json`; separate task).
- Do NOT depend on `sp version --json` or `xtmux version --json` —
  those are upstream, out of this repo.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Version source: `require('../../package.json').version` or the
  packed dist path resolution used elsewhere.
- commit: read from git if repoRoot has .git; else read from
  `dist`-embedded build metadata; else null. Do NOT hard-require git.
- dirty: `git status --porcelain` non-empty; false if no git.
- source: `npm` if repoRoot resolves inside node_modules; else
  `local`.
- built_at: attempt to read a build-timestamp file; else null.
  (Building this into tsup config is a follow-up; for now, null is
  fine.)
- runtime.node: `process.versions.node`.
- Must not crash if git is unavailable — degrade all git-derived
  fields to null.
- Must not spawn any long-running or interactive subprocess.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xt version` prints a human-readable block including version and node.
- [ ] `xt version --json | node -e 'const d=JSON.parse(require(\"fs\").readFileSync(0,\"utf8\")); if (!d.version||!d.runtime.node) process.exit(1)'` exits 0.
- [ ] Unit test asserts JSON shape.
- [ ] `xt --version` still works (regression check).
- [ ] Cli test suite green.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** existing command shape (kleur, commander) —
  copy the pattern from cli/src/commands/status.ts.
- **Stdlib:** node:child_process (spawnSync 'git'), node:fs, node:path.
- **New dep candidate:** none.

## OUTPUT

- New file diffs.
- Sample `xt version` and `xt version --json` output.
- Unit test result.
close_reason: Added cli/src/commands/version.ts with createVersionCommand() + collectVersionInfo() collector. Fields: package (xtrm-tools), version (from cli/package.json workspace-synced), commit (git rev-parse HEAD or null), dirty (git status --porcelain or null), source (npm/local from installRoot path), built_at (cli/dist/index.cjs mtime; reserved for tsup-embed follow-up), runtime.node (process.versions.node). Registered in cli/src/index.ts. Human default output = multi-line kleur block; --json emits single-line envelope. Unit test at cli/src/tests/version-command.test.ts covers 4 cases (collector shape, commander option, --json parse, human output). commander -V/--version untouched — backcompat verified. Smoke: 'xt version' + 'xt version --json' + 'xt --version' all produce expected output.

title: C1: Machine-tested command-deprecation ledger
description:
## PROBLEM

Eight command-level and two option-level deprecations are hardcoded
as free-form strings across cli/src/commands/{bootstrap,clean,pi,
claude,install-pi}.ts. Nothing links them to the CHANGELOG entry
(v0.11.1), and nothing prevents future PRs from drifting one place
without the other (help text, error message, ledger, release notes
all get out of sync).

## SUCCESS

- `docs/command-deprecations.json` — machine-readable ledger with a
  schema_version, and one entry per deprecated command/option token.
- `scripts/check-command-deprecations.mjs` — Node script that reads
  the ledger, greps for every `deprecated`/`retired`/`planned removal`
  string in cli/src/commands/*.ts, and asserts each string maps to
  a ledger entry with a matching `replacement` + `remove_in`.
- CI runs the check.

## SCOPE

- `docs/command-deprecations.json` (new)
- `scripts/check-command-deprecations.mjs` (new)
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (add one step or fold into existing)
- `package.json` (add `check:deprecations` script; consider adding to prepublishOnly)

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT delete or rewrite any existing deprecation string in
  cli/src/commands/*.ts. Ledger merely codifies what's already
  there.
- Do NOT enforce a runtime "check against ledger" on CLI startup.
- Do NOT rewrite the CHANGELOG entry (already shipped v0.11.1).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Node-only script (no jq/bash/python).
- Script must succeed under both source-tree and packed-install
  invocation (uses `fileURLToPath` for repoRoot).
- Ledger schema_version: `xtrm.command-deprecations.v1`.
- Ledger entries must include: `command`, `deprecated_since`,
  `remove_in`, `replacement`, `behavior` (execute-with-warning /
  fail-with-redirect / execute).
- Script matches by SUBSTRING (e.g., `xt clean is deprecated`) so
  the exact wording in code and ledger both survive rewording as
  long as the command token appears verbatim in the ledger entry.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `docs/command-deprecations.json` has 10 entries (8 command + 2 option).
- [ ] `scripts/check-command-deprecations.mjs` exits 0 on green tree.
- [ ] Introducing a fake "xt foo is deprecated" string in a scratch file makes the check exit 1 (manually verify).
- [ ] `npm run check:deprecations` wired.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** none directly; new capability.
- **Stdlib:** node:fs, node:path, node:url — same shape as existing scripts/check-skills-ownership.mjs.
- **New dep candidate:** none.

## OUTPUT

- Diff of new files.
- Command output of `npm run check:deprecations` green.
- List of the 10 ledger entries.
close_reason: Added docs/command-deprecations.json (schema xtrm.command-deprecations.v1, 9 entries covering all 8 command tokens + 2 option tokens seen in cli/src/commands/*.ts). Added scripts/check-command-deprecations.mjs: greps for '<token> is (deprecated|retired) —' pattern in cli/src/commands/**/*.ts, asserts each token has a ledger entry with matching replacement + remove_in. Validator confirmed exit-1 on scratch fake string, exit-0 on green tree. Wired npm run check:deprecations. Slotted into prepublishOnly right after check:skills-ownership (fail fast). Added CI step 'Verify command deprecation ledger' after 'Verify specialists vendor freshness'. Result: bidirectional match (9 ledger entries ↔ 9 code tokens).

   src/manifest.json is un-versioned and has no ownership markers.
   A schema_version + per-entry ownership marker lets tooling reason
   about the manifest and refuse invalid shapes at build time.

## SUCCESS

- `docs/command-deprecations.json` lists every deprecated command
  and option token, with `deprecated_since`, `remove_in`, and
  `replacement` fields.
- `scripts/check-command-deprecations.mjs` scans code for the string

  and fails if any command's message doesn't match a ledger entry
  with the same replacement + removal version.
- `xt version --json` returns valid JSON with all required fields.
- `packages/pi-extensions/src/manifest.json` carries
  `schema_version` and per-entry `ownership` = `xtrm`.
- `scripts/check-pi-extension-manifest.mjs` refuses invalid shapes.
- CI enforces both new check scripts.
- Existing `pi-runtime.ts` manifest consumer keeps working.

## SCOPE

- `docs/command-deprecations.json` (new)
- `scripts/check-command-deprecations.mjs` (new)
- `scripts/check-pi-extension-manifest.mjs` (new)
- `cli/src/commands/version.ts` (new)

- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (add two new check steps under existing "Verify specialists vendor freshness" or a new step)
- `package.json` scripts (add check:* entries; add to prepublishOnly gate list)

## NON_GOALS

  claim by xtrm-3xgs5. Any coordinator-launch work (P0-05) waits.
- Do NOT REMOVE any deprecated command surface — those stay until
  v0.13.0 per operator policy.
- Do NOT hard-fail the CLI on Pi manifest schema mismatch at runtime
  — the check is a build-time gate; production tolerates the old
  shape until we deliberately bump the schema.
- Do NOT introduce runtime-compatibility contracts (P1-06) or
  cross-repo schema packages (P2-02) — separate epic.
- Do NOT modify sp or xtmux behavior in this repo (their build
  identity + schema work is upstream, per audit).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Feature branch: `feature/audit-chunk-2`. Base: main (post-v0.11.1
  merge commit 721e4e2e).
- No regressions: existing CLI test suite green pre/post.
- GitNexus impact analysis required before editing any existing
  symbol (only C2 touches `cli/src/index.ts`; only C3 touches
  `packages/pi-extensions/src/manifest.json` consumed by
  `cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts`).
- Manifest schema changes must remain backwards-compatible: the
  existing consumer (`pi-runtime.ts:33`) must still read
  `active`/`disabled` cleanly with the new fields present.
- All new scripts must be Node-only (no jq / bash / python
  dependency, matching the existing `scripts/*.mjs` style).

  and packed-install invocation (path resolution via `fileURLToPath`).

## VALIDATION

      install --setup — at minimum.

      returns valid JSON.

- [ ] `npm test --workspace cli` green.
- [ ] CI green on the PR.

## OUTPUT

All 3 new validators wired into ci.yml + package.json prepublishOnly. Full test suite green (915 pass). Ready to PR.

title: Open release PR, drive CI green, merge to main
description:
## PROBLEM

After T1..T5 land locally on a release branch, the PR must open,
CI must complete green, and the branch must merge into main so the
operator can tag `v0.11.1` and cut the GitHub release (which fires
publish.yml).

## SUCCESS

- PR opens against main with an audit-aligned title/body citing
  which P0-03 gates each commit closes.
- All CI checks green (CI/test, OSV, Semgrep, Gitleaks, and any
  auto-triggered readiness dispatches).
- PR merged into main.
- Operator handoff message names the two remaining operator actions:
  (a) add `CI / test` to main branch protection required checks,
  (b) tag `v0.11.1` + create GitHub release → publish.yml auto-fires.

## SCOPE

- git push, gh pr create, gh pr merge, gh workflow view.
- No source file changes on the PR itself beyond what T1..T5 produced.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT modify branch protection settings (admin/operator action).
- Do NOT create the git tag or GitHub release (operator action).
- Do NOT run `npm publish` locally.
- Do NOT force-push or amend published commits.
- Do NOT skip hooks or bypass signing.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Branch name: `release/v0.11.1`.
- PR base: `main`.
- Commit style: follow recent convention (e.g. `release: xtrm-tools
  v0.11.1 — meet P0-03 audit gates`).
- If CI red, DIAGNOSE the specific failing check; do not force-merge.
- If merge conflict against main, rebase (not merge-commit).

## VALIDATION

      `CLEAN` sequence.
- [ ] All required checks reported by `gh pr checks` are green.

title: Local dry-run: pack + install-update-ux smoke on 0.11.1 candidate
description:

release commit" and "Node 24 build reproducibility verified" BEFORE

  dist).
- `npm pack` produces `xtrm-tools-0.11.1.tgz`.

  prints `install-update-ux-smoke: PASS`.
- `npm test --workspace cli` green.

  prepublishOnly (dry-run each without triggering publish).

## SCOPE

- May write ephemeral files under `/tmp` and `<scratchpad>`.

## NON_GOALS

  tag/release AFTER merge.
- Do NOT push a tag from this task.

## CONSTRAINTS

  verify with `node -v` before starting.
- Do not run this in a worktree; from CLAUDE.md gotcha,
  `cli/dist/` gets contaminated by worktree builds. Run from the
  main repo root (or the release branch checked out there).
- Cleanup `/tmp/xtrm-tools-*.tgz` at end.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `node -v` starts with `v24.`.
- [ ] `git diff --exit-code cli/dist/` empty after `npm ci && npm run build`.

- [ ] `npm run check:package && npm run check:skills-ownership && npm run gen-registry && npm run check:registry-pack-parity && npm run check:payload-hygiene && npm run check:specialists-vendor && npm run check:layout-guards && npm run check:gitnexus-no-counter && npm run check:skills-symlinks` all exit 0.

## LIBRARIES

## OUTPUT

- Terminal transcript summary of each command's exit status.
- Any warnings or unexpected output flagged for reviewer.
- Green/red verdict; if red, escalate rather than mutate to fix.

All 8 check:* gates green (check:package, skills-ownership, specialists-vendor, payload-hygiene (452 packed files), layout-guards, gitnexus-no-counter, skills-symlinks, changelog:update). npm pack produced xtrm-tools-0.11.1.tgz. install-update-ux-smoke on that tarball: PASS on all four assertions (packed resolver, help/retired-token matrix, owned-only cleanup and preservation, command output redaction). Full CLI test suite: 910/910 non-skipped tests pass in isolation; 1 flake surfaced under full-suite load (worktree-session-role.test.ts wait-for handshake timing) that passed cleanly on isolated re-run — same systemic flake class as main's current init-cli.test.ts flake, unrelated to release changes. Proceeding to PR.

title: Wire packed-install smoke into pre-publish-readiness + publish workflows
description:
## PROBLEM

`scripts/install-update-ux-smoke.mjs` was added in PR #445 but is
not invoked by any GitHub Actions workflow. The audit's P0-02 flags
it as a smoke harness that must be wired into the release pipeline
before the next release can be called "gated".

## SUCCESS

- `pre-publish-readiness.yml` runs the smoke against a freshly packed
  tarball, before printing "safe to tag and release".
- `publish.yml` runs the smoke against the freshly packed tarball
  BEFORE the `npm publish` step — so a broken release never reaches
  npm even if a human tag/release fires.
- Smoke step is additive; the existing `fresh_machine_smoke`
  release-contract job stays exactly as it is.

## SCOPE

- `.github/workflows/pre-publish-readiness.yml`
- `.github/workflows/publish.yml`

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT wire smoke into `ci.yml` for every PR — audit says smoke
  stays "harness, not enforced gate" for PR CI until follow-up.
- Do NOT edit `scripts/install-update-ux-smoke.mjs`.
- Do NOT modify `fresh-machine-smoke.yml` — the two are different
  contracts (release-contract vs. packaged-install UX).
- Do NOT reorder existing steps in `publish.yml`; only ADD the smoke
  step at the correct place (after pack-parity, before publish).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Smoke must run against the ACTUAL tarball that will be published
  (not `npm pack --dry-run` output). Use `npm pack --json`, extract
  filename, pass path to the smoke script.
- Runner: `ubuntu-latest` matches the rest of the release chain.
- Node 24.x: reuse existing `setup-node@v4` step in each workflow.
- The smoke script exits 0 on pass, non-zero on fail — failure must
  fail the workflow job.
- Preserve the workflow's existing permissions block; do not widen.
- Steps must remain YAML-valid; run `python -c 'import yaml; yaml.safe_load(open(f))'` on each modified file if a linter isn't available.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `pre-publish-readiness.yml` diff shows one new step invoking `node scripts/install-update-ux-smoke.mjs <tarball>` after the pack step.
- [ ] `publish.yml` diff shows the same, positioned AFTER `check:registry-pack-parity` / `check:asset-contract` and BEFORE `npm publish`.
- [ ] Both YAML files parse cleanly.
- [ ] Manual dispatch of `pre-publish-readiness.yml` on the release branch reaches the smoke step and prints PASS.
- [ ] No existing step or job is removed or renamed.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** `scripts/install-update-ux-smoke.mjs` (added in
  PR #445) — the entire behavior lives there; workflows are wiring.
- **Installed deps:** `actions/setup-node@v4`, `actions/checkout@v4`
  (already used).
- **New dep candidate:** none.

## OUTPUT

- Unified diff of both workflow files.
- Link to the pre-publish-readiness dispatch run showing the new step green.
close_reason: Added 'Pack for install-update UX smoke' + 'Install-update UX smoke on packed tarball' steps to both pre-publish-readiness.yml (after existing npm pack --dry-run) and publish.yml (after Check asset contract, before npm publish). Additive gates — fresh_machine_smoke job untouched. YAML validates clean. If smoke fails, publish blocked. Skipped ci.yml PR wiring per audit ('smoke stays harness, not enforced gate') for follow-up.

title: Pin prepublishOnly vendor step to specialists-source.json ref
description:
## PROBLEM

`package.json` `prepublishOnly` hardcodes:

    node scripts/vendor-specialists-skills.mjs --specialists-package specialists --specialists-ref master

This re-vendors from a MOVING `master` ref at publish time,
overwriting the reviewed snapshot in `.xtrm/skills/default/` that
the release commit was tested against. Audit P1-12 flags this as a
release-integrity violation.

## SUCCESS

- `prepublishOnly` reads `.xtrm/specialists-source.json` at publish
  time and re-vendors using the recorded ref (immutable
  `resolved_sha` preferred over `ref`).
- Publishing after the T1 refresh vendors against v3.21.0 — the same
  ref recorded in the release commit.
- No new file added — inline shell resolver kept small; or, if a
  helper script fits better, add ONE tiny helper.

## SCOPE

- `package.json` `scripts.prepublishOnly` (single string).

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT change any other prepublishOnly gate order.
- Do NOT remove the `--specialists-package specialists` hint (the
  script's fallback path resolution uses it when local checkout is
  absent).
- Do NOT touch `scripts/vendor-specialists-skills.mjs` internals.
- Do NOT create a new npm script unless the inline shell becomes
  unreadable.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The resolver must handle both cases: (a)
  `.xtrm/specialists-source.json` has `resolved_sha` → use it; (b)
  only `ref` present → use it. If both empty, exit non-zero with a
  clear message.
- Must remain a single npm script line (composable via `&&`).
- Must not depend on `jq` being present unless every CI env has it —
  publish.yml already uses `jq`, so it's safe there. Prefer `node
  -p "require('./.xtrm/specialists-source.json').source.resolved_sha || require('./.xtrm/specialists-source.json').source.ref"`
  for portability.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm pkg get scripts.prepublishOnly` shows no `--specialists-ref master` literal.
- [ ] `bash -c "$(npm pkg get scripts.prepublishOnly | tr -d '"')"` — dry evaluation resolves to a valid `v3.21.0` command when run at repo root after T1.
- [ ] Local `npm run prepublishOnly` (after T1) completes without diffing `.xtrm/skills/default/` — proving the recorded ref round-trips.
- [ ] Nothing else in `prepublishOnly` gate order changed.

## LIBRARIES

- **Stdlib:** `node -p` for JSON extraction (already used elsewhere in
  this repo's scripts). No jq dependency added.
- **New dep candidate:** none.

## OUTPUT

- Before/after snippet of the prepublishOnly string.
- Command output of dry-eval + local prepublishOnly run.
close_reason: Added scripts/vendor-specialists-from-manifest.mjs — 30-line wrapper that reads .xtrm/specialists-source.json, prefers source.resolved_sha over source.ref, forwards to vendor-specialists-skills.mjs, and restores human-readable source.ref after regeneration (vendor script overwrites ref with the sha we pass in). Idempotent: re-run produces no diff. package.json prepublishOnly replaced 'node scripts/vendor-specialists-skills.mjs --specialists-package specialists --specialists-ref master' → 'node scripts/vendor-specialists-from-manifest.mjs'. Publish can no longer silently overwrite the reviewed vendor snapshot from a moving master ref.

title: Refresh vendored specialists to v3.21.0 (immutable tag)
description:
## PROBLEM

`.xtrm/specialists-source.json` pins specialists at `master@50d715b2`
(a floating sha resolved from `master` when last vendored). Latest
released specialists tag is `v3.21.0`; the audit's P1-12 requires the
reviewed release commit contain the immutable ref, not a moving
`master` snapshot that a `prepublishOnly` re-vendor could silently

  `source.resolved_sha` = the sha of the v3.21.0 tag.

  parity checks all green.

- `.xtrm/specialists-source.json` (regenerated by

## CONSTRAINTS

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `jq -r .source.ref .xtrm/specialists-source.json` prints `v3.21.0`.

- [ ] `npm run check:skills-ownership` exits 0.
- [ ] `npm run gen-registry && git diff --exit-code -- .xtrm/registry.json` — either no change, or regenerated hashes match the vendored files.
- [ ] `npm run check:registry-pack-parity` exits 0.

## LIBRARIES

N/A — invocation of existing `scripts/vendor-specialists-skills.mjs`
and existing `check:*` npm scripts. No new files, no new deps.

## OUTPUT

- Diff summary: `.xtrm/specialists-source.json` before/after + list of
  changed files under `.xtrm/skills/default/`.
- Command outputs proving each VALIDATION checkbox.
- Handoff line: "Vendor refresh green, ready for T2/T3 to build on."
close_reason: Vendored specialists refreshed to v3.21.0. .xtrm/specialists-source.json records ref=v3.21.0 resolved_sha=22573c64. Vendored SKILL.md content already matched between master@50d715b2 and v3.21.0 (no .xtrm/skills/default/ diff). All validation gates green: check:specialists-vendor OK, check:skills-ownership OK, verify-asset-contract PASS. Note: local check:registry-pack-parity trips because ~/.xtrm/skills/default/gitnexus/ is gitignored (runtime artifacts) but present on my dev box, unrelated to this task — CI won't see it.

title: release: xtrm-tools v0.11.1 — meet P0-03 audit gates
description:
## PROBLEM

npm ships `xtrm-tools 0.11.0` (2026-07-16) but main is 19 PRs ahead
with material behavior: packaged Pi config resolver, Pi extension
ownership manifest, ownership-safe cleanup, unconditional Pi
reconciliation on `xt update --apply`, retired-command guards, the
consolidated `init/update/doctor/migrate` surface, and the Node 24
LTS baseline (PRs #433–#452).

The 20 July 2026 audit (~/dev/11.md, sections R-01..R-08 + P0-03)
identifies six release-integrity gaps that must close before shipping
the next patch:

1. Functional tests are not a required branch-protection check on main
   (only OSV/Semgrep/Gitleaks are).
2. `scripts/install-update-ux-smoke.mjs` was added in #445 but is not
   wired into any workflow.
3. Vendored specialists is pinned to a floating `master` sha
   (50d715b2, pre-v3.21.0); `prepublishOnly` re-vendors from `master`
   again at publish time, silently replacing the reviewed snapshot.
4. CHANGELOG `[Unreleased]` has one line; 19 merged PRs need

title: xt update --apply --force destroys .xtrm/registry.json hooks section
description:
## Symptom
Running \`xt update --apply --force\` from /home/dawid/dev/core dropped the entire \`hooks\` asset section from \`.xtrm/registry.json\`.

Before (1419 lines): assets.hooks = { source_dir, install_mode: copy, install_scope: global, files: {all 26 beads-*/quality-check-*/statusline.mjs hashes+versions} }

After (6 lines total): assets = {} — hooks section missing entirely.

## Reproduction
1. cd to xtrm-tools source repo with intact .xtrm/registry.json
2. xt update --apply --force
3. git diff .xtrm/registry.json → hooks section deleted

## Impact
- Every downstream install that reads registry.json now skips hook copying → target project's .xtrm/hooks/ never gets populated
- install-integration test suite fails 3/8 because expected tmpDir/.xtrm/hooks/beads-edit-gate.mjs doesn't exist after runInstall
- Real user impact: xt init/install into fresh repos silently ships without hooks

## Discovered during
xtrm-on2mk cleanup. After restoring registry.json from git, install-integration went 3-fail → 8/8 pass; runInstall correctly scaffolded hooks again.

## Suspected root cause
gen-registry logic during \`xt update --apply --force\` likely skips assets whose payload it can't classify under the new global-skills/hooks layout — but instead of preserving them, it drops the entire section. Bug is in either \`npm run gen-registry\` (scripts/gen-registry.mjs) or the update.ts registry-refresh path.

## Non-blocking on
Pre-existing (main HEAD) test failures in pi-runtime-safeguards.test.ts and registry.test.ts assert paths like /home/dawid/dev/packages/... (missing "core") — likely stale hardcoded paths, separate bead.
close_reason: Fixed by guarding the snapshot write in installFromRegistry when packageRoot === installRepoRoot (source-repo case). Root cause: xtrm-ya2i's registry snapshot logic, combined with createProjectRegistrySnapshot filtering under XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS mode, stripped all global-scoped assets from the source registry when 'xt update --apply [--force]' ran from the source repo. Regression test added in registry-scaffold.test.ts. Verified against real repo: registry byte-identical to backup after both --apply and --apply --force.

title: align core repo to Node 24 LTS (CI + engines + .nvmrc)
description:
## PROBLEM

Core repo pins Node 22.x across 7 CI workflow files while:

- specialists repo pins Node 24 (package-payload.yml)

- `cli/dist/index.cjs` rebuilt with Node 24 + npm ci so CI's dist-freshness check passes on the first push
- No production behavior change; strictly infrastructure/tooling alignment

## SCOPE

Files to change:
- `.github/workflows/ci.yml` (matrix: `[22.x]` → `[24.x]`)
- `.github/workflows/specialists-validation.yml` (`22.x` → `24.x`)

title: executor: make xt clean ownership-safe on current layouts
description:
## PROBLEM

`xt clean` advertises canonical hook/skill cleanup but scans retired `~/.xtrm/skills/active` and deletes every unknown file under user-owned `~/.claude/hooks`. Current managed hooks live under `~/.xtrm/hooks`/project `.xtrm/hooks`; unknown Claude hook files may be user-owned. The command also ends by recommending nonexistent `xtrm install all -y`.

## SUCCESS

Cleanup operates only on provably xtrm-owned legacy/retired artifacts, preserves unknown user hooks and skills, uses current registry/ownership helpers, and points to the canonical repair path. Its eventual merge/deprecation can proceed without a data-loss hazard.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/clean.ts::{cleanHooks,cleanSkills,createCleanCommand}`.
- Reuse boundaries in `cli/src/core/plugin-era-cleanup.ts`, `registry-scaffold.ts`, current hook roots/registry, and relevant clean/plugin cleanup tests.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not delete unknown files merely because they are not in a hard-coded current list.
- Do not broaden cleanup outside xtrm-owned hook/skill/runtime artifacts.
- Do not perform the final public-command consolidation in this safety fix.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Proposed minimal fix: delegate known legacy removal to existing ownership-aware cleanup/prune helpers and remove the retired active-layout scanner/hard-coded unknown-file deletion.
- Default/dry-run/apply output must distinguish managed removal from preserved unknown assets.
- Preserve confirmation before mutation; never log file contents, secrets, or user payloads.
- Emit a structured or deterministic cleanup outcome usable by tests; follow existing JSONL conventions if an existing cleanup log is available rather than inventing one.
- SCRUTINY: high — destructive filesystem boundary and user-owned data preservation.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unknown custom `~/.claude/hooks/custom.*` survives dry-run and apply.
- [ ] Known xtrm-owned plugin-era hook/cache artifacts are detected and removed.
- [ ] Retired active links are removed only when ownership/target is provable; arbitrary directories are preserved.

- [ ] Output uses the canonical repair command, not `install all`.
- [ ] Targeted tests, temp-HOME smoke, typecheck, build, and negative-path permission/error test pass.

- **Installed deps:** `fs-extra` already used.
- **Stdlib:** temp HOME/process smoke.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, before/after ownership matrix, user-file preservation proof, removal/error telemetry samples, targeted tests/build/smoke evidence, and remaining cleanup surfaces intentionally excluded.

2. Run `xt clean` and confirm mutation.

title: executor: make xt update reconcile Pi state when registry is current
description:
## PROBLEM

`xt update --apply` runs full `runInstall`/Pi reconciliation only when registry files drift. On an otherwise current repo it assures global npm packages and applies the external tool patch, but it does not repair project Pi package registration/settings, themes, stale global extension symlinks, conflicting `pi-dex`, legacy extension copies, or retired skills entries. Fleet-state defects can therefore survive the advertised routine update path.

## SUCCESS

Every applied single-repo/fleet update executes the canonical per-repo Pi reconciliation exactly once, even when registry hashes are current, and reports whether it repaired runtime state. Global package assurance remains bounded rather than repeated unnecessarily across fleet targets.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/update.ts::{updateRepo,createUpdateCommand}`.
- Existing `runInstall`, `runPiInstall`, and `runPiRuntimeSync` seams only as needed to return/consume reconciliation outcomes without duplicate work.
- `cli/src/tests/update.test.ts`, Pi runtime tests, and one temp-repo update smoke.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not redesign Pi package management or change first-time credential setup.
- Do not run machine bootstrap on routine repo update.
- Do not multiply global package/network calls once per fleet repo.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Proposed behavior: applied update always performs canonical project Pi reconcile; if registry refresh already invoked it, do not invoke it twice.
- Preserve update dry-run, `--all-repos`, commit behavior, strict registry handling, and project Claude hook reconciliation.
- Return structured changed/failed evidence so `already-current` is not printed after a runtime repair.
- Keep global package assurance/external patch at a single bounded point per invocation.
- Use existing bootstrap/skills logs and redacted stdout; do not log settings contents or credentials.
- SCRUTINY: high. `updateRepo` is LOW itself, but the shared `runPiRuntimeSync` path is CRITICAL and affects init/install/Pi reload.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Current-registry + stale `.pi/settings.json` is repaired by `update --apply`.
- [ ] Current-registry + retired/global stale Pi extension artifacts is reconciled without registry drift.
- [ ] Registry-drift update invokes full Pi reconciliation once, not twice.
- [ ] Fleet update performs global package assurance at most once per command invocation.
- [ ] Dry-run writes nothing and reports pending runtime repair.
- [ ] Failure result/exit code and redacted logs identify Pi reconciliation failure.
- [ ] Targeted update/Pi tests, typecheck, build, and temp-repo CLI smoke pass.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** `runInstall`, `runPiInstall`, `runPiRuntimeSync`, and existing update result table.
- **Installed deps:** none.
- **Stdlib:** existing filesystem/temp process tools.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** no — route through the existing canonical reconcile seam.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, call-count evidence for drift/current/fleet cases, GitNexus receipt, test/build/smoke output, sample redacted update rows, and residual network/performance trade-offs.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Use a repo whose `.xtrm/registry.json` hashes are current but whose `.pi/settings.json` or legacy Pi artifacts are stale.
2. Run `xt update --apply --repo <repo>`.
3. Observe `updateRepo` skips `runInstall` when `registryChanges` is false, so only global package assurance/external patch run and project Pi drift remains.

## Acceptance Criteria

All VALIDATION checks pass; applied update reconciles current and drifted repos exactly once and reports the runtime outcome.
close_reason: Implemented current-registry Pi reconciliation with structured runtime outcomes; targeted update/Pi tests pass, direct temp-output build passes, standard build/typecheck remain blocked by existing worktree guard/pre-existing test errors.

title: executor: unify Pi extension ownership across setup and package modes
description:
## PROBLEM

The secondary global/setup path still selects passive `pi-serena-compact`, expects nonexistent `extensions/core`, and omits current active `serena-pool`, `sp-terminal-overlay`, and `xtprompt`; package mode uses the newer registry. Global/setup and package modes select the same current set: `quality-gates` remains explicitly disabled; `pi-serena-compact` and `core` are not treated as active extension directories; `serena-pool`, `sp-terminal-overlay`, and `xtprompt` are included.

- Pi registry/runtime parity tests and package runtime smoke.

title: feat(cli): split bare from role launch path; drop position-0 slash guard
description:
## PROBLEM

PR #433 (xtmux-r6g.6) shipped bare `xt claude/pi --prompt "..."` by
threading a nullable `role?` through the existing role-launch machinery
(`buildRoleTmuxPlan`, `launchRoleTmuxSession`, buffered tmux transport).
Three concrete symptoms:

1. **Position-0 `/` blocker.** `checkPositionZeroSlash`
   (`cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:485+`) rejects any turn-1 body
   whose byte 0 is `/` unless the sp trusted skill prefix precedes it.
   `xt claude worker --prompt "/multiplexing take bead X"` fails today
   with a scary "runtime would parse untrusted text as a slash-command"
   error, even though `claude "/multiplexing take bead X"` at the shell
   works fine. This defeats the whole point of bare mode. The guard
   also fires on role-mode bead titles starting with `/` — same fix
   applies.
2. **Bare is bolted onto role plumbing.** `buildRoleTmuxPlan(role?:
   ResolvedRole, sessionSlug?: string)` with a runtime `if (!role &&
   !sessionSlug) throw` is a type-system-should-express-this smell.
   Every internal `if (role)` and `role?.X` is proof the function does
   two jobs. Same in `launchRoleTmuxSession`, and the launcher gate
   `if (resolvedRole || prompt || model || thinking ||
   explicitSkillPaths.length > 0 || !attach || opts.newSession)` at
   `worktree-session.ts:1231` is a five-way OR that pretends bare and
   role are one launch.
3. **Buffered tmux transport for tiny bare payloads.** A 20-byte
   `--prompt "hi"` runs through `buildBufferedRuntimeCommand()` +
   `tmux load-buffer` + two `wait-for` sync-points + a consumer wrapper
   subprocess (`worktree-session.ts:1487-1546`). That handshake exists
   for 50-1000KB role prompts past shell argv limits; for bare it's
   four unnecessary sync-points.

## SUCCESS

- `xt claude worker --prompt "/multiplexing take bead X and do Y"`
  launches cleanly and Claude Code starts with `/multiplexing …` as
  the first user turn.
- `xt claude worker --bead <id>` (no `--role`) works: `sp render-task`
  composes the initial prompt; auto-prepends `/<skill-name>\n\n` for
  each explicit `--skill` because there is no `/skill` line the
  operator can inject when the body is a rendered bead task.
- `xt pi worker --skill multiplexing --prompt "..."` verifies that
  `--skill <path>` is actually pushed to pi's argv in bare mode (spot
  check: PR #437's audit claims it's silently ignored, but the code at
  `worktree-session.ts:659` looks like it does push — verify and fix
  either the code or the doc claim).
- `xt claude worker --prompt "hi" -- --add-dir ~/notes --model claude-opus-4-8`
  works: `--` passthrough available in bare, gated by the existing
  `guardRolePassthrough` (rejects `--session-dir` / `--name` /
  `--system-prompt` / `--append-system-prompt` / `--skill`;
  warn-and-drop `--print` / `--list-models` / `--export` / `--mode`).
- Position-0 `/` blocker removed in both bare AND role paths (no
  safety story it buys: operator controls bead title at creation).
- `buildRoleTmuxPlan` has a typed non-optional `role: ResolvedRole`;
  new `buildBareTmuxPlan` handles the bare shape. `launchWorktreeSession`
  picks one at the top on `roleName` presence.
- Bare uses plain `tmux new-session -d -s <name> -c <cwd> -e <env>
  <runtime> <args>` when the composed argv fits comfortably (below
  some threshold, say 64KB). Buffered transport kept as a fallback
  above that threshold, or (simpler) kept only in the role path where
  large system prompts are the norm.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts` — split builders, unbolt the
  else-branch, drop position-0 slash guard in both paths, lift bare
  guards on `--bead` and `-- passthrough` at `worktree-session.ts:963`.
- `cli/src/commands/{claude,pi}.ts` — update help text: remove
  "Passthrough requires --role" and any "With --role: ..." qualifiers
  that no longer hold; update examples.
- `cli/src/tests/worktree-session-*.test.ts` — new tests for bare
  `--prompt "/name args"`, bare `--bead`, bare `-- passthrough`, bare
  `--skill` on both runtimes.
- `cli/dist/index.cjs` — rebuild.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not touch the `--role` specialist system-prompt / `--no-skills` /
  trusted-prefix wiring. That path stays exactly as it is.
- Do not add a new backwards-compat flag or "legacy bare mode" switch.
  Simple change; do it once.
- No new deps.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve pane options (`@agent_task`, `@agent_state`,
  `@agent_parent_session`, `@agent_bead`) in bare mode — xtmux picker
  and safe-send-pointer depend on them.
- Preserve `--no-attach` stdout contract (`session_name:pane_id`).
- Preserve session-name shape `<runtime>-<slug>` for bare and
  `role-<runtime>-<slug>[-<bead>]` for role.
- Byte ceiling check stays in both paths — real argv/OS limit.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `xt claude bare-test --no-attach --prompt "/multiplexing hello"`
      succeeds; attach and confirm Claude starts with `/multiplexing`
      as first turn.
- [ ] `xt pi bare-test --no-attach --skill multiplexing --prompt "hi"`
      succeeds and pi's argv contains `--skill <resolved-path>`
      (capture via strace or pi's own boot log).
- [ ] `xt claude bare-test --no-attach --bead <id> --skill multiplexing`
      succeeds; first turn is `/multiplexing\n\n<rendered bead task>`.
- [ ] `xt claude bare-test --no-attach --prompt "hi" -- --add-dir ~/x`
      succeeds; disallowed passthrough (e.g. `-- --session-dir /tmp`)
      still errors with the guard message.
- [ ] `xt pi role-test --role chain-coordinator --bead <id>` still
      works exactly as before.
- [ ] `npm test --workspace cli` green.
- [ ] `tsc --noEmit` green.
- [ ] `xt claude --help` and `xt pi --help` no longer imply
      passthrough / `--bead` need `--role`.

## LIBRARIES

None. Pure refactor + guard drop.

## OUTPUT

One PR that supersedes both #436 and #437. Bead notes carry the PR
URL. After merge, file a doc-refresh bead to correct Pattern 2b in
`multiplexing/SKILL.md` against the new surface, and close #436 /
#437 with a `superseded by <new-PR>` comment.
notes:
DELIVERED — PR #459 open, CI 6/6 green, MERGEABLE/CLEAN. Epic left OPEN per orchestrator instruction (awaiting merge greenlight). memory-ack already set.

PR: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/pull/459  (commit 9d50a9fd)

CHILDREN — all closed: .1 guard provenance | .2 builder split | .3 bare transport | .4 gate lift | .5 tests+docs. Follow-up .6 filed (roleless sp render-task, P3).

DIVERGENCES FROM BEAD (2, both deliberate):
1. Position-0 guard KEPT in the role path, against the SUCCESS bullet. Bead titles are mutable post-creation by any beads-store writer and sp render-task pulls the title into turn 1; dropping the guard makes the beads store a slash-command injection channel for zero benefit. Rekeyed on body PROVENANCE instead: fires on bead-derived bodies, never on operator --prompt. This delivers MORE than the bead asked — 'xt claude --role r --prompt "/multiplexing ..."' now works too, which the uniform guard had been blocking.
2. Bare --bead is metadata-only (@agent_bead/XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD/picker preview), not an sp render-task composition. 'sp render-task <name> --bead <id>' requires the specialist name positionally — no roleless render exists, so the bead's bullet had no implementation path. Side benefit: bare keeps zero untrusted turn-1 sources, making the absent guard there safe by construction. Follow-up .6 tracks the upstream change if the literal behavior is still wanted.

FINDING — bead SUCCESS bullet on pi bare --skill: the CODE WAS ALREADY CORRECT; PR #437's audit claim was wrong. Proved live via tmux #{pane_start_command}: 'pi' '--skill' '/home/dawid/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md' 'hi there'. Doc fixed, code untouched.

DRIVE-BY: fixed a PRE-EXISTING 'tsc --noEmit' failure on main (PR #439's tests pass a sessionSlug prop absent from WorktreeSessionOptions, + 3 implicit-any). npm run typecheck was red on main before this branch.

VALIDATION: all 8 boxes satisfied. 923 tests pass / 0 fail; tsc green; 9 repo check:* scripts green; CI dist-freshness simulated byte-exact before pushing (cli/dist cannot be built from a .xtrm worktree — see memory key cli-dist-build-from-worktree). Live smokes covered bare slash-prompt, pi --skill argv, bare --bead, passthrough accept+reject, and a role regression confirming the buffered transport is retained. All smoke sessions/worktrees/branches and orphaned serena MCP processes cleaned up.
close_reason: Wave 3 primary: PR #459 merged as a892a20a. Provenance-keyed slash guard (agreed with #439 defense-in-depth over bead's proposed drop); buildRole/buildBare split; bare direct tmux transport; bare --bead metadata-only. All 5 children closed. Fixed pre-existing tsc red gate on main as drive-by. Follow-up xtrm-3xgs5.6 (P3) tracks roleless sp render-task.

title: Fix PR #422 HIGH fileless transport security findings
description:
## PROBLEM
Exact security audit d12689 on PR #422 head 2a17992f returned FAIL/HIGH: rendered bead/role content remains in runtime argv; server-global tmux buffer is readable/mutable/persistent across peers; generic /skill prefix guard does not prove provenance. Operator explicitly authorizes a narrow HIGH-risk correction while preserving the accepted fileless launcher refactor.

## REQUIRED INVARIANTS
Preserve sp-owned turn-one force loading at byte 0: Pi `/skill:<name>` and Claude `/skill-<name>`, for declared/validated skills only, before untrusted task body. Preserve full sp render-task semantics; no compact pointer that drops dependencies/memories/rules. Do not restore role prompt/task files, append-system-prompt-file task transport, plugin scaffolds, or generated context files.

## SCOPE
On PR #422 branch after 2a17992f, first verify actual Pi and Claude interactive input surfaces and the OS/tmux trust boundary. Implement the smallest private fileless transport supported by both runtimes (anonymous pipe/inherited FD/memfd/stdin/PTY as actually supported), with one-shot authenticated framing, deterministic cleanup and no sensitive body in child argv, environment, tmux server-global buffers, process list, or persistent filesystem. Bind accepted slash prefix exactly to trusted sp output/declared skill metadata; hostile bead text beginning `/skill:*` or `/skill-*` must fail before worktree creation. Cover current-pane and new-session paths.

## CONSTRAINTS
HIGH scope authorized by operator after warning. TDD and adversarial proof required. No rebase/reset/force-push/PR merge/npm publish/global deployment/live ~/.xtrm mutation/anchor closure. No new dependency unless existing Node/tmux/runtime primitives demonstrably cannot support the contract; escalate before adding one. Do not claim security from random names or same-user assumptions without proving the documented trust boundary. If neither runtime supports a private fileless initial-turn channel, STOP with evidence rather than reviving files or weakening the task contract.

## VALIDATION
Process observer proves no canary in argv/environment. Hostile tmux peer attempts list/read/overwrite/delete/retain and cannot observe or alter payload. Kill/error/signal before/during consume leaves no payload. NUL/Unicode/oversize/framing tests; exact prefix provenance tests; 100KB full rendered bead byte-for-byte first-turn smoke for Pi and Claude where available; current-pane/new-session parity; full targeted/CLI/build/typecheck/registry gates isolated under /tmp; live ~/.xtrm managed hashes unchanged. GitNexus impact and detect_changes. Push normal fast-forward to xt/luho, fresh CI, then independent security re-audit and reviewer.

## OUTPUT
Design evidence, threat-boundary proof, exact files/tests, new head, CI/threads. Close only this implementation child after push/local proof; parent handles review, thread resolution and merge.
notes:
BLOCKED — required STOP condition reached before coding. No supported common private fileless initial-turn channel exists for current Pi 0.80.6 + Claude Code 2.1.210 while preserving interactive TUI, exact byte-zero skill commands, current-pane/new-session parity, and a hostile shared-tmux-peer boundary.

EXACT RUNTIME / DOC EVIDENCE
- Pi 0.80.6 source `dist/main.js`: non-TTY stdin selects print mode (`resolveAppMode`); piped stdin is read only as print input. Actual isolated run with anonymous stdin + PI_STARTUP_BENCHMARK exited 1: `PI_STARTUP_BENCHMARK only supports interactive mode`.
- Pi `@file` processing is not a raw initial turn: anonymous pipe `/proc/self/fd/N` is skipped because pipe stat size is 0; memfd is read but wrapped as `<file name="/proc/self/fd/N">\n...\n</file>`, so trusted `/skill:<name>` is not at byte 0.
- Pi RPC/SDK can accept private stdin/in-process prompts, but RPC is headless and SDK would require replacing the shipped interactive CLI/UI; it is not the accepted interactive launcher surface.
- Claude Code 2.1.210 help documents `--input-format` as print-only. Actual isolated stream-json runs, with and without explicit `--print`, emitted the same headless stream-json init and no interactive TUI.
- Claude positional `@/proc/self/fd/N` does not read the descriptor: local captured API request contained the literal text `@/proc/self/fd/4`.
- Claude SDK one-shot async stdin is documented for `--print`/stream-json, not interactive mode.

OS / TMUX EXPERIMENTS (all HOME/XDG/TMPDIR isolated under /tmp)
- Anonymous inherited FD through tmux failed with `EBADF` in both a brand-new tmux server and an already-running server: tmux closes extra client FDs before the pane command. memfd has the same inheritance barrier.
- Direct PTY injection can privately reach current-pane interactive mode: an anonymous pipe into `script(1)` delivered synthetic canaries to actual Pi and Claude TUIs; local fake API captures contained the canaries while runtime/wrapper argv and environment did not. This only proves current-pane feasibility.
- New-session has no equivalent private writer. tmux `new-session` exposes only shell-command/environment; `send-keys` exposes payload in client argv/server control; `load-buffer` is server-global; `pipe-pane -I` starts a server-owned shell and cannot inherit the launcher's FD.
- Hostile same-server peer proof: second client used `send-keys` to append `HOSTILE-SUFFIX` before submit and `capture-pane` read both `ORIGINAL-PRIVATE-TURN` and tamper. Therefore PTY delivery inside the shared tmux server cannot satisfy confidentiality or integrity against the required hostile peer.

CONCLUSION
- Anonymous pipe/stdin: private only in non-interactive/headless modes, or via direct PTY current-pane wrapper.
- Inherited FD/memfd: no raw-user-prompt consumer common to both runtimes; tmux drops descriptors.
- PTY: works directly for current pane, cannot cross new-session tmux privately and is observable/mutable by a hostile peer.
- No stdlib/native common channel satisfies SEC-422-1/2 plus current-pane/new-session parity. Implementing a socket/token bridge would put token in argv/env or rely on same-user secrecy; adding a PTY/native dependency or replacing both TUIs would violate scope and requires escalation.
- Per contract, SEC-422-3 was not partially edited after transport infeasibility was proven. No fallback, file transport, plugin scaffold, compact bead pointer, dependency, code edit, commit, or push was made.

STATE / REQUIRED EXTERNAL DECISION
- Branch remains clean at 2a17992f243208179f64cdc7e0fb0445347356a5; remote xt/luho unchanged.
- Live ~/.xtrm: 1176 entries before/after; zero added/removed and zero non-log changes. Only append-only logs/2026-07-15.jsonl changed.
- Unblock requires one explicit contract/runtime change: (a) Pi and Claude add a supported interactive `--prompt-fd`/equivalent; (b) drop shared-tmux hostile-peer/new-session parity and permit current-pane PTY only; (c) accept headless RPC/SDK surfaces instead of native interactive TUIs; or (d) authorize a different persisted/file-backed trust boundary. Current contract forbids all available choices.
OPERATOR DECISION: same-account processes and peers on the same tmux server are trusted control-plane, not hostile tenants. Prompts/beads are not a secret-storage boundary and must not contain credentials. SEC-422-1/2 are reclassified under this local single-user model; no FD/memfd/socket/PTY bridge required. Remaining implementation scope: bind byte-zero /skill prefix to trusted sp output, preserve Pi /skill:<name> and Claude /skill-<name>, strengthen bounded buffer naming/cleanup, document trust boundary, add targeted regressions, push and rerun security review against this explicit model.

IMPLEMENTED on clean PR #422 head 2a17992f: exact render-skill-prefix provenance verification before worktree creation; hostile skill-looking bead rejection; 128-bit crypto tmux buffer names; best-effort deletion on consume/wrapper failure/load-launch failure/handled signals; explicit trusted same-user tmux boundary docs. Local proof (isolated HOME/XDG/TMPDIR): targeted 87 tests pass; full CLI 963 tests pass with --testTimeout=120000 (initial default-timeout run had one unrelated pi-runtime copies-missing-extensions timeout, isolated rerun passed); typecheck/build/gen-registry/registry-pack-parity/payload-hygiene pass; asset-contract unavailable because specialists-src/dist/asset-contract.json is absent in this clean checkout; managed ~/.xtrm hash unchanged (1164 entries, logs excluded). title: runtime-inject -top files instead of static per-project render
description:
## Problem

The xtrm agent instruction top-templates (`.xtrm/config/instructions/{agents,claude}-top.md`) are the ONLY xtrm-managed context that did NOT migrate to the global asset model in the xtrm-bq7yd epic. Current flow:

- **Source**: npm-installed package `<pkg>/.xtrm/config/instructions/*.md` (or dev-checkout via npm link)
- **Injection**: `cli/src/commands/init.ts:injectProjectInstructionHeaders` reads templates, upserts marker-delimited block into per-project `CLAUDE.md` + `AGENTS.md` at `xt init` / `xt update --apply` time
- **Runtime**: static per-project rendered file, native Claude/Pi read at session start
- **Update propagation**: MANUAL per repo — every consumer must run `xt update --apply` to pick up template changes

Consequences observed:
- Fleet drift: consumer repos on this machine have -top blocks from various xtrm versions
- `upsertManagedBlock` merge logic in init.ts is fiddly (~90 lines, greedy vs lazy regex, marker-collision edge cases documented in memory `upsertmanagedblock-in-cli-src-commands-init-ts-use`)
- Two independent managed blocks in CLAUDE.md (xtrm + BEADS INTEGRATION from `bd setup claude`) — mix + collision surface
- Asymmetric with skills (~/.xtrm/skills/default/, global) + hooks (~/.xtrm/hooks/, global) which DO propagate live

## Design

Move -top files to the global asset model. Runtime-inject on both runtimes.

**Source**: `~/.xtrm/config/instructions/{agents,claude}-top.md` (canonical global; bootstrapped on `xt install` like ~/.xtrm/hooks/ was).

**Claude injection**:
- New hook `.xtrm/hooks/xtrm-instructions-reminder.mjs` (mirrors `using-xtrm-reminder.mjs` shape).
- Wired to `SessionStart` (fresh session inject) + `PreCompact` (re-inject after context compaction loses systemPrompt).
- Returns `hookSpecificOutput.additionalSystemPrompt` containing the claude-top.md body (frontmatter stripped).

**Pi injection**:
- Extend `packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-loader/index.ts before_agent_start` to read `~/.xtrm/config/instructions/agents-top.md` and prepend to systemPrompt alongside `.xtrm/memory.md`.

**Deprecate per-project marker block**:
- `injectProjectInstructionHeaders` becomes a no-op (or is deleted) — no more writes to consumer CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md.
- New `xt migrate instructions --apply` command: surgically remove existing `<!-- xtrm:start -->…<!-- xtrm:end -->` block from consumer CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md. Idempotent, marker-scoped.
- Consumer per-repo user content stays untouched.

**Per-repo override slot** (new): `.xtrm/config/instructions/*.override.md` in the consumer repo. If present, appended after the global body. Solves the current escape hatch (edit outside marker block).

## Blast radius (per gitnexus_impact model)

- `cli/src/commands/init.ts`: delete `injectProjectInstructionHeaders` + call site (~50 lines removed)
- `cli/src/core/global-assets-bootstrap.ts` (new? or extend existing): bootstrap `~/.xtrm/config/instructions/` from package on `xt install`
- New: `.xtrm/hooks/xtrm-instructions-reminder.mjs`
- `.xtrm/config/hooks.json`: wire the new hook for SessionStart + PreCompact
- Extend `packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-loader/index.ts`: add -top inject
- New: `cli/src/commands/migrate.ts` (or extend existing migrate command) — `xt migrate instructions --apply`
- Tests: 10-15 new (bootstrap, hook fires, xtrm-loader inject, override slot, marker cleanup migrate)
- Docs: `docs/instructions-runtime-inject.md` (new) + update `.xtrm/config/instructions/*.md` self-referential notes

Total ~200 LOC + tests.

## Test surface

- Bootstrap: fresh install populates `~/.xtrm/config/instructions/` from package
- Claude hook: SessionStart returns additionalSystemPrompt matching source
- Claude hook: PreCompact re-injects (returns additionalContext, not additionalSystemPrompt)
- Pi loader: appended to systemPrompt after memory.md
- Override slot: per-repo `.xtrm/config/instructions/*.override.md` appended after global body
- `xt migrate instructions --apply` removes only the marker block, preserves user content
- Idempotence: repeated migrate is no-op
- Fail-open: missing source file → hook returns undefined (does not crash)

## Migration path for existing consumers

1. Upgrade xtrm package → picks up new code path
2. `xt migrate instructions --apply` in each consumer repo → strips marker block
3. Next session starts → runtime hook injects the live global body

Optional: `xt update --apply` could auto-run the migrate step (with `--no-migrate-instructions` opt-out).

## Rollback

Revert commit. `injectProjectInstructionHeaders` is restored. Consumers who ran `xt migrate instructions --apply` need one `xt update --apply` to re-render the marker block.

## Alternative considered

Keep static render but symlink the source to `~/.xtrm/config/instructions/` — rejected because Claude Code caches CLAUDE.md aggressively and consumers still don't get updates without explicit action (some editor integrations reload on file change, most don't).

## Related

- Depends on / discovered-from: xtrm-bq7yd (global assets epic — this is the -top piece that was left out)
- Related: xtrm-8zsi1 (xtrm-loader hook shape reference)
- Related: xtrm-x12p3, xtrm-x12p3.1 (memory-processor + eager-load reduction — this is the -top instruction leg of the same story)
- Related: xtrm-0p7bp (settings.json hook reconcile pattern — same runtime-vs-static tradeoff we solved for hooks)

## Definition of done

- ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/ auto-bootstrapped on xt install
- Claude SessionStart + PreCompact hook injects live source
- Pi xtrm-loader injects live source (alongside .xtrm/memory.md)
- `xt migrate instructions --apply` strips consumer CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md marker blocks
- Per-repo override slot works
- Smoke: fresh session on Claude sees new -top content, on Pi too
- Fleet propagation verified: edit ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/*, next session both runtimes see it, zero `xt update` needed
- Docs updated
notes: Follow-up subsumption: implementing this bead makes `using-xtrm-reminder.mjs` (Claude SessionStart hook that eager-loads using-xtrm SKILL.md body) redundant — because PR #422 commit 8da33192 already folded using-xtrm's session-start reflex + trigger patterns into agents-top.md / claude-top.md. Once xtrm-148eh's runtime-inject of -top hits Claude, using-xtrm-reminder can be deleted from the SessionStart wiring. Add to DoD: remove using-xtrm-reminder.mjs from .xtrm/config/hooks.json + delete the script + strip using-xtrm-reminder tests. This closes the Claude-side asymmetry noted in claude-top.md's Project intelligence pointer section.

title: memory-processor: aggressive prune of 555 stale/redundant memories
description:
## Problem

`bd prime` currently dumps 265 KB of Persistent Memories on every SessionStart hook fire (98.7% of its 269 KB total output). The 555-memory backlog has never been synthesized in this repo; many entries are stale (superseded by later work), redundant (multiple bearings of the same fact), or contradicted (later memory disagrees with earlier one).

## Task

Run the full memory-processor workflow (via `memory-audit-transaction` skill) with an AGGRESSIVE pruning stance:

- When a memory is even PLAUSIBLY stale/redundant/contradicted, classify accordingly instead of Current.
- Skip only when genuinely unverifiable (per skill's Phase 6 conservative rule) — but do not use Skip as a hedge to keep dubious entries alive.
- Target reduction: 555 → ~50-80 Current entries in `.xtrm/memory.md` (aim for a lean, dense session-start context).

## Constraints (from memory-processor spec)

- Chunks of 20-30 memories per turn; decisions appended to `.tmp/memory-audit/decisions.jsonl`.
- Phase 6 completeness gate is non-negotiable: `wc -l .tmp/memory-audit/keys.txt` == `wc -l .tmp/memory-audit/decisions.jsonl`.
- Phase 7 atomic hash-guarded prune; per-key backups in `.tmp/memory-audit/backup/`.
- Phase 8 writes filtered Current rows to `.xtrm/memory.md`.
- No destructive git.

## Model + launch

- `--model nano-gpt/nvidia/nemotron-3-ultra-550b-a55b` (1M context — needed for the 555-memory input).
- Detached tmux session for background run.

## Success criteria

- `.xtrm/memory.md` populated (was 939-byte bootstrap placeholder).
- `bd stats` shows meaningfully fewer memories (target: 50-80).
- Next-session `bd prime` output measurably smaller (target: < 50 KB total, < 45 KB memories).
- Final report in bead notes: counts (Current / Stale / Contradicted / Redundant / Skipped) + measured reduction.

## Related

- xtrm-x12p3 (parent) — xtrm-loader eager-load reduction, this closes the memory-side of the same problem.
- Follow-up if reduction is insufficient: file a bead to strip `bd prime` from SessionStart entirely (keep only on-demand agent invocation).

title: xt --role launcher redesign: sp-owned turn-1 composition, delete file machinery and injectSkillContents (supersedes xtrm-osipt stopgap)
description:
Full redesign of the xt --role|--bead|--prompt launcher for both runtimes. Replaces the xtrm-osipt stopgap (--append-system-prompt-file) with an inline, sp-owned turn-1 composition. Contract fully frozen with the specialists side; sp owns all skill-name/dedup/surface-format logic via unitAI-qeguh + Proposal 1.

## Runtime argv (both runtimes)

    claude --append-system-prompt '<specialist identity>' \
           --dangerously-skip-permissions [--model X] \
           -- '<sp-owned prefix><body>'

    pi --append-system-prompt '<specialist identity>' \
       [--model X] [--thinking Y] \
       '<sp-owned prefix><body>'

Everything on one line, no files. --no-skills for pi is deferred (see below).

## Turn-1 body per invocation

  --bead <id>            body = sp render-task output verbatim (prefix already inside, per unitAI-qeguh Option A)
  --prompt "<text>"       body = sp render-skill-prefix <name> --surface X | .skill_prefix + <text>
  neither                body = sp render-skill-prefix <name> --surface X | .skill_prefix (empty task; pane primes skills and idles)

Mutual exclusion: --bead and --prompt cannot both be set; reject at CLI parse with a clear error.

## Deletions (all under cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts unless noted)

- injectSkillContents() function + its call site in launchWorktreeSession (was xtrm-14w28's fix; superseded — sp forces skill body load via /skill:name in turn-1 instead of stuffing bodies into sysprompt)
- Both .xtrm/role-<slug>-prompt.md and .xtrm/role-<slug>-task.md file writes
- claude's --append-system-prompt-file switch (xtrm-osipt stopgap) — back to inline --append-system-prompt <string>
- --plugin-dir emission (claude auto-discovers skills from ~/.claude/skills/; --plugin-dir was needed only to force-load bodies, which /skill-name now does deterministically)
- claude runtime's --skill <path> emission (never had one — confirm nothing sneaks back)
- prepareClaudeSkillPlugin() function + the ephemeral .xtrm/role-skills/.claude-plugin/ scaffold
- All skill-name derivation, dedup, and surface-format logic — sp owns these now (Option A)

## Additions

- Byte guard: sysprompt.length + prefix.length + body.length must be < ~50KB. Over -> loud, precise error naming the actual byte count and pointing at --bead as the right container. No silent truncation, no file fallback.
- --prompt <string> CLI flag on both xt claude and xt pi (xt-owned; forwarded as the positional argv to the runtime after prefix). Mutually exclusive with --bead.
- Preflight validation: sp view --raw + sp render-skill-prefix (and sp render-task when --bead) run BEFORE worktree creation so bad specialists / bad beads / missing skills fail fast without leaking a worktree.
- Turn-1 composition helper (thin: just concatenation + byte guard). Sp exposes the frozen contract; core doesn't reimplement.

## Position-0 '/' invariant (implicit but must be preserved)

sp emits <prefix> beginning with '/skill:name' at position 0 whenever the specialist declares any skill. Core prepends nothing between sp's prefix and the shell argv boundary. The runtime therefore sees '/' at literal byte 0 and the slash-command parser force-loads bodies.

Empty-skills edge case: when the specialist declares no skills, prefix is "" and <body> sits at position 0. If <body> starts with '/' (only realistic if a bead title begins with '/'), the runtime would try to interpret it as a slash-command. Detect this at launch (either --bead's rendered body OR --prompt's first byte is '/') and reject with a clear error asking the operator to rename the bead / adjust the prompt.

## Runtime-specific notes

pi:
  - This bead ships WITHOUT --no-skills. That flip is deferred to a follow-up commit synced with sp's unitAI-0o3pv release (specialist-side must first isolate its own spawn paths + audit specialists for undeclared-but-used skills, else operators lose functionality). Core commit for the flip is a one-line addition once sp lands.
  - Keep pi native --skill <path> emission from role.skillPaths + explicitSkillPaths for now (matches sp's current behavior). Same deferral as --no-skills — both are pool-related.
  - The prompt-suggestions / theme / etc. flags stay untouched.

claude:
  - No native pool isolation flag exists (--bare is nuclear, disables hooks/CLAUDE.md/OAuth). Accept partial isolation (global auto-discovery visible) as the current trade-off. Not a follow-up until Claude Code CLI gains a --no-skills equivalent.
  - Drop --plugin-dir. Skills are globally discoverable at ~/.claude/skills/ and /skill-name in turn-1 forces body load; the ephemeral plugin dir added complexity without benefit.

Both runtimes:
  - Keep --model, --thinking (pi only), passthrough --.
  - Keep sp view --raw call for specialist identity string (unchanged).

## Test surface (cli/src/tests/worktree-session-role.test.ts + new)

- Composition tests per case (i/ii/iii) x runtime (pi/claude) — assert exact argv shape.
- Byte-guard test: 200KB systemPrompt / 200KB prompt / etc. must error with the required copy.
- Mutual-exclusion test: --bead + --prompt rejected at CLI parse.
- Position-0 '/' safety: --prompt "/foo bar" with no declared skills rejected; --prompt "/foo bar" with declared skills accepted (prefix precedes).
- Preflight-fail-before-worktree tests: missing specialist / missing bead / bad --skill path exits(1) with no worktree side-effect.
- Smoke matrix (integration, not unit): (i)(ii)(iii) x (pi, claude) x (chain-coordinator 1.5KB, reviewer 14KB, debugger 11KB) — 18 launches, verify each pane's first response follows the fixture expectation.

## Doc + help + skill + instructions surface (do not miss)

- cli/src/commands/claude.ts + cli/src/commands/pi.ts — .addHelpText, .option() descriptions for --role/--bead/--prompt/--skill/--model/--thinking, examples in the Examples: block.
- docs/xt-pi-role.md — currently mentions --plugin-dir under the .xtrm/ ephemeral scaffold; rewrite the whole page to the new contract. Delete file-based prompt/task references. Add the three cases (--bead, --prompt, neither) with concrete examples.
- README.md — spot-check for role/bead launcher references; update.
- XTRM-GUIDE.md — same spot-check + update.
- .xtrm/config/instructions/agents-top.md and claude-top.md — the top-level agent behavior notes; sync any role/skill guidance to the new contract. (Coordinate with xtrm-x12p3 which also touches instructions; land whichever ships first and follow-up commit for the other.)
- Multiplexing skill (~/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md, source in xtrm-tools) — paragraph on the position-0 '/' invariant. Depends on xtmux-0gf audit resolving first (need to know whether xtmux delivery primitives wrap or not).
- CLAUDE.md in this repo — update the 'Session start' or 'Skill routing' section if it mentions the file-based prompt/task paths.

## Grep audit BEFORE deleting file writes

- Grep the whole repo (+ ~/.xtrm, ~/.claude, ~/.pi, statusline/picker scripts) for readers of .xtrm/role-*-{prompt,task}.md and the @agent_prompt_file pane option. Any hook, picker, statusline, or session-close report that consumes these needs an update or a shim BEFORE deletion.
- Confirm @agent_prompt_file pane option is still written (or removed cleanly if no downstream reads it).

## Rollback

Revert this commit. Behavior falls back to xtrm-osipt stopgap (--append-system-prompt-file) which is proven to work. Zero data/schema/persisted-state risk.

## Cross-repo dependencies (informational; beads live on other repos)

- specialists unitAI-qeguh (P1, awaiting operator dispatch): buildSkillPrefix helper + renderTaskPrompt prepend + new 'sp render-skill-prefix <name> --surface pi|claude' command. Frozen contract this bead codes against. Core can ship case (i) without this (sp render-task doesn't yet lead with prefix -> non-optimal but not broken); cases (ii)+(iii) require this to be released.
- specialists unitAI-0o3pv (P1, awaiting operator dispatch): --no-skills unconditional emit on both sp spawn paths + specialist audit for undeclared-but-used skills. Core --no-skills flip on pi is the follow-up commit that syncs to this.
- xtmux xtmux-0gf (P1): audit send-primitive wrapping; result gates the multiplexing SKILL.md doc paragraph.

## Non-goals (prevent scope creep)

- No changes to sp itself (unitAI-qeguh + unitAI-0o3pv own that).
- No xtmux code changes (xtmux-0gf owns that).
- No settings.json audit (xtrm-kdwvu owns that — parallel track).
- No relaxing '--skill without --role' rejection (small independent decision; if needed, file a separate bead).
- No --continue / --resume behavior change (verify existing resume still works but do not add features).

## Definition of done

- Redesign committed to core; smoke matrix green; docs/help/skill/instructions updated; grep audit clean; @agent_prompt_file consumers audited; PR merged; xt relinked; a follow-up bead filed for the --no-skills flip synced to sp's unitAI-0o3pv release.

Related: closes-follow-up-to xtrm-osipt (which is the stopgap this supersedes). Discovered-from xtrm-osipt operationally.

title: xt doctor settings — audit installer's per-repo vs global settings.json writes
description:
Post global-installation migration, need a read-only audit tool + investigation of what the installer actually writes.

## Symptoms triggering this

Spot-check on operator machine (2026-07-15) showed NO obvious legacy content in the four settings.json files inspected, BUT the audit was superficial (known-pattern grep only). Operator instinct — quoted verbatim: 'since xt migrated to full global installation, that means that those files remained a mess, very likely. i'm pretty sure that our installer does something wrong with pi and claude'.

## Specific installer concern to investigate

updatePiSettings() at cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts:1247 writes PROJECT_EXTENSION_PACKAGE_ID (@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions) into per-repo <repo>/.pi/settings.json.packages EVERY init/update. But global ~/.pi/agent/settings.json.packages ALREADY carries @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions (verified on operator machine). Post global-installation migration, per-repo package entries look redundant at best, actively wrong at worst (duplicate loading, version drift when global bumps).

Same question applies to:
- ensureGlobalStatusLine() writing ~/.claude/settings.json even in project-mode claude sync (claude-runtime-sync.ts:273) — surprising side effect
- clean.ts:149 mutating ~/.claude/settings.json — verify it strips only xtrm-owned entries
- Every reconcile/merge path — do they still write things that global installation makes redundant

## Scope

### 1. xt doctor settings — read-only sub-command
Report on both scopes (home + per-repo, optionally scan all repos under a root):
- dead hook commands: os.stat every hook 'command:' path, list nonexistent
- duplicate handlers: same event bound to same script from multiple wrappers (project + global collision)
- orphaned top-level keys: keys no reader consumes anymore (needs a known-consumers list)
- legacy patterns: active/claude, active/pi, local-legacy, xtrm-tools@, plugins/cache/xtrm, /tmp/claude-, worktrees/core-xt, dev/{repo}/cli/dist inline paths, .pi/skills/xtrm — anything the plugin-era or pre-global-migration used
- per-repo entries that duplicate global entries (packages, skills, extensions, hooks): the exact class the operator suspects the installer creates
Flags: --scope home|project|all, --scan-all-repos <root>, --json, --fix (deferred).

### 2. Installer audit
Walk every writer of .pi/settings.json and .claude/settings.json (project + home):
- claude-runtime-sync.ts:runClaudeRuntimeSyncPhase (project)
- claude-runtime-sync.ts:reconcileGlobalClaudeHooks (home)
- claude-runtime-sync.ts:ensureGlobalStatusLine (home, runs every sync)
- pi-runtime.ts:updatePiSettings (project) — PRIME SUSPECT for pi-extensions duplication
- pi-runtime-hooks.ts:reconcileGlobalPiHooks (home)
- plugin-era-cleanup.ts (both)
- clean.ts (home)
- migrate.ts (both, per-repo iteration)
For each: document what fields it touches, whether the write is still needed post-global-migration, and whether the write duplicates something already global.

### 3. Fix (separate bead)
Once the audit lands and confirms which writes are redundant, delete or condition-gate them. Likely candidates:
- updatePiSettings stops adding pi-extensions to per-repo packages (it's global)
- ensureGlobalStatusLine only runs in global-install mode
- Other per-repo entries move to global or delete

## Deliverables

- xt doctor settings sub-command (read-only)
- Installer-writes matrix (docs)
- Follow-up bead for redundant-write deletions

## Non-goals

- No auto-cleanup in this bead. Doctor is read-only; deletions ship separately after operator approves the matrix.
- No touching of the xtrm-osipt / launcher redesign work — that's a parallel track.
notes:
CONFIRMATION from xtrm-1ehjo sweep (2026-07-21) — the operator instinct quoted in this bead was correct on both runtimes.

CLAUDE side, confirmed: ~/.claude/settings.json carries the xt hook block tagged _source:'xtrm-global' pointing at ~/.xtrm/hooks/*, AND every consumer project's <repo>/.claude/settings.json still carries the pre-migration block pointing at <repo>/.xtrm/hooks/*. Claude Code merges user+project scope, so all 19 xt hook registrations fire twice, in all 8 consumer projects (152 duplicate registrations machine-wide). The project entries carry no _source, which is why the earlier known-pattern grep missed them. Hook FILES are byte-identical global-vs-project — the duplication is purely in registration.

PI side, confirmed (the updatePiSettings concern in this description): ~/.pi/agent/settings.json.packages already lists 'npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions', and all 8 projects ALSO list exactly ['npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions'] in <repo>/.pi/settings.json.packages. Same redundancy shape as the hooks. Not yet verified whether pi actually double-loads the package or dedupes internally — that verification is still open work under this bead.

Also found on the pi side: ~/.pi/settings.json declares skills: ['../.xtrm/skills/active'], but .xtrm/skills/active does not exist in any of the 8 projects nor globally (checked). Dangling skills-dir reference, likely a stale runtime view path.

Partial fix shipped: scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs (dry-run default, --apply opt-in, --json) removes ONLY project-scope Claude hook registrations that are provably covered by the global block — same (event,matcher,command) after path normalisation, plus a byte-identity check on the referenced hook file. It does not touch .pi/settings.json, does not touch ~/.xtrm/, and does not dedupe within a single settings file. The 'xt doctor settings' read-only sub-command this bead asks for is still unbuilt; the script is the standalone precursor.

See docs/legacy-hook-duplication.md for the leftover taxonomy.
close_reason: audit tool + matrix shipped read-only; fixes split to xtrm-tzzud (core) and xtmux-2zh (cross-repo)
