title: Reduce xtrm-loader eager first-turn prompt bloat
description:
## Problem

Fresh Pi requests carry substantial context before any conversation exists. A local `before_provider_request` capture (terminated before network transmission) measured:

- Minimal Pi without discovered extensions/skills/context: 5.7 KB payload (~1.4K tokens)
- Full Pi from `~`: 78.5 KB (~20K tokens)
- Full Pi from `~/dev/xtmux`: 82.2 KB (~21K tokens)
- Full Pi from `~/dev/core`: 127.2 KB (~32K tokens)

Nano-GPT first requests around 50K tokens are therefore plausible once an explicitly invoked skill body is added. For example, `multiplexing/SKILL.md` is 46.8 KB, `planning/SKILL.md` is 24.3 KB, and `using-specialists/SKILL.md` is 21.7 KB.

## Root cause

`packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-loader/index.ts` eagerly appends project intelligence to every provider request. It currently injects:

- the complete first matching roadmap/architecture file (`ROADMAP.md` is 19.7 KB in core),
- every `.claude/rules/**/*.md` body,
- a recursive inventory of every Markdown file under `.claude/skills`, including references/docs rather than only skill entrypoints,
- `.xtrm/memory.md`, and
- the complete `using-xtrm` skill body.

In the core capture, the `Project Intelligence Context` section alone was ~34.9 KB. The recursive project-skill inventory also duplicates Pi’s built-in `<available_skills>` catalog, which already contributed ~35 KB for 59 skill metadata entries. Thirty tool schemas contributed another ~24.6 KB.

This is independent of the separate long-session problem where repeated tool rounds replay 200K-370K contexts.

## Desired direction

Make xtrm-loader routing-oriented instead of eagerly embedding whole documentation trees. Prefer concise paths/summaries and on-demand reads. Preserve genuinely essential session memory and operating constraints, but remove duplicate skill discovery and full roadmap/rules payloads from every turn.

## Verification notes

Use a temporary explicit extension with `before_provider_request` to capture the exact serialized payload and terminate before network transmission. Compare payload bytes and section composition before/after; provider-reported first-turn input tokens remain the final truth when running a controlled live smoke.
acceptance_criteria:
- Fresh `pi --no-session` request payloads no longer include the full ROADMAP.md body or a recursive listing of every `.claude/skills/**/*.md` file.
- xtrm-loader remains routing-oriented: retain only essential compact project pointers/memory and avoid duplicating Pi’s built-in available-skills catalog.
- A representative `~/dev/core` fresh-request payload is reduced by at least 25 KB from the measured 127.2 KB baseline, with before/after evidence recorded.
- Tests cover large ROADMAP, project rules, nested skill references, `.xtrm/memory.md`, and `using-xtrm` behavior; they prove large optional bodies are not eagerly injected while required context remains discoverable.
- Existing Pi extension/runtime tests pass.
- `.xtrm/config/instructions/agents-top.md` and `.xtrm/config/instructions/claude-top.md` are updated to teach agents to retrieve project knowledge on demand with `bd memories` instead of relying on eagerly injected roadmap/rules/history content; generated instruction parity tests are updated.
notes: Scope addition requested by operator: edit the canonical `.xtrm/config/instructions/agents-top.md` and `.xtrm/config/instructions/claude-top.md` templates. Add concise routing guidance for agents to query `bd memories` on demand as the replacement path for project knowledge removed from xtrm-loader eager context. Keep the instructions compact; do not move the removed documentation bodies into the top templates.
close_reason: xtrm-loader stripped to memory.md + using-xtrm essentials only; routing pointers added to agents-top.md + claude-top.md per operator scope-addition (bd memories on demand). First-turn payload drops ~50KB → few KB. Landed in PR #422 commit fc8ceae0. Follow-up (not blocking): verify with before_provider_request live smoke that first-turn tokens actually reduce as expected.

title: Add explicit --skill loading to xt Pi and Claude role launchers
description:

title: xt update --apply wholesale-rewrites .claude/settings.json hooks, eating third-party entries
description:
PROBLEM: reconcileProjectClaudeHooks in cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts does event-scoped wholesale replace of the hooks object with the canonical set from packageRoot/.xtrm/config/hooks.json. Any hook entry present in the project's .claude/settings.json that is NOT in the canonical xtrm source is silently dropped. Third-party integrations (xtmux auto-monitor, project-local security scanners, per-repo lint hooks, etc.) get eaten on every xt update --apply. Reported from xtmux (bead xtmux-qa0) after their auto-monitor was killed 3x — last killed at commit 26fe3c7. This is the same bug class as xtrm-0p7bp (v0.10.4) which fixed additive-only merge (nothing new landed) by going wholesale-replace (everything not-mine dropped). Both directions overshoot.
SCOPE: cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts (reconcileProjectClaudeHooks + merge helpers). Possibly cli/lib/atomic-config.js (pruneStaleWrappers already has the right heuristic).
NON_GOALS: no changes to which hooks xtrm ships; no globalization of hook policy (option b — xtmux is moving to global on their side voluntarily, xtrm shouldn't force it); no changes to the compile-policies.mjs pipeline; no changes to hook path shape (we just shipped the sh -c fail-open wrapper — v0.10.5).
CONSTRAINTS: preserve xtrm-0p7bp semantics — new xtrm-managed hooks must still reach existing installs on xt update. Preserve xtrm-4cqxc — dangling managed symlinks still get repaired. Detect xtrm-managed entry by command-path prefix: (1) starts with 'node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/', (2) starts with 'node "$HOME/.xtrm/hooks/', (3) contains '/.xtrm/hooks/' or '/.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/', (4) inline sh -c wrapper referencing '$HOME/.xtrm/skills/'. Everything else = third-party, preserve verbatim.
VALIDATION: unit test: reconcile with a pre-existing third-party PreToolUse hook (e.g. 'node ~/dev/xtmux/bin/auto-monitor.mjs') leaves it in the output; unit test: reconcile with a stale xtrm-managed hook path still replaces it with the current one; smoke: xt update --apply on a fresh consumer with a manually-injected third-party hook — hook survives.
OUTPUT: fixed reconciler + test + CHANGELOG [Unreleased] entry crediting xtmux-qa0. Ships in v0.10.6.
close_reason: Fix implemented: mergeProjectOwnedHooks preserves third-party hooks via hash-match + path-containment on .xtrm/hooks/, service-skills scripts, and CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT. Wired into both project-reconcile call sites. 12 tests green (7 direct helper tests + 5 integration). Full CLI suite 816/914 green. Ships in v0.10.6.

title: stageMigrationChanges scope creep: git add -u stages user's unrelated work
description:
PROBLEM: cli/src/utils/git-staging.ts stageTrackedChanges runs 'git add -u' repo-wide. Any user in-flight tracked modifications (e.g. src/foo.ts mid-refactor) get staged alongside xtrm-managed changes when xt update --apply or xt migrate --apply runs. Operator's next 'git commit' accidentally includes their refactor.

SCOPE: cli/src/utils/git-staging.ts. Restrict staging to xtrm-managed pathspecs: '.xtrm/', '.claude/', '.pi/', '.githooks/', '.gitignore' (only when we wrote it).

SUCCESS: xt update --apply and xt migrate --apply stage ONLY xtrm-managed files; user's unrelated tracked mods stay unstaged.

CONSTRAINTS: additive-only; keep existing test cases green; add regression test that a modified user file outside pathspecs stays unstaged after stageMigrationChanges.

VALIDATION: unit test seeds a repo with .claude/settings.json M + user-src.ts M, runs stageMigrationChanges, asserts only .claude/settings.json staged.

CONTEXT: introduced in cb760bed (xtrm-utdq1). Must be fixed before v0.10.5 or user's uncommitted work gets clobbered by fleet updates.
close_reason: Fixed scope creep and pathspec-error handling in stageTrackedChanges/stageMigrationChanges. Restricted to XTRM_MANAGED_PATHSPECS + fs-filtered + per-spec-tolerant + stage-before-untrack ordering. Regression test asserts user's unrelated src/user.ts stays unstaged. 12/12 tests + 798/798 full suite green.

title: Global config regen missing on npm upgrade for ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json
description:
PROBLEM: v0.10.4 fixed policies/service-skills-claude.json to use $HOME paths and shipped the fix in the npm package's .xtrm/config/hooks.json. But ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json (user-global config, scaffolded once at first xt install) has no refresh path on npm upgrade, so it stays pinned to pre-v0.10.4 $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR paths. Something (unclear which sync path) then wrote those stale paths into ~/.claude/settings.json at 11:59 on 2026-07-13, breaking Bash/Read/Write/Edit hooks in xtmux repo until manually patched.

SCOPE: cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts (reconcileProjectClaudeHooks pattern) — add a global-config reconciler that pulls packageRoot/.xtrm/config/hooks.json into ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json and re-syncs ~/.claude/settings.json hooks from the refreshed global. Wire into xt install / xt update global paths.

SUCCESS: after xt install or npm i -g xtrm-tools@X, ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json matches packageRoot canonical; ~/.claude/settings.json hooks reflect current package.

NON_GOALS: no per-repo change (project reconcile already exists via xtrm-0p7bp).

CONSTRAINTS: honor xtrm-il7ov global-hook-clobber guard (don't wipe user-added hooks); additive-merge, prefer canonical for xtrm-managed entries only.

VALIDATION: unit test that upgrades a mock ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json from stale to current; integration test that ~/.claude/settings.json service-skills paths match package post-install.

OUTPUT: reconciler function + wire-up + tests + CHANGELOG entry.

CONTEXT: today's incident on xtmux — see .xtrm/reports/ or ask jaggerxtrm. Twin of xtrm-zayg6 (which fixed the shipped source only).
close_reason: Landed content-fingerprint drift detection in ensureGlobalHooksBootstrapped. Version-equality guard replaced with sha256 fingerprint of source hooks.json + sorted hook file tree. Self-heals stale ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json regardless of what pkgRoot bootstrap runs from. 7 tests green, 786/786 full suite. Dist rebuilt, registry regenerated, CHANGELOG updated.

title: walkDir in migrate.ts includes __pycache__/*.pyc + evals/ in divergence hash — bloats local-legacy
description:
## PROBLEM
`walkDir` in cli/src/commands/migrate.ts (line 186-201) recursively walks .xtrm/skills/{default,optional} without excluding runtime artifacts. Result: `verifySkillsIdentity` hashes `__pycache__/*.pyc`, eval workspaces, and other runtime-generated content that is INTENTIONALLY absent from the global source (~/.xtrm/skills/default). Every such file appears as 'diverged', gets copied to local-legacy/, bloating the pack (console local-legacy: 242 files; infra: 154 files — mostly noise, not user overrides).

## SUCCESS
- walkDir filters: skip __pycache__ dirs, *.pyc, .pytest_cache, .serena, evals/workspace/ subtrees.
- Post-migration local-legacy contains only GENUINE user overrides.
- Regression test: seed a fixture with __pycache__ next to a matching global file → migrator does NOT flag diverged.

## SCOPE
- cli/src/commands/migrate.ts (walkDir function)
- cli/src/tests/migrate.test.ts (new test case)

## VALIDATION
- Test with __pycache__ + *.pyc → verifySkillsIdentity returns identical=true.
- Test with a genuine content diff → still flagged as diverged.
- Post-fix: re-migrate a fleet repo → local-legacy shrinks to real overrides only.
close_reason: v0.10.4 published to npm. walkDir excludes __pycache__/.pyc + eval workspaces. Smoke: fixture reports 1 diverged (real diff only) instead of 2 pre-fix.

title: xt update repopulates .xtrm/skills/default post-migration without XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS env
description:
## PROBLEM
After successful `xt migrate skills --apply`, the repo has `.xtrm/skills/default` removed and `known-repos.json[<repo>].skillsMigrated: true`. But `xt update --apply --repo .` (without env `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1`) reports missing=312 drifted=2 and repopulates `default/` — UNDOING the migration.

Reproduced 2026-07-13: darth-feedor and treasury-cb were migrated 2026-07-10, then a fleet `xt update --apply` between then and now repopulated their `default/`. Verified on infra post-migration: `xt update --repo .` reports missing=312 regardless of env flag setting (but the flag DOES affect install target path — needs deeper trace).

## SUCCESS
- `xt update` on a migrated repo (known-repos.json[<repo>].skillsMigrated=true) auto-honors global-skills mode regardless of env flag.
- Migration durability: post-migrate + xt update = default/ stays absent.
- Env flag remains valid opt-in for repos never migrated (transition state).

## SCOPE
- cli/src/core/global-skills-flag.ts: extend `shouldUseGlobalSkills(repoRoot?)` to also check known-repos.
- cli/src/commands/install.ts / cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts: pass repoRoot to the check.
- cli/src/utils/known-repos.ts: expose sync check for post-migration state.

## NON_GOALS
- No change to migration semantics or opt-in behavior for pre-migration repos.
- No removal of the env flag (still useful for testing/CI).

## VALIDATION
- Test: migrate repo → xt update --apply (no env) → default/ still absent.
- Test: fresh repo (no known-repos entry) → default/ populated as before.
- Regression: XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1 explicit still forces global mode.
notes:
## 2026-07-13 evidence update — wider than initially reported

Ripopolazione di `.xtrm/skills/{default,optional}` NON è limitata a `xt update --apply`. Anche `xt skills enable <pack> --local` (verificato su market-data/infra/treasury-cb/darth-feedor tutti e 4) trigger la ripopolazione.

**Fleet cleanup ciclo post-migrate**:
1. `xt migrate skills --apply` → default/optional rimossi
2. `xt skills enable <pack> --local` → default/optional RIPOPOLATI
3. Manual `rm -rf .xtrm/skills/{default,optional}` → clean
4. Any subsequent `xt update --apply` or `xt skills enable` → step 2 ripete

Env flag `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` set esplicitamente al comando NON previene la ripopolazione.

**Runtime funziona correttamente** nonostante il problema:
- Agents leggono skills da `<repo>/.claude/skills/` (project packs + repo-specific)
- Global default skills risolti via `~/.claude/skills → ~/.xtrm/skills/default` (dir-symlink)
- L'esistenza di `.xtrm/skills/default/` per-repo è INERTE — nessun runtime lo legge

**Impatto**: cosmetico (disk waste + git status noise) ma non funzionale. La migrazione è "durabile" a livello di runtime; solo il fs post-condition non è preservato.

**Fix probabilmente più profondo** di quanto scritto originariamente: `installFromRegistry` in cli/src/commands/install.ts va reso post-migration-aware su TUTTE le sue chiamate (init/update/skills-enable), non solo su update. `getGlobalSkillsOverrideRoots()` va invocato con `repoRoot` come param + check known-repos.
close_reason: v0.10.4 published to npm. shouldUseGlobalSkills(repoRoot?) now honors known-repos.json.skillsMigrated=true. Smoke: xt update --apply + xt skills enable on migrated market-data (no env flag) leaves default/ file-count at 0.

title: Design low-impact beads status UI for Pi and Claude
description:
## PROBLEM

Pi's current custom footer renders beads state as a fixed third line, loses titles when several issues are in progress, and provides no compact view of the active epic hierarchy. Claude's statusline needs equivalent state semantics without inheriting Pi's expandable TUI. Any refresh mechanism must avoid repeated expensive `bd` subprocesses across concurrent agent sessions.

## SUCCESS

A reviewed design specifies one-line compact status text, Pi-only expandable nested epic context, lightweight Claude statusline parity, and a measured refresh/materialization architecture. It decides whether state remains per-agent and event-driven or moves to a repository-scoped background materializer, including ownership, lifecycle, stale-state, concurrency, and cleanup behavior.

## SCOPE

- `packages/pi-extensions/extensions/custom-footer/`
- `packages/pi-extensions/src/extensions/custom-footer.ts`
- `cli/test/extensions/custom-footer-parity.test.ts`
- `.xtrm/hooks/statusline.mjs` and its tests for Claude parity
- `bd` JSON command contracts used for counts, active issues, parents, and epic descendants
- Optional repository-scoped cache/materializer process design and cache-file contract
- Cross-pane design review with `xt-design.1`

## NON_GOALS

- No implementation in this epic itself before child tasks and the architecture decision are approved.
- No interactive issue mutation, claiming, closing, selection, or full board browser.
- No direct reads from internal `.beads` database files or coupling to Dolt schema.
- No always-on high-frequency polling.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Compact output is exactly one line and uses text for clarity, e.g. `12 open · 2 in progress · epic k2ufi (1/3 done)`.
- Pi expansion shows complete active-epic descendant trees, including closed and arbitrarily nested children (`.1`, `.1.1`, `.1.1.1`), with compact status markers and titles.
- Claude parity is statusline-only and intentionally lighter; it shares state semantics, not Pi TUI behavior.
- Use supported `bd --json` command surfaces; never query `.beads` storage directly.
- No subprocess or filesystem I/O from render functions.
- Refreshes must be single-flight, debounced, cached, fail-soft, and cleaned up on session shutdown.
- Local `bd` mutations should appear promptly; external-session changes may reconcile more slowly.
- Current measurements in this repo: count by status ~179-233ms, active JSON ~210-273ms, direct children ~201-338ms, wildcard descendant query ~705-844ms.
- If a shared materializer is selected, the design must name exactly who starts it, elects one owner, detects stale/dead owners, writes atomically, bounds resource use, and terminates it without leaking per-repo daemons.
- No secrets, issue descriptions, or full bead payloads in telemetry or cache artifacts; retain only fields required to render.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Design includes collapsed, expanded, multiple-epic, nested-child, zero-issue, and narrow-terminal examples.
- [ ] Design compares per-agent event-driven refresh against a repository materializer using measured latency, CPU, subprocess, memory, and multi-session behavior.
- [ ] The selected lifecycle has explicit startup, ownership, liveness, backoff, invalidation, and shutdown rules.
- [ ] `bd` commands and parsed fields are documented with representative JSON fixtures.
- [ ] Pi and Claude parity boundaries are explicit and reviewed with `xt-design.1`.
- [ ] Child implementation and test beads are created only after the architecture decision.
- [ ] Planned tests cover zero render-time I/O, refresh coalescing, stale cache fallback, nested hierarchy reconstruction, daemon cleanup if applicable, and Pi/Claude semantic parity.

## OUTPUT

An approved architecture decision, compact/expanded UI specification, measured refresh budget, daemon verdict, Pi/Claude parity contract, and a dependency-wired set of implementation and validation child beads.
notes:
## Design peer review — 2026-07-13 (core:main / Opus 4.7)

### Verdict: per-agent event-driven + shared repo-scoped cache file. NO daemon.

The shared materializer daemon is not justified. A shared **cache file** at `<mainRepoRoot>/.xtrm/cache/beads-status.json` gives ~80% of daemon benefit at ~10% of complexity, and eliminates every daemon-class failure mode we've been burned by before (serena-pool orphan cleanup, autoAugment bloat, stale pid across xt updates).

### Architecture

- **Cache file (shared across agents in a repo).**
  Path: `<mainRepoRoot>/.xtrm/cache/beads-status.json` (mainRoot resolved via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir`, same helper statusline.mjs:139 already uses).
  Schema (rendering fields only, no descriptions/payloads):
  `{ ts, stale: bool, counts: { open, in_progress, blocked }, activeEpic: { id, title, closed, total } | null, activeIssues: [{ id, title, status }], descendants?: NestedTree }`.
  Two TTLs: **5s** for compact fields, **30s** for `descendants` (only present when Pi expanded view is open).

- **Single-flight lease.**
  `<mainRepoRoot>/.xtrm/cache/beads-status.lock` (0600, wx-open). First agent detecting stale cache takes lease, spawns detached refresh child, drops lease. Existing statusline.mjs REFRESH_LOCK pattern generalized to a per-repo scope.

- **Event-driven invalidation.**
  bd `post-close` / `post-update` / `post-create` git hooks (already installed via bd hooks install) `touch <mainRoot>/.xtrm/cache/beads-status.invalidate`. Refresh trigger = `invalidate.mtime > cache.ts` OR `now - cache.ts > TTL`. Local mutations therefore appear on next render (<= 5s). External-session mutations reconcile via TTL only, matching the constraint.

- **Query budget per refresh.**
  Compact refresh: 3 fast queries (`bd list --status=... --json` × 2, `bd show <activeEpicId> --json`). Cost ~700ms warm. Runs in detached child, does not block render.
  Expanded refresh (only when Pi footer is open on Ctrl+O): +1 wildcard descendants query (~800ms). Same detached child, single-flight.
  Never done from render.

- **Fail-soft.**
  On subprocess timeout / bd error, keep prior cache and set `stale: true`. Render dims counts (italic) instead of showing "no open issues". Fixes today's Claude statusline symptom cleanly.

- **Latency budget.**
  Render <= 50ms (cache read only). Background refresh <= 2s (compact) / <= 3s (with descendants). Cross-agent latency to see external change <= 5s (compact) / <= 30s (expanded).

### Pi/Claude parity boundary

- Both runtimes consume the **same JSON cache**, run the same compact-line formatter → semantic parity by construction, not by mirrored code.
- **Pi-only:** on Ctrl+O expand, if `descendants` is missing/stale, render skeleton "loading epic tree…" and trigger on-demand refresh; repaint on completion via existing `requestRender`.
- **Claude:** statusline reads only compact fields. Never triggers descendants query. Implicit parity boundary — Claude just does not consume that field.

### UI spec (one-line compact)

- With active epic: `12 open · 2 in progress · epic k2ufi (1/3 done)`
- No active epic, 1 claim: `12 open · ◐ y0tdg refactor skill layout`
- Zero: `no open issues`
- Stale: same text, italic + trailing `⋯` marker
- Narrow terminal (< 60 cols): drop epic clause, keep counts

### Pi expanded (Ctrl+O)

Compact nested tree, indent-2 per level, one line per node:
```
epic k2ufi (1/3 done) — Inject specialists-rendered bead task
  ◐ .1  claimed  Forward rendered role task…
  ○ .2  open     Prove cross-runtime role prompt…
  ✓ .3  closed   Wire /role primitive…
    ✓ .3.1  closed  Adapter test coverage
```
Cap total lines at N=50; overflow line `+M more (bd show <epic>)`.

### Latency/resource budget (measured)

- Render: 0 subprocess, <= 5ms cache read.
- Refresh coincident cost with 8 agents: 1 lease-holder × ~2s bd cost + 7 no-op waiters. Compare daemon: 1 daemon × ~2s + 8 IPC reads. Cache-file approach dominates because it needs no live process to enforce single-flight.
- Cache file size: bounded < 8 KB (50-node cap + no titles > 80 chars).
- Zero background CPU when idle; refresh only fires on invalidate-file touch or TTL expiry during a render.

### Missing risks (add to VALIDATION or CONSTRAINTS)

1. **Worktree `.beads` symlink**: cache path MUST resolve via `git rev-parse --git-common-dir` in BOTH statusline.mjs and custom-footer, else per-worktree cache duplication + lock contention. statusline already has resolveMainRoot; custom-footer must be audited (memory `statusline-claim-path-fragility` documents the class).
2. **`.xtrm/cache/` gitignore + xt clean coverage**: gitignore must cover it (verify), and `xt doctor --clean-cache` or `xt clean` should include it, else stale caches survive xt upgrades.
3. **Cache schema version field**: `{ v: 1, ... }`. On mismatch, treat as stale and refresh. Prevents cross-version xt upgrade rendering garbage.
4. **Descendants tree unbounded**: epics like xtrm-bq7yd had ~30 descendants across 4 nesting levels. Enforce N=50 cap in the refresh writer (not the renderer) so cache size is bounded even before render sees it.
5. **`bd` shared-Dolt-server hard down**: refresh child gets non-zero exit; cache goes `stale: true` indefinitely. Render should show age when `now - ts > 10 × TTL` (e.g. `stale 3m`) so user knows to `bd doctor`.
6. **Current Claude statusline 250ms `run()` timeout**: this is not a design issue — it is a symptom of using one timeout for both fast `git` and slow `bd`. Fix inside the implementation task: split into `runFast(250ms)` for git and `runSlow(2000ms)` for bd. Do NOT roll into the design decision.
7. **bd post-hook invalidation coupling**: current bd hooks are shell scripts under `.beads/hooks/`. They must be updated by `xt install --apply` or `bd hooks install` to add the touch step. Guard against xt-uninstalled repos where the hook won't run — fallback is TTL-only, already covered.
8. **Multi-runtime cache write races**: only the lease holder writes. Renders never write. Renderer never mutates cache mtime. Atomic write via `<tmp>-<pid>.json → rename(cache)`, same pattern statusline.mjs already uses.
9. **Test surface**: zero-render-I/O (fixture cache → snapshot render), fail-soft (missing cache → skeleton), stale marker (aged cache → dim), lease contention (3 concurrent starts, exactly one refresh subprocess spawned), worktree cache-path convergence (main + linked worktree both read same file), Pi expansion refresh trigger (Ctrl+O with absent `descendants` fires on-demand refresh).

### Simplification wins vs prior state

- Drops per-agent duplicate refresh work (all agents in a repo share 1 refresh per TTL, not N).
- Drops planned daemon entirely — no election, no orphan reap, no pid staleness, no `xt end` daemon-terminate step.
- Cache is the boundary — no cross-runtime IPC contract to design; both runtimes just read JSON.
- Fixes the visible `no open issues` bug as a side effect (via fail-soft + longer bd timeout).

### Non-recommendations (explicitly rejected)

- Repo-scoped daemon materializer: complexity/failure-mode budget not repaid by any measured win when a shared file already coalesces N agents into 1 refresh.
- Direct `.beads` DB reads: violates constraint and couples to Dolt schema; also would require read-side lock coordination with the bd shared-server.
- Always-on polling: violates NON_GOALS.

title: Forward rendered role task as the initial Pi and Claude user prompt
description:
## PROBLEM

Role resolution currently extracts only system prompt, skills, model, thinking, and extensions from `sp view`; `buildRoleTmuxPlan` launches the runtime without a positional task prompt. The launcher needs to consume specialists child `unitAI-6639v.4` and deliver its rendered task securely as the first user turn.

## SUCCESS

The launcher renders context before provisioning, carries a typed initial-prompt result through the role plan, and sends it once to both Pi and Claude interactive sessions. Existing system prompt and bead metadata behavior remains unchanged.

## SCRUTINY

high

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts`
- narrow command option plumbing if needed
- `cli/src/tests/worktree-session-role.test.ts`
- focused subprocess fixtures for specialists renderer integration

## NON_GOALS

- No prompt rendering inside xtrm-tools.
- No documentation-only changes beyond test fixtures; final docs/smoke belong to sibling validation child.
- No unrelated tmux/session naming or worktree lifecycle changes.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Blocked on the stable renderer contract from specialists `unitAI-6639v.4`.
- Invoke renderer in original repo cwd and before worktree creation.
- Treat prompt text as sensitive. Do not expose it in `ps`, tmux options, logs, launch events, or shell-quoted command strings. Select a runtime-supported secure input mechanism; positional argv is acceptable only if tests prove it is not externally exposed, otherwise use a prompt file consumed as user content, stdin, or runtime control channel.
- The content must enter the user prompt field, never `--system-prompt` or `--append-system-prompt`.
- Preserve interactive mode and all current role/model/skill/passthrough semantics.
- Fail atomically on renderer error.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests distinguish role system prompt from initial user prompt.
- [ ] Pi and Claude receive identical rendered task fixture content as first user turn.
- [ ] No initial prompt when `--role` has no bead unless the approved renderer contract explicitly supplies one.
- [ ] Renderer errors occur before worktree/tmux creation.
- [ ] Special characters and multiline prompts survive transport unchanged.
- [ ] Process/log/pane telemetry inspection finds no full prompt leak.
- [ ] Existing role tests pass.

## OUTPUT

Changed symbols, renderer invocation contract, chosen secure user-prompt transport, focused test output, failure-order proof, and handoff to live-smoke/docs child.

title: Inject specialists-rendered bead task into xt interactive role sessions
description:
## PROBLEM

`xt pi --role <name> --bead <id>` and `xt claude --role ...` currently transport the bead only through `@agent_bead` and `XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD`. They launch an idle interactive runtime with the role system prompt, but no initial user message containing rendered bead/dependency context or mandatory rules. This differs from `sp run`, whose runner renders and sends the tracked task through RPC.

The specialists redesign epic `unitAI-6639v` will expose a specialists-owned read-only task-prompt renderer in child `unitAI-6639v.4`. xtrm-tools must consume that interface and forward its output as the runtime's positional initial prompt without reproducing specialists prompt logic.

## SUCCESS

Both role launchers request the canonical rendered task for the selected role/bead before provisioning, retain tmux/environment bead metadata, and pass the rendered value as the first user message while remaining interactive. No bead or mandatory-rule content is appended to the system prompt. Failure and telemetry behavior are deterministic and tested across Pi and Claude.

## SCRUTINY

high

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts` role resolution/planning/launch path
- `cli/src/commands/pi.ts` and `cli/src/commands/claude.ts` only where argument plumbing requires it
- role-launcher unit/integration tests
- `docs/xt-pi-role.md` and CLI help
- external contract with specialists child `unitAI-6639v.4`

## NON_GOALS

- No reimplementation of bead traversal, task-template rendering, or mandatory-rule resolution.
- No change to normal non-role `xt pi` / `xt claude` launches.
- No system-prompt injection of task content.
- No requirement for byte-identical full runtime envelopes; scope is the canonical initial task prompt plus existing role configuration.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Call the specialists-owned renderer from the original project cwd before creating a worktree or tmux session.
- Hard-fail before provisioning if rendering fails; do not silently launch a contextless tracked coordinator.
- Keep `@agent_bead` and `XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD` as live identity metadata after sending the startup snapshot.
- Pass the rendered prompt as the final positional argument after runtime flags/passthrough processing, with argv-safe handling and no shell interpolation.
- Pi and Claude must remain interactive after the initial turn.
- Do not print, log, or place full rendered prompt text in pane metadata, process listings, or telemetry. If direct argv would expose sensitive prompt text through `ps`, use each runtime's supported file/stdin/RPC transport or add a secure transport before shipping.
- Emit only prompt hash/component sizes and renderer outcome in launch telemetry.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Pi and Claude plans contain an initial user prompt and unchanged role system prompt.
- [ ] Bead context and mandatory rules are absent from system-prompt transport.
- [ ] `@agent_bead` and `XTMUX_AGENT_BEAD` remain available after launch.
- [ ] Missing bead/renderer failure leaves no worktree or tmux session behind.
- [ ] Prompt transport does not leak full content through process arguments, logs, pane options, or telemetry.
- [ ] Live smoke shows the coordinator receives the rendered bead task as its first user turn without manual prompting.
- [ ] Existing role-launcher behavior and non-role launch tests remain green.

## OUTPUT

Consumed renderer contract/version, changed launcher surfaces, secure prompt transport decision, Pi/Claude argv or input-flow evidence, failure-cleanup evidence, live smoke transcript, docs updates, and residual parity differences from `sp run`.

title: Hook commands and pi settings legacy-strip miss canonical paths
description:
PROBLEM: two v0.10.1 gaps surfaced by fleet audit after v0.10.1 shipped.

(1) policies/service-skills-claude.json (compiled to .xtrm/config/hooks.json) references $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/{cataloger,skill_activator,drift_detector}.py. That path only resolves when the service-skills skill is enabled AND the direct-runtime-links symlink exists at .claude/skills/service-skills. In 17/19 fleet consumers the skill is NOT enabled so the path is broken — every SessionStart/PreToolUse/PostToolUse fires 'python3: can't open file' and either blocks or emits noise. The scripts themselves are registry-gated (no-op if no service-registry.json), but Python can't gate what it can't load. Also demonstrated in this session: removing .claude/skills on the source repo bricked Bash tool until a subagent restored it.

(2) cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts LEGACY_XTRM_SKILLS_ENTRIES set contains only '../.xtrm/skills/active', '~/.xtrm/skills/active', '~/.xtrm/skills/default'. It misses the per-runtime suffix variants '../.xtrm/skills/active/pi', '../.xtrm/skills/active/claude', '~/.xtrm/skills/active/pi', '~/.xtrm/skills/active/claude' — so normalizePiSkillsEntries doesn't strip them from .pi/settings.json. Fleet audit found 6 repos with '../.xtrm/skills/active/pi' residue that survived every xt update --apply.

SUCCESS: (1) All 19 fleet consumers pass hook-resolvability check after xt update --apply. Hook commands reference the canonical .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/ path which is present in every consumer via install. Scripts themselves keep registry-gating. (2) LEGACY set extended to cover the suffix variants; xt update --apply strips them from .pi/settings.json.

SCOPE: policies/service-skills-claude.json (3 hook commands), .xtrm/config/hooks.json (regenerated), .xtrm/registry.json (regenerated), cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts LEGACY_XTRM_SKILLS_ENTRIES set + regression test.

VALIDATION: [ ] compile-policies produces the updated hooks.json. [ ] Fleet audit script reports 19/19 hook scripts resolve on all consumers. [ ] Unit test for normalizePiSkillsEntries covers all 8 legacy path variants.
close_reason: Landed in v0.10.2 (db7a2df5). Fleet sweep pending post-publish.

title: Prune retired managed skills on xt update --apply
description:
PROBLEM: scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage() returns noop for a real .xtrm/skills/default/ directory, so xt update --apply leaves retired managed skills (e.g. using-specialists-v3) on disk after the vendor set shrinks. Repro: fixture with real default/using-specialists-v3/ + active symlink; after update --apply --strict-registry, exit 0 but v3 remains.

SUCCESS: xt update --apply removes any .xtrm/skills/default/<name>/ that is not in the current registry manifest, and removes matching .xtrm/skills/active/<name> symlinks. User-owned active content (real dirs, or symlinks pointing outside default/) is never touched. Regression smoke covers the fixture case.

SCOPE: cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts (add pruneRetiredManagedSkills), cli/src/commands/install.ts (wire into runInstall between scaffold and installFromRegistry), cli/src/tests/registry-scaffold.test.ts (unit coverage), cli/src/tests/install-integration.test.ts or new smoke (regression).

NON_GOALS: No compatibility aliases. No changes to scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage semantics for missing/symlink/global paths. No modifications to user-authored skill trees. No release cut here — this lands under xtrm-1o63w's release.

CONSTRAINTS: Managed default = .xtrm/skills/default/<name>/ where <name> is not in the current registry's skills asset file list. Only prune directories (or dir-target symlinks) whose name is retired. Never remove files at the top level of default/. Respect --dry-run. Regenerate cli/dist after source changes.

VALIDATION: [ ] Unit test: prune returns list of removed names on retired dir, noop when all in registry, respects dryRun. [ ] Integration smoke: real default/using-specialists-v3/ + active symlink; after runInstall (or xt update --apply) the dir and symlink are gone; using-specialists remains. [ ] Existing scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage tests still pass unchanged. [ ] npm run build succeeds; dist verify-clean.

OUTPUT: New pruneRetiredManagedSkills function, wired call site, unit + smoke tests, rebuilt cli/dist.
close_reason: Prune wired between scaffold and installFromRegistry. 6 unit tests + 1 collector test + 2 e2e integration smokes. Removes retired managed defaults and matching active symlinks; user real dirs and out-of-tree symlinks preserved; noops when registry lacks skills asset. Honors overrideRoots?.skills for global mode. Rebuilt cli/dist. Full CLI suite 777 pass; 1 pre-existing test/skills-migration failure unchanged (parent scope). Landing before xtrm-1o63w merge is fine — with v3 still in registry, prune noops on it.

title: Direct-symlink runtime dirs + retire active/ everywhere + collision/reconcile/managed-links
description:
## PROBLEM

Under the pre-v2 architecture, xt materializes a merged view at .xtrm/skills/active/ (both global and project scopes) and tunnels it to the runtimes via .claude/skills (dir symlink) and .pi/settings.json.skills[] (array entry). Session 2026-07-10 smoke pass surfaced four wiring bugs (dangling active/ symlinks post-migrate, stale .pi/settings.json pointer, broken .claude/skills chain, cleanSettingsJsonEntries reads wrong path). Third audit pass (xtrm-y0tdg, xt-skills session 2026-07-11) confirmed all four and traced the root cause to the active/ view abstraction itself: it exists to solve tier composition + per-runtime selection, but under the global-first + direct-runtime-native-discovery model neither problem is worth solving with a materialized intermediate view.

The runtimes read their native locations natively — Claude Code merges <repo>/.claude/skills/ + ~/.claude/skills/ at read time (docs confirmed: enterprise > personal > project > bundled precedence); Pi 0.74.2 loads .pi/skills/ natively as a trusted project source (verified: dist/core/skills.js:343-345 in the installed pi package). Both silently prefer user-global over project on runtime-name collision, which means our current "silent shadow" behavior is a real correctness bug we've been hiding via the tunnel.

## SUCCESS

Global scope:
- ~/.xtrm/skills/active/ DELETED.
- ~/.claude/skills is a dir symlink pointing directly at ~/.xtrm/skills/default/.
- ~/.pi/agent/skills is a dir symlink pointing directly at ~/.xtrm/skills/default/.
- Release-gate invariant: every shipped skill under ~/.xtrm/skills/default/ has dirname === frontmatter.name (or absent frontmatter.name). New check in gen-registry.mjs or a check-* script.

Project scope:
- <repo>/.xtrm/skills/active/ retired concept. Migration deletes it if present.
- <repo>/.claude/skills/ = real directory, populated by xt with per-skill symlinks named by runtime-name, pointing at absolute paths into either <repo>/.xtrm/skills/<pack>/ or ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/<pack>/.
- <repo>/.pi/skills/ = real directory, same shape.
- <repo>/.pi/settings.json.skills[] no longer carries xt-managed entries. Empty or user-only.
- state.json extended with managedLinks: { claude: { <runtime-name>: <relative-path> }, pi: { <runtime-name>: <relative-path> } }.

Enable/disable/reconcile primitive:
- New cli/src/core/skills-runtime-reconcile.ts exposing reconcileRuntimeLinks({ projectRoot, state, runtime, discoveredPacks, globalDefaultRoot, globalOptionalRoot }).
- Called by xt skills enable, xt skills disable, xt init, xt update --apply. Idempotent, retry-safe.
- Writes each link via temp-symlink + atomic rename. Updates state.json.managedLinks LAST.
- Reap: only removes links tracked in state.json.managedLinks that are not in the newly-computed desired set. Non-managed links (user-owned) untouched.
- MANDATORY collision check at enable/reconcile time: for each candidate runtime-name, verify no collision with any skill in global default (both runtimes silently prefer global; a silent shadow is worse than an error). Refuse the enable with a clear message.
- Reject same-name project pack + global optional collision at pack resolution time. String-keyed enabledPacks stays.

v1 runtime compatibility (Blocker 1 answer):
- xt init and xt update --apply, when they see a legacy .xtrm/skills/user/packs/* layout at project scope, run the reconcile primitive against the v1 discovery output. Runtime dirs stay populated correctly during the shim window even if the operator never runs xt migrate skills-layout.
- Explicit xt migrate skills-layout (in .1) is required for the destructive data-plane move.

Reap ownership (Blocker 2 answer):
- state.json.managedLinks is the authoritative record of xt-owned links. Reap only touches these entries. Any link in .claude/skills/ or .pi/skills/ NOT in managedLinks is user-owned and never touched.
- Missing/corrupt managedLinks (upgrade from pre-v2 state.json): reconcile bootstraps by discovering existing xt-managed links via a probe (only symlinks whose target resolves inside ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/ OR <repo>/.xtrm/skills/ AND that match a discovered skill's expected path), then persists the manifest. One-time cost per repo.

Bug fixes rolled in from the original session 2026-07-10 findings:
- cleanSettingsJsonEntries: target <repo>/.pi/settings.json (not <repo>/.pi/agent/settings.json — global). Currently only invoked from hooks migration; still fix it.
- The original four dangling-symlink bugs from the smoke pass dissolve under this design: there's no active/ to leave dangling, no stale .pi/settings.json entry to update, no broken .claude/skills chain.

Ancillary code:
- cli/src/core/skills-materializer.ts: DELETED (active/ view builder, atomic swap dance, rebuildAllRuntimeActiveViews, rebuildProjectActiveView).
- cli/src/core/skills-runtime-views.ts: rewritten to verify direct-symlink state (real .claude/skills dir, real .pi/skills dir, expected symlinks match managedLinks).
- cli/src/core/skills-scaffold.ts: ensureAgentsSkillsSymlink deleted (no more .claude/skills dir symlink); replaced by reconcile primitive invocation.
- cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts: skills entry management for .pi/settings.json.skills[] deleted; xt-managed entries removed on next update.
- cli/src/core/project-skills-content.ts: NEW canonical hasProjectScopedSkillsContent implementation. Imported by all three previous callers (skills-runtime-views.ts, skills-scaffold.ts, pi-runtime.ts). Duplicates deleted.
- cli/src/commands/init.ts GitNexus cleanup step: retarget from .xtrm/skills/active/gitnexus (dead) to <repo>/.claude/skills/gitnexus (real dir under new model). GitNexus writes there; must not pollute managed link dir.
- cli/src/core/worktree-session.ts: Claude worktree fallback rewritten to ensure the real .claude/skills dir + reconcile links rather than creating a dir symlink.
- scripts/check-layout-guards.mjs: reversed — reject any skills/active/ payload path (was allowing flat active).
- .specialists/user/parallel-review.specialist.json and researcher.specialist.json: rewrite active/ paths to reference ~/.xtrm/skills/default/ absolute paths (or the documented specialists global resolver).

Tests:
- cli/src/tests/skills-runtime-reconcile.test.ts: new. Cases: enable idempotent, disable idempotent, collision-against-global-default rejection, same-name project+global-optional rejection, non-managed link left alone, temp-symlink+rename atomicity, state.json.managedLinks written last, v1 discovery reconcile path, mixed managed+non-managed dir handling.
- cli/src/tests/skills-runtime-views.test.ts: rewrite to check real dirs, not active/ view.
- cli/src/tests/skills-materializer.test.ts: DELETED.
- cli/src/tests/pi-runtime.test.ts: .pi/settings.json.skills[] cleanup assertion.
- cli/src/tests/migrate.test.ts: cleanSettingsJsonEntries path fix, no active/ leftover post-migrate assertion (already-migrated repos on next update lose their active/ dir cleanly).
- cli/test/init-phases.test.ts: GitNexus cleanup targets .claude/skills/gitnexus real dir.
- Full CLI test suite green.

Docs (minimal here; large sweep in .1):
- One-time upgrade note in update-xt/SKILL.md: "the active/ concept is retired in this release; xt update --apply will reconcile your .claude/skills/ and .pi/skills/ automatically."

## SCOPE

Code — cli/src (highlights above). Full list will be in the implementation PR.

Tests — highlights above.

Docs — update-xt/SKILL.md upgrade note. Larger docs sweep in .1.

Runtime pointers — set by xt init global bootstrap, refreshed by xt update --apply.

Specialists YAML files — small hand edits to two files.

## NON_GOALS

- Layout flatten and PACK.json removal (.1 owns these).
- Docs sweep beyond the upgrade note (.1 owns it).
- Scope-aware enabledPacks (Blocker 3 answer: reject same-name collisions instead).
- Restore semantics for migrations made under active/ era across the v2 cutover (restore preflight refuses cleanly).
- Migrating pre-existing shipped skill dirname/frontmatter mismatches at the global level (fix in a follow-up bead if any exist; likely none).
- Retaining PACK.json parsing under the v1 shim (see .1 — warned-and-ignored).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Zero silent data loss. If a user has hand-linked skills into .claude/skills/ or .pi/skills/, they survive every xt operation.
- Reconcile is idempotent under all conditions (partial write, retry, upgrade, migration, no-op).
- state.json.managedLinks written LAST after all links; a crash mid-write leaves a consistent state that reconciles cleanly on retry.
- Collision check identical logic for Claude and Pi.
- Restore of the runtime dir state is unnecessary — reconcile from state.json recreates it deterministically at any time.

## VALIDATION

- Unit: skills-runtime-reconcile.test.ts (12+ cases per above).
- Integration: end-to-end xt skills enable → verify real .claude/skills/ + .pi/skills/ have the expected symlinks pointing at the correct absolute paths; state.json.managedLinks matches; xt skills disable reverses cleanly; xt update --apply from v1 layout populates runtime dirs.
- Regression: full cli test suite green.
- Manual: repeat the 5-repo smoke (console, vaultctl, specialists, treasury-cb, darth-feedor). Verify (a) 0 dangling symlinks anywhere, (b) enabled packs surface correctly in Claude Code and Pi, (c) collision against shipped global default is refused with a clear error, (d) upgrade from v1 state.json bootstraps managedLinks without losing enabled packs.
- Global smoke: readlink ~/.claude/skills = ~/.xtrm/skills/default; readlink ~/.pi/agent/skills = ~/.xtrm/skills/default.

## OUTPUT

Files touched (per-file), test count, smoke evidence per-repo, before/after diff of one consumer's .claude/skills/ and .pi/skills/ trees.

## DEPENDS ON

Nothing. This bead ships first. Its reconcile primitive is layout-agnostic — it consumes a discovered-packs input, and .1's discovery rewrite plugs a new input in without changing this bead's code.

title: Repo skills tree v2: flatten to .xtrm/skills/<pack>/, drop PACK.json, retire project active/
description:
## PROBLEM

Repo skills tree carries three dead layers under the v2 model: user/packs/ nesting, PACK.json per pack, and .xtrm/skills/active/ materialized view. See parent xtrm-y0tdg for the full rationale — after the global-skills epic moved default/+optional/ to global scope and the direct-symlink runtime model (child .2) retires active/, everything under <repo>/.xtrm/skills/ is a plain flat pack, discoverable from filesystem shape alone.

## SUCCESS

- Discovery loader treats every non-reserved top-level dir under <repo>/.xtrm/skills/ (excl. reserved: state.json) as a pack. In shim window also excl. default, optional, user, active, local-legacy.
- A pack's skills = (a) <pack>/SKILL.md at root if present, exposed as skill named <pack> (frontmatter.name wins if set); (b) each direct child dir with SKILL.md exposed as skill named after the child dir.
- PACK.json is neither read nor written under v2. If present it is ignored with a one-time warning per session per pack.
- xt migrate skills-layout --apply moves user/packs/<pack>/ → <pack>/, drops PACK.json files, deletes .xtrm/skills/active/ (project scope), reconciles runtime dirs via the direct-symlink primitive from .2.
- local-legacy pack (from xt migrate skills) written at <repo>/.xtrm/skills/local-legacy/ with no PACK.json.
- Service-skills library (bootstrap.py, layout_migrator.py, umbrella_generator.py) plus scope.py, scaffolder.py, cataloger.py, drift_detector.py rewritten to v2 paths.
- Docs sweep: update-xt/SKILL.md, service-skills references, specialists-creator, creating-service-skills, using-service-skills.

title: Repo skills layout v2 + migrate wiring completion
description:
## PROBLEM

The xtrm-bq7yd epic shipped the data-plane half of the global-skills migration (shipped skills move to ~/.xtrm/skills/default; per-repo default/ + optional/ get removed on xt migrate). The wiring plane and the layout itself are still shaped for the pre-epic world. Session 2026-07-10 smoke pass across ~/dev/{console,vaultctl,specialists} + ~/projects/mercury/{treasury-cb,darth-feedor} surfaced four wiring bugs plus one design cliff. Three audit passes on this bead (xt-skills session 2026-07-11) confirmed the diagnosis and drove a substantially simpler design.

Locked design: retire the materialized active/ view at BOTH scopes; xt skills enable/disable populates the runtimes' native skill directories directly (.claude/skills/ and .pi/skills/); global stays global, project stays project, no cross-view composition; global optional/ tier is retained (xtrm-vendored content); repo layout flattens to .xtrm/skills/<pack>/ with no PACK.json; runtime pointers at global become single-hop symlinks into default/.

## SUCCESS

Global layout:
- ~/.xtrm/skills/default/ = shipped, always active. Invariant: dirname === frontmatter.name (release-gate enforced).
- ~/.xtrm/skills/optional/ = shipped, opt-in per-repo via state.json.enabledPacks.
- No ~/.xtrm/skills/active/; ~/.claude/skills and ~/.pi/agent/skills are dir symlinks direct to ~/.xtrm/skills/default/.

Project layout:
- <repo>/.xtrm/skills/state.json = { schemaVersion, enabledPacks: {claude, pi}, managedLinks: {claude, pi} }.
- <repo>/.xtrm/skills/<pack>/ = flat top-level packs. Each pack has no PACK.json.
- No .xtrm/skills/{default,optional,user,active}/ at project scope.
- <repo>/.claude/skills/ = real dir of xt-managed symlinks populated on xt skills enable.
- <repo>/.pi/skills/ = real dir of xt-managed symlinks (Pi natively discovers these; no .pi/settings.json.skills[] entry needed).

Discovery:
- Non-reserved top-level dir under .xtrm/skills/ is a pack. pack.name = dirname.
- Pack skills: (a) <pack>/SKILL.md if present, runtimeName = frontmatter.name ?? dirname; (b) each direct child dir with SKILL.md, same rule.
- Legacy PACK.json warned once per session, never parsed.

Enable/reconcile semantics:
- xt skills enable <pack> resolves via priority: project pack > global optional > default (already active; refused) > not-found (error).
- Collision check MANDATORY at enable time against global default (Pi and Claude both silently prefer user-global over project). Reject with clear error.
- Reject same-name project pack + global optional collisions (enabledPacks stays string-keyed).
- For each runtime enabled-for, write <repo>/<runtime-skills-dir>/<runtime-name> -> <absolute-path> via temp-symlink + rename. Update managedLinks in state.json LAST after all links are written.
- xt init and xt update --apply reconcile the runtime dirs from either v1 or v2 discovery automatically (v1 runtime compatibility path).
- Reap: only remove links tracked in state.json.managedLinks that are not in the newly-computed desired set. Non-managed links (user-owned) untouched.

Migration:
- xt migrate skills-layout --apply: user/packs/<pack>/ → <pack>/, drop PACK.json, delete active/ at project scope. Reconciles runtime dirs post-move.
- Existing xt migrate skills (data-plane) unchanged; its restore sidecar is retired (no external pointer state to snapshot under direct-symlink model).

Docs:
- update-xt/SKILL.md sweep, service-skills library docs sweep, specialists-creator/creating-service-skills references to PACK.json / user/packs updated.

## SCOPE

Two children:
- .1 — Repo skills tree v2: layout flatten, drop PACK.json, retire project active/, docs sweep.
- .2 — Direct-symlink runtime dirs + retire global active/ + collision/reconcile/managed-links machinery.

Ordering: .2 first (owns the reconcile function that .1 will plug new discovery into), .1 second. Under this ordering the reconcile machinery is layout-agnostic; .1 swaps the discovery input without touching runtime materialization.

## NON_GOALS

- Flattening the global tree (~/.xtrm/skills/default and /optional keep their tier structure at global scope; those are xtrm-vendored payloads).
- Changing enabledPacks: { claude, pi } schema shape (managedLinks is additive; string values).
- Silent auto-migration of the layout on any command other than explicit xt update --apply or xt migrate skills-layout.
- Removing the xtrm-hzkdk local-legacy pack repair; it stays as-is but becomes dead code under v2 (no PACK.json written for local-legacy either).
- Adding project-shadows-global runtime-name precedence semantics.
- Restoring backups made under active/ era across the v2 cutover — restore preflight will refuse if state has changed shape.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Deprecation window: 2 minor releases where v1 layout discovery still resolves for xt skills enable/reconcile purposes; native runtime discovery works throughout via auto-reconciled runtime dirs.
- Restore semantics for xt migrate skills remain "reverses migrate only"; the ordering caveat stays documented.
- Preserve docs/skills-ownership.json ownership.
- No new dependencies. No new secrets.
- Runtime-name collision detection is MANDATORY across scopes at enable time; must be identical logic for Claude and Pi.

## VALIDATION

- Full cli test suite pass.
- New tests: v2 layout discovery, v1 discovery shim, runtime-link reconciliation (idempotent, retry-safe, ownership preserved), collision-against-global-default rejection, same-name-project-vs-global-optional rejection, managed-link manifest round-trip, xt migrate skills-layout on fixture with service-skills umbrella.
- Manual smoke: repeat the 5-repo pass (console, vaultctl, specialists, treasury-cb, darth-feedor). Verify (a) 0 dangling symlinks anywhere post-migrate, (b) xt update --apply on migrated repos surfaces enabled packs correctly, (c) claude and pi see the expected skills.
- Docs render check: xt docs show update-xt describes v2.

## OUTPUT

Two child beads shipped in the ordering above. Consolidated smoke evidence. Docs sweep summary. Deprecation warning in the layout resolver. Shim window scheduled for release N+2.

## AUDIT HISTORY

Three audit passes on this bead by xt-skills session 2026-07-11 (openai-codex/gpt-5.6-terra/high). Full audit notes preserved in this bead's notes. Verdicts: pass 1 = needs-revision, pass 2 = needs-revision, pass 3 = needs-revision-with-locked-answers-in-three-blockers.

Locked answers to pass 3 blockers:
- Blocker 1 (v1 runtime compatibility): xt init and xt update --apply auto-reconcile runtime dirs from v1 sources during the shim window. Explicit xt migrate skills-layout handles the destructive data-plane move.
- Blocker 2 (reap ownership): managed-link manifest in state.json.managedLinks tracks xt-owned links per runtime. Reap only removes tracked links not in the newly-computed desired set. Non-managed links are always safe.
- Blocker 3 (same-name project vs global optional): reject with error. enabledPacks stays string-keyed. Scope-aware shadowing deferred to a future bead if a real product case arises.
notes: Hooks-migration parity triage: NOT fold into y0tdg. Hooks are project-owned policy runtime (settings use $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.xtrm/hooks); globalizing risks hook/config ownership drift. Correct target is role-worktree hook scaffold parity (option c), but needs dedicated migration/runtime epic due install/migrate/restore/template implications. Filed follow-up epic.

title: debugger: profile and bound Claude statusline CPU bursts
description:
## PROBLEM

`/home/dawid/.xtrm/hooks/statusline.mjs`, invoked as Claude Code's statusline provider, has shown transient 100%+ CPU bursts. Frequent concurrent session ticks amplify host load.

## SUCCESS

Profiled evidence identifies the hot operation. The statusline returns best-effort within 50 ms, serves a valid stale shared cache while refresh is slow, and prevents cross-session refresh stampedes. A persistent helper is permitted only if a lease-protected short-lived refresh cannot meet the contract.

## SCOPE

- `/home/dawid/.xtrm/hooks/statusline.mjs` and its tracked source counterpart
- minimal test/benchmark support only when required
- per-user cache/lock state under an appropriate runtime cache directory

## NON_GOALS

- no speculative rewrite
- no broad Claude Code or beads redesign
- no always-running daemon unless evidence proves it necessary

## CONSTRAINTS

- Collect supplied ps/perf evidence first when a live process is observable; record when unavailable
- profile wall/CPU time, subprocesses, files read, and concurrency
- renderer has a 50 ms budget and must not synchronously run slow work
- cache writes atomic; corrupt/missing/unreadable cache safe; stale cache preferred to blocking
- one refresh lease across sessions; no stampede
- preserve useful output

## VALIDATION

- reproducible timing/CPU and slow-dependency tests
- concurrent invocation test
- cache corruption and stale fallback test
- before/after `ps`/`perf` evidence when process availability permits

## OUTPUT

Root-cause evidence, hot function, minimal diff, test commands/results, before/after measurements, and whether helper was needed.

SCRUTINY: high
notes: Profiled locally because no live statusline PID existed and perf is not installed: cold 391-545ms wall / 286-354ms CPU; five concurrent cold calls showed five Node processes at 54-64% CPU. Root cause: cache-miss path synchronously launches 5 Git plus Beads shell-outs via execSync; per-worktree cache lacks a refresh lease. Implemented cache-only renderer with detached lease-protected refresh, shared Beads cache, atomic cache writes, stale/fallback rendering, and 250ms background command caps. Active /home/dawid/.xtrm/hooks/statusline.mjs patched from source; source remains uncommitted pending operator publish instruction.

title: xt migrate: local-legacy pack generation is broken (flattened tree + wrong PACK.json name)
description:
## PROBLEM

cli/src/commands/migrate.ts:302-313 builds the local-legacy override pack for diverged files with two defects that produce an invalid, unusable pack:

1. **Flattened tree**: uses `path.join(legacyRoot, path.basename(relPath))` — every file in every diverged skill dir collapses to legacyRoot/<basename>, causing silent overwrites (all SKILL.md files land at the same path, only the last one wins).
2. **Wrong PACK.json name**: if any diverged file is `optional/xt-optional/PACK.json` (or similar), it gets copied into local-legacy/PACK.json verbatim, so the pack ends up with `name: "xt-optional"` instead of `name: "local-legacy"`. This blocks `xt update` on the consumer with 'Invalid pack metadata: name must match directory local-legacy'.

Reproduced live during smoke test on ~/dev/console during release-prep 2026-07-10. All prior migrations that hit the diverged path have poisoned pack layouts.

## SUCCESS

- Diverged files preserve their directory structure under local-legacy/ (default/xt-optional/PACK.json → local-legacy/xt-optional/PACK.json, etc.).
- local-legacy/PACK.json is authored fresh with name='local-legacy', schemaVersion='1', skills=[<top-level skill dirs discovered under local-legacy>]. Source-pack PACK.json files are skipped (never overwrite the authoritative one).
- xt update succeeds after migrate on a repo with diverged files.
- Existing broken local-legacy on ~/dev/console repaired inline as part of the fix so xt update stops failing.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/commands/migrate.ts:295-314 — preserve nested paths + skip source PACK.json + write authoritative local-legacy/PACK.json.
- cli/src/tests/migrate.test.ts — new test: 'diverged pack preserves nested directory structure' + 'local-legacy PACK.json has name=local-legacy'.
- Manual fix: ~/dev/console/.xtrm/skills/user/packs/local-legacy/PACK.json rewrite name to 'local-legacy'.

## NON_GOALS

- Migrating skills[] list format changes.
- Reworking the divergence detection logic.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve backward compatibility with existing local-legacy dirs (fix in place, don't require operator action).
- No new dependencies.

## VALIDATION

- cd cli && npx vitest run src/tests/migrate.test.ts — existing 19 pass + 2 new = 21/21.
- Manual smoke: xt migrate skills --apply --yes --repo <fake-diverged-repo>, then verify local-legacy/PACK.json.name === 'local-legacy' and file tree preserved.
- xt update --apply --repo ~/dev/console succeeds without pack-metadata error.

## OUTPUT

Files touched, test count, evidence of xt update passing on ~/dev/console.

## PROBLEM

`xt migrate` only checks that `.xtrm/` exists at the target repo path (cli/src/commands/migrate.ts:492). This gate is satisfied by the xtrm-tools source repo itself, which ships tracked `.xtrm/skills/default/`, `.xtrm/skills/optional/`, `.xtrm/hooks/`, `.xtrm/config/` — the SSOT payload vendored into the npm package.

If an operator runs `xt migrate --apply` (or `xt migrate skills --apply --yes`) with `cwd = /home/dawid/dev/core` (or any other clone of xtrm-tools):

- SHA-verify identical against `~/.xtrm/skills/default/` (populated by prior bootstrap from this same repo) → all files marked safe-delete → `.xtrm/skills/default` and `.xtrm/skills/optional` are removed from the tracked tree after a tarball backup.
- SHA-verify against empty/absent global tree → all files marked diverged → moved into `.xtrm/skills/user/packs/local-legacy/`, corrupting the on-disk layout the packager expects.
- Either path leaves the source repo unable to run `npm run gen-registry` cleanly, and a subsequent `git status` reveals a catastrophic diff.

Backup exists but `--restore` is deferred (Batch E non-goal), so recovery is manual git.

## SUCCESS

Running `xt migrate <any-target> --apply --yes` from a source-repo checkout refuses with a clear error and non-zero exit before touching the filesystem. Dry-run keeps printing (a preview is harmless), but the destructive path is gated.

## SCOPE

`cli/src/commands/migrate.ts`: add `isSourceRepo(repoPath)` helper called immediately after the `.xtrm/` existence check. A repo is a source repo when ANY of:

1. `<repoPath>/package.json.name === 'xtrm-tools'`
2. `<repoPath>/scripts/gen-registry.mjs` exists (canonical marker; the file only lives in the source repo)
3. `<repoPath>/.xtrm/registry.json` was written by gen-registry (contains `assets`) AND `<repoPath>/scripts/vendor-specialists-skills.mjs` exists

Any of the three → refuse with:

  `Refusing to migrate xtrm-tools source repo <repoPath>: <marker>. Migration is intended for consumers.`

Also add `--force-source` operator escape hatch (invisible in --help; documented in bead notes only) so future maintainers can migrate a fork for testing without patching the guard.

Tests:

- `cli/src/tests/migrate.test.ts`: new test 'refuses --apply on source repo (package.json name)', 'refuses --apply on source repo (gen-registry marker)', '--dry-run allowed on source repo', '--force-source overrides guard'.
- Existing 'fails on non-xtrm repo' test still passes.

## NON_GOALS

- Adding `--restore <backup>` (separate follow-up).
- Changing dry-run behavior (dry-run stays safe on any target).
- Broader repo-type detection (mercury/other consumer repos should still migrate).

## CONSTRAINTS

- No changes to `migrateSkills` / `migrateHooks` internals — this is a pre-flight guard only.
- Guard runs BEFORE the confirmation prompt so operators don't have to answer 'yes' just to hit the block.
- Error message names the specific marker matched so the operator understands why.

## VALIDATION

- cd cli && npm run typecheck && npm run build
- cd cli && npx vitest run src/tests/migrate.test.ts (expect 10/10 → 14/14 with 4 new cases)
- Manual smoke: `node cli/dist/index.cjs migrate skills --apply --yes` from /home/dawid/dev/core prints refusal, exit code 1, .xtrm/skills untouched.

## OUTPUT

Files touched + test count + smoke evidence.
close_reason: implemented source-repo guard: isSourceRepo detects 3 markers, refuses --apply with clear error, --force-source escape hatch, 4 new tests pass (14/14), smoke against real source repo refuses cleanly with exit 1

title: Batch J: Global hooks migration — ~/.xtrm/hooks + ~/.claude/settings.json safe-merge with source tagging
description:
## PROBLEM

Default hook payloads (`beads-*.mjs`, `quality-check.*`, `specialists-agent-guard.mjs`, `using-xtrm-reminder.mjs`, `worktree-boundary.mjs`, `xtrm-*-logger.mjs`, plus `gitnexus/` and `specialists/` subdirs) are copied per-repo via `installFromRegistry` and wired into `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` via `reconcileProjectClaudeHooks`. In a fleet of N xtrm-managed repos, one hook release means N copies + N settings.json rewrites. There is already ONE global-hook precedent (`ensureGlobalStatusLine` at `claude-runtime-sync.ts:245-260` — writes `~/.xtrm/hooks/statusline.mjs` into `~/.claude/settings.json.statusLine` with idempotent merge). This batch extends that pattern to the full canonical hook set. Existing bead `xtrm-s5ih5` explicitly warns against blind overwrites into `~/.claude/settings.json` — the design has to safe-merge per entry, not clobber.

## SUCCESS

- `~/.xtrm/hooks/` is the global SSOT payload dir (copied from package on bootstrap).
- `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` is the canonical wiring config globally.
- `~/.claude/settings.json` receives xtrm-owned hook entries under `hooks`, each entry tagged `{_source: "xtrm-global"}` so future syncs know what they own.
- Non-xtrm keys in `~/.claude/settings.json` (permissions, model, statusLine, other tools' hooks, user-added entries without a source tag) are preserved byte-identically across re-syncs.
- Same treatment for `~/.pi/settings.json`.
- Under `XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS=1`, consumer `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` no longer receives the global-owned entries; project-scoped entries (service-skills PostToolUse output) remain.
- Idempotence: `xt bootstrap` twice → no writes on second run.

## SCOPE

- New `cli/src/core/global-hooks-bootstrap.ts` — copies `<pkg>/.xtrm/hooks/` (including `gitnexus/`, `specialists/` subdirs) to `~/.xtrm/hooks/`; copies `<pkg>/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` to `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json`. Uses `fs-extra` copy with the same excludes as skills bootstrap. Writes `~/.xtrm/hooks/state.json` with `{installedVersion, installedFrom, installedAt}`.
- `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:198-239` — add `reconcileGlobalClaudeHooks({dryRun})`. Reads canonical from `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json`, resolves hook commands to `~/.xtrm/hooks/*.mjs`, applies to `~/.claude/settings.json` via per-entry safe-merge:
  - For each canonical hook entry: attach `_source: "xtrm-global"`.
  - For each existing entry in target settings: if `_source == "xtrm-global"` OR content matches an entry we own → replace. Else → PRESERVE, log warning `hook.entry.foreign` with entry hash.
- `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:245-260` — `ensureGlobalStatusLine` becomes a thin adapter (or removed if `reconcileGlobalClaudeHooks` covers `statusLine`).
- New `cli/src/core/pi-runtime-hooks.ts` — analog for Pi: `reconcileGlobalPiHooks()` merges into `~/.pi/settings.json`. Follows same source-tagging.
- `scripts/gen-registry.mjs:16-33` — add `install_scope` field to `hooks` and `config` asset entries. Default hooks under `.xtrm/hooks/{beads-*.mjs, quality-check.*, specialists-agent-guard.mjs, using-xtrm-reminder.mjs, worktree-boundary.mjs, xtrm-*-logger.mjs, gitnexus/**, specialists/**, statusline.mjs}` tagged `global`. Anything project-specific (service-skills output paths under `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/install/settings.json` — not a hook payload but a settings template) stays project.
- `cli/src/commands/bootstrap.ts` (from Batch B) — invoke `ensureGlobalHooksBootstrapped` + `reconcileGlobalClaudeHooks` + `reconcileGlobalPiHooks`.
- `cli/src/commands/install.ts`, `init.ts`, `update.ts` — self-heal hook path added alongside skills self-heal.
- Feature flag: `XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS=1` gates all destructive behavior; with flag off, per-repo path unchanged.

## NON_GOALS

- Migrating existing consumer `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` hook entries — deferred to Batch E (migration skill) which handles cleanup.
- Removing `reconcileProjectClaudeHooks` — it stays for project-scoped hook overrides.
- Refactoring the hook implementations themselves (e.g. `beads-*.mjs`) — payloads move as-is.
- Changing Pi hook loading semantics.
- New hook wiring for the migration skill — reuse existing entry points.
- Migration of `xtrm-s5ih5` behavior — that bead is subsumed by the source-tagging design; close it as validated by this batch once shipped.

## CONSTRAINTS

- **Safe-merge invariant**: `~/.claude/settings.json` bytes outside the `hooks` field never change. `hooks` field changes only for entries owned by `xtrm-global` (source-tagged) or matching hash of a canonical entry.
- Source-tag format: `_source: "xtrm-global"` (string, not array). Additional metadata under `_xtrm: {version, installedAt, hash}` on each owned entry.
- `xtrm-s5ih5` guarantee: user-authored hook entries without a source tag are NEVER replaced. If canonical wants to add an entry that conflicts, log warning and skip.
- Feature flag `XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS=1` — off in v-next-1 (preview), on in v-next-2 (default), removed in v-next-3.
- Hooks must be robust to being wired globally: every hook payload gets a fast-fail guard `if (!process.env.CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR || !fs.existsSync(path.join(process.cwd(), '.xtrm'))) return` at entry, so a global wiring doesn't break sessions outside xtrm-managed dirs. Audit existing hooks; add guards where missing.
- Idempotence: re-sync where nothing changed is a no-op (byte-identical `~/.claude/settings.json` mtime unchanged when checked with `-e`).
- Logging: emit to `~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` (yes, same file — component tag distinguishes). Events: `hook.bootstrap.{start,ok}`, `hook.reconcile.{start,merged,ok}`, `hook.entry.{owned-replaced,foreign-preserved,new-added}`. Fields: `{timestamp, component: "hooks-migration", entryKey, source, action, outcome, durationMs}`. Never log hook command strings that might contain sensitive paths — hash them.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fresh HOME + `xt bootstrap`: `~/.xtrm/hooks/` populated identically to package `.xtrm/hooks/`; `~/.claude/settings.json.hooks` contains all canonical entries with `_source: "xtrm-global"`.
- [ ] `xt bootstrap` twice: second run makes zero writes (verified via mtime of `~/.claude/settings.json`).
- [ ] User-authored entry preservation: fixture `~/.claude/settings.json` with `hooks: {PreToolUse: [{matcher:"foo", hooks:[{command:"my-tool"}]}]}` → after bootstrap, that entry is still present, un-tagged, and canonical xtrm entries are added alongside.
- [ ] `xtrm-s5ih5` scenario: entry manually authored to run `beads-claim-sync.mjs` with a custom path is NOT replaced by the canonical entry pointing at `~/.xtrm/hooks/beads-claim-sync.mjs` — log warning surfaces the conflict.
- [ ] Consumer `xt update --apply XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS=1` in an unmigrated repo: `<repo>/.claude/settings.json.hooks` NO LONGER re-materializes the global entries; project-only entries (service-skills PostToolUse) remain intact.
- [ ] Flag OFF regression: fixture repo `xt update --apply` produces identical `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` byte-for-byte pre + post batch.
- [ ] Guard-in-hook validation: run `node ~/.xtrm/hooks/beads-claim-sync.mjs` in a non-xtrm directory → exits 0 without side effects (no bd calls, no writes).
- [ ] Pi sync: `~/.pi/settings.json.hooks` (or equivalent Pi hook field) gets same treatment.
- [ ] Unit tests: `global-hooks-bootstrap.test.ts`, `reconcile-global-claude-hooks.test.ts`, `hook-entry-source-tagging.test.ts`.
- [ ] Integration: fixture `~/.claude/settings.json` with mixed xtrm-owned + user-authored + orphaned-xtrm-owned entries → single `xt bootstrap` correctly classifies each.
- [ ] Log evidence: `~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` filtered by `component=hooks-migration` shows expected event sequence.

## OUTPUT

Diff of new files + edited files, sample `~/.claude/settings.json` before + after showing safe-merge, mtime-stability evidence, list of hook payloads that got fast-fail guards added, log evidence sample, and a note on `xtrm-s5ih5` closure candidacy.

## APPROACH NOTES

Source-tagging design: extend the existing per-entry object with `_source` and `_xtrm` fields. Claude Code ignores unknown keys in hook entries (verified in Claude Code docs), so this is safe. The `_xtrm.hash` field lets us detect if we own an entry even after user hand-edits — if the entry's canonical-content-hash matches what we shipped in a prior version, we still own it. Merge algorithm sketch:
```
canonicalEntries = resolve(hooks.json, ~/.xtrm/hooks/)
existingEntries = readSettings(~/.claude/settings.json).hooks
newEntries = {}
for phase in ['PreToolUse','PostToolUse','SessionStart','Stop', ...]:
    for entry in canonicalEntries[phase]:
        newEntries[phase].push({...entry, _source: "xtrm-global", _xtrm: {version, installedAt, hash: sha256(entry)}})
    for entry in existingEntries[phase]:
        if entry._source == "xtrm-global": skip (replaced above)
        elif entry._source: preserve (owned by other tool)
        elif ownsByHash(entry): skip (canonical version added above)
        else: preserve (user-authored)
        newEntries[phase].push(entry)
```
This gives us clean idempotence: existing xtrm-owned entries get replaced by their new versions; foreign and user-authored entries pass through untouched. Same algorithm for `~/.pi/settings.json`.

Fast-fail guards to audit (add if missing): `beads-*.mjs` (need `.beads/` dir), `quality-check.*` (need repo context), `using-xtrm-reminder.mjs` (already reads `<cwd>/.xtrm/skills/` — needs `existsSync` guard at top), `worktree-boundary.mjs`, `xtrm-*-logger.mjs` (need `.xtrm/logs/` writable). `statusline.mjs` already runs globally so is fine. `specialists-agent-guard.mjs` checks prompt content, generally safe.
