title: Batch D: Runtime pointers global — ~/.claude/skills, ~/.pi/agent/skills, pi-runtime cleanup
description:
## PROBLEM

After Batches A–C, `~/.xtrm/skills/active/` is populated but nothing points at it from Claude Code or Pi at HOME scope. Currently Pi's `settings.json.skills` has `~/.xtrm/skills/default` as a *fallback*; we make it the primary. Claude Code's `~/.claude/skills` is not wired at all. This batch closes that gap so agent runtimes actually see the global skills.

## SUCCESS

- `xt bootstrap` (and lazy self-heal) creates `~/.claude/skills → ~/.xtrm/skills/active` and `~/.pi/agent/skills → ~/.xtrm/skills/active` symlinks (or leaves valid ones alone).
- Runtime view assertion (`assertRuntimeSkillsViews`) verifies BOTH the global pointers and the per-repo pointers (per-repo skipped if repo is fully migrated).
- Pi `USER_DEFAULT_SKILLS_ENTRY` = `~/.xtrm/skills/active` (was `~/.xtrm/skills/default`); array is single entry (`[global-active]`) with the per-repo `../.xtrm/skills/active` prepended only when a project user pack or service-skills output exists.
- Refuses to replace a non-symlink `~/.claude/skills` (existing dir) without `XTRM_FORCE_SKILLS_MIGRATION=1`.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts:82-87` — replace `USER_DEFAULT_SKILLS_ENTRY = '~/.xtrm/skills/default'` with `~/.xtrm/skills/active`. Update `PROJECT_SKILLS_ENTRY` fallback logic (line 1139-1161).
- `cli/src/core/skills-scaffold.ts:82-116` — add `ensureUserAgentsSkillsSymlink()` variant that targets `~/.claude/skills → ~/.xtrm/skills/active` (absolute path) with the same non-symlink-refuse policy. Called from bootstrap.
- `cli/src/core/skills-scaffold.ts:118-153` — `ensureAgentsSkillsSymlink` project variant checks if repo has no user packs/service-skills; if not and global is bootstrapped, prints "project-scope skills pointer skipped (using global)".
- `cli/src/core/skills-runtime-views.ts:89-100` — `assertRuntimeSkillsViews` extends to accept `{scope: 'global'|'project'|'both'}` and validates the right pointers.
- `cli/src/commands/bootstrap.ts` — calls `ensureUserAgentsSkillsSymlink()` after materializer runs.
- `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts` — reports both global and project pointer state.

## NON_GOALS

- Migration skill — Batch E.
- `xt skills` scope flip — Batch F.
- Deleting legacy `~/.agents/skills` code path — Batch G.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Symlink target format: `~/.claude/skills → ~/.xtrm/skills/active` uses an ABSOLUTE symlink (HOME is stable enough; relative would traverse via `~/.claude/` which is confusing).
- Non-symlink refuse policy identical to today's project-scope behavior: warn, exit non-zero, require env override.
- Pi `settings.json.skills` array flatten: if global covers everything, array becomes `["~/.xtrm/skills/active"]`; if project has user packs, prepend `"../.xtrm/skills/active"`. Never duplicate entries.
- Compatibility: existing consumer `.pi/settings.json` with the old `["../.xtrm/skills/active", "~/.xtrm/skills/default"]` array is auto-normalized on next `xt update`.
- Logging: every pointer create/refuse/normalize logs to `~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` with event `pointer.{create|refuse|normalize}` and fields `{scope, target, existing, action, outcome}`.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fresh HOME + `xt bootstrap`: `readlink ~/.claude/skills` == `~/.xtrm/skills/active` (absolute) AND `readlink ~/.pi/agent/skills` == same.
- [ ] Existing `~/.claude/skills` as a real dir with foreign file: `xt bootstrap` refuses with non-zero exit; sets `XTRM_FORCE_SKILLS_MIGRATION=1` succeeds after backup.
- [ ] Pi settings normalization: fixture repo with array `["../.xtrm/skills/active", "~/.xtrm/skills/default"]` → after `xt update --apply XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` → array is `["../.xtrm/skills/active", "~/.xtrm/skills/active"]`; then if no local user packs, array becomes `["~/.xtrm/skills/active"]`.
- [ ] `assertRuntimeSkillsViews({scope:'both'})` passes on a fully-migrated system.
- [ ] `xt doctor` reports "Global skills pointer: ok" and "Project skills pointer: skipped (empty)" for a migrated repo.
- [ ] Unit tests: `pi-runtime-safeguards.test.ts:309-355` updated to assert new resolution order.
- [ ] `~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` `pointer.*` events emitted in the format above.

## OUTPUT

Diff of pi-runtime + skills-scaffold + runtime-views changes, sample `.pi/settings.json` array before/after normalization, `xt doctor` output on migrated + unmigrated repos, log evidence, and enumeration of updated tests.

## APPROACH NOTES

title: Batch C: Retire per-repo default/optional scaffold under XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS (breaking gate)
description:
## PROBLEM

With Batches A+B, global bootstrap works but per-repo `default/optional/` still installs on every `xt init`. This batch stops the per-repo materialization under the feature flag so consumer repos become skill-payload-free (they retain only `user/`, `active/`, `state.json`, and service-skills output). This is the highest-risk batch — it changes the observable shape of `<repo>/.xtrm/skills/`.

## SUCCESS

- With `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1`, `xt init` on a fresh repo creates ONLY `.xtrm/skills/{user/packs/,active/,state.json,INVARIANTS.md}` — no `default/`, no `optional/`.
- `xt update --apply XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` on an unmigrated repo emits a migration nudge and DOES NOT re-materialize per-repo `default/optional/` (leaves existing untouched but stops re-syncing them from registry).
- Flag OFF: unchanged behavior.
- Generated registry snapshot in newly installed consumer repos omits `skills` and `skills_optional` asset blocks (they are global).

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts:87-126` — `scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage` short-circuits when `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` and global tree is present. Only ensures project `user/packs/` structure.
- `cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts:140-298` — `installFromRegistry` under flag routes `skills`/`skills_optional` entries to global root; project root receives only `hooks`/`config`.
- `scripts/gen-registry.mjs:16-33` — add `install_scope` field to each asset entry (`skills`/`skills_optional`: `"global"`; others: `"project"`). Consumer registry snapshot honors this.
- `cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts` — consumer `registry.json` write path (line ~286-287) omits assets flagged `install_scope: "global"`.
- `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:314` — worktree bootstrap under flag calls only `verifyGlobalPointer()` instead of `ensureAgentsSkillsSymlink(worktreePath)` when the worktree lacks project user packs.

## NON_GOALS

- Migration skill — Batch E handles cleaning existing per-repo `default/optional/`.
- Runtime pointer swap — Batch D handles `.claude/skills`, `.pi/settings.json`.
- `xt skills` scope flip — Batch F.
- Legacy code deletion — Batch G (this batch keeps the code paths, just gates them).

## CONSTRAINTS

- `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` env flag is the ONLY toggle; no config-file gate in this batch.
- Flag OFF must produce byte-identical results to pre-batch (regression fixture: snapshot `<tmp-repo>/.xtrm/` after `xt init` before batch, compare after batch — assert equal).
- Registry snapshot compatibility: consumer `<repo>/.xtrm/registry.json` must remain readable by older xtrm-tools versions (they will just ignore the `install_scope` field — JSON is additive-safe).
- Migration nudge: printed to stdout once per update run, includes `xt migrate skills` CTA and doc URL.
- Logging: every asset skip logs `install.skip.global-managed` with `{asset, count}`.
- No `bd update <id> --claim` for this batch until Batch B has landed on the base branch.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Flag OFF regression: snapshot fixture `xt init` output before + after batch — byte-identical `.xtrm/` tree.
- [ ] Flag ON fresh install: `xt init --yes` produces empty `.xtrm/skills/default/` (absent) and `.xtrm/skills/optional/` (absent); `~/.xtrm/skills/default/` populated.
- [ ] Flag ON re-sync: `xt update --apply` on a fixture repo with pre-existing `.xtrm/skills/default/` leaves it untouched, prints nudge to stdout matching regex `/Run \`xt migrate skills\`/`.
- [ ] Worktree fixture: `xt worktree create` in a migrated repo does NOT recreate per-repo skills; symlinks resolve via global.
- [ ] Registry snapshot: `jq '.assets.skills.install_scope' <consumer>/.xtrm/registry.json` returns `"global"`.
- [ ] Old-version compat: source-checkout of xtrm-tools @ prior release parses new registry.json without error (test via `node -e 'require("./cli/dist/index.cjs")'` on a captured old release).
- [ ] All existing tests updated for asset-scope: `installFromRegistry.test`, `registry-scaffold.test`, `install-integration.test`.
- [ ] `~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` records `install.skip.global-managed` events during flag-on install.

## OUTPUT

Diff of registry-scaffold + gen-registry changes, the fixture-snapshot regression test scaffolding, migration nudge sample output, evidence of flag-off byte-identical behavior, and enumeration of test files updated (expect 4-6).

## APPROACH NOTES

Two-pass check in `installFromRegistry`: read `entry.install_scope` (default `"project"`); if `"global"` AND flag ON → route to `~/.xtrm/`; else current code path. This keeps the code close to today's shape while enabling scope routing. Nudge printer can live in `cli/src/utils/nudge.ts` (new) with a state file `~/.xtrm/nudges/<key>.json` for dedup.

title: Batch B: xt bootstrap command + lazy self-heal wiring in install/init/update
description:
## PROBLEM

Batch A ships the primitives; nothing calls them yet. This batch wires the global bootstrap into the CLI so users can trigger it explicitly (`xt bootstrap`) and every `xt` command self-heals a missing/outdated global tree. Consumer repos still get per-repo scaffold too (Batch C removes that) — this batch adds the global path in parallel.

## SUCCESS

- `xt bootstrap` command exists and populates `~/.xtrm/skills/{default,optional,active}/` from the running package.
- `xt init`, `xt install`, `xt update --apply` all call `ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped()` early; second call is a no-op when version matches.
- Behind `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` flag, `xt update --apply` retargets `checkDrift` for `skills`/`skills_optional` assets to the global root; when flag is off, current per-repo path unchanged.

## SCOPE

- New `cli/src/commands/bootstrap.ts` — Commander subcommand `xt bootstrap [--force]`. Calls `ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped(packageRoot, {force})`. Prints resulting `state.json` summary. Exit 0 on ok, 1 on failure.
- `cli/src/commands/install.ts:150-231` — insert `await ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped(packageRoot)` between line 155 (`getContext`) and 169 (`scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage`). Gate the retarget of `installFromRegistry`'s skills-asset destination behind `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS`.
- `cli/src/commands/init.ts:812-858` — same bootstrap call before Phase 6.
- `cli/src/commands/update.ts:68-152` — call bootstrap in `updateRepo`; when `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1`, `checkDrift` for `skills`/`skills_optional` runs against `~/.xtrm/` root (extend `drift.ts:44-75` with an optional `overrideRoots: Record<assetKey, string>` param).
- `cli/src/commands/index.ts` (or wherever commands register) — register `bootstrap`.
- `cli/src/core/drift.ts:44-75` — add `overrideRoots` param, default undefined.

## NON_GOALS

- Per-repo `default/optional/` scaffolding is NOT retired in this batch — Batch C.
- Runtime pointer changes (`.claude/skills`, `.pi/settings.json`) — Batch D.
- Migration skill — Batch E.
- `xt skills` command scope flip — Batch F.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Feature-flag `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` gates any behavior change to `installFromRegistry`/`checkDrift`. With flag off, this batch is a pure additive (bootstrap runs but doesn't alter downstream install).
- `xt bootstrap` must be safely runnable from any cwd (not just an xtrm-managed repo).
- `ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped` is idempotent — running `xt bootstrap` twice in a row is a no-op printing "already up to date @ version X".
- Logging: every command that calls bootstrap logs `bootstrap.trigger` with `{command, cwd, pkgVersion}` fields at start. Preserve existing xtrm log format.
- Cold-start cost: bootstrap must complete under 3s on a warm system with ~55 default skills.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run build` clean.
- [ ] `xt bootstrap` in a scratch HOME populates `~/.xtrm/skills/{default,optional,active}` with the source repo's skills.
- [ ] `xt bootstrap` a second time prints "up to date"; runs in <200ms; no file writes (verified via `strace -e trace=openat,write` or mtime check).
- [ ] `xt init` in a fresh repo (flag OFF) still produces identical `.xtrm/skills/default/` tree as pre-batch — verified byte-for-byte against a captured baseline.
- [ ] `xt update --apply XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` in an unmigrated repo does NOT touch per-repo `.xtrm/skills/default/`, but confirms global tree is present.
- [ ] Unit test for `drift.checkDrift` with `overrideRoots` mapping skills assets to a tmp global root — SHA compare hits the global path.
- [ ] Smoke: `xt bootstrap && xt init` on a scratch repo — both succeed; global tree + per-repo tree both populated.
- [ ] Log evidence: `jq 'select(.event | startswith("bootstrap"))' ~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` shows expected event chain.

## OUTPUT

CLI diff summary, new bootstrap command help text, sample `xt bootstrap` output, evidence that flag-off behavior is unchanged (baseline compare hash + test log), and a note on the drift.ts signature change (should be backwards-compatible via optional param).

## APPROACH NOTES

`ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped` in `runInstall` should happen BEFORE `scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage` so that later batches can detect "global tree exists, skip per-repo scaffold" cleanly. Package root resolution already exists at `registry-scaffold.ts:51-64` (`resolvePackageRoot`) — reuse. For `xt bootstrap` command registration, mirror `xt doctor` registration shape.

Bead SUCCESS requires ~/.xtrm/skills/active/ populated after bootstrap. title: Batch A: Global scaffold primitives (skills-layout, materializer, runtime-views split)
description:
## PROBLEM

The current skill core assumes a single per-repo `skillsRoot`. To materialize skills globally, we need path/composition primitives that understand two scopes (global HOME + project) without breaking existing per-repo callers. This is the foundation for all subsequent batches.

## SUCCESS

Core primitives support both global and project skill roots; existing per-repo behavior is unchanged when only the project root is passed; new global helpers are testable in isolation with no consumer wiring yet.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/core/skills-layout.ts:18-38` — add `resolveGlobalSkillsRoot()` (returns `~/.xtrm/skills` via `os.homedir()`) alongside existing `resolveSkillsRoot(scopeRoot)`. Do NOT change existing function signature.
- `cli/src/core/skills-runtime-views.ts:16-17` — replace hardcoded `CLAUDE_POINTER_TARGET = '../.xtrm/skills/active'` and `PI_SKILLS_ENTRY = '../.xtrm/skills/active'` with a `getRuntimePointerTarget({scope: 'global'|'project'})` returning the right relative-or-absolute target.
- `cli/src/core/skills-materializer.ts:90-223` — extract `rebuildActiveViewInternal(skillsRoot, extraSourceRoots?: string[])` from existing `rebuildAllRuntimeActiveViews`. Add `rebuildGlobalActiveView(globalSkillsRoot)` (default + optional composition). Add `rebuildProjectActiveView(projectSkillsRoot, {globalSkillsRoot})` that composes symlinks to global's active-view targets plus local user/service-skills entries.
- New `cli/src/core/global-skills-bootstrap.ts` — pure function: `ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped(pkgRoot: string, opts: {force?: boolean}) → { installedVersion, changed: boolean }`. Copies `<pkgRoot>/.xtrm/skills/{default,optional}` into `~/.xtrm/skills/`, writes `state.json` with schemaVersion 1 + installedVersion + installedFrom + installedAt.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT change any command wiring yet (`install.ts`, `init.ts`, `update.ts` untouched).
- Do NOT touch the migration skill.
- Do NOT delete the current per-runtime `active/{claude,pi}` code paths — Batch G handles that.
- Do NOT flip `xt skills` scope default — Batch F.

## CONSTRAINTS

- `resolveSkillsRoot(scopeRoot)` existing callers must pass the same argument and get identical output. New helper is additive.
- All new functions pure (no side effects except `global-skills-bootstrap` which writes to HOME).
- `rebuildProjectActiveView` must produce a superset symlink set: global skills reachable via project active view.
- Logging: on bootstrap write to `~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` — event `bootstrap.start`, `bootstrap.copy.<asset>`, `bootstrap.ok`, `bootstrap.error`, with fields `{timestamp, component: "skills-bootstrap", pkgVersion, source, target, filesCopied, durationMs, outcome}`. Redact only paths outside `~/.xtrm/`; hashes only, no bytes.
- Backwards-compat: no changes to `state.json` schema for project scope; new global `state.json` extends schema with optional `installedVersion`, `installedFrom`, `installedAt`.
- Test-first: unit tests for each new helper before landing.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm test --workspace cli -- skills-layout.test skills-runtime-views.test skills-materializer.test global-skills-bootstrap.test` all green.
- [ ] New unit tests: `resolveGlobalSkillsRoot` returns `~/.xtrm/skills`; `getRuntimePointerTarget` returns correct relative target per scope; `rebuildGlobalActiveView` produces expected symlinks in a tmp `~/.xtrm/skills` fixture; `ensureGlobalSkillsBootstrapped` is idempotent (2nd call `changed: false`).

title: [epic] Global skills + hooks migration: default payloads move from per-repo to ~/.xtrm
description:
## PROBLEM

Default and optional **skill** payloads AND default **hook** payloads are currently copied per-repo into `<repo>/.xtrm/{skills/{default,optional},hooks}/` on every `xt init`/`xt update --apply`, and xtrm-owned hook entries are written into `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` on every reconcile. Users managing xtrm across 10+ repos hit N drift diffs, N update runs, N re-materialized symlink farms per skill release, AND N settings.json rewrites per hook release. Symlink management has broken twice already (PR #197 regression guard `check-skills-symlinks.mjs`). Hook wiring has its own outstanding safety concern (`xtrm-s5ih5`: `xt install --global must not overwrite project hooks in ~/.claude/settings.json`). Sibling project `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` cut over to a canonical-package model for specialists; we lag behind for skills and hooks.

## SUCCESS

- `~/.xtrm/skills/{default,optional,user,active}/` is the single source of truth for default + optional skills.
- `~/.xtrm/hooks/` is the single source of truth for canonical hook payloads.
- `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` holds canonical hook wiring globally.
- New xtrm-tools installs no longer materialize `<repo>/.xtrm/skills/{default,optional}/` or `<repo>/.xtrm/hooks/*` (only project-scoped overrides remain per-repo).
- `~/.claude/skills` and `~/.pi/agent/skills` are symlinks into `~/.xtrm/skills/active/`.
- `~/.claude/settings.json.hooks` and `~/.pi/settings.json.hooks` receive xtrm-owned entries via safe-merge with per-entry source tagging (`_source: "xtrm-global"`, `_xtrm: {version, installedAt, hash}`) — non-xtrm keys never touched (subsumes `xtrm-s5ih5`).
- Per-repo `<repo>/.xtrm/skills/user/`, `service-skills/`, and project-scoped hook payloads/entries continue to work unchanged.
- `xt migrate all` cleanly removes per-repo default skills, per-repo global-covered hook payloads, and xtrm-owned hook entries from `<repo>/.claude/settings.json` — with SHA-verified equality + tarball backup + `--all-repos` batch mode + `--restore <backup>` reversal.
- `xt update` in a fresh install pulls new defaults globally via `xt bootstrap` (or lazy self-heal) — no per-repo action required.
- Every hook payload survives being wired globally: fast-fail guard at entry (`existsSync(cwd/.xtrm)` check) prevents side effects in non-xtrm sessions.
- Zero regressions in current test suites.

## SCOPE

Bounded surfaces affected (full file map in `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-dawid-dev-core/07e1094c-64b5-4516-9179-c11a451cf97e/scratchpad/skills-global-migration-plan.md` §6):

**Skills**:
- `cli/src/core/`: `skills-layout.ts`, `skills-runtime-views.ts`, `skills-materializer.ts`, `skills-scaffold.ts`, `skills-state.ts`, `skill-discovery.ts`, `registry-scaffold.ts`, `service-skills-ensure.ts`, `pi-runtime.ts`, `drift.ts`, new `global-skills-bootstrap.ts`.
- `cli/src/commands/`: `install.ts`, `init.ts`, `update.ts`, `skills.ts`, `clean.ts`, `doctor.ts`, `worktree-*.ts`, new `bootstrap.ts`, new `migrate.ts`.
- `cli/src/adapters/claude.ts` (skills capability path).

**Hooks**:
- `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:198-260` — extend `reconcileProjectClaudeHooks` and `ensureGlobalStatusLine` into full global-hook reconciler with source tagging.
- New `cli/src/core/global-hooks-bootstrap.ts`.
- New `cli/src/core/pi-runtime-hooks.ts` (Pi analog of the reconciler).
- `.xtrm/hooks/`: audit every payload for fast-fail guard (`beads-*.mjs`, `quality-check.*`, `specialists-agent-guard.mjs`, `using-xtrm-reminder.mjs`, `worktree-boundary.mjs`, `xtrm-*-logger.mjs`, `gitnexus/`, `specialists/`).
- `.xtrm/config/hooks.json` — canonical wiring stays authored in-repo; ships to `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` at bootstrap.
- `policies/`: `service-skills.json`, `service-skills-claude.json` — hook commands resolve via the composed active view.

**Shared / cross-cutting**:
- `cli/src/utils/`: `worktree-session.ts`, `repo-root.ts`.
- `scripts/`: `gen-registry.mjs` (add `install_scope` field to `skills`, `skills_optional`, `hooks`, `config`), `check-registry-pack-parity.mjs`, `check-skills-symlinks.mjs`, `check-layout-guards.mjs`, `verify-asset-contract.mjs`, `vendor-specialists-skills.mjs`, `verify-specialists-vendor.mjs`, `check-skills-ownership.mjs`, new `check:global-skills-parity`.
- `packages/pi-extensions/`: `extensions/service-skills/index.ts`, `extensions/xtrm-loader/index.ts` + stale mirrors.
- `.xtrm/skills/default/migrating-to-global/` — new skill.
- `docs/`: `skills.md`, `skills-tier-architecture.md`, `skills-ownership.{json,md,release.json}`, `project-skills.md`, `service-skills-auto-reconcile.md`, `xtrm-directory.md`, `policies.md`, `cli-architecture.md`, `pi-extensions.md`, `hooks.md`, `plans/global-skills-hooks-migration.md` (new).
- Root docs: `README.md`, `CLAUDE.md`, `XTRM-GUIDE.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`.
- Tests: 28 skill test files + hook-reconciler and safe-merge tests (added in Batch J and Batch I).

## NON_GOALS

- Per-repo user packs (`.xtrm/skills/user/packs/`) migration — stays project-scoped.
- Per-repo project-scoped hook payloads and settings.json entries — stay project-scoped.
- Service-skills v2 machinery redesign — writes to per-repo `user/packs/<repo>-services/` unchanged.
- Global specialists — specialists already migrated; no further work here.
- Windows-specific dev-mode symlink workarounds.
- Replacing hook resolution with pure package resolution à la specialists' `import.meta.url` — runtime hooks reference absolute paths (`~/.xtrm/hooks/*.mjs`) in settings.json.
- Migrating settings.json fields other than `hooks` (permissions, model, statusLine handled by existing `ensureGlobalStatusLine`).
- Refactoring the hook implementations themselves — payloads move as-is; only fast-fail guards added.
- Migrating the ownership manifest to a runtime resolver — `docs/skills-ownership.json` stays authoring-time.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Sequencing: Batches A→B→{C, D, J}→E is hard-sequential (scaffold → bootstrap → per-repo retirement + hook wiring → migration cleanup). F can parallelize once A lands. G/H land after E. Rollout in three release phases: preview (feature-flagged `XTRM_GLOBAL_SKILLS=1` AND `XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS=1`) → default-on (opt-out `XTRM_LEGACY_SKILLS=1` / `XTRM_LEGACY_HOOKS=1`) → legacy code removal.
- Wire-format compatibility: registry.json v1 schema stays; `skills`/`skills_optional`/`hooks`/`config` assets gain `install_scope: "global"|"project"`.
- Migration destructive actions only when: global bootstrap done AND git-clean under `.xtrm/skills/default/` and `.xtrm/hooks/` AND (SHA-equality OR user-approved discard/relocate) AND for hook entries: `_source == "xtrm-global"` OR hash matches canonical AND global equivalent exists. Backup mandatory.
- Runtime pointer assertions (`assertRuntimeSkillsViews`) migrate atomically with pointer emission.
- **Safe-merge invariant for settings.json**: bytes outside the `hooks` field never change. `hooks` field changes only for entries owned by `xtrm-global` (source-tagged or hash-matched). This directly answers the `xtrm-s5ih5` concern.
- Every hook payload gets a fast-fail guard at entry to survive being wired globally into non-xtrm sessions.
- Logging: every install/update/bootstrap/migrate step logs to xtrm's structured format at `~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` with `component: "skills-bootstrap"|"hooks-bootstrap"|"skills-migrate"|"hooks-migrate"|"hooks-reconcile"`. Never log absolute file contents or hook command strings that might carry sensitive paths; hash them.
- Public CLI surface: `xt bootstrap`, `xt migrate [skills|hooks|all]`, `xt skills --global` (default flip). Backwards-compat: existing `xt update --apply` in unmigrated repos still succeeds with a nudge.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fresh install: `npm i -g @jaggerxtrm/xtrm-tools@<preview>` then `xt init` in a scratch repo → global `~/.xtrm/{skills/{default,optional,active},hooks,config/hooks.json}` populated, `~/.claude/skills` symlink created, `~/.claude/settings.json.hooks` receives xtrm-global entries, no per-repo copies.
- [ ] `xt update --apply` in an unmigrated repo → composes global active + repo user, prints migration nudge, no destructive action.
- [ ] `xt migrate all --dry-run` on 5 real repos (`vaultctl`, `transcriptoz`, `console`, `xtrm`, `specialists`) → clean verdict table for both skills and hooks, zero false-diverged.
- [ ] `xt migrate all --apply` on same 5 → tarballs at `~/.xtrm/migration-backups/`, per-repo `default/optional/` gone, global-covered hook payloads gone, xtrm-global hook entries removed from `<repo>/.claude/settings.json`, foreign + user-authored entries preserved, `user/`+`service-skills/`+project hooks preserved, runtime pointers valid.
- [ ] `xt migrate --restore <backup>` → repo returns to pre-migration state byte-identical.
- [ ] All 28 skill test files + new hook-reconciler tests pass green.
- [ ] `npm run check:registry-pack-parity`, `check:skills-symlinks`, `check:skills-ownership`, new `check:global-skills-parity`, new `check:hook-source-tagging` all green in `prepublishOnly`.
- [ ] `xt doctor` on migrated repo reports clean; on unmigrated repo surfaces both pending migrations.
- [ ] Smoke: `service-skills` cataloger + activator + drift-detector still fire in a repo with a live `service-registry.json`.
- [ ] Smoke: `beads-*.mjs` fast-fail guard verified — running `node ~/.xtrm/hooks/beads-claim-sync.mjs` in a non-xtrm dir exits 0 with no side effects.
- [ ] Safe-merge invariant: fixture `~/.claude/settings.json` with user-authored `permissions` block + user-authored `hooks` entry + orphaned xtrm-global entry → after `xt bootstrap`, permissions untouched, user-authored entry preserved, orphaned entry updated/removed.
- [ ] xtrm-s5ih5 explicitly closed as validated by this epic.
- [ ] Log evidence: `jq '.event' ~/.xtrm/logs/skills-migration.jsonl` returns `bootstrap.*`, `hook.reconcile.*`, `migrate.repo.*`, `migrate.skills.*`, `migrate.hooks.*` sequences.

## OUTPUT

At epic close: PR chain (one per batch), demo run of full migration across the 5 fixture repos with backups uploaded to a release artifact, upgrade notes in `CHANGELOG.md`, `docs/plans/global-skills-hooks-migration.md` marked shipped, telemetry sample confirming migration audit log format matches contract, `xtrm-s5ih5` closed with pointer to Batch J's source-tagging design, residual-risk note enumerating repos on old xtrm-tools versions that haven't upgraded yet.

## REFERENCES

- Migration plan draft: `/tmp/claude-1000/-home-dawid-dev-core/07e1094c-64b5-4516-9179-c11a451cf97e/scratchpad/skills-global-migration-plan.md` (full architecture, batches, risks — updated to cover hooks).
- Sibling precedent: `/home/dawid/dev/specialists` — canonical-asset-resolver (`src/specialist/canonical-asset-resolver.ts`), loader precedence (`src/specialist/loader.ts:130-192`), drift-detector (`src/specialist/drift-detector.ts`), prune-stale-defaults CLI (`src/cli/prune-stale-defaults.ts`).
- Existing global-hook precedent in this repo: `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:245-260` (`ensureGlobalStatusLine`) — safe-merge pattern already used for statusline; Batch J generalizes it.
- Prior art in this repo: `xtrm-9xg2.2` (flat active layout guards), `xtrm-9xg2.3` (runtime checks) — subsumed by this epic. `xtrm-s5ih5` — directly addressed by Batch J's source-tagging design.
- Adjacent: `xtrm-n74m8` (stale pre-v2 service-skills trinity) — the migration skill can also nudge cleanup.

## APPROACH NOTES

Recon: three parallel Explore agents produced the impact map. Blast-radius summary: MEDIUM aggregate. Batch C (per-repo skills scaffold retirement) and Batch J (hook safe-merge into `~/.claude/settings.json`) are the two individually higher-risk tasks — both feature-flagged. Symbols with widest fan-out: `scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage`, `installFromRegistry`, `ensureAgentsSkillsSymlink`, `reconcileProjectClaudeHooks`. None have HIGH/CRITICAL impact alone; aggregate risk comes from the coupled pointer + scaffold + registry + settings-merge retargeting.

Batches A(scaffold)/B(bootstrap)/D(runtime pointers)/C(retire per-repo)/J(global hooks)/E(migrate CLI)/F(scope flip)/G(dead-code)/H(docs). Batch I test-polish deferred to xtrm-bq7yd.12; security hardening deferred to xtrm-bq7yd.11. Ready for merge to main.

title: Add xt audit surface for PRs that need rebase or operator attention
description:
## PROBLEM

Even after xt can classify PR merge-state, operators and bots need a command surface that lists branches/PRs requiring rebase or escalation. Today that notification lives in operator memory.

## SUCCESS

`xt doctor` or `xt worktree` exposes an audit mode that scans managed branches/worktrees and prints actionable findings: clean, needs-rebase, conflicted, blocked, closed, or unknown.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts`
- `cli/src/commands/worktree.ts`
- command help/tests in `cli/src/tests/doctor.test.ts` or `worktree` tests

## NON_GOALS

- Do not delete branches; branch GC is separate.
- Do not auto-rebase in the first version unless explicitly gated by a flag and tests.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must support human output and `--json` output.
- Logging/telemetry: findings include `repo`, `branch`, `pr_url`, `classification`, `suggested_action`, `suggestion_command`, `checked_at_ms`.
- Safe default: audit-only. Any modifying remediation must require an explicit flag.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] CLI tests cover human and JSON output for mixed PR states.
- [ ] Smoke with mocked `gh` shows `needs-rebase` findings are visible without manual inspection.

## OUTPUT

New audit command/flag, examples in help text, test output, and handoff explaining how specialists should consume it.

title: Durable xt PR/worktree drift primitives for autonomous operation
description:
## PROBLEM

Mercury devops collaborator and future autonomous xtrm flows need reliable git/worktree/PR drift primitives. Today xt has partial PR state reads and rebase-cascade ownership, but no first-class `needs rebase` / `conflict` / branch-GC / restart-audit surface for agents or operators to compose.

## SUCCESS

xt exposes durable, repo-agnostic primitives for PR merge-state refresh, branch/worktree audit, safe branch GC, and operator-facing remediation hints. Containerized agents and manual operators can compose xt commands instead of reimplementing inline bash.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/worktree.ts`
- `cli/src/commands/merge.ts` only where rebase-cascade handoff/metadata needs integration
- `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts`
- `cli/src/commands/clean.ts`
- tests under `cli/src/tests/`
- docs that describe xt command ownership, especially `docs/cli-architecture.md` if command semantics change

## NON_GOALS

- Do not implement specialist/job observability columns; that belongs in `~/dev/specialists`.
- Do not implement the Mercury webhook receiver/container lifecycle; that belongs in `~/dev/xtrm` docs and Mercury infra.
- Do not replace bd `merge-slot`; lease state remains bd/substrate-owned.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Durable target: post-substrate these git/worktree signals attach to the substrate container/worktree row; bridge CLI names should survive where practical.
- Logging/telemetry: every audit/remediation command must emit structured JSON in `--json` mode with repo, branch, pr_url/pr_number, merge_state, action, outcome, duration_ms, and redacted error context.
- Safety: auto-rebase/force-push is allowed only with `--force-with-lease`; conflict states must be reported, never hand-resolved.
- Preserve existing xt `worktree`, `merge`, `end`, `doctor`, and `clean` behavior unless a new flag is explicitly used.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests cover PR state parsing for OPEN/MERGED/CLOSED plus mergeStateStatus values such as CLEAN/BEHIND/DIRTY/BLOCKED.
- [ ] CLI smoke with mocked `gh` output proves `xt` reports `needs-rebase` and `conflict` without network access.
- [ ] Branch GC dry-run prints candidates and apply mode deletes only merged/closed PR branches.
- [ ] JSON output includes the required structured fields and redacts command stderr safely.

## OUTPUT

A set of xt commands/primitives and tests that other repos can reference: especially specialists consuming PR drift state and Mercury container docs composing xt instead of inline bash.

## REFERENCES

- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/mercury-devops-collaborator.md` Sections 4-7
- `~/dev/specialists/docs/design/roadmap/specialists-roadmap.md` Opp 1/Opp 7 and durability follow-up
- Existing xt PR helper: `cli/src/commands/worktree.ts` `getPrStatus()`

CI checks passed before merge: Gitleaks, OSV, Semgrep, test (22.x, 3.11). Remote branch xt/zzrs deleted by PR merge; local worktree/branch left in place (xt end not run).

title: [bug] Workflow gates auto-PR on parser success — loses real edits when wrapper fails
description: When sp script wrapper fails (parser error, schema mismatch, etc.) the auto-reconcile PR step is skipped — even though Serena may have applied real edits to the filesystem during the run. Edits die with the ephemeral GH runner. Need recovery path independent of parser success.
notes:
[surfaced from market-data run 28120048262, post xtrm-23qsu]

Reusable workflow at xtrm-dev/core/.github/workflows/service-skills-drift-sweep.yml:557-579:

  - name: Build auto-PR body
    if: (steps.rx.outputs.status == 'success' || steps.rx.outputs.status == 'partial')
        && steps.rx.outputs.reconciled_count != '0'
  - name: Open auto-reconcile PR
    if: (steps.rx.outputs.status == 'success' || steps.rx.outputs.status == 'partial')
        && steps.rx.outputs.reconciled_count != '0'
    uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@22a9089...

The gate AND-conditions on (a) parser status + (b) reconciled_count from parser output. ANY parser failure → both skip → real disk edits abandoned on ephemeral runner.

## Two paths

### Path A — defensive gate (cheap, minimal)
Change condition to `if: always() && hasGitChanges`. peter-evans/create-pull-request already auto-detects git status diff and will only PR if files changed. So even on parser-failure, real Serena edits land in a PR. The PR body becomes "auto-reconcile (parser failed — see logs)" but the work is preserved.

Implementation: 2-line change. peter-evans does have a `base` + auto-commit-changes behavior. Just need a step that runs `git add -A` first, then peter-evans on always().

### Path B — architectural shift (deeper)
Have the specialist itself open the PR. service-skills-sync.specialist.json already declares:
- capabilities.required_tools: includes bash
- capabilities.external_commands: ['git', 'python3', 'bd']

Add a Phase 6 to the system_prompt: 'When you have applied edits, create branch xtrm-auto-reconcile/<sha>, git add, commit, push, and open PR via gh CLI.' Requires:
- gh CLI installed in runner (already is, GH actions image bundles it)
- GITHUB_TOKEN propagated to specialist's bash env (current workflow exports it to the sp script step — should already work)
- Specialist permission_required (currently MEDIUM) allows shell git/gh commands

Path B eliminates the entire parser-gate dependency. Workflow becomes just orchestration; specialist owns end-to-end outcome. JSON output becomes telemetry, not authoritative state. Trade-off: more responsibility on the LLM (it must remember to commit + push); recovery if specialist forgets to push is harder.

### Recommendation

Ship Path A first (immediate safety net for any future wrapper failures, recoverable even if parser is buggy).
Then evaluate Path B as a v2 architecture — the gain is significant: machine-readable telemetry decouples from work delivery, and Phase C becomes resilient to LLM-instruction-decay on the final output (which is the very thing that bit us today).

Operator framed this as 'mi sembra assurdo imporre queste cagate alla fine di una job quando è lo specialist a dover fare il lavoro' — strong endorsement of Path B as the proper long-term shape.
[milestone 2026-06-25] PR #326 ships Path A (defensive gate) + Path B prerequisite (GITHUB_TOKEN env). Codex-side Phase 6 system_prompt extension filed as xtrm-vu2ro.1.

Path A details:
- New step 'Detect uncommitted specialist edits' on always() — git status --porcelain → has_edits=true/false
- Open auto-reconcile PR gate OR'd with has_edits
- PR body branches: parser-clean uses old JSON summary; parser-failed-disk-dirty uses explanatory note + first 2KB of raw sp output

Path B prereq:
- GITHUB_TOKEN propagated to specialist sp script step env
- gh CLI already on runner images
- When codex extends specialist system_prompt with Phase 6, no further xtrm-tools wiring needed

Note: Path A and Path B are not mutually exclusive — keeping Path A as belt-and-suspenders even when Path B lands, because the specialist could still forget to push and we don't want to regress.

title: [bug] sp script wrapper strict-JSON parser rejects model prose, loses 32min of real work
description: Phase C run 28120048262 (market-data, post-stall_timeout fix) ran specialist for 1934783ms (32min) without stalling — first time ever. But final output failed: error 'JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier "Now"', error_type invalid_json. model: nano-gpt/moonshotai/kimi-k2.6 (no thinking)

{"success":false,"error":"JSON Parse error: Unexpected identifier \"Now\"","error_type":"invalid_json","meta":{...}}

The 'Now' is the model's output starting with "Now ..." prose before the expected JSON object. System prompt explicitly forbids this in script_template:
"...return JSON only. Top-level object must contain keys `summary`, `services`, and `actions`. Inner shapes may be best-effort, but do not emit prose, markdown fences, preamble, or trailing commentary."

But kimi-k2.6 ignored the directive after 32min of work and prefixed prose anyway. This is a known LLM failure mode for long-tool-using sessions — instruction-following decays over many turns.

## Proposed fixes (in order of robustness)

1. **Tolerant parser**: in sp script wrapper, when parser sees prose, extract the LAST valid {...} JSON object (or the largest balanced one) before failing. Tons of prior art (e.g. regex /\{[\s\S]*\}/ then balance-count). Trades strict-JSON contract for real-world model behavior.

2. **Second turn cleanup**: if first parse fails, automatically issue a follow-up turn "Re-emit your final output as JSON ONLY. No prose. Schema: {summary, services, actions}." Cost: one extra round-trip; benefit: deterministic recovery.

3. **Response format forcing via provider API**: nano-gpt + many providers support response_format={type:'json_object'}. Wire this through pi-coding-agent and specialist execution config. Lossless but requires provider support.

4. **Preserve work**: when JSON parse fails, still commit any filesystem changes made by Serena before failing. peter-evans would still PR them with a generic body. (Mitigation, not root fix.)

## Why this matters

The fix-stack so far:
- :thinking drop (PR #324) — needed but not sufficient
- stall_timeout_ms=600000 (PR #325) — needed but not sufficient

This bug is the THIRD layer. Until tolerant parser OR response_format forcing lands, Phase C cannot reliably produce edits for ANY repo with non-trivial drift.

Recommendation: ship fix 1 (tolerant parser) as fastest path; track fix 3 (response_format) as proper long-term solution.
[milestone 2026-06-25] PR #326 opened (xtrm-dev/core, branch xtrm-23qsu-vu2ro-tolerant-parser-and-fallback, HEAD 9ad255c851fd).

Tolerant parser shipped (option 1 from bead): scans r.output for largest balanced {...} dict containing at least one of summary/services/actions when sp returns error_type=invalid_json. Marks tolerant_rescue=true; emits notice. 4 fixtures verified locally.

Path B (option 3: provider response_format) is the proper long-term fix; not implemented here. If kimi/nano-gpt continues prose-prefixing under load, the rescued path will still extract it; that's the design intent.

PR URL: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/pull/326

  (b) rescue prose+JSON via tolerant parser (notice fires), OR
  (c) fall through to xtrm-vu2ro Path A safety net (PR opens because git diff has uncommitted edits)
All three open the auto-PR.

title: Phase C.2: specialists pinning decision (main vs tag)
description: Decide whether reusable workflow clones xtrm-dev/specialists @ latest main (fast drift, breakage risk) or pinned tag (stable, requires release cadence). Record in bead notes + workflow comment.
notes:
[decision 2026-06-23] Pin to exact specialists npm tag (e.g. @jaggerxtrm/specialists@3.17.0), not 'latest' or main HEAD.

Reasoning:
- specialists ships frequent releases (3.14.1 → 3.17.0 within recent weeks); 'latest' would shift under our feet between caller runs
- exact pin = deterministic CI behavior; failures are reproducible against a known version
- bump path: PR that edits the reusable workflow's pin input → operator/dependabot review → merge → consumers pick it up via reusable@main reference
- aligns with operator 'no-premature-readiness-claims' policy: every version move is an explicit, reviewable event
- Mechanism: reusable workflow exposes an input 'specialists-version' (default '3.17.0' initially); caller can override per-repo if needed

Rejected alternatives:
- main HEAD via git clone: requires git+bun on runner, breakage propagates instantly, harder to roll back
- npm 'latest' tag: same drift risk as main; defeats the point of pinning
- semver caret (^3.17.0): minor bumps land silently; specialists minor != API-stable contract per their CHANGELOG

Decision recorded. Closing C.2.

title: GitHub Action wrapper: case → skill → PR comment + verdict label
description:
## PROBLEM

Once the inspector (C1) and skill (B) exist, there is no automated path from a Dependabot/Renovate PR to a posted verdict. Operators still run the skill by hand. This task wraps the pipeline into a minimal-permission GitHub Action (spec §16).

## SUCCESS

A reusable GitHub Action triggers on dependency PRs (Dependabot/Renovate/manual bump), runs the deterministic inspector, invokes the skill, and posts a PR comment with the upgrade-dossier summary + verdict label. No mutation beyond a comment and label. Works on the specialists repo as the first adoption target (cross-linked specialists CI epic).

## SCOPE

Action definition (action.yml + workflow) in xtrm-tools, shippable to consumer repos. Wires inspector (C1) → skill (B) → pr-comment template. Read-only checkout + `pull-requests: write` (comment/label only). Does NOT implement auto-commit, auto-merge, or code mutation.

## NON_GOALS

- No automatic commit/merge/patch push (spec §16; gated, low-risk-only, deferred).
- No substrate materialization (E1, specialists).
- No deployer/SRE hand-off automation (v2 roadmap).
- No multi-repo backlog UI (v3).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Minimal permissions: contents:read, pull-requests:write (comment+label). No secrets scope, no OIDC deploy scope.
- Must degrade gracefully: if inspector or advisory feed is unavailable, post an explicit UNKNOWN verdict and `dependency-review/incomplete` label — never silently pass.
- SECURITY_FORCED / BLOCKED → set a failing check (verdict label `dependency-review/blocked`); advisory verdicts → non-blocking label.
- Deterministic run: same PR input → same comment shape.
- No secrets/tokens logged; comment content scrubbed.
- Pin all third-party Actions to full-length commit SHAs (spec §11).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] action.yml + workflow valid; runs on pull_request opened/synchronize by Dependabot/Renovate
- [ ] Posts a PR comment using templates/pr-comment.md with verdict + label
- [ ] SECURITY_FORCED/BLOCKED produces a failing check; advisory verdicts do not block
- [ ] Graceful degradation verified (feed offline → UNKNOWN label, no silent pass)
- [ ] Permissions audit: no write beyond comment+label
- [ ] Smoke: end-to-end on a scratch Dependabot PR

## OUTPUT

action.yml + workflow + any helper scripts; smoke evidence from a scratch repo; documented consumer-repo install steps (the specialists CI epic consumes this).

## REFERENCES

- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md` §16 (Action wrapper)
- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` §6 (pipeline), §4.1 (SECURITY_FORCED)
- Depends on B (xtrm-r1ed7.1) and C1 (xtrm-r1ed7.2)
- Consumed by specialists CI-adoption epic (A1)

Live GitHub smoke completed on scratch issue xtrm-dev/core#314:
- Created scratch issue: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/issues/314
- Ran .github/actions/dep-review/review.mjs with GH_TOKEN against PR_NUMBER=314 using PASS case (vite 8.0.13 -> 8.0.16).
- Script exited 0 and reported verdict=PASS label=dependency-review/pass.

title: Deterministic dependency inspector → dependency_update_case.json
description:
## PROBLEM

The skill and the PR classifier need a stable, model-independent object describing the bump. Without a deterministic inspector, the agent invents direct/transitive classification, release age, advisory matches, and usage — reintroducing hallucination. This task builds the deterministic layer (spec §6).

## SUCCESS

A script/harness takes PR metadata + diff + lockfile + manifest (+ optional SBOM/advisory feed) and emits a valid `dependency_update_case.json` (schema `xtrm.dependency_update_case.v0`). Output is deterministic, repeatable, and independent of any LLM.

## SCOPE

New inspector under xtrm-tools (propose location in approach — likely `packages/dep-inspect/` or `cli/src/dep/`). Inputs: PR/diff, lockfile, manifest, ecosystem, registry metadata, advisory lookup (OSV/GHSA), release timestamp, usage/import graph, service ownership. Outputs: the case JSON per spec §7. May add a bin entry. Does NOT do migration/research (that is the skill) and does NOT post PR comments (D1).

## NON_GOALS

- No LLM calls — deterministic only.
- No PR comment / GitHub Action wiring (D1).
- No tarball/install-script deep diff (v0 uses heuristic warnings; spec §20).
- No per-ecosystem cooldown tuning beyond the 7d default + SECURITY_FORCED bypass.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Deterministic-first (spec §6): direct/transitive, prod/dev/build/test, release age, cooldown status, advisory match, malicious-package indicators, usage map, affected services/workflows, test surface, missing signals — all computed, not invented.
- Must validate against schemas/dependency_update_case.schema.json (B).
- SECURITY_FORCED classification rules (policy doc §4.1): KEV / public exploit / EPSS≥0.7 / CVSS≥9.0-and-runtime-reachable / active-attack.
- GitHub Actions treated as build-infrastructure dependency: pin to full SHA, permissions, triggers, maintainer trust (spec §11).
- Structured logging at boundaries (start/end, advisory lookup, registry fetch, failures); no secrets in output.
- bun is the canonical runtime where TS is used.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Inspector runs on a sample PR diff and emits case JSON that validates against the schema
- [ ] Direct vs transitive classification correct on a known nested-entry case (e.g. the PR #152 vitest/vite shape)
- [ ] Advisory lookup matches OSV for a known-vulnerable sample
- [ ] Release-age / cooldown computed correctly (7d window, SECURITY_FORCED bypass)
- [ ] Unit tests for parser, classifier, and SECURITY_FORCED rules
- [ ] Smoke on a real Dependabot PR in a scratch repo

## OUTPUT

Inspector script/bin + unit tests + sample case JSON artifacts; proposed `xt dep inspect` shim noted (not implemented) for the v3 command surface (spec §17).

## REFERENCES

- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md` §6 (deterministic layer), §7 (schema), §11 (GitHub Actions)
- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` §4.1 (SECURITY_FORCED), §6 (pipeline)
- Consumes schema from B (xtrm-r1ed7.1)
notes:
Implemented v0.1 inspector: scripts/dep-inspect.mjs (standalone ESM, zero build-coupling so the D1 Action can run it in consumer CI) + scripts/dep-inspect.test.mjs (node:test, 10/10 pass).

Deterministic layer (spec §6/§7):
- OSV advisory lookup for the TO version (live) -> stale FROM-version transitive entries correctly excluded (PR #152 fix verified: vite@8.0.16 returns 0 advisories).
- npm registry: release age + deprecation -> cooldown (7d policy D2; bypass_security on SECURITY_FORCED; blocked on yanked/suspicious).
- direct/transitive + runtime/dev/build/test scope from manifest.
- CVSS extraction: CVSS_V3 trailing base score OR GHSA qualitative label fallback (CRITICAL>=9/HIGH/MODERATE/LOW) -- needed because OSV now serves CVSS_V4 pure vectors with no trailing score.
- SECURITY_FORCED per policy §4.1: CVSS>=9 AND runtime_reachable, OR known_exploited, OR public_exploit, OR CISA KEV.
- preliminary_verdict walks taxonomy (blocked/security_forced/research_required/cooldown/safe_candidate/unknown).

Validation: 10 unit tests pass; live smokes ok (vite 8.0.16 clean->safe_candidate; vite 8.0.13 HIGH/MODERATE->research_required advisory; CRITICAL control->security_forced). Emits schema xtrm.dependency_update_case.v0.

v0.1 approximations documented in-code: EPSS derived from CVSS (no offline EPSS feed); KEV/public-exploit default false unless passed via input; CVSS_V4 base score not computed (qualitative label used).
close_reason: Done: deterministic inspector implemented and verified. Added scripts/dep-inspect.mjs + scripts/dep-inspect.test.mjs; 10/10 node:test pass; live OSV/npm smoke validates PR #152 fixed-version case and vulnerable-version advisory case; CRITICAL control produces SECURITY_FORCED.

title: updating-dependencies capability v0→v1.5: deterministic dep-bump skill + inspector + PR Action
description:
## PROBLEM

Dependency bumps are too noisy and too expensive to handle ad hoc. Across the xtrm ecosystem, every Dependabot/Renovate PR or lockfile/security workflow touch risks a disproportionate amount of operator time on scanners that block merges on ambiguous or low-risk cases, stale transitive lockfile entries, CI payload gates that fail for harness reasons, and toolchain micro-debugging instead of real risk reasoning. There is no repeatable capability that turns a dependency bump into an evidence-backed decision an agent can make consistently.

This epic builds that capability in its natural home — xtrm-tools — so it ships to every repo via `xt update`. Design decisions are locked in `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` (bead `unitAI-3v5sn`, specialists DB); the exhaustive spec is `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md`.

## SUCCESS

A v0 `updating-dependencies` skill package is shipped in `.xtrm/skills/default/`, a deterministic inspector emits a stable `dependency_update_case.json`, and a minimal-permission GitHub Action wraps them to comment a verdict + label on dependency PRs. An agent (or human) invoking the skill on a real bump produces a consistent upgrade dossier and a verdict from the taxonomy, without inventing the process. The specialists repo adopts the output via its own CI-adoption epic (cross-linked).

## SCOPE

xtrm-tools repository, under `.xtrm/skills/default/updating-dependencies/` (skill, templates, schemas), and a new inspector + Action surface (location TBD by C1/D1 — likely `cli/` or a dedicated `packages/dep-inspect/`). May touch `xt update` asset contracts if new shippable files are added. Does NOT touch specialists workflow YAMLs (that is the specialists adoption epic) and does NOT modify deployer/SRE specialists (delivery boundary per spec §3).

## NON_GOALS

- Not a DevOps monolith: no auto-deploy, auto-rollback, or incident handling (spec §2).
- Not replacing SCA/SBOM/Dependabot/OSV/Snyk — consuming them (spec §2).
- No `xt dep` CLI command in this epic (deferred to v3+ after real cases prove the primitives, spec §17).
- No deployer/SRE specialist modifications; integration is via substrate issue + evidence refs (spec §3, §13).
- No lowering of security gates blindly — advisory/blocking split is evidence-based (policy doc §4).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Deterministic-first: anything computable (direct/transitive, prod/dev, release age, advisory match, usage) MUST come from parsers/scanners/registry metadata, not LLM invention (spec §6).
- Delivery boundary: capability prepares case + may propose patch/comment; deployer decides delivery; SRE observes post-deploy (spec §3).
- Skill must be rigid: specify inputs, source matrix tiers, verdict taxonomy with decision rules, cooldown policy, GitHub-Actions special case, required outputs — no free-form agent process invention (spec §8).
- v0 cooldown default = 7 days; bypass only via SECURITY_FORCED (policy doc §4.1).
- GitHub Action wrapper v1 permissions: read-only + PR comment only; no aggressive auto-mutation (spec §16).
- Telemetry/logging: inspector emits structured JSON (`dependency_update_case.json`, schema `xtrm.dependency_update_case.v0`); Action run produces a stable PR comment artifact and a machine-readable verdict label. No secrets/tokens in any emitted artifact.
- One branch per issue; PR workflow; no direct commits to default branch.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] v0 skill package present: SKILL.md + templates/{upgrade-dossier,pr-comment,research-matrix,post-deploy-watch-spec}.md + schemas/{dependency_update_case,upgrade_dossier}.schema.json
- [ ] Skill invokes cleanly on a sample bump and produces a dossier with all stable sections + a verdict from the taxonomy
- [ ] Inspector produces valid `dependency_update_case.json` (passes its JSON schema) from a sample PR diff/lockfile
- [ ] Action wrapper posts a PR comment with verdict + label on a test dependency PR; no write beyond comment
- [ ] Asset contract / `xt update` picks up the new skill so it installs into a target repo
- [ ] Smoke: end-to-end on one real Dependabot PR in a scratch repo (case → skill dossier → PR comment)
- [ ] No secrets/tokens present in any emitted artifact (grep check)

## OUTPUT

Shipped skill package + inspector + Action in xtrm-tools; version-tagged release that `xt update` can promote. Each child bead hands back changed-file lists, schema validation evidence, and the scratch-repo smoke result. Residual risks (ecosystem cooldown tuning, tarball diff depth) documented as follow-ups.

## REFERENCES

- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependency-bump-policy.md` — decision layer (locked D1–D4, advisory/blocking policy, phased board)
- `~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/dependencies-updating.md` — exhaustive spec (§1–21)

title: agent-docs-maintainer: skill misses repo-identity check and is too aggressive on line caps
description:
Field test on ~/projects/mercury/infra and 5 sibling repos (market-data, darth-feedor, economic-data, treasury-cb, website) exposed several gaps in agent-docs-maintainer:

## What the skill misses

1. **No repo-identity check.** The audit measures line counts, command-ref counts, code-fence density, but never asks the single most important question: 'does a fresh agent learn what this repo IS from the first 20 lines?' All 5 sibling repos open with identical XTRM workflow boilerplate — no description of the repo's role, services, or place in the platform — and the audit happily reports them as clean (apart from soft line-cap notes). The user explicitly flagged this as the gap. Recommendation: add a heuristic that flags 'leads with managed block (xtrm:start) without any preceding prose H1/H2' and recommends a 'Stack Overview' / 'Repo Identity' section.

2. **Line caps applied universally without content awareness.** 300-line preferred / 500-line soft maximum are presented as absolute. After adding a deliberate 142-line prose stack overview to infra (role, services, public surface, sibling networks, data flow, what's NOT here), the audit recommended 'trim' even though the new content is the most valuable in the file. The caps should apply to *boilerplate + CLI manual* sections, not to substantive repo-identity prose. Suggestion: split the size budget — managed/boilerplate blocks measured separately from prose stack overview, with separate caps.

3. **No template for the missing positive content.** references/claude-template.md and references/agents-template.md (per skill description) focus on what to TRIM. There's no template for the 'Stack Overview' / 'Repo Identity' section that's currently missing from every Mercury repo. Suggestion: ship a 'stack-overview-template.md' with sections: role (1 sentence), what runs here (prose, 2-4 paragraphs), public surface (table), sibling stacks / external networks (table), operational entry points (commands), data flow (numbered list), what's NOT in this repo (pointer list). Use ~/projects/mercury/infra/CLAUDE.md committed 2026-06-11 as the reference example.

4. **STALE_TERMS list grows organically — needs project-specific extension.** Currently hardcoded 'YFinance', 'Clavix', 'Jaggers Agent Tools'. Mercury sibling repos surfaced both YFinance (market-data) and Clavix (treasury-cb) hits. Other unrelated projects will have their own. Suggestion: support per-repo stale_terms override via .xtrm/agent-docs.toml or similar config so each project can extend.

5. **BLOAT_HEADINGS over-broad.** 'Quick Reference' is flagged as bloat-prone but in CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md is often the only place essential bd commands live. Need finer-grained scoring: 'Quick Reference' with >30 lines of inline command dumps = bloat; same heading with 5-10 carefully-picked commands = good.

6. **command_ref count penalizes operational entry points.** Counting every backtick command as a bloat indicator means a prose section listing 'make networks / make init / make up' triggers 'trim command references'. A make-target enumeration is load-bearing, not bloat. Suggestion: distinguish between (a) full CLI manuals (e.g. inline 'bd' command reference table) and (b) operational-entry-point pointers (3-10 commands with one-line purposes each).

## Concrete artifacts to update

- scripts/audit_agent_docs.py — add repo-identity-check, split size budget
- references/audit-rules.md — clarify when 300/500 line caps apply
- references/claude-template.md, agents-template.md — add Stack Overview pattern
- NEW references/stack-overview-template.md — prose pattern + example
- SKILL.md — document the new heuristics and the repo-identity expectation

## Reference example

The canonical example of what the skill should encourage is at:
~/projects/mercury/infra/CLAUDE.md (top section 'Mercury Platform — Infra (central gateway + observability)', committed 2026-06-11 via bead infra-w3n). It runs 142 lines of prose+tables ABOVE the xtrm:start marker, covering: role, 3 conceptual layers (edge / observability backbone / MCP read surface), public subdomain table, sibling-stack network table, Makefile entry points, .env requirements, end-to-end data flow, and explicit 'what's NOT in this repo' routing. That is the target shape.
close_reason: Done: added repo-identity audit heuristics, split size/command bloat scoring, per-repo stale-term config, Stack Overview templates, and regression tests.

title: xt spec apply — composition-gate respect: no bypass of sp chain review/approve
description:
## PROBLEM

title: xt spec apply — dispatch planner specialist and persist run linkage
description:
## PROBLEM
Creating the planner bead (.10) is inert without dispatching the planner specialist to act on it. Dispatch must capture the run/job id so spec.yaml can later be reconciled against the produced board.

After .10 creates the planner bead, apply invokes `sp run planner --bead <planner-bead-id> --background`, captures the returned job id, and persists `{planner_bead_id, planner_job_id, dispatched_at}` to a sidecar file (`<spec-dir>/.apply-state.json`) atomically. ## SCRUTINY: high

## SCOPE

- cli/lib/spec/dispatch.ts (new — sp invocation wrapper)
- cli/lib/spec/apply-state.ts (new — sidecar reader/writer with atomic rename)

- Modifying sp invocation semantics

- Sidecar write is atomic (write to .tmp + rename); never half-written state
- Sidecar path is deterministic per spec (next to spec.yaml)

A `xt spec doctor` (or `xt spec apply --check-only`) command inspects deployed planning + test-planning SKILL.md files + planner specialist config, runs a capability matrix check, and reports {capability, present|missing, required_for}. Exit 0 = ready; exit 1 = missing capabilities listed.

title: cataloger bulk-bumps last_sync without verification and writes no last_sync_ref → masks all drift
description:
## Problem
The cataloger (SessionStart hook) bulk-sets last_sync to 'now' for every service in service-registry.json without verifying any SKILL.md against code, and never writes last_sync_ref. Two consequences:
1. drift_detector scan uses last_sync mtime as the pre-filter — once all last_sync = now, the mtime pre-filter returns 0 candidates → real drift is masked (false-clean). This is the 'timestamp-only sync without evidence' anti-pattern the librarian's own prompt forbids, performed by the machinery itself.
2. No last_sync_ref means the gitnexus committed-range compare (last_sync_ref..HEAD) has no base → no_ref → semantic tiering can't run even when gitnexus is available.

## Incident (mercury-market-data)
After a session, all 16 services showed last_sync=2026-05-31T23:19:31 with no last_sync_ref. Drift scan returned 0 despite 20+ changed files in serving-market-api etc. Had to manually reset last_sync + last_sync_ref to the last genuine baseline commit to surface the real drift (75 candidates across 12 services).

## Recommended fix
Cataloger must NOT touch last_sync (that belongs to verified-sync only). Sync operations (drift_detector sync) should write BOTH last_sync (timestamp) AND last_sync_ref (HEAD commit) atomically, only after a verified audit. Distinguish 'catalogued/registered' from 'verified-synced'.
close_reason: register_service no longer stamps last_sync (catalog != verified-sync); scan_drift surfaces never-synced services (no/sentinel last_sync) as drift instead of skipping. Pair is essential: B prevents the masking just moving from false-clean to silent-skip. Tests: test_catalog_vs_synced.py. 49/49 green, mirror synced.

title: _gitnexus_repo_name() resolves to worktree basename → librarian gets no gitnexus in its auto-worktree
description:
## Problem
bootstrap._gitnexus_repo_name() returns os.environ['GITNEXUS_REPO'] or Path(project_root).name. In a git worktree, get_project_root() returns the worktree path, so .name is the worktree dir basename (e.g. 'mercury-market-data-uh1r-service-skills-sync'), which gitnexus has NOT indexed. run_gitnexus_json injects --repo <that-name> → gitnexus can't resolve → cli_error → is_gitnexus_available=False → drift engine silently falls back to mtime-only tiering.

## Impact
The service-skills-sync librarian is a MEDIUM specialist that sp ALWAYS auto-provisions in a worktree. So the librarian NEVER gets gitnexus enrichment — it always runs mtime-only and does unverified wholesale SKILL.md rewrites. The release 5119bd19 --repo auto-injection works in the MAIN checkout (basename matches the indexed label) but is defeated in every worktree. Also: sp does NOT propagate GITNEXUS_REPO to the specialist subprocess, so the env workaround fails.

## Recommended fix
_gitnexus_repo_name() should resolve to the indexed repo label via the git COMMON dir / main worktree (git rev-parse --git-common-dir → parent repo name) or the git remote name, NOT the per-worktree basename. Optionally have sp propagate GITNEXUS_REPO to specialist subprocesses.
close_reason: _gitnexus_repo_name resolves indexed label via git --git-common-dir parent (main worktree), not project_root basename; also fixed hardcoded Path(project_root).name in scan_drift _enrich_item call. Test: test_gitnexus_repo_name.py. 45/45 green, mirror synced.

title: drift_detector scan_drift(enrich_with_gitnexus=True) is an OOM footgun — unbounded per-item gitnexus subprocess fan-out
description:
## Problem
service-skills scripts/drift_detector.py: scan_drift(enrich_with_gitnexus=True) (and _enrich_item → _gitnexus_compare) spawns ONE 'npx gitnexus' subprocess PER drifted candidate with no concurrency cap and no candidate limit. Each subprocess loads the repo graph into memory. Over a large/unfiltered territory this fans out to thousands of concurrent node processes and OOMs the host.

## Real incident (mercury-market-data, 32GB Netcup VPS)
A territory glob 'rust_ingestor/**/*' matched 3646 gitignored target/ build artifacts → scan surfaced 4991 candidates → enrich_with_gitnexus tried to spawn ~thousands of 'npx gitnexus' procs concurrently on a host already running 3 dolt sql-servers + DoltLab + the app stack. Operator had to kill it to prevent OOM.

## Root causes (two, compounding)
1. No bound on enrichment fan-out: per-item subprocess, no semaphore/pool, no max-candidates.
2. Territory globs match the FILESYSTEM (glob.glob), not git-tracked files — .gitignore is ignored, so build/vendor trees (rust target/, __pycache__) get scanned. (Separate but it's what made the candidate set huge.)

## Recommended fix
- Cap enrichment concurrency (small pool, e.g. 2-4) and/or batch a single gitnexus compare for all candidates of a service instead of per-file.
- Add a hard max-candidates guard with a loud warning when exceeded.
- Pre-filter candidates: respect .gitignore (or exclude common build/vendor/cache dirs) before enriching.
- Document that enrich_with_gitnexus over a broad territory is expensive; default scans should stay use_gitnexus mtime-surface + bounded per-service compare.

## Severity
P1 — can take down a shared host; hit during normal first-run drift validation.
close_reason: Fixed 3 compounding OOM defects in drift_detector: (1) gitignore-respect via git ls-files filter before enrichment, (2) hard candidate cap (DRIFT_MAX_ENRICH=200) with mtime fallback + loud warning, (3) process-group kill (Popen start_new_session + os.killpg) so npx's node grandchild cannot linger. post_merge sweep forced to mtime-only (use_gitnexus=False). Source+mirror synced, registry parity 330/330, 41 service-skills tests green (2 new OOM-guard tests). Branch fix/xtrm-08i0b-drift-oom.

title: drift_detector.py sync never stamps last_sync_ref (update_sync_time passes project_root=None to _git_head)
description:
## PROBLEM
drift_detector.py update_sync_time (skills/service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py:46-62)
is the canonical way to stamp a service as synced. On the CLI path (`drift_detector.py sync
<id>`) main() calls update_sync_time(service_id) with project_root=None. Line 55 then calls
_git_head(project_root) i.e. _git_head(None) -> subprocess.run(['git','-C',None,'rev-parse',
'HEAD']) which raises (None is not a str), caught at line 56-57 -> last_sync_ref = "".

Net effect: `sync` stamps last_sync (timestamp) but last_sync_ref is ALWAYS "" on the CLI
path. Since scan_drift requires last_sync_ref to do the committed-range gitnexus compare
(last_sync_ref..HEAD), an empty ref forces gitnexus_status=no_ref -> tier_source=mtime for
EVERY service, permanently. This is the mechanical root cause behind the whole
'drift_detector degrades to mtime / librarian falls back to grep' saga (xtrm-0p7bp / q7436):
even a correctly-wired hook can never tier semantically because the ref is never stored.
Proven on mercury/darth-feedor: 11/11 services had no last_sync_ref after a librarian run;
`drift_detector.py sync <id>` wrote '' for each (had to stamp manually).

## SUCCESS
`drift_detector.py sync <id>` stamps last_sync_ref to the current HEAD (resolved via the same
project-root resolution load_registry uses) on the CLI path, not "". scan then measures
last_sync_ref..HEAD and tiers semantically.

## SCOPE
skills/service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py (update_sync_time / _git_head project-root
resolution) + mirror; a regression test under skills/service-skills/tests/.

## NON_GOALS
- Not changing scan_drift tiering or the registry schema.
- Not the in-session hook wiring (xtrm-0p7bp) or post-merge sweep (xtrm-jcmub).

## CONSTRAINTS
- Resolve project_root via bootstrap (same as load_registry) before _git_head; keep the
  try/except '' fallback only for a genuine git failure (detached/no-commits), not for None.
- Idempotent; preserve last_sync timestamp behavior.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] sync <id> in a tmp git repo stamps last_sync_ref to HEAD (non-empty)
- [ ] regression test asserts non-empty ref after sync
- [ ] mirror + registry parity green

## OUTPUT
Fix + test + note that this unblocks semantic tiering for all service repos.

## REFERENCES
darth-feedor py_backend-0ndo (manual ref stamp commit 3d4755e). Related: xtrm-0p7bp, xtrm-q7436,
xtrm-jcmub. Epic xtrm-b86y5.
close_reason: Fixed update_sync_time: resolve project_root via get_project_root() before _git_head so CLI 'sync <id>' stamps last_sync_ref=HEAD instead of ''. Unblocks semantic tiering (no more forced mtime fallback) for all service repos. Test added; 39 pytest green; parity 330/330.

title: service-skills updating: gitnexus triage mandatory; forbid string-only drift verdicts even when drift_detector pre-script fails
description:
## PROBLEM
A librarian (service-skills-sync) run on darth-feedor did a string-level path-migration
sweep (legacy path -> .xtrm path) but NEVER used gitnexus for semantic triage: the
pre-script emitted 'drift_detector not available', and the librarian pattern-matched on
that tooling-failure signal and silently downgraded to grep-driven string hunting for the
WHOLE run. It then applied the strong label 'audited-and-unchanged' (which implies
gitnexus-backed triage) to services whose Architecture/Data-Flow/Failure-Mode sections it
never verified against current symbols (e.g. SemanticDeduplicatorTSDB, GmailSubstackImporter
existence/signatures unconfirmed). Correctness of the path rewrites is fine; the VERDICT
LABEL is inflated. Root: the updating contract lets a tooling-failure license a weaker mode
+ a stronger-than-earned verdict.

## SUCCESS
The updating-service-skills contract (skill + specialist) makes gitnexus-backed semantic
triage MANDATORY and forbids string-only verdicts:
- a failed/absent drift_detector pre-script is NOT license to skip semantic triage — the
  librarian must fall back to gitnexus directly (gitnexus_detect_changes / gitnexus_impact
  or the CLI), not to grep-only.
- verdict vocabulary is split: only 'audited-and-unchanged' when gitnexus-backed symbol/flow
  verification ran; otherwise the weaker, honest 'synced (string-level only, no semantic
  verification)' must be used.
- if gitnexus itself is unavailable, that is a BLOCKER to claim 'unchanged' — the run reports
  the gap and leaves the service at the weaker label, not the strong one.

## SCOPE
skills/service-skills/references/updating.md (triage steps + verdict taxonomy + the
'tooling-failure != skip semantic' rule) and its mirror; the service-skills-sync specialist
contract in /home/dawid/dev/specialists (config/specialists/service-skills-sync.specialist.json
and/or its mandatory rules) so 'first triage action is gitnexus' and 'no string-only
unchanged verdict' are enforced, not advisory.

## NON_GOALS
- Not the path-migration sweep itself (those rewrites are valid; ship them).
- Not changing drift_detector tiering logic (xtrm-jcmub / b86y5 own that).
- Not the darth-feedor SKILL.md semantic audit itself — that is a separate darth-feedor-scoped
  bead (gitnexus-mandatory; first action must be gitnexus_detect_changes), filed in that repo.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Prerequisite for any real audit run: `xt update --apply` so the drift_detector hook is
  actually wired (xtrm-0p7bp) — document that the 'not available' signal usually means the
  consumer is un-updated, not that semantic triage is excused.
- Keep the string-level fast path as a labelled, weaker mode — do not delete it.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] updating.md states: drift_detector pre-script failure => fall back to gitnexus, never grep-only
- [ ] verdict taxonomy distinguishes 'audited-and-unchanged' (gitnexus-backed) from 'synced (string-level only)'
- [ ] service-skills-sync specialist mandatory-rule forbids string-only 'unchanged' verdicts
- [ ] a dry-run / example shows the weaker label applied when gitnexus is unavailable

## OUTPUT
Updated updating.md (+ mirror) + service-skills-sync specialist contract change + note on the
xt update --apply prerequisite. Cross-link the darth-feedor semantic-audit follow-up bead.

## REFERENCES
Librarian retrospective on darth-feedor (2026-06-01). Related: xtrm-0p7bp (hook wiring),
xtrm-jcmub (post-merge sweep), epic xtrm-b86y5.
close_reason: Hardened both sides: updating.md (+mirror) now repairs gitnexus on tooling-failure + Verdict Taxonomy forbidding string-only audited-and-unchanged; specialists service-skills-sync v1.3.0 + new mandatory-rule service-skills-gitnexus-triage enforce gitnexus-cited unchanged verdicts. Specialist resolves clean (sp list --full); parity 330/330.

title: layout_migrator must update PACK.json + force active-view rebuild after service-skills migration
description:
## PROBLEM
The v2 service-skills migration (ensureServiceSkills → layout_migrator.py) has two compounding bugs that surfaced migrating mercury repos (darth-feedor, market-data, treasury-cb) on 0.8.2:

1. **PACK.json not updated**: migrate_pack() moves per-service dirs from pack-root (packs/<pack>/<svc>/) into packs/<pack>/service-skills/services/<svc>/, but does NOT update the pack's PACK.json skills[] list. PACK.json keeps listing the moved services (now metadata-only) and omits the new 'service-skills' umbrella (filesystem-only) → PACK_METADATA_MISMATCH. This BLOCKS 'xt init' active-view rebuild (skills invariant fails). All 3 migrated repos had broken PACK.json; only those whose active view happened to rebuild during a drift-triggering 'xt update' pass escaped visible breakage.

2. **Active view not rebuilt after migration**: when a repo migrates on a 2nd apply pass (or any apply that reports drifted=0), the skills-materializer skips rebuilding .xtrm/skills/active, so the new 'service-skills' machinery + per-repo '<repo>-services' umbrella never get symlinked into the active view → the consumer sees NO new service-skills skill. darth-feedor hit this (active frozen at pre-migration date; service-skills present in default but absent from active).

Also observed: stale non-symlink .xtrm/skills/active/gitnexus pollution (xtrm-wbfd) co-occurs and trips activeReady.

## SUCCESS
After 'xt update --apply' migrates a service-skills pack, PACK.json reflects the actual pack-root skills (regular skills + 'service-skills' umbrella, NOT the nested services), the active view is rebuilt to include 'service-skills' + the '<repo>-services' umbrella, and a subsequent 'xt init' passes the skills invariant cleanly.

## SCOPE
skills/service-skills/scripts/layout_migrator.py (update PACK.json in migrate_pack), cli/src/core/service-skills-ensure.ts (force active-view rebuild after migration), cli/src/core/skills-materializer.ts / skills-runtime-views (rebuild trigger when default has skills absent from active even at drifted=0).

## NON_GOALS
- Removing the stale pre-v2 trinity skills (creating/scoping/updating/using-service-skills) lingering in consumer default/active — separate cleanup.

## CONSTRAINTS
- PACK.json skills[] = top-level pack-root dirs containing SKILL.md (idempotent; reuse the xt-skills-enable auto-sync logic).
- Migration must remain idempotent and safe.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] E2E: migrate a flat pack, assert PACK.json skills[] updated (moved services removed, service-skills added)
- [ ] E2E: assert active view contains service-skills + <repo>-services after a single apply
- [ ] regression: 'xt init' passes invariant on a freshly-migrated repo
- [ ] covers the 2-pass / drifted=0 case (active rebuilt even when registry drift is 0)

## OUTPUT
Migrator + ensure + materializer changes, E2E coverage. Field-fixed manually in mercury/{darth-feedor,market-data,treasury-cb} PACK.json on 2026-05-31.
close_reason: layout_migrator now syncs PACK.json skills[] to direct-child dirs with SKILL.md (umbrella in, ghost services out) clearing PACK_METADATA_MISMATCH; ensureServiceSkills forces rebuildAllRuntimeActiveViews after migration (init+update) so migration-only passes no longer leave the active view frozen. Tests: test_layout_migrator_packjson.py + service-skills-ensure.test.ts. Full python + ensure/skills/init/update suites green; 3 pre-existing pi-runtime env failures unrelated.
