title: xtrm finish CLI command: phase1 + poll loop + phase2 with conflict auto-rebase
description:
Single blocking command that replaces the entire manual closure flow. Returns only when worktree is cleaned up or an unrecoverable state is reached.

Phase 1 (fast, <10s):
1. Read .xtrm-session-state.json → get issueId, branch, worktreePath
2. git add -A && git commit -m 'feat(<issueId>): <branch>' (skip if working tree clean)
3. git push -u origin <branch>
4. gh pr create --fill → capture prNumber + prUrl from output
5. gh pr merge --squash --auto
6. Write prNumber, prUrl to state file, phase: waiting-merge

Poll loop (blocks, 5s interval, 10min timeout):
- gh pr view <prNumber> --json state,mergeStateStatus,mergeable
- state=MERGED            → phase 2
- mergeStateStatus=BEHIND → git fetch + git push (rebase not needed, just push)
- mergeable=CONFLICTING   → conflict resolution:
    a. git fetch origin && git rebase origin/main
    b. if clean: git push --force-with-lease → continue polling
    c. if conflicts remain: write phase=conflicting + conflictFiles → exit with message
       'Conflicts in: <files>. Resolve, push, then re-run xtrm finish.'
- timeout (10min):        → write phase=pending-cleanup → exit with:
       'PR #<n> not yet merged. Run xtrm finish when ready.'

Phase 2 (on MERGED):
- git worktree remove <worktreePath> --force
- git fetch --prune
- write phase=cleanup-done
- print: 'Done. PR #<n> merged. Worktree removed.'

CLI: xtrm finish (no args — reads all context from state file)
Re-entrant: if state=waiting-merge/pending-cleanup, skips phase 1 and resumes poll loop with stored prNumber.
Re-entrant: if state=conflicting, expects conflicts resolved, skips to push+poll.
close_reason: Implemented

title: Streamlined session closure: xtrm finish + worktree-first workflow
description:

- Worktree auto-created on bd claim (beads-claim-sync.mjs extended)
- .xtrm-session-state.json is the single source of truth: issueId, branch, worktreePath, prNumber, prUrl, phase
- xtrm finish is a single blocking command: phase1 (commit+push+PR+auto-merge) + poll loop + phase2 (worktree cleanup) — returns only when done

Phase lifecycle:
  claimed → phase1-done → waiting-merge → (conflicting →) merged → cleanup-done

title: Adapt ralphi autonomous loop pattern for xtrm workflow
description:
## Overview

Adapt the [@manojlds/ralphi](https://github.com/manojlds/ralphi) autonomous loop pattern to integrate with the xtrm-tools workflow, replacing its native PRD/stories system with beads issue tracking and integrating all xtrm enforcement mechanisms.

## What ralphi Provides

ralphi is a Pi-native implementation of the Ralph autonomous loop pattern:

- **`/ralphi-init`** — initialize project config and guardrails
- **`/ralphi-prd`** — generate PRD markdown from feature idea
- **`/ralphi-convert`** — convert PRD markdown to \`.ralphi/prd.json\`
- **`/ralphi-loop-start`** — run iterative implementation against PRD

Key features:
- Fresh-context loop iterations (child sessions)
- PRD-driven story selection with dependency handling
- Quality gates via config.yaml commands
- Trajectory guard (drift detection)
- Reflection checkpoints

## Adaptation Goals

### 1. Replace PRD/stories with Beads

| ralphi | xtrm-adapted |
|--------|--------------|
| \`.ralphi/prd.json\` | \`.beads/issues.jsonl\` |
| `userStories[].status` | bd issue status (open/in_progress/closed) |
| `userStories[].priority` | bd priority (0-4) |
| `userStories[].dependsOn` | bd dependencies (`--blocked-by`) |

### 2. Integrate xtrm Components

- **main-guard**: PR-only workflow enforcement
- **beads gates**: Edit/commit/stop gates with claim tracking
- **quality-gates**: Lint/typecheck via Pi extension
- **test-planning**: Create companion test issues automatically
- **gitnexus**: Impact analysis before changes
- **using-xtrm**: Session operating manual

### 3. New Command Structure

```
/xtrm-init           # Initialize project with xtrm guardrails
/xtrm-prd <desc>     # Generate PRD, create bd epic + child issues
/xtrm-loop-start     # Start autonomous loop against bd issues
/xtrm-loop-status    # Show loop progress
/xtrm-loop-stop      # Halt loop
```

### 4. Loop Behavior

1. Controller reads `bd ready` to find unblocked issues
2. Claims issue: `bd update <id> --claim`
3. Fresh child session implements the issue
4. Quality gates run automatically (via Pi extension)
5. On completion: `bd close <id> --reason`
6. Next iteration picks next unblocked issue
7. Loop ends when no more ready issues

### 5. Test Planning Integration

When PRD generates issues:
- Classify each by layer (core/boundary/shell)
- Create companion test issues per test-planning skill
- Link via dependencies

## Key Differences from ralphi

| Aspect | ralphi | xtrm-adapted |
|--------|--------|--------------|
| Issue store | \`.ralphi/prd.json\` | beads (Dolt-backed) |
| Claim model | None | Session-scoped claims |
| Quality gates | config.yaml commands | Pi extension + hooks |
| Branch protection | Manual config | main-guard enforcement |
| Test strategy | None | test-planning skill |
| Code intelligence | None | gitnexus integration |

## Deliverables

1. Pi extension: `xtrm-loop.ts`
2. Skills: `xtrm-init`, `xtrm-prd`, `xtrm-loop-start`, `xtrm-loop-status`
3. Config schema: \`.xtrm/config.yaml\` structure
4. Integration tests with beads workflow
5. Documentation update to XTRM-GUIDE.md

## References

- ralphi source: https://github.com/manojlds/ralphi
- ralphi npm: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@manojlds/ralphi
- beads docs: https://github.com/steveyegge/beads

title: Hook integration for test-planning lifecycle (UserPromptSubmit/PostToolUse/SessionEnd)
description:
Purpose
Implement hook-level lifecycle integration for the test-planning skill so testing strategy is consistently introduced at planning time, validated at closure time, and reviewed at session end.

Dependency Requirement
This epic depends on completion of:
- xtrm-thn4 (Test-planning v1.1)
The hook automation in this epic must consume and enforce the improved skill guidance from that foundation epic.

Problem Statement
Today, test-planning quality relies heavily on manual invocation and agent discipline. Even with good skill docs, drift happens during high-throughput issue planning and closure. We need deterministic hook touchpoints that provide high-signal nudges (and optional strict gating) without noisy false positives.

Goals
1) Integrate test-planning at precise lifecycle points with minimal noise
2) Detect planning and closure intents automatically from tool events
3) Run a closure safety net to prevent implementation issues from being closed without planned test coverage
4) Preserve configurability through policy modes (advisory vs strict)
5) Maintain parity between Claude hook behavior and Pi extension behavior

Non-Goals
- Do not rewrite the core test-planning strategy content in this epic (owned by dependency epic)
- Do not enforce universal strict blocking by default
- Do not introduce heavyweight background indexing/polling

Scope of Work
A. UserPromptSubmit Intent Detection
- Add prompt-level detection for planning/closure phrases:
  - “create issues”, “break into tasks”, “close issue”, “bd create”, “bd close”, “bd children”
- On detection, emit targeted suggestion to apply test-planning skill
- Ensure suppression for clearly unrelated prompts to avoid noise

B. PostToolUse Deterministic Triggering (Bash + bd commands)
- For tool executions containing bd commands:
  1. On `bd create`:
     - classify issue as implementation vs non-implementation
     - check for matching/batched companion test issue
     - if absent: emit recommendation (advisory mode) or enforce next-step gate (strict mode)
  2. On `bd close`:
     - run closure gate check (existing test issue? still accurate to built scope?)
     - if missing/outdated: emit actionable update/create guidance
- Include parsing resilience for flag order variations and quoted values

C. Stop / SessionEnd Safety Net
- At session end, summarize implementation issues touched without test-plan linkage
- Default behavior: non-blocking warning + suggested bd commands
- Strict mode option: require acknowledgement or block stop until recorded exception path

D. Policy Modes + Configuration
- Add explicit config modes:
  - `advisory` (default): suggest, never block
  - `strict-close`: block/deny close path when no test plan linkage exists
  - `strict-session`: enforce end-session acknowledgement
- Document env/config toggles and precedence order

E. Claude/Pi Parity Layer
- Ensure equivalent behavior mapping in:
  - Claude hooks configuration/path
  - Pi extension equivalents
- Add parity matrix documenting event, trigger, action, and strictness behavior per runtime

F. Messaging UX
- Standardize concise, actionable messages:
  - what failed/missing
  - why it matters
  - exact `bd` command snippets to remediate
- Avoid verbose diagnostics in normal path; detailed logs only in debug mode

G. Observability + Debugging
- Add debug mode to log per-event decisions:
  - invoked / skipped / matched-intent / remediation-generated
- Include skip reasons for false-positive tuning

Deliverables
1) Hook/extension integration implementation for 3 lifecycle points:
- UserPromptSubmit
- PostToolUse (bd create/bd close)
- Stop/SessionEnd

2) Runtime configuration model for advisory/strict policies

3) Parity documentation (Claude vs Pi behavior table)

4) Test coverage for trigger detection and gating behavior

Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: Planning-intent prompts trigger test-planning suggestion with low false positives
- AC2: `bd create` path detects implementation issues and checks companion test-plan presence
- AC3: `bd close` path runs closure gate checks and emits deterministic remediation
- AC4: Session end summarizes unresolved test-plan gaps; strict mode behavior works as configured
- AC5: Advisory and strict modes are configurable, documented, and covered by tests
- AC6: Claude and Pi implementations show behavior parity for equivalent events
- AC7: Messaging includes copy/paste-safe bd remediation commands

Risk Analysis
- Risk: Over-triggering could create friction
  - Mitigation: conservative intent matching + skip reasons + advisory default
- Risk: Command parsing edge cases
  - Mitigation: robust parser tests for quoting/flag order/compound commands
- Risk: Runtime drift between Claude and Pi
  - Mitigation: parity test suite + parity matrix as release gate

Suggested Work Breakdown
1. Implement intent detector + unit tests
2. Implement PostToolUse bd parser + create/close handlers
3. Implement SessionEnd safety net
4. Add mode config and wire toggles
5. Build parity tests (Claude vs Pi)
6. Add docs and operational examples

title: Test-planning v1.1: deterministic strategy, anti-pattern controls, and DoD templates
description:
Purpose
Elevate the existing skills/test-planning skill from a strong baseline to a production-grade planning standard for test strategy in bd-driven workflows.

Background
The current test-planning skill already provides excellent foundations:
- layer-based classification (core/boundary/shell)
- strategy routing (TDD/spec-first/property/contract/characterization/example-based)
- planning-phase + closure-gate behavior
- batching guidance and bd-native issue structures

This epic upgrades that baseline with sharper quality controls, deterministic prioritization, and explicit Definition-of-Done standards so generated/updated test issues are consistently actionable.

Problem Statement
Current skill guidance can still produce variability across agents/sessions:
- anti-patterns are described indirectly but not enforced as a standard checklist
- test issue priorities are not consistently normalized against implementation risk
- layer guidance exists, but completion criteria are not codified as strict DoD templates
- teams may over-focus on broad coverage percentages over critical-path confidence
- advisory vs enforcement boundaries are implied but not explicit

Goals
1) Add explicit anti-pattern prevention checklist for planning + closure review
2) Add risk-based priority model for generated test issues
3) Add per-layer Definition of Done templates with concrete pass criteria
4) Replace blanket coverage framing with critical-path and risk-path expectations
5) Clarify policy boundary: what skill recommends vs what hooks enforce

Non-Goals
- Do not implement hook automation in this epic (tracked separately)
- Do not add new runtime dependencies
- Do not rewrite quality-gates behavior itself beyond documentation alignment

Scope of Work
A. Anti-Pattern Checklist Integration
- Add a standardized checklist section used at both triggers (planning and closure)
- Required checks:
  1. assertion-free tests
  2. tautological assertions (self-fulfilling logic)
  3. context leakage/shared mutable state
  4. over-mocking internal collaborators
  5. test cases that cannot fail under realistic regressions
- Add “how to detect” and “how to fix” bullets per anti-pattern

B. Priority Heuristics for Test Issues
- Introduce deterministic priority mapping:
  - P0/P1: boundary/security/auth/protocol compatibility/regression-critical paths
  - P1/P2: core domain logic with high business impact
  - P2/P3: low-risk internals, non-critical adapters
  - P3/P4: polish-level test debt
- Add inheritance rule from implementation issue priority with bounded adjustment
- Add examples for when tests should be equal priority vs +1 priority

C. Layer-Specific Definition of Done Templates
- Core DoD template:
  - positive + negative path assertions
  - edge cases explicitly enumerated
  - invariants/properties included where applicable
  - deterministic fixtures and no shared mutable state
- Boundary DoD template:
  - schema/contract assertions
  - error code and retry/fallback behavior where relevant
  - drift-safe assertions (field presence/types, not brittle internals)
  - live-first policy and fallback hierarchy documented
- Shell DoD template:
  - end-to-end observable outcomes
  - failure-mode UX (exit codes/messages) assertions
  - cross-component wiring checks

D. Coverage Guidance Modernization
- Remove/avoid blanket numeric coverage framing as primary success metric
- Require “critical path map” in issue description:
  - paths covered
  - risk rationale
  - known deferred paths (with follow-up issue references)

E. Enforcement Boundary Clarification
- Add explicit section in SKILL.md:
  - advisory from skill (planning quality, strategy selection)
  - enforced by hooks/extensions (quality-gates, branch/claim rules)
- Include examples to avoid policy confusion

Deliverables
1) Updated skill file:
- skills/test-planning/SKILL.md with all new sections/templates/checklists

2) Example patterns in-document:
- at least 2 end-to-end issue description examples using new templates

3) Consistency alignment:
- terminology alignment with using-quality-gates and broader xtrm testing philosophy

Acceptance Criteria
- AC1: SKILL.md includes a mandatory anti-pattern checklist used in both trigger flows
- AC2: Priority heuristic table exists with deterministic mapping + examples
- AC3: DoD templates exist for core, boundary, shell with concrete pass/fail criteria
- AC4: Guidance uses critical-path coverage framing, not blanket percentage mandates
- AC5: Advisory vs enforcement boundaries are explicitly documented with examples
- AC6: At least two realistic issue examples show the new format end-to-end

Risks
- Over-prescriptive templates could increase issue creation overhead
- Priority heuristics may need calibration after first few real-world uses

Mitigations
- Keep templates concise and structured
- Collect first-iteration feedback and tune thresholds in follow-up task(s)

Dependencies
- None (foundation epic)

Out of Scope Follow-ups
- Hook-based automation and gating integration (separate epic)

Definition of Complete
This epic is complete when the test-planning skill documentation is upgraded to a deterministic, reusable standard that reliably produces high-quality, risk-aware test planning issues without requiring runtime hook automation.

title: Test: policy compiler — integration + schema validation tests
description:
## What this covers

Covers: xtrm-ei6 (policy schema), xtrm-o52 (compiler), xtrm-cuk (main-guard + beads policies)

## Layer classification

- `policies/schema.json` → Core (pure data, JSON Schema definition)
- `scripts/compile-policies.mjs` → Shell (CLI tool: reads files, writes hooks.json)

## Strategy: Integration tests (shell layer, deterministic I/O)

The compiler is a pure function over the filesystem: given N policy files → produces hooks.json. No external I/O beyond file reads/writes. Integration tests with fixture directories are ideal.

## Test file structure

`tests/compile-policies/` (or `scripts/tests/` if colocated with the script):
- `fixtures/policies/` — sample policy JSON files
- `fixtures/expected-hooks.json` — expected compiler output
- `compile-policies.test.mjs` — test suite

## What to assert

### Compiler correctness
- [ ] Given the 5 current policy files → output matches `hooks/hooks.json` exactly (golden file test)
- [ ] Same-matcher hooks from multiple policies merge into one group (order preserved)
- [ ] `order` field controls policy execution sequence within the same event
- [ ] Policies with `runtime: pi` are excluded from hooks.json output
- [ ] No matcher entry is emitted as `null` or empty string — omitted entirely

### CLI flags
- [ ] `--dry-run`: prints JSON to stdout, does NOT write hooks.json
- [ ] `--check`: exits 0 when hooks.json matches; exits 1 when stale (with useful error message)
- [ ] Write mode: overwrites hooks.json, prints per-policy hook counts

### Schema validation (if validation is added to compiler)
- [ ] Policy missing required `id` → validation error
- [ ] Policy with unknown field → validation error (additionalProperties: false)
- [ ] Policy with invalid `runtime` value → validation error

### Edge cases
- [ ] Empty policies/ directory → empty hooks object `{}`
- [ ] Policy with no `claude.hooks` → contributes nothing to output
- [ ] Timeout omitted → no timeout field in generated entry

## Acceptance criteria

All assertions pass. `npm run check-policies` passes in CI (add to .github/workflows/ci.yml).

description:
## Description

The Pi equivalent should:

title: memory-gate fires every session + marker file unwritable on main
description:
## Problem

beads-memory-gate stop hook fires every session because it checks `bd list --status=closed` (all ever-closed issues) rather than issues closed *this* session. Once triggered, it requires `touch .beads/.memory-gate-done` — but the absolute path was being used, which doesn't match the main-guard allowlist pattern `/^touch\s+\.beads\//`. Using relative path `touch .beads/.memory-gate-done` from project CWD works fine.

## Root Cause

**beads-memory-gate.mjs**: checked all-time closed issues instead of scoping to the current session's claimed issue.

## Fix

Only fire the gate if the session had a claimed issue that is now closed. Use `getSessionClaim(sessionId, cwd)` to retrieve the claim, then check if it appears in `bd list --status=closed`.

title: Use manifest for drift detection
description:
The .jaggers-sync-manifest.json tracks:

title: Debug: Beads claim workflow not working reliably
description:
## Problem

The beads claim workflow should auto-set `bd kv claimed:<session_id> <issue_id>` when running `bd update <id> --claim`, but it's not working reliably.

## Expected Behavior

1. Run `bd update <issue-id> --claim`
2. Hook or extension auto-sets `bd kv set "claimed:<session_id>" "<issue-id>"`
3. Statusline shows claimed issue (e.g., `bd:r34◐`)
4. Edits are unblocked

## Actual Behavior

- The claim is set on the issue (status becomes `in_progress`)
- But the kv entry is NOT set
- Statusline shows open count (`bd:2○`) instead of claimed issue
- Manual `bd kv set` is required

---

## Architecture

### Components Involved

| Component | Location | Role |
|-----------|----------|------|
| Pi Extension | `cli/extensions/beads.ts` | Should catch `bd update --claim` via `tool_result` event and set kv |
| Pi Extension | `config/pi/extensions/custom-footer.ts` | Reads kv to display beads chip in statusline |
| PostToolUse Hook | `hooks/beads-claim-sync.mjs` | Should catch `bd update --claim` and set kv |
| PreToolUse Hook | `hooks/beads-edit-gate.mjs` | Checks kv to allow/block edits |

### Session ID Strategy (Attempted)

| Attempt | Session Key Source | Problem |
|---------|-------------------|---------|
| 1. PID | `process.pid.toString()` | Hook runs in subprocess, different PID than Pi |
| 2. Project path | `input.cwd` | Works but doesn't match Pi's PID-based key |

title: CLI: restructure install into all / basic / project subcommands
description:
## Context
The current xtrm install flow is monolithic and interactive. Users need granular control: some want everything, some only skills, some only project hooks. The new structure gives three clear install profiles while preserving all existing functionality.

## New install command structure

### xtrm install all
Global install of everything:
- All skills (skills/)
- All global hooks: general hooks (Python + main-guard.mjs) + beads gate hooks (beads-*.mjs)
- MCP server registration (~/.claude/mcp.json or settings.json)
- Runs beads+dolt dependency check BEFORE installing beads hooks (see separate issue)
- Prompts: 'Install beads+dolt? Required for workflow enforcement hooks [y/N]'
- On yes or already installed: installs beads hooks
- On no: installs everything except beads hooks, prints note

### xtrm install basic
Global install without beads hooks:
- All skills (skills/)
- General global hooks only (Python hooks + main-guard.mjs)
- MCP server registration
- No beads dependency check — beads hooks are intentionally excluded
- Safe to run anywhere with zero external deps

### xtrm install project
Project-scoped install (must be run from a project directory with a .git root):
- Installs project-skills/ (py-quality-gate, ts-quality-gate, tdd-guard, service-skills-set)
- Merges settings.json hooks into project's .claude/settings.json (deep merge, no clobber)
- Fails clearly if not in a git project directory

## Flags (all subcommands)
- --dry-run: show what would be installed, no writes
- --yes / -y: non-interactive, accept all prompts
- --no-mcp: skip MCP registration
- --force: overwrite existing files

## Acceptance criteria
- xtrm install all installs all components, runs beads check
- xtrm install basic installs skills + general hooks + mcp, skips beads
- xtrm install project installs project-skills into cwd
- --dry-run prints install manifest without writing
- --yes suppresses all prompts (for CI/automation)
- Banner displayed in all subcommand views
- No regression: existing install behavior preserved or improved

## Open idea review
Should there be even finer granularity? e.g., xtrm install hooks, xtrm install skills, xtrm install mcp as atomic subcommands composable by power users? The three profiles (all/basic/project) cover 90% of use cases but flags like --no-mcp within each profile may be cleaner than extra subcommands. What is the right granularity boundary?

title: skillbridge: mount python-backed skills as importable kernel modules (v1 + reload)
description:
PROBLEM: Capabilities are prompt-described (SKILL.md into context, one tool round trip per op). Kernel `_ns` starts bare; no discovery surface. Verified anchors: DRIVER template at index.ts:34, `_ns = {}` line ~37, spawn+env at :150-158, static tool description at :355+.

DESIGN (3 seams):
1) DRIVER bootstrap: after `_ns = {}`, read PI_SKILL_PATHS (os.pathsep-joined roots) -> sys.path.insert(0, p); read PI_SKILL_IMPORTS (comma list) -> importlib.import_module each into _ns[name]; per-module failures recorded to _sk_errors, boot never dies. Zero-install sys.path mount (skills have no external deps; uv-venv deferred - pythonBin override is the escape hatch).
2) TS discovery at init: scan ~/.pi/agent/skills/*, project .pi/agent/skills/*, repo .agents/skills/* for python-backed skills (SKILL.md + src/<import_name>/__init__.py, prime-agent Agent Skills convention); blurb from SKILL.md frontmatter description; pass PI_SKILL_PATHS/PI_SKILL_IMPORTS in spawn env; append to tool description: "Importable skill modules: a, b, c - pre-imported in namespace; help(x) for docs."
3) reload_skills tool param: del sys.modules[name] + re-import + refresh _ns (dev-loop honesty; stale-import trap documented in global prompt).

SUCCESS: model experience = `import sre_chain; sre_chain.load(...); sre_chain.run(dry_run=True)` with zero host round trips; boot reports per-module import status in tool details; description lists available modules; reload param works.
VALIDATION: extension unit test for discovery scan; manual: mount a fixture skill, python call `import <fixture>; <fixture>.fn()`; bad-skill boot continues with _sk_errors surfaced.
NON_GOALS: no uv install management; no audit enforcement (separate child).
close_reason: skillbridge: DRIVER boot mounts PI_SKILL_PATHS/PI_SKILL_IMPORTS into _ns with _sk_errors surfacing (boot never dies); TS discovery scans skill roots for SKILL.md+src/<name>/__init__.py with blurb; spawn env carries paths/imports; reload_skills tool param re-imports (del sys.modules + re-import, pyc cache disabled); description lists importable modules. 6 new tests + 10 existing pass; full pi-extensions suite 24 pass; npm run typecheck + check:pi-manifest + check:runtime-compat clean.

title: python-kernel extension v2: skills-as-imports (prime-agent pattern) + robustness
description:
PROBLEM: The python-kernel extension (core/packages/pi-extensions/extensions/python-kernel/ (npm @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions; installed globally via `pi install npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions`)) exposes a persistent CPython kernel as one `python` tool, but capabilities stay prompt-described: skills are SKILL.md prose burned into context, every operation costs a tool round trip, and there is no discovery surface for what the kernel can do. prime-agent (pi-mono fork by Prime Intellect) demonstrates the upgrade path: install skill packages INTO the kernel namespace so capabilities become importable libraries (their one-tool ipython + src/<import_name>/ convention).

SUCCESS: Model experience shifts from "SKILL.md text + N tool calls" to "import sre_chain; sre_chain.run()" for python-backed skills, while pi's discrete host-guarded tools remain unchanged. Kernel boot self-verifies imports; dev loop gains honest reload; giant outputs stop burning context.

SCOPE: Source of truth is core/packages/pi-extensions (this repo). Release contract: `npm run release:pi-extensions` -> npm -> `pi install`. The ~/.pi/agent/local/pi-extensions tree is an installed copy, not the source.

NON_GOALS: Replacing pi's discrete tools with a single-ipython collapse (prime-agent model); sandboxing the kernel; per-skill venvs (pythonBin override exists as escape hatch).
FURTHER IDEAS (not beaded yet): streaming partial stdout via onUpdate; error-time locals snapshot (failing frame digest); optional per-cell net/permission profile; dataframe repr guard for pandas if ever present.

## SUCCESS

- New table specialist_forensic_events (mirror the specialists schema; keep name distinct if xtmux prefers xtmux_forensic_events) written alongside the existing events row
- Every emit site (agents.state, command, bridge, journal, pane, session, message, retention, monitor) writes BOTH the legacy row AND the forensic row during the dual-write window
- host_id populated on every forensic event (source of truth: src/domains/identity/host-id.ts)
- Legacy xtmux log surface unchanged — regression test suite passes
- New table has indexes: (job_id, t), (event_family, event_name, t), (correlation.bead_id) for xt log filter performance
- Feature flag: XTMUX_FORENSIC_EMIT=on|off (default on after B5 cutover; during migration off means legacy-only)

## SCOPE

- xtmux repo: src/cli-log.ts, src/domains/identity/, all src/domains/*/... call sites of the current event emit function
- src/db/migrations/ — add new table migration
- src/observability/ — new module for forensic envelope construction (mirror pattern from specialists/src/specialist/forensic-events.ts)
- Tests in tests/unit/observability/ and tests/integration/

## NON_GOALS

- Do not migrate historical events; new table starts empty at deploy time.
- Do not change xtmux log CLI shape (it continues to read the legacy table until B5).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Dual-write must be atomic per emit call (single transaction). If forensic-write fails, log a diagnostic but DO NOT fail the legacy write.
- host_id must never be missing; if identity module returns null, emit a stale_warning to xtmux log.
- Latency budget: forensic emit adds <=1ms per event under load (measured by fixture bench).

- SCRUTINY: high (touches every emitter).

- **Installed deps:** better-sqlite3 (or xtmux's current sqlite binding)

title: xt log: unified runtime observability across sp forensic, xt debug, xtmux
description:
## PROBLEM

Runtime observability is split across three stores with three incompatible envelopes and three CLIs. Answering \"what happened to bead X / chain Y / session Z\" requires running sp log, xt debug, and xtmux log separately and merging by hand. Cross-store correlation exists via bead_id/session_id/host_id — xtmux even stamps host_id/runtime_origin into payloads specifically so specialists can join back — but nothing actually joins. Chain view is cut off at every layer boundary: sp log has trace_id/span_id/parent_span_id/chain_id/node_id/conversation_id; xt debug and xtmux have none of it. Operators reflexively expect \`xt log\` and it does not exist.

## SUCCESS

- \`xt log\` command answers cross-store queries in one call: \`--bead\`, \`--session\`, \`--pane\`, \`--chain\`, \`--source specialists|xtmux|xtrm|all\`, \`--family\`, \`--severity\`, \`--since\`, \`--limit\`, \`--json\`, \`-f\`.
- All three producers (specialists, xt debug, xtmux) emit xtrm.forensic.v1 envelopes natively — same event_family/event_name taxonomy, same correlation block, same severity + redaction fields.
- host_id join key surfaces xtmux pane/session events inside a specialist chain-view.
- Retention/severity/redaction is one story across all three stores.
- Backwards-compat: sp log, xt debug, xtmux log continue to work.

## SCOPE

Cross-repo epic:
- \`jaggerxtrm/xtrm-tools\` (core): new \`xt log\` command in cli/src/commands/, adapter layer in cli/src/observability/, xt debug emitter refactor.
- \`Jaggerxtrm/xtmux\`: emitter refactor in src/cli-log.ts + domains/identity/, new forensic table (or dual-write into existing observability.db), preserve host_id/runtime_origin as first-class correlation.
- \`xtrm-dev/specialists\`: type-only shim publish or vendor path for the forensic-v1 envelope so adapters have a single source of truth; no producer changes.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not migrate historical data. Backfill is a follow-up bead.
- Do not build a UI. \`xt log\` is CLI-only.
- Do not unify retention/rotation infrastructure in this epic; only document the residual gap.
- Do not touch \`sp log\`, \`xt debug\`, \`xtmux log\` CLIs beyond keeping them working — they stay as-is.
- Do not add a new observability store. Everything reads from the three existing DBs.
- Do not depend on OpenTelemetry libraries — emit forensic-v1 natively; OTEL export is a future epic.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Sequencing: Phase A (viewer/projection) ships end-to-end before Phase B (native emitter migration) starts. Phase B replaces projection with passthrough at the end.
- Envelope: xtrm.forensic.v1 as defined in specialists/src/specialist/forensic-events.ts is the single source of truth. Do not fork the schema.
- Emitter refactors are additive during migration (dual-emit both legacy and forensic) — flip cutover only after adapters land.
- Timestamps in unified view are t_unix_ms; adapters normalize from ISO/epoch as needed.
- xt log auto-discovers all .specialists/db/observability.db under a parent dir, mirroring sp log's aggregation model.
- Logging/telemetry contract for this epic itself: each phase's completion emits a xt debug event (\`kind=xtrm.log-epic.<phase>-complete\`) with children ids for audit trail.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] \`xt log --bead <id>\` returns rows from all three sources merged and sorted by t_unix_ms
- [ ] \`xt log --chain <id> --source specialists\` returns identical rows to \`sp log --limit N\` for the corresponding job(s)
- [ ] \`xt log --pane <%id>\` surfaces xtmux pane/session/agent_state events that xtmux log emits
- [ ] \`xt log -f\` follows across all three sources with <1s latency after emission
- [ ] Post Phase B: xtmux + xt debug producers emit xtrm.forensic.v1 events with valid event_family/event_name/correlation/severity/redaction
- [ ] host_id from xtmux events joins into specialists chain-view (proven via one integration test that runs a specialist chain from a specific pane and cross-checks correlation)
- [ ] \`sp log\`, \`xt debug\`, \`xtmux log\` behavior unchanged (regression: run existing test suites in each repo)
- [ ] Cross-repo integration smoke: spawn a specialist chain via xt pi, tail \`xt log -f --chain <id>\` in parallel, verify events from all three producers appear in order

## OUTPUT

Orchestrator hands back at epic close: the xt log CLI surface + adapter layer + native emitters in xtmux and xt debug; cross-repo integration smoke transcript; updated docs (xt help, CLAUDE.md skill routing, using-specialists reference to xt log); follow-up beads for Phase C (chain-view tree renderer, retention unification, backfill).

## REFERENCES

- specialists/src/specialist/forensic-events.ts — canonical envelope
- specialists/src/cli/log.ts — reader pattern for forensic events
- xtrm-tools/cli/src/commands/debug.ts — xt debug reader, .xtrm/debug.db schema
- xtmux/src/cli-log.ts — xtmux log reader/writer
- xtmux/src/domains/identity/{runtime-context,host-id}.ts — join-key stamping
- xtrm-tools/cli/src/commands/topology.ts — existing cross-source aggregation pattern

- packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-ui/{index.ts,format.ts}
- Compare cold-start vs post-reload code paths for the thinking row
- Identify the ambient state / hook / event that reload restores but cold-start doesn't
- Root-cause the bug; propose a fix; if trivial, open a PR

DELIVERABLES: root-cause writeup in bead notes + a fix PR if the fix is deterministic. If bug is intermittent/race-shaped, propose a repro procedure first.

NON_GOALS: no numbering changes, no release cut, no scope expansion beyond xtrm-ui rendering.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE (verified by repro): thinkingFollowsToggle (index.ts ~line 275) is process-lifetime module state, not session state. pi caches the extension factory per process (core/extensions/loader.js extensionCache + PATCHED_ASSISTANT_MESSAGE marker on the shared prototype prevents re-patching), so once ANY session in the process renders a thinking block with hideThinkingBlock=true (persisted Ctrl+T hide), the latch stays true forever. A later in-process session boundary (/new, resume, fork) with hideThinkingBlock=false then renders the FIRST thinking block via buildExpandedThinkingBlock -> full raw trace dumped (compact = hideThinkingBlock===true || !thinkingFollowsToggle = false). Kill+reattach/new pi launch re-evaluates the module -> latch false -> compact rows, which is why reload 'fixes' it.

REPRO (real patch code + real pi AssistantMessageComponent, /tmp/xtrm-think-repro/repro.ts): session A component with hideThinkingBlock=true -> collapsed; toggle show; session B component with hideThinkingBlock=false -> EXPANDED (bug). After fix: COLLAPSED.

FIX: reset thinkingFollowsToggle=false in the session_start handler (pi emits it for startup/new/resume/fork/reload = every session boundary). session_switch/session_fork handlers are dead (pi never emits those events) - left untouched.

RELATED OBSERVATION (out of scope): setHideThinkingBlock re-renders with the already-converted lastMessage (thinking blocks replaced by text rows), so the latch only fires on a component's first updateContent and toggles never re-render existing rows. Not part of this bead; noted for a future toggle fix.
close_reason: Root-caused + fixed: thinkingFollowsToggle process-lifetime latch leaked across in-process sessions; reset at session_start. PR #580. Repro + verify in /tmp/xtrm-think-repro/repro.ts. Tests pass (1 pre-existing unrelated xtprompt failure).

title: skill(deploy-monitor): deploy-gap guard is blind to committed-artifact CLI deploys — merged-but-not-deployed hit 3x in one session
description:
## PROBLEM

`deploy-monitor` exists for one failure: "a PR merges, but the running container is still the old image, so monitoring measures the pre-fix baseline. First responsibility is not 'watch metrics' — it is 'refuse to watch the wrong artifact.'"

Its deploy-gap guard covers exactly two deployment shapes: Docker (`docker inspect` StartedAt vs mergedAt) and GitOps/Kubernetes (`kubectl rollout status`). Both assume a running artifact you can inspect.

**A third shape exists in this estate and the guard is blind to it: CLI tooling deployed as a committed build artifact inside a local checkout.** There is no container, no rollout, and nothing for `verify-deploy-applied` to inspect — so the guard silently passes on a deployment that never happened.

This was hit three times in one session on 2026-08-05/06, and each time the merge looked complete by every other signal:

1. `xt worktree reap` (dev/core PR #543) — merged, bead closed, systemd timer installed and scheduled to fire with `--apply --yes`. `xt` resolves to `dev/core/cli/dist/index.cjs`; local main was **5 commits behind origin**, so the subcommand did not exist. The timer would have invoked a missing command nightly.
2. The `@agent_state` liveness fix (dev/xtmux PR #95) — merged, CI green pre- and post-merge, bead closed with full validation. `xtmux` resolves to `dev/xtmux/bin/tmux-session-picker`; local main was **16 commits behind** and the merge commit was not an ancestor of local HEAD. Three panes reported `running` for 28 hours after the fix that stops exactly that was already merged.
3. Same class again during the same teardown.

In cases 1 and 2 the artifact (`cli/dist/index.cjs`, `bin/tmux-session-picker`) is **committed to the repo**, so `git pull` IS the deployment — no build step. That makes the fix cheap and the omission easy to miss: nobody rebuilt anything, so nobody noticed nothing was deployed.

The mechanic is documented at `update-xt/SKILL.md:215` ("After merging changes to `cli/src/`, the dist must be rebuilt before `xt` picks up"), but `update-xt` is a how-to-update-your-install skill. It is not where an orchestrator looks after merging a PR, and it carries no guard.

## SUCCESS

An orchestrator following `deploy-monitor` after merging a tooling PR cannot conclude the deploy applied when it did not. The guard names a check for the committed-artifact shape as concretely as it does for Docker.

## SCOPE

Edit `.xtrm/skills/default/deploy-monitor/SKILL.md` only. Add a third case to the "Deploy-gap guard — before the first sample" section, alongside Docker and GitOps/Kubernetes. It must give a runnable check, in the idiom of the existing two. Something equivalent to:

- resolve what the command actually runs (`readlink -f "$(command -v <cmd>)"`) — it may be an npm link into a dev checkout;
- confirm the merge commit is an ancestor of that checkout's HEAD (`git merge-base --is-ancestor <mergeSha> HEAD`);
- confirm the built artifact is newer than the merge, or that the artifact is committed and the checkout is not behind origin (`git rev-list --count HEAD..origin/main`);
- PASS only if all hold; otherwise BLOCKED, exactly as the Docker case does.

Note in the text that when the artifact is committed, `git pull` is the deployment and no rebuild is required — and that when it is NOT committed, a rebuild is required and `update-xt` carries the worktree caveat about building from `.xtrm/worktrees/*` contaminating dist with absolute paths.

Keep it proportionate. `deploy-monitor` is 175 lines of tight doctrine; this is one case added to an existing section, not a new chapter.

## NON_GOALS

Do NOT edit `sre-triage`, `capacity-reclaim`, `update-xt`, or any other skill — the gap is specific to this guard and was checked against the others. Do NOT restructure `deploy-monitor` or touch its verdict vocabulary, sampling plan, or message policy. Do NOT add a command lookup table; the skill states explicitly that the CLIs are authoritative. Do NOT invent deployment shapes that were not observed — three real instances exist and that is the evidence base.

## CONSTRAINTS

Prose change to one file. No builds, no image pulls. Nothing large under `/tmp` (16 GB tmpfs, consumes RAM). Set file modes explicitly — this repo's `SKILL.md` files are 0664 and a pull under `umask 077` has already landed one at 0600.

One branch, one PR. You do NOT merge.

## VALIDATION

- The new case is runnable as written — execute it against `xt` and `dev/core` PR #543 and show it correctly reports the state.
- Frontmatter still parses; the skill's existing content-test (if any) still passes.
- Confirm no other skill was modified.

## OUTPUT

A bd note with the added text, the runnable-check demonstration, and the PR link.

REFERENCE: originating incident `mercury-market-data-9kjj4`; the shipped `capacity-reclaim` skill covers the reclaim half of the same session. Related: `xtrm-osoxx` (squash-merge false-hold, separate defect).

SCRUTINY: medium
notes:
FINAL — lane complete, handing back to orchestrator (pane %429).

DELIVERABLE: PR https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/pull/545
  branch docs/xtrm-7tjik-deploy-gap-committed-artifact, commit d812d6a5, base main. NOT merged.

FILES IN THE PR (2, exactly as scoped):
  .xtrm/skills/default/deploy-monitor/SKILL.md   +12 lines (175 -> 187), mode 0600 -> 0664
  scripts/check-skill-root-budget.mjs            deploy-monitor budget 180 -> 190

POST-PR ACTION (operator-directed, NOT in the PR):
  ~/.xtrm/skills/default/deploy-monitor/SKILL.md synced from the branch copy, mode 0664, byte-identical.
  Consequence: the global install now carries an UNMERGED change and is ahead of main. If review
  changes the text, the global copy must be re-synced. `xt update --apply` realigns it at merge.
  This is the mirror image of the defect the bead documents — running artifact NEWER than the merge.

DECISIONS RESOLVED:
  Budget 180 -> 190 — operator confirmed. Keep as committed. No trim to deploy-monitor doctrine.

VALIDATION (all re-confirmed at hand-back):
  check-skill-root-budget       OK, deploy-monitor 187/190
  check-forbidden-phrases       87 files, 0 violations
  check-payload-hygiene         ok, 402 packed files
  check:registry-pack-parity    318 registry / 318 packed
  Guard executed verbatim, cmd=xt, PR #543 (691f19ba, mergedAt 2026-08-05T16:28:08Z):
    is-ancestor 0 / behind 0 / ls-files 0  => PASS  (correct for the current checkout)
  Negative branch, incident state reconstructed (5 commits behind):
    is-ancestor 691f19ba 691f19ba~5 -> non-zero  => BLOCKED  (correct)

OPEN FOR THE ORCHESTRATOR:
  1. Merge authority — not assigned to this lane, PR left open.
  2. Bead closure authority — not assigned, bead left in_progress.
  3. bd claim is held by actor claude/a2bca, not by this pane; --claim was rejected at lane start.
  4. dev/xtmux PR #95 was not usable as a second live demonstration: gh returns an empty
     mergeCommit.oid. Contract required dev/core PR #543 only; that ran.

=== FOURTH DEPLOY SHAPE — observed 2026-08-07 by the KAN-127 lane (FYI, not a scope change) ===

Your case list covers committed-artifact-in-a-dev-checkout, where `git pull` IS the deploy. On this
host two of the three xtrm CLIs are a shape that is not covered and fails differently:

  xt    -> /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/lib/node_modules/xtrm-tools/cli/dist/index.cjs   (npm global)
  sp    -> /home/linuxbrew/.linuxbrew/lib/node_modules/@jaggerxtrm/specialists/...      (npm global)
  xtmux -> /home/jagger/dev/xtmux/bin/tmux-session-picker                               (your shape)

For an npm-global install, merging a PR never deploys AT ALL — not "deploys late". `git pull` in the
dev checkout changes nothing, so an ancestor check against the checkout HEAD passes while the running
binary is untouched. It needs a publish plus reinstall (or an npm link into the checkout).

The reason this is worth a line in the guard: the obvious cheap check does not catch it.

  installed xt : 0.11.4
  core repo    : 0.11.4      <- identical
  xt --help    : no `codex` command

Core main currently carries the whole merged K2/K3/K4 Codex surface (deterministic launch outcomes,
`xt codex`, distribution parity). None of it exists in the installed xt, and the version string is
equal on both sides. A version-equality check reports PASS here. The sound check for this shape is
capability or resolved-path provenance: readlink -f the command, and if it lands outside any git
checkout, treat version equality as NO evidence and require the publish/reinstall to be shown.

Suggested wording only; your bead, your call whether it belongs in #545 or a follow-up.

=== HEADS-UP ON YOUR POST-PR GLOBAL SYNC ===

Noted that you synced ~/.xtrm/skills/default/deploy-monitor/SKILL.md from the unmerged branch, leaving
the global install ahead of main, and that `xt update --apply` realigns it at merge. This host has
accumulated xt-managed asset drift that the KAN-127 lane is about to reconcile. Running
`xt update --apply` BEFORE #545 merges would revert your global copy to main's version. Flagging so it
is a decision rather than a surprise; the KAN-127 lane will not apply it over your change without the
operator saying so.

Adds the committed-artifact case to the deploy-gap guard with three runnable checks (merge-base ancestor, not-behind-origin, artifact-committed) plus the not-committed mtime fallback, and names both real traps by path. Budget raised 180->190 with an inline justification. title: [bug] xt worktree reap holds squash-merged worktrees forever — predicate has no patch-equivalence test
description:
POST-MERGE FIELD FINDING — squash-merged worktrees are held forever by the predicate.

Observed 2026-08-06 while tearing down this programme's lanes. The darth-feedor lane worktree carried commit caad1c4 "fix(cd): build mercury-base when absent...". `git rev-list --count origin/main..HEAD` reported 1, so the no-unpushed-commits condition FAILED and the worktree was held. But that commit IS in main, as 226c9ab, merged via squash in PR #191 — identical subject, different sha.

Neither of the predicate's two accepted forms recognises this:
  - "zero unpushed commits vs upstream" — false, the squash rewrote the sha
  - "branch is an ancestor of origin/HEAD" — false, for the same reason

So any repo using squash-merge produces worktrees the reaper can never reclaim. It is a FALSE HOLD, not a false reap, so it is safe — it fails closed, which is the right direction. But on a squash-merge repo the reaper's effective yield drops toward zero, and the accumulation this bead exists to fix continues silently while the tool reports it is working. That is the failure mode worth caring about: a guard that is safe and useless looks identical to a guard that is safe and effective.

Suggested third accepted form, in addition to the two existing ones:
  - every commit in `origin/main..HEAD` has a subject-and-patch-id match already in origin/main
`git cherry origin/main HEAD` answers this directly and is the idiomatic test — it marks commits with '-' when an equivalent change is already upstream regardless of sha. A branch whose every commit is marked '-' is fully merged, squash or not.

Recommend verifying against a repo that squash-merges before implementing, and adding a regression test with a squash-merged branch fixture. This programme's own repos differ: mercury/infra and dev/core merge with merge commits, darth-feedor squashes — so both paths are exercised in the field today.

Recorded from orchestrator teardown, not from a lane. Both held worktrees were inspected by hand and removed after confirming the work was upstream; no data was lost. The other held worktree (dev/core) was dirty only in .xtrm/skills/state.json and .specialists/user, both tooling scaffolding — the reaper's own exclusion list already covers those, so it was correct there and my ad-hoc teardown filter was the thing that was too narrow.

title: chore(gitnexus): point GitNexus at a shared parent-repo index instead of one per worktree
description:
Producer finding from xtrm-oentn (KAN-128) reap validation.

Each worktree grows its own ~129 MB .gitnexus index. During the 2026-08-04 capacity P0, 102 abandoned worktrees held 11.8 GB of .gitnexus alone. xtrm does not create them (worktree creation touches .beads only — cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:1767-1779); GitNexus does, on first analyze inside the worktree.

xt worktree reap now treats .gitnexus as a regenerable artifact and reclaims it, but that is symptom management: per capacity-reclaim rule 3, reclaim without a source fix is theatre, and regenerating a full index per worktree wastes CPU as well as disk.

ASK: evaluate pointing GitNexus at a shared parent-repo index (or a content-addressed cache keyed on the common git dir) so linked worktrees reuse one index.

REFERENCE: xtrm-oentn scope item 6; incident bead mercury-market-data-9kjj4.

title: chore(repo): add an asset-permission normalisation target to dev/core
description:
## PROBLEM

dev/core has no permission normalisation target. Verified 2026-08-05 during xtrm-gvek4: `.xtrm/skills/default/capacity-reclaim/SKILL.md` landed mode 0600 in the orchestrator's checkout while `sre-triage` and `deploy-monitor` were 0664, and the orchestrator normalised it by hand post-merge.

Root cause is rule 10 of the skill the bead produced: git tracks only the executable bit, so a file's read mode is set by the umask of the shell that checks it out. The authoring `chmod 644` was a no-op on what git delivers. In the authoring worktree all three sibling skills read 0600, which confirms the mode is a property of the checkout, not of the repo.

The fault only hits files NEW to a given checkout — files already present keep their existing mode — which is why the tree looks correct until something new arrives.

## SCOPE

Add a repo target (npm script and/or Makefile rule) that normalises xtrm-managed asset modes to the tree convention (0664 files, 0775 dirs) after checkout, pull, or `xt update --apply`.

Rule 11 from the same skill applies directly and is the main design constraint: the normaliser must cover the WHOLE asset tree, not the subset that failed first. `make alert-perms` in mercury/infra covered `prometheus/alerts/*.yml` only and silently did not cover `prometheus.yml`, `web.yml` or `alertmanager.yml` — a remediation narrower in scope than the fault it remediates. Do not repeat that shape here.

Rule 12 also applies: a target that must be run by hand is detection without disarming the producer. Consider wiring it to the operations that create the fault (post-merge/post-checkout hook, or the tail of `xt update --apply`) rather than leaving it as a command an operator must remember.

## NON_GOALS

Do not change any skill's content. Do not attempt to make git carry the mode — it cannot.

## VALIDATION

After a fresh clone or pull under `umask 077`, running the target leaves every xtrm-managed asset at the tree convention, and a check target fails when it does not.

Separate hygiene concern from this bead's permission target; flagged for the operator, not filed as work.

title: skill(devops): author capacity-reclaim — third materialization of the devops-sre role, sibling to sre-triage and deploy-monitor
description:
## PROBLEM

The devops-sre skill family has a gap. `sre-triage` answers "is anything broken right now". `deploy-monitor` answers "is the thing we just shipped actually running and healthy". Neither answers "is this host about to run out of a resource, what do I reclaim, and how do I know the reclaim held" — and on 2026-08-04 that gap produced a P0: /dev/vda4 reached 100% used with both database volumes on it, then the same host reached 0 free swap, twice, unannounced.

`sre-triage` calls itself "the first materialization of the devops-sre / monitor role". This is the third, after `deploy-monitor`.

The evidence base is unusually good: twelve rules, all derived from a single incident worked end to end, three of which were WRONG when first written and were corrected by being acted on. The corrections matter as much as the rules.

## SUCCESS

A `capacity-reclaim` skill exists in the canonical location, is loadable, and encodes only mechanisms that were verified in production. A reader who follows it would not have made the three mistakes this programme made: would not have reported RAM as disk, would not have trusted a probe that could not fail correctly, and would not have recreated a config-bind-mounted service without checking readability first.

## SCOPE

CANONICAL LOCATION — RESOLVED, do not re-investigate. The source of truth is the `dev/core` repo (git@github.com:xtrm-dev/core.git), tracked at `.xtrm/skills/default/`. title: Test: xt models CLI — shell integration + smoke across all four verbs
description:
Layer: shell
Strategy: integration + smoke (function-level Commander invocation and/or subprocess against the built cli/dist), covering CLI wiring/orchestration as distinct from the pure logic already covered by xtrm-2azdj.7 (T1) and xtrm-2azdj.8 (T2).
Covers: xtrm-2azdj.2 (refresh), xtrm-2azdj.3 (rank), xtrm-2azdj.4 (compare), xtrm-2azdj.5 (recommend), xtrm-2azdj.6 (aggregator/index.ts wiring)

What implementation it covers: this is the first point where all four verbs are reachable together end-to-end through the real top-level `xt`/`xtrm` program, so it is the epic's integration proof — not just "each command's action function returns the right string" but "the program actually routes `models <verb>` to the right handler with real commander option parsing and real (test-injected) I/O."

Test file structure: cli/src/tests/models-cli-integration.test.ts, following whichever existing convention (function-level program invocation vs subprocess) cli/src/tests/worktree-pr-status.test.ts or an equivalent shell-layer test in this repo already uses for CLI-level coverage.

Assertions required:
- [ ] `models --help` (after wiring) lists all four verbs (refresh, rank, compare, recommend) with non-empty descriptions.
- [ ] Top-level `--help` includes `models` in the command list (proves xtrm-2azdj.6's index.ts addition took effect).
- [ ] `models refresh` end-to-end with an injected fake fetchFn writes the expected cache file to an injected tmp cacheFile path and prints a success message including model count.
- [ ] `models refresh` with a fetchFn that rejects prints a clear stderr message and exits non-zero, and does not touch/corrupt any pre-existing cache file at the injected path.
- [ ] `models rank --capability agentic` against a pre-seeded tmp cache file prints the expected sorted rows (reuses a small fixture cache, not live data).
- [ ] `models rank` with no cache file present (fresh tmp dir, nothing seeded) → the documented "run xt models refresh" error and non-zero exit — proves the CLI layer surfaces xtrm-2azdj.1's missing-cache condition correctly, not just that the underlying function can detect it.
- [ ] `models compare <a> <b>` and `models recommend --role <name>` each get at least one smoke-level happy-path invocation through the real CLI entry point (full assertion depth for their logic lives in T1/T3 — this bead only proves they're wired and reachable).
- [ ] `--capability` with an invalid value is rejected by commander's own validation with a non-zero exit before any cache read is attempted.

Smoke/E2E commands for test-runner:
- Setup: `npm run build` (compiles cli/dist), create a tmp HOME/cache dir so no test writes into the real `~/.xtrm/cache/model-benchmarks.json`.
- `node cli/dist/index.cjs models --help` — expect stdout lists refresh/rank/compare/recommend.
- `node cli/dist/index.cjs --help` — expect stdout includes a `models` line.
- Cleanup: remove the tmp HOME/cache dir; do not touch the operator's real `~/.xtrm/cache/`.

Fixture policy:
- [ ] Every test uses an injected/tmp cache path and injected fetch/now — never the operator's real `~/.xtrm/cache/model-benchmarks.json`, never a real network call.
- [ ] No shared state between tests — fresh tmp dir per test.

Anti-pattern check:
- [ ] Not over-mocked: only the true system boundary (fetch, cache file path) is faked; commander parsing and command dispatch run for real.

Critical paths covered:
- Missing-cache UX end-to-end (not just the pure-function level) — risk: xtrm-2azdj's SUCCESS criterion explicitly requires read commands to "fail with an actionable message" and only integration-level testing proves the CLI layer doesn't swallow or reformat that message incorrectly.
- Aggregator wiring itself — risk: a typo in cli/src/index.ts's import or addCommand line (xtrm-2azdj.6) would otherwise go undetected by any of the per-verb unit tests, since those exercise the command factories directly rather than the assembled program.

Known deferred paths:
- Full live end-to-end against the real OpenRouter API — deferred, see xtrm-2azdj.8 (T2)'s "Known deferred paths" for the same live-key limitation; no separate follow-up needed here since T2 already tracks it.

Debuggability evidence required: refresh's failure-path stderr message content is asserted verbatim (or via substring match) so a future debugging session can grep for it; no other logging/telemetry contract applies to this CLI surface.

Done when: all assertions pass via `npm test --workspace cli`, and the two named smoke commands both produce their expected output after a clean `npm run build`.

title: Test: recommend --role specialist-file resolution — isolated fixture directory
description:
Layer: boundary (file I/O)
Strategy: isolated tmp fixture directory (mkdtempSync + fake *.specialist.json files), not the live .specialists/user/ tree.
Covers: xtrm-2azdj.5 (recommend --role)

What implementation it covers: the filesystem-resolution half of xt models recommend — locating a role's *.specialist.json file, listing available role names on a miss, and parsing `.specialist.execution.model` out of the file — as distinct from xtrm-2azdj.7 (T1), which covers the pure recommendForRole matching/ranking logic given an already-extracted model string.

Precondition on xtrm-2azdj.5's implementation: the specialists directory path must be an injectable parameter (mirroring cacheFile/now/fetchFn injection elsewhere in this epic), not a hard-coded `.specialists/user/` literal — otherwise this test cannot run against a fixture directory without mutating the real repo tree. Flag this explicitly back on xtrm-2azdj.5 if not already covered by its CONSTRAINTS.

Test file structure: cli/src/tests/models-recommend-resolve.test.ts.

Assertions required:
- [ ] Known role name (present in the injected fixture dir) → correct execution.model string extracted, matching the nested `.specialist.execution.model` shape confirmed in .specialists/user/researcher.specialist.json:18-20.
- [ ] Unknown role name → error message lists the ACTUAL role names found in the injected fixture directory (e.g. 2 fake roles "alpha", "beta"), not a hard-coded list and not the live repo's real specialist names — proves the error path reads the directory at call time rather than using a stale/hard-coded list.
- [ ] Malformed *.specialist.json (missing execution.model field, or invalid JSON) → clear error naming the offending file, not a raw JSON.parse stack trace surfaced to the operator.
- [ ] Empty specialists directory (zero *.specialist.json files) → clear "no specialist roles found" message, not a confusing empty-array error.

Fixture policy:
- [ ] Fixture directory created fresh per test via mkdtempSync with hand-written fake *.specialist.json files — never reads or depends on this repo's real .specialists/user/ contents, so the test stays stable if real specialist roles are added/removed/renamed later.

Anti-pattern check:
- [ ] Not tautological: the "lists actual role names" assertion checks against the specific fake names written into the fixture in that test, not a value derived from the same directory-listing call being tested.

Critical paths covered:
- Directory-read failure UX — risk: a raw stack trace or an empty silent result on a typo'd --role value is a worse operator experience than the epic's stated goal of listing real available names.
- Malformed specialist file handling — risk: a corrupt or hand-edited specialist file elsewhere in the fleet must not crash the whole recommend command for every other role.

Known deferred paths: none — this is a small, fully-enumerable path set.

Debuggability evidence required: none beyond the assertions above; no logging contract specific to this path.

Done when: all assertions pass in `npm test --workspace cli`, and xtrm-2azdj.5's implementation confirms the specialists-directory path is injectable (add a note to xtrm-2azdj.5 if its current CONSTRAINTS don't already say so).

title: Test: benchmark cache module — DI unit tests + recorded-fixture contract check
description:
Layer: boundary
Strategy: DI-injected unit tests (repo convention, mirrors cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts) as primary, plus one recorded-fixture contract test using a real captured OpenRouter response sample. Live tests against the real API are not run in CI (no committed OPENROUTER_API_KEY) — this is the documented live-first fallback.
Covers: xtrm-2azdj.1

What implementation it covers: fetchBenchmarks, readCache/writeCache, refreshBenchmarks orchestration in cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts.

Test file structure: cli/src/tests/model-benchmarks.test.ts, mirroring cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts's pattern (inject cacheFile via mkdtempSync, now via fixed clock, fetchFn as a plain fake function — no HTTP-mocking library).

Assertions required:
- [ ] Cold cache (file absent) → refreshBenchmarks calls the injected fetchFn and writes the cache file with the fetched data + fetchedAt.
- [ ] Fresh cache (within TTL) → does NOT call fetchFn; returns cached data as-is.
- [ ] Expired cache → calls fetchFn again; on success, overwrites the cache entry and timestamp.
- [ ] fetchFn throws/rejects → existing cache file (if any) is left untouched; refreshBenchmarks surfaces a clear typed error, does not write partial/garbage data.
- [ ] Missing OPENROUTER_API_KEY (injected as absent) → clear typed error before any network attempt; fetchFn is never invoked in this path.
- [ ] Cache write failure (e.g. unwritable directory) → does not throw out of refreshBenchmarks (best-effort-swallow semantics matching npm-latest.ts:59-66); caller still receives the freshly fetched data even though persistence failed.
- [ ] Recorded-fixture contract check: a committed fixture file (e.g. cli/src/tests/fixtures/openrouter-benchmarks-sample.json) containing a real captured response shape (obtained manually during xtrm-2azdj.1 implementation with a personal API key, NOT a live call in the test itself) is parsed by the module's type/parsing logic and asserted to produce the expected typed cache entries — this catches drift between the assumed field names (model_permaslug, agentic_index, coding_index, intelligence_index, pricing.prompt, pricing.completion) and the module's actual parsing code, without requiring network access in CI.

Fixture policy:
- [ ] No shared mutable state — each test gets its own mkdtempSync directory.
- [ ] Deterministic `now` injection — no bare Date.now() in the test.

Anti-pattern check:
- [ ] Not over-mocked: fetchFn is a plain injected function per the module's own DI design (matches the repo's existing convention for exactly this kind of external call), not a patch of an internal collaborator.

Critical paths covered:
- Cache-miss vs cache-hit branching — risk: an off-by-one in TTL comparison silently causes either constant unnecessary network calls or permanently stale data.
- API-key-absent short-circuit — risk: an unauthenticated request would either fail with a confusing error deep in the fetch call or, worse, silently succeed against a public/free endpoint with wrong data.
- Recorded-fixture schema check — risk: this epic's rank/compare/recommend field-name assumptions were explicitly flagged as unverified in xtrm-2azdj's CONSTRAINTS; if the real API shape differs, this is the one test that would catch it before it reaches production.

Known deferred paths:
- True live-network contract test (hitting the real OpenRouter endpoint) — deferred because no committed API key exists in this repo. Follow-up: if the team later adds a CI-safe test API key/secret, create a `@live`-tagged test that supersedes the recorded fixture as primary evidence (to be created — no bd issue yet, note this in xtrm-2azdj's epic notes at close).

Debuggability evidence required: refreshBenchmarks failure paths should be catchable with the injected fetchFn's rejection reason surfacing unchanged in the thrown/returned error (test asserts the error message/type, not just "it throws").

Done when: all assertions pass in `npm test --workspace cli`, and the recorded-fixture file is committed alongside the test.

title: Test: rank/compare/recommend core logic — unit tests
description:
Layer: core
Strategy: unit (example-based) + edge cases
Covers: xtrm-2azdj.3 (rank), xtrm-2azdj.4 (compare), xtrm-2azdj.5 (recommend)

What implementation it covers: the pure, non-CLI functions each verb factors out per its bead's SCOPE — rankModels(cache, capability), compareModels(cache, slugs), recommendForRole(cache, specialistModel). These take plain data in, return plain data/strings out, no file I/O, no network, no commander.

Test file structure: cli/src/tests/models-rank.test.ts, models-compare.test.ts, models-recommend.test.ts (or a single models-core.test.ts if the three functions are small enough to share a file — match whatever granularity cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts uses for a comparable module).

Assertions required:
- [ ] rankModels: sorts descending by the requested capability index; ties broken deterministically (stable order, no crash on equal values); rejects/errors on an unrecognized capability string before touching data.
- [ ] rankModels: never emits a blended/composite score field — assert the output object/row only carries the three raw indices + pricing, never a computed average.
- [ ] compareModels: all-slugs-found path returns rows in the same order as the input slugs (not cache iteration order).
- [ ] compareModels: partially-unmatched-slugs path returns a distinguishable "not found" marker for the missing slug's row/warning, while still returning full rows for the found ones (does not throw, does not silently drop the whole request).
- [ ] recommendForRole: exact/normalized match found → correct rank position computed against the full cache (e.g. "4th of 23"), and the alternative-suggestion logic only fires when a genuinely higher-ranked model exists (no suggestion when the current model is already top-ranked).
- [ ] recommendForRole: no match found → returns the graceful fallback data (top N agentic_index entries) rather than throwing or returning empty/undefined.
- [ ] Edge cases: empty cache (zero models) for all three functions — must return an empty-but-valid result / clear "no data" signal, not throw.
- [ ] Edge cases: single-model cache for rank/recommend (rank position is trivially 1st of 1; no alternative to suggest).

Fixture policy:
- [ ] No shared mutable state between tests — construct a fresh fake cache object per test.
- [ ] Deterministic fixtures — hand-written small cache arrays (3-5 fake models with known index values), no reliance on real cached data or the live repo's specialist files.

Anti-pattern check:
- [ ] Not tautological: rank/compare/recommend expected outputs are computed independently in the test (e.g. by pre-sorting the fixture by hand), not derived from calling the function under test itself.
- [ ] Not over-mocked: nothing here should mock internal collaborators — these are pure functions, call them directly.

Critical paths covered:
- Never-blend-scores invariant — risk: violating the epic's core design promise (separate capability axes) silently regresses to a misleading single score.
- recommend's no-match fallback — risk: a naming-scheme mismatch between specialist execution.model strings and OpenRouter permaslugs is the expected common case (flagged in xtrm-2azdj.5's CONSTRAINTS), so this path WILL be hit in real usage and must never crash.

Known deferred paths:
- Property-based/fuzz testing of arbitrary cache shapes — deferred, example-based fixtures are sufficient for v1 given the small, well-typed cache schema from xtrm-2azdj.1.

Debuggability evidence required: none beyond standard test failure output — these are pure functions with no logging contract of their own.

Done when: all assertions above pass in `npm test --workspace cli`, and removing any one of rank's sort-by-capability logic, compare's unmatched-slug handling, or recommend's fallback branch causes at least one test to fail (verify by temporarily reverting the relevant logic during test authoring).

title: xt models recommend --role — benchmark-check a specialist's declared model
description:
## PROBLEM

Specialist files under .specialists/user/*.specialist.json each hard-code an execution.model with no data-driven check that the choice is still a good one. There is no command that closes the loop between "what model does this specialist use" and "how does that model actually rank."

## SUCCESS

`xt models recommend --role <name>` resolves .specialists/user/<name>.specialist.json (erroring clearly if the file doesn't exist — list available role names in the error), reads its execution.model, and attempts to match that string against the cached model_permaslug values. If matched: reports the model's agentic_index rank position (e.g. "ranked 4th of 23 on agentic_index") and names the top-ranked alternative if a meaningfully higher-ranked one exists. If NOT matched (naming schemes differ, e.g. "nano-gpt/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash:thinking" vs OpenRouter's permaslug format): reports clearly that no direct match was found, and instead prints the current top-ranked models on agentic_index as a general reference — never crashes or silently returns nothing. Missing cache file → same clear error as rank/compare.

## SCOPE

New file cli/src/commands/models/recommend.ts exporting createModelsRecommendCommand(): Command. Reads .specialists/user/*.specialist.json (parse `.specialist.execution.model`, per the shape confirmed in .specialists/user/researcher.specialist.json:18-20). Depends on cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (Task A, xtrm-2azdj.1). Matching/ranking logic as a plain exported function (e.g. recommendForRole(cache, specialistModel)) separate from file I/O and from the commander action.

## NON_GOALS

- No fuzzy/heuristic string-similarity matching algorithm for v1 — exact or simple normalized (case/whitespace) match only; log the no-match case honestly rather than building a matching engine now. Add fuzzy matching later only if the exact-match miss rate proves it's needed.
- No writing back to the specialist file (no auto-update of execution.model) — recommend only reports, never mutates.
- No capability-weight-per-role heuristic beyond agentic_index for v1, since specialist files don't currently declare a capability weighting themselves (confirmed: researcher/parallel-review/transcriber specialist.json files have no such field) — this is an explicit, intentional simplification, not an oversight.

## CONSTRAINTS

- --role value must resolve against real files in .specialists/user/ (confirmed present in this repo: researcher, parallel-review, transcriber) — never a hard-coded manager/implementer/junior list.
- Never write to any .specialist.json file from this command.
- Follow the spec/*.ts thin-command-file convention.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit test: unknown --role name → error lists actual available role names read from .specialists/user/ at test time (inject a fixture directory, don't depend on this repo's live specialist set in the test).
- [ ] Unit test: execution.model string that matches a cache entry → correct rank position and alternative-suggestion logic.
- [ ] Unit test: execution.model string with no match → graceful fallback output (top agentic_index models), not a crash or empty output.
- [ ] Unit test: missing cache file → documented error path.
- [ ] `npm run build` clean.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (Task A) for cache; existing pattern for reading a *.specialist.json file (check cli/src/commands/pi.ts's --role handling, e.g. around pi.ts:103-133, for how it currently locates/reads specialist files, and reuse that path-resolution helper if one already exists rather than re-deriving the .specialists/user/ path).
- **Installed deps:** commander; JSON.parse via fs (no schema-validation library needed for a single known field read).
- **Stdlib:** node:fs, node:path.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** yes.

## OUTPUT

New recommend.ts + test file, sample output for both the matched and unmatched cases.
