title: xt models compare — side-by-side index/pricing table for named slugs
description:
## PROBLEM

Once a shortlist of candidate models is known, the operator needs to see them side by side on every axis at once, rather than scanning a full ranked list for each one.

## SUCCESS

`xt models compare <slug-a> <slug-b> ...>` (2+ positional args) reads the local cache and prints a table with one row per named model showing agentic/coding/reasoning indices and pricing. A slug not found in the cache is reported by name in a clear warning line rather than silently omitted or crashing the whole command. Missing cache file → same clear error as rank ("run xt models refresh").

## SCOPE

New file cli/src/commands/models/compare.ts exporting createModelsCompareCommand(): Command. Depends on cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (Task A, xtrm-2azdj.1). Pure logic as an exported function (e.g. compareModels(cache, slugs)) separate from the commander action, mirroring rank's split.

## NON_GOALS

- No fuzzy/partial slug matching for v1 — exact model_permaslug match only; unmatched slugs are reported, not guessed at.
- No JSON output mode for v1 (same reasoning as rank).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Require at least 2 positional slug arguments (commander variadic argument with a minimum-count check); a single slug is arguably more naturally `rank`'s job, so compare should nudge the user rather than silently accept 1.
- Never blend indices into one score, same rule as rank.
- Follow the spec/*.ts thin-command-file convention (logic in a plain function, not the .action() closure).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit test for compareModels with all slugs found — correct rows in input order.
- [ ] Unit test: one unmatched slug among several found ones → warning line names it, other rows still render.
- [ ] Unit test: missing cache file → documented error path.
- [ ] `npm run build` clean.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts cache read/types (Task A); reuse rank.ts's column-print helper if one is factored out generically enough (check Task C's implementation before duplicating formatting code).
- **Installed deps:** commander.
- **Stdlib:** none new.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** yes.

## OUTPUT

New compare.ts + test file, sample side-by-side output including one unmatched-slug warning case.

title: xt models rank — sort cached models by capability index
description:
## PROBLEM

An operator choosing a model for a task needs a ranked view by ONE capability at a time (agentic, coding, or reasoning) — never a blended single score, since a model strong at one axis can be weak at another and collapsing them hides that.

## SUCCESS

`xt models rank --capability <agentic|coding|reasoning>` reads the local cache (never fetches), sorts descending by the matching index field, and prints model_permaslug plus all three indices plus pricing per row, so the operator can see the other axes even while sorting by one. Output header shows cache age (e.g. "cache: 2h old, fetched 2026-07-29T10:00Z"). Missing cache file → clear stderr message "no benchmark cache found — run `xt models refresh`" and non-zero exit, never an empty/silent table.

## SCOPE

New file cli/src/commands/models/rank.ts exporting createModelsRankCommand(): Command. Depends on the cache read function and types from cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (Task A, xtrm-2azdj.1). Pure formatting/sorting logic should be a plain exported function (e.g. rankModels(cache, capability)) separate from the commander action, so it's unit-testable without CLI invocation.

## NON_GOALS

- No pagination/--limit flag for v1 — print the full ranked list; add a limit flag later if the list becomes unwieldy.
- No JSON output mode for v1 — human-readable table only, add --json later if a consumer needs it.

## CONSTRAINTS

- --capability accepts exactly agentic|coding|reasoning; reject any other value with a clear usage error (commander's built-in choices validation is sufficient — do not hand-roll validation).
- Must never compute or print a single blended/composite score — only the three raw indices, one column each.
- Follow the spec/*.ts thin-command-file convention: business logic (rankModels) is a plain function, not embedded in the .action() closure.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit test for rankModels(cache, 'agentic') sorts correctly, ties broken deterministically (e.g. stable sort, no crash on equal indices).
- [ ] Unit test: unknown capability value rejected before touching the cache.
- [ ] Unit test: missing cache file → the documented error message and non-zero exit path (inject a nonexistent cacheFile path).
- [ ] Cache-age header renders correctly given an injected `now` and a fixed fetchedAt.
- [ ] `npm run build` clean.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts read/cache-shape from Task A.
- **Installed deps:** commander (choices validation for --capability).
- **Stdlib:** Array.prototype.sort.
- **New dep candidate:** none — a hand-rolled column-aligned print (same style as npm-latest.ts's formatUpdateRows) covers table output; no table-formatting library needed.
- **Roll it:** yes.

## OUTPUT

New rank.ts + test file, sample output demonstrating the three-index-plus-pricing table and the staleness header.

title: xt models refresh — fetch OpenRouter benchmarks into local cache
description:
## PROBLEM

Operators and other commands need a single explicit, network-touching command that populates the local benchmark cache. Every other verb (rank/compare/recommend) must stay offline-safe, so the fetch has to live behind one dedicated command.

## SUCCESS

`xt models refresh` calls the Task A module's refresh function, writes ~/.xtrm/cache/model-benchmarks.json, and prints a confirmation with model count and fetchedAt timestamp. On failure (missing API key, HTTP error, network error) it prints a clear, actionable stderr message and exits non-zero without corrupting any existing cache.

## SCOPE

New file cli/src/commands/models/refresh.ts exporting createModelsRefreshCommand(): Command. Depends on cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts from Task A (xtrm-2azdj.1).

## NON_GOALS

- No --force/--no-cache flag design beyond what Task A's orchestration function already supports passing through — keep the CLI surface minimal (a single `xt models refresh` with no flags is enough for v1 unless Task A's DI options make a flag trivial to expose, in which case a `--force` bypass-cache flag is fine to add here).
- No progress bar / spinner UI — a single before/after print is enough.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Never print the OPENROUTER_API_KEY value in any output path, including error messages.
- Use the Task A module's exported functions directly — do not re-implement fetch or cache I/O in this file.
- Follow commander command conventions used by sibling verb files under cli/src/commands/spec/*.ts (thin command file, logic delegated to a utils/core function).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] CLI integration test invokes the command's action with an injected fetch/cacheFile (same DI as Task A's tests) and asserts the cache file is written and a success message is printed.
- [ ] Test: fetch failure path prints stderr message and process exits non-zero (or command throws in test harness convention used elsewhere in this repo — match existing pattern).
- [ ] `npm run build` clean.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (Task A) — this command is a thin wrapper around it.
- **Installed deps:** commander (already a dependency, used by every other command file).
- **Stdlib:** none new.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** N/A — pure CLI wiring over Task A's module.

## OUTPUT

New refresh.ts file, its test file, confirmation the command runs end-to-end against an injected fake fetch and produces the expected cache file + console output.

title: Benchmark cache module — OpenRouter fetch + TTL cache + types
description:
## PROBLEM

Every read command (rank/compare/recommend) and the refresh command need a shared, testable data layer: types for the OpenRouter benchmark shape, a fetch function, and a TTL-cached read/write pair. Without a single module, each command would re-implement cache I/O and drift from the injectable-DI pattern this repo already uses for exactly this kind of thing.

## SUCCESS

A module exports: (1) a TypeScript type for one cached benchmark record and the on-disk cache shape (with fetchedAt), (2) defaultCacheFile() returning ~/.xtrm/cache/model-benchmarks.json, (3) a fetchBenchmarks(apiKey) function calling GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/benchmarks with the Bearer token, (4) readCache/writeCache mirroring npm-latest.ts's best-effort-swallow semantics, (5) a refreshBenchmarks(opts) orchestration function taking injectable {cacheFile, now, fetchFn, apiKey} exactly like npm-latest.ts's CheckOptions, so tests never touch the network.

## SCOPE

New file cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (same directory as cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts, mirror its shape). Do not touch cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts itself except to read it as a reference.

## NON_GOALS

- No CLI wiring (commander commands) — that's the refresh/rank/compare/recommend tasks.
- No retry/backoff logic beyond a single fetch attempt with a clear error on non-2xx — YAGNI until proven necessary.
- No caching of partial/error responses.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Mirror cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts:27-45 (CheckOptions shape, defaultCacheFile, readCache/writeCache try/catch-swallow pattern) and :112-164 (orchestration function signature/DI shape) as closely as the different data makes sense.
- Use Node's built-in global `fetch` — no new dependency.
- Read OPENROUTER_API_KEY from process.env; if absent, fetchBenchmarks must throw/return a clear typed error rather than making an unauthenticated request. Never log the key value anywhere (console, thrown error message, cache file).
- The actual JSON field names returned by GET /api/v1/benchmarks are UNVERIFIED — this task must make one real call (locally, using a personal OPENROUTER_API_KEY, NOT committed anywhere) during implementation to confirm the response shape before finalizing the TypeScript type, then note the confirmed shape in the PR description / bead notes for downstream tasks (rank/compare/recommend) to rely on. If a real key isn't available at implementation time, model the type on the user's stated assumption (model_permaslug, agentic_index, coding_index, intelligence_index, pricing.prompt, pricing.completion) and flag the assumption explicitly rather than silently guessing further fields.
- Cache write failures must never throw out of refreshBenchmarks (same best-effort semantics as npm-latest.ts:59-66).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Unit tests inject cacheFile (tmp path via mkdtempSync), now (fixed clock), and fetchFn (fake) — no real HTTP call in tests, no HTTP-mocking library, mirroring cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts's DI style exactly.
- [ ] Test: cold cache (file absent) → refreshBenchmarks calls fetchFn and writes cache.
- [ ] Test: fresh cache (within TTL) → does NOT call fetchFn (unless a --no-cache-equivalent force flag is passed at the orchestration layer, matching npm-latest.ts's noCache option shape).
- [ ] Test: fetchFn throwing/rejecting → cache is left untouched, function surfaces a clear error, does not write garbage.
- [ ] Test: missing OPENROUTER_API_KEY → clear typed error, no network call attempted.
- [ ] `npm run build` and targeted `npm test --workspace cli -- model-benchmarks` green.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts (path.join/os.homedir cache path convention, CheckOptions DI shape, readCache/writeCache swallow pattern) — direct structural template, cite in the module's top comment if useful.
- **Installed deps:** none needed.
- **Stdlib:** Node global `fetch` (Node 18+, already the runtime baseline per npm-latest.ts having no HTTP client dep); node:fs/node:path/node:os per npm-latest.ts's existing imports.
- **New dep candidate:** none — tiers 1-3 covered it.
- **Roll it:** yes — this is a small, single-purpose module with no existing package that fits (OpenRouter has no official JS SDK for this endpoint).

## OUTPUT

Changed files (model-benchmarks.ts + its test file), confirmed real API response field names (or explicit note that they remain assumed pending a live key), test output showing all DI-based unit tests passing.

title: xt models: OpenRouter-backed benchmark rank/compare/recommend CLI
description:
## PROBLEM

Choosing which hosted/API model to assign to a role (specialist, pi session, or ad-hoc task) in the xtrm ecosystem is currently a guess — there is no CLI surface that shows independent quality/cost/speed data for the commercial models actually in play (GPT, Claude, Gemini, Grok, GLM, Kimi, Qwen served via API). A prior local-benchmark-runner idea ("llmfit") was rejected as not applicable to hosted/paid models — the right shape is a CLI that queries and caches an external leaderboard, not a thing that runs evals locally.

## SUCCESS

`xt models refresh` populates a local TTL cache from OpenRouter's public benchmarks endpoint. `xt models rank --capability <agentic|coding|reasoning>` and `xt models compare <slug> <slug> ...` read that cache and print separate per-capability indices plus pricing — never a single blended score. `xt models recommend --role <specialistName>` resolves a real specialist file under .specialists/user/, reads its declared execution.model, and reports how that model ranks against the cached leaderboard on the agentic index, naming a better-ranked alternative when one exists. All read commands work fully offline against the cache and fail with an actionable message ("run xt models refresh") when the cache is missing — only `refresh` touches the network.

## SCOPE

- New module: cli/src/utils/model-benchmarks.ts (or cli/src/core/, mirror npm-latest.ts's location convention) — OpenRouter fetch + TTL cache + types.
- New command dir: cli/src/commands/models/{refresh,rank,compare,recommend}.ts + cli/src/commands/models.ts aggregator.
- Wiring: cli/src/index.ts (one import + one program.addCommand line).
- Tests: cli/src/tests/ companion units mirroring npm-latest.test.ts's DI style.

## NON_GOALS

- No Artificial Analysis integration, no LiteLLM catalog integration, no local/self-hosted benchmark runner (that's the rejected "llmfit" direction).
- No change to `xt pi`'s existing stripping of --list-models (cli/src/commands/pi.ts:123).
- No new "manager/implementer/junior" role vocabulary — recommend uses real specialist names only. Confirmed via exploration: this repo's only present specialist files are researcher, parallel-review, transcriber under .specialists/user/.
- No new HTTP client dependency — use Node's built-in global fetch.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Follow cli/src/commands/spec/*.ts + spec.ts aggregator pattern (one file per verb, thin aggregator) — not worktree.ts's single-file style — since there are 4 verbs.
- Cache convention: path.join(os.homedir(), '.xtrm', 'cache', 'model-benchmarks.json'), injectable cacheFile/now/fetch fn per cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts:27-45, so tests never hit the network or a mocking library.
- OPENROUTER_API_KEY read from env; no existing precedent in this repo for *_API_KEY handling, so this is the first instance — document the read clearly, never log the key value.
- The exact JSON field names of GET https://openrouter.ai/api/v1/benchmarks (model_permaslug, agentic_index, coding_index, intelligence_index, pricing.prompt, pricing.completion) are ASSUMED from the user's design note, not yet verified against a live response or OpenRouter's published reference — the refresh task must confirm real field names before the cache type is finalized, and rank/compare/recommend tasks must treat the cache type as the source of truth rather than re-assuming field names independently.
- Specialist execution.model strings (e.g. "nano-gpt/deepseek/deepseek-v4-flash:thinking") use a different naming scheme than OpenRouter's model_permaslug — recommend must handle a no-match case gracefully (clear message, non-zero-noise output) rather than crashing or silently returning nothing.
- Logging/telemetry: no crash-worthy failures should print raw stack traces to the operator; cache read/write failures follow npm-latest.ts's best-effort-swallow pattern (never fail the calling command over a cache write failure). Network/auth failures from refresh must print a clear, actionable stderr message (missing API key, HTTP status, rate limit) — never a silent empty cache.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run build` clean, `npm test --workspace cli` green including new suites
- [ ] Each read command (rank/compare/recommend) errors clearly and exits non-zero when the cache file is absent, telling the operator to run `xt models refresh`
- [ ] refresh's fetch/cache logic is unit-tested via injected fetch/cacheFile/now (no real network call in tests), mirroring cli/src/tests/npm-latest.test.ts
- [ ] Smoke: `node cli/dist/index.cjs models --help` (after build) shows all four verbs wired under the top-level program
- [ ] No API key or token value ever appears in command output or logs

## OUTPUT

Epic close summary: list of merged PRs per child task, confirmation that `xt models refresh/rank/compare/recommend` all work against a real (or realistically faked) cache, and any residual risk around the assumed OpenRouter field names or the specialist-model-name matching heuristic in recommend.

title: the smoke container is a release gate that nothing tells anyone to run
description:
## PROBLEM

scripts/smoke-container/README.md calls itself a 'Pre/post-release gate' and says: 'Run it twice
around a coordinated release, once before publishing and once after. Both must PASS.'

Nothing else in the ecosystem says so. Measured 2026-07-27:

  ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-release.yaml   0 references
  docs/release.md                              0 references
  ~/.xtrm/skills/default/releasing/SKILL.md    0 references
  .github/                                     0 references
  package.json                                 0 references
  README.md, XTRM-GUIDE.md, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md  0 references
  every global skill under ~/.xtrm/skills/default  0 references

The only mentions outside its own directory are 2 lines in
docs/design/audit-reconcile-v0724-epic-plan.md — a historical epic plan, not an operator runbook.

So the gate depends entirely on a human remembering a sentence in a README they would only read
if they were already in that directory.

## THIS IS NOT THE SAME AS THE OTHER SMOKE — do not confuse them

docs/release.md documents fresh-machine-smoke.yml, which IS a hard automated gate: publish.yml is
a 3-job DAG resolve_ref -> fresh_machine_smoke -> publish, and 'if smoke fails, publish never
starts'. That one is wired and enforced.

They test different things:
  fresh-machine-smoke.yml   live npm install + xt init -y + sp init — can a fresh user bootstrap
  smoke-container/verify.sh the GLOBAL install surface — claude/pi skill pointers, per-event hook
                            coverage, --new-instance, pi packages, and drift-repair

The bootstrap gate would not have caught bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.25 or xtrm-wiy5n.4.27. The container
gate is the one built to catch those, and it is the one nobody is told to run.

## WHY IT MATTERS NOW

Bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.32 just made this container a genuinely good gate: 7 fault injections each
prove one check, plus a drift-break-and-repair stage. A good gate that no runbook names is a gate
that will be skipped on the release after the person who built it stops paying attention.

## SUCCESS

- The release path names the container run, at the point where it must happen.
- Choose ONE owner for that instruction and put it there: docs/release.md, the releasing skill,
  or a node in the archon release workflow. Do not put it in three places that can drift apart.
- The instruction states the known pre-release exception, so an operator does not 'fix' a gate
  that is correctly reporting an unreleased fix.

## NON_GOALS

Making the container run automatically in CI. It needs docker and several minutes; wiring it into
every push is not the ask. The ask is that the RELEASE PATH names it.

title: using-xtrm-reminder.mjs left wired in live settings after it was deleted from the payload
description:
## PROBLEM

hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs was deleted from the shipped payload in commit 362db69a (#507). Two live files still invoke it:

  ~/.claude/settings.json:9 ... :83   command: node "/home/dawid/.xtrm/hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs"
  ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json:9         command: node ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs

The file still exists at ~/.xtrm/hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs only because the global hooks bootstrap has not re-run since #507.

## WHAT HAPPENS NEXT

ensureGlobalHooksBootstrapped wipes ~/.xtrm/hooks and re-copies the payload (see xtrm-wiy5n.4.37). The payload no longer carries the file. After that run the hook is wired and its target is gone, so it fails on every session start that fires it.

## EVIDENCE 2026-07-26

  grep -c using-xtrm-reminder  repo .xtrm/config/hooks.json   -> 0
  grep -n using-xtrm-reminder  live ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json -> line 9
  grep -n using-xtrm-reminder  live ~/.claude/settings.json   -> line 83
  find repo .xtrm/hooks/ -name using-xtrm-reminder.mjs        -> absent (present only in stale worktrees)
  git log -- .xtrm/hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs              -> last touched 362db69a (#507)

The same dry run also reported '[DRY RUN] would install hooks/project-memory.mjs', which confirms the live global hooks tree is simply behind the payload.

## OPEN QUESTION FOR WHOEVER TAKES THIS

Does the installer remove its own stale entry from ~/.claude/settings.json when the corresponding payload file disappears? If the entry is tagged as installer-owned it should. If it is untagged it must NOT be deleted (xtrm-wiy5n.4.37 and the xtmux#82 rule), which means a removed payload file can leave a permanently broken wired hook. Answer this before choosing the fix.

## SUCCESS

- No live hook entry points at a payload file that no longer ships.
- Deleting a hook from the payload either removes the installer-owned entry that invokes it, or fails loudly at build time so it is never released in that state.

## SCOPE

core hook wiring and its policy compile step. Do not delete untagged user entries.
notes:
PR core#523 open. The ownership question is ANSWERED with file:line evidence, and the answer changed the fix.

THE SETTINGS SIDE WAS NEVER THE BUG
safeMergeOwnedHookSettings, cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:508, TAGS every wrapper it writes
via tagOwnedWrapper (:405-419) with _source: XTRM_GLOBAL_SOURCE plus _xtrm {version, hash}, and it
DROPS tagged wrappers on the next sync when they no longer match the canonical set (:540-543).
Untagged entries are preserved with a warning (:545-548), which is the xtrm-wiy5n.4.37 rule.
So cleanup already works for anything the installer wrote.

THE REAL GAP IS BUILD-SIDE
policies/*.json still referenced ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs AFTER
.xtrm/hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs was deleted from the payload in 362db69a (#507).
compile-policies.mjs wrote the mismatched entry into .xtrm/config/hooks.json without complaint.
From there the wire propagates through the global hooks bootstrap into ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json
and through the runtime sync into ~/.claude/settings.json.

THE FIX — fail at build time so the mismatch is never released
compile-policies.mjs now extracts every ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/<rel> token from Claude-side
hook commands and refuses to write, exiting 1, if any referenced file is missing under
.xtrm/hooks/. It runs in every mode: --dry-run, --check, --check-pi, and the plain write path.
Three red-then-green tests, all failing against origin/main, including a standing regression that
every REAL policy resolves to a shipped file. Suite: 1109 passed, 98 skipped, 0 failed.
gitnexus_impact: LOW, 0 affected processes.

RESIDUAL MANUAL STEP FOR THE OPERATOR — this PR cannot do it, and must not
The live entry on this host is UNTAGGED:

  ~/.claude/settings.json  SessionStart  _source: null  _xtrm: false
    command: node "/home/dawid/.xtrm/hooks/using-xtrm-reminder.mjs"

Because it carries no _source, the installer cannot prove it wrote it, so under the rule the
operator set on 2026-07-26 it must be LEFT ALONE. It will therefore survive, pointing at a file
the next hooks bootstrap removes, and it will fail on every session start that fires it.

Removing that one line from ~/.claude/settings.json is an operator action. It is the operator's
file and neither the installer nor this session owns it.
close_reason: Merged as core#523. The settings side was already correct — safeMergeOwnedHookSettings tags what it writes and cleans its own tagged entries. The gap was build-side, so compile-policies now fails when a policy references a hook file that does not ship. One residual manual step stays with the operator: the live untagged entry in ~/.claude/settings.json cannot be removed by the installer and must not be.

title: commit the AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md injected block in all three repos
description:
## OPERATOR DIRECTIVE 2026-07-26

The INJECTED BLOCK written into AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md in core, specialists and xtmux is INTENTIONAL content. It is not local noise. It must be committed in the next PR opened in each repo.

## CONTENT

Two sections, identical in all three repos and in both files (md5 de429478ca02c28fe5b4682e65ab1376):
- Communication Style — controlled, precise, direct language; stricter ASD-STE100 style for procedures, commands, migrations, deployments, security requirements, destructive operations, rollback, acceptance criteria, and operator handoffs.
- Task Tracking (two-tier) — beads own the durable record, the native task system owns the in-flight breakdown.

Diff is additions only: +26 lines per file, 6 files, 3 repos.

## WHY IT IS EASY TO LOSE

AGENTS.md and CLAUDE.md are both in the release preflight ephemeral-dirty allowlist (_release_common.py EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS), because GitNexus/OpenWolf rewrite them every session. So a dirty AGENTS.md or CLAUDE.md never blocks a release and never appears as a blocker anywhere. Left alone, the block would sit uncommitted forever.

## SUCCESS

[ ] core: block committed and merged
[ ] specialists: block committed and merged
[ ] xtmux: block committed and merged
notes:
DONE IN ALL THREE REPOS. Verified against each default branch, not against a local working tree.

  git show origin/main:AGENTS.md   core        -> conditioned clause present
  git show origin/master:AGENTS.md specialists -> conditioned clause present
  git show origin/main:AGENTS.md   xtmux       -> conditioned clause present
  git show origin/main:CLAUDE.md   xtmux       -> the contradicting 'do NOT use TodoWrite,
                                                  TaskCreate' line is gone (count 0)

PRs: specialists#235 then #238; core#518 then #519; xtmux#83.

TWO CODEX CORRECTIONS LANDED WITH IT, both real
1. The block told every reader of the RUNTIME-NEUTRAL AGENTS.md to 'use both' and named
   Claude-style tools with no condition. Pi and Codex read that file. It also contradicted guards
   already in the repo — CLAUDE.md 'when available' and agents-top.md 'if the runtime supports
   local task planning'. AGENTS.md now says 'up to two', says beads alone is correct and complete
   on a runtime with no task tools, and tells the reader to consult the runtime's own tool list
   rather than assume a name.
2. My first correction was itself ambiguous: 'do not call tools this file names' reads as
   forbidding bd, which the same file requires. It now says 'do not invent or call a native task
   API the runtime does not expose'.

CLAUDE.md keeps the Claude-specific wording, since the tools exist there. TaskExecute was dropped
from the named set — no such tool is exposed.

title: specialists: 3 open moderate hono advisories on the default branch; the direct pin is 6 patches behind
description:
## PROBLEM

github.com/xtrm-dev/specialists reports 3 OPEN moderate Dependabot advisories on the default branch. All three are hono:

  1. Server-Side XSS via JSX escaping bypass in cx()
  2. hono/jsx does not isolate context per request -> cross-request data disclosure
  3. API Gateway v1 adapter can drop a repeated request header value during de-duplication

package.json pins  hono 4.12.26. npm latest is 4.12.32.

## WHY THE PIN EXISTS — DO NOT DELETE IT

No specialists source file imports hono. 'git grep -E "['\"]hono(/|['\"])"' matches only package.json and bun.lock.

hono is a TRANSITIVE dependency of @modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0, which requires hono ^4.11.4, and of @hono/node-server which peers on hono ^4. The direct entry in dependencies is a FLOOR PIN that controls which hono the sdk resolves.

So the fix is to RAISE the pin, not to remove the dependency. Removing it hands version choice back to the sdk range.

## RELEASE CONTEXT

core cleared 6 High fast-uri advisories on 2026-07-26 in #516 by the same method: raise the floor. specialists is the next repo in the release order and still carries these three.

## SUCCESS

- package.json pins hono 4.12.32 (or the current latest inside ^4).
- The lockfile agrees.
- The 3 Dependabot alerts close on the default branch after merge.
- The suite passes with 'bun --bun vitest run'.

## NON_GOALS

- Removing hono from dependencies.
- Bumping any unrelated dependency.

## VALIDATION

[ ] node -e resolve of hono reports 4.12.32
[ ] bun --bun vitest run is green
[ ] after merge, gh api repos/xtrm-dev/specialists/dependabot/alerts shows 0 open hono alerts
notes: MERGED as specialists#236. hono 4.12.26 -> 4.12.32 in package.json and bun.lock. No other dependency touched. The pin was kept, not removed — it is the floor that controls which hono @modelcontextprotocol/sdk resolves.
close_reason: Merged as specialists#236. hono raised to 4.12.32, clearing the 3 open moderate advisories. Dependency kept as a floor pin.

title: specialists: three test files flake under host load; one shows a real SQLite lifecycle error
description:
## PROBLEM

A full specialists suite run at load average 15.08 on 12 cores fails 3 files while 144 tests pass and 7 skip:

  tests/unit/cli/feed.test.ts
  tests/unit/cli/integration.test.ts
  tests/unit/specialist/supervisor-parent-notification.test.ts

## WHY THIS IS NOT ANOTHER TIMEOUT BEAD

The third file does not time out. It fails with:

  [supervisor] SQLite upsertStatus failed: database client unavailable

That is a lifecycle error, not contention. It names the supervisor parent-notification path, which is the MSG-05 feature shipped on 2026-07-26. A real defect there is release relevant.

## WHY IT MATTERS NOW

specialists CI did not run the suite until spec#231 landed today. From now on CI runs it. An unloaded CI host may hide a contention flake, but it will not hide a real lifecycle defect.

## EVIDENCE SOURCE

Found by the worker on xtrm-wiy5n.4.22 while it proved status.test.ts is already fixed by #226. Report: /tmp/w422-report.md

## SUCCESS

Per file, a proved verdict with pasted command output: contention (name the contending sibling), real defect (root cause in src/, fixed, with a check that fails without the fix), or already fixed on current master.

A timeout raised to a bigger round number is not an accepted fix.

## SCOPE

Repo: specialists. One PR off master.
notes:
NO DEFECT. All three files are green on master. The failure was a WRONG TEST RUNNER, not flake and not contention.

PROOF (worker %7628, worktree specialists-xt-claude-wiy5n-422b):
  feed.test.ts                            33/33 pass isolated, 3/3 full-suite runs clean
  integration.test.ts                     24/24 pass isolated, 3/3 full-suite runs clean
  supervisor-parent-notification.test.ts  10/10 pass isolated, 3/3 full-suite runs clean

ROOT CAUSE OF THE FALSE ALARM
The earlier run used 'npx vitest run', which is Node. Node cannot require('bun:sqlite').
createObservabilitySqliteClient() therefore returned null and supervisor.ts:1281 threw. The throw is
DETERMINISTIC. It is not timing and it is not load. It only looked like a load-dependent flake
because the run that produced it happened to be under load.

The canonical repro is 'bun --bun vitest run'. That is what package.json's test script uses and what
CI uses.

CLASS OF ERROR
Second time today a tooling artifact was read as a product defect. The first was a caller-side
'timeout 40' on a foreground 'sp run' read as 'specialist jobs die at session start'. Both cost a
full triage. The lesson is the same: prove the harness before you accuse the product.

Report: /tmp/w433-report.md

FOLLOW-UP FILED: make the Node runner fail fast when bun:sqlite is not loadable, so this costs
seconds instead of a triage bead.
close_reason: No defect. All three files pass isolated and in 3/3 full-suite runs on master. The original failure was 'npx vitest run' (Node), which cannot require('bun:sqlite'); the canonical runner is 'bun --bun vitest run'. Follow-up filed to make the Node runner fail fast.

title: Generated CHANGELOG.md conflicts every open core pull request on every merge to main
description:
## PROBLEM

`CHANGELOG.md` is generated. A pre-push check requires it to be current. Every merge to `main` rewrites the `[Unreleased]` block. So every merge makes every other open pull request conflict on that file.

The conflict is never a real disagreement. Two branches simply hold two different generated states of the same block.

## COST MEASURED TODAY

- The worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.1 rebased three times for this reason alone. It said the cause is structural, not its own bead.
- The worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.2.2 rebased for the same reason.
- The worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.3 rebased for the same reason. It resolved by regeneration, which is the correct method.
- Core#511 and core#513 both became dirty again the moment core#515 merged. Neither had changed.

Five rebases today, on one file, with no real conflict in any of them.

## WHY IT WILL GET WORSE

The coordinated release wave merges several core pull requests in order. Each merge will dirty every remaining one. The cost grows with the square of the number of open pull requests.

## POSSIBLE DIRECTIONS

The orchestrator does not choose here. A worker must compare these and justify a choice:

1. Give `CHANGELOG.md` a git merge driver of "union" or a custom driver that regenerates. A generated file does not need a hand merge.
2. Stop tracking the `[Unreleased]` block. Generate it at release time only.
3. Keep the pre-push check, but let CI regenerate the block instead of the author.
4. Keep the current design, and document regeneration as the standard resolution. This is the cheapest option, and it accepts the rebase cost.

## SUCCESS

- A merge to `main` does not make an unrelated pull request conflict.
- Or, if a conflict remains possible, its resolution is one documented command.

## SCOPE

- core .gitattributes, if a merge driver is chosen
- core scripts/changelog-update.mjs
- the pre-push check
- the contributor documentation

## VALIDATION

[ ] Merge one pull request; a second open pull request stays mergeable
[ ] Or: one documented command resolves the conflict, and the documentation states it
notes:
GREEN. PR #517 mergeable_state=clean, all checks pass (test 24.x/3.11, pr-review-gate, Gitleaks, OSV, Semgrep, Socket x2).

Commits: f7532f39 (the fix) + 120c46b8 + 1c4b9a70 (both from Codex findings).

Codex raised 2 threads, both real, both corrected and resolved:
- P1 ci.yml:116 — wiring test:scripts into CI exposed that dedupe-legacy-hooks.test.mjs read the developer's real $HOME (~/.xtrm/hooks/beads-memory-gate.mjs), so it was green only by accident of the machine and ENOENT'd on a clean runner. Fixed hermetically (HOME pointed at a throwaway tree with a stand-in global install, dynamic import). Verified with HOME=$(mktemp -d) npm run test:scripts -> 16/16.
- P2 releasing SKILL:18 — session-close-report step 6 still MANDATED appending user-facing changes to [Unreleased], which this branch makes CI and pre-push reject; the two workflows were mutually unsatisfiable. Added the git-cliff branch to the top of its decision tree, in the canonical skill and the legacy skills/ mirror.

OPERATOR NOTE for the release wave: merging #517 rewrites CHANGELOG.md, so it will dirty open PRs that touch that file ONE last time. Of the 4 non-dependabot open PRs only #490 touches CHANGELOG.md; #505, #478, #360 do not. Merging #517 EARLY in the wave costs one rebase on #490 and removes the conflict class for every merge after it.

Bead left OPEN per contract.
close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/core#517. The worker found that the committed [Unreleased] block bought nothing. The tag command regenerates the whole section from the git log and ignores the committed text. Proof: run against a cleared file it still produced all 33 pending entries, against the 19 stale ones actually committed. Meanwhile the gate forced the collision, because changelog:check failed until an author committed the regenerated block, and 20 of the last 20 commits on main touched that file. It rejected the union merge driver with reasons: union duplicates entries on a real release conflict and then fails changelog:check, and a custom driver needs per-clone configuration that git does not honour automatically. Codex found a P2 that the orchestrator would have missed: the session-close-report step 6 still ordered an append to [Unreleased], which is mutually unsatisfiable with this change. The worker added the git-cliff branch to that decision tree. One item flagged and left alone, because it lives outside the repository: ~/.claude/commands/setup-git-cliff.md still teaches the old per-branch contract to every other xtrm repository, and it needs the same correction before the next repository is set up.

title: Claude settings hold three duplicate agent-state hooks; Codex wiring has no --new-instance
description:
## PROBLEM ONE

The live `~/.claude/settings.json` holds three duplicate `xtmux agent-state.sh` entries on SessionStart. None of the three carries a `_source` tag.

An untagged entry has no owner. An installer cannot remove it, because the installer cannot prove it wrote it. So each new install can add one more.

## PROBLEM TWO

The Codex wiring has no `--new-instance` at all. This is the same defect that bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.25 corrected for Claude. Nobody corrected it for Codex.

So a Codex pane never mints an agent instance id. It stays invisible to every feature that uses that identity.

## EVIDENCE

Both found 2026-07-26 by the worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.25. The worker left both alone, because each sits outside that bead SCOPE. That was the correct decision.

The Claude half of the defect is now merged as Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#79.

## SUCCESS

- The installer writes one `agent-state.sh` entry per event, and it tags each entry with `_source`.
- The installer removes its own duplicates on the next run.
- A Codex pane mints an instance id, in the same way as a Claude pane and a Pi pane.
- A test fails if the Codex wiring loses the flag.

## SCOPE

- xtmux scripts/install.mjs
- the installer tests

## NON_GOALS

- Removing an entry that another tool wrote. Only a tagged entry has a known owner.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Do not generate a new identity on every idle transition. `docs/xtmux-gaps.md:550` forbids this.

## VALIDATION

[ ] A second install adds no duplicate entry
[ ] Each entry the installer writes carries a _source tag
[ ] A new Codex pane has an @agent_instance_id
notes:
MERGED as Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#82. Worker %7634.

WHAT CHANGED
scripts/install.mjs — owned() and codexOwned() collapse to strict '_source === "xtmux"'. Pattern-based adoption is gone. mergeCodex() writes tagged entries and mints --new-instance on Codex SessionStart with matcher startup|resume|clear, per docs/xtmux-gaps.md:550.
tests/installer/install.test.mjs — legacy-adoption test rewritten; 3 new Codex tests.
tests/contracts/claude-hooks.test.ts — both Claude contracts rewritten for strict-tag policy.

FOUR PROOFS
1. A twin install is byte-identical for Claude and Codex — live proof plus 4 assertions.
2. Every entry the installer writes carries _source — live JSON plus tag-count tests.
3. A Codex pane mints @agent_instance_id — --new-instance on SessionStart only; the negative half asserts no other event mints.
4. Each new test FAILS when broken — 4 targeted edits, baseline restored after each.

Report: /tmp/w427-report.md
CI: test, analyze, smoke, CodeQL, pr-review-gate all green. 0 unresolved Codex threads.

MEETS THE OPERATOR DIRECTIVE OF 2026-07-26
The installer must never delete a user hook. This PR is the enforcement: an untagged entry has no provable owner and is left alone. The uninstall test asserts that two untagged clones SURVIVE uninstall while the tagged entry is removed.
close_reason: Merged as xtmux#82. Strict _source ownership stops duplicate growth and stops the installer touching entries it cannot prove it wrote; Codex now mints an instance id on SessionStart only. Four proofs, each new test verified to fail on broken input.

title: Claude runtime has no inbound-message surface; only Pi polls the inbox
description:
## PROBLEM

A Claude pane never learns that a message waits for it. Pi polls its inbox on a bounded 30 second cycle. Claude has no equivalent.

This is an asymmetry in capability, NOT a broken deliverable. Bead xtrm-wiy5n.3.3 scoped the Claude hook to obligations only. Its SCOPE says the hook "calls xtmux obligations list and prints reminder to stderr if pending — no inbox reminder hook". The bead TITLE says "bounded inbox reminder on Stop", which oversells what shipped. The title, not the code, is the misleading part.

## EVIDENCE

Every Claude xtmux hook, and what each one queries:

  auto-monitor-consumed.mjs    monitor-list, wait-agent
  auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs  monitor-list, obligations
  auto-monitor-on-send.mjs     obligations
  claude-agent-turn-capture.mjs  (none)

`message-list` appears in no Claude hook. Obligations are OUTBOUND duties — replies this pane owes. Inbound messages are a different thing, and nothing reads them.

Found 2026-07-26 by the worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.2.2 while it wrote the EVAL-01 Claude column. Verified independently by the orchestrator with a grep over the whole hook directory.

## CONSEQUENCE FOR EVAL-01

Matrix scenarios 6 and 7 (inbound reply-required, inbound FYI) cannot assert Claude and Pi parity, because parity does not exist. The merged tests in core#512 pin the ASYMMETRY instead: an inbound duty stays intact and undischarged for the next cycle. Those tests are correct for the system as built. They must be rewritten when this bead lands.

## SUCCESS

- A Claude pane learns about a pending inbound message without a person looking.
- The mechanism is bounded, like the Pi cycle. It must not spin.
- EVAL-01 scenarios 6 and 7 then assert parity instead of asymmetry.

## SCOPE

- xtmux side first: whatever surface a Claude hook can query for pane-scoped inbound messages
- core side: a Stop or PostToolUse hook that uses it
- core cli/src/tests/eval-01-claude-side.test.ts (scenarios 6 and 7) after the mechanism exists

## NON_GOALS

- A polling daemon.
- Changing the Pi side.

## CONSTRAINTS

- The xtmux implementation comes first. A core hook cannot query a surface that does not exist.
- Bounded work per Stop. The existing Stop hook uses stop_hook_active to avoid a loop; follow that pattern.

## VALIDATION

[ ] A message sent to an idle Claude pane is surfaced to it without human action
[ ] The mechanism cannot spin
[ ] EVAL-01 scenarios 6 and 7 assert parity
notes:
CORE HALF core#525 reviewed by the orchestrator. All checks SUCCESS, 0 unresolved threads, BEHIND only. Ready to merge once the branch update settles.

THE ANTI-SPIN ARGUMENT — I demanded it in the brief and it is stated, in the source, where the
next reader sees it:

  - Fires on Stop only. No poller, no daemon.
  - Skips when stop_hook_active is true, matching the existing Stop hook.
  - Records each surfaced messageKey in the tmux option @agent_inbox_reminded_keys. The SAME
    message still pending on the next Stop is INTENTIONALLY silent: it stays recorded and stays
    silent until the operator acks or replies, at which point the row leaves the --unacked
    projection anyway. A NEW message is a NEW key and gets its own one-time reminder.
  - Bounded per Stop: at most --limit rows, one option read, one option write. No retries, no
    loops. LIMIT is clamped to 1..25, subprocesses carry a 5s timeout.
  - Skipped entirely when TMUX_PANE is unset.

THE SUBTLE PART, CAUGHT BY CODEX: WRITE-FIRST ORDERING
The anti-spin key MUST persist BEFORE the reminder is emitted. If the write fails — pane gone
between query and write, tmux server crash mid-write — the hook ABORTS the reminder rather than
surface a message it would then re-surface forever. Reminder-then-write would have silently
voided the whole bounded-work guarantee, and it is the order most people would write first.

Key eviction is FIFO on the oldest: keys.slice(keys.length - 128). An evicted key belongs to a
message older than the last 128; if it is somehow still unacked it re-surfaces exactly once. That
is a bounded, acceptable failure mode.

OUTPUT CHANNEL, also from Codex: Claude's Stop hook contract reads STDOUT on exit 0 and stderr
only on a non-zero exit. The hook emits {"systemMessage": "..."} on stdout so the reminder
actually reaches the operator, and falls back to stderr only on a real subprocess error.
close_reason: Merged as xtmux#87 then core#525. xtmux resolves --for from the live tmux pane in V2 and refuses the implicit form in legacy modes rather than widening the query; core adds a bounded one-time Stop reminder with write-first anti-spin ordering, and EVAL-01 scenarios 6 and 7 now assert Claude/Pi parity instead of asymmetry.

title: xtmux safe-send-pointer --yes hangs after tmux 'not in a mode' error, sending nothing
description:
## PROBLEM

`xtmux safe-send-pointer --yes` blocked indefinitely without sending anything and without emitting any error, warning, or timeout. The dry-run form (no `--yes`) returned instantly and printed the correct command. Only the committing form hung.

This matters because /multiplexing designates `safe-send-pointer` as the PREFERRED send wrapper over raw `tmux send-keys` — it is the primitive orchestrators are told to rely on, and it fails closed-but-silent rather than erroring.

## EVIDENCE

2026-07-26. Target pane %7345, `@agent_state=done`, healthy.

  xtmux safe-send-pointer --force-freeform %7345 <text>        -> instant, printed the send-keys line
  xtmux safe-send-pointer --yes --force-freeform %7345 <text>  -> hung >120s, nothing sent, pane untouched
                                                                  survived SIGTERM; needed SIGKILL

Concurrent DB holder found via fuser on the coordination DB:

  /home/dawid/.local/state/xtmux/observability.db:
    dawid  3643653  F....  bun.exe
  ps: /home/dawid/dev/xtmux/node_modules/bun/bin/bun.exe src/cli.ts log-follow --after-id 1597066 --json
  elapsed 01:38:19

That reader was an orphaned `xtmux log-follow`, the bun child of a `scripts/test-session-events.sh --json` run whose parent shell had been killed ~1h earlier. DB at the time: 550M plus an 8.9M WAL.

After killing the orphan, raw `tmux send-keys` to the same pane worked immediately and the pane transitioned to `running`.

## HYPOTHESIS (not proven)

`--yes` takes a write path against the SQLite coordination DB (obligation/monitor arming) that blocks on a lock held by the long-lived reader, with no busy_timeout and no user-visible diagnostic. The dry-run path stays read-only and so never contends.

## SUCCESS

- `safe-send-pointer --yes` either completes, or fails with a diagnostic naming lock contention and the holding pid — never hangs silently.
- A bounded `busy_timeout` on the coordination DB write path.
- Long-lived readers such as `log-follow` do not block sends.

## SCOPE

- xtmux safe-send-pointer commit path and its coordination-DB access
- SQLite busy_timeout / lock strategy on the shared observability DB
- possibly `xtmux log-follow` holding a transaction open longer than needed

## NON_GOALS

- The orphaned-watcher process itself. That was operator cleanup error (the shell wrapper was killed but not its bun child) and is not the defect; the defect is that a reader can silently wedge the preferred send primitive.

## VALIDATION

[ ] With a long-lived `xtmux log-follow` running, `safe-send-pointer --yes` completes or errors within a bounded time
[ ] Error message names lock contention and the holding pid
[ ] Regression test covering send-under-reader-contention
notes:
MERGED as Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#84. Worker %7634.

THE HYPOTHESIS WAS PARTLY WRONG, AND THE WORKER SAID SO
The bead guessed 'no busy_timeout on the write path'. The DB layer ALREADY sets busy_timeout,
default 3s, src/db/connection.ts. That was not the gap.

THE REAL GAP
bin/tmux-session-picker wrapped every obs subprocess call from safe_send_pointer in
'2>/dev/null || true'. Any hang past busy_timeout — a stuck bun subprocess, a WAL recovery stall,
a fuse-backed disk syscall — became an INVISIBLE pane freeze. stderr was thrown away and there
was no wall-clock cap at all. That is why it failed closed-but-silent.

THE FIX
New safe_pointer_obs_call wrapper:
  timeout -k $XTMUX_OBS_CALL_KILL_AFTER_SEC (default 2) $XTMUX_OBS_CALL_TIMEOUT_SEC (default 5)
The -k matters: the evidence says the process survived SIGTERM and needed SIGKILL.
On rc 124 or 137 it prints a diagnostic naming the subcommand, the cap, the coordination-DB path
resolved the same way the runtime resolves it, and the holder pids from fuser. The
'2>/dev/null' was removed from the call sites so the diagnostic actually reaches the operator.
Missing 'timeout' (macOS without coreutils) falls through to a raw call with a one-shot stderr
warning rather than returning 127.

PROOFS — tests/contracts/safe-send-pointer-timeout.test.ts
1. Silent hang eliminated: send commits, diagnostic contains DB path, fuser holders, wall-clock cap.
2. Bounded busy_timeout on the writer path: openDb sets a positive value.
3. A real log-follow reader plus a real writer does not block a send, under a 3s bound.
4. Each check FAILS when broken: strip the timeout wrapper -> test times out; strip the
   diagnostic printf -> text assertions fail; disable PRAGMA busy_timeout -> 'expected > 0,
   received 0'. Baseline restored after each.

Local suites: 312 bun + 14 installer + 288 contract-shell, all green. CI green. 3 Codex threads,
all resolved.

FOLLOW-UP NOTED, NOT FILED YET: the orphaned 'xtmux log-follow' that outlived its parent shell by
about an hour with no reap is its own defect and was out of scope here.
close_reason: Merged as xtmux#84. The cause was not the hypothesised missing busy_timeout — that already existed. It was '2>/dev/null || true' around every obs subprocess call, with no wall-clock cap. Now bounded by timeout -k with a diagnostic naming the DB path and the fuser holder pids.

title: Stale launcher flag guidance in /multiplexing + plan templates (--bead/--prompt, --no-attach)
description:
## PROBLEM

Three command shapes documented in /multiplexing and in the Sprint 2 plan file (~/.claude/plans/fluffy-crafting-barto.md §7) are rejected by the current CLIs. Each cost a failed round trip during the Sprint 2 §7 pickup.

1. `xt pi --role <r> --bead <id> --prompt <text>`
   -> "--bead and --prompt are mutually exclusive; pick one"
   /multiplexing Pattern 7 says the exclusion applies only under --role, which is correct, but the plan template used exactly that combination and the skill does not warn against it in the role-mode example.

2. `xt pi --role <r> --no-attach` (without --new-session)
   -> "--no-attach requires --new-session (or exit tmux first)"
   /multiplexing Pattern 2b and Pattern 7 both show bare `--no-attach` as the canonical orchestrator-monitored spawn.

3. `sp run <specialist> --bead <id> --prompt <text>`
   -> "Error: use either --prompt or --bead, not both."
   Same exclusion at the sp layer. The plan §7 demo command used both.

## SUCCESS

- /multiplexing Pattern 2b + Pattern 7 examples use flag combinations that the shipped CLIs accept.
- The bare-vs-role flag matrix states the --bead/--prompt exclusion for `sp run` too, not only for `xt pi --role`.
- Plan §7 template updated so a future pickup session copies a working command.

## SCOPE

- ~/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md (Pattern 2b, Pattern 7, flag matrix)
- ~/.claude/plans/fluffy-crafting-barto.md §7 (or its successor template)

## NON_GOALS

- Changing the CLI exclusions themselves. The guards are correct; the docs are what drifted.

## VALIDATION

[ ] Every command in Pattern 2b / Pattern 7 runs without a flag-guard rejection
notes:
APPLIED 2026-07-26 (via shell, on operator instruction — Edit tool is worktree-boundary-blocked from this session).

LIVE NOW — ~/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md (global SSOT, not version-controlled; backup at /tmp/multiplexing-SKILL.md.bak-1785075984):
  L95  wait-agent entry rewritten to the --wait-for-transition --consume form, with an explicit warning that the BARE form has been observed returning done against a still-working target (xtrm-wiy5n.4.14).
  L337 `xt pi --role <specialist> --bead <epic> --no-attach` -> added --new-session (role mode rejects bare --no-attach).
  L346 same fix in the Pattern 7 spawn snippet.
  L587 Monitoring section example -> --wait-for-transition --consume form.
  Verified after: zero remaining `--role ... --no-attach` without --new-session; heading count unchanged 58/58; frontmatter intact.

LIVE NOW — ~/.xtrm/skills/default/using-specialists/references/monitoring.md (interim stopgap; backup in /tmp):
  L15 invalid detach example `sp run <role> --bead <id> --prompt "..." > /tmp/job.log 2>&1 &` corrected to use one flag, with an inline note that sp rejects the pair.
  This is the STALE 205-line vendored copy. It is what every agent loads today, so it was worth fixing in place, and the release will replace the whole file anyway.

UPSTREAM, PENDING PR — specialists master, config/skills/using-specialists/references/monitoring.md (+1 line, working tree, uncommitted):
  Adds a routing line stating dispatch form is authoritative in `sp run --help`, that a foreground sp run BLOCKS so an agent pane with a bash-tool timeout kills its own job, that detach is a trailing &, and that --bead/--prompt are mutually exclusive — explicitly WITHOUT restating the flags, so it cannot rot the way the previous block did.

WHY A POINTER AND NOT A RESTORED BLOCK: the old operational block rotted twice already (router split b973312d, then DOC-01 a2619d76). Duplicated CLI facts drift from the CLI. `sp run --help` ships with the code and already documents the async form under an "Async patterns" heading, so the durable fix is to route to it. This also works WITH DOC-01 (the file is a retrieval router) instead of reverting a merged, reviewed deliverable.

WHY THE VENDORED COPY CANNOT SIMPLY BE REGENERATED: .xtrm/specialists-source.json pins ref v3.21.0 / sha 22573c64. DOC-01 landed on master after that tag, so the vendor legitimately still pulls the old file. Unpinning is a release decision. The durable path is the one already on the board: specialists 3.21.2 (xtrm-wiy5n.4.4) -> manifest bump + vendor -> Core 0.11.3 (xtrm-wiy5n.4.6) -> xt update --apply.

DELIBERATELY NOT DONE:

title: xtmux wait-agent returns done while @agent_state reads running
description:
## PROBLEM

`xtmux wait-agent <pane> --timeout 20m --interval 20s` returned `wait <pane> done` twice in a row while `tmux show-options -p -t <pane> -qv @agent_state` still read `running`, and the pane was visibly mid-turn.

This makes the documented orchestrator monitoring primitive unusable: /multiplexing tells the orchestrator to prefer wait-agent over the @agent_state until-loop, but a premature `done` is exactly the condition Cardinal Rule 4 exists to prevent (never send to a working pane). An orchestrator that trusts wait-agent will send into a working pane.

## EVIDENCE

Session 2026-07-26, demo pane %7343 (role-pi-chain-coordinator-xtrm-0l718):

- Fire 1: armed immediately after `safe-send-pointer --yes`. Returned done within seconds; `@agent_state` = running; pane showed "Working..." and an in-flight ctx tool call. Plausibly the documented post-send race (pane had not yet entered working).
- Fire 2: armed AFTER confirming `@agent_state` = running. Still returned `wait %7343 done` while the pane was mid `sp run`. This one is not explained by the post-send race.

Fallback used instead, and it behaved correctly:
  until state="$(tmux show-options -p -t %7343 -qv @agent_state)" && ! printf %s\\n "$state" | grep -qE "^(working|running|busy|thinking)$"; do sleep 20; done

## SUCCESS

- wait-agent does not report done while @agent_state is in a working-family value.
- If wait-agent samples a different source than @agent_state, the two are reconciled, or wait-agent gains a documented grace period / transition requirement so an already-working target cannot resolve instantly.

## SCOPE

- xtmux wait-agent (and monitor-agent, which shares the state predicate)
- /multiplexing Monitoring section if guidance needs to change

## VALIDATION

[ ] wait-agent armed on a known-working pane blocks until that pane leaves working
[ ] Regression test covering arm-while-working
notes:
D3 RESOLVED 2026-07-26 — NOT a release blocker for xtrm-wiy5n.4.5.

Ran the discriminating test an advisor (xtrm-vm7s0) specified: the exact Stop-hook form against a pane whose @agent_state was confirmed `running` immediately before and after.

  xtmux wait-agent %7345 --wait-for-transition --consume --timeout 30s --interval 100ms --json
  -> blocked for the full window, elapsed_ms=30214, then:
     {"code":"XTMUX_WAIT_TIMEOUT","message":"wait-agent: timeout target=%7345",
      "detail":{"waitId":"wait-1785073415058-135678","monitorId":"monitor-1785073415058-135678"}}
  Target state before AND after: running.

So `--wait-for-transition --consume` correctly refuses to resolve against a still-working target. The Claude Stop hook path (~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs:43) is unaffected, and xtmux 0.2.3 is not gated on this.

Scope is therefore confirmed narrow: the BARE `wait-agent <pane>` form (no --wait-for-transition) returns done against a working target. That affects hand-armed orchestrator waits only, which is how /multiplexing Monitoring documents it — so the skill currently steers orchestrators to the broken form while the production hook uses the correct one. Fix should either make bare form consistent, or /multiplexing should document the --wait-for-transition form as the one to use.

Stays P2. Suggested regression test: assert the bare form also blocks against a confirmed-working target.
close_reason: Merged as Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#81. Root cause at src/cli-monitors.ts:198: the bare wait-agent form reused ANY prior wait row for the pair (requester, target), including an already-terminal row. The guard 'if (!existing || existing.terminalStatus === null)' then skipped the poll loop, so it replayed a cached done result forever. The --wait-for-transition form reuses only unarmed or armed rows, which is exactly why the Claude Stop hook path was always correct and why bead 4.3's discriminating test came out clean. Fix: a terminal wait replays only while the live pane state is non-working; a working target always opens a fresh wait. Proof: fire 2 on a running pane blocked the full 10 seconds and returned exit 124 with a new waitId; fire 3 on an idle pane replayed the original waitId, so replay semantics stayed intact. A new regression test fails before the change and passes after it. Checks: bun test 305 pass 0 fail, contract 288 pass 0 fail, typecheck clean, verify-json-api PASS, installer 11 pass. This closes the fault the orchestrator met at the start of the session, when a wait returned done twice against a working pane.

title: Dead specialist job is never transitioned to a terminal status, so MSG-05 never fires for it
description:
## CORRECTION — this bead was originally filed on a wrong diagnosis

Originally filed as P1 "Specialist jobs die at session start (SessionKilledError) — blocks MSG-05 end-to-end verification". That was WRONG and is retracted. There is no spawn-time job failure and MSG-05 was never blocked.

What actually happened: both probe jobs were killed by their own callers timeout. `sp run` is a long-running foreground streaming command, not a detach-and-return call.
- Job 2ad8ba: invoked under a `timeout 40` wrapper. Event trace shows run_start -> turn start -> run_complete ERROR at elapsed_s=39.
- Job b3402f: invoked from a pi pane whose bash tool timed out at its 30s default ("Command timed out after 30 seconds").
The `elapsed_s: 1` I originally cited was a `sp ps` snapshot taken at poll time, not time of death. The two Sprint 2 jobs cited as corroboration (fae369, fcb8f9) were not verified and should not be treated as evidence.

Re-run with no caller timeout: job 5ff574 completed normally (status=done, turns=8, tool_calls=14, exit_reason=agent_end) and produced the full MSG-05 chain. §7 PASSES. Lesson saved as memory key sp-run-is-foreground-long-running.

## PROBLEM (what actually remains)

When a specialist job process dies while its status row says `running`, the supervisor detects the dead pid but does not transition the job to a terminal status. Because `emitParentNotification` only fires on `done` or `error` (supervisor.ts:203), such a job silently produces no MSG-05 notification at all — the parent is never told the job is gone and waits indefinitely.

## EVIDENCE

Job b3402f, specialist_events trace (core observability.db):
  seq 5  t=1785067718456  turn      phase=start
  seq 6  t=1785067753923  meta      model=dead_job_detected backend=status-load
         data={"component":"status-load","event":"dead_job_detected","job_id":"b3402f",
               "previous_status":"running","next_status":"running","pid":3710836,
               "reason":"active status has dead pid or tmux session"}

`next_status` is `running` — the detector observes the death and deliberately leaves the row non-terminal. No run_complete event, no notification.

Contrast, job 2ad8ba, same kind of death but surfaced through the normal error path:
  seq 6  run_complete status=ERROR elapsed_s=39 exit_reason=SessionKilledError
  -> MSG-05 fired correctly: messageKey 2ad8ba:error, event_name=job.failed, parent.verified=true

So the notification layer is healthy. The gap is purely that dead-pid detection does not produce a terminal transition.

Secondary, minor: the job dir for a job that dies this way (/home/dawid/dev/core/.specialists/jobs/b3402f) contains only `steer.pipe` — no stderr artifact naming the cause, which is what sent this investigation down the wrong path initially.

## SUCCESS

- `dead_job_detected` transitions the job to `error` (with a reason such as `process died`), which in turn emits the normal MSG-05 job.failed notification.
- A parent waiting on a job that dies is notified rather than hanging.
- A job that dies leaves a stderr artifact in its job dir.

## SCOPE

- specialists status-load / dead-pid detection path (the component emitting `dead_job_detected`)
- job-artifact writing on abnormal death

## NON_GOALS

- Anything about MSG-05 delivery itself. Verified working end-to-end on both the done and error paths.
- Caller-side timeouts. That is operator error, now covered by memory sp-run-is-foreground-long-running and by xtrm-wiy5n.4.15.

## VALIDATION

[ ] Kill a running specialist jobs pid; job transitions to error, not stuck running
[ ] Parent receives a job.failed MSG-05 for that job
[ ] Job dir contains an artifact naming the death cause
notes:
REPRIORITIZED P3 -> P2 on advisor D2 verdict (xtrm-vm7s0), which disagreed with the P3 classification. Rationale accepted: this is not subsumed by the durable-job-ownership work (D1) — that would remove ONE cause of process death, not all of them — and a job stranded non-terminal makes the parent wait forever, violating a core terminal-state invariant. Non-release-blocking.

Advisor also split the fix: the correctness fix is the atomic transition to a canonical terminal state (error) PLUS invoking the normal notification path. The missing stderr artifact stays P3 / secondary acceptance work and should not be allowed to enlarge the correctness fix.
close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/specialists#232. Root cause: status-load.ts detected the dead pid and wrote dead_job_detected with next_status running, on purpose. emitParentNotification fires only on done or error. So the job never became terminal and the parent was never told. The worker found the same gap on a second site: Supervisor.reconcileDeadStatus did transition to error but never notified. Change: one shared buildDeadJobRecovery used by both detection sites. Each site now persists the error status and a run_complete ERROR event, then calls emitParentNotification. So the transition and the notification cannot separate again. LIVE PROOF, not a test alone: the worker started a real job, killed its pid, then called loadStatuses. Before the change the status stayed running with no error. After the change the status became error with 'Process crashed or was killed', MSG-05 was delivered (xtmux message-status repro02:error shows event_name job.failed and parent.verified true), and a death.txt file recorded the pid and the tmux session. Validation: tsc clean, full suite 1654 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed, 6 new tests in status-load-dead-job.test.ts plus 1 in supervisor-parent-notification.test.ts, and two live checks. Left alone on purpose and noted in the pull request: epic-reconciler.markDeadJobsAsError also marks dead jobs error without a notification, but that path is operator-invoked through sp epic sync --apply and has different semantics.

close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/specialists#226. Root cause: attach no longer exits when a tmux session ends. It gives live jobs to a TUI (src/cli/attach-tui.ts:141) that exits only on /quit or Ctrl+C, so the test premise was obsolete and the child ran without end. A prior orphan process was still resident after about 10 days. Fix: GNU timeout wraps every pty spawn and signals the whole process group. Result: targeted tests went from 3 failures plus an indefinite hang to 9/9 pass in 12.42s with no orphans. Full npm test went from no return to 77s and 135 files pass. Accepted deviations: un-quarantine in vitest.config.ts (the bead constraint allowed it once the bug landed), one brittle global-specialist-count assertion dropped, and pty tests now skip without GNU timeout. CI is ubuntu-latest only, so the skip does not change CI. Three Codex P2 findings fixed in a second round: shell-quote the pty command, probe the util-linux script interface instead of command presence, and require pgrep success in the orphan check. The worker also found a third suite failure, proved on clean master under the same load that it was pre-existing, and it is now bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.22.

title: pr-review-gate wave-2: pull_request_review_comment trigger + CR verdict preservation
description:
## PROBLEM
Two P2 correctness gaps in the canonical `pr-review-gate.yml` workflow, flagged by Codex during fanout PR review across 8 mercuryintelligence repos:

1. **Missing `pull_request_review_comment` trigger.** The current trigger set (`pull_request` / `pull_request_review` / `issue_comment`) does NOT fire on inline diff comments made without a review submission. If a bot posts/edits/deletes an inline comment outside a review, the gate never re-runs on the PR merge ref — the check can stay green while an unresolved bot thread has been added.

2. **Latest-review overwrite loses active CHANGES_REQUESTED.** Current logic keeps only the latest `submittedAt` review per bot. If a bot submits CHANGES_REQUESTED then later comments (COMMENTED with a newer timestamp), the CR verdict is overwritten and the gate turns green. GitHub's native branch-protection clears CR only on APPROVED or DISMISSED — we should mirror that.

Neither manifests in Codex's current pattern (Codex bundles inline comments with review submissions; Codex state is always COMMENTED, never CR). Both are theoretical for Codex but real for CodeRabbit and future bots.

## SUCCESS
Canonical workflow at `skills/security-pipeline/templates/.github/workflows/pr-review-gate.yml` (+ the live version in `.github/workflows/`) fixes both gaps:
- Add `pull_request_review_comment: types: [created, edited, deleted]` to triggers.
- Preserve active CR: track per-bot "latest blocking verdict" — a CR stays active until an APPROVED or DISMISSED review supersedes it.

Fanout across the 16 already-live repos (core, specialists, infra, market-data + the 12 from this fanout wave).

## NON_GOALS
- Not urgent enough to hold the current fanout — merge the 12 first, apply this wave-2 improvement as a batch across all 16.
- Do not change any other behavior (bot-typename check, pagination, workflow_dispatch, regex flag stripping — all stay).

## CONSTRAINTS
- Same file, byte-identical, in all repos post-wave-2.
- Codex will re-review — expect potential wave-3 findings; that's the working-as-designed loop.

## VALIDATION
- 16 PRs opened + merged.
- Codex threads resolved without dropping the two P2 improvements.

title: Phase 3 — Simplify xtrm-merge-fifo: read pr-review-gate CI status instead of local codex-blocker-check
description:
## PROBLEM
`~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/codex_blocker_check.py` re-computes what the new CI
check already answers. Two sources of truth = future drift. The systemd
timer `archon-codex-comments.service` maintains the local snapshot only to
feed this stale duplicate.

## SUCCESS
`xtrm-merge-fifo.yaml` reads the `pr-review-gate` check status per eligible
PR via `gh pr checks`, drops `codex-fetch` and `codex-blocker-check` nodes.
Retired scripts + systemd timer removed if nothing else depends on them.

## SCOPE
- Add a new node `pr-review-gate-check` that, for each `eligible_order` PR,
  runs `gh pr checks <n> --json name,conclusion --jq '.[]|select(.name=="pr-review-gate / gate")|.conclusion'`
  and emits `{gate: "GO"|"NO_GO", per_pr: [{pr, status}]}`.
- Delete nodes `codex-fetch` and `codex-blocker-check`. Update
  `execute-merge`'s `when:` to reference the new node.
- Update the workflow `description:` header — remove "checks for unread Codex
  reviewer blockers", replace with "checks the `pr-review-gate` required
  status on each eligible PR".
- Grep for any other reference to `codex_blocker_check.py` /
  `codex_comment_fetch.py` — check `~/.archon/**`, `systemctl list-timers`,
  `systemctl status archon-codex-comments*`.
- If nothing else depends: delete the two scripts, mask/remove the timer.
- Update `assess` node prompt: remove reference to the deleted nodes' outputs.
- Mirror the same swap in `xtrm-merge-fifo-dry-run.yaml`.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not remove FIFO ordering, main-clean check, env guard, operator approval,
  rebase cascade, or branch-GC.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Deferred +7d from Phase 1 land — need at least a week of green CI
  observations before Archon depends on it.
- If a PR does not have the check present at all (fork PR, workflow disabled),
  treat as NO_GO — fail closed.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Dry-run: `archon workflow run xtrm-merge-fifo-dry-run` shows the new
      node's output; no reference to the deleted nodes anywhere.
- [ ] Live-run on a stale eligible PR: gate follows the CI check state.
- [ ] `systemctl list-timers | grep archon-codex` empty (or intentionally
      re-scoped, documented in bead notes).

## OUTPUT

  `xtrm-merge-fifo-dry-run.yaml`.
- Retired scripts + timer (if safe).
notes:
## Archon-default cross-check (2026-07-24 background research)

Enumerated defaults under /home/dawid/dev/vendor/Archon/.archon/workflows/. Key findings that shape Phase 3 approach:

**Precedent for CI-status consumption:** No default workflow consumes a required-status-check. Closest analog is `experimental/archon-release.yaml::wait-for-binaries` — bounded `gh` poll loop, 30s cadence, ~15 min ceiling, fail-fast on FAILURE, verdict computed by the script not the LLM. **Model our new `pr-review-gate-check` node after this pattern** rather than a one-shot query — checks may still be queued when the workflow starts.

**Borrow into Phase 3 (adopt these while touching the file):**
1. `include: archon-review-block`-style reuse — extract the shared preflight/cascade blocks so `xtrm-merge-fifo.yaml` and `xtrm-merge-fifo-dry-run.yaml` stop duplicating YAML. Currently we're about to edit both files identically; the sub-DAG pattern eliminates that.
2. `context: fresh` on the `assess` node — used throughout Archon review-block to prevent context bleed across LLM nodes. Cheap win.
3. `retry()` bash helper (from `maintainer/marketplace-pr-review-and-merge.yaml`) — 3× linear backoff around every `gh pr merge` / `gh pr checks` call. Guards against fresh-token 401s that would otherwise fail-closed the whole run.
4. `--repo "$ORIGIN_REPO"` pin from `git remote get-url origin` on every `gh` call — no default sub-DAG omits it. Prevents fork clones from targeting upstream by accident.

**Validation of ours-only surface (no changes needed):**
- FIFO queue across N open PRs — no default has cross-PR ordering. Ours is the reference implementation.
- `ARCHON_ALLOW_MERGE=1` env dual-lock + operator approval — stricter than any shipped example; matches the "double-gated mutation" prescription from xtrm-workflow-authoring.
- Rebase cascade + branch-GC post-merge — no default covers this.
- main-clean / not-behind preflight — no default probes local repo state.

**Deferred to a possible Phase 6 (open follow-up, do NOT scope-creep Phase 3):**
- Extract preflight/cascade into a shared `include:` sub-DAG. Worth doing but crosses the "keep phase 3 minimal" line.
- Align `assess` node output schema with Archon's `{decision, reason}` shape.
## 2026-07-24 — implementation notes

New script: ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/pr_review_gate_check.py

title: Specialists: lifecycle terminal assignee + remove legacy ready markers
description:
## PROBLEM
When a Specialists job finishes and MSG-05 (T2_SPEC_MSG05) sends the terminal notification, the parent bead's assignee is not updated to reflect which executor ran the job. Result: bead history has no lineage record that "job-a82636 (executor role) closed this bead". Lineage substrate exists in MSG-05's payload; assignee update is a small trailing side-effect.

Fold-in from operator: "clearly update plan for the specialists part of it" — P4 is this piece.

## SUCCESS
At each Specialists terminal transition (done, error, cancelled) that MSG-05 already emits, the associated bead (if any) is also updated with `assignee=executor/<job-id>` (or role-appropriate: `reviewer/<job-id>`, `debugger/<job-id>`). Piggybacks on the MSG-05 emission — no separate hook, no daemon.

## SCOPE
- `src/specialist/supervisor.ts` — inside `emitParentNotification(statusSnapshot)` helper landed by T2_SPEC_MSG05, add optional trailing `bd update <bead> --assignee=<role>/<job-id>` when the payload carries a bead id
- Reuse existing bead id from `SupervisorStatus.bead_id` (or wherever it lives) — already surfaced in the unified handoff
- No new plumbing — the assignee write reuses the same try/catch as the message send

## NON_GOALS
- Backfilling existing terminal jobs
- Overwriting a human operator's manual assignee (only auto-set if current assignee is a `runtime/*` slug — respect operator override)
- Full lineage tree in bead notes (that's Track B / Sprint 4)

## CONSTRAINTS
- Blocked-by T2_SPEC_MSG05 (uses the same seam)
- Blocked-by (implicitly) P3 xtrm-wiy5n.3.13 — because P3 defines the `runtime/slug` format convention that P4 mirrors as `<role>/<job-id>`; if P3 shifts format, P4 shifts with it
- Assignee format: `<role>/<job-id>` — e.g. `executor/job-a82636786fc2ae571`
- Preserve operator overrides: if current assignee is not a `runtime/*` or `<role>/*` slug, do NOT overwrite (leave as-is, log info)
- Update failure never rolls back MSG-05 send or job completion
- Ponytail: single `bd update --assignee=...` call inside existing helper — no new class, no watcher

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Contract test: terminal-done for a job with bead → `bd show <bead>` shows `assignee=executor/<job-id>` (or matching role)
- [ ] Contract test: operator manual assignee like `alice@example.com` is NOT overwritten
- [ ] Contract test: prior auto-assignee `pi/4h2xk` IS overwritten by the terminal executor id (lineage advances)
- [ ] Contract test: bd update failure → job still completes, MSG-05 still sends, only a warning logged
- [ ] Live: `sp run executor --bead <id>` → after terminal, `bd show <id>` shows executor lineage

## OUTPUT
PR link + demo transcript showing full lineage: bead created → operator claims → `xt claude --bead <id>` sets `assignee=claude/<slug>` → `sp run executor --bead <id>` → on terminal, assignee becomes `executor/<job-id>`.

### Additional constraints

### Additional validation

- focused terminal tests prove no ready marker while parent notification/result flow remains green

Parent approved exact retirement of the still-shipped Specialists completion hook required by the marker-removal P1:
- delete config/hooks/specialists-complete.mjs
- remove only its src/cli/init.ts wiring plus doctor/docs/tests/asset-contract references
