title: Core: xt pi/claude --bead auto-populates bead assignee from runtime-origin
description:
## PROBLEM
`xt pi --bead <id>` and `xt claude --bead <id>` currently launch the runtime against the bead but do not stamp ownership on the bead itself. Result: `bd show <id>` shows the bead is claimed but not which runtime/session actually did the work. Lineage substrate (`xtrm.forensic.v1` runtime-origin) already exists at spawn time — just not wired to bd `assignee`.

Fold-in from operator: fold P3 into Sprint 2; P1/P2 (slug generation + worktree/branch propagation) are free-of-charge because reusing `xtrm.forensic.v1` runtime-origin means the slug already exists at spawn.

## SUCCESS
When `xt pi --bead <id>` or `xt claude --bead <id>` starts, the bead is updated with `assignee=<runtime>/<slug>` — e.g. `assignee=pi/4h2xk` or `assignee=claude/9y3mn`. The slug comes from the existing runtime-origin id (audit-selected format). `bd show <id>` reflects the assignee immediately. Idempotent on repeated `--bead` launches.

## SCOPE
- `cli/src/commands/pi.ts` and `cli/src/commands/claude.ts` — after runtime spawn + `--bead` claim, call `bd update <bead> --assignee=<runtime>/<slug>`
- `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts` — if the slug seam lives here instead, wire from there
- Small helper: extract runtime-origin slug (short-form, human-readable) from the xtmux runtime-context

## NON_GOALS
- Worktree/branch name propagation (P2) — deferred to Track B / Sprint 4
- Retroactive assignment for existing claims
- New slug format — reuse `xtrm.forensic.v1` runtime-origin id
- Auto-claim if `--bead` not passed

## CONSTRAINTS
- Assignee format: `runtime/slug` (e.g. `pi/4h2xk`, `claude/9y3mn`) — human-readable, greppable
- Slug source: existing `xtrm.forensic.v1` runtime-origin id (short-form; if source is a URI, extract the tail slug)
- Idempotent — repeated `--bead` launches (e.g. after crash) update to current runtime, no error
- Ponytail: no new slug generator; one `bd update --assignee=...` call after successful claim
- If `bd update --assignee` fails, log warning but do NOT abort the session

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Integration test: `xt pi --bead <id>` → `bd show <id>` shows `assignee=pi/<slug>`
- [ ] Integration test: `xt claude --bead <id>` → `bd show <id>` shows `assignee=claude/<slug>`
- [ ] Slug matches runtime-origin id extracted from xtmux runtime-context
- [ ] Restarting the session updates assignee to new slug (idempotent, no error on stale value)
- [ ] Assignee update failure does not abort session (warning only)
- [ ] `bd list --assignee=pi/*` returns claimed beads (validates format)

## OUTPUT
PR link + before/after `bd show` example + note that P4 (Specialists lifecycle assignee) is separate bead.

title: PR5b: canary policy for future auto-merge (decision doc + threshold ratification)
description:
## PROBLEM

PR2 ships a 6-tier gate lattice where even PASS opens a normal PR (no auto-merge on day one). PR5a produces empirical measurement of verifier FP/FN + retrieval precision/recall + stale-claim escape rate + activator consumption + token cost.

Neither PR decides which subset (if any) of PASS verdicts is safe to auto-merge. That's an operator decision requiring: (a) baseline data (from PR5a), (b) explicit threshold policy, (c) operator sign-off. This bead is that decision document + threshold ratification + tooling to enable the switch — NOT the switch itself.

## SUCCESS

- ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge-canary.md written: which claim classes MAY be auto-merged, under which measured conditions, with what override paths.
- Threshold policy ratified with operator: 30d observation window with ≥ 200 verifier runs, verifier FP rate < 0.02, verifier FN rate < 0.05 on golden set + eval corpus, PLUS operator sign-off per this policy. Auto-merge limited to path/symbol/literal/env-var/image/config-value low-risk claim classes only (per research §5.1). Causal claims, procedure claims, security-posture claims, complete-set critical claims stay with review permanently.
- `service-knowledge canary status` CLI subcommand reports: are we in observation window? current metric values vs thresholds? green/yellow/red? days remaining?
- `service-knowledge canary enable --classes path,symbol,literal,env-var,image,config-value` gated by (a) all thresholds met (b) operator confirmation prompt (c) explicit override env for CI. Enabling flips a config flag read by reconcile.py at the moment atomic_write is about to happen.
- Reserved package version v1.0.0 for the canary-enable moment (v0.7.0 ships this bead; v1.0.0 comes when operator flips the switch).

## SCOPE

- NEW: ~/dev/xtrm/docs/devops/service-knowledge-canary.md (the policy)
- NEW: src/service_knowledge/canary/  (status + enable/disable subcommands + config flag)
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/cli/  (canary subcommand tree under the package CLI)
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/scripts/reconcile.py — read canary config flag at the atomic_write branch; auto-merge only when: flag=on AND verdict=PASS AND all claims in enabled classes
- Config file: .xtrm/state/service-knowledge/canary.json (per-repo, gitignored, {enabled: bool, classes: [...], enabled_at: timestamp, enabled_by: str})

## NON_GOALS

- Does NOT enable auto-merge — only ships the mechanism + the policy + the ratification
- Does not change the 6-tier lattice from PR2
- Does not change verifier claim taxonomy from PR1
- No auto-merge for causal / procedure / security-posture / complete-set-critical claim classes — ever, in this rollout
- No cross-repo canary state (per-repo canary config only)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Canary CAN NOT be enabled without: (a) PR5a shipped, (b) 30d of measured data, (c) all threshold checks green, (d) operator confirmation on the CLI prompt.
- Enable action logged loud: telemetry event {component=canary, event=enable, classes, enabled_by, thresholds_at_enable_time, git_commit} → append-only .xtrm/state/service-knowledge/canary.jsonl
- Disable action equally loud + preserves history
- Reconcile.py canary read must fail closed: if config file unreadable or invalid, treat as canary=off (no auto-merge). Never fail open on canary check.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] docs/devops/service-knowledge-canary.md landed + operator-ratified (operator sign-off recorded in bd notes)
- [ ] `service-knowledge canary status` returns valid JSON with metric snapshot + threshold status
- [ ] `service-knowledge canary enable` refuses when thresholds not met (fixture with fake bad metrics)
- [ ] `service-knowledge canary enable` succeeds when thresholds met + operator confirms
- [ ] reconcile.py smoke: canary=on + PASS + all claims in enabled classes → atomic_write + auto-merge
- [ ] reconcile.py smoke: canary=on + PASS + at least one claim outside enabled classes → atomic_write + NORMAL PR (no auto-merge)
- [ ] reconcile.py smoke: canary=off + PASS → normal PR (no auto-merge)
- [ ] Fail-closed test: canary config file corrupted → reconcile.py treats as off
- [ ] Telemetry: grep 'component=canary' finds enable/disable events with full context

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse: reconcile.py atomic_write branch, service-knowledge CLI framework, PR5a telemetry format
- Installed deps: none new
- Stdlib: json, pathlib
- Roll it: canary logic is ~150 LOC

## OUTPUT

- docs/devops/service-knowledge-canary.md (the policy)
- src/service_knowledge/canary/ module
- CLI subcommand tree
- reconcile.py canary-read diff
- Operator ratification recorded in bd notes at close
- Package version v0.7.0

## APPROACH NOTES

- Dispatch: sp run executor --bead xtrm-56flm.7 --worktree.
- Parallelization: blocked-by PR5a (needs the measurement baseline). Runs in wave-4 alongside PR5a's tail.
- The 'canary enable' is deliberately behind an operator confirmation prompt in the CLI — no CI-only path to flip auto-merge. If operator wants CI-only enable, that's a separate follow-up bead requiring explicit trust-boundary review.
- v1.0.0 is reserved for the canary-enable moment. That is: when the operator actually flips the switch on the first low-risk claim class, cut v1.0.0 with a loud CHANGELOG entry.
- If the eval corpus (PR5a) does not converge on the thresholds within 30d, the policy stays 'canary disabled' — no pressure to relax thresholds to hit them. Auto-merge is not the goal; safety is.

title: xt version --check-updates: detect outdated xtrm-tools + xtmux + specialists
description:
## PROBLEM
Operators and agents currently have no in-band way to check whether the installed xtrm trio is stale. Top-files DOC-04 addition (fold-in on xtrm-wiy5n.3.9) tells agents to "check for newer versions" but there's no dedicated command — falls back to raw `npm outdated -g` which mixes xtrm packages with unrelated globals.

## SUCCESS
`xt version --check-updates` queries npm for `xtrm-tools`, `@jaggerxtrm/xtmux`, `@jaggerxtrm/specialists` latest versions, compares against installed, and prints a compact 3-row status. `xt doctor` gains an "updates" diagnostic row calling the same check. Both cache results ~24h so agents can call freely without rate-hitting the npm registry.

## SCOPE
- `cli/src/commands/version.ts` (or wherever `xt version` lives) — add `--check-updates` flag
- `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts` — add "updates" check row
- Optional: shared helper `cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts` (fetch + cache)
- Package.json script entry if desired

## NON_GOALS
- Auto-upgrading anything
- A dashboard UI
- Per-consumer telemetry
- Checking non-xtrm packages

## CONSTRAINTS
- Fetch via `npm view <pkg> version --json` (already installed on any node env)
- Cache result at `~/.xtrm/cache/npm-latest.json` with per-package TTL of 24h
- Ponytail: ~30 lines total; no HTTP client library; no new dep
- Never fail the command on npm unreachable — emit `unknown` and continue
- Compact output: 3 rows, `<pkg>  installed=<v>  latest=<v>  [ok|stale]`

## VALIDATION
- [ ] `xt version --check-updates` prints 3 rows in a fresh env
- [ ] Second invocation within 24h uses cache (no npm call — verify with strace or `--no-cache` fallback)
- [ ] `xt doctor` shows "updates" row summarizing any stale packages
- [ ] `xt version --check-updates --json` yields structured output
- [ ] npm unreachable → `latest=unknown`, exit 0 (does not break agent workflows)
- [ ] `xt version --check-updates --no-cache` forces fresh fetch

## OUTPUT
PR link + sample output showing 1 stale package + cache-file path shown to operator.
notes:
PR core#524 open, 0 unresolved threads, all scans green. Waiting on a branch update after #523 merged.

WHAT SHIPPED
  cli/src/utils/npm-latest.ts   shared fetch + cache, 24h TTL, cache at ~/.xtrm/cache/npm-latest.json
  cli/src/commands/version.ts   --check-updates, one compact row per package
  cli/src/commands/doctor.ts    an 'updates' row calling the SAME helper
  11 tests across npm-latest.test.ts and version-command.test.ts

THE THREE DESIGN POINTS I DEMANDED ARE ALL COVERED BY NAMED TESTS
  no network + no cache        -> state=unknown, does not throw, does not write cache
  no network + expired cache   -> shows the cached latest as information, but state STAYS unknown
                                  and never asserts unverified freshness
  dangling / unreadable global -> state=not-installed, does not throw
  corrupt cache file           -> treated as empty, no throw, overwritten on the next success

LIVE PROOF ON THIS HOST — it handles the exact broken install I warned about
  node cli/dist/index.cjs version --check-updates
    xtrm-tools               installed=not-installed  latest=0.11.2  [not-installed]
    @jaggerxtrm/xtmux        installed=0.2.2          latest=0.2.2   [ok]
    @jaggerxtrm/specialists  installed=3.21.1         latest=3.21.1  [ok]
    cache: /home/dawid/.xtrm/cache/npm-latest.json

'not-installed' for xtrm-tools is CORRECT here: the global xtrm-tools is a dangling npm link to a
worktree that no longer exists. The command reports it instead of throwing.

BASE HANDLING WORTH NOTING: main advanced with #520 mid-PR. The worker MERGED rather than rebased,
to avoid the history rewrite its brief forbids, and rebuilt the tracked dist to resolve the bundle
conflict. That is the behaviour bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.12 was written to produce, and it appeared on
the first PR after that policy merged.
close_reason: Merged as core#524. xt version --check-updates and a doctor row share one helper with a 24h cache. 11 tests cover the no-network, expired-cache, dangling-install and corrupt-cache paths. Live run on this host correctly reports the dangling global xtrm-tools as not-installed instead of throwing.

title: PR5a: eval corpus + telemetry dashboards + alert-to-service routing
description:
## PROBLEM

PR0-4 ship package + verifier + gate + index + dispatch integration. Without measurement, we cannot answer: does the verifier catch what it should? Is retrieval precision high enough? What's the stale-claim escape rate? Are agents actually consuming bundles?

Research §3.9 mandates a labeled eval corpus (80-150 cases from real closed issues / merged PRs / real alerts / incidents / drift history / diagnostic tasks) with a specific metric set. Research §3.7 requires retrieval telemetry (retrieval_events table) for ignored-activation rate, citation utilization rate, stale-claim escape rate. PR3 declared the table; this PR populates it with hooks and dashboards.

**Ponytail split**: canary policy for future auto-merge is a decision doc, not code. Split into PR5b — unblocks separately when operator ratifies thresholds. This PR (PR5a) is shovel-ready measurement + alert-to-service surface.

## SUCCESS

- Labeled eval corpus at ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/eval/corpus/ with 80-150 cases across: closed bd issues (bug + feature), merged PRs with operational changes, real Prometheus alerts (from mercury-infra history), incident reports, drift history, diagnostic tasks, past questions that produced wrong commands or claims.
- Each case labeled per §3.9: query_or_task, touched_paths, expected_services, required_evidence, forbidden_evidence, expected_probes, cross_repo_required, outcome.
- Eval harness runs the corpus against the shipped system and emits the 12 metrics from §3.9.
- Retrieval telemetry hooks emit to retrieval_events (PR3 table) on every knowledge_search/_get/_evidence_for_files call + on every activator invocation.
- Weekly report at .beads/eval-reports/YYYY-WW.md (raw values, week-over-week delta, threshold status green/yellow/red, corpus expansion suggestions).
- Alert-to-service routing tool (new small MCP wrapper): incident_routing takes an Alertmanager-shaped payload → knowledge_search → returns top-K service + runbook probes → evidence bundle. Advisory only.
- Post-merge reindex hook completes on mercury-infra + any other consumer that has installed (from operator-triggered wave-2 installs) within the 60s budget from PR3.

## SCOPE

- NEW: src/service_knowledge/eval/
  - corpus/*.json — labeled cases
  - harness.py — runs the corpus, computes metrics
  - metrics.py — metric definitions + aggregation
  - reports/  — output artifacts
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/index/query.py — telemetry emission on every query (PR3 declared the table; this PR populates it)
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/scripts/skill_activator.py — telemetry on inject + block + override decisions (from PR4)
- EXTEND: src/service_knowledge/scripts/verifier/ — FP/FN accounting hooks on golden-fixture runs
- NEW: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/.github/workflows/eval-weekly.yml — cron running eval harness, publishing report as artifact + sticky-commenting summary on a tracking issue
- NEW: src/service_knowledge/mcp/incident_routing.py — thin wrapper over knowledge_search with alert-shape input
- Post-merge reindex wiring for mercury-infra + wave-2 consumers (extend PR3's hook or add if not wired)

## NON_GOALS

- No auto-merge ENABLE in this PR — canary policy is PR5b
- No embedding/vector rollout (metrics might trigger it — follow-up)
- No cross-repo aggregation switch (metrics might trigger it — follow-up)
- No new claim types in verifier (that's a PR1 follow-up if telemetry demands)
- No new MCP tools beyond incident_routing wrapper
- No security-auditor pipeline changes
- No operator dashboard UI beyond CSV/Markdown reports + optional Grafana panels

## CONSTRAINTS

- Eval corpus MUST include the 3 regression cases from the observed api-gateway/runners specialist failure
- Corpus cases MUST have permalinks to source artifacts (bd IDs, PR numbers, alert IDs, incident report paths)
- Metric definitions match §3.9 exactly — same names, same semantics
- Telemetry payloads: no PII, no raw query text (hash instead), no secret values per PR3 constraint

title: Bare Alpine install-process investigation: full runtime bootstrap + broad tests
description:
## PROBLEM

Install-order regressions surface late — usually at release time or on operators' fresh machines. The existing `fresh-machine-smoke.yml` runs on GH Actions ubuntu-latest which ships with Node, npm, python, curl, and dozens of other tools already. That masks bootstrap steps that would fail on a truly bare system. We have no reproducible harness that starts from "nothing but the OS image" and lands at "xt / sp / pi all functional, tests pass". Alpine is a good stress case because it's small, uses musl (not glibc), and lacks most preinstalled tooling.

## SUCCESS

Reproducible harness that:
1. Starts from `alpine:latest` (or a pinned tag) with nothing but base + apk
2. Installs the full runtime stack step by step, capturing every failure mode: system deps (bash, git, curl, python3, build-base for native compiles) → Node LTS via nvm or Alpine's own node package → bun (for `sp` which shebangs `bun`) → optionally rust for git-cliff if any repo still resolves it via cargo → pi (`@mariozechner/pi-coding-agent` or the fork we ship) → claude (the Claude Code CLI) → beads binary → xtrm-tools (`xt`) via npm global → specialists via `sp init`
3. Runs a broad smoke matrix: `xt init -y`, `xt doctor --json`, `xt update --apply`, `sp init`, `sp doctor`, `sp list`, `sp render-bead`, `pi --version`, `claude --version`, at least one xtmux command (`xtmux picker --dry-run`), and the workflows (a dry-run `xrm-release` and `xtrm-merge-fifo` at least).
4. Emits a diagnostic report (which step failed, what package was missing, exit code, tail of output) — should be trivially readable for someone triaging.
5. Runs in CI as a matrix leg alongside the existing ubuntu-latest smoke — not replacing it.

## SCOPE

- `.docker/alpine-install-smoke/` (new dir): Dockerfile + entrypoint script + expected-outcomes fixture + docs
- `.github/workflows/alpine-install-smoke.yml` (new): workflow_dispatch + optional pull_request trigger scoped to installer-surface changes (mirror `xtrm-xnf7g` selectivity)
- Docs: `docs/alpine-smoke.md` explaining the harness + how to run locally (`docker run` one-liner)
- Update `docs/release.md` §3 pre-flight section to include the alpine smoke

## NON_GOALS

- Not a full production runtime (musl + Alpine has real caveats — e.g., `@beads/bd` prebuilt binaries may not have musl variants). If a step is fundamentally not-alpine-compatible, document it as such rather than working around it.
- Not replacing ubuntu-latest fresh-machine-smoke — this is complementary.
- Not fixing every failure the harness surfaces — first pass just captures them.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Container must start from a bare Alpine image, no pre-built xtrm-tools image
- Every install command logged with stdout+stderr + exit code
- Report must be machine-readable JSON alongside human-readable log
- Reproducible: two identical runs produce identical reports modulo timestamps
- CI leg allowed to fail (surface findings without blocking release cadence) initially

## VALIDATION

- Local: `docker run --rm -v $PWD:/repo alpine-smoke-image` produces a report
- CI: workflow triggered on demand + on installer-surface PRs, uploads artifacts
- First run generates a real punch-list of things that don't work on musl / Alpine
- Report format is stable enough to diff run-over-run (regression detection)

## OUTPUT

Working Dockerfile + workflow + docs + initial punch-list report as artifacts of the first CI run. Follow-up beads filed for each real bug found.

## REFERENCES

- `docs/release.md` §3 (existing fresh-machine-smoke path)
- `.github/workflows/fresh-machine-smoke.yml` (the ubuntu-latest baseline)
- `.github/workflows/install-order-matrix.yml` (workflow_dispatch-only regression harness)
- `xtrm-5k0o` family (PATH cache bootstrap issues — likely relevant)
- `xtrm-xnf7g` (installer-surface PR gate — model for selective triggering)

title: xtmux release.yml: migrate to npm Trusted Publishing (OIDC, no NPM_TOKEN)
description:
## PROBLEM
NPM_TOKEN in Jaggerxtrm/xtmux repo 401s in CI despite proper env wiring. Root cause hypothesis: classic automation token (bypass 2FA) restricted by npm. Trusted Publishing solves this by removing the token entirely.

## SUCCESS
release.yml uses OIDC (id-token: write already granted) — no NPM_TOKEN secret, no NODE_AUTH_TOKEN env, no registry-url in setup-node. npm publish --access public --provenance authenticates via GitHub Actions OIDC. Provenance is automatic.

## SCOPE
- Operator: npmjs.com → @jaggerxtrm/xtmux → Settings → Publishing → add GitHub Actions trusted publisher (Jaggerxtrm/xtmux repo, workflow release.yml)
- PR against xtmux: strip NPM_TOKEN wiring from release.yml

## VALIDATION
Cut v0.2.2 patch via workflow. release.yml publishes without token. npm view shows 0.2.2 with attestations.

## NON_GOALS
Migrating Core or Specialists (operator kept those on current paths).

## OUTPUT
PR against xtmux; updated release.yml. Operator confirms npm trusted publisher configured. v0.2.2 smoke.
close_reason: @jaggerxtrm/xtmux@0.2.2 published via trusted publishing with provenance attestation. release.yml auth path proven. Follow-up: release_execute.py or release.yml should coordinate on gh release create (currently both do it — release.yml step is redundant/errors when release_execute ran first).

title: Phase 2: YAML DAG wiring for xtrm-release + archon validate clean
description:
## PROBLEM

Phase 1 scripts done, self-tested + live-proven. Need Archon DAG YAML that wires them into the sequenced (Specialists → Core with revendor → xtmux) release flow with double-gated mutations, per-repo when:-branches, dry-run everywhere.

## SUCCESS

~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-release.yaml exists. `archon validate workflows xtrm-release` from a git repo cwd emits 0 warnings/errors. Full dry-run end-to-end (no ARCHON_ALLOW_RELEASE=1) completes anyFailed:false and routes cleanly through classify → synthesize → approval (reply 'dry-run all') → per-repo dry-run branches → verify.

## SCOPE

Only ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-release.yaml. Do NOT touch scripts unless a bug is exposed. Do NOT touch repos. Do NOT run a live release.

## AUTHORITATIVE REFERENCES

- ~/.archon/state/xtrm-release-phase0-audit.md (Phase 0 findings)
- Phase 1 script signatures + JSON schemas (read the scripts you just wrote at ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/release_*.py — their stdin/stdout/env contracts are load-bearing)
- Exemplar 1: ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/sre-triage-v2.yaml (deterministic-verdict + operator-directed-routing pattern)
- Exemplar 2: ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-merge-fifo.yaml (env-guard + operator-approval + when:-gated mutation stages)

## CONSTRAINTS

- provider: pi, worktree.enabled: false
- Deterministic core: no LLM decides gate/verdict; prompt nodes ADVISORY only with output_format schema + allowed_tools: []
- Every mutation gated twice: ARCHON_ALLOW_RELEASE=1 AND operator-approval
- Executor re-derives eligibility at run time
- No autonomous action nodes (auto-* are REPORT-ONLY, never side effects)
- Cross-repo order fixed: specialists → (revendor-core) → core → xtmux
- Each stage has BOTH a dry-run branch and a live branch, when:-gated
- prompt-node bash substitutions ($node.output) already shell-quoted by Archon — do NOT wrap
- approval.capture_response: true for operator directive parsing
- Route-decision node parses operator reply grammar: "dry-run all" | "release: core minor, specialists patch, xtmux skip" | "release: core minor v0.12.0" | "abort"

## DAG SHAPE

env-guard → repo-inventory → per-repo-scan → binding-check → preflight-gates → classify → synthesize (advisory) → operator-approval (capture) → route-decision
  → dry-run-specialists  when: route.specialists.dry_run == true
  → execute-specialists  when: env-guard.merge_allowed && route.specialists.action == "release"
  → wait-specialists-published (npm view poll)
  → revendor-core        when: specialists just released OR binding.core_pin_drifted
  → dry-run-core / execute-core (with release-PR flow: create branch, push, PR, wait CI, merge, tag, gh release create)
  → wait-core-published (gh run watch --exit-status publish.yml)
  → dry-run-xtmux / execute-xtmux
  → wait-xtmux-published (gh run watch --exit-status release.yml)
  → verify-post-release (release_verify.py)

## VALIDATION

- archon validate workflows xtrm-release: 0 warnings, 0 errors
- Full dry-run E2E: cd ~/dev/core && archon workflow run xtrm-release --no-worktree "dry-run smoke"; approve with "dry-run all"; anyFailed:false; per-repo dry-run outputs written to ~/.archon/state/
- Route-decision unit test: bash the parser against 4 canonical replies (dry-run all / release: core minor / abort / bare approve)
- README/notes explaining operator directive grammar and gate ordering

## OUTPUT

- YAML at ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-release.yaml
- Validation output pasted in bead notes
- Dry-run run-id + summary in bead notes

## APPROACH NOTES

- Read both exemplar YAMLs FIRST end-to-end — the safety patterns aren't summarizable
- Reuse the ARCHON_ALLOW_MERGE workaround pattern for env-pass regression IF you hit it during execute-* (see /home/dawid/.archon/state and my post-compact-brief.md)
- The env-guard node output must be: {"merge_allowed": true|false}; route-decision must parse operator reply into per-repo actions
- Use timeout: on nodes doing gh api / npm view / gh run watch
- Publish workflow polling: gh run list --workflow=<name> --limit=1 --json databaseId,status,conclusion to grab run-id, then gh run watch --exit-status
- Specialists post-tag: workflow ends with instruction to operator to run `npm publish --access public` locally (report-only prompt in verify stage)
notes:
Phase 2 YAML at ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-release.yaml (523 lines, 22 nodes).

archon validate workflows xtrm-release: 1 valid, 0 with errors, 0 warnings.

Full dry-run smoke: run-id 82fec96b06a266dc69b5f17c14ffdd5f, anyFailed:false.
  cd ~/dev/core && archon workflow run xtrm-release --no-worktree "dry-run smoke phase 2 v4"
  archon workflow approve <run-id> "dry-run all"
  Node results:
    env-guard, repo-inventory, per-repo-scan, binding-check, preflight-gates,

    route-decision                              Completed (115 ms)  mode=dry-run
    dry-run-specialists                         Completed (341 ms)  v3.21.0 -> v3.21.1
    dry-run-core                                Completed (356 ms)  v0.11.1 -> v0.11.2 (BLOCKED but plan rendered)
    dry-run-xtmux                               Completed (559 ms)  BLOCKED but plan rendered

Route-decision parser unit test (7/7 pass) — canonical replies from the bead
plus 3 edge cases:
  "dry-run all"                    -> mode=dry-run, all repos dry-run
  "release: core minor"            -> mode=release, core release+minor, others skip
  "release: core minor v0.12.0"    -> mode=release, core release+minor v0.12.0, others skip

BEAD CONSTRAINTS COMPLIANCE
  provider: pi, worktree.enabled: false                                       yes
  Deterministic core; prompt-node advisory-only, allowed_tools:[], schema     yes (synthesize)
  Double-gated mutations: ARCHON_ALLOW_RELEASE=1 + operator-approval          yes (guard-off downgrades release->dry-run; approval names repos)
  No autonomous actions                                                       yes (no execute path fires without operator approval + guard)
  Cross-repo order: specialists -> revendor -> core -> xtmux                  yes (depends_on chains + revendor-decision node)
  Each stage has dry-run branch + live branch, when:-gated                    yes (dry-run-* / execute-* pairs)
  Route-decision parses reply into per-repo action map                        yes (parser unit test passing)
  prompt-node $node.output substitutions unquoted                             yes

DAG SHAPE (22 nodes):
  env-guard -> repo-inventory -> per-repo-scan -> binding-check -> preflight-gates
    -> classify -> synthesize -> operator-approval -> route-decision
    -> [dry-run-specialists | execute-specialists]
    -> wait-specialists-published (execute-branch only)
    -> revendor-decision -> [dry-run-revendor-core | execute-revendor-core]
    -> [dry-run-core | execute-core] -> wait-core-published (execute-branch only)
    -> [dry-run-xtmux | execute-xtmux] -> wait-xtmux-published (execute-branch only)
    -> verify-post-release (trigger_rule: none_failed_min_one_success)

CI-PUBLISH POLLING
  wait-core-published:  gh run list --workflow=publish.yml --limit=1 --json databaseId
                        -> gh run watch <run-id> --exit-status  (30 min timeout)
  wait-xtmux-published: same shape, --workflow=release.yml
  wait-specialists-published: npm view @jaggerxtrm/specialists version poll (10 min)
                              (Specialists uses local publish per Phase 0 audit Q1)

PHASE 1 SCRIPT BUG FIXED IN-FLIGHT (flagged per brief instruction)
  release_execute.py --dry-run used to hard-fail when classifier verdict != READY.
  That defeats the "dry-run all" smoke on BLOCKED repos, which is exactly when
  an operator most wants to see what WOULD happen. Fix: --dry-run now emits the
  full plan and attaches the classifier verdict to the payload; live mode still
  refuses. 9/9 self-tests still pass; the DAG dry-run smoke now completes
  end-to-end. This was the only script edit; no other Phase 1 script touched.

DEVELOPMENT PATH (surfaced Archon-workflow gotchas for future authors):
  1. Archon 'env:' block on bash nodes doesn't substitute $node.output —
     produced KeyError at runtime. Fix: use inline positional args like
     'python3 - $node.output $other.output <<PY' (mirrors sre-triage-v2).
  2. Archon 'when:' expressions only accept ONE hop after .output —
     $node.output.field works, $node.output.a.b silently drops as
     dag_node_skipped_condition_parse_error. Fix: route-decision emits a FLAT
     schema (specialists_action / core_bump / ...) not a nested one.
  3. verify-post-release fanning in from mutually-exclusive branches needs
     trigger_rule: none_failed_min_one_success or it silently skips itself.

description:

## SUCCESS

7 scripts under ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/ implementing release_scan.py, release_binding_check.py, release_preflight.py, release_classify.py, release_execute.py, release_revendor.py, release_verify.py. Each has --self-test passing. release_scan/binding/preflight/classify runs LIVE against all 3 repos and produces sensible JSON.

## SCOPE

Only scripts under ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/. No YAML. No workflow validation. No editing repos.

## AUTHORITATIVE REFERENCES

- ~/.archon/state/xtrm-release-phase0-audit.md (LOAD FIRST — decisions + constraints)
- ~/.xtrm/skills/default/releasing/SKILL.md (mental model)
- ~/dev/core/docs/release.md (release contract)
- Exemplars: ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/{sre_probe,sre_classify,sre_escalate,merge_fifo_preflight,merge_fifo_execute}.py

## CONSTRAINTS

- Deterministic core; NO LLM in scripts
- Read-only default; release_execute.py has BOTH env guard ARCHON_ALLOW_RELEASE=1 AND --dry-run mode
- Executor re-derives eligibility at execute time (don't trust upstream output)
- Uniform release-PR flow for ALL 3 repos: release-vX.Y.Z branch off publish branch → commits → push → PR → wait CI → merge → fetch → tag → gh release create
- xtmux publish model: NPM_TOKEN + provenance (matching Core)
- Preflight refuses when: dirty publish branch, unpushed commits ahead, wrong branch, orphan tag detected
- Post-tag: Core+xtmux gh run watch --exit-status the publish workflow; Specialists reports "run npm publish locally"
- Orphan tag detection: tag exists on origin but npm view returns 404 — surface as WARN not BLOCKER (needs manual unstick)
- Cross-repo ordering fixed: Specialists → Core (with revendor between) → xtmux
- .xtrm/skills/state.json + .specialists/user + sqlite -wal/-shm + .beads/interactions.jsonl are ephemeral — filter out of dirty check (see orch_hygiene.py EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS constant)

## VALIDATION

- All 6 --self-test invocations pass
- release_scan.py --repo ~/dev/core --repo ~/dev/specialists --repo ~/dev/xtmux emits valid JSON with per-repo fields
- release_binding_check.py detects: current specialists-source.json pin vs specialists master, runtime-compatibility.json window vs installed
- release_classify.py against current state emits: Core=SKIP (no commits since v0.11.1), Specialists=SKIP (post-release drift check), xtmux=BLOCKED (never published + no NPM_TOKEN)
- release_preflight.py flags xtmux dirty tree (5 known dirty files in main WIP)

## OUTPUT

Bead notes: paths of all 7 scripts, output of each --self-test, output of live scan on all 3 repos.

## APPROACH NOTES

Read the audit report FIRST. Every constraint there is load-bearing. Preserve exit codes, JSON schemas, and env-var conventions from the SRE exemplars — the YAML that consumes these scripts follows those conventions.
notes:
Phase 1 scripts landed at ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/:
  - _release_common.py       (shared repo registry, semver, ephemeral filter, git/npm helpers)
  - release_scan.py          (per-repo state, --skip-network mode)
  - release_binding_check.py (specialists-pin drift + runtime-compat range check)
  - release_preflight.py     (branch/dirty/ahead/behind + orphan-tag WARN)
  - release_classify.py      (SKIP/READY/BLOCKED/UNKNOWN verdicts; xtmux gates)
  - release_revendor.py      (vendor-specialists-skills.mjs --specialists-ref + verify)
  - release_execute.py       (ONLY mutating; ARCHON_ALLOW_RELEASE=1 AND --dry-run gates)
  - release_verify.py        (post-tag tag+npm cross-check; orphan → WARN)

SELF-TESTS — all 44 pass:
  scan 6/6  binding 8/8  preflight 2/2  classify 9/9  execute 9/9  revendor 5/5  verify 5/5

LIVE against 3 repos:
  SCAN:  specialists tag=v3.21.0 commits=6 clean, on master, [Unreleased]=yes.
         core        tag=v0.11.1 commits=28 dirty_ne=1 (?? .xtrm/skills/default/xtrm-workflow-authoring/), on main.
         xtmux       tag=v0.2.0  commits=0  dirty_ne=3 (AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .beads/interactions.jsonl), on main.
  BINDING: specialists-pin=DRIFT (v3.21.0 sha vs specialists master head — 6 new commits).
           runtime-compat=BREACH (xtmux 0.2.0 outside declared >=0.1.0 <0.2 range).
  PREFLIGHT (skip-network): go_status=NO_GO. specialists=GO. core=NO_GO (1 dirty). xtmux=NO_GO (3 dirty).
  CLASSIFY: specialists=READY (6 commits since v3.21.0).
            core=BLOCKED (1 non-ephemeral dirty).
            xtmux=BLOCKED (CI publish model no XTMUX_HAS_NPM_TOKEN; half-released tag v0.2.0 npm 404).
  EXECUTE --dry-run (specialists patch): 3.21.0 → 3.21.1 → tag v3.21.1 → branch release-v3.21.1.
    Steps: checkout_new_branch → promote_changelog → bump_package_json → git_add → commit → push
           → pr_create → pr_wait_merge → fetch → tag → push_tag → gh_release.
    publish_model=local, next_step="npm publish --access public locally".

  Audit expected Core=SKIP and Specialists=SKIP. Since audit time 28 commits landed on
  Core and 6 on Specialists; classifier correctly reports both as READY (Core would be
  READY once the untracked file is dealt with). xtmux remains BLOCKED as audited.

DESIGN CHOICE surfaced during live scan:
  latest_semver_tag() prefers the tag matching package.json version, falling back to
  most-recent-by-creator-date among semver-shaped tags. Without this, Core's legacy
  v5.1.0 initial-commit tag (Jan 2026) would eclipse the real release lineage v0.11.1.

WORKFLOW-CONTRACT COMPLIANCE:
  exit 0 success + JSON stdout · exit 1 gate NO_GO · exit 2 argv misuse · --self-test
  per script · executor re-derives eligibility · ephemeral files filtered (5 canonical
  entries mirroring orch_hygiene.EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS) · orphan tag = WARN not BLOCKER
  · fixed ordering encoded in DEFAULT_REPOS: specialists(1) → core(2, revendor between) → xtmux(3).

title: xtrm-release: Archon workflow for cross-repo (Specialists → Core → xtmux) release orchestration
description:
## PROBLEM

Cutting a release across the three repos is manual per-repo: /releasing skill covers one repo at a time. Cross-repo binding (specialists asset-contract → Core re-vendor → Core publish) is enforced by docs but not machine-checked. Real risks: forgetting to re-vendor Core after Specialists releases, or bumping a compat floor without shipping the sibling first, or pushing an unclean tree.

## SUCCESS

Operator runs `archon workflow run xtrm-release "…"` — workflow detects which of the 3 repos need release, verifies dirty state / unpushed / release-PR readiness, asks minor/patch, then in fixed order (Specialists → Core with re-vendor → xtmux) drives every step deterministically through git push + GitHub Release, with publish.yml/local-publish handling the actual npm publish. Dry-run mode exercises the full chain without mutations.

## SCOPE

- ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-release.yaml (new DAG)
- ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/release_scan.py + release_binding_check.py + release_preflight.py + release_classify.py + release_execute.py + release_revendor.py + release_verify.py (all with --self-test)
- Skill delta: ~/.xtrm/skills/default/releasing/SKILL.md — Mechanized flow section
- xtmux publish config alignment (separate child bead)
- Optional: audit doc capturing Phase 0 findings

## NON_GOALS

- Auto-rollback (destructive — manual per skill rules)
- npm publish from Archon (publish.yml + local-npm-publish per repo already work)
- Rewriting specialists' local-publish model
- install-order-matrix invocation (operator triggers out-of-band)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Deterministic core + LLM-advisory-only per xtrm-workflow-authoring skill
- ARCHON_ALLOW_RELEASE=1 required for any execute-* branch
- Executor re-derives eligibility at execute time
- worktree.enabled: false — release must be in operator's working tree
- Release-branch/release-PR pattern enforced (dirty-state gate); the workflow refuses to release from a dirty tree or from a tree with unpushed commits ahead of upstream
- xtmux MUST have a clear+matching npm publish config before its execute branch can go live (either mirror specialists local-publish OR wire NPM_TOKEN)

## VALIDATION

- Phase 0 audit report captures the 5+ open questions with answers
- Every script's --self-test passes
- Dry-run against all 3 repos completes with anyFailed:false
- Live release drives one real Specialists patch bump end-to-end (test-vetted)
- archon validate workflows xtrm-release → 0 warnings

## OUTPUT

Working DAG + scripts + updated /releasing skill + Phase 0 audit report as .md
notes:

Live releases via release_execute.py:

Bugs found + fixed IN-FLIGHT during smoke:

- git wrapper timeout 60s too tight for post-checkout hooks. Bumped to 180s.

- EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS expanded: + AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .wolf/

title: orch_hygiene: classify delivered-worker-prunable so PostToolUse hook surfaces them before dispatch
description:
## PROBLEM

Today four wave workers (8a, 8b, 9, 10) sat with delivered PRs merged and idle sessions, and orch_hygiene never surfaced them because its stale threshold is 30 days and they were <1 day old. Only manual `xtmux audit` inspection caught them. The 'clean git before dispatches' workflow the operator wants requires these to be surfaced BEFORE the next dispatch by the automated PostToolUse/systemd path — not from a human running the picker.

## SUCCESS

`orch_hygiene.py` classifies a fresh worktree as 'delivered-worker-prunable' when: all commits landed upstream (cherry summary unlanded==0) AND dirty count (excluding ephemeral regenerable files) is 0. A new bucket + total surfaces this alongside stale_safe_to_prune. No behavior change for recent-active worktrees with real dirty state.

## SCOPE

Single-file edit: ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/orch_hygiene.py

## NON_GOALS

- xtmux audit classifier change (separate PR against ~/dev/xtmux if desired later)
- Actual mutating cleanup workflow (still operator-approved manual step; this bead only fixes the SIGNAL)

## CONSTRAINTS

- No new dependencies
- Ephemeral file list must be documented as a module constant
- Non-destructive: worktrees still not touched by this script

## VALIDATION

- Manual: run against ~/dev/core after next merge — new bucket exists and includes wave-11 delivery once it lands
- Field 'ephemeral_dirty' present on each recent entry so operator can see what was filtered

## OUTPUT

Diff of orch_hygiene.py; sample JSON output showing new bucket.
notes:
IMPLEMENTATION

Files touched:
- ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/orch_hygiene.py: added EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS constant + _strip_ephemeral() + delivered_worker_prunable bucket in scan_repo() + entry in totals + per-entry {real_dirty_count, real_dirty_sample, ephemeral_dirty_count}
- ~/.xtrm/skills/default/xtrm-checks/SKILL.md: R2 references the new bucket

Classifier logic:
- Fresh worktree (age < recent_days)
- unlanded_commits == 0 (all commits landed upstream via `git cherry`)
- landed_commits > 0 (branch actually delivered something, not empty)
- real_dirty (post-ephemeral filter) == 0

VALIDATION

Real run against ~/dev/core surfaced 3 previously-invisible delivered-prunable worktrees:
- core-xt-claude-revert-perm-defaults (branch xt/revert-perm-defaults, landed=1)
- core-xt-pi-latency-recovery (branch xt/latency-recovery, landed=1)
- core-xt-pi-r6g-w2-core (branch xt/r6g-w2-core, landed=1)

Not mine — left untouched per operator hygiene rule.

Wave 11 active worktree correctly stayed in `recent` (real_dirty=1, real WIP).

DELIVERABLE

Script edit is live — next PostToolUse hook run + systemd timer fires will surface the new bucket. No PR needed (~/.archon/ is not under git repo control; operator dotfiles).
close_reason: orch_hygiene.py extended with delivered_worker_prunable bucket + ephemeral-file filter; xtrm-checks skill R2 updated. Verified live: surfaced 3 previously-invisible prunable worktrees in core. No PR needed — ~/.archon and ~/.xtrm/skills are operator dotfiles, not repo-controlled.

title: Suite A: assert the user-owned skill location contract across xt update --apply
description:
## PROBLEM

xtrm-kvsrd.4 established that user-owned skill survival across
`xt update --apply` is a LOCATION contract, not a marker. Suite A step 20
currently only OBSERVEs the negative half (a skill dropped into the managed
default tree is pruned) and has no assertion for the positive half, so a
regression that started eating optional/ or foreign runtime entries would pass.

## SCOPE

Integration suite (Suite A) + docs/skills-ownership.md.

## ASSERTIONS TO ADD

Positive (must SURVIVE `xt update --apply`):
[ ] a skill under `~/.xtrm/skills/optional/<pack>/`
[ ] a real directory at `.claude/skills/<name>` not present in managedLinks
[ ] a runtime-view symlink pointing OUTSIDE the managed roots
[ ] a `.claude/skills` runtime dir that is itself a symlink (must refuse with
    "Refusing to replace user-owned runtime directory")

Negative (must be PRUNED / refused):
[ ] a skill under `~/.xtrm/skills/default/<name>` not in the registry manifest
    is removed (current step 20 behavior — keep, but assert rather than observe)
[ ] a real dir in `.claude/skills/<name>` colliding with a MANAGED skill name
    makes reconcile fail loudly with "is user-owned", not overwrite

## DOCS

Document the contract where operators will find it (docs/skills-ownership.md):
`default/` is registry-owned and delete-on-update; `optional/`, project packs,
and foreign runtime entries are preserved. This is the gap that surprised
Suite A — the behavior is correct, the documentation is absent.

## REFERENCES

- Contract derivation with line refs: xtrm-kvsrd.4 notes.
- Enforcement: registry-scaffold.ts:188 pruneRetiredManagedSkills;
  skills-runtime-reconcile.ts:84/:157-167/:176/:185.
close_reason: Suite A step 20b/20c now assert the location contract (project runtime entry + outside-root symlink preserved, non-manifest default/ entry pruned, ~/.claude/skills repaired). The two loud refusals got unit coverage in skills-runtime-reconcile.test.ts (they had none anywhere). docs/skills-ownership.md documents the contract. optional/ half could NOT be asserted green: copyTier wipes the tier — filed xtrm-vtqlg.8 (P1) and reported as BLOCKED in-suite.

title: ensureSkillsTreeStructure re-scaffolds retired per-repo default/optional on every skills-state write
description:
## PROBLEM

Discovered while fixing xtrm-agxxs. `cli/src/core/skills-state.ts:73-76`
`ensureSkillsTreeStructure()` unconditionally `ensureDir`s `default/` and
`optional/` under whatever skills root it is handed, and it is called from
BOTH `readSkillsState()` and `writeSkillsState()`.

Those two run against the per-repo skills root from skills-runtime-views.ts:35,
skills-runtime-reconcile.ts:194 and skills-materializer.ts:77/203 — so any repo
that touches skills state re-creates the two managed tiers that the global-SSOT
migration exists to retire. Per-repo `default/`/`optional/` are deprecated
(CLAUDE.md), yet the state layer keeps minting them.

xtrm-agxxs prunes them in `xt migrate skills`, which is durable in practice
(xtmux has state.json and no tiers), but any later skills-state write in a
migrated repo brings the empty dirs back.

## WHY THIS IS NOT PART OF xtrm-agxxs

`cli/src/tests/skills-state.test.ts:69` asserts `optional/` exists after
`writeSkillsState` on a temp root. That makes the scaffolding an intentional
current contract, not an accident — changing it is a design call touching the
install/update path, not a P3 cleanup.

## LIKELY SHAPE

Make the scaffolding scope-aware: only the GLOBAL skills root
(`resolveGlobalSkillsRoot()`) still needs its tiers, since that is where the
SSOT lives and `global-skills-bootstrap.ts:121` depends on it. Repo-scope calls
should no-op. Requires updating skills-state.test.ts to assert the new split.

## VALIDATION

[ ] Repo-scope readSkillsState/writeSkillsState creates no default/optional.
[ ] Global-scope still scaffolds both tiers; global-skills-bootstrap unaffected.
[ ] `npm test --workspace cli` green (note: run failing files in isolation —
    the full suite has load-induced timeouts unrelated to any change).
close_reason: ensureSkillsTreeStructure is scope-aware: repo scope creates only state.json, global scope still scaffolds default/+optional/. Updated 3 test files that asserted the old contract; full cli suite green (worktree-session-role flake passes in isolation).

title: Integrate Archon (YAML DAG runner) with xt-merge / xtmux / specialists coordination stack
description:
## PROBLEM

Archon (v0.6.0, YAML-DAG workflow engine) is now operational on the host and a validated FIFO PR merger draft (verified INERT without ARCHON_ALLOW_MERGE=1) has been prepared at ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-merge-fifo.yaml + scripts. Reference: /tmp/archon-merge-fifo-handoff.md.

The draft's own safety model is sound (env-guard + deterministic merge set from merge_queue.py + operator-approval + per-PR re-verify + abort-on-fail + captured SHAs for manual revert). But we already have overlapping surfaces:
- xt-merge skill: FIFO merges queued xt-worktree PRs with rebase-cascade
- xtmux: runtime identity + coordination + message-passing
- specialists (sp): bounded expert judgment
- beads: durable task state
- Operator: production GO/NO-GO

Question: which shape do we adopt for Archon, and how do the boundaries stay clean?

## SUCCESS

A written integration proposal + a validated audit-mode run + a decision on shape (invoked-tool vs replace vs specialist-embedded vs deploy-monitor-gated). No armed-merge run until (a) the queue is unblocked (blockers today: PRs 207-218, 293/294, 332/360/429) and (b) explicit operator sign-off on the shape.

## SCOPE

- Read/review ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/*.yaml + scripts, confirm safety claims.
- Run audit-mode from ~/dev/core, capture output.
- Compare against xt-merge skill: which does the rebase-cascade, which is auditable/resumable/gated, when to invoke each.
- Recommendation writeup on this bead.
- File children beads for each decision that turns into work.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT set ARCHON_ALLOW_MERGE=1 without explicit operator approval on the integration shape.
- Do NOT run archon setup (breaks Pi auth — use archon ai default pi …).
- Do NOT enable enableExtensions on Archon's embedded pi (breaks multi-node runs; safe globally).
- Do NOT duplicate xt-merge; either invoke it, replace it, or coexist with explicit boundaries.
- Do NOT put mutations in prompt: nodes; hard gates stay bash: scripts.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Operator owns production GO/NO-GO — no auto-arming.
- Read-only-first posture per bundle's docs/PRODUCTION_GUARDRAILS.md.
- Mutations must be idempotent, aborting-on-fail, with captured rollback SHAs.
- Archon = progression; xtmux = coordination; specialists = judgment; git/beads/jira = truth. Nest, don't overlap.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Audit-mode run from ~/dev/core produces evidence + advisory + NO_GO preflight (proves inert)
- [ ] Written proposal comparing invoked-tool / replace / specialist-embedded / deploy-monitor-gated shapes
- [ ] Operator decision on shape recorded in this bead
- [ ] Children beads filed for chosen shape's implementation

## OUTPUT

Recommendation writeup + audit-mode transcript + children beads.

## REFERENCES

- /tmp/archon-merge-fifo-handoff.md (12KB, self-contained handoff)
- ~/.archon/workflows/xtrm/xtrm-merge-fifo.yaml (DAG)
- ~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/merge_fifo_{preflight,execute}.py
- ~/.claude/skills/xt-merge/SKILL.md (existing surface — for comparison)
- ~/dev/archon-xtrm-local-bootstrap/**/docs/PRODUCTION_GUARDRAILS.md
- xtrm-vtqlg (audit close-out epic — SEPARATE scope, not blocked by this)
notes:
## Integration recommendation (2026-07-22, from orchestrator review of the handoff)

**Recommended shape: Archon-as-invoked-tool (option 1)**, NOT replace-xt-merge. Rationale:

1. **xt-merge already has the rebase-cascade path** the Archon draft deliberately defers (v2). That capability is real value we shouldn't lose.
2. **Archon's differentiators over xt-merge**: gated DAG + resumable + auditable persistence in ~/.archon/archon.db + human approval node + specialist judgment nodes optional. These fit CI-adjacent / post-deploy / multi-repo audit-trail use cases where xt-merge's shell-only shape is thinner.
3. **Boundary that stays clean**:
   - Operator-triggered fast FIFO merges of xt-worktree helper PRs → xt-merge (current pattern)
   - Post-deploy / scheduled / audit-required FIFO merges → Archon workflow (invoked by orchestrator or a coordinator bead)
   - Both write evidence to beads via message-send + notes
4. **Specialist embedding**: yes, but ONLY at the assess node. Use sp reviewer/overthinker for deeper per-PR judgment via existing run-specialist-readonly.sh wrapper. Do NOT let a specialist run mutations — mutations stay in the bash: execute node behind the guard.
5. **Deploy-monitor gating**: worth adopting once xtrm-deploy-observe-readonly's deploy-monitor-native lands. Merge-fifo consumes the verdict as a preflight input alongside merge_queue eligibility.

**Immediate next actions (BEFORE armed run):**

1. Prerequisite: the queue is currently BLOCKED (207-218 failing checks, 293/294 conflicts, 332/360/429 behind main). Remediation comes first:
   - Use bundled archon-resolve-conflicts on 293/294 (in audit mode from ~/dev/core)
   - Use bundled archon-smart-pr-review to triage 207-218 batch
   - Update-branch or rebase 332/360/429
2. Run audit mode from ~/dev/core: 'archon workflow run xtrm-merge-fifo --no-worktree "integration audit"'. Confirm evidence pipeline + NO_GO preflight without guard.
3. Only after (1)+(2)+operator sign-off: single armed run in a controlled window.

**Children to file (post-audit-mode + operator decision):**

- Wire orchestrator invocation: coordinator bead 'run archon xtrm-merge-fifo in armed mode' documented in xtmux/coordinator flow (small doc PR).
- Adopt xt-merge as the fast path in xt-worktree contexts (already done); document when to reach for Archon instead (docs PR).
- Optional: enhance assess node to call sp reviewer for LARGE PRs (>N lines) — needs sp integration proof, small script.
- Optional: build deploy-monitor-native prompt: node (per handoff §5) — unblocks bundle's deploy-observe workflow.

**Explicit non-recommendations (don't do these):**

- Do NOT replace xt-merge with Archon merge-fifo. Different use cases; keeping both is not duplication.
- Do NOT let the LLM (assess node) expand the merge set. Deterministic merge_queue.py stays authoritative.
- Do NOT ship a rebase-cascade variant of the Archon workflow until v2 justifies the added surface area — for now, per-PR re-verify + skip-if-conflicted is safer.

**Scheduling note**: this bead is P2 and deliberately NOT parented to the audit close-out epic (xtrm-vtqlg). Different scope; not blocked by close-out; close-out not blocked by this. Revisit when queue is unblocked (Waves 7-9 will clear some of the audit-domain PRs; dependabot batch is separate).

title: Implement aggregated viewer views over the topology projection (P2-06)
description:
## PROBLEM

Audit ~/dev/11.md:1389 (P2-06). The projection from P2-05 is machine-readable JSON; an
operator staring at a 14-pane fleet cannot read it. The audit lists the views the operator
actually needs: runtime topology, coordinator chains, specialist lineage, worktree and
branch graph, integration status, live journal feed, reply obligations, monitors and
wakes, pane preview, git diff, bead state, worktree collisions, PR evidence, deployment
evidence.

The risk this task must not fall into: reimplementing fourteen bespoke data pipelines.
Most of these are the SAME snapshot sliced differently, and several are already served by
existing commands (`xtmux dashboard`, `xtmux monitor-list`, `xtmux obligations list`,
`xtmux log query`, `xtmux pane capture`, `xt worktree audit-prs`). The viewer's job is to
render the one projection and to route to the existing owner for the streaming/diagnostic
surfaces, not to duplicate them.

## SUCCESS

`xt topology` renders the projection as operator-readable views, selected by `--view
<name>`, with a sensible default. Views that are slices of the snapshot are computed from
the snapshot. Views that are live streams or diagnostics (journal feed, pane preview) are
delegated to their owning command rather than reimplemented, and the viewer documents
that routing. No view infers completion from terminal text.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/commands/topology.ts: `--view <name>` surface + renderers.
- cli/src/core/topology-views.ts (new, if the renderers outgrow the command file).
- cli/src/tests/topology-views.test.ts (new).
- docs/ operator documentation for the command and its views.

## NON_GOALS

- Inferring completion from terminal output. A pane is "done" only per bead state, PR
  merge state, or an emitted lifecycle event. Explicit audit non-goal; enforced by test.
- Copying pane capture into the durable journal, persisting it, or sending it via
  message-send. Pane preview is diagnostic, on-demand, and routed to
  `xtmux pane capture` which already bounds and clamps it.
- Reimplementing the live journal follow, monitor registry, or obligations store. Those
  are xtmux-owned surfaces with existing commands; route to them.
- A TUI, a watch loop, or a web view. Static rendered output only. Console is forge-df3a.
- Changing the projection shape. If a view needs a field the snapshot lacks, that is a
  change to the P2-05 child or a cross-repo follow-up, not an inline addition here.
- Deployment evidence beyond what the projection already carries from PR state. Full
  deploy-gap verification is /deploy-monitor's job.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Views are pure functions of the snapshot: (snapshot) -> string. That is what makes them
  unit-testable without a live host and what prevents a view from quietly acquiring its
  own data source.
- Rendering must degrade with the projection: a view whose source was unavailable says so
  from the sources[] ledger instead of rendering a convincing empty table. A blank view
  that means "sp is not installed" and a blank view that means "no jobs running" must be
  visually distinguishable.
- Reuse the repo's existing output conventions: cli-table3 and kleur are already
  dependencies and already used by worktree.ts report printers. Match that style; do not
  introduce a second table/colour idiom.
- Colour must degrade when not a TTY, matching existing command behavior.
- `--json` continues to emit the raw projection unchanged. Views are additive; the
  machine contract from P2-05 is untouched.
- Any view that would need pane content must instead print the exact
  `xtmux pane capture --pane <%id>` command for the operator to run. The viewer never
  shells into capture itself, so capture output can never transit this process.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run build` clean; `npm test --workspace cli` green.
- [ ] Unit: each view renders from a fixture snapshot with no subprocess calls at all —
      asserted, since a view that shells out has escaped its contract.
- [ ] Unit: a snapshot with a degraded source renders an explicit unavailability notice,
      distinguishable from an empty result.
- [ ] Unit: no renderer reads a completion signal from any free-text/terminal field;
      asserted against a fixture whose pane text says "done" while its bead is open.
- [ ] Unit: no renderer emits pane capture content.
- [ ] Smoke: `node cli/dist/index.cjs topology` and each `--view` on the live host render
      without error.
- [ ] `xt topology --help` documents every view and the routing to xtmux-owned surfaces.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/commands/worktree.ts printBranchGcHuman (:702) and the
  audit-prs human printers are the house rendering style — follow them. cli-table3 and
  kleur are already wired.
- **Installed deps:** cli-table3 ^0.6.5, kleur ^4.1.5, boxen ^8.0.1 — all present.
- **Stdlib:** none additional.
- **New dep candidate:** none. Explicitly rejected ink/blessed/any TUI toolkit: the
  output is static rendered text, and a TUI is both out of scope and a new dep class.
- **Roll it:** yes for the view functions themselves — they are small pure formatters
  over a known shape.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, rendered sample output per view from the live host, the no-subprocess and
no-completion-inference test output, test summary, and the PR URL with CI state.

title: Implement read-only aggregated topology projection + xt topology --json (P2-05)
description:
## PROBLEM

Audit ~/dev/11.md:1358 (P2-05). The operator view needs a single join across tmux pane ->
interactive runtime -> role -> coordinator -> root specialist jobs -> descendant
specialist jobs -> bead -> worktree -> branch -> integration target -> pull request. The
data exists but is split across xtmux topology + journal, the Specialists observability
DB, Core worktree metadata, Beads state, git, and GitHub. There is no command that joins
them, so the operator does it by hand across five CLIs whose outputs share no key.

## SUCCESS

`xt topology --json` emits one xtrm.topology.projection.v1 snapshot, computed live at
invocation from the owning systems' published read-only JSON surfaces, joined on stable
keys (pane_id, bead_id, worktree path, branch name). Running it twice writes nothing and
changes nothing. Each source is queried independently and its outcome recorded in
`sources[]`, so a host without `sp` or without `gh` still produces a useful partial
projection instead of failing or silently reporting an empty world.

## SCOPE

- cli/src/core/topology-projection.ts (new): per-source readers, the join, snapshot
  assembly.
- cli/src/commands/topology.ts (new): `xt topology` command with `--json`.
- cli/src/index.ts: one import + one `program.addCommand(createTopologyCommand())` line.
- cli/src/tests/topology-projection.test.ts (new): join, degradation, read-only tests.

Source surfaces consumed (all read-only, all already published):
- `xtmux topology --json` -> xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1 (panes/sessions/windows)
- tmux `show-options -p -t <pane> -qv @agent_role|@agent_worktree|@agent_branch|
  @agent_bead|@agent_parent_session|@agent_task` -> lineage the xtmux topology `agent`
  object does not yet carry
- `sp ps --json` -> specialist jobs: bead_id, worktree_path, branch, epic_id, chain_id,
  chain_root_job_id, status
- `bd list --json` / `bd show <id> --json` -> bead state
- `git worktree list --porcelain` -> worktree/branch/HEAD
- `gh pr list --json` -> PR evidence per branch

## NON_GOALS

- Any write to any source system. No bd update, no sp mutation, no git checkout, no
  journal emission. The projection is a pure reader.
- Persisting the snapshot. No cache file, no materialized graph, no DB table. This is the
  audit's explicit non-goal and the wave-5 brief's hardest constraint.
- Reading .specialists/db/observability.db or the xtmux state DB directly. Those are
  private schemas owned by other repos; `sp ps --json` and the xtmux CLI are the
  contracts.
- Re-deriving tmux topology. Consume `xtmux topology --json`.
- Pane capture in any form. Not collected, not joined, not emitted.
- Rendering. Human-facing views land in the P2-06 child.

## CONSTRAINTS

- No new runtime dependency. Use node:child_process execFile against the source CLIs.
- Every subprocess is bounded: explicit timeout and maxBuffer, and a non-zero exit or a
  timeout degrades that ONE source to status=error with a reason — it never throws out of
  the projection.
- A source binary that is absent degrades to status=unavailable, not error. The
  distinction matters: unavailable means "not installed here", error means "installed and
  it failed", and only the latter is a bug signal.
- Sources are queried concurrently; total wall time is bounded by the slowest source, not
  their sum.
- `gh` is the slowest and most rate-limited source; it must be opt-out-able so the
  projection stays fast on a laptop, and its absence must not degrade the rest.
- Output must validate against xtrm.topology.projection.v1 from @xtrm/contracts. Import
  the published validator; do not re-declare the shape.
- Read-only guarantee is enforced by test: the subprocess layer is injectable, and a test
  asserts the exact argv of every command issued, failing if any is not a known read-only
  invocation.
- No secrets, tokens, or pane content in the snapshot or in any error reason.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run build` clean; `npm test --workspace cli` green.
- [ ] Unit: the join links a pane to its bead, worktree, branch, specialist jobs and PR
      from fixture source output.
- [ ] Unit: each source independently degraded (absent binary, non-zero exit, timeout,
      malformed JSON) yields the right sources[] entry and a still-valid snapshot.
- [ ] Unit: argv allow-list test proves no mutating command is ever issued.
- [ ] Unit: emitted snapshot validates against the published contracts validator.
- [ ] Smoke: `node cli/dist/index.cjs topology --json` on the live host returns a
      non-empty panes[] and a fully-populated sources[] ledger.
- [ ] Evidence findable via: `xt topology --json | jq '.sources'`.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** cli/src/commands/worktree.ts audit-prs/restart-audit already
  establishes the "shell out, parse JSON, emit a --json report, degrade gracefully"
  pattern including gh usage — follow its conventions for option naming and report shape.
  cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts already queries tmux pane options via spawnSync
  (resolveLauncherPaneRole around :1207) — reuse that technique.
- **Installed deps:** commander ^14 for the command surface; @xtrm/contracts for the
  validator. Nothing else needed.
- **Stdlib:** node:child_process execFile for bounded subprocess reads; node:util
  promisify for concurrency via Promise.allSettled.
- **New dep candidate:** none. Explicitly rejected better-sqlite3 — reading another
  repo's private DB schema would couple Core to Specialists' internals when `sp ps --json`
  is the published contract, and it would add a native dependency to a CLI that has none.
- **Roll it:** the join itself, yes — it is ~100 lines of key matching and nothing
  packages "join these six CLIs".

## OUTPUT

Changed files, the sources[] ledger from a live smoke run, the argv allow-list test
output proving read-only, test summary, and the PR URL with CI state.
notes:
CI FIX (PR #468 first run red, fixed on the same branch as a follow-up commit — no amend of a pushed commit):

FAILURE: 'Failed to resolve entry for package "@xtrm/contracts"' in
src/tests/topology-projection.test.ts. 962 passed, 1 suite failed.

ROOT CAUSE: @xtrm/contracts' package.json entry points (main/module/types) resolve to
./dist, which is gitignored. cli is the FIRST in-repo consumer of that package, so CI had
never needed to build it — ci.yml goes straight from 'npm ci' to 'cd cli && npm run build'
to tests. It passed locally only because I had run npm run build:contracts earlier in the
session for the P2-05 schema PR, leaving a stale-but-present dist on disk.

Not a flake and not a test bug: a genuine build-order dependency I introduced.

FIX (2 lines):
  .github/workflows/ci.yml — 'Build contracts package' step (npm run build:contracts)
    inserted before 'Build TypeScript', with a comment explaining the dist/gitignore reason.
  package.json — root build is now 'npm run build:contracts && npm run build --workspace cli'
    so a fresh clone gets the same ordering locally, not just in CI.

REPRODUCED AND VERIFIED LOCALLY:
  rm -rf packages/contracts/dist
  npm test --workspace cli -- topology-projection  -> FAIL, identical error to CI
  npm run build:contracts
  npm test --workspace cli -- topology-projection  -> 29/29 passed

WHY NOT AVOID THE DEPENDENCY INSTEAD: the alternative was to re-wire ajv against the raw
schema JSON inside the cli test. Rejected — the bead's constraint is to import the
PUBLISHED validator rather than re-declare the shape, and testing the artifact consumers
will actually use is more faithful than testing a hand-rolled parallel path. The build-order
step is the honest fix for a real workspace dependency.

NOTE: CI has no typecheck step, so only the test import surfaced this. The production code
uses 'import type' only and is erased at build time — cli/dist is unaffected, and the
'Verify dist is up to date' gate passed on the first run.
close_reason: xt topology --json read-only projection implemented; 27 unit tests + full suite 989 green; live smoke 6/6 sources ok, contract-valid

title: Publish xtrm.topology.projection.v1 aggregated-projection schema in @xtrm/contracts
description:
## PROBLEM

P2-05 requires an aggregated topology projection joining six source systems. The wave-5
non-negotiables forbid inventing shapes inline: every emitted shape must reference a
schema in @xtrm/contracts, and contracts changes must land as their own PR based on main
before consumers exist. Without a published schema the projection command has no contract
to validate against and no cross-repo consumer (Console, forge-df3a) can depend on it.

Existing contracts cover the pieces but not the join: xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1 describes
tmux panes, xtrm.branch.integration.v1 describes one merge result, xtrm.runtime-origin.v1
describes specialist lineage. None expresses "this pane, under this coordinator, owns
these jobs, this bead, this branch, and this PR".

## SUCCESS

`xtrm.topology.projection.v1` is published in @xtrm/contracts with a JSON Schema, a
TypeScript type, a runtime validator, and a golden fixture, following the exact pattern
of the sibling schemas added in PR #457 and #462. The schema composes the existing
topology/branch-integration/runtime-origin vocabularies by reference or by mirrored field
naming rather than redefining them, and carries a `sources[]` ledger so a consumer can
distinguish "no coordinators running" from "sp was unavailable".

## SCOPE

- packages/contracts/schemas/xtrm.topology.projection.v1.json (new)
- packages/contracts/src/ — type + validator + index export, mirroring the existing
  per-schema layout
- packages/contracts/test/ — golden fixture + validation test
- packages/contracts/README or docs entry if the package indexes its schemas

## NON_GOALS

- Any cli/ change. This PR ships the contract only; the producer lands separately.
- Redefining pane/session/window shapes already owned by xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1.
- Redefining the specialist job shape owned by Specialists.
- A v2 bump of any existing schema. This is purely additive.

## CONSTRAINTS

- snake_case field naming, matching xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1's deliberate cross-repo
  convention.
- `additionalProperties: false` at every object level, matching sibling schemas.
- Required top-level: schema_version, generated_at_ms, host, sources, panes.
- `sources[]` entries carry: name, status (ok|unavailable|error), reason (nullable),
  duration_ms — this is the projection's own observability surface and the only way a
  consumer can tell degraded output from empty output.
- Pane capture MUST NOT be representable in this schema. No content/preview/capture
  field may exist, so that the audit's "never journalled, never persisted" rule is
  enforced by the type system rather than by discipline.
- Follow whatever registration/export the package already requires so
  `npm run test:contracts` picks it up automatically.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run build:contracts` clean.
- [ ] `npm run test:contracts` green, including the new golden fixture.
- [ ] Golden fixture round-trips: validator accepts it, and rejects a fixture with an
      unknown property and one with a missing required field.
- [ ] A negative test asserts no capture/content field is accepted.
- [ ] `npm run check:runtime-compat` and other prepublish schema checks still pass.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** packages/contracts existing schema+type+validator layout from PR
  #457 (xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1) and PR #462 (xtrm.beads.lifecycle-event.v1) — copy that
  structure exactly; it already carries the build and test wiring.
- **Installed deps:** ajv ^8.20.0 (already a devDependency) for validation, as the
  sibling schemas use.
- **Stdlib:** none applicable.
- **New dep candidate:** none — tiers 1-2 cover it.
- **Roll it:** no. The pattern is established; this is one more instance of it.

## OUTPUT

The new schema path, the type/validator export names, the fixture path, the
`npm run test:contracts` summary, and the PR URL with CI state.
notes:
DONE — schema published, awaiting PR merge.

FILES:
  packages/contracts/schemas/xtrm.topology.projection.v1.json (new, 184 lines)
  packages/contracts/src/types.ts (+108: TopologyProjectionV1 + 7 sub-types, SCHEMA_ID.topologyProjection, ContractTypeMap entry)
  packages/contracts/fixtures/golden.json (+122: coordinator pane w/ full join + bare shell pane + orphan job + orphan detached worktree)
  packages/contracts/fixtures/invalid.json (+8: bad source status enum)
  packages/contracts/test/contracts.test.ts (+74: 12 targeted cases)
  packages/contracts/README.md (+4: contracts index entry)

NO validate.ts CHANGE NEEDED: loadSchemas() (validate.ts:12-16) discovers schemas by
directory scan, so a new schema file self-registers. Only the TS-side SCHEMA_ID /
ContractTypeMap needed touching, and contracts.test.ts:19-21 already asserts the two
sets match exactly — so a schema added without its TS constant fails the suite.

DESIGN NOTES:
- sources[] ledger is the projection's own observability surface. status distinguishes
  unavailable (binary absent — not a bug) from error (present but failed — a bug signal).
  Without it an absent sp and zero running jobs are indistinguishable: both yield [].
- orphans{jobs,worktrees} exists so a job whose coordinator pane died, or a worktree whose
  session was killed, does not silently vanish. That leak is what an operator most needs.
- Join slots (agent/bead/worktree/pull_request) are REQUIRED and nullable rather than
  optional, so consumers are total: 'we looked and found none' is explicit null, and
  'we did not look' is readable from sources[].
- job.status is an open string on purpose — enumerating it would fossilize Specialists'
  private vocabulary inside a Core contract.
- NO pane-capture representation at any level. additionalProperties:false everywhere means
  a producer cannot smuggle terminal text through this contract even by accident. Six test
  cases assert it (content/capture/preview/output/terminal_text at pane level, capture
  nested under agent). This is the audit's P2-06 rule enforced by type system, not comment.

VALIDATION:
  npm run test:contracts      -> 65/65 passed (741ms)   [was 53, +12 new]
  npm run build:contracts     -> clean (CJS+ESM+DTS)
  npm run typecheck -w @xtrm/contracts -> clean
  npm run check:runtime-compat -> ok
  npm run check:payload-hygiene -> ok (446 packed files)
  gitnexus_detect_changes     -> 0 changed symbols, risk low (purely additive)

title: [epic] audit sprint wave 5 cluster D: aggregation surface (P2-03 + P2-05 + P2-06)
description:
## PROBLEM

~/dev/11.md flags three related gaps in the operator-facing aggregation surface. An
operator running N concurrent panes has no single read-only answer to "what is running
where, under which coordinator, on which worktree/branch, against which bead, and has it
landed?". The facts exist but are scattered across six systems that never join: xtmux
topology + journal, the Specialists observability database, Core worktree metadata,
Beads state, git, and GitHub. Today the operator reconstructs that join by hand from
`xtmux dashboard`, `sp ps`, `bd list`, `git worktree list` and `gh pr list` — five
commands whose outputs share no key.

P2-03 (explicit coordinator identity) is the identity prerequisite for that join.
Archaeology finding: it ALREADY SHIPPED in PR #465 (xtrm-6hey0.2) — `@agent_role` is
written at worktree-session.ts:728 and `XTMUX_AGENT_ROLE` is derived generically at
:871, with `@agent_task` / `XTMUX_AGENT_TASK` preserved intact. Suite C step 5 asserts
both. The audit bullet is stale; this epic verifies and closes it rather than re-doing it.

## SUCCESS

`xt topology --json` returns a single read-only snapshot that joins pane -> runtime ->
role -> coordinator -> specialist jobs -> bead -> worktree -> branch -> integration
target -> pull request, conforming to a published `@xtrm/contracts` schema. `xt topology`
renders that same snapshot as operator views. No source of truth is duplicated: every
field is read live from its owning system at call time, and nothing is written back or
cached. Every source degrades independently — a missing `xtmux`, `sp`, `bd`, or `gh`
yields a recorded unavailability reason, never a hard failure or a silently-empty join.

## SCOPE

- packages/contracts/schemas/xtrm.topology.projection.v1.json (+ src/types, validator,
  golden fixture, index export) — schema-only PR, lands FIRST, based on main.
- cli/src/core/topology-projection.ts (new — source readers + join)
- cli/src/commands/topology.ts (new — command surface)
- cli/src/index.ts (single addCommand registration line)
- cli/src/tests/topology-*.test.ts (new)
- docs/ (operator documentation for the new command)

## NON_GOALS

- Persisting a duplicate mutable graph. The projection is computed per invocation from
  live sources. No cache file, no materialized view, no write-back, no second git or
  bead authority. This is the audit's explicit P2-05 non-goal.
- Inferring completion from terminal output. Any "done" signal comes from bead state,
  PR merge state, or an emitted lifecycle event — never from parsing pane capture.
  This is the audit's explicit P2-06 non-goal.
- Copying pane capture into the durable event journal, persisting it, or streaming it
  via message-send. Pane preview stays diagnostic and on-demand.
- Reading the Specialists or xtmux SQLite databases directly. Those are private schemas
  owned by other repos; the projection consumes their published `--json` CLI surfaces.
- Re-implementing tmux topology. `xtmux topology --json` already publishes
  `xtrm.xtmux.topology.v1`; the projection consumes it rather than rebuilding it.
- Changing `@agent_task` / `XTMUX_AGENT_TASK` semantics (P2-03 is additive, and already
  landed).
- Console/web viewer. Deferred as forge-df3a.
- P2-07 (async bridge subprocesses) — a separate audit item, not this cluster.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Three sequential PRs, NOT stacked. This repo's CI only fires on PRs targeting main;
  a stacked PR stalls without CI (Wave 4 hit this). Each PR waits for its predecessor
  to merge before the next opens.
- Contracts changes land as their own PR based on main, per the wave-5 brief's
  do-not-touch boundary on packages/contracts/**.
- Every emitted shape references a schema in @xtrm/contracts. No inline shapes.
- No new runtime dependency. Core's CLI has no sqlite dep and must not grow one;
  node:sqlite (already used by xtrm-logger since PR #461) is likewise not needed
  because every source publishes a CLI JSON surface.
- Cross-repo etiquette: if xtmux or Specialists needs a new field or command, file a
  follow-up bead in that repo. Do not monolith across repos in one PR.
- Do NOT touch .xtrm/hooks/xtrm-logger.mjs, cli/src/core/legacy-hook-dedupe.ts,
  scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs.
- Do not merge, force-push, or --amend a pushed commit. Orchestrator greenlights merges.
- Telemetry: the projection is read-only and emits no new lifecycle events. Its own
  observability is the `sources[]` array in the snapshot, which records per-source
  ok/unavailable/error state and duration_ms — that is the debugging surface.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `npm run build` clean; `npm test --workspace cli` green at each PR.
- [ ] `npm run test:contracts` green after the schema PR.
- [ ] `xt topology --json` output validates against xtrm.topology.projection.v1.
- [ ] Unit tests cover the join, per-source degradation, and the read-only guarantee.
- [ ] Smoke: `xt topology --json` on a live host returns a non-empty pane set and a
      populated sources[] ledger.
- [ ] Suite C step ledger reported before -> after with an explicit reason for any
      remaining SKIP.
- [ ] No write syscall to any source system: asserted by test, not by inspection.

## OUTPUT

Three PR URLs in merge order with CI state, the P2-03 already-satisfied verdict with
file:line evidence, per-child closure notes, the Suite C step ledger, cross-repo
follow-up bead ids, and a divergences-from-audit list with rationale.

## REFERENCES

- Audit: ~/dev/11.md L1294 (P2-03), L1358 (P2-05), L1389 (P2-06)
- Prereqs: PR #465 (lineage metadata), #466 (launch validation), #457 (contracts pkg),
  #462/#463 (Beads lifecycle events), specialists PR #199 (branch.integration.v1)
- Suite C: test/integration-suite/suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs
- Cluster B epic: xtrm-6hey0

title: Suite C: opt-in live-agent lane for steps 7-10 (specialist chain ancestry)
description:
## PROBLEM
