because they dispatch a real specialist chain and inspect the branches it creates:
7 (dispatch a specialist child), 8 (specialist branch derives from the coordinator
branch), 9 (descendant runtime-origin lineage), 10 (merge accepted specialist
branch into the coordinator branch). All four need real agents plus API
credentials, so they cannot run in the hermetic lane.

They are also the only assertions that would prove the *other half* of audit
P1-03: Core publishes @agent_branch, but nothing yet verifies that Specialists
consumes it as the base for sp/* branches.

## SUCCESS

An opt-in lane (env-gated, e.g. XTRM_SUITE_C_LIVE=1 plus credentials present)
dispatches one real short specialist chain under a coordinator and asserts steps
7-10. Default behavior is unchanged: without the gate the steps stay SKIP with
their current reasons.

## SCOPE

- test/integration-suite/README.md

## NON_GOALS

- Making it run in hermetic CI. It costs credentials and wall-clock; it is a
  pre-release lane, not a per-PR gate.
- Replacing the sp/runtime shims in the existing hermetic path.
- Implementing the Specialists-side base-branch derivation itself (separate bead).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must remain SKIP-by-default; a runner without the gate stays green.
- Isolation discipline is non-negotiable: private tmux -L server, isolated
  HOME/XDG_STATE_HOME, throwaway repo. Never the operator's real worktrees.
- Pick the cheapest possible specialist chain — this asserts branch topology, not
  agent quality.
- Step 8 will FAIL until Specialists consumes @agent_branch. That is the correct
  outcome; do not weaken the assertion to make it pass.

- **Stdlib:** node:assert, node:child_process.

The gated lane, a sample run transcript with the gate on, and the step-8 verdict
against the current Specialists release.

title: Adopt Beads-owned lifecycle event contract
description:
## PROBLEM
Core hooks emit past-tense `bd.claimed`/`bd.closed`, xtmux telemetry emits imperative `bd.claim`/`bd.close`, creation/reopen coverage is absent, and Pi/Claude parity is unclear. Consumers cannot safely merge events without aliases or duplicate semantics.

## SUCCESS
A versioned Core-owned event contract defines canonical names and fields for create, claim, update/status transition, close, and reopen; Claude and Pi producers conform; xtmux and Console have explicit projection/reconciliation responsibilities.

## SCOPE
Core Beads hooks, Pi extensions, policy/asset generation, contract tests/docs, plus tracked integration contracts for xtmux and Console.

## NON_GOALS
- Do not make Specialists a Beads lifecycle emitter.
- Do not use Console polling as exact live truth.
- Do not remove legacy names without migration coverage.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Mutation-point emission is primary; Console snapshot diff is reconciliation/backfill.
- Event names and required fields must be runtime-neutral and idempotently identifiable.
- Preserve fail-open workflow gates and avoid secrets/raw commands.
- Decide compatibility aliases before changing producers.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Contract fixture covers every lifecycle action and required field.
- [ ] Claude and Pi emit byte-compatible normalized events.
- [ ] Duplicate/retry behavior is specified and tested.
- [ ] xtmux stream and Console materializer follow-up issues are linked.

## OUTPUT
Canonical schema/taxonomy, producer changes, tests, migration/alias notes, and linked consumer work.

## LIBRARIES
- Reuse in repo: Core hook and Pi lifecycle producers.
- Installed deps: none applicable.
- Stdlib: existing JSON/SQLite facilities.
- New dep candidate: none.
- Roll it: no.
notes:
2026-07-21 discovery corrects the initial ownership premise:

- Beads 1.1.0 already writes canonical lifecycle facts to its Dolt `events` table for every mutation, including `created`, `claimed`, `updated`, `closed`, `reopened`, and `status_changed`.
- Rows carry a stable UUIDv7 `id`, `issue_id`, `actor`, `old_value`, `new_value`, `comment`, and `created_at`. Current DB counts prove broad use: 1825 created, 1182 claimed, 1738 updated, 1926 closed, 97 reopened, 246 status_changed.
- Therefore Beads owns lifecycle names/facts. Core must not emit a competing lifecycle record. Core owns only the reusable projection/enrichment contract; xtmux owns host-stream transport; Console owns materialized reconciliation; Specialists remains correlation-only.
- Canonical stream kinds mirror Beads exactly with namespace: `bd.created`, `bd.claimed`, `bd.updated`, `bd.closed`, `bd.reopened`, `bd.status_changed`. Legacy Core `bd.claimed`/`bd.closed` already match; xtmux imperative `bd.claim`/`bd.close` become aliases only.
- The event UUIDv7 timestamp is correct UTC and is the idempotency/cursor key. Beads 1.1.0 currently renders the DATETIME `created_at` as local wall time with a `Z` suffix (+02:00 on this host), so consumers must decode UUIDv7 time until Beads fixes timestamp serialization.
- Runtime/session/tmux/repo fields are enrichment joined by time/repo/issue; they are not part of the Beads source fact.

Implementation now means adapter + fixtures + consumer follow-ups, not new Claude/Pi lifecycle producers.
Consumer follow-ups filed: xtmux-ck7 (host-wide stream projection, P1; external_ref core:xtrm-etmv4.2) and forge-df3a in Console (exact-event ingestion plus snapshot reconciliation, P2; same external_ref).
xtmux-ck7 completed: host stream now consumes Beads events directly, canonicalizes as bd.<event_type>, uses UUIDv7 id/time, preserves old/new/actor, and emits exact or candidate tmux IDs. Console forge-df3a remains open.
LANDING STATUS 2026-07-21: decomposed into xtrm-etmv4.2.1 (Core PR #462, contract schema/fixtures/helper; CI green) and xtrm-etmv4.2.2 (Core PR #463, retire duplicate Claude lifecycle diagnostics; CI running). xtmux transport is PR #56, CI green. Console forge-df3a deferred until #462/#463/#56 merge; no provisional schema duplication. All beads remain open pending orchestrator merge.
FINAL LANDING REPORT posted on parent xtrm-etmv4. PRs #56/#462/#463 are open with all CI green; Console forge-df3a deferred; all implementation beads remain open pending orchestrator merge.
close_reason: Both children (.1 contract, .2 alignment) merged. Consumer side landed in xtmux PR #56 (3153184e).

title: xtmux hook entries registered 3x in ~/.claude/settings.json (installer not idempotent)
description:
Found during xtrm-1ehjo sweep — separate from the xtrm hook duplication, and likely owned by the xtmux repo rather than xtrm-tools.

Every xtmux hook in ~/.claude/settings.json appears three times: one copy tagged {_source:'xtmux', _xtmux:{version,hash}} plus two untagged clones. Affected events and commands:
  SessionStart / PreToolUse / PostToolUse / Stop / UserPromptSubmit / Notification / SubagentStop / SessionEnd -> agent-state.sh (x3 each)
  PostToolUse -> auto-monitor-on-send.sh (x3), auto-monitor-consumed.sh (x3)
  Stop -> auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs (x3)
Entry counts: PostToolUse 14 entries (8 tagged / 6 untagged), Stop 7 (3/4), SessionStart 5 (2/3).

Consequence: agent-state transitions fire three times per event; the auto-monitor drain runs three times per Stop. Root cause is presumably an installer that appends its block without first removing entries it previously wrote — the untagged copies predate provenance tagging, so a hash/_source-based sweep alone will not find them.

scripts/dedupe-legacy-hooks.mjs deliberately does NOT touch these: it only removes PROJECT-scope entries that the GLOBAL scope already covers, and these are all global-scope. Deduping within a single settings file is a different operation and needs the xtmux installer's own ownership rules.
notes: Investigated in Wave 6 (xtrm-kdwvu). CONFIRMED xtmux-owned: all 33 registrations invoke ~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/*, none reference .xtrm/hooks. Core ships DETECTION only — 'xt doctor settings --scope home' reports all 11 tuples at 3x and names xtmux as the owner in its remediation string. The FIX is filed cross-repo as xtmux-2zh. Core deliberately adds no workaround: it has no ownership rules for another installer's block, and deduping within a single settings file is a different operation from the project-vs-global proof in legacy-hook-dedupe.ts. Close this bead when xtmux-2zh lands.
close_reason: Wave-6 worker (PR #472) verified fix belongs to xtmux repo, not core. All 33 duplicate xtmux hook registrations invoke ~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/*; none reference .xtrm/hooks. Core ships detection only via xt doctor settings; the fix bead is xtmux-2zh (P2, filed in xtmux repo). Closing this as detection-only-in-core; xtmux-2zh owns the fix.

title: global ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/*-top.md is stale vs every consumer project
description:
Found during xtrm-1ehjo sweep. ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/claude-top.md is 66 lines and agents-top.md is 64 lines (both dated May 8), while ALL 8 consumer projects carry a 125-line version of each — identical to one another, differing from global by 8 hunks (xtmux messageKey reply guidance, 'Code restraint' section, bd set-state commands). The other 12 files under .xtrm/config/ are byte-identical global-vs-project, so this is isolated to the instruction templates.

Direction of drift is the notable part: global is BEHIND the projects, i.e. the global config tree was not refreshed when the instruction templates were updated. Any project bootstrapped fresh from global today would get the older CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md managed block.

Fix: identify the canonical source for the instruction templates in this repo, confirm the 125-line version is it, and re-publish to ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/. Then verify a fresh 'xt init' produces the current block.
notes:
PUSHBACK from Wave 6 — the stated consequence does not hold; do not republish yet.

Investigated at a1fdc4ca. ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/ has NO READER and NO WRITER in this repo:
- init.ts:47-48 getInstructionsDir() = getPackageRoot() + '.xtrm/config/instructions' — the npm package or dev checkout.
- resolvePackageRoot() (core/registry-scaffold.ts:54-67) walks up from the CLI's own __dirname looking for .xtrm/registry.json, so it can only ever land on the package. It cannot resolve to ~/.xtrm/.
- grep over cli/src, scripts, .xtrm/hooks and packages/pi-extensions finds no other reader. xtrm-loader/index.ts:16 mentions the path in a doc comment only.
- Only ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json is maintained globally (global-hooks-bootstrap.ts). The rest of ~/.xtrm/config/ is dated 8 May — seeded once in the plugin era and never refreshed.

So the bead's premise — 'any project bootstrapped fresh from global today would get the older managed block' — is FALSE. xt init reads the package (125-line current version) and renders the current block. The 64/66-line global copies are inert residue; the drift has no runtime effect on any consumer.

RECOMMENDATION: do not republish. This bead already depends-on xtrm-148eh, which is the bead that MAKES ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/ canonical (bootstrap on install + runtime-inject on both runtimes). Publishing into a dead directory ahead of that design creates a second apparent source of truth with no reader — it makes the stale dir look authoritative without making it so. Either fold this into xtrm-148eh's bootstrap step, or close as superseded. A one-line operator-side refresh of the local dir is available as a cosmetic stopgap if desired, but it is a machine action, not a PR.

Left OPEN and UNCLAIMED for the operator to decide. No code shipped for this bead in Wave 6.
close_reason: Superseded by xtrm-148eh (its dep). Wave-6 worker (PR #472) verified the bead's premise is false: ~/.xtrm/config/instructions/ has NO reader (getInstructionsDir() at init.ts:47 resolves via resolvePackageRoot(), which walks up from CLI's __dirname — can only land on npm package or dev checkout, never ~/.xtrm/). So a fresh xt init already renders the current 125-line block; the 64/66-line global copies are inert 8-May residue. Republishing into a dead directory ahead of xtrm-148eh — which is what makes that path canonical — would create a second apparent source of truth with no reader. Close as false-premise; the real fix is xtrm-148eh.

title: Clarify user-owned SKILL preservation contract across xt update --apply
description: P2-01 Suite A step 20 OBSERVE finding: xt update --apply repairs the managed skills tree from package payload and removes an unmarked user skill dropped into ~/.claude/skills (and ~/.xtrm/skills/default). Hooks and extensions ARE preserved (foreign-preserved). Question for owner: is there a supported marker/location for a genuinely user-owned skill that survives update (cf. skills-runtime-reconcile.ts:84 'Refusing to replace user-owned runtime directory')? If yes, document it and add a positive assertion to Suite A. If no, decide whether that is a gap. Evidence in xtrm-kvsrd.2 notes + suite-a [OBSERVE] output.
notes:
ANSWER (wave-9): YES, there is a supported way to own a skill across
xt update --apply — but it is a LOCATION contract, not a marker. There is no
"user-owned" flag to set, and none is needed. Suite A step 20 observed correct
behavior, not a gap.

## The contract, as the code actually implements it

### REPLACED / REMOVED (managed — never put user content here)

1. `~/.xtrm/skills/default/**` — registry-owned payload tree.
   `scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage()` (registry-scaffold.ts:114) repairs it
   from the package payload, and `pruneRetiredManagedSkills()` (:188) removes
   any dir-like entry whose name is not in `collectManagedDefaultSkillNames(registry)`.
   THIS is what deleted the unmarked skill in Suite A step 20 — the file was in
   the managed tree, so by contract it was not user-owned.
   Two guards worth noting: the pruner refuses entirely if the root is a symlink
   or not a directory (:199), and refuses if the registry declares zero managed
   default skills (:206) — it cannot distinguish "retired" from "not in scope".
2. Runtime-view symlinks that are simultaneously (a) recorded in
   `state.managedLinks[runtime]`, (b) resolving INSIDE a managed root, and
   (c) no longer desired. All three conditions required
   (skills-runtime-reconcile.ts:157-167).
3. `~/.xtrm/skills/active/<name>` symlinks that point at a just-pruned default
   entry — and only those; the sweep compares the resolved target exactly.

### PRESERVED (foreign — safe for user content)

1. `~/.xtrm/skills/optional/**` and project packs `.xtrm/skills/<pack>/`.
   The pruner only ever targets `defaultRoot`. Optional and project tiers are
   DISCOVERED, never payload-repaired. This is the supported home for a
   user-authored skill that must survive update.
2. A real directory placed at `.claude/skills/<name>` or `.pi/skills/<name>`.
   The removal loop iterates only over `managed` entries, so an untracked entry
   is never even considered. If its name collides with a managed skill,
   reconcile REFUSES loudly rather than overwriting:
   `Cannot enable skill '<name>': <path> is user-owned.` (:176).
3. A symlink in the runtime view pointing OUTSIDE the managed roots — preserved
   even when tracked, because removal additionally requires
   `roots.some(root => isInside(resolved, root))`.
4. The runtime directory itself when it is a symlink:
   `Refusing to replace user-owned runtime directory` (ensureRuntimeDirectory,
   :84 — the line this bead cites).
5. Non-symlink managed entries are never silently clobbered:
   `Cannot replace non-symlink managed entry <path>.` (:185).
6. Hooks and extensions — already confirmed foreign-preserved by kvsrd.2.

## Verdict on "is that a gap?"

No. The design is coherent: `default/` is the registry's tree and the registry
is authoritative over it; everything else is either discovered or refused-with-
an-error. A marker inside `default/` would be strictly worse — it would make
the payload tree partially user-owned, which is exactly what makes drift
undetectable.

The real gap is DOCUMENTATION, not behavior: nothing tells an operator that
dropping a skill into `~/.xtrm/skills/default/` is a delete-on-next-update
action while `~/.xtrm/skills/optional/` is not. That is what surprised Suite A.

## Follow-ups filed

- Suite A positive assertion: a skill in `optional/` and a real dir in
  `.claude/skills/` both survive `xt update --apply`, while one in `default/`
  is pruned. Turns this contract into a regression test.
- Document the location contract in the skills-ownership docs.
close_reason: contract documented in notes: location-based, not marker-based; optional/ + foreign runtime entries preserved, default/ is registry-owned; Suite A assertions + docs split out to xtrm-vtqlg.7

title: Test isolation: guard test env-leak + vitest globbing into .xtrm/worktrees
description:
## Symptom
\`npx vitest run\` from repo root reports ~70 failing tests. Investigation shows this is 2 real failures multiplied by:
1. Vitest globbing test files across all .xtrm/worktrees/* (34 present) → runs same file ~17x
2. retry: {count: 2} config

## Two independent bugs

### A. Guard test env-leak
cli/src/tests/claude-runtime-sync-global-guard.test.ts (from #330, xtrm-il7ov) asserts \`runClaudeRuntimeSyncPhase({ isGlobal: true })\` early-returns without writing. That contract was written pre-global-hooks-flag. Since #372, the isGlobal branch has a nested \`if (shouldUseGlobalHooks())\` which reads process.env.XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS. Operators using the global-hooks feature export XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS=1 in their shell → vitest inherits → the test drops into the new branch → reads ~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json which the test's tmp-HOME doesn't have → ENOENT. Sibling tests (install-runInstall, prune-retired-managed-skills, update) all vi.mock('../core/global-hooks-flag.js'); this one was missed.

Verify: \`env -u XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS npx vitest run …global-guard.test.ts\` → 2/2 pass.

### B. Vitest globs worktrees
No repo-root vitest.config.* → default include of \`**/*.test.ts\` picks up every .xtrm/worktrees/*/cli/src/tests/*. Correct entry point per CLAUDE.md is \`npm test --workspace cli\` (or run from cli/), but the footgun should not exist.

## Fixes
- A: add \`vi.mock('../core/global-hooks-flag.js', () => ({ shouldUseGlobalHooks: () => false }))\` to the guard test.
- B: cli/test/setup.ts beforeEach — \`delete process.env.XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS\` so no test inherits it.
- C: add vitest.workspace.ts (or vitest.config.ts) at repo root with \`test.exclude: ['.xtrm/worktrees/**', 'node_modules/**']\`.

## Not affected
No real user config is at risk — test/setup.ts has a HOME-leak detector guarding ~/.xtrm/{hooks,skills}/state.json.
close_reason: Fixed: (a) vi.mock global-hooks-flag in guard test; (b) test/setup.ts strips XTRM_GLOBAL_HOOKS/SKILLS in beforeEach and hashes ~/.xtrm/{hooks,skills/default} trees for leak detection instead of state.json mtime; (c) added repo-root vitest.config.ts excluding .xtrm/worktrees/**. Test count: 6 pre-existing failures on main → 2 with my changes (both pre-existing, unrelated). Also discovered and filed xtrm-5ts3l for a related P1 (xt update --apply --force destroys registry.json hooks section).

title: xt claude {install,status,reload,doctor}: misdetects project root via findRepoRoot() → targets ~/dev/core
description:
## Symptom (reported from consumer repo)
Operator runs \`xt claude install\` in ~/dev/market-data → no-op. \`xt claude status\` reports the target repo as ~/dev/core. Had to hand-rewrite .claude/settings.json to swap 16 hook paths from a stale local prefix to /home/dawid/.xtrm/hooks/.

## Root cause
cli/src/commands/claude.ts uses \`findRepoRoot()\` in all 4 subcommands (install:132, reload:152, status:170, doctor:204). \`findRepoRoot()\` is the **source-bundle** resolver — it prefers \`__dirname\`-relative lookup (\`resolveBundleRootFromRuntime\`) which, when the installed CLI is running from anywhere reachable from ~/dev/core, always returns ~/dev/core. Every claude subcommand then targets ~/dev/core/.claude/settings.json regardless of cwd.

## Correct API
\`resolveMainProjectRoot(process.cwd())\` — already used by install.ts:115 and update.ts:75; docstring at cli/src/utils/repo-root.ts:120 explicitly names \`xt init/update/claude\` as its callers.

## Fix
Swap 4 call sites in cli/src/commands/claude.ts. Add regression test that runs the status/install helpers from a subdir outside ~/dev/core and asserts the resolved settings path is the cwd project, not the bundle root.

## Non-scope
- status.ts:44 uses findRepoRoot correctly (needs source-bundle for calculateDiff).
- pi.ts uses findRepoRoot() but labels the var \`bundleRoot\` — intentional for extension packaging.
close_reason: Fixed: swapped findRepoRoot() → resolveMainProjectRoot(process.cwd()) in cli/src/commands/claude.ts (install/reload/status/doctor). Added regression test cli/src/tests/claude-project-root-detection.test.ts. Memory saved: dual-repo-root-api-footgun.

title: executor: consolidate setup update repair and doctor command UX
description:
## PROBLEM

Even after correctness fixes, operators still face overlapping first-time, routine refresh, targeted runtime repair, diagnostics, cleanup, and one-time migration verbs. Duplicate aliases (`claude install/reload/reinstall`), redundant Pi setup flags, runtime doctors, and standalone bootstrap obscure the intended path.

## SUCCESS

The public UX has a staged, backward-compatible hierarchy: `xt init` for first-time bootstrap, `xt update [--apply]` for routine refresh/repair, `xt doctor` for diagnosis, and `xt migrate` for explicit one-time migrations. Domain commands remain only where they perform distinct work, with deprecation/tombstone messaging and retained flags documented by executable help tests.

## SCOPE

- Registration/help and command handlers in `cli/src/index.ts` and `cli/src/commands/{update,bootstrap,pi,install-pi,claude,doctor,clean,reset,migrate,claude-sync,skills}.ts`.
- Tests and dist help snapshots for the migration matrix.
- Depends on the correctness/safety children under `xtrm-f42ns`; do not consolidate onto an incomplete update path.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not change launcher behavior of bare `xt pi [name]` / `xt claude [name]` beyond retired-token safety.
- Do not remove distinct `reset`, `migrate`, `skills`, or `claude-sync` behavior.
- Do not silently delete commands in one release without compatibility messaging.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Classification to implement after prerequisite fixes: KEEP `init`, `update`, `doctor`, `migrate`, `reset`, `skills`, `claude-sync`, Pi `setup` (credentials) and runtime `status`; MERGE `bootstrap` into update repair/force, Pi `setup --check` into status, redundant `setup --setup` into setup default, Claude `reload|reinstall` into its single targeted repair alias, runtime doctor checks into top doctor, and clean/Pi reload/Claude repair into canonical update where parity is complete; REMOVE only dead unregistered install wrappers/phantom Pi install after tombstone coverage.
- Preserve required flags by moving only proven distinct behavior; add no speculative component framework.
- Deprecation stderr must state replacement and planned removal window; help must mark aliases consistently.
- Existing bootstrap/update JSONL evidence remains; no new telemetry for pure aliases beyond deterministic stderr/exit codes.
- SCRUTINY: high — cross-cutting public CLI surface. GitNexus command constructors are LOW, but shared Pi runtime is CRITICAL; do not edit it in this UX-only phase.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Root/subcommand help matches the approved classification with no implicit verb.
- [ ] Legacy muscle-memory invocations produce deterministic redirects and preserve retained flags during the compatibility window.
- [ ] `xt update --apply` and `xt doctor` have behavior parity before any runtime repair/doctor alias is deprecated.
- [ ] `xt init`, `migrate`, `reset`, `skills`, and `claude-sync` remain behaviorally distinct and green.
- [ ] Complete help/exit matrix, targeted unit/integration tests, typecheck, build, dist freshness, and npm-installed smoke pass.
- [ ] Changelog/user docs explain only the final approved surface, not internal audit detail.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** existing Commander handlers, update/doctor helpers, confirmation and help-test patterns.
- **Installed deps:** `commander`.
- **Stdlib:** subprocess help smoke.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** no — route aliases into current handlers and delete only dead wrappers.

## OUTPUT

Final command classification/migration matrix, changed files, retained-flag map, help/exit smoke transcript, test/build/dist/npm smoke evidence, deprecation window, and residual compatibility risks.

## Acceptance Criteria

All VALIDATION checks pass after correctness prerequisites close; help, redirects, retained flags, and deprecation windows match the approved classification matrix.
close_reason: Implemented staged command UX, compatibility redirects, retained-flag help matrix, changelog, dist refresh, and npm-pack/help smoke. Typecheck is blocked by pre-existing worktree-session-bare-slash.test.ts errors outside this scope.

title: executor: remove dead install guidance and guard retired Pi install
description:
## PROBLEM

The shipped CLI does not register root `install`, but live messages still recommend `xt install`/`xtrm install all -y`, and dead `createInstallCommand` wrappers remain in source. `xt pi install` is not a maintenance subcommand: Commander treats `install` as the optional worktree session name, while `--help` silently shows parent Pi help and exits 0. These redirects make repair guidance misleading and can launch an unintended session.

## SUCCESS

No user-facing or source guidance points to the dead install facade. Retired maintenance tokens such as `xt pi install` fail safely with a concise current redirect and cannot become worktree names; the shared internal `runInstall` helper remains available to init/update.

## SCOPE

- Dead root install command constructors in `cli/src/commands/install.ts`, preserving `runInstall`.
- `cli/src/commands/pi.ts` retired-token guard/tombstone and CLI help/exit-code tests.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not implement the wider bootstrap/doctor/reload consolidation.
- Do not rename the internal `runInstall` helper solely for aesthetics.
- Do not block legitimate arbitrary session names except an explicit, documented retired-command set.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Proposed redirects: missing registry → `xt init` for bootstrap or `xt update --apply --repo <path>` for repair; post-clean → the canonical repair command; Pi drift check → `xt pi reload` until consolidation lands.
- `xt pi install` and its `--help` must not launch a session and must provide one actionable redirect with deliberate exit semantics.
- Preserve source compatibility for internal imports of `runInstall`.
- Evidence is stdout/stderr and exit code; no product telemetry or user payload logging.
- SCRUTINY: medium — public CLI compatibility and launcher ambiguity.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] CLI help smoke, targeted tests, typecheck, build, and dist freshness checks pass.

- **Installed deps:** `commander` already owns parsing.
- **Stdlib:** none beyond existing process output.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** no — delete dead wrappers and add one bounded guard/tombstone.

## OUTPUT

Changed files, removed stale-string list, command/exit matrix, launcher non-invocation proof, tests/build/dist evidence, and compatibility window for the retired token.

## Steps to Reproduce

1. Run root help and observe no `install` command.
2. Search CLI source for `xt install`/`xtrm install all -y` recommendations.
3. Run `xt pi install --help`; it prints parent Pi help and exits 0 because `install` is parsed as a session name.

## Acceptance Criteria

All VALIDATION checks pass; dead guidance is absent and retired Pi install tokens cannot reach the launcher.

title: revert: drop permissionsDefaults seed (PR #434) — mechanism was unneeded
description:
## PROBLEM

The `permissionsDefaults` seed mechanism shipped by PR #434 was proposed and shipped as a "durable fix" for approval-prompt fatigue that only ever existed because the operator bypassed `xt claude` (which already adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions` automatically at `worktree-session.ts:1223`). The mechanism does not solve a real problem: any correctly-launched worker via `xt claude` never sees the approvals; any main-pane Claude session that wants bypass can use `shift+tab` mode cycling.

Meanwhile the mechanism actively causes harm:
- `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` currently has `permissionsDefaults` populated with a 45-pattern list that includes items the orchestrator ADMITTED were too broad or wrong: `TodoWrite` (forbidden by CLAUDE.md — beads-only), `Bash(python3:*)` / `Bash(bun:*)` (arbitrary exec), `Bash(awk:*)` / `Bash(sed:*)` (write via `-i`), `Bash(xt:*)` / `Bash(xtmux:*)` / `Bash(sp:*)` / `Bash(pi:*)` (heavy actions like publish/kill), `Bash(chmod/mv/touch/ln:*)` (mutating), `WebFetch` / `WebSearch` / `Agent` (high-impact).
- Every `xt update --apply` propagates these patterns to every xtrm-managed repo's `.claude/settings.json` — the operator's over-inclusive list becomes durable global policy.
- The code path in `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts` (or the equivalent seed logic PR #434 added) reads `permissionsDefaults` and injects them into `.claude/settings.json` on install/reload.

## SUCCESS

- `~/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` no longer contains a `permissionsDefaults` key.
- `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts` (and any related file PR #434 touched) no longer references `permissionsDefaults`. The seed for `.claude/settings.json` `permissions` block is back to `{ allow: [], defaultMode: 'default' }` OR whatever existed pre-PR#434.
- Existing `.claude/settings.json` files in xtmux/specialists/core with the leftover 45-pattern block are NOT auto-touched by this PR (operator commits/cleans those separately — this bead does not touch repo-tracked state).
- Existing tests updated: `install-integration.test.ts` regressions PR #434 added should be removed; other tests should still pass unchanged.
- `~/.claude/settings.json` orchestrator patch backup at `.bak-r6g` — reference only; not part of this PR.

## SCOPE

- `/home/dawid/dev/core/cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts` (revert seed logic)
- `/home/dawid/dev/core/cli/src/tests/install-integration.test.ts` (revert the tests PR #434 added)
- `/home/dawid/dev/core/.xtrm/config/hooks.json` (remove `permissionsDefaults`)
- Any other file PR #434 touched — find them with `git log --format='%H' --all --grep='xtmux-r6g.7\|permissionsDefaults\|seed Claude permission' | head -5` and `git show <sha> --stat`

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT touch existing `.claude/settings.json` files in xtmux/specialists — those have the leftover patterns from prior `xt update --apply` runs. Operator will clean separately.
- Do NOT touch `~/.claude/settings.json` (user's global) — leave the operator's `.bak-r6g` restore workflow intact.
- Do NOT revert PR #433 (bare `--prompt` sans `--role`) — that was a legitimate independent change.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Small PR. Doc + code revert + test revert.
- Include a PR body section "Why revert" that cites this bead's PROBLEM.
- No new deps.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `grep -rn 'permissionsDefaults' cli/` returns 0 matches
- [ ] `grep -n 'permissionsDefaults' .xtrm/config/hooks.json` returns 0 matches (after PR merges + `xt update --apply`)
- [ ] `npm test` (or the repo's canonical test command) passes
- [ ] `npm run typecheck` clean
- [ ] `xt claude install` on a fresh worktree produces `.claude/settings.json` with the pre-PR#434 shape

## LIBRARIES

N/A — pure revert. No new code, no new deps.

## OUTPUT

Small PR on xtrm-dev/core titled "revert: drop permissionsDefaults seed (PR #434) — mechanism was unneeded". Close bead with PR URL.

Read PR #434's diff first via `gh pr view 434 -R xtrm-dev/core --diff` to know exactly what to undo. The PR added: (a) reader logic in `claude-runtime-sync.ts` or a helper, (b) seed application in the install/reload path, (c) integration tests. Undo all three surgically.

title: fix(cli): pi bare-mode --skill silently ignored (post PR #433)
description:
## PROBLEM

Bare `xt pi <name> --no-attach --prompt "..." --skill multiplexing` accepts `--skill` at the CLI layer but silently ignores it — the skill lines are never injected into pi's initial prompt. Root cause at `cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts:1039`:

```javascript
if (runtime === 'claude' && explicitSkillPaths.length > 0) {
    trustedPrefix = `${claudeExplicitSkillLines(explicitSkillPaths)}\n\n`;
    composedTurn1Body = trustedPrefix + composedTurn1Body;
}
```

Condition excludes `runtime === 'pi'`. Result: pi bare-mode delegates never load their `--skill` argument. Symmetric to the claude bare-mode path but broken.

## SUCCESS

- `xt pi <name> --no-attach --prompt "..." --skill multiplexing-team` produces a pi session whose initial prompt starts with `/skill:multiplexing-team` (pi's slash syntax) — verified via `tmux capture-pane` on the spawned session.
- Multi-skill (`--skill A --skill B`) supported symmetric to claude path.
- Existing --role path unchanged.

## SCOPE

`cli/src/utils/worktree-session.ts` — the `runtime === 'claude'` guard at ~line 1039 in the bare-mode branch (else block starting ~line 1028).

Likely need a small helper `piExplicitSkillLines(paths)` that emits `/skill:<name>` per line, symmetric to `claudeExplicitSkillLines`.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT re-open `--bead` / passthrough in bare mode — separate concern
- Do NOT touch the `--role` path (which uses `resolvedRole.skillPaths` merged with `opts.skills`)

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve pi vs claude slash-syntax difference (`/skill:name` vs `/name`)
- Keep the `checkPositionZeroSlash` invariant working with the new prefix
- No new deps

## VALIDATION

- [ ] New unit test: `worktree-session-role.test.ts` (or bare-mode equivalent) asserts pi bare with `--skill foo --skill bar` produces `/skill:foo\n/skill:bar\n\n<prompt>` as turn-1 body
- [ ] Manual smoke: `xt pi <name> --no-attach --prompt "hi" --skill multiplexing-team` — verify pi loads the skill
- [ ] Existing claude bare `--skill` tests still pass

## LIBRARIES

- Reuse in repo: `claudeExplicitSkillLines(paths)` helper in the same file — model the pi variant after it.
- Installed deps: N/A
- Stdlib: N/A
- New dep candidate: none
- Roll it: yes — 5-10 line helper + guard adjustment

## OUTPUT

Small PR on xtrm-dev/core with the fix + test. Close bead with PR URL.
close_reason: Not a bug — verified worktree-session.ts:659-664 iterates [...role.skillPaths, ...explicitSkillPaths] and emits --skill <path> unconditional on role. The :1039 guard is Claude-only prefix-injection of /<name> turn-1 slash lines; pi doesn't need that path because pi consumes --skill natively. Bare pi --skill DOES reach pi's CLI. Closed while reworking PR #437 docs to match reality.

title: docs(multiplexing): document bare xt claude/pi --prompt launch mode (post PR #433)
description:
## PROBLEM

The `multiplexing` skill (canonical `.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md`) does NOT document the bare `xt claude/pi <name> --prompt "..."` launch mode enabled by PR #433 (xtmux-r6g.6). The skill still teaches only the `--role <specialist>` pattern from PR #391. Downstream: orchestrators lacking `--role` reach for the raw `tmux new-session -d claude` workaround, which also drops the `--dangerously-skip-permissions` flag that the xt wrapper adds automatically (worktree-session.ts:1223).

Concretely observed during xtmux-r6g sprint: orchestrator launched all Claude Code delegates via `tmux new-session -d "claude"` (no permission bypass) → hundreds of manual approval prompts, mixed `/skill:name` (pi syntax) vs `/name` (Claude syntax), and one wedged worker chain because the skill implied `--role` was mandatory.

## SUCCESS

`multiplexing` SKILL.md documents the bare launch mode explicitly:
- `xt claude <name> --no-attach --prompt "<text>"` — no `--role` required
- `xt pi <name> --no-attach --prompt "<text>"` — no `--role` required
- Bare Claude mode adds `--dangerously-skip-permissions` automatically
- Slash-command syntax differs: `/name` for Claude, `/skill:name` for pi
- Pattern 7 (Interactive role coordinator) stays for `--role` use cases; bare mode is the answer when the delegate is a general-purpose worker, not a specialist config

## SCOPE

`/home/dawid/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing/SKILL.md` (canonical).
Optionally mirror in `/home/dawid/dev/core/skills/multiplexing/SKILL.md` if kept in sync.

## NON_GOALS

- Do NOT rewrite Pattern 7 — bare and role modes are complementary
- Do NOT change the CLI (PR #433 already shipped the code side)
- Do NOT touch other skills (delegating, using-specialists) — separate concern

## CONSTRAINTS

- Small doc-only PR
- No new tests required (SKILL.md is prose)
- Reference PR #433 explicitly so future readers can trace history

## VALIDATION

- [ ] `grep -n 'without --role\|bare mode\|--prompt.*no.*role' <canonical path>` returns matches
- [ ] Reader can find the launch pattern under Pattern 2 (Assisted hand-off) or a new Pattern 7b
- [ ] Slash-command syntax difference (`/name` vs `/skill:name`) explicitly documented near the launch section

## LIBRARIES

N/A — pure docs edit; no new deps or code.

## OUTPUT

Small PR on xtrm-dev/core with the SKILL.md diff. Bead closed with PR URL.

Correct behavior: xt claude --prompt '/name <instructions>' is the canonical bare-mode shape — Claude Code resolves the slash at turn-1 and expands the skill body into system prompt by design. xtrm-8zsi1 kept role.systemPrompt small; skill-via-slash landing in system prompt is intended, not a leak. title: Remove vendored Pi auto-update extension
description:
## PROBLEM

The retired Pi auto-update extension is no longer configured or registered, but its source, package shims, runtime inventory entry, legacy migration mapping, mirrored payloads, and generated references remain. This dead payload creates misleading package noise and can be accidentally restored by sync/update flows.

## SUCCESS

No shipped XTRM/Pi package, runtime inventory, legacy mapping, generated payload, or active documentation/test fixture contains the retired auto-update extension. Unrelated uses of the phrase auto-update remain untouched.

## SCOPE

- packages/pi-extensions/src/shared/legacy-path-map.ts

## NON_GOALS

- Do not change Pi core update behavior or `pi update`.
- Do not remove unrelated documentation phrases such as service-skill auto-updates.
- Do not change active extension behavior.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Delete rather than deprecate or add another disabled-list entry.
- Preserve plugin-era cleanup recognition if it is needed to delete stale consumer installs; otherwise justify removal with tests.
- Regenerate tracked assets using repository scripts where available.
- No new runtime logging is needed because this removes an unreachable extension; validation evidence is command output and package inspection.

title: Show parent-child context in expanded Pi beads footer
description:
## PROBLEM

The expanded Pi beads footer only renders an active epic tree. In-progress work that belongs to an ordinary parent-child group has no sibling context, so completed siblings and the active child are invisible together.

## SUCCESS

When no active epic is available, the expanded `/beads` / Alt+G footer renders the first active structural parent-child group: its parent plus all direct children, including closed children while that group still has active work. It does not infer groups from `discovered-from`, blocking, or related edges.

## SCOPE

- `packages/pi-extensions/extensions/custom-footer/index.ts`
- `cli/test/extensions/custom-footer-parity.test.ts`
- `.xtrm/hooks/beads-status-cache.mjs` and its focused test, only to retain the direct parent id in the active-issue cache data.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not change the compact footer, native Alt+B behavior, or the bead graph.
- Do not render `discovered-from`, `blocks`, `relates-to`, `tracks`, or other non-`parent-child` relationships.
- Do not add render-time subprocess calls or a new polling loop.
- Do not render more than one parent group or exceed the existing 50-row expansion cap.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Resolve only structural parent-child data using the existing `bd children <parent> --json` behavior, which includes closed children.
- Fetch only after the expanded view is opened; retain the existing 30-second expanded-data freshness boundary.
- Preserve the current bounded rendering behavior and fail-soft loading state.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Focused custom-footer tests cover a non-epic parent with mixed closed/in-progress children and the one-group bound.
- [ ] Tests prove non-parent dependency metadata cannot create a group.
- [ ] Shared cache tests retain a structural parent id from `bd list` output.
- [ ] Typecheck and Pi-extension runtime verification pass.
- [ ] Manual Pi smoke shows closed siblings and an in-progress child in the expanded Alt+G view.

## OUTPUT

Minimal parent-child-only footer implementation, regression tests, and focused verification evidence.
notes: Implemented parent-child-only expanded footer context. It chooses one active structural parent, calls bd children (which includes closed children), keeps a 30s in-memory group cache and 50-row cap, and never follows non-parent edges. Added fallback bd show(active) for older cache payloads missing parent ids. Evidence: custom-footer parity tests pass (10 tests); beads-status-cache node tests 15/15; cli typecheck + pi-extension runtime verification pass; global Pi fresh tmux smoke via physical Alt+G displayed xtrm-vu2ro parent with xtrm-vu2ro.1 and had no shortcut/theme/extension conflicts. Full cli suite remains baseline-unrelated: 12 failed, 771 passed, 98 skipped across registry/install/init tests; custom-footer suite is green.
close_reason: Implemented parent-child-only expanded footer context; focused tests, typecheck/runtime verification, and true-global Alt+G Pi smoke passed.

title: xt migrate/update should not leave hundreds of dirty tracked files in consumer repos
description:
PROBLEM: v0.10.3 fleet migration + v0.10.4 hook path fix left ~300 dirty files per consumer repo. Two orthogonal issues:

1. .xtrm/skills/default/** was tracked in v1 layout. xt migrate skills v1→v2 deletes on disk but doesn't touch git — every operator sees ~300 unstaged D lines. Cleaned manually across 12 repos on 2026-07-13 (fix(xtrm): finalize v2 skills migration commits).

2. Runtime state was accidentally tracked in v1 templates: .xtrm/skills/state.json, .xtrm/worktrees/* gitlinks, .pi/skills/. These are per-machine and should never be tracked.

SUCCESS: (a) xt migrate skills --apply auto-stages the retirement (git rm --cached -r on the v1 default/ tree) and warns 'run git commit to persist migration' — or offers a --commit flag with a canonical message. (b) Runtime paths gitignored by fresh init template (.xtrm/skills/state.json, .xtrm/worktrees/, .pi/skills/, .xtrm/cache/). (c) xt update --apply that modifies tracked files (.claude/settings.json + .xtrm/config/hooks.json for hook-path hotfixes) auto-stages them and prints operator instructions.

SCOPE: cli/src/commands/migrate.ts (post-migration git housekeeping), cli/src/commands/update.ts (post-apply housekeeping), .xtrm/config templates for fresh init .gitignore.

NON_GOALS: no auto-commit without operator confirmation flag; no push.

CONSTRAINTS: never bypass beads commit-gate; never commit while any bead is claimed; respect existing user gitignore entries additively.

VALIDATION: unit test that xt migrate skills --apply on a fresh v1 fixture stages the D tree; xt update --apply on a fixture with hook drift stages the M; --commit flag creates a canonical commit.

OUTPUT: 3 code paths + gitignore template + tests + CHANGELOG entry.

CONTEXT: Fleet cleanup done manually 2026-07-13 across barchart-scraper, darth-feedor, economic-data, platform, quant, sierra-vps, terminal, terminalbeta, treasury-cb, website, xtmux. See commits chore(xtrm): finalize v2 skills migration in each. infra + 4 repos with real user content in local-legacy remain for operator review.
close_reason: Landed stageMigrationChanges helper wired into xt migrate / xt update / xt init. Auto-stages tracked mods+deletions after fleet events, untracks known runtime paths from index, seeds runtime gitignore block on fresh init. Never commits. 11 tests green, 797/797 full cli suite. Fleet dirty-state accumulation cannot happen again.

Pi custom-footer duplicates statusline logic and does no cross-agent coalescing. Design (xtrm-77t9q notes) requires it to consume the same shared cache as Claude statusline for compact rendering, plus render an on-demand nested epic descendants tree on Ctrl+O.

## SUCCESS

- Compact line matches Claude statusline (same formatter — extracted to shared module).
- Expanded (Ctrl+O) view renders nested descendants tree (indent-2 per level, cap N=50, +M more overflow); on absent/stale descendants field, shows skeleton and triggers on-demand refresh.
- Tests cover: fixture-cache render, expanded tree reconstruction from nested JSON, skeleton-then-repaint flow.

## SCOPE
- packages/pi-extensions/extensions/custom-footer/**
- packages/pi-extensions/src/extensions/custom-footer.ts
- cli/test/extensions/custom-footer-parity.test.ts (extend)

## DEPENDS ON

## NON_GOALS
- No Claude statusline changes.
- No bd hook wiring.
- No changes to the schema defined by xtrm-77t9q.1.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Same TTLs (5s compact, 30s descendants).
- Render zero-I/O; refresh detached via SubprocessRunner.
- Preserve existing session-flow / footer dispose semantics.

## VALIDATION
- Custom-footer parity test green.
- Manual: pi footer shows same counts as Claude statusline in same worktree.

## OUTPUT
Refactored custom-footer + expanded tree renderer + tests.
notes: FOLLOW-UP FIX: decoupled epic-tree expansion from Pi's global Ctrl+O tool-output state. Ctrl+O remains tool-only; Ctrl+B and /beads independently toggle the beads tree. Regression test proves toolsExpanded=true alone does not reveal descendants; focused footer 6/6, typecheck, diff check pass. GitNexus impact/detect retried but unavailable due spawn gitnexus ENOENT; prior indexed footer impact was LOW.

title: Claude statusline + shared beads-status cache library
description:
## PROBLEM
Statusline shows 'no open issues' because bd calls exceed the 250ms run() timeout, and there is no shared cross-agent cache for compact status. Design (xtrm-77t9q notes) resolves this via a repo-scoped shared JSON cache with single-flight lease, TTL-based refresh, and fail-soft stale marker.

## SUCCESS
- New shared cache module written+consumed by statusline.
- Statusline renders the compact line spec (12 open · 2 in progress · epic <slug> (n/m done)) with fail-soft stale marker.
- 250ms bug fixed via split runFast (git) / runSlow (bd) timeouts.
- All rendering is zero-subprocess/zero-fs-write (read-only cache).
- Tests cover: fixture-cache snapshot render, stale marker, lease contention (single-flight), worktree common-dir path convergence.

## SCOPE
- New .xtrm/hooks/beads-status-cache.mjs (shared module: reader, atomic writer, lease, invalidate check, bd query wrappers, schema { v:1, ts, stale, counts, activeEpic, activeIssues })
- .xtrm/hooks/statusline.mjs (refactor to consume cache; keep detached refresh; fix timeout split)
- .xtrm/hooks/statusline.test.mjs (extend)
- New .xtrm/hooks/beads-status-cache.test.mjs

## NON_GOALS
- No Pi custom-footer changes (owned by xtrm-77t9q.2).
- No bd git hook touch-invalidation this task (TTL-only reconciliation is sufficient MVP; hook wiring is a followup).
- No descendants tree materialization (Pi expanded view is xtrm-77t9q.2 scope).

## CONSTRAINTS
- Cache path <mainRoot>/.xtrm/cache/beads-status.json where mainRoot = dirname(git rev-parse --git-common-dir), atomic rename write, 0600 perms.
- TTL 5s compact fields.
- Render budget <= 50ms; refresh budget <= 2s.
- No secrets/descriptions in cache payload; only render fields.

## VALIDATION
- npx vitest .xtrm/hooks/ green.
- Manual: statusline shows real counts within 5s in main worktree; still shows counts (dim) if bd is stopped.

## OUTPUT
Refactored statusline + new cache lib + tests.
notes: PR: https://github.com/xtrm-dev/core/pull/404
close_reason: Shared beads-status cache module + statusline consumer landed; 17/17 tests green; smoke on core repo confirms real counts render (58 open · 3 in progress) instead of 'no open issues' fallback. Fixes the 250ms subprocess-timeout bug via runFast/runBd split. Unblocks xtrm-77t9q.2 (Pi custom-footer consumer) — contract published to session  and stored as bd memory beads-status-shared-cache-contract.

### Finding 1
- ID: SEC-PI-RUNTIME-001

    - delete `xtrmExternalCompact`

title: Audit xtprompt prompt-smith extension
description:
## PROBLEM

The shipped Pi xtprompt extension is branded and instructed as a Mercury-specific prompt smith, even though it belongs in this generic xtrm-tools repository. Its prompt transformation and context gathering may also diverge from the canonical planning and prompt-improving skills, and it may ignore the active chat when rewriting an editor draft.

## SUCCESS

Produce an evidence-backed audit that identifies every Mercury-specific leak, structural or behavioral mismatch with planning/prompt-improving (including their references), and whether Pi's extension/session APIs can safely provide relevant prior conversation context. Findings are prioritized and cite exact files/lines or symbols, with a minimal remediation design but no implementation.

## SCOPE

- packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtprompt/index.ts
- packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtprompt/package.json
- .xtrm/skills/default/planning/SKILL.md and evals
- .xtrm/skills/default/prompt-improving/SKILL.md, README.md, and references/
- Installed Pi extension/session/TUI documentation and relevant examples

## NON_GOALS

- No code or documentation edits
- No redesign of unrelated Pi extensions
- No Mercury project inspection beyond identifying leaked assumptions
- No release, commit, or publish work

## CONSTRAINTS

- READ_ONLY
- Distinguish confirmed defects from optional improvements
- Prefer the smallest generic design that reuses canonical skill rules rather than duplicating project-specific doctrine
- Treat session content as potentially sensitive; recommend bounded context extraction, not indiscriminate transcript forwarding

## VALIDATION

- Cross-check each finding against current source and current Pi docs/examples
- Verify the feasibility and limitations of reading the previous assistant/user messages through SessionManager
- Check package metadata, command/shortcut naming, intent detection, prompt contract, context gathering, model call, cancellation, and UI mode handling
- Run existing focused checks if the package exposes any; otherwise report the coverage gap

## OUTPUT

A prioritized audit with severity, evidence, user impact, and minimal recommended correction; include an explicit answer on chat-context support and a concise target architecture.

SCRUTINY: none
notes: Audit complete. Confirmed: (1) Mercury branding/domain rules are hard-coded into every rewrite; (2) transformation diverges from canonical planning + prompt-improving intent/ambiguity/XML/reference behavior; (3) SessionManager can provide prior chat context, demonstrated by Pi qna/summarize examples, but xtprompt only reads git branch + first project-wide in-progress bead; (4) ctx.hasUI incorrectly admits RPC even though ctx.ui.custom is TUI-only; (5) model auth env is dropped; (6) no xtprompt-focused tests exist and verify:runtime only checks asset presence. Package runtime asset check passes; GitNexus impact for detectIntent/buildSystemPrompt/gatherContext is LOW (one direct caller: enhance).

title: Add pi extension latency isolation smoke for xtrm-ui and xtmux
description:

It must explicitly identify loaded packages and raw extension files, and include a verdict taxonomy: PASS/no evidence, SUSPECT/needs isolation, CONFIRMED/bottleneck.

NON_GOALS: Do not benchmark model latency. Do not require external services. Do not permanently disable user extensions.

CONSTRAINTS: Measurements must be cheap and reversible. Prefer env toggles or temporary extension renames over reinstalling packages. Preserve bd/security gates unless explicitly testing no-extension baseline.

title: Post-compaction: audit xtrm-ui tool rendering overhead and pi tool-call slowdown
description:

It re-registers/wraps built-in tools, stamps metadata through tool_result middleware, computes previews/diffs/line counts, and may be fighting pi's native tool rendering pipeline. Separately, recent investigation observed pi still feels too slow at each tool call and may hang or delay on agent turn end, even after auto-update/oh-pi cleanup improved startup-ish behavior. This needs a focused post-compaction audit before more UI work accumulates complexity.

SCOPE: Explore pi extension load/render/tool lifecycle in /home/dawid/dev/core/packages/pi-extensions, especially extensions/xtrm-ui/index.ts and format.ts. Compare current xtrm-ui replacement-style rendering against vanilla pi's built-in renderer and identify what can be deleted or moved to thinner decoration. Include slowdown triage for per-tool-call and turn-end hooks across loaded extensions: xtrm-ui, beads/edit gate, git-checkpoint, quality-gates if still loaded through settings, serena/pi-serena tooling, and the recently created ~/dev/xtmux multiplexing extension as a suspect. Treat xtmux as a hypothesis, not a conclusion.

SUCCESS: Produce a concrete implementation plan with: (1) minimal renderer architecture that preserves the desired visual output while avoiding duplicate execute/tool plumbing when possible, (2) measured or evidence-backed bottleneck list for tool-call latency and agent-turn-end hangs, (3) a safe migration plan with smoke tests for bash/read/write/edit/grep/find/ls rendering, including success and failure rows, (4) recommendation on whether xtmux extension contributes to latency.

NON_GOALS: Do not rewrite xtrm-ui during planning. Do not disable arbitrary extensions permanently without evidence. Do not optimize by removing required bd claim gates, security hooks, or payload-preserving behavior for read/search tools.

CONSTRAINTS: Use pi docs as authority for package/install/rendering behavior before changing assumptions. Prefer deleting execution/meta plumbing over adding more state. Preserve model-facing tool payloads; UI compaction must not blind headless agents. Capture exact install/load paths using pi list and docs/packages.md before testing. If investigating xtmux, inspect its extension hook registrations and measure whether it runs per tool_call/tool_result/turn_end.

It must also include a performance smoke comparing vanilla/no-extension or xtrm-ui-disabled latency vs xtrm-ui/xtmux-enabled latency for at least several tool calls, plus evidence from logs or timestamps around turn_end. Test gate should include a human-visible TUI rendering check and a scripted timing check.

Include files/symbols touched, hook/event lifecycle map, before/after screenshots or text captures of tool rows, and a verdict on xtmux involvement: PASS/no evidence, SUSPECT/needs isolation, or CONFIRMED/bottleneck.
notes: FINDINGS 2026-07-10: xtmux extension suspicion is valid. Installed global extension exists at ~/.pi/agent/extensions/xtmux-agent-state.ts -> /home/dawid/dev/xtmux/extensions/pi-agent-state.ts, so it is likely loaded even though pi list does not show raw extension files. title: xt migrate --restore <backup>: restore per-repo skills/hooks from migration tarball
description:
## PROBLEM

Batch E of xtrm-bq7yd shipped xt migrate --apply with tarball backups at ~/.xtrm/migration-backups/{skills,hooks}-<repo>-<ts>.tgz but no restore path. If an operator regrets a migration or the global tree diverges, recovery today is manual tar -xzf into .xtrm/ + hand-editing .xtrm/state/known-repos.json. Follow-up to Batch E, deferred at merge, and the natural completion of xtrm-svb0n (source-repo guard shipped 2026-07-09).

## SUCCESS

xt migrate --restore <backup-path> --repo <repo> extracts a migration tarball back into <repo>/.xtrm/, refuses if the target subdirectory already exists (unless --force), and clears the corresponding migrated flag in known-repos state. --dry-run prints what would extract without touching filesystem.

## SCOPE

cli/src/commands/migrate.ts:
- Add --restore <path> option (mutually exclusive with target arg + --apply).
- Detect component from backup filename prefix (skills-* → .xtrm/skills, hooks-* → .xtrm/hooks); refuse on unknown prefix.
- Refuse if <repo>/.xtrm/<component> already exists AND not --force.
- Extract via tar -xzf into <repo>/.xtrm/ (parent-dir extraction).
- Update known-repos.json via markRepoMigrated({ skillsMigrated: false } / { hooksMigrated: false }) — new inverse helper OR pass explicit false.
- appendMigrationLog with event 'skills.restore.ok' / 'hooks.restore.ok'.

cli/src/utils/known-repos.ts:
- Extend markRepoMigrated to accept false values (currently only unions truthy). No new function.

## NON_GOALS

- Auto-selecting the latest backup (operator names the tarball).
- Restoring settings.json entries that cleanSettingsJsonEntries removed (deferred; document as known limitation).
- Cross-component atomic restore (each restore is independent).

## CONSTRAINTS

- Source-repo guard applies to --restore too (same isSourceRepo check) unless --force-source.
- Backup path must be an absolute or ~-expandable path; refuse relative paths with explicit message.
- No backup path traversal: after extraction verify all top-level entries land under <repo>/.xtrm/ (realpath containment).

## VALIDATION

- cd cli && npm run build
- cd cli && npx vitest run src/tests/migrate.test.ts (existing 14/14 + 4 new)
- New tests: 'restore skills backup extracts into repo', 'restore refuses when target exists', '--force overrides target-exists', '--dry-run prints planned extraction only'.
- Manual smoke: migrate a fake repo → restore → diff shows equivalence.

## OUTPUT

Files touched + new test count + smoke evidence.
close_reason: shipped xt migrate --restore <backup>: detects component from filename prefix, refuses target-exists without --force, --dry-run works, source-repo guard still applies, path traversal check post-extract. 4 new tests pass (18/18); smoke roundtrip verified. Known limitation: does not restore settings.json entries removed by cleanSettingsJsonEntries.

- BJ-SEC-003 (low, CWE-377): non-atomic writes (writeJson + appendFile) can leave partial JSON on crash; installedAt fingerprint is unnecessary metadata.

## SUCCESS

Single commit on feature/xtrm-bq7yd.10-executor addressing all 3:

FIX BJ-SEC-001 + BJ-SEC-003 (atomic writes + symlink defense on writes):
  Add helper writeJsonAtomic(targetPath, data): validates target and parent are not symlinks pointing outside their normal roots (realpath check), writes tmp file '<targetPath>.tmp-<pid>-<rand>' in the same dir, fs.rename to target. Apply to:
  - cli/src/core/global-hooks-bootstrap.ts (~/.xtrm/hooks/state.json)
  - cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts (~/.claude/settings.json in reconcileGlobalClaudeHooks)

  In cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts commandTargetsGlobalHook (~L516-537): after computing resolvedTokenPath, call fs.realpathSync on both globalHooksRoot and resolvedTokenPath (catch ENOENT and return false). Then check if realpath(resolvedTokenPath) is a descendant of realpath(globalHooksRoot). Only descendants of the CANONICAL root count as canonical.

DROP installedAt from _xtrm metadata (BJ-SEC-003 second half):

## Summary

Scoped Batch J security audit found 3 findings. Main risk: global config/hook writes trust filesystem paths under `os.homedir()` and follow symlinks. Canonical-conflict check stays lexical, not `realpath`-based. `state.json` write not atomic.

## Status

findings

## Changes

No files changed. Scan-only.

## Verification

- `bd update xtrm-bq7yd105 --claim`
- `gitnexus_query("global hooks bootstrap runtime sync state.json write", ...)`
- `gitnexus_context("ensureGlobalHooksBootstrapped" | "reconcileGlobalPiHooks" | "safeMergeOwnedHookSettings" | "conflictsWithCanonical" | "tagOwnedWrapper" | "commandTargetsGlobalHook" | "resolveStatePath" | "readInstalledVersion")`
- `git diff 56ff6bea..HEAD -- [scoped files]`
- `nl -ba cli/src/core/global-hooks-bootstrap.ts`
- `nl -ba cli/src/core/pi-runtime-hooks.ts`
- `nl -ba cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts`
- `nl -ba .xtrm/hooks/*.mjs`
- `gitnexus_detect_changes({scope:"compare",base_ref:"56ff6bea"})`

## Risks

- Global writes to `~/.claude/settings.json`, `~/.pi/agent/settings.json`, `~/.xtrm/hooks/*`, `~/.xtrm/hooks/state.json` can follow symlinks.
- Foreign-entry canonical conflict logic does not dereference symlinks before trust decision.
- `installedAt` ownership metadata remains stable across merges and fingerprints install age.

## Follow-ups

- Add symlink-safe write helper: `lstat` each path component, reject symlink targets, write temp file in same dir, `fsync`, `rename`.
- Add `realpath` containment check for canonical hook detection and for all target roots before copy/write.
- Remove `installedAt` from persisted hook ownership metadata, or replace with coarse non-identifying generation marker if needed for idempotency.
- Make `state.json` atomic and avoid second `appendFile` step.

## Security Audit Summary

- Scope reviewed:  
  `cli/src/core/global-hooks-bootstrap.ts`  
  `cli/src/core/global-hooks-flag.ts`  
  `cli/src/core/pi-runtime-hooks.ts`  
  `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts`  
  `cli/src/commands/{init,install,update,bootstrap}.ts`  
  `scripts/gen-registry.mjs`  
  `.xtrm/hooks/*.mjs`
- Overall risk: medium
- Mode(s) used: static secure-code review, agent/config security scan, bounty-style exploitability triage
- Commands/sources used: GitNexus query/context/detect_changes; local `git diff`; line-number review with `nl -ba`

## Findings

- ID: BJ-SEC-001  
  Severity: medium  
  Category/CWE when applicable: CWE-59 Improper Link Resolution Before File Access  
  Evidence:  
  - `cli/src/core/global-hooks-bootstrap.ts:103-113` uses `fs.remove(targetHooksRoot)`, `fs.copy(...)`, `fs.copy(...)`, `fs.writeJson(statePath, ...)`, `fs.appendFile(statePath, ...)` on paths from `os.homedir()`  
  - `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:257-260`, `291-294` writes `~/.claude/settings.json` directly  
  - `cli/src/core/pi-runtime-hooks.ts:46-49` writes `~/.pi/agent/settings.json` directly  
  Reachability/exploitability: Local same-user attacker can pre-place symlink at target file or ancestor path under home dir before privileged CLI run in same account context. Code performs no `lstat`/`realpath`/`O_NOFOLLOW` validation.  
  Impact: Arbitrary same-user file clobber inside writable filesystem namespace; corrupt runtime settings or redirect writes outside intended `~/.claude` / `~/.pi` / `~/.xtrm` targets.  
  Recommended fix: Resolve and validate parent dirs with `realpath`; reject symlinks on target and parents; write temp file in same directory, `fsync`, then `rename`; avoid `fs.remove` on symlinkable roots without precheck.  
  Verification after fix: Create symlinked `settings.json` and symlinked `.xtrm/hooks` target in temp home; confirm command aborts without modifying symlink target.

- ID: BJ-SEC-002  
  Severity: low  
  Category/CWE when applicable: CWE-59 / CWE-22 path trust flaw  
  Evidence:  
  - `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:516-525` `conflictsWithCanonical` trusts `commandTargetsGlobalHook(...)`  
  - `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:528-537` uses `path.resolve(expandTilde(token))` + `path.relative(globalHooksRoot, resolvedTokenPath)` only  
  - No `realpath` call in canonical-path check path  
  Reachability/exploitability: Foreign hook command string like `node "~/.xtrm/hooks/link.mjs"` passes lexical containment even if `link.mjs` is symlink to non-canonical target. Check does not prove command resolves inside canonical hooks root.  
  Impact: Fix-loop goal not met. Symlinked path under `~/.xtrm/hooks/` can masquerade as canonical-adjacent during conflict classification. Current code only warns/preserves, so protection against hijack-by-symlink is absent.  
  Recommended fix: `realpath` both `globalHooksRoot` and extracted command path, then enforce descendant check on dereferenced path. Treat failed `realpath` as non-canonical/untrusted.  
  Verification after fix: Foreign wrapper pointing to `~/.xtrm/hooks/link.mjs -> /tmp/evil.mjs` must classify as non-canonical.

- ID: BJ-SEC-003  
  Severity: low  
  Category/CWE when applicable: CWE-377 insecure temp/write pattern, integrity weakness  
  Evidence:  
  - `cli/src/core/global-hooks-bootstrap.ts:108-113` writes `state.json` with `writeJson` then separate `appendFile`  
  - `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:257-260`, `291-294`; `cli/src/core/pi-runtime-hooks.ts:46-49` same pattern for settings files  
  - `cli/src/core/claude-runtime-sync.ts:402-412` preserves `_xtrm.installedAt` from prior wrapper  
  Reachability/exploitability: Power loss/crash/interruption between write and append can leave partial/truncated JSON. Metadata persistence not remote leak, but stable fingerprint remains in global settings.  
  Impact: Mostly integrity/forensics issue. Non-atomic state update can brick future bootstrap logic or leave malformed settings. `installedAt` exposes installation age/history to any local reader of settings file.  
  Recommended fix: Atomic temp-file write + rename. Emit trailing newline in same write buffer. Drop `installedAt` from persisted `_xtrm` metadata unless hard requirement exists.  
  Verification after fix: Fault-injection test around write path leaves either old valid file or new valid file, never partial JSON. Re-run merge twice and confirm no timestamp fingerprint remains.

## Dependency Advisory Triage

No dependency-audit findings in scoped delta. No manifest/lockfile security delta required for this review.

## Non-findings / Dropped Noise

- `os.homedir()` path construction alone not reported as path traversal bug. No remote/user-input route in scoped code; risk comes from filesystem symlink abuse around home-dir targets, not string concatenation itself.
- `.xtrm/hooks/*.mjs` fast-fail guards reviewed. No new high-signal injection sink introduced by Batch J delta within non-goal boundary.
- `shouldUseGlobalHooks()` env gate in `cli/src/core/global-hooks-flag.ts:1-3` not security issue by itself. Feature flag only.

## Residual Risk and Follow-ups

- Highest-value next bead: implement shared symlink-safe atomic writer for all global settings/state paths.
- Add regression tests for symlinked target file, symlinked parent dir, symlink inside `~/.xtrm/hooks`, interrupted write.
- Re-audit after fix loop because GitNexus `detect_changes` flagged compare scope risk as critical breadth, though concrete reachable findings here rank medium overall.

- Claimed: `xtrm-bq7yd105`
- Closed: `xtrm-bq7yd105`

title: Port PR #351 (xtrm-824xs draft/ready gate + rule #15) to specialists master, then re-vendor using-specialists-v3
description:
## PROBLEM

PR #351 (xtrm-tools, xtrm-824xs) added the \`contract:draft/ready\` bead-promotion gate + rule #15 hard-refuse + Draft-Beads section to \`.xtrm/skills/default/using-specialists-v3/SKILL.md\`, bumping the vendored version from 3.6 → 3.7. CLAUDE.md rule: *"Specialist-owned skills must be edited in the specialists repo first, then vendored into xtrm-tools."* PR #351 violated that — it edited the vendored copy in-tree without first porting to specialists.

Result: specialists master (~/dev/specialists) is at v3.5 and lacks the draft/ready gate content. The vendor manifest hash was papered over in a follow-up patch (this bead's parent PR) so CI is green, but the divergence remains. If anyone runs \`npm run vendor-specialists-skills\`, PR #351's content will be silently reverted.

## SUCCESS

- \`~/dev/specialists/config/skills/using-specialists-v3/SKILL.md\` on master contains the draft/ready gate + rule #15 + Draft Beads And The Promotion Gate section at v3.7.
- \`~/dev/specialists/CHANGELOG.md\` records the v3.6 → v3.7 bump with the same rationale as xtrm-tools PR #351.
- After running \`npm run vendor-specialists-skills\` in xtrm-tools, \`git diff\` shows only manifest-hash change (or nothing) — SKILL.md content already matches.
- \`npm run check:specialists-vendor\` still green post-re-vendor.

## SCOPE

**In ~/dev/specialists**:
- \`config/skills/using-specialists-v3/SKILL.md\` — bump 3.5 → 3.7, add rule #15, add Draft Beads section (copy from xtrm-tools current vendored copy).
- \`CHANGELOG.md\` — entry for v3.6 (xtrm-tools PR #349, parent-child nesting + title convention) and v3.7 (xtrm-tools PR #351, draft/ready gate).
- Any node/lib rebuild artifacts as required by specialists' release flow (\`dist/\` — check whether this is auto-generated or hand-committed there).

**In xtrm-tools**:
- Run \`npm run vendor-specialists-skills\` after specialists master carries the port.
- Commit the resulting no-op-or-hash-update.

## NON_GOALS

- Reverting PR #351's changes to \`.xtrm/skills/default/planning/SKILL.md\`, \`using-xtrm/SKILL.md\`, \`templates/claude-md-fragments/bd-workflow.md\` — those are xtrm-tools-owned, no vendoring needed.
- v3.6 archaeology — PR #349 also bypassed the vendor flow. If specialists master is at v3.5 today, the v3.6 changes need porting too. If a specialists branch already carries them, use that.
- Redesigning the vendor process to prevent this recurrence — separate concern.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Do NOT run \`vendor-specialists-skills\` in xtrm-tools before specialists master carries the port — that would revert PR #351.
- Two-step commit: land specialists change first, verify hash in \`specialists\` dist output, then re-vendor here.
- Keep \`.xtrm/specialists-source.json\` in sync with the specialists version once ported.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] \`sha256sum ~/dev/specialists/config/skills/using-specialists-v3/SKILL.md\` after port matches \`sha256sum ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/default/using-specialists-v3/SKILL.md\` byte-for-byte.
- [ ] \`~/dev/specialists\` CHANGELOG has entries for v3.6 and v3.7 with correct authorship / cross-links to xtrm-tools PRs.
- [ ] \`npm run vendor-specialists-skills\` in xtrm-tools is a no-op-on-content (only manifest metadata regenerates).
- [ ] \`npm run check:specialists-vendor\` green.

## OUTPUT

- Specialists PR/commit reference.
- Diff summary in xtrm-tools showing manifest regeneration.

## APPROACH NOTES

The specialists repo currently has an in-flight branch \`origin/feature/unitAI-fxgt1-draft-bead-gate\` (commit c899ce94) that started this work but never landed on master and its SKILL.md hash matches master (\`a9dfcb44…\`) — i.e. the branch didn't actually change SKILL.md content, only other files. So the port here is a fresh edit against specialists master using PR #351 as the source diff.

Also has 8 uncommitted files in ~/dev/specialists working tree — clean up or rebase before starting the port.

title: Batch G: Legacy dead-code removal (per-runtime active/{claude,pi}, ~/.agents/skills, stale xtrm-loader mirrors)
description:
## PROBLEM

Legacy code paths accumulate over migrations. Post-migration there are three classes of dead code to remove: (1) per-runtime `active/{claude,pi}` scan in `clean.ts` (already stale — materializer writes flat active), (2) `~/.agents/skills` fallback branches (deprecated pre-2.0), (3) three mirrored copies of `xtrm-loader/index.ts`. Leaving them creates ambiguity for future maintainers and wastes surface area.

## SUCCESS

- All three legacy branches deleted with tests updated or removed.
- No references to `active/claude`, `active/pi`, `~/.agents/skills` remain in `cli/src/`, `packages/pi-extensions/`, or `.xtrm/hooks/`.
- Two stale xtrm-loader mirrors (`.xtrm/ext-src/xtrm-loader/`, `.xtrm/packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-loader/`) are deleted.
- `xt clean --skills-only` still works, cleaning only the current flat `active/` layout.
- Grep of `git grep -E "active/(claude|pi)|\.agents/skills"` returns no live-code hits.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/clean.ts:35, 99-100` — remove `ACTIVE_SKILLS_RUNTIMES = ['claude','pi']` and per-runtime scan; simplify to flat `active/` scan.
- `cli/src/commands/clean.ts:144-149, 337` — remove `~/.agents/skills` deprecation branch.
- `cli/src/core/skills-scaffold.ts:144-146` — delete `.agents/skills` deprecation-notice branch.
- `cli/src/core/skills-runtime-views.ts:78, 94-95` — remove `hasDeprecatedAgentsSkillsPath` field.
- `cli/src/core/plugin-era-cleanup.ts:268`, `cli/src/core/preflight.ts:57` — legacy `~/.agents/skills` handling deleted.
- `packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-loader/index.ts:30-32` — drop `~/.agents/skills` and `~/.pi/agent/skills` fallbacks (loader targets `~/.claude/skills` directly).
- Delete `.xtrm/ext-src/xtrm-loader/` (mirror).
- Delete `.xtrm/packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-loader/` (mirror).
- `cli/test/extensions/xtrm-loader.test.ts:30, 53-56` — remove legacy fallback test branches.

title: Batch F: xt skills scope flip — list/enable/disable default to --global, compose global+local state
description:
## PROBLEM

`xt skills` command already has `--global`/`--local` scope plumbing (`skills.ts:48-62`) but only that one command uses it, and it defaults to `local`. With SSOT moving to HOME, `xt skills list` should show what's globally active by default, and enable/disable should mutate global state. Users on the new model expect this; keeping the local default would be surprising.

## SUCCESS

- `xt skills list` (no flags) shows global scope: global default + globally enabled optional packs + global user packs.
- `xt skills list --local` shows the composed effective view (global base + local user + local pack overrides).
- `xt skills enable/disable <pack>` mutates `~/.xtrm/skills/state.json` by default.
- `xt skills create-pack <name>` stays `--local` default (project-scoped authoring is more natural).
- `state.json` composition rule: global sets baseline enabled packs; project `.xtrm/skills/state.json` records overrides only (delta).

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/skills.ts:48-54` — `resolveScope` returns `'global'` by default for `list`, `enable`, `disable` (per-subcommand default). `create-pack` keeps `'local'`.
- `cli/src/commands/skills.ts:104-146` — `collectListState` composes global + local: if `--local`, produce merged view; if `--global`, produce global only.
- `cli/src/commands/skills.ts:203-231` — enable/disable target the correct `state.json`.
- `cli/src/core/skills-state.ts:22-88` — `readStateOrDefault` accepts a `mergeStrategy: 'override'|'compose'` so a project state can be interpreted as a delta on top of global.
- `cli/src/core/skills-materializer.ts:29-88` — `selectRuntimeSkills` composes global default+enabled + project deltas.

## NON_GOALS

- Adding a `xt skills copy-to-global` subcommand — out of scope; users move manually or via migrate skill.
- Changing state schema major version — extensions are additive.
- Renaming any subcommand.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Backwards-compat: if a user has a local `state.json` with `enabledPacks.claude = ["security-ops"]`, that stays enabled locally after the flip. It composes: global enabled ∪ local enabled.
- `xt skills list --local` output must clearly label which packs come from global vs local (e.g. `security-ops [global]`, `my-project-pack [local]`).
- Error text: `xt skills disable <pack>` where pack is globally enabled and command run without `--global` prints "pack is globally enabled; use `--global` to disable everywhere or leave alone and add a local override".
- Logging: state mutations emit `skills-state.mutation` with `{scope, action, pack, runtime, before, after}` fields.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Fresh install: `xt skills list` shows only global default + globally enabled optional; no per-repo output.
- [ ] Fixture repo with `state.json.enabledPacks.claude = ["security-ops"]` (local): `xt skills list --local` shows composed view including `security-ops` labeled `[local]`.
- [ ] `xt skills enable code-quality` (no flags): writes `~/.xtrm/skills/state.json`; `~/.xtrm/skills/active/` rebuilt to include code-quality skills; log event `skills-state.mutation` recorded.
- [ ] `xt skills enable code-quality --local` in a repo: writes `<repo>/.xtrm/skills/state.json`; project active view includes code-quality; global unchanged.
- [ ] `xt skills disable <globally-enabled-pack>` (no `--global`): prints helpful error, exit 1.
- [ ] `xt skills create-pack my-pack` (no flags): creates `<repo>/.xtrm/skills/user/packs/my-pack/`.
- [ ] Updated tests: `skills-command.test.ts`, `skills-command-json.test.ts`, `skills-state.test.ts` all green.
- [ ] JSON output of `xt skills list --json` includes a top-level `scope` field.

## OUTPUT

Command diff, help text before/after, sample list output for both scopes, log evidence of state mutation, and test file changes.

## APPROACH NOTES

The compose rule is: `effective(runtime) = union(global.enabledPacks[runtime], local.enabledPacks[runtime])`. To DISABLE a globally-enabled pack in a specific project, users add a `disabledPacks` array to local state (schema extension). Default this batch supports enable-only override; disable-override can be a follow-up. Consider small helper `composeState(globalState, localState) → effective`.

title: Add xt worktree/branch restart audit for autonomous containers
description:
## PROBLEM

After an autonomous container or operator session restarts, xt can list worktrees and branches but does not provide a single audit of stale managed directories, branch PR state, and remediation hints.

## SUCCESS

xt has a restart-safe audit that reports orphaned managed directories, managed branches without worktrees, PRs needing rebase/conflict attention, and suggested cleanup commands.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/worktree.ts`
- `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts`
- tests under `cli/src/tests/`

## NON_GOALS

- Do not mark specialist jobs cancelled; sp owns job rows.
- Do not run container-specific webhook replay.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Durable target: post-substrate this becomes container/worktree reconciliation data.
- Logging/telemetry: output includes `repo`, `worktree_path`, `branch`, `pr_classification`, `finding_kind`, `suggested_action`, and redacted failure details.
- Must be safe to run repeatedly at container startup and from cron.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Tests cover orphaned managed dirs, branch-without-worktree, worktree-with-closed-PR, and PR-needs-rebase cases.
- [ ] CLI smoke shows idempotent JSON output.

## OUTPUT

Audit command/flag with tests and a sample container-entrypoint invocation for docs to consume.

Chosen command/flag surface and output shape:
- New audit-only command: xt worktree restart-audit [--prefix xt/] [--json]
- Default managed prefix is xt/; --prefix accepts comma-separated conservative prefixes for future bot branches.
- The command is startup/cron safe and idempotent: it only reads git worktree metadata, managed dirs, local branches, and gh PR state. It does not delete branches, remove directories, mark specialist jobs cancelled, or replay webhooks.
- JSON output component: xt.restart_audit
- Finding output component: xt.restart_audit.finding
- Required telemetry fields included per finding: repo, worktree_path, branch, pr_classification, finding_kind, suggested_action, suggestion_command, checked_at_ms, plus pr_url/pr_number and redacted error when available.
