title: Add xt branch GC for merged or closed managed PR branches
description:
## PROBLEM

xt worktrees and PR branches accumulate after sessions and bot runs. The Mercury collaborator design needs branch cleanup based on PR state, but that git plumbing belongs in xt, not in every bot.

## SUCCESS

`xt clean` or `xt worktree prune` can dry-run and apply deletion of managed branches whose PRs are MERGED/CLOSED, while never deleting active or unknown-state branches by default.

## SCOPE

- `cli/src/commands/clean.ts`
- `cli/src/commands/worktree.ts`
- tests under `cli/src/tests/clean.test.ts` / worktree tests

## NON_GOALS

- Do not remove specialist terminal job worktrees; sp still owns job worktree GC.
- Do not delete upstream protected branches.
- Do not delete branches with unknown PR state unless a separate explicit unsafe flag exists.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Default to dry-run or confirmation; apply mode must be explicit.
- Use configurable managed prefixes such as `xt/*` and future bot prefixes, with conservative defaults.
- Logging/telemetry: each candidate emits `branch`, `pr_state`, `action=delete|skip`, `reason`, and outcome.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Tests prove merged/closed candidates are selected and open/unknown branches are skipped.
- [ ] Dry-run output lists exact branches and commands without mutating git.
- [ ] Apply-mode test uses a temp repo/fake remote or mocked git to prove deletion command shape.

## OUTPUT

Branch-GC command/flag, tests, and safety notes for Mercury/container docs.
notes:
Final report for xtrm-lk4on.3:

Changed files:
- cli/src/commands/worktree.ts
- cli/src/commands/help.ts
- cli/src/tests/worktree-pr-status.test.ts

GitNexus impact before edit:
- Ran upstream impact on createWorktreeCommand, getPrStatus, and createHelpCommand in repo /home/dawid/dev/xtrm-tools before editing existing command/help symbols.
- Blast radius observed as xt command registration/help and worktree PR status flows; no high/critical warning surfaced in tool output.
- Ran gitnexus_detect_changes after edits; changed scope matches worktree PR status/audit/branch-GC helpers plus help/tests.

Chosen command/flag surface and safety defaults:
- New subcommand: xt worktree branch-gc [--prefix xt/] [--apply --yes] [--json]
- Default mode is dry-run: lists candidates and exact git branch deletion commands, but performs no mutation.
- Apply/deletion mode requires explicit --apply; confirmation is still required unless --yes is also supplied.
- Conservative managed prefix default is xt/. Prefixes are configurable with comma-separated --prefix values, e.g. --prefix xt/,bot/.
- Selection rule: delete candidates only when PR state is MERGED or CLOSED (or structured classification=closed). OPEN, unknown, no-pr, checked-out branches, and non-matching prefixes are skipped.
- The implementation does not remove worktrees. Branches currently checked out in any worktree are skipped with a reason to finish/remove the worktree first, so specialist job worktree GC remains sp-owned.

Telemetry / JSON output shape:
```json
{
  "component": "xt.branch_gc",
  "repo": "/repo",
  "checked_at_ms": 1782660000000,
  "mode": "dry_run",
  "prefixes": ["xt/"],
  "summary": { "delete": 2, "skip": 3, "deleted": 0, "failed": 0 },
  "findings": [
    {
      "component": "xt.branch_gc.finding",
      "repo": "/repo",
      "branch": "xt/merged",
      "pr_state": "MERGED",
      "classification": "closed",
      "action": "delete",
      "reason": "PR is merged",
      "outcome": "dry_run",
      "checked_at_ms": 1782660000000,
      "command": "git -C /repo branch -D xt/merged",
      "pr_url": "https://example.test/pr/10",
      "pr_number": 10
    }
  ]
}
```

Sample dry-run human output:
```text
xt worktree branch GC
repo: /repo
mode: dry_run
prefixes: xt/
branches checked: 5
delete candidates: 2

delete xt/merged (dry-run)
  pr_state: MERGED classification: closed
  reason: PR is merged
  command: git -C /repo branch -D xt/merged

Dry run — no branches deleted. Re-run with --apply --yes to delete candidates.
```

Sample apply JSON output:
```json
{
  "component": "xt.branch_gc",
  "mode": "apply",
  "summary": { "delete": 2, "skip": 3, "deleted": 2, "failed": 0 },
  "findings": [
    { "branch": "xt/merged", "action": "delete", "outcome": "deleted" },
    { "branch": "xt/closed", "action": "delete", "outcome": "deleted" }
  ]
}
```

Tests/smoke run:
- cd cli && npm test -- --run src/tests/worktree-pr-status.test.ts src/tests/worktree-session-beads-noise.test.ts -> PASS (2 files, 16 tests)
- cd cli && npm run typecheck -> PASS
- git diff --check -> PASS
- Mocked CLI smoke covers branch-gc dry-run JSON selection, human dry-run command listing, and apply mode command shape. It proves MERGED/CLOSED branches are selected, OPEN/unknown/no-pr branches are skipped, sp/job-1 is excluded by default prefix, and git branch -D is called only for safe candidates in explicit --apply --yes mode.

Residual risks/blockers:
- Branch GC deletes local branches only; remote branch deletion remains out of scope for this safe default implementation.
- Closed-but-unmerged PR branches are eligible only in explicit apply mode; this follows the task contract but remains intentionally operator-gated.
- Branches checked out in worktrees are skipped rather than removing worktrees; run xt worktree clean/finish sessions separately.
- OpenWolf files (.wolf/anatomy.md/.wolf/cerebrum.md/.wolf/buglog.json) were absent in this worktree, so no OpenWolf updates/buglog entry were possible.
- No merge, release, tag, publish, branch deletion, auto-rebase, or xt end was performed.

title: reconcile.py: --max-files truncation silently masks deferred drift (codex on PR #137)
description:
PROBLEM: reconcile.py line ~222 (current main): `selected = drifted[: options.max_files] if options.max_files is not None else drifted`. When --max-files=N < len(drifted), the loop only processes the first N items but the post-loop call to bump_last_sync_ref unconditionally stamps `last_sync = now` for ALL services in the registry. scan_drift compares file mtime > last_sync → the skipped drifted files (mtime older than 'now') become invisible. Silent masking.

Surfaced by Codex review on mercury-infra PR #137 (the post-#310-merge auto-reconcile run) 2026-06-23. PR already admin-merged — no live damage because no production caller uses --max-files yet, but the trap is real.

SUCCESS: when --max-files truncates the drift set, the un-processed drifted services remain visible on the next scan_drift run.

SCRUTINY: medium

SCOPE:
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py (truncation + bump logic)
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/tests/test_reconcile.py (regression test)

NON_GOALS: no broad rewrite of the partial/success semantics. No workflow YAML changes.

CONSTRAINTS: must not break existing 12 unit tests. Must preserve current --max-files==None behavior (no truncation → unchanged).

VALIDATION:
- New unit test: with N drifts and --max-files = N-1, status==partial AND bump_last_sync_ref is NOT called (or last_sync stays unchanged for the un-processed services).
- Existing 12 tests still pass.

OUTPUT: minimal reconcile.py patch + regression test. Decision recorded: chose Option 1 (status=partial on truncation) or Option 2 (per-service stamp). Operator hint: 'either set status=partial when truncated, OR stamp last_sync only for the services whose files were actually reconciled'.

REFERENCES:
- bd recall drift-detector-mtime-vs-last-sync-2026-06-23 (the original convergence fix this builds on)
- bd recall phase-b-smoke-evidence-2026-06-23
- mercury-infra PR #137 codex review
close_reason: reconcile() marks status=partial + appends deferred entries to failed[] when --max-files truncates; bump_last_sync_ref is skipped (existing guard). 13/13 unit tests pass (added regression test_max_files_truncation_marks_partial_and_lists_deferred_xtrm_vlxug).

title: Phase B child .1 security audit (secrets/network surface)
description:
PROBLEM: reconcile.py (executor f37cf0, commit 4444a595 on feature/xtrm-pm5d8.1-executor) handles NANO_GPT_API_KEY env, makes outbound HTTPS to nano-gpt.com, writes SKILL.md files atomically. Will run on GitHub Actions runners where logs are public. Auth/secrets/network surface — security audit required.

SUCCESS: Findings on:
1. API key leakage paths: log statements, exception text, error responses, stack traces from httpx, CalledProcessError on git subprocess
2. Header vs query auth (verify Bearer header use; no key in URL)
3. Atomic write race (tempfile placement, NamedTemporaryFile with delete=False semantics, os.replace cross-mount risk)
4. Prompt injection from user-controlled drift_detector evidence (could a service file in the repo inject instructions into the LLM prompt?)
5. Response trust: LLM-generated SKILL.md content written verbatim — any path traversal via skill_path? Any executable content concern?
6. Subprocess for git rev-parse: shell-injection vector?
7. Environment variable trust: NANO_GPT_API_URL is env-overridable — could a malicious env redirect API calls?

SCRUTINY: high

SCOPE: feature/xtrm-pm5d8.1-executor branch HEAD (commit 4444a595):
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/tests/test_reconcile.py

NON_GOALS: no edits, no package vuln scans, no live exploit tests, no penetration testing.

CONSTRAINTS: LOW permissions. Scan-only. Recommendations only — executor applies fixes if findings exist.

VALIDATION: Findings cite file:line, identify risk surface, give concrete recommendations or confirm clean.

OUTPUT: Markdown findings (or JSON) with severity + recommendations.

  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/tests/test_reconcile.py`

## Findings

- ID: SEC-RECONCILE-001
- Severity: high
- Category/CWE when applicable: CWE-22 Path Traversal, CWE-73 External Control of File Name or Path
- Evidence:
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:128-136` `find_skill_path()` accepts `drift["skill_path"]` or registry `service["skill_path"]` with no validation
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:182` `skill_path = project_root / skill_path_value`
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:197` `atomic_write(skill_path, llm_result.content)`
- Reachability/exploitability:
  - Reachable through repo-controlled registry content. `scan_drift()` loads registry and emits drift records from repo state: `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py:232-251`
  - If `skill_path` in registry becomes absolute path or contains `../`, join does not constrain write to repo root
- Impact:
  - Arbitrary file overwrite within runner permissions
  - LLM-controlled content written to chosen path
  - Can tamper workspace files, CI artifacts, later build inputs
- Recommended fix:
  - Resolve candidate path with `.resolve()`
  - Reject absolute paths
  - Enforce resolved path stays under approved service-skills root or repo root allowlist
  - Prefer deriving path from trusted resolver, not raw registry/drift field
  - Add tests for `../evil`, absolute path, symlink target edge
- Verification after fix:
  - Unit tests must fail on traversal/absolute paths
  - Assert writes only occur under expected skill directory

- ID: SEC-RECONCILE-002
- Severity: medium
- Category/CWE when applicable: CWE-918 SSRF / credential exfil by untrusted endpoint selection
- Evidence:
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:21` `NANO_GPT_URL = os.environ.get("NANO_GPT_API_URL", "...")`
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:105-108` bearer token sent to chosen URL in `Authorization` header
- Reachability/exploitability:
  - Any actor controlling process env for job can redirect request to attacker host
  - On GitHub Actions, env often comes from workflow, vars, or step composition; misconfig or unsafe reuse can expose token
- Impact:
  - `NANO_GPT_API_KEY` exfiltration to attacker-controlled HTTPS endpoint
  - Prompt contents also exfiltrate repo source and current `SKILL.md`
- Recommended fix:
  - Remove env override in production path, or gate behind explicit `--allow-custom-api-url` / test-only flag
  - Enforce allowlist: exact `https://nano-gpt.com/api/v1/chat/completions` or known hosts only
  - Validate scheme `https`, hostname allowlist, no embedded credentials, no query auth
- Verification after fix:
  - Tests for rejected custom host, rejected `http://`, accepted canonical URL only

- ID: SEC-RECONCILE-003
- Severity: medium
- Category/CWE when applicable: CWE-74 Injection, LLM prompt injection / persistent instruction injection
- Evidence:
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:61-84` prompt includes repo-derived fields, current `SKILL.md`, full source file evidence verbatim
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:184` reads source file and current `SKILL.md` straight into prompt
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:197` writes model output verbatim to `SKILL.md`
  - `scan_drift()` sources `file_path` from tracked repo files: `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py:248-259`
- Reachability/exploitability:
  - Malicious contributor can place prompt-injection text in service source file comments/strings or existing `SKILL.md`
  - Model sees injected text as part of prompt, then output becomes persistent `SKILL.md` content later consumed by agents
- Impact:
  - Poisoned service skill docs
  - Persistent agent instruction injection in future sessions
  - Possible unsafe commands/social-engineering content inserted into trusted docs
- Recommended fix:
  - Treat source evidence and current docs as untrusted data
  - Wrap untrusted blocks with explicit delimiters and instruction hierarchy
  - Use structured extraction/summarization of code facts instead of full-file verbatim prompt
  - Post-validate output: required headings only, forbid dangerous patterns, length cap, maybe human review on CI
- Verification after fix:
  - Add adversarial tests with source comment like “ignore previous instructions”
  - Assert sanitization/delimiting and output policy enforcement

- ID: SEC-RECONCILE-004
- Severity: low
- Category/CWE when applicable: CWE-209 Information Exposure Through Error Message
- Evidence:
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:199-201` per-file exceptions serialized as `str(exc)`
  - `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:216-218` top-level exceptions serialized as `str(exc)` and printed
- Reachability/exploitability:
  - Public CI logs expose exception text
  - No direct API key print found in this file
  - But network/IO error text can leak internal paths, full URL, remote error text, or source file names
- Impact:
  - Low-grade info leak in public logs
  - Can aid attacker recon
- Recommended fix:
  - Replace raw `str(exc)` with normalized error codes/messages
  - Log detailed exception only in private/debug mode
  - Keep file path minimal if logs are public
- Verification after fix:
  - Tests assert public JSON uses redacted error strings
  - Simulate HTTP failure and path error

- Bearer header vs query auth: clean
  - Evidence: `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:105-108`
  - Key sent in `Authorization: Bearer ...`
  - No key in URL/query built here

- Git subprocess shell injection: clean
  - Evidence: `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:123-125`

- `CalledProcessError` leak path: not reachable in current code

  - Evidence: `.xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py:115-120`
  - Temp file created in `dir=path.parent`, then `os.replace()`
  - Same-dir temp avoids normal `EXDEV` cross-mount failure
  - Remaining issue only minor cleanup on failure, not main security finding

## Residual Risk and Follow-ups

- Executor should fix `skill_path` containment first. Highest impact.
- Executor should lock down `NANO_GPT_API_URL` next. Secret exfil path.
- Executor should harden prompt/output trust model before public CI rollout.
- Add tests for:
  - rejected traversal/absolute `skill_path`
  - rejected custom API hosts
  - adversarial prompt-injection strings
  - redacted public error output

- Re-audit after fixes land
- Add CI tests for path containment and URL allowlist
- Add prompt-injection regression tests
- Decide whether public logs should contain per-file failure details at all

title: Phase B child: reconcile.py Python script (zero-install runner-callable)
description:
PROBLEM: Phase B needs a runner-callable Python script that reconciles service-skills drift end-to-end without sp/specialists/bun. Today the only reconcile path goes through sp script service-skills-sync which needs bun + specialists install + pack resolution (researcher verdict: showstopper on runner — packs commonly .gitignore'd).

SUCCESS: A standalone reconcile.py at .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py that:
1. Imports drift_detector.scan_drift() and runs it
2. For each drifted SKILL.md: reads current content, reads source file evidence (drift_detector already has citations), builds a reconcile prompt
3. Calls nano-gpt API via httpx.post() with header auth (NANO_GPT_API_KEY env)
4. Parses LLM response, writes updated SKILL.md content
5. After all writes, bumps last_sync_ref to current HEAD SHA in service-registry.yml
6. Returns JSON {status, drift_count, reconciled_count, failed[], cost_tokens, last_sync_ref_old, last_sync_ref_new}
7. Supports XTRM_AUTO_RECONCILE_COST_LIMIT_TOKENS env (halt if total exceeds)
8. Validates NANO_GPT_API_KEY early; exit 2 with explicit error if absent
9. CLI args: --json (machine-readable output), --dry-run (no writes), --max-files N

SCRUTINY: high

SCOPE:
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py (new file, single-file scope)
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/__init__.py (verify, no edits expected)
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/tests/test_reconcile.py (new file)

- specialists config/specialists/service-skills-sync.specialist.json (READ-ONLY reference for current prompt + behavior; replicate the prompt shape, not the JSON)
- memory key phase-b-architecture-verdict-2026-06-22

NON_GOALS:

## Summary

**Verdict: sp-on-runner is OVERKILL for this job. Use direct Python + nano-gpt API call instead.**

Phase B's core function is dead simple: merge fires → run drift scan → call LLM to reconcile SKILL.md → commit changes + bump `last_sync_ref`. That's ≤50 lines of Python calling `httpx.post()`. The existing Phase A workflow already has Python + `drift_detector` imported. Adding `sp` + `bun` + pack resolution + specialists CLI + tool-call JSON parsing adds 5 failure modes for zero functional benefit.

## Status

Research complete. All sources checked and cited.

## Architecture

Current local E2E (proven):
```
post_merge_drift_sweep.py → subprocess("sp script service-skills-sync ...") → specialist makes nano-gpt API call → writes SKILL.md + bumps last_sync_ref
```

Proposed Phase B (runner-optimized):
```
workflow.yml → setup-python → python reconcile.py → drift_detector.scan_drift() → httpx.post(nano-gpt endpoint) → writes SKILL.md + updates registry → peter-evans/create-pull-request@v7
```

Eliminated layers: `sp` CLI install, `bun` install, pack resolution, specialists JSON parsing, tool-call markup leakage risk, specialist version drift.

## Changes

### sp-on-runner verdict: NO — reject

**Why sp-on-runner is wrong shape for this job:**

| Concern | sp-on-runner | Direct Python |
|---|---|---|
| Install time first run | ~20-40s (bun + npm i -g specialists) | 0s (Python already present) |
| Failure modes added | 5: sp not found, pack not resolvable, specialists JSON leakage, sp timeout, tool-call markup in stdout | 0 |
| Complexity | 4 layers (bun → sp → specialist → nano-gpt) | 1 layer (Python → nano-gpt) |
| `.xtrm` pack dependency | REQUIRED — `_resolve_pack` walks `.xtrm/skills/user/packs/` — if packs are .gitignore'd, FAILS | ONLY needs `drift_detector.py` which is in the repo |
| Privilege required | Needs `.xtrm` write access + pack resolution | Just needs to call API |
| Debuggability | "sp script returned non-JSON" — opaque | Direct `httpx.post()` — standard HTTP debugging |

**Critical constraint discovered**: `_resolve_pack()` in the local hook walks `.xtrm/skills/user/packs/*/` to find a pack that contains a service-registry. On the Actions runner, this directory exists only if committed to the repo. If packs are in `.gitignore` (common practice — they're user-local), the pack resolution FAILS on every run. The hook silently returns "no pack resolvable" and skips reconcile. This makes sp-on-runner non-functional in the default checkout scenario without extra `git add --force` of user packs.

### Runtime picks with tradeoffs

| Option | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| R1: setup-bun + npm i -g specialists | ❌ Not recommended | 40s overhead per run, adds 5 failure modes. Only justified if specialist logic is truly complex. It's not — the specialist calls nano-gpt API and writes files. A Python script does the same with less risk. |
| R2: Prebuilt GHCR image | ❌ Over-engineered | Maintenance burden (build CI, publish, pin SHA, version bumps). Worth it only for orgs with 200+ repos running this daily. XTRM projects are ~5 repos. |
| R3: actions/cache | ❌ Avoid unless R1 chosen | Caches npm: ~15-20s savings. Still slower than zero-install Python. |
| **R4: Direct Python script** | ✅ **Recommended** | Zero-install. imports drift_detector directly. Calls nano-gpt via httpx or requests. Same diff algorithm. No sp/bun/pack/specialists overhead. |

### Auth picks

| Option | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| A1: per-repo NANO_GPT_API_KEY secret | ✅ **Recommended** | Smallest blast radius. Each repo manages its own. Rotations isolated. Matches existing pattern (OPENAI_API_KEY in Codex auto-fix). Mid-size secret management burden. |
| A2: org-level secret | ❌ Not for cross-org | Bead notes xtrm-dev/core is cross-org to mercuryintelligence. Org secrets don't cross org boundaries. Would need to be set on both orgs. |
| A3: GitHub App | ❌ Over-engineered | Heavy setup (app registration, private key rotation, token exchange). Worth it only for 50+ repos or enterprise compliance. |

**Evidence for A1**: OpenAI's own Codex auto-fix cookbook uses per-repo `OPENAI_API_KEY` secret (source: https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/codex/autofix-github-actions). Renovate's standard auth is PAT per platform. Per-repo secrets are industry standard for this scale.

| Option | Verdict | Rationale |
|---|---|---|
| O1: auto-commit [skip ci] on default branch | ❌ Blocked by branch protection | GITHUB_TOKEN cannot push to protected branches. PAT or GitHub App required — adds auth complexity. GitHub documentation explicitly states: default token cannot push to protected branches (source: https://github.com/orgs/community/discussions/25305). |
| **O2: auto-PR from xtrm-auto-reconcile/\<sha\>** | ✅ **Recommended** | Works with GITHUB_TOKEN + `contents: write` + `pull-requests: write` permissions. ### How auto-PR works with GITHUB_TOKEN (the pattern)

```yaml
- name: Create Pull Request
  uses: peter-evans/create-pull-request@v7
  with:
    commit-message: "chore: auto-reconcile service-skills drift [skip ci]"
    branch: xtrm-auto-reconcile/${{ github.sha }}
    base: ${{ github.event.workflow_run.head_branch || github.ref_name }}
    title: "auto-reconcile: service-skills drift post-merge"
    body: |
      Auto-generated reconciliation of service-skills drift
      detected after merge of ${{ github.sha }}.
    labels: auto-reconcile
    delete-branch: true
```

The `[skip ci]` in commit message prevents infinite loop. `delete-branch: true` auto-cleans up after merge. Confirmed by stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action docs: use `skip-checks:true` or `[skip ci]` to prevent workflow re-trigger (deepwiki evidence).

### Failure-modes inventory revisited

| Failure mode from bead | sp-on-runner | Direct Python |
|---|---|---|
| sp timeout >10min | unavoidable | eliminated (no sp) |
| nano-gpt rate-limit/quota | same risk | same risk |
| specialists install drift | unavoidable | eliminated (no specialists) |
| gitnexus absence (use_gitnexus=False) | same | same |
| Tool-call markup JSON leakage | unavoidable until specialists PR #146 ships | eliminated (no sp) |
| `.xtrm/packs` not in checkout | CRITICAL — pack resolution fails silently | unaffected (no pack needed) |
| **TOTAL independent failure modes** | **6+** | **2** (rate-limit + gitnexus) |

### Risks bead doesn't enumerate

1. **Branch protection blocks direct commit (O1 is infeasible without PAT).** This isn't just a concurrency concern — it's a fundamental blocker. Any auto-commit to default branch requires either: (a) PAT stored as secret, (b) GitHub App with installation token, or (c) disabling branch protection. O2 (auto-PR) is the only viable path with GITHUB_TOKEN. Sources: deepwiki on peter-evans/create-pull-request, community discussion #25305, stefanzweifel/git-auto-commit-action wiki.

2. **Merge race condition: no transactional lock.** Two PRs merged within 30s → both trigger `pull_request.closed` workflow → both run reconcile → first writes, second reads stale state → either merge conflict on push (auto-PR) or lost update (auto-commit). Renovate handles this by processing one branch/PR per target branch per run (deepwiki evidence). Phase B needs either: (a) concurrency group on the workflow keyed by `github.ref`, or (b) `last_sync_ref`-based compare-and-swap (read ref, write only if unchanged). Currently unaddressed.

3. **API key security leakage via workflow run logs.** If reconcile script prints the API key or the API call includes it in query params (not headers), it leaks to public Actions logs. This is why the Codex auto-fix cookbook checks `OPENAI_API_KEY` early and exits with explicit message if missing. Phase B should validate secret exists early and mask all API calls.

4. **Cost blow-up from frequent merges.** nano-gpt API costs accumulate per merge. If market-data has 30 PRs/day, that's 30 API calls × ~10K tokens each = 300K tokens/day ≈ $3-15/day depending on nano-gpt pricing. No cost cap or budget alert in current design. Consider `XTRM_AUTO_RECONCILE_COST_CAP` env var in the reconcile script.

5. **Workflow-run token has `pull-requests: write` but cannot trigger `pull_request` workflows.** Per GitHub docs, GITHUB_TOKEN commits do NOT trigger new workflow runs. This is a feature (prevents infinite loops) but means auto-PR won't run CI on the PR. Approve and run workflows button required for first-time contributors. The Codex auto-fix pattern handles this by verifying tests PASS before creating PR.

| Pattern | Repo/Source | Architecture | Write-back method |
|---|---|---|---|
| **Codex auto-fix CI failures** | openai/openai-cookbook (Sep 2025) — https://cookbook.openai.com/examples/codex/autofix-github-actions | Codex CLI on runner → make changes → Create PR | peter-evans/create-pull-request@v6, unique branch per run |
| **GitHub Models AI inference** | actions/ai-inference@v1 — https://github.com/actions/ai-inference | `models:read` permission, no API key, uses GitHub Models catalog | Output to step summary, no built-in writeback |
| **Copilot CLI programmatic in Actions** | docs.github.com — https://docs.github.com/en/copilot/how-tos/copilot-cli/automate-copilot-cli/automate-with-actions | npm i -g @github/copilot, copilot -p "..." --allow-tool=write | stdout to job output, manual commit |
| **Renovate auto-merge** | renovatebot/renovate — deepwiki | PAT or GitHub App, platform automerge, one branch/PR per target per run | Branch automerge (direct push) or platform automerge (PR auto-merge) |
| **Dependabot** | GitHub native | Auto-PR per dependency update | peter-evans/create-pull-request-like pattern (native) |
| **GitHub Agentic Workflows** | Technical Preview (Feb 2026) — https://github.github.com/gh-aw/ | Markdown-defined, sandboxed, safe-output gates, read-only token in agent | Scoped write in downstream job, NOT production-ready |
| **Self-healing CI (GH AW)** | pascoal.net (Mar 2026) — https://pascoal.net/2026/03/12/self-healing-ci-using-gh-aw/ | Agentic Workflow triggered on CI failure, AI generates fix, PR created | Still technical preview, sandboxed execution |

## Follow-ups

1. **Direct Python script path is strictly dominant.** Eliminates 5 failure modes, zero-install, leverages existing Phase A Python setup. No new dependencies needed beyond `httpx` or `requests` (both common on Actions runners).

2. **If team insists on sp-on-runner:** use R1 (setup-bun) + manual checkout of `.xtrm/packs` (or commit packs to repo) + patch `_resolve_pack` to accept explicit pack path via env var. Test pack resolution path FIRST — it's the hidden showstopper.

3. **Recommended R/A/O: R4 (direct Python) + A1 (per-repo secret) + O2 (auto-PR).** This is the simplest architecture that achieves the stated goal, survival-tested against all 7 failure modes, and matches established patterns in the ecosystem.

4. **Cost cap and concurrency guard are essential, not optional.** Add `XTRM_AUTO_RECONCILE_COST_CAP` (halt if per-run token count exceeds limit) and `concurrency: group: ${{ github.ref }} cancel-in-progress: true` to the reusable workflow.

5. **Do NOT use GitHub Agentic Workflows** — still technical preview, design decisions not finalized, sandbox limits what the agent can do. Re-evaluate when GA.

## Risks

| Risk | Likelihood | Impact | Mitigation |
|---|---|---|---|
| `.xtrm/packs` not committed → pack resolution fails silently | HIGH (common practice) | HIGH (reconcile never runs) | Direct Python script eliminates this risk entirely |
| Branch protection blocks auto-commit | CERTAIN (if protections exist) | HIGH | O2 auto-PR is the ONLY viable path |
| Merge race → lost update | MEDIUM (2+ PRs/min) | MEDIUM (missed drift) | concurrency group + last_sync_ref CAS |
| API key leaked in logs | LOW | HIGH | Validate & mask early; httpx.post with header auth |
| Cost blow-up from frequent merges | MEDIUM (depends on repo) | MEDIUM | Cost cap env var; log token usage |

title: Phase B: GitHub Action auto-reconcile via sp script on runner (close the loop)
description:
## CONTEXT

Phase A (xtrm-g7j08) shipped + E2E verified 2026-06-22 (xtrm-dev/core PR #296 + mercury-infra PR #110/#111/#112). Reusable workflow .github/workflows/service-skills-drift-sweep.yml DETECTS drift on merged PRs and posts sticky comment. NO reconcile — operator must remember to run /updating-service-skills.

This bead closes the loop: action ALSO RECONCILES on the runner, mirroring what the local hook+sp script combo does today (xtrm-tg33i memory: phase2-script-specialist-e2e-pattern-2026-06-20).

## PROBLEM (what 'unnoticed' really means)

Detect-only still requires human-in-loop. The 11 real drift findings surfaced in smoke evidence (PRs #111/#112) on mercury-infra would stay unfixed until someone notices a comment. That defeats the stated goal: drift sync should happen automatically post-merge.

## GOAL

Extend reusable workflow with reconcile step that:
1. Runs sp script service-skills-sync on the runner with full local-hook parity
2. On reconcile success: marker cleared + last_sync_ref bumped + SKILL.md content updated where needed
3. Persistence: either auto-commit [skip ci] on default branch OR auto-PR from xtrm-auto-reconcile/<sha> branch (decide via /planning)
4. Failure resilient: if sp/key/network fails, fallback to Phase A behavior (comment only, marker stays)

## OPEN DESIGN (input for /planning)

### Runtime
- Option R1: oven-sh/setup-bun + npm install -g @jaggerxtrm/specialists (slowest first run, simplest)
- Option R2: pre-built container image with sp+bun preinstalled, pinned by SHA (faster, requires building/publishing image to GHCR)
- Option R3: cached npm/bun with actions/cache (compromise)

### Auth
- Option A1: NANO_GPT_API_KEY per-repo secret (each Mercury repo configures its own; rotation burden distributed)
- Option A2: org-level secret on mercuryintelligence org (one config point, but requires xtrm-dev/core to be in scope of that secret which is cross-org)
- Option A3: GitHub App that mints short-lived tokens (heaviest)

### Output policy
- Option O1: auto-commit [skip ci] on default branch — closest to 'unnoticed' goal, but requires write-permission token + skips review
- Option O2: auto-PR from xtrm-auto-reconcile/<sha> — needs explicit review, more 'noticed' but safer
- Option O3: hybrid — auto-commit for last_sync_ref-only bumps (mtime drift, no SKILL.md content change), auto-PR for SKILL.md content edits

### Concurrency
- Two PRs merged within 1min on same default branch: does sp script lock? Idempotency? Test with synthetic race.
- Action's GITHUB_TOKEN can write commits but cannot push directly to main if branch protection is on. Need GH App or PAT for direct-commit path (option O1).

### Failure modes inventory (from local-hook E2E history)
- sp timeout (>10min default budget)
- nano-gpt API rate limit / quota exhaustion (history: infra-5y7)
- specialists install fails (npm-link-mode vs npm-publish-mode drift)
- gitnexus CLI not on runner — drift_detector should already use_gitnexus=False, verify
- Tool-call markup leakage into JSON (resolved by specialists PR #146, but verify on runner)

### Caller-template vendoring

- [ ] mercury-infra opted-in to reconcile-enabled
- [ ] Smoke 1 (golden path): forced drift PR + merge → reconcile completes → either auto-commit or auto-PR materializes → next merge sees zero drift
- [ ] Smoke 2 (failure): same setup but secret absent → action degrades to Phase A behavior + clear annotation
- [ ] Smoke 3 (concurrency): 2 dummy PRs merged within 30s window → no race, both reconcile attempts converge
- [ ] Documentation: docs/<file>.md describing the per-repo enablement procedure (secret setup + caller template)

title: Migrate service-skills auto-reconcile from local git-hook to GitHub Action
description:
## PROBLEM

Current post_merge_drift_sweep.py + auto-reconcile (xtrm-tg33i) is a LOCAL git post-merge hook. It fires when:
- a dev runs `git merge` or `git pull` LOCALLY
- AND HEAD lands on default branch
- AND env XTRM_AUTO_RECONCILE_DRIFT=1 is set in their shell

This means:
- GitHub web 'Merge pull request' button does NOT trigger the hook (server-side)
- The hook fires on the next dev who pulls the merged main locally — non-deterministic timing
- Different devs with different env settings get different behavior
- A repo whose maintainers never pull (CI-only consumers, dependabot-merged repos) never gets drift reconciled

## SUCCESS

GitHub Action (in xtrm-tools or a per-repo template) runs on `pull_request.closed + merged == true` against default branch. The action:
1. Sets XTRM_AUTO_RECONCILE_DRIFT=1
2. Invokes the same post_merge_drift_sweep.py logic
3. On marker + auto-reconcile success: commits SKILL.md changes + last_sync_ref bumps as a follow-up commit (push protected with [skip ci])
4. On failure: opens a GitHub Issue (or writes a workflow annotation) so it's visible

## SCOPE / OPEN DESIGN

- Reuse existing post_merge_drift_sweep.py logic — wrap in a workflow YAML
- Authentication: GitHub App with contents:write OR a PAT in repo secrets
- Specialists CLI install: action installs sp/bun on the runner OR uses a published container image
- Idempotence: drift_detector + last_sync_ref stamping is naturally idempotent; double-runs OK
- Cost: typical run is 5min budget — ~/usr/bin/zsh.04/run on Ubuntu, well within free minutes for small repo cadence
- Composable: provide a 'xtrm/auto-reconcile' reusable workflow that consumer repos add via `uses:`

## NON_GOALS

- Not removing the local hook — keeps the dev-feedback loop fast
- Not changing the specialist contract

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Pilot on mercury-infra: GitHub Action runs on PR merge, auto-reconciles, commits with [skip ci]
- [ ] Failure mode: forced drift + non-existent service triggers issue creation
- [ ] Concurrency: 2 PRs merged in <1min sequence -> action queues, no race on registry write
- [ ] Cost dashboard: track minutes/month

## REFERENCES

- xtrm-jcmub (closed): local hook detection
- xtrm-tg33i (closed): local hook auto-reconcile via sp script
- specialists unitAI-4zask + unitAI-mally + unitAI-qrr21 (closed): script-specialist refit
- Discussion 2026-06-22 with operator: local hook OK as backup, GitHub Action is the production path
close_reason: Phase A + Phase B both complete; smoke evidence in phase-b-smoke-evidence-2026-06-23; follow-up xtrm-qxu4y P3 tracked separately.

title: Auto-reconcile post-merge drift via sp script service-skills-sync
description:
## PROBLEM

post_merge_drift_sweep.py (shipped via xtrm-jcmub) currently DETECTS drift on master merges and writes a .xtrm/.service-skills-drift-pending marker, but the reconcile is agent-driven (operator runs /updating-service-skills manually). Specialists PR #145 (unitAI-4zask refit) made service-skills-sync script-specialist invocable end-to-end via:

  sp script service-skills-sync \
    --template-field script_template \
    --vars repo=<name> --vars pack=<pack> --vars cwd=<repo-root> \
    --allow-local-scripts --allow-write-capable --json

This closes the loop: post-merge hook detects drift → invokes script-specialist → reconciles SKILL.md + advances last_sync_ref → removes marker. No human in the path.

## SUCCESS

When post_merge_drift_sweep.py writes the drift-pending marker, it immediately invokes sp script service-skills-sync against the host repo, parses the JSON result, and:
  - on success: removes marker (or lets the specialist do it), stamps observation in a runlog
  - on failure: leaves marker in place, surfaces error to operator

## SCOPE

- xtrm-tools: extend .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/post_merge_drift_sweep.py (or sibling) to call sp script when marker is written
- Gating: respect existing registry-gated + default-branch-only logic; only auto-reconcile if 'sp' is on PATH (don't break repos without specialists installed)
- Cost bound: timeout from CLI (default 600s); skip clean if drift_scan shows no services to process

## NON_GOALS

- Not changing detection logic
- Not changing specialist contract

## CONSTRAINTS

- Must not regress existing detection (registry-gated, default-branch-only)
- Must not crash repos without specialists CLI
- Must propagate errors clearly (stderr + non-zero exit) so the CI/git-hook surfaces them

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Synthetic master merge in registry-gated repo with drift -> marker + auto-reconcile + marker removed
- [ ] Master merge in non-registry repo -> noop (no specialist call)
- [ ] Master merge with no drift -> noop (no specialist call)
- [ ] Repo without sp on PATH -> falls back to current marker-only behavior, no crash
- [ ] Failure injection (e.g. sp returns success:false) -> marker stays, error logged

## REFERENCES

- xtrm-jcmub (CLOSED 2026-06-04): detection shipped
- specialists PR #145 (MERGED 2026-06-21): script-specialist refit
- mercury-infra PR #107 (MERGED 2026-06-20): first manual smoke validating the loop end-to-end

title: xt spec archive — gating on epic completion + validation evidence + high/critical review gates
description:
## PROBLEM
Archiving a spec before its work is done converts it into a false historical record. Archive must refuse unless linked epic is closed, validation evidence is present, and (for high/critical SCRUTINY) review gates are complete.

## SUCCESS
`xt spec archive <path>` checks: linked epic.status == closed; every child in spec.links is closed; for SCRUTINY ∈ {high, critical}, a `reviewed` evidence marker exists; no open drift from .15. On pass: sets spec.status = archived, writes immutable snapshot at `archive/<slug>.yaml`. On fail: refuses with named missing condition.

## SCRUTINY: high

## SCOPE
- cli/commands/spec/archive.ts (new)
- cli/lib/spec/archive-gate.ts (new — gating logic)
- cli/lib/spec/__tests__/archive.test.ts (new — gate refusal cases)
- docs/specs/ARCHIVE-GATE.md (new — gate criteria reference)

## NON_GOALS
- Auto-closing bd issues
- Hard-removing the spec.yaml (archive snapshots; original remains)
- Reopening archived specs (out of scope MVP)

## CONSTRAINTS
- Gate criteria documented before implementation (write doc first)
- Snapshot path: `<spec-dir>/archive/<slug>.yaml`; never overwrites
- Refusal must name the SPECIFIC failing gate (`epic_open`, `child_open: <id>`, `review_missing`, `drift_present`)
- Log: `{event: spec_archived OR spec_archive_refused, spec_id, gate, reason}`

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Gate-criteria doc reviewed before code
- [ ] Refusal cases each have a unit test (epic open / child open / review missing / drift)
- [ ] Archive snapshot byte-matches spec.yaml at archive time
- [ ] High/critical SCRUTINY without review marker → refused
- [ ] Idempotency: re-archiving an archived spec is no-op + warning

## OUTPUT
Archive command, gate module, refusal tests, snapshot sample, doc.
close_reason: cli/src/spec/archive-gate.ts + commands/spec/archive.ts. 7 gates: wrong_status, epic_missing, epic_open, child_open, test_open, review_missing (high/critical via bd kv reviewed:<epic>), drift_present (calls computeStatus). Snapshot at <spec-dir>/archive/<id>.yaml never overwrites. spec.status mutated to archived in place via parseDocument (preserves comments). 6/6 refusal tests green covering all branches. docs/specs/ARCHIVE-GATE.md documents criteria + review-evidence convention.

title: xt spec status — drift detection against linked bd state
description:
## PROBLEM
After apply, the spec.links block is a snapshot. bd state evolves: issues close, children get added, edges change. Without drift detection, operators don't know whether spec still reflects reality before archive.

## SUCCESS
`xt spec status <path>` reads spec.links, queries `bd show <id> --json` for each, and reports: open vs closed counts, missing/orphaned ids, newly-added bd children not in spec, dependency-cycle status (via `bd dep cycles`). Exit 0 = in sync; exit 1 = drift detected; exit 2 = warnings.

## SCRUTINY: medium

## SCOPE
- cli/commands/spec/status.ts (new)
- cli/lib/spec/drift.ts (new — diff spec.links vs bd reality)

## NON_GOALS
- Auto-fixing drift
- Modifying bd state
- Archive gating (.16 calls status internally)

## CONSTRAINTS
- Read-only on filesystem and bd
- Output format: human (default) + `--json`
- Cycle check uses `bd dep cycles`; no homemade graph walk
- Log: `{event: spec_status, spec_id, open_count, closed_count, drift_kind[]}`

## VALIDATION
- [ ] In-sync spec returns exit 0
- [ ] Orphan link (deleted bd issue) → exit 1 + named id in output
- [ ] New bd child not in spec → reported as drift_kind=new_child
- [ ] --json output schema documented
- [ ] Cycle in linked epic → reported

## OUTPUT
Status command, drift module, --json schema, sample drift report.

Drift kinds: orphan_link (id absent in bd), new_child (bd has children not in spec), cycle (bd dep cycles --scope <epic>). Exit 0 in-sync / 1 drift / 2 warnings. Structured spec_status log with drift_kind array. XT_SPEC_BD_BINARY honored for tests.

title: xt spec apply — consume planner result and write links back to spec.yaml
description:
## PROBLEM
After planner finishes, the produced board (epic, child chains, test issues) must be linked back to spec.yaml so status/archive (.15, .16) can reconcile state.

## SUCCESS
`xt spec apply <path> --reconcile` (or auto-run when sidecar shows planner job complete) reads planner output via `sp result <job-id> --json`, extracts {epic_id, children[], test_issues[], first_task}, validates each id exists in bd, and writes them to spec.yaml `links.{epic, children, test_issues, planner_bead}` atomically.

## SCRUTINY: medium

## SCOPE
- cli/commands/spec/apply.ts (--reconcile path)
- cli/lib/spec/reconcile.ts (new — planner output → spec.links)
- cli/lib/spec/yaml-writer.ts (new — preserves comments + ordering via yaml AST library)

## NON_GOALS
- Drift detection (.15)
- Archive gating (.16)
- Mutating bd state (links flow spec ← bd, not the other way)

## CONSTRAINTS
- yaml writer preserves comments and original key order (use a yaml AST lib, not parse+stringify)
- Atomic write: tmp + rename
- Each id round-tripped through `bd show <id> --json`; missing ids surface as `reconcile_orphan_link` error
- Idempotent: running --reconcile twice produces identical spec.yaml byte-for-byte
- Log: `{event: apply_reconciled, planner_bead_id, epic_id, children_count, test_issues_count}`

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Reconcile produces correct spec.yaml.links block from planner JSON
- [ ] Idempotency: byte-for-byte identical on second run
- [ ] Comments + ordering preserved (compare via diff)
- [ ] Orphan link → exit non-zero, helpful stderr
- [ ] Log line emitted

## OUTPUT

title: Implement spec.yaml validator core (schema + 7-section mappability + SCRUTINY infer + scope/testability/dep-cycle)
description:

Pre-dispatch gates from the original epic require: 7-section mappability, vague-scope detection, untestable requirement detection, missing-layer-hint inference, dependency cycle detection, SCRUTINY explicit-or-inferred with floor-can-only-raise discipline, unresolved-high-risk-open-question check.

## SUCCESS
A pure-logic validator module exports `validate(spec, opts) -> { ok, errors[], warnings[], inferred }`. Errors are actionable (field path + reason + fix hint). SCRUTINY inference table mirrors specialists-roadmap auto-escalation surfaces.

title: drift_detector territory globs match the filesystem, not git — .gitignore ignored, build/vendor trees scanned
description:
## Problem
scan_drift expands territory patterns with glob.glob(pattern, recursive=True) against the working tree, so .gitignore is not respected. A territory like 'rust_ingestor/**/*' matches the gitignored rust target/ build tree (3646 files vs ~10 real source). This bloats the candidate set (noise) and, combined with per-item gitnexus enrichment (see the OOM footgun bug), is dangerous.

## Recommended fix
Filter candidates through git (git ls-files / check-ignore) or exclude common build/vendor/cache dirs (target/, node_modules/, __pycache__/, *.pyc, .venv/) before surfacing/enriching. Optionally validate registry territories at write time and warn when a pattern matches a gitignored tree. (Pairs with the enrich fan-out OOM bug.)
close_reason: Core (gitignored trees swept into drift candidates) already fixed at scan time by xtrm-08i0b git-tracked filter. This adds the optional operator surface: territory_gitignore_report + 'validate-territories' CLI + scan_drift stderr advisory. Verified live on market-data (2 patterns, 107 gitignored .pyc flagged). Test: test_territory_validation.py. 56/56 green.

title: layout_migrator leaves stale .claude/skills/<old>/scripts paths inside migrated SKILL.md bodies
description:
## Problem
scripts/layout_migrator.py moves per-service diagnostic scripts to service-skills/services/<id>/scripts/ but does NOT rewrite the in-body references inside each SKILL.md, which still point at the old flat path .claude/skills/<oldname>/scripts/.

## Incident (mercury-market-data)
After migrating, 27 stale refs remained across 8 service skills (Data Inspection blocks, 'make -C .claude/skills/<old>' targets, Diagnostic Scripts sections). Old path segment is the container name for self-refs (mmd-data-feed→ingesting-ohlcv, mmd-api→serving-market-api, mmd-mcp-server→serving-mcp-tools, mmd-backup-service→backing-up-database, mmd-snapshot-feed→computing-snapshots) and a service-id for platform/pipeline umbrella cross-refs. All had to be fixed by hand.

## Recommended fix
During migration, rewrite '.claude/skills/<name>/scripts/' (and 'make -C .claude/skills/<name>') refs in moved SKILL.md bodies to '.xtrm/skills/user/packs/<pack>/service-skills/services/<mapped-id>/scripts/', mapping old container/skill names → service-id via the registry.
close_reason: layout_migrator rewrites legacy in-body .claude/skills/<alias> refs (alias=service-id or registry container) to the new .xtrm services/ dir during the move; unmapped segments left intact + reported. Test: test_layout_migrator_refs.py. 52/52 green, parity 330/330, mirror synced.

title: One-time layout migrator + hard-cut wiring
description:
## PROBLEM
Existing installs (market-data: 16 services) use the flat `packs/<repo>/<svc>/` layout with broken `.claude/skills` skill_path values. A one-time LAYOUT migrator (distinct from the content `skill_migrator`) must move files into `packs/<repo>/service-skills/services/<svc>/`, rewrite registry `skill_path` to the real `.xtrm` location, relocate the registry under the umbrella, and generate the umbrella. After cutover, resolvers assume the NEW layout only (hard-cut, no dual-read).

## SUCCESS
`layout_migrator.py` run against a flat-layout fixture produces: services moved under `service-skills/services/<svc>/`, registry relocated to `service-skills/service-registry.json` with every `skill_path` rewritten to an existing `.xtrm/skills/user/packs/<repo>/service-skills/services/<svc>/SKILL.md`, and a generated umbrella SKILL.md. Idempotent (re-run = no-op). install/install-service-skills.py invokes it on upgrade. Resolvers (child .2/.3) read only the new layout.

## SCOPE
- skills/service-skills/scripts/ — NEW `layout_migrator.py` (move dirs, rewrite + relocate registry, call generate_umbrella)
- install/install-service-skills.py — invoke layout_migrator before content skill_migrator on install/upgrade; detect old-layout presence
- bootstrap.py registry/service resolvers — assume new layout (remove/avoid any flat-layout fallback)
- tests/ — fixtures: a flat 2-service pack → assert migrated tree + registry

## NON_GOALS
- No dual-read/back-compat window (decision: hard-cut). Do NOT add old-layout fallback branches to resolvers.
- Does not change service CONTENT (content skill_migrator already handles devops-section upgrades and runs after).
- No automatic git commit of the migrated user pack — migrator writes files; operator commits.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Must be idempotent and SAFE: never delete a service dir before its move is confirmed; refuse + report if target exists with divergent content.
- Distinct from content skill_migrator — layout_migrator moves/relocates; skill_migrator edits headings. Order: layout first, then content.
- Preserve each service's SEMANTIC block during the move (move file verbatim; do not regenerate).
- Telemetry: print per-service `migrated: <old> -> <new>` / `skipped: <reason>` lines so install can report a summary.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Unit: flat fixture (2 services) → migrated tree exactly matches expected; registry skill_path values all resolve to existing files
- [ ] Idempotence: second run prints all-skipped, mutates nothing
- [ ] Safety: target-exists-with-divergence case refuses and reports (no data loss)
- [ ] Integration: install-service-skills.py on an old-layout tmp repo performs layout migration then content migration; umbrella generated
- [ ] Smoke evidence: capture migrator stdout summary in handoff

## OUTPUT
layout_migrator.py, install wiring diff, fixture + test evidence, sample migration summary, residual risks (esp. partial-migration recovery).

## APPROACH NOTES
Depends on .2 (resolvers/new skill_path) and .3 (generate_umbrella). This is the executor of the hard-cut. The real market-data install is the acceptance target but migrate a FIXTURE in tests; the live pack is migrated by the operator running install after merge.
close_reason: One-time layout migrator (flat->umbrella): layout_migrator.py moves services into service-skills/services/, relocates+rewrites registry to .xtrm, generates umbrella; SAFE (MigrationRefused on divergence, dedupes identical, idempotent). Hard-cut: get_service_skill_dir + scaffolder now new-layout. Resolved xtrm-g9bvw by removing the vestigial per-service .claude/skills symlink (per-service skills resolve via registry skill_path). installer run_layout_migration wired before content migration; both iterate packs. 4 migrator tests + scaffold/CLI smokes; 27 total, parity 329/329.

title: Per-repo umbrella SKILL.md generated from registry
description:
## PROBLEM
Per-repo service skills sit flat under packs/<repo>/ mixed with non-service skills, with a bare registry and no umbrella/entry-point. Each repo needs ONE coherent umbrella over its services: a generated SKILL.md (name `<repo>-services`) with a service map + cross-service health + navigation, plus the registry moved under it.

## SUCCESS
A generator produces `.xtrm/skills/user/packs/<repo>/service-skills/SKILL.md` from `service-registry.json`: a service table (id/container/territory/skill_path/last_sync), a Cross-Service Health section, and a Navigation section. Human narrative lives in a `<!-- SEMANTIC_START -->`/`<!-- SEMANTIC_END -->` block preserved across regeneration. The skill `name:` is repo-qualified (`<repo>-services`) to avoid catalog collision with the machinery `service-skills` skill. The registry is relocated to `packs/<repo>/service-skills/service-registry.json`; services target `services/<svc>/SKILL.md`.

## SCOPE
- skills/service-skills/scripts/ — NEW `umbrella_generator.py` (or a function in bootstrap) `generate_umbrella(registry, repo_name) -> str`, idempotent, SEMANTIC-preserving (reuse skill_migrator's marker logic)
- bootstrap.py — registry path helpers updated to the umbrella location `packs/<repo>/service-skills/service-registry.json`
- install/install-service-skills.py — call generate_umbrella on install/upgrade
- references/using.md + router SKILL.md — document the umbrella as the per-repo entry point

## NON_GOALS
- The one-time move of EXISTING files into services/ and registry relocation execution is child .4 (migrator). This child builds the GENERATOR + new-layout path helpers; .4 wires it into the cutover.
- No change to per-service SKILL.md content.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Repo-qualified name derivation must be deterministic (repo basename) and collision-safe vs machinery `service-skills`.
- SEMANTIC block: reuse the exact marker constants from skill_migrator (`<!-- SEMANTIC_START -->`). Regeneration must preserve human prose verbatim.
- Generation must be a pure function of (registry, repo_name, existing_semantic_block) — no network, no Date.now equivalent in committed fixtures.

## VALIDATION
- [ ] Unit: generate_umbrella over a fixture registry yields a table matching the services; re-running with an edited SEMANTIC block preserves the block
- [ ] Generated umbrella `name:` == `<repo>-services` and parses as valid skill frontmatter
- [ ] Cross-service health + navigation sections present
- [ ] pytest skills/service-skills/tests covers generator idempotence + SEMANTIC preservation

## OUTPUT
The generator, a sample generated umbrella, unit/idempotence test evidence, residual risks (e.g. repo-name collisions).

## APPROACH NOTES
Depends on .1 (location) and .2 (resolvers + new skill_path model). Mirror skill_migrator's marker-find logic for the SEMANTIC block. The umbrella is regenerated, never hand-edited outside the SEMANTIC region.

title: Path model: resolve via bootstrap, .claude/skills as Claude-only view
description:
## PROBLEM
There are 52 hardcoded `.claude/skills/...` strings across the machinery (script defaults, scaffolder-generated SKILL.md bodies, registry skill_path writes). `.claude/skills -> .xtrm/skills/active/claude` is EMPTY, so every registry skill_path is broken. Cross-tool consumers (specialists, scripts) use `.xtrm/skills`, not `.claude/skills`. Paths must resolve through bootstrap, with `.claude/skills` demoted to a Claude-Code-only view.

## SUCCESS
No cross-tool code path emits or reads a hardcoded `.claude/skills` string. scaffolder generates SKILL.md bodies whose script invocations resolve to the active skill dir (or .xtrm-resolved path), not `.claude/skills/{service_id}/...`. New registry `skill_path` values point at real `.xtrm/skills/user/packs/.../service-skills/services/<svc>/SKILL.md`. Claude PreToolUse/SessionStart hooks MAY use `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/...` (Claude-only) but prefer the active dir; this is documented, not hardcoded into shared scripts.

## SCOPE
- skills/service-skills/scripts/scaffolder.py (canonical_sections bodies at ~L144-145: health_probe/log_hunter/data_explorer paths; registry skill_path write)
- skills/service-skills/scripts/{drift_detector.py, cataloger.py, skill_activator.py, scope.py, skill_migrator.py} — replace literal `.claude/skills` with bootstrap resolver calls
- skills/service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py — add a `get_service_skill_dir(service_id)` / `resolve_script_path` helper if needed so generated bodies are path-model-agnostic
- references/*.md and router SKILL.md — replace illustrative `.claude/skills` paths with resolver-based guidance; explicitly state the .claude/skills = Claude-only-VIEW rule
- install/service-skills-readme.md — update Project Structure / Registry sections

## NON_GOALS
- Do NOT move files or change the on-disk layout (that's child .4 migrator). This child only changes how paths are RESOLVED/EMITTED.
- Do NOT touch the generated umbrella (child .3).
- Claude-specific hooks keeping `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/...` is allowed — not every `.claude` ref is a bug.

## CONSTRAINTS
- bootstrap resolvers are the single source: get_project_root/get_pack_path/get_registry_path/get_skills_root (+ any new helper). Never reintroduce literal cross-tool path strings.
- Keep scaffolder's security boundary intact (ensure_legacy_symlink confinement).

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Scaffold a service in a tmp repo; generated SKILL.md script paths resolve to a real file under the active skill dir

- [ ] pytest skills/service-skills/tests green (scaffolder + drift + migrator)

## OUTPUT
Changed files, before/after grep counts of hardcoded refs, sample generated SKILL.md showing resolved paths, pytest summary, residual `.claude` refs with justification (Claude-only).

Depends on .1 (scripts already co-located). The 12-file / 52-ref inventory: `grep -rn '.claude/skills' skills/service-skills`. scaffolder.py L144-145 are the highest-value fixes (they propagate into every generated service skill).

title: Service Skills v2: consolidate machinery + per-repo umbrella + .xtrm canonical paths
description:
DRAFT epic umbrella for /planning to decompose. Builds on completed xtrm-tkqjn (devops+gitnexus awareness). This is a REPACKAGING + PATH-MODEL FIX, not a rewrite — contract SSOT, gitnexus drift engine, migrator, devops template, gitnexus navigation all carry over unchanged.

GOAL: Make service-skills respect the canonical .xtrm/skills/ model (default + active-symlink + user/packs), kill the Claude-specific .claude/skills hardcoding, consolidate the fragmented machinery into ONE skill, and give each repo a coherent umbrella over its per-service skills.

BROKEN STATE (evidence 2026-05-30):
- Registry skill_path records ".claude/skills/<service>/SKILL.md" but real files live at ".xtrm/skills/user/packs/<repo>/<service>/SKILL.md", and ".claude/skills -> .xtrm/skills/active/claude" is EMPTY -> every registry skill_path is broken (market-data: 16 services).
- Machinery is 4 separate skills (creating/updating/scoping/using-service-skills) + non-active service-skills-set bundle; cross-skill sys.path hack into bootstrap.py.
- 54 hardcoded .claude/skills refs across the 4 skills (per-service paths, machinery self-refs, registry path).
- Per-repo service skills sit flat under packs/<repo>/ mixed with non-service skills (using-tdd-guard); bare registry, no umbrella/map.

NAMING (resolves machinery<->umbrella collision):
- Machinery skill (singleton, shipped): name "service-skills".
- Per-repo umbrella (one per repo): folder packs/<repo>/service-skills/ but SKILL.md name is REPO-QUALIFIED (e.g. "market-data-services") to avoid catalog collision.
- Per-service skills keep verb-noun names (serving-mcp-tools, ingesting-ohlcv, ...).

PART A — Consolidate machinery into ONE service-skills skill (skills/service-skills/ + .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/, active-symlinked):
  SKILL.md (router: triggers + when to create/update/use + navigation; ABSORBS scoping)
  references/{creating.md, updating.md, using.md, system-guide.md, service_skill_contract.json}
  scripts/ (bootstrap, scaffolder, deep_dive, drift_detector, skill_migrator, cataloger, skill_activator, scope — all together, removes cross-skill import hack)
  tests/
  install/ (was service-skills-set: install.py, service-skills-readme.md, settings.json, git-hooks/)
  - Scoping dropped as a separate skill; routing folds into router SKILL.md, scope.py stays a helper.
  - Trade-off for planning: 4 precise descriptions -> 1; mitigate with broad-but-clear description; hooks fire regardless.

PART B — Per-repo umbrella:
  .xtrm/skills/user/packs/<repo>/service-skills/
    SKILL.md (name: <repo>-services; repo service map + cross-service health + navigation)
    service-registry.json (moves here)
    services/<svc>/SKILL.md (one per service)
  - Separates service skills from other pack skills; single repo entry point; devops cross-service map.

PART C — Path model: canonical .xtrm, resolved, not hardcoded:
  - .claude/skills is a Claude-Code VIEW (symlink); specialists use .xtrm/skills.
  - Claude hooks may use $CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/skills/... (Claude-only) but prefer active skill dir.
  - Everything cross-tool (registry skill_path, specialist prompt, script defaults) resolves via bootstrap.py (get_project_root/get_pack_path/get_registry_path) — no hardcoded strings. Fix broken skill_path to real .xtrm location.

MIGRATION & BACK-COMPAT:
  - One-time LAYOUT migrator (distinct from content skill_migrator): packs/<repo>/<svc>/ -> packs/<repo>/service-skills/services/<svc>/; move + rewrite registry skill_path; generate umbrella SKILL.md from registry.
  - xt update / install understands BOTH old and new layouts during transition.
  - Existing installs (market-data, 16 services) upgrade cleanly.

CROSS-REPO: specialists repo service-skills-sync.specialist.json — update skill/registry/scope.py paths to consolidated service-skills/scripts/ + per-repo umbrella registry.

OPEN QUESTIONS FOR /planning:
  - Keep 4 old skill dirs as thin back-compat shims for one release, or hard-cut?
  - Umbrella SKILL.md generated from registry on sync/install, or hand-authored + drift-checked?
  - Does scope.py/router need pack name, or infer single pack per repo?
  - Back-compat window for .claude/skills skill_path reads.

NON-GOALS: no change to service-skill CONTENT model (contract/devops/gitnexus — done); no new infra telemetry; no drift-tiering behavior change beyond path resolution.

NEXT: decompose via /planning into children (consolidate, umbrella, path-fix, layout-migrator, back-compat, specialist update, validation).

title: draft: xtrm-workboard Pi extension for beads + specialists graph
description:
DRAFT / DESIGN BEAD

Goal: build a polished Pi workboard inspired by https://github.com/Soleone/pi-tasks, but specialized for XTRM's beads + specialists workflow rather than a generic task list.

Target UX:

  ✶ Executor writing boundary-layer tests… (26m 49s · thinking)
    ⎿  ◼ u4fdd.9 — Test: boundary launch/control
       ◻ u4fdd.7 — Smoke test: sp chat end-to-end
       ◻ u4fdd.6 — sp chat entrypoint: TUI + pi-tui
       ✔ u4fdd.4 — Status row component polling Supervisor
       ✔ u4fdd.3 — ChatFeed row-buffer component
        … +4 completed

Epic view should show the parent and children, plus specialist state inline:

  ✶ Epic u4fdd — sp chat TUI integration
    ⎿  ◼ u4fdd.9  reviewer   active     reviewing boundary tests
       ◐ u4fdd.7  executor   running    smoke test implementation
       ◻ u4fdd.6  ready      —          sp chat entrypoint
       ✔ u4fdd.4  closed     —          status row component
        … +4 completed

Reference inspected:
- Soleone/pi-tasks exists and is a Pi TUI extension for task backends.
- It provides commands/hotkeys (`/tasks`, ctrl+shift+r / alt+x), list/detail/edit views, keyboard navigation, and backend adapters.
- Its beads adapter is generic/flat: uses `bd list --status open --json`, `bd list --status in_progress --json`, `bd show <id> --json`, `bd update`, and `bd create`.
- Useful reference files from the repo:
  - `src/extension.ts` for command registration, backend initialization, session context injection.
  - `src/backend/adapters/beads.ts` for bd CLI JSON adapter shape.
  - `src/ui/pages/list.ts` and `src/controllers/list.ts` for pi-tui list rendering and key intent handling.

XTRM-specific requirements:
1. Build inside `@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions`, likely as `packages/pi-extensions/extensions/xtrm-workboard/`.
2. Prefer a read-only v1 that renders current work state before adding mutating actions.
3. Data sources:
   - `bd show <id> --json` for selected/current bead.
   - `bd list --parent <id> --json` or equivalent child query for epic/parent-child views.
   - `bd list --status=in_progress --json`, `bd ready --json`, and/or `bv --robot-next` for ready/current work.
   - `sp ps --json` for active jobs, epics, readiness, process health, and specialist-to-bead mapping.
4. Must show parent/child hierarchy, not only flat tasks.
5. Must integrate specialist state inline: executor/reviewer/overthinker/researcher, running/waiting/thinking/failed/pass, elapsed time, bead id, job id where useful.
6. Must respect XTRM/beads workflow gates: no silent status mutations; claim/close/dispatch actions should be explicit and safe.

Useful `sp ps --json` facts gathered:
- Top-level shape includes:
  - `counts`: `{ jobs, nodes, trees }`
  - `flat`: active jobs list (empty when no active jobs)
  - `nodes`, `trees`, `epics`
  - `epic_readiness`: map keyed by epic id
  - `process_health`: status, reasons, specialist processes, dolt processes, serena workspaces, orphan processes
- `epic_readiness.<epic>` includes:
  - `epic_id`
  - `persisted_state`, `readiness_state`, `next_state`, `can_transition`
  - `prep`: total/done/running/failed/blocker_job_ids
  - `chains[]`: chain_id, chain_root_bead_id, state, reviewer_verdict, has_active_jobs, job_ids, optional blocking_reason
  - `blockers[]`
  - `summary`
- Example blocked epic data:
  - `xtrm-9xg2` persisted_state=`resolving`, readiness_state=`blocked`, chains all blocked due to missing terminal reviewer verdicts.
- Example merge-ready epic data:
  - `xtrm-sk7f`, `xtrm-jwkf`, `xtrm-2yn4`, etc. readiness_state=`merge_ready`, chains pass.
- `process_health.specialistProcesses[]` can be used to infer live specialists even when `flat` is empty; entries include pid, kind, role, cmdline, cwd, rssBytes, cpuPct, ageSeconds, worktree.
- Example live specialists from provided output:
  - reviewer on `unitAI-u4fdd.9` with `--job 2384e4`
  - executor on `unitAI-u4fdd.7 --keep-alive`
  - reviewer on `unitAI-u4fdd.7 --job fe33e8`
- `process_health` also surfaces warnings such as `dolt sql-server count 2 > expected 1`, useful as a small health footer/status line.

Suggested UI modes:
- Current work mode: current claimed bead + siblings/children + active specialist status.
- Epic mode: selected parent/epic and all children grouped by active/ready/blocked/closed.
- Specialist mode: active jobs grouped under bead/epic.
- Ready mode: next actionable work from bd/bv.

Suggested interactions after read-only v1:
- Enter: inspect bead/detail panel.
- Tab: insert selected bead context into prompt.
- c: claim selected bead (explicit confirmation or clear action label).
- s: dispatch specialist for selected bead.
- r/f: open specialist result/feed for selected job.
- Space/status mutations only after safety design; avoid accidental gate-breaking edits.

Open design questions:
- Should this be a fork/contribution to `Soleone/pi-tasks` or a native XTRM extension? Current recommendation: native `xtrm-workboard` inside `@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions`, using pi-tasks as reference, because XTRM needs tight integration with beads claim state, `bv`, specialists, xtrm-ui style, and session/footer state.
- Should `sp ps --json` expose a more direct active-job-to-bead summary to avoid parsing `process_health.specialistProcesses[].cmdline` when `flat` is empty?
- How much process health should be shown in the polished default view vs hidden behind a details key?

Validation plan:
- Unit-test parsers/normalizers for bd JSON and `sp ps --json` fixtures, especially `epic_readiness` and process-health-only live specialist cases.
- Snapshot-test row model rendering for current-work, epic, blocked, merge-ready, no-active-job, and warning-health states.
- Manual Pi smoke: `/xtrm-workboard`, current bead, selected epic, active specialist jobs, empty state, narrow terminal, and keyboard close/navigation.

Non-goals for v1:
- No write actions in first implementation.
- No replacement for `bd`, `bv`, or `sp`; this is a compact visualization/control surface.
- No broad dependency on pi-tasks internals unless deliberately forked later.

title: Surface full bd command surface in triage skill + using-xtrm / using-specialists docs (esp. dep --type relationship types)
description:
We're under-using bd's full command surface. Triage and skill docs only reference a small subset (mostly bd ready, bd create, bd dep add, bd close), leaving the richer relationship vocabulary and query/decision/epic features invisible to agents and humans.

## Specific gaps

### Relationship types (bd dep add --type ...)
The full list — almost none of which appear in skills or CLAUDE.md:
- blocks (default) — hard dependency, gates ready state
- tracks — follows another issue's progress without blocking
- related / relates-to — non-blocking 'see also' link (also bd dep relate)
- parent-child — epic/child structural edge (set automatically by bd create --parent)
- discovered-from — follow-up issue spawned during work on another
- until — time/condition-bound link
- caused-by — bug caused by another issue (root-cause link)
- validates — issue verifies/proves another (e.g. test validates feature)
- supersedes — replaces an older issue

### Likely under-used commands
- bd query — SQL-like compound filters (only briefly mentioned in CLAUDE.md)
- bd decision — record/list/manage architectural decisions with rationale
- bd epic — epic management subcommands beyond --parent
- bd compact / bd restore — semantic summarization of old closed issues
- bd audit — append-only JSONL agent-interaction log
- bd label — label management
- bd preflight --check — pre-PR readiness gate
- bd kv get/list — beyond memory-acked usage
- bd dep relate / --blocks shorthand vs --type forms

## Where to surface

1. **Triage skill (planned, see prior session)** — when building the bead-triager, it should USE the right relationship types automatically:
   - caused-by for bug → root-cause edges
   - discovered-from when spawning follow-ups during triage
   - supersedes when merging duplicates
   - validates when linking test issues to features
   - tracks for non-blocking 'watch this' links
   Without these, the triager will default to blocks/relates-to and lose semantic richness.

2. **using-xtrm skill** — add a 'Relationship vocabulary' section + a one-screen cheat-sheet of high-value bd commands beyond the basics (query, decision, preflight, audit, epic, compact).

3. **using-specialists / using-specialists-v3 skills** — clarify which relationship type to use when chaining specialist beads:
   - executor → reviewer: blocks (reviewer can't run until executor waits) or tracks?
   - debugger root-cause findings → fix bead: caused-by
   - follow-ups spawned during a specialist run: discovered-from
   - test bead ↔ impl bead: validates

4. **CLAUDE.md** — expand the bd Command Reference block with --type table + brief note on bd query/decision/preflight.

## Deliverables
- Cheat-sheet section in using-xtrm SKILL.md
- Relationship-type mapping section in using-specialists-v3 SKILL.md  
- Triage skill design must reference the relationship vocabulary explicitly
- CLAUDE.md bd reference expanded

## Why
Agents (and the operator) default to a 3-verb subset of bd. The dep graph stays semantically thin — every edge is 'blocks' even when 'caused-by' / 'validates' / 'supersedes' would carry more meaning for future triage and reporting. Fixing the docs is the cheapest leverage to upgrade every future session.

## Related
- Prior session: bead-triager skill idea (not yet filed as issue)
- ~/dev/specialists#unitAI-ylphl — workflow catalog epic (these conventions should reference the relationship vocabulary too)

## Problem

`xt init` (and `xt install`) read `packageRoot/.xtrm/registry.json` and call `installFromRegistry` to copy hooks/skills into `userXtrmDir`. They never write `registry.json` itself into the user repo. As a result:

1. `xt update --root <dir>` can't discover newly initialized repos. `repo-discovery.ts:5-7` walks for `.xtrm/registry.json` as the managed-repo marker. Without it, fresh-init repos are invisible to bulk update.
2. Operators have to manually `cp $NPM_PKG/.xtrm/registry.json <repo>/.xtrm/registry.json` after init to make the repo discoverable. Reproduced this session across 12 mercury subprojects.

Memory: `xt-init-does-not-copy-xtrm-registry-json`.

## Proposals

### Option A — copy registry.json on init/install (minimal change)

At the end of `installFromRegistry` in `cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts:127`, write `packageRoot/.xtrm/registry.json` → `userXtrmDir/registry.json`.

- Pros: tiny diff, keeps existing discovery logic, matches what `~/dev/xtrm-tools` and `~/dev/specialists` already look like.
- Cons: per-repo registry becomes a version-stamped artifact that drifts after `npm i -g xtrm-tools@latest` until `xt update --apply` runs. Same model as today for repos that already have one.

### Option B — user-scope registry + per-repo marker

Stop copying the manifest into each repo. Read it directly from the installed npm package (`node_modules/xtrm-tools/.xtrm/registry.json`) for both install and doctor. `xt init` drops a tiny `.xtrm/.managed` (e.g., `{"managedBy":"xtrm-tools"}`) that `repo-discovery.ts` walks for instead.

- Pros: no per-repo manifest drift class. `xt doctor` always reads canonical hashes from package, so refresh-after-`npm install` is automatic. Cleaner mental model.
- Cons: loses ability to pin a repo to an older xtrm-tools via checked-in registry.json (notional — no one is doing this today; all consumer registries observed are verbatim copies of the package). Migration path: leave existing registry.json alongside the new marker; `repo-discovery.ts` accepts either; remove old form in a later release.

## Files

- `cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts:47` — `resolvePackageRoot`
- `cli/src/core/registry-scaffold.ts:127` — `installFromRegistry`
- `cli/src/core/repo-discovery.ts:5` — `REGISTRY_MARKER`
- `cli/src/commands/init.ts:760-780` — init flow
- `cli/src/commands/install.ts:140-180` — install flow
- `cli/src/commands/doctor.ts:174,283` — doctor reads `<cwd>/.xtrm/registry.json`
- `cli/src/commands/update.ts:24,29` — update reads `<repo>/.xtrm/registry.json`

## Recommendation

Option A first (1-line fix, unblocks bulk init), then Option B as a follow-up that removes per-repo registry.json from the model entirely. Option B is the cleaner long-term answer.

## Acceptance

- After `xt init` in a fresh repo, `xt update --root <parent>` discovers it without manual cp.
- `xt doctor` works in newly initialized repos.
- Existing repos with `registry.json` continue to work unchanged.

### Specialist Output — researcher (job 5df5d5) [DONE]

## Summary

**caveman-compress** is a Claude Code skill that compresses natural language memory files (CLAUDE.md, todos, preferences) into "caveman-speak" to reduce input tokens by ~46% on average.

### What It Does

| Aspect | Details |
|--------|---------|
| **Purpose** | Reduce input tokens every session by compressing context files |
| **Mechanism** | Rewrites prose to caveman format while preserving all technical content |
| **Savings** | ~46% average token reduction (benchmarks: 36-60% range) |
| **Output** | `FILE.md` (compressed) + `FILE.original.md` (human-readable backup) |

### CLI Usage

```bash
# Via Claude Code skill (recommended)
/caveman:compress CLAUDE.md
/caveman:compress docs/preferences.md
/caveman:compress todos.md

# Direct Python CLI (from repo)
cd caveman-compress && python3 -m scripts <absolute_filepath>
```

### What Gets Compressed vs Preserved

| Compressed | Preserved Exactly |
|------------|-------------------|
| Articles (a, an, the) | Code blocks (```...```) |
| Filler (just, really, basically) | Inline code (`backticks`) |
| Pleasantries ("sure", "happy to") | URLs and links |
| Hedging ("might be worth") | File paths |
| Redundant phrasing | Commands (npm, git, docker) |
| Connective fluff (however, furthermore) | Technical terms, API names |
| | Dates, versions, numbers |
| | Headings, tables, structure |

### When to Use

- **CLAUDE.md / AGENTS.md** — loads every session, high ROI
- **Project preferences** — coding standards, style guides
- **Todo lists** — natural language task tracking
- **Session reports** — historical context files
- **Any `.md`/`.txt` natural language file** — not code/config

### Application to xtrm-tools Workflows

| xtrm File | Benefit | Notes |
|-----------|---------|-------|
| `.xtrm/memory.md` | High | Injected every session — 46% savings compounds |
| `CLAUDE.md` / `AGENTS.md` | High | Session-start context, ~1000+ tokens typical |
| `.xtrm/reports/*.md` | Medium | Historical context for new sessions |
| `docs/*.md` | Low | Only if referenced in session context |
| `*.py`, `*.ts`, `*.json` | ❌ Skip | Code/config files auto-skipped |

### Implementation Notes

- **One-time cost**: Compression uses tokens once; savings apply every session thereafter
- **Validation**: Headings, code blocks, URLs, paths validated post-compression

title: Fix YouTube transcript fetch for non-English videos
description:
youtube_yt.py fails to fetch transcripts for non-English YouTube videos. Two root causes:

1. _fetch_transcript_ytdlp() hardcodes --sub-lang en (line 375), so yt-dlp skips videos with only non-English auto-captions (e.g. Italian-only live streams).

title: P0: Create symlinks for npm package extensions (pi-gitnexus, pi-serena-tools) during xt init/reload
description:
## Problem

Specialists spawns pi with `--no-extensions` then selectively re-enables extensions via `-e <path>`. The code already has logic to load `gitnexus` and `serena` from `~/.pi/agent/extensions/`, but these are installed as npm packages, not directory extensions.

## Root Cause

- `pi-gitnexus` is installed at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v25.2.1/lib/node_modules/pi-gitnexus`
- `pi-serena-tools` is installed at `~/.nvm/versions/node/v25.2.1/lib/node_modules/pi-serena-tools`
- Specialists looks for them at `~/.pi/agent/extensions/gitnexus` and `~/.pi/agent/extensions/serena`
- Without symlinks, specialists subprocesses don't get gitnexus/serena tools

## Solution

Add symlink creation to `xt init` or `xt reload`:

```bash
# GitNexus
ln -sf ~/.nvm/versions/node/v25.2.1/lib/node_modules/pi-gitnexus \
       ~/.pi/agent/extensions/gitnexus

# Serena
ln -sf ~/.nvm/versions/node/v25.2.1/lib/node_modules/pi-serena-tools \
       ~/.pi/agent/extensions/serena
```

## Impact

Without this fix, specialists (debugger, executor, etc.) don't have access to:
- `gitnexus_query`, `gitnexus_context`, `gitnexus_impact`, `gitnexus_detect_changes`
- Serena tools for code navigation and LSP features

## Verification

After fix, specialists should show gitnexus tools in their available tool list and be able to call `/gitnexus status` successfully.
