title: main-guard: default-deny Bash with safe allowlist on protected branches
description:
## Context
Issue xyi identified that arbitrary Bash file-write commands (cat >, tee, cp, mv, sed -i) bypass main-guard on protected branches. Reviewer comment #4 on xyi recommends the stronger fix: default-deny all Bash on protected branches, with a narrow allowlist of safe/non-mutating commands.

## Reviewer recommendation (xyi comment #4)
'On protected branches, default-deny Bash with a small allowlist for safe/non-mutating branch-exit and inspection commands, plus an explicit emergency override path.'

## Proposed allowlist (safe on protected branches)
- git checkout -b <name>     (create feature branch — the intended exit path)
- git switch -c <name>       (same)
- git status / git log / git diff / git branch (read-only inspection)
- git stash                  (safe, doesn't write to branch)
- bd <any>                   (beads issue tracking, no file mutations)
- cat <file> (read-only, no redirect)

## Block by default
- Any command containing output redirect: >, >>
- cat/tee/cp/mv/sed -i/awk writing to paths under input.cwd
- git commit / git push (already handled, confirm preserved)
- npm/python/sh script execution (potential indirect writes)

## Emergency override
- Env var: MAIN_GUARD_ALLOW_BASH=1 (escape hatch, visible and explicit)

## Acceptance criteria
- On main, cat > file is blocked
- On main, git status is allowed
- On main, git checkout -b feature/x is allowed
- On main, bd create is allowed
- MAIN_GUARD_ALLOW_BASH=1 bypasses the Bash default-deny
- Existing Write/Edit blocking unchanged

## Open idea review
The allowlist approach assumes we can enumerate safe commands — but shell is composable and creative bypasses exist. Is default-deny Bash the right tradeoff between security and usability? Should there be a 'warn but allow' mode vs hard block, configurable per-project? Consider how often legitimate Bash on main is needed (hot fixes, deploy scripts) and whether that warrants a softer default.

title: main-guard: Bash file-write commands bypass protection on main branch
description:
## Bug

The main-guard hook (`~/.claude/hooks/specialists-main-guard.mjs`) protects Write/Edit/MultiEdit/NotebookEdit tools completely, but its Bash protection is narrowly scoped to git operations only.

## Current Bash check

```js
if (tool === 'Bash') {
  if (/^git commit/.test(cmd)) { /* block */ }
  if (/^git push/.test(cmd))   { /* block */ }
  // everything else → process.exit(0)
}
```

## The gap

All shell-based file writes bypass the guard entirely on main:
- `cat > file << 'EOF'`
- `echo 'content' > file`
- `tee file`
- `cp src dst`
- `mv src dst`
- `sed -i`
- `awk '...' > file`

## Observed in this session

All four beads hooks (`beads-edit-gate.mjs`, `beads-stop-gate.mjs`, `beads-commit-gate.mjs`, `beads-close-memory-prompt.mjs`) and the new `beads-gate-utils.mjs` were written via `cat > heredoc` in Bash while on `main`. Main-guard never fired.

Note: those writes targeted `~/.claude/hooks/` (outside the project repo), so they wouldn't have been harmful — but the gap exists for in-repo writes too.

## Proposed fix

**Option A — Pattern matching**: detect common shell file-write patterns in the Bash command string. Brittle — easy to bypass or over-match.

**Option B — Scope check (preferred)**: check whether the Bash command touches files inside `input.cwd` (the project directory). If the command contains a path that falls under the project root, block it on main.

Challenges with Option B:
- Bash commands don't always make target paths explicit or easy to parse
- Multi-command strings (`cmd1 && cmd2`) need full parsing or heuristic scanning
- Could still be bypassed with indirect writes (subshells, scripts)

**Option C — Hybrid**: block known write-pattern prefixes (`cat >`, `tee `, `cp `, `mv `, `echo >`) only when the target path is inside `input.cwd`. Narrow enough to avoid false positives, covers the most common cases.

## Question for reviewer

Is Option C the right tradeoff? Or is this gap acceptable given that the main-guard's primary surface is structured tools (Write/Edit), and Bash is already a power-user escape hatch that implies intentionality?
close_reason: Fixed by main-guard v2 (ea36a92). Default-deny Bash with SAFE_BASH_PATTERNS allowlist is implemented in hooks/main-guard.mjs. All unlisted Bash commands are blocked on protected branches.

Reason:

- The observed bypass came from Bash behavior in `specialists-main-guard.mjs`.

title: Refactor beads-edit-gate to use session-scoped issue claiming via bd kv
description:
## Problem

The current beads-edit-gate.mjs checks if ANY issue is in_progress globally. In multi-agent or multi-session scenarios (parallel subagents, concurrent sessions), agent B can free-ride on agent A's in_progress issue — making edits without ever claiming work itself. The gate's intent (enforce ownership before editing) is not met in these cases.

## Goal

Gate on whether THIS agent/session has explicitly claimed an issue, not whether anyone has one in_progress.

## Design

### Primitives available
- Hook input JSON includes `session_id` (unique per Claude Code session)
- `bd kv set/get/clear` is project-scoped (stored in .beads/dolt) — confirmed real
- `bd kv list` shows all keys; memories use the `memory.*` prefix

### Claim registry pattern

**Claiming** (agent takes ownership):
```bash
bd update <id> --status=in_progress
bd kv set "claimed:<session_id>" "<issue_id>"
```

**Gate check** (beads-edit-gate.mjs):
```js
const sessionId = input.session_id;
const claimed = execSync(`bd kv get "claimed:${sessionId}"`, { cwd, encoding: 'utf8', ... });
if (!claimed.trim()) {
  // block — this session has not claimed an issue
}
```

**Release** (on close — beads-close-memory-prompt.mjs already fires on bd close):
- Parse closed issue ID from the Bash command
- Run `bd kv clear "claimed:<session_id>"`

### Files to modify
1. `~/.claude/hooks/beads-edit-gate.mjs` (and project-skills source if one exists)
   - Replace global in_progress check with `bd kv get "claimed:<session_id>"` check
   - Fall back to old behavior if session_id is absent (non-Claude environments)
   - Keep the open=0 bypass for clean-start state (no issues at all)

2. `~/.claude/hooks/beads-close-memory-prompt.mjs`
   - After detecting `bd close`, also run `bd kv clear "claimed:<session_id>"`
   - Use session_id from hook input

3. Update SKILL.md for using-main-guard / beads workflow docs to show:
   `bd update <id> --status=in_progress && bd kv set "claimed:<session_id>" "<id>"`
   OR expose a wrapper alias/command

### Open questions before implementing
1. Should we expose a `bd-claim <id>` thin shell wrapper (in hooks/scripts/) to bundle update + kv set in one command, so the workflow stays ergonomic?
2. What should happen if the agent crashes mid-session and the kv claim is never cleared? Consider a TTL or session-start cleanup of stale claim keys.
3. beads-stop-gate.mjs and beads-commit-gate.mjs also use global in_progress — should they be updated in the same pass to check session-scoped claims instead?

## Acceptance criteria
- Agent A has issue X in_progress; agent B cannot edit files without running its own claim
- Single-agent workflow unchanged: claim → edit → close → claim cleared automatically
- Gate fails open (exit 0) if bd kv is unavailable or session_id is missing
- Tests cover: claimed session allowed, unclaimed session blocked, multi-session isolation
close_reason: Implemented session-scoped claiming in all four beads hooks via bd kv

title: beads-edit-gate fires on legitimate close-then-write workflow
description:
The beads-edit-gate blocks writes immediately after closing completed issues, even when the agent is still in the middle of a session with follow-up work. Two friction patterns observed:

1. Close-then-write: batch-closing multiple done issues (bd close A B C) leaves in_progress=0, then the next Write/Edit fires the gate before a new issue is created. Forces redundant re-marking cycle every time work transitions.

2. Post-compaction reset: after /compact, all in_progress issues revert to open in the gate's view — the compaction hook (bd prime) injects context but doesn't restore status. Agent must re-run bd update --status=in_progress before the first write of the resumed session.

Root cause: gate checks live bd list --status=in_progress with a hard 0=block rule. No grace period, no awareness of recent close, no session-level tracking concept.

Possible fixes to evaluate:
- Allow if ALL issues are closed and none are open (session-complete state is valid)
- Grace period: if bd close ran in the last N seconds, skip the check
- Session issue: auto-create/suggest a session tracking issue at start via SessionStart hook
- Gate tolerance: skip for markdown/docs-only files when no in_progress exists

title: Smoke: explore extension override merge path with installed tools
description: READ-ONLY smoke. Trace how ~/.config/specialists/user.json execution.extensions flows through schema validation, layered per-key merge, and Pi argv construction across package and script paths. Report exact symbols/files and independently count relevant definitions/usages. Do not edit files. Use the tools naturally available to the explorer; record which tools were actually used and whether any newly configured extension tool is selected autonomously.
notes:
### explorer · deepseek-v4-flash · [turn 5 · WORKING]

## Summary
In this Core repo the schema validation + layered per-key merge for `~/.config/specialists/user.json` `execution.extensions` do NOT exist here — they live in the external Specialists runtime (`~/dev/specialists`, a `sp` binary Core shells out to). Core only consumes the already-merged output of `sp view <name> --raw`, parses `execution.extensions` into a `Record<string,boolean>`, stores it on `ResolvedRole`, and then deliberately does NOT forward it to Pi argv (trusts Pi discovery). The package path (`xt pi --role`) drops it; the script path (Specialists dispatch) is outside this worktree boundary. A separate, unrelated extension mechanism exists in `core/pi-runtime.ts` (Pi `settings.json` `extensions` symlink deployment).

## Status
success (read-only; no edits)

## Architecture

title: python-kernel audit seam: kernel-side mutation events visible to host (phase 2)
description:
PROBLEM (phase 2, guardrail seam): once skills run in-kernel, pi's host guardrails (claim gate, quality hooks) are blind to kernel-side file mutations - the one real tradeoff of the prime-agent pattern.
DESIGN (convention-first, zero enforcement initially): DRIVER reserves _AUDIT list; skill convention = append {"op":"write","path":...} entries; driver includes _AUDIT in every run_cell reply; TS host logs to session details and (later) policy-gates mutating ops (e.g., block writes outside session cwd). Mirror-image of prime-agent's harness.py/rlm.run bridge which exists to manage exactly this.
SUCCESS: kernel cells that mutate files produce host-visible audit entries; policy hook exists behind a flag before any enforcement ships.
VALIDATION: unit: fixture skill appending _AUDIT shows entries in reply; host log line appears in tool details.
NON_GOALS: sandboxing; blocking-by-default.
close_reason: audit seam: _AUDIT reserved+initialized in driver, bound into skill module namespaces, copied into every run_cell reply; TS surfaces audit in tool details + policy hook (auditPolicy option, off by default) flags out-of-session writes report-only. 3 new tests (entries flow, policy on/off). Full pi-extensions suite 30 pass/0 fail, typecheck + check:pi-manifest clean.

title: python-kernel QoL: stdlib prelude + output truncation with shape hint
description:
PROBLEM: QoL/context-guard gaps in the kernel: (a) first cells always burn boilerplate imports (json, re, os, sys, subprocess, pathlib.Path); (b) a huge repr (big list/dict/dataframe) can flood the context window - driver returns full stdout uncapped.
DESIGN: (a) DRIVER prelude: import json,re,os,sys,subprocess + from pathlib import Path into _ns at boot (documented in tool description). (b) stdout/repr cap: configurable max (default ~20KB): if over, return head 8KB + "\n...[truncated N chars]...\n" + tail 4KB + object-shape hint when detectable (len/type); full output optionally written to a temp file path included in reply.
SUCCESS: boilerplate imports gone from typical first cells; a 2MB print() comes back truncated with shape hint + temp path, never floods context.
VALIDATION: unit test on truncation logic; manual: print("x"*3_000_000) => truncated reply with path.
NON_GOALS: pandas-specific formatting (generic shape hint only); streaming (further-ideas list).
close_reason: QoL: DRIVER prelude pre-loads json/re/os/sys/subprocess/Path into _ns (documented in tool description); driver-side output cap (default 20KB) returns head 8KB + marker + tail 4KB with shape hint (type+len) and full copy in a temp file whose path is in the reply; exported truncateOutput() pure helper + 9 new/updated tests. Full pi-extensions suite 27 pass/0 fail, npm run typecheck + check:pi-manifest clean.

title: skill(devops): host administration without root — four evidenced findings looking for a home
description:
## PROBLEM

Four findings from the 2026-08-04/05 capacity P0 are sysadmin-shaped rather than capacity-shaped. `capacity-reclaim` absorbed only the ones that touched reclaim; these four are evidenced, cost real time, and currently live nowhere except bead notes and an ad-hoc script in the operator's home directory.

They share one theme: **an agent operating on a host without root**. That is a different competence from "is anything broken" (`sre-triage`), "is what we merged running" (`deploy-monitor`), or "what can I safely reclaim" (`capacity-reclaim`).

## EVIDENCE — all four from real failures, none invented

1. **The unprivileged agency boundary.** User dawid has no passwordless sudo. This blocked work four separate times in one incident: two root-owned `rust_ingestor/target` dirs on disk, two root-owned cargo trees in tmpfs, the systemd timer install, and `chgrp 65534` on a credential file. Each time the correct move was to stop and hand the operator exact commands, not to work around it. An agent needs to recognise the wall on first contact and escalate with a precise, runnable command block — silently under-delivering a reclaim total is the failure mode.

2. **systemd unit installation.** `install -m` never `cp -p` — a preserved mode is the umask fault in another costume. Dry-run before enable. Verify with `systemctl list-timers`, not with the absence of an error. Always print the undo command. This pattern exists today only in `~/install-runner-sweep-timer.sh`; nothing captures it.

3. **journald readability.** `journalctl -u <unit>` returns "No entries" — not an error — unless the caller is in `adm` or `systemd-journal`. The unit had run fine (`Result=success`, `ExecMainStatus=0`); only the journal was unreadable. Cost a confused round trip. Fix is `sudo journalctl` or `usermod -aG systemd-journal`. Generalises: a read that returns empty because of group membership looks identical to a read that returns empty because nothing happened.

4. **Container-versus-host identity.** Containers run as `nobody` (65534) against host-owned bind mounts. Host file modes govern what the container can read. Narrowing a credential file properly needs `chgrp 65534 && chmod 0640`, which requires root, so an unprivileged agent's only lever is world-read — a security trade-off it must surface rather than take silently.

## ROUGH SCOPE — TBD, deliberately draft

Candidate: a thin sibling skill, `host-admin-unprivileged` or similar, in `dev/core` at `.xtrm/skills/default/`, following the shape `deploy-monitor` sets (tight doctrine, ~175 lines, not a command lookup table).

It is NOT a general sysadmin skill. Users, networking, backups, package management have no verified evidence behind them from this incident, and inventing them is precisely the failure mode the `capacity-reclaim` contract was written to prevent. Four evidenced items is enough for a thin skill and not enough for a broad one.

## WHY THIS IS DRAFT AND NOT READY

The same reason `xtrm-gvek4` sat in draft until its lanes finished: four findings from one incident is a thin base. Before promoting, either (a) wait for a second incident to exercise and extend them, or (b) audit the existing beads and service knowledge for other unprivileged-agency findings already recorded elsewhere. Promote only when the rule set is demonstrably not a sample of one.

Open question for whoever promotes it: does this belong as its own skill, or as a section inside `capacity-reclaim`? Rules 1, 8, 9, 10 and 11 of that skill already brush against it. Splitting has a real cost — two skills that both half-cover container-vs-host identity is worse than one that covers it fully. Decide that before writing a line.

## REFERENCES

Incident bead `mercury-market-data-9kjj4`. Skill bead `xtrm-gvek4` (capacity-reclaim, merged as PR #541). Lane beads `infra-2e7s`, `infra-j6x2`, `infra-hoky`, `infra-y435`. Script: `~/install-runner-sweep-timer.sh`.

title: npm pack includes gitignored .xtrm/skills/default/gitnexus from a local working copy
description:
## PROBLEM

package.json 'files' includes '.xtrm/skills/default' wholesale. npm pack honours 'files' and
.npmignore, NOT .gitignore. So a directory that is gitignored but present on disk still gets
packed.

.xtrm/skills/default/gitnexus/ is gitignored at .gitignore:181 and is present in this working
copy (mtime 2026-07-13, 6 skill directories, 0 tracked files).

Result, in this checkout:

  npm run check:registry-pack-parity
    Missing from npm pack: none
    Missing from registry:
    - .xtrm/skills/default/gitnexus/gitnexus-cli/SKILL.md
    - ... 6 files

Verified NOT caused by any current change: the same failure appears with the working registry
edit stashed.

## WHY CI IS GREEN

CI packs from a fresh clone, where a gitignored directory does not exist. So the check passes
there and fails only on a developer or agent machine that has the local gitnexus skills.

## ACTUAL RISK — narrow, but real

core and xtmux publish from CI, so they are safe today. specialists publishes LOCALLY
(release_execute.py: 'run npm publish --access public locally'), so a local publish from a
polluted tree would ship files the registry does not list. specialists does not currently have
this directory, which is the only reason it has not happened.

## SUCCESS

- npm pack never includes a path that .gitignore excludes, or the parity check explains the
  difference instead of reporting a bare mismatch.
- Simplest shape: add the same exclusion to the 'files' negations, next to the existing
  '!**/__pycache__/**' entries.
- A local 'npm pack' from a polluted working copy produces the same file list as a clean clone.

## NON_GOALS

Removing the local gitnexus skills. They are deliberately gitignored and useful locally.

## NOT A RELEASE BLOCKER

Recorded during the 2026-07-27 release preparation. core publishes via CI; specialists lacks the
directory. Verify the specialists tree is clean immediately before its local npm publish.

title: xtmux log-follow can outlive its parent shell with no reap
description:
## PROBLEM

An 'xtmux log-follow --after-id <n> --json' bun subprocess was found alive 1h38m after the shell that started it had been killed. Nothing reaped it.

## HOW IT WAS FOUND

While gathering evidence for xtrm-wiy5n.4.17. fuser on the coordination DB reported:

  /home/dawid/.local/state/xtmux/observability.db:
    dawid  3643653  F....  bun.exe
  ps: .../bun.exe src/cli.ts log-follow --after-id 1597066 --json
  elapsed 01:38:19

Its parent was a scripts/test-session-events.sh --json run whose shell had been killed about an hour before. The DB was 550 MB with an 8.9 MB WAL.

## WHY IT MATTERS

A long-lived reader on the coordination DB is exactly the load that exposed the silent hang in 4.17. 4.17 makes the hang visible and bounded. It does not stop the orphan from being created.

## SUCCESS

A log-follow subprocess ends when the shell that started it ends, or it is reaped by something that outlives both.

## SCOPE

xtmux log-follow process lifecycle, and scripts/test-session-events.sh.

## NON_GOALS

Reworking the observability DB.
notes:
MERGED as Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#86. Worker %7634.

THE NON-OBVIOUS ROOT CAUSE
Bun CACHES process.ppid at process startup. The worker verified this directly: /proc/self/status
reported 'PPid: 1' while process.ppid still returned the original parent. So a follower that
checked process.ppid could never notice it had been reparented, and would run forever.

THE FIX
log-follow reads the LIVE parent from the kernel on each poll tick — /proc/self/status on Linux,
'ps -o ppid=' elsewhere — and exits when it sees ppid 1 or 0. It returns 0 on error, which
preserves the 'unknown ppid means treat as reparented' semantic. SIGHUP is now handled too.

scripts/test-session-events.sh traps SIGHUP alongside INT and TERM, so a closed terminal or a
detached tmux pane reaches the same graceful teardown path as a Ctrl-C.

PROOFS
SIGKILL the parent — the child dies within 5s with no signal reaching it. HUP-trap contract on the
shell script. Both verified to fail when broken. Suites: 317 bun + 242 contract-shell, green.
5 CI checks SUCCESS, no Codex threads.
close_reason: Merged as xtmux#86. log-follow self-reaps by reading the live parent pid from the kernel each tick, because Bun caches process.ppid at startup and would never see reparenting. SIGHUP now reaches the same teardown path.

title: specialists repo carries 146 stale specialist worktrees and 322 local branches
description:
## MEASURED 2026-07-26

  git worktree list | wc -l              166
  git worktree list | grep -c unitAI-    146
  git branch --list | wc -l              322

The 146 are per-job specialist worktrees under .worktrees/unitAI-*/ from earlier epics — reviewer, executor, sync-docs, debugger. Their jobs are long finished. A handful of xt/* worktrees under .xtrm/worktrees/ are also stale.

## WHY IT MATTERS

- 'git worktree list' is unreadable, which makes ordinary cleanup verification expensive. This bead exists because that output buried a real check today.
- xt worktree branch-gc cannot collect a branch that a worktree still holds. Its own output says so: 'branch is checked out in a worktree; remove/finish the worktree first'. So the worktrees block the branch GC, and the branch count stays at 322.
- Disk and inode cost, unmeasured.

## NOT DONE, DELIBERATELY

Removing 146 worktrees is destructive and none of them are mine. The operator decides. This bead records the measurement so the decision has numbers.

## SUGGESTED SEQUENCE WHEN AUTHORISED

1. xt worktree branch-gc --json          — dry run, already verified to work here
2. xt worktree audit-prs --json          — find PR drift first
3. Remove worktrees whose owning job is terminal, checking each for a dirty tree and for unpushed commits BEFORE removal
4. Re-run branch-gc, which can now collect what the worktrees were pinning

## SUCCESS

The worktree list fits on a screen. branch-gc is no longer blocked by dead worktrees. No worktree with uncommitted or unpushed work is removed.
notes:
READ-ONLY AUDIT DONE, then REFINED by the orchestrator. Nothing was deleted.

Worker %7640 produced /tmp/w439-audit.md and /tmp/w439-audit.json — one row per worktree with
path, branch, dirty count, unpushed commits, PR state, age, verdict. Its raw verdicts were
161 REVIEW / 4 SAFE_TO_REMOVE / 1 KEEP. Correctly conservative, but not usable as a decision.

WHY 161 REVIEW WAS A FALSE SIGNAL
The verdict keyed on a RAW dirty count. Nearly every dirty entry is machine-generated churn:

  AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md                       GitNexus/OpenWolf rewrite them every session; both
                                             are already in the release-preflight ephemeral
                                             allowlist (_release_common.py EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS)
  .xtrm/skills/active/gitnexus/*/SKILL.md     the generated runtime skills view

None of that is human work. Re-classified with the ephemeral filter applied:

  total worktrees                                166
  fully clean                                     15
  dirty ONLY with ephemeral files                145
  dirty with REAL files                            6
  rows with unpushed commits                      14

  SAFE once the ephemeral filter applies         148
  NEEDS A HUMAN (real dirt or unpushed)           18

0 rows have an OPEN PR, so nothing is at risk of being stranded.

THE 18 THAT NEED A HUMAN — real_dirty / unpushed
  ctb4u-rebase                              1 / 0   sp
  spec-r6g-w3                               0 / 2
  specialists (main checkout)               0 / 1
  specialists-postmerge-190                 2 / 0   dist/index.js, dist/lib.js
  specialists-xt-claude-7dgf                0 / 3
  specialists-xt-claude-specialists-origin  0 / 3
  specialists-xt-pi-6mcc                    0 / 3
  specialists-xt-pi-b9nh                    1 / 0   .xtrm/session-meta.json
  specialists-xt-pi-rn2t                    0 / 8
  unitAI-0lxyc-reviewer                     0 / 1
  unitAI-4de2k-reviewer                     0 / 1
  unitAI-ctb4u.28-executor                  1 / 1   src/specialist/script-runner.ts
  unitAI-nf2xq-reviewer                     0 / 1
  unitAI-npupu-reviewer                     0 / 1
  unitAI-q5t29-executor                     2 / 0   package.json, .xtrm/reports/...
  unitAI-zflxc-reviewer                     0 / 1
  xtmux-3ua10-specialists                   2 / 1   .beads/issues.jsonl, dist/.unitai/trace.jsonl
  xtrm-56flm.4.1-specialists-creator        0 / 2

Several of the 'real dirty' entries are themselves build output (dist/*.js, trace.jsonl) and
would likely clear on inspection, which would shrink the list further. I did not assume that.

STILL NOT AUTHORIZED. The operator decides. The proposed shape is: remove the 148, leave the 18,
then re-run 'xt worktree branch-gc --json' — which currently refuses with 'branch is checked out
in a worktree; remove/finish the worktree first' — and see how much of the 322-branch count it
can then collect.
close_reason: CLEANED, operator-authorised 2026-07-28. worktrees 166->49, unitAI-* 146->33, local branches 324->115, disk 6.4G->4.0G (2.4G freed). METHOD: classified every worktree read-only before touching anything — dirty (ignoring generated/ephemeral paths: .xtrm/skills/state.json, .xtrm/skills/active/, .specialists/user, .specialists/db/, .beads/interactions.jsonl, AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .wolf), unpushed vs origin/master, and live-in-tmux. Verdicts 117 SAFE / 38 UNPUSHED / 5 DIRTY / 0 LIVE. Each SAFE worktree was RE-VERIFIED at the moment of deletion, not from the stale list. --force was needed only because AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md are rewritten every session by OpenWolf/GitNexus and git worktree remove cannot know they are ephemeral. Branches: xt worktree branch-gc --apply deleted 4 (merged PRs, xt/ prefix only); then 205 feature/unitAI-* branches proven ancestors of origin/master were deleted with the SAFE 'git branch -d', which git itself refuses on anything unmerged — 0 refusals, so all 205 were genuinely merged. PRESERVED: 5 worktrees with real uncommitted work, 38 with unpushed commits, 44 unmerged feature branches. SUCCESS CRITERIA MET: worktree list fits on a screen, branch-gc no longer blocked, and no worktree with uncommitted or unpushed work was removed.

title: specialists: the Node test runner must fail fast when bun:sqlite is not loadable
description:
## PROBLEM

Running the specialists suite with 'npx vitest run' (Node) does not say that the runner is wrong. It fails deep inside the product: createObservabilitySqliteClient() returns null because Node cannot require('bun:sqlite'), and supervisor.ts:1281 then throws.

The error surfaces as:
  [supervisor] SQLite upsertStatus failed: database client unavailable

Nothing in that message names the runner.

## COST ALREADY PAID

On 2026-07-26 this produced a false flake report against three test files, then a P2 bead (xtrm-wiy5n.4.33), then a full triage worker. Every one of the three files was already green. The whole chain was avoidable.

## SUCCESS

Running the suite under Node stops within seconds and states, in one line, that the suite requires bun and that the command is 'bun --bun vitest run'.

## SCOPE

specialists: the test setup file or the test:node script. Do not change product code to accommodate the wrong runner.

## NON_GOALS

Making the suite actually work under Node. bun:sqlite is a bun builtin. The goal is a fast, clear refusal, not a port.

## VALIDATION

[ ] 'npx vitest run' exits fast with a message naming bun and the correct command
[ ] 'bun --bun vitest run' is unaffected
[ ] CI is unaffected
close_reason: Merged as specialists#237. The suite now refuses under Node in one line naming bun and the correct command, instead of failing deep inside supervisor.ts with a message that named neither.

title: archon CLI cannot resume an approved workflow run; run 40737a6f is stuck
description:
## PROBLEM

An approved workflow run cannot resume from the command line. The run then stays paused, and a reject is refused.

## HOW IT HAPPENED

2026-07-26. The orchestrator started the release workflow for a read-only dry run.

  archon workflow run xtrm-release "dry-run all"

The run paused at its operator-approval node. That pause is correct and by design. The node printed two commands:

  Approve: /workflow approve <run-id>
  Reject:  /workflow reject <run-id>

The orchestrator sent the approve command. Archon answered:

  Workflow xtrm-release approved.
  Type your response in this conversation to resume the workflow.

There is no command-line way to type that response. `archon --help` lists no resume, reply or continue-run command. `archon chat "dry-run all"` opens a NEW orchestrator conversation instead, and that conversation ran an unrelated dry run of pytest and docker compose.

A reject is then refused:

  Failed to reject workflow run: <id> was already approved and is awaiting resume.

So the run is stuck in state paused, approved, awaiting a reply that the CLI cannot send.

## CURRENT STUCK RUN

  id:   40737a6f61e661c3d4f1872d731395ce
  name: xtrm-release
  path: /home/dawid/dev/core

It holds no danger. No mutation ran. ARCHON_ALLOW_RELEASE was not set, so every execute node would skip. The approval reply was going to be "dry-run all", which mutates nothing.

An operator can resume it in the web UI with `archon serve`, or leave it.

## SUCCESS

- A command-line user can send an approval reply, for example `archon workflow reply <run-id> "<text>"`.
- Or, `approve` accepts the reply text in the same command.
- Or, a reject succeeds after an approve, while the run still waits.

## SCOPE

- archon CLI workflow subcommands

## NON_GOALS

- Changing the operator-approval design. The human gate is correct.

## VALIDATION

[ ] An approved run can resume from the command line
[ ] Or an approved run can be cancelled from the command line
notes:
WHERE A FIX WOULD HAVE TO LAND — checked 2026-07-27, and it changes what 'fix this' means.

  which archon            -> ~/.bun/bin/archon
  readlink                -> ~/.bun/install/global/node_modules/@archon/cli/src/cli.ts
  installed version       -> 0.6.0
  local checkout          -> /home/dawid/dev/vendor/Archon, version 0.6.0
  its origin              -> https://github.com/coleam00/Archon

So archon is a THIRD-PARTY upstream, not one of the three xtrm repos. Adding
'archon workflow reply <run-id> "<text>"' means an upstream contribution to someone else's
project, or a local fork. That is an operator decision, not something to start unilaterally, so
no work was begun.

WHAT IS AVAILABLE WITHOUT TOUCHING ARCHON
The operator runbook on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.4 routes around the gap: start the release from a
context that can type a reply — an interactive Claude or Pi conversation with the archon skill,
or possibly the 'archon serve' web UI, which I have NOT verified. That makes this bead a
convenience item rather than a release blocker.

STILL TRUE: run 40737a6f61e661c3d4f1872d731395ce is paused and cannot be resumed or rejected from
the CLI. If nothing can clear it, the second-best outcome is that reject should work on an
approved-awaiting-resume run so a stuck run can at least be removed from 'workflow status'.
close_reason: PREMISE PARTLY WRONG — corrected by using the CLI during the 0.11.3 release. archon workflow DOES expose resume/abandon/approve/reject (full list: list,run,status,get,runs,resume,abandon,approve,reject,cleanup,event,search,install). There is no 'cancel' despite the paused-run banner saying '/workflow cancel'. Reject is refused only AFTER approval ('already approved and is awaiting resume'); abandon always works and is the right call for a stale paused run. Stuck run 40737a6f: ABANDONED 2026-07-28, workflow status now clean; it was a 30h-old 'dry-run all' whose preflight/classify data predated every fix, so resuming it would have acted on stale input. THE REAL DEFECT, which this bead missed: 'archon workflow approve <id>' WITHOUT the reply text silently drops the directive — route-decision receives 'approved', matches no repo, skips every gated node, and the run reports 'completed successfully' having released nothing (10 completed/12 skipped in 1s). Passing the text gives 15 completed/7 skipped and the execute nodes run. Saved to memory as archon-workflow-approve-resume + bd key archon-approve-directive.

title: specialists CI uses bun-version latest; one bun release can stop every pull request
description:
## PROBLEM

Two specialists workflows set `bun-version: latest`. They are `telemetry-contract.yml` and the new `tests` job from xtrm-dev/specialists#231.

A new bun release changes the runtime under every pull request at the same moment. Nobody changed the repository. Every pull request stops together.

## EVIDENCE

Found 2026-07-26 by the worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.26. The worker did not change it. It said the value matches house style, and it did not want to change house style alone. That was the correct decision.

## WHY IT MATTERS MORE NOW

Before #231, only one job used bun, and a paths filter guarded that job. So the exposure was small.

After #231, a bun job runs on every pull request. The exposure is now total.

## SUCCESS

- The bun version is pinned in every workflow.
- A separate, deliberate change moves the version.
- A comment records why the version moved.

## SCOPE

- specialists .github/workflows/telemetry-contract.yml
- specialists the tests workflow added by #231

## NON_GOALS

- Pinning every other action here. #231 already pinned the new actions by SHA.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Use one version value in both files. Two values create a second problem.

## VALIDATION

[ ] No workflow uses bun-version latest
[ ] The pinned version passes the suite
close_reason: Merged as xtrm-dev/specialists#233. The bun version is pinned now, so one bun release cannot stop every pull request at the same moment. The exposure grew when specialists#231 added a bun job that runs on every pull request; before that, a paths filter guarded the only bun job. Flagged and left alone on purpose, per the bead NON_GOALS: package-payload.yml and release-gate.yml also carry bun-version latest, but neither runs on every pull request.

title: specialists: tests/unit/cli/status.test.ts flakes on a 20s timeout under machine contention
description:
## PROBLEM

`tests/unit/cli/status.test.ts` fails intermittently on a 20 second timeout. It fails only when the machine is under load. It passes on an unloaded host and on CI.

## EVIDENCE

Found 2026-07-26 by the worker on bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.10, which verified rather than assumed: it stashed its own changes and ran the full suite on clean master under the same load. The result was identical — the same 3 failures including status.test.ts. So the flake is pre-existing and is not caused by the attach-test work.

At that time the host was running six concurrent agent worktrees, which is what produced the contention.

CI runs ubuntu-latest and is unloaded, so CI does not show this. That is why it stayed hidden.

## WHY P3

It does not block a release. CI is green. The cost is local: a developer or an agent running the suite on a loaded machine sees a red suite and must decide whether it is real. Today that cost was paid twice.

## SUCCESS

- The test passes under load, or its timeout is justified by measurement rather than by a round number.
- If the 20s bound is genuinely needed, the failure message says so, and says that contention is the likely cause.

## SCOPE

- specialists tests/unit/cli/status.test.ts
- the timeout helper it uses, if the bound is shared

## NON_GOALS

- Raising every timeout in the suite.
- Marking the test skipped.

## VALIDATION

[ ] Suite green while several agent worktrees run concurrently
[ ] The chosen bound has a stated reason
notes:
VERIFIED FIXED BY #226 (c3eca682) — no code change needed.

Worker claude-wiy5n-422b, branch xt/wiy5n-422b in sync with origin/master.
Host load average 15.08 on 12 cores during all runs (real contention).

status.test.ts isolated, 3 runs at load 15: 1 file / 11 tests PASS each time (49.5s, 52.0s, 49.6s wall).
Full suite at load 15: 3 files failed / 144 passed / 7 skipped. status.test.ts grep count in failure set: 0.

ROOT CAUSE (matches the lead in the original notes): the flake was never the 20s bound. It was
contention from orphan pty processes that survived attach.integration.test.ts. #226 bounded that pty
with GNU timeout and un-quarantined the test. With the orphans gone status.test.ts stays inside its
bound even on a genuinely loaded host.

Report: /tmp/w422-report.md

FOLLOW-UP (out of scope, filed separately): three other files still flake under load 15 —
tests/unit/cli/feed.test.ts, tests/unit/cli/integration.test.ts,
tests/unit/specialist/supervisor-parent-notification.test.ts (the last fails with
'[supervisor] SQLite upsertStatus failed: database client unavailable').
close_reason: Already fixed by #226. Verified live under real load 15.08/12 cores: status.test.ts passes 3/3 isolated and is absent from the full-suite failure set. No code change warranted.

title: xtmux monitor-list state column does not reflect terminalStatus, so terminal monitors render as running
description:
## CORRECTION — the original premise of this bead was wrong

Filed as "registry accumulates non-terminal entries (208 non-done, 199 dead requester)" and endorsed on that framing by an advisor (xtrm-vm7s0, D5) which recommended building requester-scoped orphan reconciliation. BOTH were wrong. Reconciliation already exists and already works.

Direct measurement:

  non-done by state:                    210
    of which terminalStatus IS set:     210
    genuinely non-terminal:               0

  terminalStatus breakdown of those 210 rows:
    process_gone: 192
    timeout:       12
    done:           5
    killed:         1

Every row reported as non-done is in fact terminal. The 192 `process_gone` rows ARE the requester-death reconciliation that was claimed to be missing — it ran correctly. Nothing is leaking and no GC subsystem is needed.

## PROBLEM (what is actually wrong)

`monitor-list` renders a `state` column that does not incorporate `terminalStatus`. A monitor whose `terminalStatus` is `timeout` / `process_gone` / `killed` still displays `state=running`. Every consumer that filters on `state` — humans, hygiene checks, and the orchestrator guidance in /multiplexing — draws a false conclusion about leaked waits.

Confirmed from the other side by `monitor-kill`, which refuses with the correct internal truth while the list shows the opposite:

  IllegalTransitionError: monitor monitor-1785073415058-135678:
    illegal transition timeout -> killed: monitor is already terminal; terminal status is absorbing
    at assertTransition (src/domains/monitors/terminal.ts:61)

So the store knows the monitor is terminal; only the list projection disagrees.

## SUCCESS

- `monitor-list` reports a state consistent with `terminalStatus`; a terminal monitor never renders as `running`.
- `--json` output makes the effective state unambiguous without the consumer having to join two fields.
- Hygiene guidance filters on the corrected field.

## SCOPE

- xtmux monitor-list projection / state derivation
- src/domains/monitors/store.ts, terminal.ts (read path only — the transition logic is correct)
- /multiplexing end-of-session hygiene wording

## NON_GOALS

- Requester-scoped orphan reconciliation. It exists and works; do not build it.
- Any bulk cleanup of the current rows. They are correctly terminal.

## HYGIENE WORDING (still valid, the only surviving part of the original recommendation)

"xtmux monitor-list empty" is unsatisfiable — the registry is host-global and retains terminal history. Replace with:

  No monitor rows lacking a terminalStatus remain whose requesterSessionId or requesterPaneId
  belongs to this session. Terminal rows and unrelated host-global rows are informational and do
  not fail session hygiene.

## VALIDATION

[ ] A timed-out monitor renders as terminal, not running, in both table and --json output
[ ] Hygiene check written against the corrected field passes on a clean session
notes:
MERGED as Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#85. Worker %7634. No GC subsystem was built, as instructed — the corrected premise held.

THE FIX IS A PROJECTION OVERLAY, NOTHING MORE
monitorProjection now sets the emitted 'state' from terminalStatus when the monitor is terminal,
and from the observed pane state otherwise. row.state is the TARGET PANE's agent state; it churns
every poll and still reads 'running' on a monitor that timed out, was killed, or lost its target.

BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY KEPT
A new 'paneState' field always carries the raw pre-overlay pane state, so a caller that needs the
split still has it. terminalStatus keeps its own field. Nothing was taken away.

Both the pretty view and --json carry the same truth, so hygiene checks and humans now agree.
The contract docs were updated for monitor-list and monitor-agent.
close_reason: Merged as xtmux#85. monitor-list's state now reflects terminalStatus when set, with the raw pane state preserved in a new paneState field. No reconciliation added — the bead's corrected premise was right that none is needed.

title: demo: sprint 2 MSG-05 end-to-end verify
description:
## PROBLEM

Ephemeral probe verifying the Sprint 2 MSG-05 wave end-to-end: Specialists emitParentNotification -> xtmux inbox -> message-get -> sp result --json.

## SUCCESS

Four payloads captured and reported to the parent orchestrator:
1. sp job.completed event rendered in the xtmux event stream.
2. Parent inbox receives the MSG-05 terminal notification (expects-reply=false).
3. xtmux message-get <messageKey> --json returns the terminal snapshot.
4. sp result <job-id> --json returns the specialists structured output.

## SCOPE

Run exactly this sequence, nothing else:

1. sp run explorer --bead xtrm-0l718 --prompt "one-line probe: list top-level dirs"
2. Note the returned job id. Poll sp ps until that job reaches a terminal state.
3. xtmux message-list --for $XTMUX_AGENT_PARENT_SESSION --since 30m --json  -- find the MSG-05 notification for the job. Extract its messageKey.
4. xtmux message-get <messageKey> --json
5. sp result <job-id> --json
6. Append all four raw payloads (trimmed to the essential fields) to this beads notes via bd update xtrm-0l718 --notes, then report the same summary as your final message.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not dispatch any specialist other than the single explorer probe above.
- Do not modify any repo file, open any PR, or touch any other bead.
- Do not run the xtrm-release workflow.

## CONSTRAINTS

- xtmux CLI calls need BOTH TMUX and TMUX_PANE set in the environment; if a subprocess loses them, re-export before retrying.
- If any of the four payloads cannot be produced, record the exact failure text in the notes and report it. A failure is a reportable finding, not something to work around.
- Hard stop after step 6. Do not continue into other work.

## VALIDATION

[ ] Four payloads present in xtrm-0l718 notes
[ ] Final report states PASS or the specific failing step

## OUTPUT

The four payloads plus a one-line PASS/FAIL verdict.
notes: MSG-05 retry step 6 — job b3402f. A (sp job.completed event): NOT PRODUCED. Exact sp ps --json evidence: {"id":"b3402f","specialist":"explorer","status":"running","is_dead":true,"pid":3710836,"bead_id":null}; repeated polls never reached terminal. B (parent inbox MSG-05 row): NOT PRODUCED. Exact filter result: no message-list row matched job b3402f, so no messageKey. C (message-get terminal snapshot): NOT PRODUCED — no messageKey from step 3. D (sp result --json): NOT PRODUCED — retry stopped per constraint after missing terminal notification/messageKey; no workaround. Step 1 raw result included job id b3402f, then command timed out after 30 seconds.
close_reason: Probe complete — verdict FAIL, recorded as evidence not as a pass. All four MSG-05 payloads unproduced because every specialist job dies ~1s after spawn (SessionKilledError, status=running/is_dead=true), so emitParentNotification never fires. Root cause is upstream of the MSG wave and owned by xtrm-wiy5n.4.13. Transcript in xtrm-wiy5n.3 notes.

title: Sprint 3: reinforce no-force / no-history-rewrite in worker briefs
description:

Escalation matrix names the specific reply-required message shape for asking permission.

- Coordinator prompt template (or specialists chain-coordinator prompt at Sprint 2 bead 3.8 — already merged, follow-up PR needed) — enumerate the escalation shape.

- Blocking force-with-lease entirely (it's the safer form; when authorized, still preferred over --force).
- Rewriting the specialists escalation matrix.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Formalize the threshold class (force / force-with-lease / no-force) so workers cite the case number when escalating.

notes:
MERGED as core#521 with xtrm-wiy5n.4.8.

REBASE-PUSH is now a sequence, not a prohibition:
  rebase onto latest origin/main -> run the agreed suite locally -> NORMAL fast-forward git push

If the push is rejected as non-fast-forward, request operator authorization BEFORE any
--force-with-lease or --force, using this exact reply-required shape:

  decision needed: rebase-push needs --force-with-lease on <branch>; reason <one-line>; proceed?

The line states plainly that the ban is on using either flag WITHOUT authorization, not on the

title: core: Stop hook xtmux/auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs needs TMUX env propagation
description:
## PROBLEM
~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs (a Stop hook) shells out to `xtmux obligations list` to gate the Stop cycle, but the Claude Code Stop hook subprocess does NOT inherit $TMUX / $TMUX_PANE from the parent Claude session. Result: every Stop fires the error XTMUX_NOT_IN_TMUX and the guard falls back to allowing the next Stop through. Benign, but noisy and defeats the drain-check intent.

## SUCCESS
Hook either:
(a) wraps the xtmux call to auto-discover the parent tmux socket + session/pane and export TMUX/TMUX_PANE, or
(b) checks env presence first and skips silently (no error output) when not in tmux, or
(c) uses a socket-based fallback that doesn't require TMUX env at all.

Preferable: (a), because auto-discovery preserves the drain-gate semantic.

## SCOPE
- ~/.claude/hooks/xtmux/auto-monitor-drain-stop.mjs (add env discovery / graceful skip)

## NON_GOALS
- Redesigning the auto-monitor state model.

## CONSTRAINTS
- Must remain a Stop hook (no interactive prompts, no long blocking calls).

## VALIDATION
- Fresh Claude Code session (spawned outside tmux) does not see the XTMUX_NOT_IN_TMUX error on Stop.
- Existing tmux-in-tmux sessions still get the drain-gate to run correctly.

## OUTPUT
PR link + one-line diff on the hook script.

title: Core P3: define prolonged-QUEUED scanner admin-merge threshold
description:
## PROBLEM
Sprint 2 Core PR #507 exposed an ambiguity: the documented admin-merge exception covered terminal zero-step OSV/Semgrep/Gitleaks failures, but not checks that remain QUEUED without progressing. The lane merged while checks were still QUEUED, forcing a post-merge risk decision.

## SUCCESS
The merge policy defines an evidence-backed, explicit minimum duration and no-progression test for prolonged QUEUED scanners, keeps terminal zero-step failure handling distinct, and makes premature admin-merge mechanically harder.

## SCOPE
- Coordinator/lane guidance that documents CI infra-flake tolerance
- Relevant merge policy tests or helper logic, if an executable gate exists

## NON_GOALS

- Weakening test, smoke, pr-review-gate, Codex, or real scanner findings
- Defining release publication policy outside PR merge gating

## CONSTRAINTS

- Require exact check timestamps/status evidence and document the exception in bead/PR notes
- No immediate exception for merely QUEUED checks

## VALIDATION

title: Sprint 3: amend admin-merge policy — distinguish zero-step failures from prolonged QUEUED
description:
## PROBLEM
Sprint 2 (bead xtrm-wiy5n.3.9/.3.10, PR xtrm-dev/core#507) surfaced a policy gap: the current admin-merge exception was stated as 'authorized when scanners fail zero-step (started_at == completed_at, 0 steps) as GitHub Actions infra flake'. A worker admin-merged while scanners were still QUEUED (never started) — same operational reason (no signal) but not the same terminal state, so it exceeded the stated exception. Test/smoke/pr-review-gate/Codex all green, no user harm, but policy ambiguity produced coordinator escalation.

## SUCCESS
Admin-merge policy explicitly covers three scanner states that all authorize bypass when other required checks are green:
1. Terminal zero-step failure (started_at == completed_at, 0 steps) — pre-existing.
2. Prolonged QUEUED with no state progression for > N minutes (define N, likely 10-15min).
3. Terminal FAILURE with 'GitHub Actions has encountered an internal error' annotation.

Policy documented in /multiplexing-team or a dedicated Sprint-orchestration reference; workers know the criteria without escalating each case.

## SCOPE
- Update relevant skill root (candidate: /multiplexing-team failure section) with the 3-case matrix.
- Update Sprint 2 coordinator memory / bd remember if this recurs across sprints.

## NON_GOALS
- Rewriting the whole admin-merge doctrine.
- Fixing GitHub Actions infra flakes (upstream, out of scope).

## CONSTRAINTS
- Policy stays LEAN — 3 lines in a routing table + escalation-still-encouraged clause for edge cases.

## VALIDATION
- Worker following updated skill can distinguish the 3 cases without escalating.
- Coordinator quotes the specific case number when authorizing admin-merge.

## OUTPUT
PR link + one-line skill-root diff.
notes:
MERGED as core#521 with xtrm-wiy5n.4.12. Worker %7659. Two lines added to .xtrm/skills/default/multiplexing-team/SKILL.md, plus the regenerated registry hash.

ADMIN-MERGE BYPASS — now three authorized scanner states, all conditional on every OTHER required check being green (test, smoke, pr-review-gate, Codex, threads, no conflict):
  1. terminal zero-step — started_at == completed_at, 0 steps
  2. QUEUED > 15 min with no state progression
  3. terminal FAILURE annotated 'GitHub Actions has encountered an internal error'

N = 15 min, justified in line: 15 minutes covers typical Actions runner-backpressure drain; longer means no signal rather than backlog.

NEVER bypassed, stated explicitly so the rule cannot be stretched: a real test failure, a real scanner finding, an unresolved bot review thread, a merge conflict.

The worker is told to cite the case number when escalating.
close_reason: Merged as core#521. Three authorized scanner states, N=15 min justified in line, and an explicit list of what is never bypassed.

title: release-train: retire .xtrm/ext-src/ + decide pi-extension @xtrm/pi-service-skills future
description:
Followup from ext-src investigation (2026-07-25, ~/dev/xtrm branch xt/ext-src-invx read-only helper, report at /tmp/ext-src-report.md, also captured in ~/dev/xtrm bd memory 'ext-src-investigation-findings-report-at-tmp-ext').

## Findings summary

.xtrm/ext-src/ is vestigial pre-v0.7.8 dead code — DEPRECATED marker in docs/xtrm-directory.md:74,116,161, no writers in cli/src/, no readers at runtime. Consumer pi loads extensions via 'npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions' materialized into ~/.pi/agent/extensions/, not from .xtrm/ext-src/.

The pi-extension @xtrm/pi-service-skills is silently DORMANT on every consumer:
- Canonical (post-v0.7.8) resolveSkillScript targets .claude/skills/service-skills/scripts/ + .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/ — neither exists on any consumer (~/.xtrm/skills/default/ has no service-skills nor service-knowledge dir)
- Both hook handlers return undefined when scripts not found → silent no-op
- Actual scripts live in the pipx service_knowledge python package; extension has zero code path to reach them

Rename impact = zero runtime effect (extension is no-op before AND after).

## Work items (release-train scope)

### 1. Prune .xtrm/ext-src/ on 9 consumer repos

Consumer copies enumerated at investigation time (2026-07-25):
- ~/projects/mercury/{barchart-scraper,darth-feedor,economic-data,infra,platform,quant,treasury-cb,website}
- ~/dev/transcriptoz

Approach options:
- Ship 'xt migrate ext-src' — proper migrator, idempotent rm-rf across .xtrm/ext-src/, one command per repo, could tail into 'xt update --apply'
- One-shot script (bash loop over the list above)
- Defer until each consumer naturally does xt update --apply which could also clean

NOT to include: ~/dev/core/.xtrm/ext-src/ (this repo's own ext-src) — core is authoritative, prune here decoupled from the migrator ship

### 2. Decide pi-extension @xtrm/pi-service-skills future

Two shapes (pick one):

**Retire** (zero consumer impact)
- Remove packages/pi-extensions/extensions/service-skills/
- Drop from packages/pi-extensions/src/manifest.json 'active' list
- Add to 'disabled' block with note (pattern: quality-gates, pi-serena-compact, gitnexus, serena)
- No follow-up migrator needed (consumers pick it up on xt pi setup)

**Rebuild** (revives the drift-injection + cataloger-injection UX on Pi sessions)
- Rename extensions/service-skills → extensions/service-knowledge
- Rename manifest.json id 'service-skills' → 'service-knowledge'
- Update MACHINERY_SKILL constant to 'service-knowledge' (dual-name array optional for one-release backward-compat)
- Add fallback in resolveSkillScript: when no on-disk script found, invoke 'python3 -m service_knowledge.scripts.<name>' (adjust the two SubprocessRunner.run() call sites to accept argv-array or resolve to that Python invocation)
- Ship in next @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions release

## Coordinate with

- Jira epic ISSUE-51 (mercuryintel.atlassian.net/browse/ISSUE-51) — bootstrap-remaining-mercury-repos (8 P0 bd issues open, one per repo)
- xtrm-dev/infra bead infra-cwfj — duplicate/mirror of this bead scoped to infra's board
- Package: ~/dev/xtrm/packages/service-knowledge/ v0.7.0
- Recent shipped substrate: xtrm-dev/xtrm#21-#27, xtrm-dev/specialists#217, xtrm-dev/core#503

## Timing

Deferred until the current core sprint closes. No urgency: extension is dormant, ext-src is dead code, no user-facing pain today.

title: board-audit: --epic <id> flag for scoped export (epic + descendants with notes)
description:
## PROBLEM
`board-audit` exports the entire bd corpus. For focused audits on a single epic (like `xtrm-wiy5n` audit-reconcile program, 31 beads), operators want a scoped export: epic + all descendants recursively, with full description AND notes. Today: `bd list --parent` = direct children only + omits notes; `bd export` = whole board no filter; `bd show --json` = per-bead only. Must be wrapper-composed.

## SUCCESS
`board-audit --epic <id>` walks the tree rooted at `<id>` (BFS via `bd list --parent` recursion) and hydrates each with `bd show --json` (has notes). Bundle prompt notes the scope — bucket-C/D/silent-supersede analysis stays within the epic subtree; sister-repo relocations still allowed since they cross-repo.

Combines with `--no-pr` — an operator may want epic scope + no PR corpus.

## SCOPE
- `.xtrm/skills/default/issue-triage/resources/board-audit` — arg parse + BFS walk + prompt scope note
- `.xtrm/skills/default/issue-triage/resources/README.md` — document the flag

## NON_GOALS
- Multi-epic union export
- Cross-repo epic walking (bd is per-repo)
- Adding a `bd list --parent-tree` upstream feature (that's a separate follow-up)

## CONSTRAINTS
- BFS walk uses `bd list --parent <id> --json --all` recursively; dedupe by id
- Hydration via `bd show --json` (preserves notes)
- Auto-window PR pull still anchored to oldest bead IN THE SUBSET (not the whole board) when --epic + PRs both active
- Ponytail: one shell function + one branch on existing bd-corpus block
- Compatible with existing `--no-pr` flag

## VALIDATION
- [ ] `board-audit --epic xtrm-wiy5n --no-pr` exports 31 beads with description + notes
- [ ] `board-audit --epic <nonexistent>` fails cleanly
- [ ] `board-audit --epic <id>` (with PRs) computes PR window from subset, not whole board
- [ ] `board-audit` (no flag) unchanged behavior
- [ ] README documents `--epic` alongside `--no-pr`

## OUTPUT
PR link + demo run on xtrm-wiy5n confirming 31-bead export with notes.
close_reason: shipped via PR #498 (a20d52e5, admin-merged around persistent GH Actions trigger flake): --epic <id> BFS walk + bd show hydration preserves notes; verified 31-bead export of xtrm-wiy5n with 7 notes intact

title: changelog:check produces different output on GH Actions runners than local — investigate
description:
## PROBLEM
`npm run changelog:check` passes on local (ubuntu, node 24, git-cliff 2.13.1) but fails on GH Actions runners (same OS, same node version, git-cliff installed via same devDep + package-lock). After ruling out fetch-depth, PATH, git-cliff version, and timezone (UTC-normalized), the actual regen output differs but source of difference is unknown.

## SUCCESS
CI can run `changelog:check` and it matches local's output on the same commit. Then re-add as CI backstop step.

## SCOPE
Debug divergence — likely candidates: git-cliff config resolution, workspace subrepo history visibility, or cliff.toml parser cache.

## NON_GOALS
Blocking on this — the pre-push hook + release-time regen (reyem.10) cover the primary risk.
close_reason: ^Merge skip parser fix landed core #489 + xtmux #71; specialists already had it. CI check re-enabled on core (merged in #489). Doctrine captured in /setup-git-cliff.

title: auto-refresh CHANGELOG [Unreleased] across core/specialists/xtmux: pre-push hook + CI check
description:
## PROBLEM
scripts/changelog-update.mjs is installed on all 3 repos but nothing calls it automatically. [Unreleased] rots between releases (specialists: 2 commits since v3.21.1 not in Unreleased). release_execute.py fixes this at release time (reyem.10), but between-release staleness confuses everyone.

## SUCCESS
All 3 repos have:
1. .githooks/pre-push that runs `npm run changelog:check` — abort push if [Unreleased] out of date, message prompts `npm run changelog` + re-push. Wired via `prepare` npm script setting core.hooksPath.
2. CI check job on PRs: runs `npm run changelog:check` — fail PR if stale. Backstop for direct-push-from-another-machine cases.

## SCOPE
- 3 x .githooks/pre-push (new file)
- 3 x package.json `prepare` script edit
- 3 x .github/workflows/ci.yml (or equivalent) add changelog-check step

## NON_GOALS
Auto-committing the updater output — that hides intent from the author.

## VALIDATION
- Commit a code change without running `npm run changelog` → push blocked by local hook
- Bypass hook + push → PR CI check fails
- Run `npm run changelog` + push → both pass
close_reason: Cross-repo wiring landed: core #488 (6e7040df7) + spec #208 (05c57e568) + xtmux #70 (44ffb266e). Doctrine captured in /setup-git-cliff. Pre-push hook wired on core+spec; xtmux skipped (beads-managed hooksPath). CI backstop deferred as reyem.13.

title: xtmux needs an idempotent scripts/changelog-update.mjs (mirror core/specialists pattern)
description:
## PROBLEM
xtmux scripts/changelog.mjs is a bare git-cliff wrapper that prints to stdout. Core + Specialists ship scripts/changelog-update.mjs — smart idempotent in-place rewriter that preserves title, preamble, and released sections. Without it, xtmux's release_execute.py cliff regen path can't refresh a stale [Unreleased] body.

## SUCCESS
xtmux has scripts/changelog-update.mjs matching the core/specialists pattern. release_execute.py detects and uses it. Stale [Unreleased] body is refreshed live at release time.

## SCOPE
Copy + adapt ~/dev/core/scripts/changelog-update.mjs into ~/dev/xtmux/scripts/. PR against xtmux main.

## VALIDATION
node scripts/changelog-update.mjs on xtmux with a stale [Unreleased] rewrites it in place; running it again is a no-op.
close_reason: Merged as PR #69 (sha 02cb45509).

title: release_execute: regen [Unreleased] via cliff even when header present but body stale
description:
## PROBLEM
promote_changelog only runs scripts/changelog{-update,}.mjs when [Unreleased] header is MISSING. If header is present with stale body (e.g. bullets from 3 months ago while git log has 20 new commits), promotion moves stale content forward as if it were the release notes.

## SUCCESS
For repos with has_cliff_updater=true, promote_changelog ALWAYS regens [Unreleased] from the current git log before promotion. Body reflects actual commits since last tag.

## SCOPE
~/.archon/scripts/xtrm/release_execute.py promote_changelog + _regen_unreleased helpers.

## NON_GOALS
Repos without cliff (session-close-report writes manually curated bullets — do NOT auto-overwrite those).

## VALIDATION
Manual: on a repo with existing but stale [Unreleased], run release_execute --dry-run and confirm the diff shows freshly-generated bullets.
notes: Fix landed: promote_changelog now ALWAYS runs cliff regen when has_cliff_updater=true (was: only when [Unreleased] header missing). Verified on core (dry-run shows changelog-update.mjs invoked; changed:true). LIMITATION: xtmux ships only a bare git-cliff wrapper (scripts/changelog.mjs prints stdout, doesn't write in place). For xtmux the regen call happens but produces no file write. Xtmux needs its own idempotent scripts/changelog-update.mjs mirroring core/specialists's pattern — filed as sibling bead.
close_reason: promote_changelog always regens via cliff for repos with cliff updater. Verified live on core. Xtmux gap tracked as reyem.11 (needs its own smart updater).

title: xtmux release.yml NPM_TOKEN produces ENEEDAUTH in CI despite proper NODE_AUTH_TOKEN wiring
description:
## PROBLEM
xtmux release.yml (with PR #64 env wiring merged) still gets ENEEDAUTH on npm publish. NPM_TOKEN secret exists on Jaggerxtrm/xtmux. Local publish with ~/.npmrc token works (v0.2.1 shipped). Difference: either the CI token is a different value, or npm's new 2FA-bypass restriction blocks classic automation tokens for direct publishing.

## SUCCESS
release.yml on next v* tag push completes npm publish successfully, gets provenance attestation, creates GH release.

## SCOPE
Jaggerxtrm/xtmux repo secrets + optionally package.json publishConfig.

## HYPOTHESES
1. Secret is a classic automation token (bypass 2FA) which npm now restricts. Fix: create a granular access token with @jaggerxtrm scope + read+write + no 2FA bypass, then gh secret set NPM_TOKEN with the new value.
2. Secret value has whitespace or trailing newline from `gh secret set` piping.
3. registry-url in setup-node doesn't inject NODE_AUTH_TOKEN because the .npmrc format differs.

## VALIDATION
Cut a v0.2.2 patch bump via the workflow — should ship end-to-end via CI + provenance.
close_reason: Superseded by xtrm-reyem.9: trusted publishing removes the NPM_TOKEN dependency entirely. No need to debug the 2FA-bypass token restriction — that whole path is retired for xtmux.

title: release: filter GitNexus-regenerated AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md + auto-populate CHANGELOG when [Unreleased] missing
description:
## PROBLEM
Two friction points blocking xtmux (and any other repo with GitNexus + no [Unreleased]) from the workflow:
1. AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md accumulate GitNexus symbol-count updates every session — dirty but not WIP.
2. release_execute.promote_changelog returns changed:false when [Unreleased] missing. Should regen via changelog.mjs (xtmux) or changelog-update.mjs (core/specialists) FIRST.

## SUCCESS
_release_common.py EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS includes AGENTS.md + CLAUDE.md. release_execute.py auto-runs the repo's changelog regenerator BEFORE promote_changelog when [Unreleased] absent. xtmux classifier goes READY (assuming 1+ commit since v0.2.0).
notes: Fixed: (a) EPHEMERAL_DIRTY_PATHS adds AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, .wolf/. (b) strip_ephemeral() robust to sh() output-strip whitespace edge case (first porcelain line lost leading space when status starts with space). (c) release_execute.py.promote_changelog now runs scripts/changelog{-update,}.mjs when [Unreleased] missing. (d) release_classify downgrades no-[Unreleased] from BLOCKED to WARN when has_cliff_updater=true. Live post-fix: specialists=SKIP, core=READY (28 commits), xtmux=READY (1 commit) with 2 advisory warnings.
close_reason: Ephemeral filter fixed + AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/.wolf added + CHANGELOG auto-regen when [Unreleased] missing + classify downgrade to WARN. Live retest: xtmux READY.

title: give listBranchIntegrations a read surface — branch_integration_events is write-only
description:
## PROBLEM

Decided in xtrm-vtqlg.1: xtrm.branch.integration.v1 keeps its single producer
(sp merge) because the job_id -> commit_sha linkage it records is the one thing
git cannot answer. But the store has ZERO production readers —
listBranchIntegrations() (specialists observability-sqlite.ts:1213/:1839) is
called only from tests/unit/specialist/observability-sqlite.test.ts.

A write-only store is a liability regardless of how cheap the write is: nobody
can tell whether the data is correct, because nobody looks at it.

## SCOPE

Specialists repo. Core is NOT a participant — per xtrm-vtqlg.3, Core has
nothing honest to emit and nothing to read here.

## WHY THIS IS SMALL

The query layer already exists. listBranchIntegrations() accepts
ListBranchIntegrationFilters { targetBranch, sourceJobId, limit } and the table
carries idx_branch_integration_target / _source_job. What is missing is a verb,
not a query.

Likely shape: `sp forensic branch-integrations [--job <id>] [--target <branch>]
[--limit N] [--json]`, or fold it into the existing KPI/observability surface.

## VALIDATION

[ ] A merge performed via sp merge is visible through the new surface.
[ ] --json output validates against xtrm.branch.integration.v1.
[ ] Filters (job, target branch, limit) exercised.

## REFERENCES

- Decision: xtrm-vtqlg.1 notes.
- Producer: specialists src/cli/merge.ts:958 recordBranchIntegrationAfterMerge.
close_reason: Added 'sp integration list' in Specialists (src/cli/integration.ts + index.ts dispatch + help). --json emits the stored xtrm.branch.integration.v1 payload verbatim. Verified end-to-end against a seeded observability.db: human + json output, target-branch/job/limit filters all exercised. Cross-repo PR in specialists.

title: READ-ONLY CONTRACT:
READ-ONLY CONTRACT:

description: cli/src/tests/install-integration.test.ts intermittently times out at the 30s vitest default when the machine is loaded; the same file passes 8/8 in ~17s with --testTimeout=120000. The tests run the real installer against /tmp, so their wall-clock is load-dependent. Fix: give the file an explicit per-suite timeout rather than leaving it on the global default. Observed during Wave 6 (xtrm-kdwvu).
