title: osv-diff.sh runs osv-scanner in an extracted base tree with GIT_DIR still inherited
description:
Same hazard class as xtrm-bjbdf, but NOT currently damaging — filing so it isn't rediscovered.

scripts/osv-diff.sh extracts the baseline via 'git archive' into a scratch dir, then 'cd "$base_tree"' and runs osv-scanner there. When invoked from the pre-push hook, GIT_DIR is still set and still points at the INVOKING worktree's gitdir, so any git lookup osv-scanner performs inside base_tree resolves against the wrong repo.

Today this is benign: osv-scanner does not check out or mutate git state, which is why only semgrep produced the detach. It is latent, not active.

Fix is the same three lines already added to scripts/semgrep-diff.sh (strip GIT_DIR and friends when the repo is still discoverable from cwd). If a third consumer appears, extract those lines into a shared scripts/lib helper rather than copying them a third time.

Not folded into the xtrm-bjbdf PR to keep that fix minimal and to avoid claiming a behavioural fix that has no reproduction behind it.
close_reason: strip inherited GIT_DIR and friends in osv-diff.sh before the extracted base-tree scan; same pattern as semgrep-diff.sh (PR #471)

title: Suite C steps 7-10 remain SKIP: document the live-agent gate and file the specialists-side lane
description:
## PROBLEM

The wave-5 brief requires Suite C to go from 5 PASS / 4 SKIP to 9 PASS, or an explicit
explanation for any remaining SKIP. Investigation says the four SKIPs cannot be closed by
this cluster, and the brief's premise is mistaken about why they skip.

The four deferred steps are, per suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs:43-48:
- step 7: dispatch a specialist child from the coordinator — needs a live specialist chain
  (real agent + API credentials)
- step 8: verify specialist branch derives from coordinator branch — sp creates specialist
  branches; Core only publishes the base via @agent_branch (audit P1-03)
- step 9: verify descendant runtime-origin lineage — runtime-origin propagation is
  Specialists-side (SupervisorStatus), needs a dispatched job
- step 10: merge accepted specialist branch into coordinator branch — needs 7-8's branches

None of these is blocked on the absence of an aggregation projection. They are blocked on
the absence of a live-agent lane: a real `sp run` with API credentials that actually
creates specialist branches. A read-only projection in Core cannot dispatch a specialist,
and shimming `sp run` to fabricate branches is exactly what the suite's own header
declares out of bounds ("they stay SKIP with a stated reason rather than being faked into
a pass", :24-26). Faking them would convert an honest SKIP into a dishonest PASS.

## SUCCESS

The reason steps 7-10 remain SKIP is recorded where a future reader will find it, the
Cluster D report states it plainly instead of claiming 9/9, and a specialists-repo bead
exists for the live-agent lane that would actually close them.

## SCOPE

- A follow-up bead filed in the specialists repo for the credentialed live-agent lane.
- The wave-5 Cluster D report's SUITE C STATE section.
- Optionally a clarifying comment in suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs LIVE_ONLY if the
  existing reasons need sharpening.

## NON_GOALS

- Shimming `sp run` to fabricate specialist branches so steps 7-10 report PASS. This is
  the whole point: a faked pass is worse than an honest skip because it retires the
  ledger entry that would otherwise keep the gap visible.
- Changing the capability gate so the suite reports BLOCKED again. PASS/SKIP with stated
  reasons is the shape xtrm-6hey0 deliberately graduated to.
- Building the live-agent lane in this cluster. It needs credentials in CI and belongs to
  the repo that owns specialist dispatch.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Steps 2-5 and 11 must stay PASS; nothing here may perturb them.
- The recorded reason must name the actual blocker (live-agent dispatch + credentials),
  not a vague "not implemented".

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Suite C still reports 5 PASS / 4 SKIP with reasons and exit 0 on a capable host.
- [ ] A specialists-repo bead id exists and is cited in the report.
- [ ] The Cluster D report's SUITE C STATE section states before -> after and the reason,
      rather than claiming 9/9.

## LIBRARIES

N/A — documentation and bead filing, no new code.

## OUTPUT

The Suite C step ledger, the specialists-repo bead id, and the report paragraph.
notes:
VERDICT: Suite C stays 5 PASS / 4 SKIP / 0 BLOCKED. 9/9 is NOT achievable from Cluster D,
and the wave-5 brief's premise about why steps 7-10 skip is mistaken.

LIVE LEDGER (run against the packed Core artifact, node test/integration-suite/suite-c-coordinator-lineage.mjs):
  [PASS] step 2  launch main orchestrator from main worktree
  [PASS] step 3  launch subordinate chain coordinator through Core
  [PASS] step 4  verify distinct coordinator worktree and branch
  [PASS] step 5  verify parent session, role and bead pane metadata  (role=chain-coordinator)
  [SKIP] step 7  dispatch a specialist child — needs a live specialist chain (agent + API credentials)
  [SKIP] step 8  specialist branch derives from coordinator branch — sp creates those branches
  [SKIP] step 9  descendant runtime-origin lineage — Specialists-side (SupervisorStatus)
  [SKIP] step 10 merge accepted specialist branch — needs 7-8's branches to exist
  [PASS] step 11 confirm main remains unchanged
  suite-c: PASS (5 live, 4 deferred to a live-agent lane)

WHY THE PROJECTION CANNOT CLOSE THEM: steps 7-10 are not blocked on the absence of an
aggregation projection. They are blocked on the absence of a lane that can really DISPATCH
a specialist — an sp run with credentials that actually creates specialist branches and
worktrees. A read-only projection in Core cannot dispatch anything; that is its defining
constraint (P2-05's 'READ-ONLY, no write-back').

WHY NOT SHIM IT: Suite C's own header (:24-26) declares the boundary — steps 7-10 'stay
SKIP with a stated reason rather than being faked into a pass'. Extending the existing sp
shim to fabricate branches would turn an honest SKIP into a dishonest PASS and retire the
ledger entry that keeps the gap visible. Declined deliberately.

SIDE BENEFIT: step 5 passing is independent live proof that P2-03 (@agent_role) is
satisfied — see xtrm-d1fod.1.

CROSS-REPO FOLLOW-UP FILED: specialists unitAI-kiequ — 'Credentialed live-agent lane so
Suite C steps 7-10 can run instead of SKIP'. That is the work that would actually close them.
close_reason: Suite C verified 5 PASS/4 SKIP; steps 7-10 gated on live-agent dispatch not on the projection; specialists unitAI-kiequ filed

title: cli prebuild worktree guard is over-broad — blocks build even when the worktree has its own node_modules
description:
## PROBLEM

`cli/package.json`'s `prebuild` refuses any `npm run build` whose cwd contains
`/.xtrm/worktrees/` (commit b86d9d68). The stated reason is that tsup/esbuild
embeds deep relative paths to node_modules when building from a worktree, breaking
CI's `git diff --exit-code cli/dist/` check.

That premise only holds when the worktree LACKS its own dependencies. Verified
during xtrm-6hey0: after `npm ci` at the worktree root and in `cli/`, the
node_modules layout is identical to the main repo, and `npx tsup` produces a
bundle whose sourcemap sources still start `../../node_modules/...` with zero
absolute paths and zero worktree paths.

Net effect today: every worktree agent that changes CLI source hits a hard stop on
a check that does not apply to them, and either bypasses it blindly (learning
nothing about when it does apply) or cannot produce the tracked dist their PR
needs.

## SUCCESS

`npm run build` succeeds in a worktree that has its own node_modules, and still
refuses — with the current message — in one that does not.

## SCOPE

- `cli/package.json` `prebuild` script.

## NON_GOALS

- Removing the guard. Its failure mode is real; CI's dist check does break.
- Changing the tsup config or what `cli/dist` contains.
- Making CI build from a worktree.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Keep it a one-liner in `prebuild`; this does not deserve a script file.
- The check to add is presence of `cli/node_modules` (and the repo root's), not a
  path-shape heuristic.
- Error message must keep explaining WHY, and should now name the remedy
  (`npm ci` in the worktree) rather than only "build from the main repo".

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Worktree with node_modules: build succeeds; `grep -c '/home/' cli/dist/index.cjs cli/dist/index.cjs.map` is 0.
- [ ] Worktree without node_modules: build refuses with the improved message.
- [ ] Main repo: unchanged.

## LIBRARIES

- **Reuse in repo:** the existing inline `node -e` guard — extend it, do not replace it.
- **Installed deps / Stdlib:** `node:fs.existsSync`.
- **New dep candidate:** none.
- **Roll it:** no.

## OUTPUT

The one-line diff plus the three validation transcripts.

## REFERENCES

- Guard origin: b86d9d68 "fix(build): prevent worktree-path contamination in dist".
- Evidence it is over-broad: bd memory `dist-rebuild-from-worktree-safe-after-npm-ci`.
notes: EVIDENCE (wave-8a, 2026-07-22): hit this while building for xtrm-7h5xh. Bypassing the guard with 'npx tsup' in a worktree WITHOUT node_modules silently bundles the ROOT conf@15 instead of cli/node_modules conf@12 — dist diverges from CI's build and 'Verify dist is up to date' fails (CI run 29880314814). After 'npm ci' at the worktree root + cli/, tsup reproduced main's committed dist BYTE-IDENTICALLY. So the guard's premise is real; the fix is to make it conditional on cli/node_modules existing (and matching the lockfile), NOT to delete it.
close_reason: prebuild guard now fires only when the worktree lacks real node_modules at cli/ and its root; verified dist rebuilt from a provisioned worktree is byte-identical to main

title: Strip mcp__serena__* dead-references from policies/*.json hook matchers
description:
## PROBLEM

Every consumer project's .claude/settings.json still lists mcp__serena__* tool names inside hook matcher regex alternations (Edit|Write|MultiEdit|NotebookEdit|mcp__serena__rename_symbol|...). These are dead references — serena was disabled globally 2026-07-21 (enabledPlugins['serena@claude-plugins-official']=false in ~/.claude/settings.json) and the MCP server no longer runs. The regexes never match, so they are inert but visually cluttered.

Source of truth: policies/*.json in xtrm-tools. Consumer settings.json files get regenerated from these on every xt update --apply — direct edits don't stick.

## SUCCESS

- No policies/*.json hook matcher references mcp__serena__* tool names.
- npm run compile-policies regenerates .xtrm/config/hooks.json cleanly with the alternations removed.
- xt update --apply on a consumer project drops the dead references from its .claude/settings.json.
- No serena removal outside hook matchers — this bead is cleanup only, not a policy change on tool coverage.

## SCOPE

- policies/*.json in xtrm-tools (grep-then-sed the mcp__serena__* alternations out).
- Regenerate .xtrm/config/hooks.json via npm run compile-policies.
- Regenerate registry.json hashes for anything that shifts.
- Update ~/dev/core/.claude/settings.json via xt update --apply as post-merge smoke.

## NON_GOALS

- Do not remove or add support for other MCP servers.
- Do not change matcher shape (still xxxxx|Read|Write|...) — only drop serena alternatives.
- Do not add a serena-install opt-in flow to xt; Claude Code owns plugin lifecycle.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Preserve every non-serena tool in each matcher.
- If a matcher becomes single-tool after strip (e.g. was just Write|mcp__serena__replace_symbol_body → Write), keep it — a redundant alternation is not equivalent to the underlying tool alone in Claude Code's matcher semantics.
- Change is idempotent under npm run compile-policies + git diff --exit-code.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] grep -R 'mcp__serena__' policies/ returns nothing.
- [ ] npm run compile-policies clean; git diff on .xtrm/config/hooks.json is only the matcher strips.
- [ ] npm run check:package + check:registry-pack-parity green.
- [ ] Smoke: cd ~/dev/xtmux && xt update --apply → .claude/settings.json diff is only the matcher strips.

## OUTPUT

One small PR to xtrm-tools. Bundle into Wave 6 hygiene batch (xtrm-29b67, xtrm-xus17, xtrm-kdwvu).

## LIBRARIES

N/A — regex/text edit in JSON policies.

## REFERENCES

Serena kill 2026-07-21: ~/.claude/settings.json.pre-serena-disable-20260721-172131 backup.
close_reason: stripped mcp__serena__* from 3 policy matchers; compile-policies + gen-registry clean, parity/hygiene green

title: xt migrate skills leaves empty default/optional dirs and local-legacy residue in consumer projects
description:
Found during xtrm-1ehjo sweep. The skills half of the global migration landed correctly — 7 of 8 consumer projects have zero files under .xtrm/skills/default and .xtrm/skills/optional (~/dev/core is the source repo and legitimately keeps 338 files). But the migration leaves behind:
  - empty .xtrm/skills/default/ and .xtrm/skills/optional/ directories in 7 projects
  - .xtrm/skills/local-legacy/ with real content in 5: console (240 files), vaultctl (46), transcriptoz (23), specialists (1), xtrm (1)

local-legacy is by design a holding pen for skills that could not be attributed to the global SSOT, so it is NOT automatically safe to delete — console's 240 files in particular include project-authored content (analyzer.md, xiaohongshu_api.py, orchestrator.py, gitleaks.yml). Needs a per-entry triage pass, not a blanket rm.

The empty default/optional dirs are cosmetic but make it harder to tell at a glance whether a project has migrated. 'xt migrate skills --apply' could prune them once it confirms local-legacy has been triaged.

Also noted: ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/state.json is still schemaVersion 1 with enabledPacks {claude:[mypack], pi:[mypack]} while all 7 other projects are on schemaVersion 2 with managedLinks. Probably test residue in the source repo; worth confirming it is not a migration miss.
notes:
RESOLVED (wave-9): empty-tier prune added to xt migrate skills.

Scope delivered:
- `pruneRetiredManagedTiers()` in cli/src/commands/migrate.ts, called from the
  `alreadyMigrated` branch of migrateSkills — the only path the 7 already-migrated
  consumer repos take. The normal migration path already fs.remove's both tiers
  wholesale, so no second call site is needed.
- Removes .xtrm/skills/default and .xtrm/skills/optional only when recursively
  empty of files (no exclusions — a tier holding only .venv/__pycache__ is NOT
  treated as empty, unlike walkDir). Protects ~/dev/core (511 default files).
- local-legacy deliberately NOT pruned, per the bead: console alone holds 240
  project-authored files. Reported instead with a yellow "needs per-entry triage
  (left in place)" line so the operator sees cleanup is pending.
- Honors --dry-run: prints "would remove empty <path>" and touches nothing.

3 new tests in cli/src/tests/migrate.test.ts (prune / keep-non-empty+local-legacy
/ dry-run). Suite 31/31 green; cli typecheck clean.

NOT FIXED HERE — filed as xtrm-vtqlg.5 (P2): skills-state.ts
ensureSkillsTreeStructure re-scaffolds both tiers on every readSkillsState /
writeSkillsState against a REPO skills root, so the prune is durable in practice
but not permanent. It is asserted by skills-state.test.ts:69, i.e. intentional
current contract — flipping it is a design change on the install/update path,
out of scope for a P3.

state.json sub-question answered: ~/dev/core/.xtrm/skills/state.json is tracked
at schemaVersion 1 but was already auto-upgraded to 2 with empty managedLinks in
the working tree by a local run. So it is source-repo test residue, NOT a
migration miss. Left uncommitted — it is runtime state and belongs to whoever
owns the source repo's skills fixtures.
close_reason: xt migrate skills now prunes empty managed tiers and reports untriaged local-legacy; recreator residual split out to xtrm-vtqlg.5

title: sp: roleless render-task so bare --bead can compose a turn-1 task
description: Discovered while implementing xtrm-3xgs5. 'sp render-task <name> --bead <id>' requires the specialist name positionally, so 'xt claude worker --bead X' (no --role) cannot render the tracked task as its turn-1 body — xtrm-3xgs5 shipped bare --bead as pane/env metadata only. If the epic's original intent (bare --bead composes via sp render-task) is still wanted, it needs a specialists-repo change first: a roleless render mode, or a default/generic task template. Core-side change afterwards is small: reuse the existing bead composition branch and re-arm the position-0 slash guard for the newly-untrusted bead-derived body (the guard is already provenance-keyed, so it is a one-condition change).
notes:
SPECIALISTS SIDE SHIPPED — Specialists PR #202 (xtrm-dev/specialists), bead unitAI-oc5zw, branch feature/unitAI-oc5zw-sp-render-bead.

Chose option (a) from this bead: a new verb, NOT an optional positional on render-task. Rationale: core reads this over a machine boundary, so a dropped argv slot must stay a hard 'usage' error instead of silently degrading a role render into a roleless one.

  sp render-bead <id> [--bead <id>] [--cwd <path>] [--context-depth <n>] [--surface pi|claude]

Emits the SAME envelope as render-task with specialist: null, skills: [], skill_prefix: "".
Composable as required: render-task.ts now exports parseRenderArgs/renderAndEmit/fail; render-bead
feeds a synthetic SpecialistSchema spec (task_template '$prompt', no skills) through the same
renderTaskPrompt call. One task-side assembly, no duplication. render-task behavior unchanged.

CORE-SIDE WORK REMAINING (this bead's own scope, per its description):
1. In the bare launch branch, call 'sp render-bead <bead> --surface claude|pi' and use initial_prompt as the turn-1 body (today bare --bead is pane/env metadata only).
2. Re-arm the position-0 slash guard for the bead-derived body. skill_prefix is "" by construction for a roleless render, so the guard has nothing legitimate to whitelist at position 0 — the provenance-keyed guard becomes a one-condition change as predicted.
3. Keep --prompt and --bead composable in bare mode (mutual exclusion applies only under --role).
close_reason: Specialists PR #202 merged e613819b. sp render-bead roleless render-task landed. Bare xt claude --bead <id> can now compose turn-1 via specialists CLI.

The /multiplexing and /multiplexing-team skills — the discovery surface where these change orchestrator/delegate behavior — did not mention them. Check whether either is vendor-tracked/hash-pinned before editing (see xtmux memories vendored-skill-files-in-core / skills-global-sync-lags-canonical) — if pinned, edit upstream and re-vendor rather than in place.

title: Unread-message indicator in Claude statusline (parity with Pi custom-footer)
description:
## PROBLEM
Pi custom-footer surfaces unread xtmux messages per-pane via the pi-inbox-reply extension. Claude statusline has no equivalent — an agent-coordinator or operator working in a Claude pane cannot see at a glance whether the sibling pane has queued a message for them, and must poll manually via 'tmux-session-picker message-list --for $SID'. This is asymmetric UX.

## SUCCESS
- Claude statusline surfaces unread count for the current pane, prepended to line3.
- Empty state (0 unread) renders nothing (no line noise).
- Freshness marker for stale unacked messages (e.g. bold red '!' if oldest > 5 min).
- Zero render-time subprocess: fetched in detached refresh, cached per-pane.
- Fail-soft: TMUX absent, tmux-session-picker missing, or non-tmux invocation → no indicator, no crash.
- No regression on the existing beads-status shared cache — this is a separate per-pane cache.

## SCOPE
- .xtrm/hooks/statusline.mjs (extend refresh + render)
- .xtrm/hooks/statusline.test.mjs (fixture unread cache, verify prepend + fail-soft paths)
- Optional new helper .xtrm/hooks/unread-cache.mjs if the surface warrants extraction

## CONSTRAINTS
- Per-pane cache path: <CACHE_DIR>/xtrm-sl-unread-<paneHash>.json where paneHash = md5(TMUX_PANE).slice(0,8).
- Schema: { ts, count, oldestUnackedAtMs }.
- TTL: 5s (align with existing statusline caches).
- Query: tmux-session-picker unread-count --for $SID --pane $TMUX_PANE where $SID = 'tmux display-message -p #{session_id}'.
- Runtime for tmux-session-picker call: warm ~110ms (measured 2026-07-13 on this machine — under detached refresh budget).
- Render format: '✉ N · <rest of line3>'. Bold red '!' marker if age > 5 min.
- No changes to Pi custom-footer or shared beads cache module.

## VALIDATION
- Test: fixture cache with count=3, oldest recent → line3 starts with '✉ 3 ·'.
- Test: fixture cache with count=0 → no marker.
- Test: TMUX env absent → no indicator, no throw.
- Test: tmux-session-picker missing (PATH stripped) → no indicator, no throw.
- Manual smoke: send a test message via message-send to current session, wait 5s, see counter increment.

## OUTPUT
Extended statusline + tests + optional helper module.

## NOTES
- Discovered during xtrm-77t9q.3 release-cut discussion after operator noticed Pi has this indicator via custom-footer but Claude does not (2026-07-13).
- Defer to after xtrm-77t9q.3 (release cut) to keep MVP scope tight.

title: publish.yml only publishes root xtrm-tools; coordinated pi-extensions release needs manual step
description:
PROBLEM: .github/workflows/publish.yml line 100 runs only 'npm publish --provenance' at repo root — publishes xtrm-tools@X.Y.Z but NOT @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions@X.Y.Z from the packages/pi-extensions workspace. For coordinated releases (v0.10.1 pattern) the operator has to manually 'npm publish -w @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions --access public' after gh release create fires. Missed on v0.10.0 as well (which sigstore-blocked anyway).

Manifests via sync:cli-version already bump both package.json versions in lockstep, so the workspaces are ready — publish.yml just doesn't step through them.

SUCCESS: A single gh release create v<tag> --generate-notes triggers publish.yml which publishes BOTH xtrm-tools@<tag> AND @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions@<tag> to npm with sigstore provenance. No manual step needed.

SCOPE: .github/workflows/publish.yml Publish job — add a second 'npm publish -w @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions --provenance --access public' step after the root publish. Consider ordering (root first so consumers pinning xtrm-tools bring pi-extensions along via workspace) and error handling (if root publish succeeds but workspace fails, either fail-fast or continue with a warning).

NON_GOALS: No changes to the version-sync mechanism (sync:cli-version prebuild hook already handles it). No changes to workspace tarball contents.

CONSTRAINTS: sigstore provenance signing must work for both packages (repository.url now correct on both as of v0.10.1). Must not accidentally publish xtrm-cli (the cli/ workspace) which is intentionally private.

VALIDATION: [ ] Next coordinated release (v0.10.2 or v0.11.0) publishes both packages via a single gh release create trigger. [ ] Both packages verified on npm within 1 minute of workflow completion. [ ] cli workspace is NOT published (verify via npm view xtrm-cli errors 404).

OUTPUT: PR updating publish.yml. Verify next release cycle.
close_reason: PR #402 merged. publish.yml adds second npm publish step for pi-extensions workspace after root; both packages will publish atomically on next gh release create.

title: Prevent gitignore + pre-commit mangling of vendored specialists eval fixtures
description:

Recurring class: any future re-vendor from specialists master or a tag will hit the same trap unless we harden the vendor + hygiene surface.

SUCCESS: Vendor re-runs land cleanly without operator having to (a) git add -f fixture files or (b) SKIP pre-commit whitespace hooks. verify-specialists-vendor and check:specialists-vendor pass on the first commit.

SCOPE: One or a combination of: (a) .gitignore whitelist for tracked skill eval trees under .xtrm/skills/default/<skill>/evals/ that are listed in .xtrm/specialists-source.json; (b) .pre-commit-config.yaml excludes for .xtrm/skills/default/** in trailing-whitespace + end-of-file-fixer; (c) vendor-specialists-skills.mjs post-copy step that git-add -f's manifest files and warns on hook-modified state.

NON_GOALS: No changes to the manifest format. No changes to the shipped tarball surface (package.json 'files' still excludes evals/ via existing negation).

CONSTRAINTS: Must not accidentally start shipping eval fixtures in the npm tarball. Must not weaken security-related pre-commit hooks (detect-secrets, gitleaks, semgrep-diff, osv-diff). No compatibility aliases.

VALIDATION: [ ] Re-run scripts/vendor-specialists-skills.mjs against specialists master; commit produces no untracked fixture files and no whitespace-mangled files. [ ] verify-specialists-vendor + check:specialists-vendor pass on the first commit. [ ] npm pack tarball listing still excludes evals/. [ ] check:payload-hygiene passes.

OUTPUT: PR fixing gitignore/pre-commit hygiene, vendor-script hardening if included, and a note in docs/release.md under 'Pre-commit / gitignore hazards' cross-linked from the release checklist.

title: Dependency Surface section rollout across service-skills
description:
## PROBLEM

Service skills have no standard place to record runtime-critical deps, fragile deps, canonical post-bump tests, and post-deploy watch signals. Without it, the dependency capability cannot look up service-specific impact and must reason in the abstract (spec §12). This task adds the standard section and seeds it where it matters.

## SUCCESS

A documented `## Dependency Surface` section template is part of the service-skill convention, and the most critical service skills in the ecosystem have a seeded section. The dependency skill/inspector can look up tests, watch signals, and failure modes per service.

## SCOPE

xtrm-tools service-skill conventions + seeding. Adds the section schema (Package Managers & Lockfiles / Runtime-Critical / Build-Test-CI / GitHub Actions / Container-Base Image / Known Fragile / Historical Migration Notes / Canonical Tests After Dep Updates / Post-Deploy Watch Signals / Missing Signals) per spec §12. Librarian/service-skills-sync proposes updates when drift is found. Lower priority than B/C1/D1.

## NON_GOALS

- No backfilling every service skill — seed the critical ones only; rest via drift-driven proposals.
- No changes to deployer/SRE specialists.
- No automated test generation.

## CONSTRAINTS

- Section must be proposal-driven: the dependency skill proposes a patch/follow-up when it finds drift, not in-place indiscriminate edits (spec §12).
- Keep sections accurate and dated; avoid stale migration notes.
- Follow existing service-skill authoring conventions.

## VALIDATION

- [ ] Section template documented in the service-skill convention
- [ ] At least the top critical service skills seeded
- [ ] service-skills-sync/librarian can propose Dependency Surface updates from a dependency case
- [ ] Smoke: a bump touching a seeded service reads tests + watch signals from the section

## OUTPUT

title: Phase B follow-up: auto-PR squash-merge re-triggers drift on same file set (non-convergence)
description:
PROBLEM: Phase B auto-PR merges can spawn immediate-follow-up auto-PRs against the same drift set, suggesting drift_detector's mtime comparison may not converge cleanly after a squash-merge of an auto-PR. Observed 2026-06-23: PR #130 admin-squash-merged on mercuryintelligence/mercury-infra at 01:06:07Z; PR #136 (auto-reconcile, same 8 files of the 9 in #130) opened 34s later from a new post-#130-merge action run.

HYPOTHESIS: Squash-merge to main creates a new commit SHA + new file mtimes. drift_detector compares source file mtime against last_sync_ref (which was bumped during #130's reconcile to the auto-PR's tip SHA, NOT main's post-squash SHA). After the squash, source files have mtime newer than last_sync_ref's reference time → re-classified as drift → fresh reconcile fires.

SUCCESS: scan_drift either (a) recognizes 'this file was last touched by the auto-reconcile commit that became my current last_sync_ref so it should not be drift', or (b) bumps last_sync_ref to the POST-MERGE HEAD SHA after the auto-PR lands (workflow-side update), or (c) compares against git-history rather than mtime to avoid mtime-vs-commit-SHA mismatch on squash-merge.

SCRUTINY: medium

SCOPE:
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py (scan_drift mtime logic)
- .xtrm/skills/default/service-skills/scripts/reconcile.py (last_sync_ref bump timing)
- .github/workflows/service-skills-drift-sweep.yml (whether to do a post-merge ref-only sync)

NON_GOALS: no new architecture; this is a convergence fix within the existing R4+A1+O2 pipeline. No security/scrutiny escalation beyond medium.

CONSTRAINTS: must preserve current behavior on first-time drift and on real source changes. Must NOT silently mask actual drift.

VALIDATION: after fix, an admin-squash-merge of an auto-PR followed by a no-op unrelated merge shows drift_count=0 (full convergence). Repro via mercury-infra: merge any unrelated PR after this fix; expect zero auto-PR.

OUTPUT: minimal change to drift_detector or reconcile.py that closes the convergence gap; bd remember insight.

REFERENCES:

- bd recall reconcile-runner-script-shape-2026-06-22

title: fix: Skills Runtime 'incomplete: active' warning persists on first xt init in fresh repo
description:
PROBLEM: A fresh 'xt init -y' in an empty git-init'd repo reports '⚠ Skills Runtime — incomplete: active' in the Verification Summary even though 'Activated 47 default skills → .xtrm/skills/active' succeeded. Re-running 'xt init -y' immediately after resolves it. The 'activeReady' check in skills-runtime-views.ts (activeEntries.length > 0 + all valid symlinks) flags initial state as not-ready even though materialization just finished — likely an order-of-operations issue between Skills phase (which materializes active view) and the Verification Summary (which reads it). Reproduced under v24.15.0 + xtrm-tools 0.7.18 on 2026-05-14.

SUCCESS: First 'xt init -y' in a fresh git-init'd repo reports '✓ Skills Runtime' in the Verification Summary. No second run needed.

SCOPE: cli/src/core/init-verification.ts (when Skills Runtime check runs), cli/src/core/skills-runtime-views.ts (activeReady logic), cli/src/core/skills-scaffold.ts (rebuildAllRuntimeActiveViews completion signaling).

NON_GOALS: Don't change the active view shape or the resolution semantics.

VALIDATION: Single 'xt init -y' in mktemp + git init repo shows ✓ Skills Runtime. Add regression test mirroring this flow.
notes: ROOT CAUSE confirmed 2026-05-14: bare 'gitnexus analyze' (called by xt init Project Bootstrap) unconditionally writes 6 skills to <project>/.claude/skills/gitnexus/<name>/SKILL.md (verified via gitnexus dist/cli/ai-context.js:178 installSkills). xtrm-tools makes .claude/skills a symlink to .xtrm/skills/active, so the writes land at .xtrm/skills/active/gitnexus/ — a non-symlink directory that breaks activeReady's hasOnlyValidSymlinkEntries check (skills-runtime-views.ts:38). The gitnexus subdir is redundant: xtrm-tools' own mirror already vendors the same skills as flat gitnexus-cli, gitnexus-debugging, etc. under .xtrm/skills/default/ and symlinks them into active/ flat. title: Install managed GitNexus post-commit analyze hook
description:
Problem: specialists runtime can auto-commit edit-capable specialist checkpoints, but GitNexus analyze should be triggered by a managed git post-commit hook owned by xtrm-tools, not hard-coded as specialists runtime policy. Current project hooks can be stale/absolute-path based, and no reliable xtrm-managed post-commit analyze hook is guaranteed.

Scope: xtrm-tools hook/template/install/update flow.

Requirements:
- Add/manage a local git post-commit hook that triggers GitNexus analyze after real commits.
- Preserve embeddings: if .gitnexus/meta.json indicates stats.embeddings > 0, run analyze with --embeddings; otherwise run normal analyze.
- Run non-blocking/detached with a lock to avoid concurrent analyze storms.
- Resolve repo root/worktree root correctly; avoid absolute paths to developer checkouts.
- Install/update idempotently through xt install/init/update-managed-assets path.
- Chain safely with existing git hooks rather than overwriting user hooks.
- Emit a discoverable log/status artifact so tools can prove the hook fired or failed.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fresh install has the managed post-commit hook without requiring a repo clone/symlink.
- A normal git commit triggers GitNexus analyze in the repo/worktree.
- Existing hook chains are preserved.
- Re-running xt update/install is idempotent.
- Tests or smoke script cover hook installation and a simulated post-commit invocation.
close_reason: Done: added managed GitNexus post-commit hook installer and analyze helper, wired install/init/update, preserved no-stats/embeddings behavior, and added regression/smoke tests.

title: drift_detector: optional --enrich-with-gitnexus for semantic + impact-ranked drift
description:
PROBLEM: skills/updating-service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py currently flags any territory file with mtime > last_sync. Most flagged entries are cosmetic (formatting, imports, comments) and don't warrant SKILL.md updates. On a real drift sweep this produces high noise — operators get a 50-entry list when only 5 are semantically meaningful. Has no notion of impact: every entry is flat, no ranking, no cross-territory signal.

SUCCESS:
- New optional flag '--enrich-with-gitnexus' on scan and check subcommands. Default off; tool functions identically to today when flag is absent or GitNexus is unreachable.
- When enabled and GitNexus index is fresh:
  - Per drifted file, call gitnexus_detect_changes (scoped to territory) to distinguish real symbol changes from cosmetic edits.
  - Per touched symbol, call gitnexus_impact(direction=upstream) to compute blast radius (callers, affected processes).
  - Output groups entries into 'high impact' / 'medium' / 'cosmetic' tiers with cited symbol names and affected process flows.
  - Cross-territory edge note: when a symbol from territory A is imported into territory B's territory file, surface as 'cross-territory drift signal' so the librarian considers updating both SKILLs.
- When GitNexus is unreachable or index is stale (gitnexus_detect_changes warns), tool emits a stderr line ('gitnexus enrichment skipped: <reason>') and falls through to mtime-only output. Never blocks.

SCOPE:
- skills/updating-service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py — scan/check subcommands, output formatter.
- skills/creating-service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py — small helper for GitNexus availability probe (importable; safe import; no top-level I/O).
- Tests: fresh project with fixture commits exercising cosmetic vs semantic edits; assert tier ranking; assert graceful fallback when GitNexus unavailable.

NON_GOALS:
- No replacement of mtime-based trigger. mtime stays primary; GitNexus is enrichment only.
- No automatic SKILL.md mutation; this remains the librarian's call.
- No GitNexus install or index management; tool only consumes if already available.
- No new env vars beyond optional GITNEXUS_DISABLE escape hatch.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Pure stdlib for the core path; GitNexus calls behind try/except so missing tools never break scan.
- Pre-flight check: gitnexus_detect_changes with timeout 2s; if it doesn't return cleanly, skip enrichment.
- Output remains parseable line-by-line so existing pipes/grep usage by operators keeps working; add structured fields after the existing 'service: file (last sync: ...)' line.

VALIDATION:
- pytest fixtures: cosmetic-only edit (returns mtime drift but enriched as 'cosmetic' tier); signature change (high tier, cites symbol + processes); cross-territory import (both services flagged, edge annotated).
- Live: run scan --enrich-with-gitnexus on darth-feedor immediately after a real session; expected: 50 mtime drift entries reduced to ~5-8 high-impact entries with the rest tagged cosmetic.

REFERENCES:
- Sibling bead xtrm-upm1 (registry-resolver fix). This bead depends on xtrm-upm1 because enrichment is moot if scan can't even find the registry.
- darth-feedor session 2026-05-07 motivated this — first real-world large-scale drift scan that produced too-noisy output to act on directly.
- gitnexus tool availability is broadly assumed across xtrm projects per CLAUDE.md conventions but not strictly required.
notes:

title: service-registry resolver doesn't probe canonical xtrm pack layout
description:
PROBLEM: skills/creating-service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py:get_registry_path probes only two locations: <root>/service-registry.json (preferred) and <root>/.claude/skills/service-registry.json (legacy). xtrm-tools itself ships service-registry.json under .xtrm/skills/user/packs/<pack>/service-registry.json (e.g. mercury pack on darth-feedor). Result: drift_detector.py scan returns 'No drift detected' WITHOUT erroring on any project that uses an xtrm pack — silent false-clean state. Confirmed live on darth-feedor 2026-05-07; required a manual symlink (ln -s .xtrm/skills/user/packs/mercury/service-registry.json service-registry.json) to make the detector functional. Same trap will hit any project that consumes an xtrm pack of service skills.

SUCCESS:
- get_registry_path additionally probes <root>/.xtrm/skills/user/packs/*/service-registry.json (sorted glob; first hit wins; if multiple exist, prefer one matching the project's active pack manifest if discoverable, else lexicographically first with a warning).
- Resolution order documented in module docstring updated.
- When NO registry is found, scan/sync subcommands print a one-line stderr hint pointing at expected paths (instead of silently returning empty).

SCOPE:
- skills/creating-service-skills/scripts/bootstrap.py — get_registry_path + module docstring.
- skills/updating-service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py — scan/sync error path, only if it currently swallows the no-registry case.
- Mirror updates under .xtrm/skills/default/{creating,updating}-service-skills/ if those exist.

NON_GOALS:
- No new env var beyond existing SERVICE_REGISTRY_PATH override.
- No automatic registry creation.
- No symlink-management on consumer projects.

CONSTRAINTS:
- Backward-compatible: if root/legacy registry already exists, behavior unchanged.
- Pure stdlib (Path.glob).
- No I/O during import; resolution stays lazy.

VALIDATION:
- New unit test fixtures: project with xtrm pack-only registry; project with both root and xtrm pack (root wins); project with no registry (clear stderr).
- Live: drop into a fresh clone of darth-feedor (after removing the workaround symlink), run drift_detector.py scan — should find drift across the territories without manual setup.

title: Agent memory: context graphs, reasoning traces, entity extraction pipeline
description:
## Source

Distilled from: qMV64p-4Deo — 'Building Context Graphs for AI Agents' by Will Lyon, Neo4j (April 2026)
Analysis file: dev/omni-search-engine/docs/qMV64p-4Deo.analysis.md

## Core Concept: The Missing Why

A context graph is a knowledge graph that contains all information necessary to make decisions throughout a system — crucially including *why* decisions were made, not just what decisions were made.

Current xtrm agent sessions lose reasoning context between turns and sessions. Specialists produce outputs but don't record their reasoning traces in a queryable form.

## Three Memory Types (apply to xtrm specialist pipeline)

### 1. Short-term memory
Conversation/session state — the current turn's working context.
Already partially solved by bd prime + bead notes.

### 2. Long-term memory
Extracted entities and facts persisted across sessions.
Currently fragmented: bd memories, MEMORY.md files, bead notes — no unified graph.

### 3. Reasoning memory (MOST IMPORTANT — least supported)
Tool call traces, decision steps, token usage, specialist outputs — recorded as auditable history.
Currently: specialist results exist in job feeds and bead notes, but are not queryable or connected.

## Key Insight: Reasoning Memory as Precedent

When an agent makes a decision (e.g. executor chose approach X over Y because of Z), recording that decision in the memory graph makes it available as precedent for future similar decisions. The memory graph becomes self-improving.

Applied to xtrm: when a specialist closes a bead with --reason, that reason + the full decision context (what was tried, what failed, what worked) should be indexed as a retrievable precedent, not just a log entry.

## Entity Extraction Pipeline (cost-efficient)

Neo4j production approach — never LLM-first:
  1. spaCy / statistical NER (fast, free, CPU)
  2. GLINER 2 — local model, runs on CPU, fine-tuned for entity+relationship extraction
  3. LLM fallback ONLY when statistical methods fail

This is the right approach for extracting entities from specialist outputs, bead notes, and session logs without burning tokens on every entry.

## Proposed xtrm Integration Points

### A. bd remember enhancement
Current: bd remember 'insight' — flat key-value store
Proposed: tag entities from the insight automatically (people, tools, concepts, decisions)
so that bd memories 'keyword' can traverse entity relationships, not just keyword-match strings.

### B. Specialist reasoning traces
After each specialist run, extract the decision trace (tools called, findings, decisions made)
and store as a reasoning memory node linked to the bead.
Queryable: 'what did we try when fixing X?' returns tool call trace from that session.

### C. Precedent lookup before dispatch
Before dispatching an executor, check reasoning memory for similar past beads:
  bd precedent 'auth token refresh bug'  →  returns past decisions on similar tasks

### D. Session handoff context
When a new session starts, bd prime could surface not just active beads but relevant
reasoning memories from past sessions that match current bead topics.

## Implementation Notes

- Storage: extend the existing bd/dolt graph — reasoning memory as a new node type
- Extraction: run entity extraction on bead close (PostToolUse hook on bd close)
- No new infrastructure: leverage existing SQLite/dolt in .beads/
- GLINER 2 local model runs on CPU in seconds per document
- Start simple: capture bead close --reason text + specialist result summaries as first pass

title: RFC: global pi extensions with project-level manifest validation
description:
## Problem

Per-project pi extension management via .pi/settings.json → .xtrm/extensions/ symlinks is fragile. Symlinks break across worktrees, pi-core disappears requiring xt pi reload repair cycles, and every worktree bootstrap needs to re-establish the symlink tree. This was identified during hgpu (worktree-per-executor isolation) work in the specialists repo — the worktree Pi bootstrap step exists solely because of this fragility.

## Current design

Extensions installed per-project under .xtrm/extensions/node_modules/. .pi/settings.json points to project-local paths. Worktrees need symlinks (.pi → main/.pi) to share the install. Symlinks break → RPC timeout → xt pi reload to repair.

## Proposed design

Global install, project-level opt-in manifest:

1. Extensions installed globally at ~/.pi/agent/extensions/ (many already are via npm)
2. Project declares requirements in a manifest (e.g. .pi/extensions.json or pi.extensions in package.json):
   ```json
   {
     "required": ["pi-gitnexus", "pi-serena-tools", "@xtrm/pi-core"],
     "optional": ["pi-mcp-adapter"]
   }
   ```
3. On pi startup: validate globals satisfy manifest, warn/error if missing
4. Project-level overrides still possible via .xtrm/extensions/ but only when explicitly needed (dev/testing)

## Benefits

- Worktrees just work — no symlinks, no bootstrap, no repair
- Traceability preserved — manifest is committed, teammates see what's needed
- Skills control preserved — manifest declares intent, pi validates
- Simpler xt pi/xt claude bootstrap (skip symlink step entirely)
- hgpu worktree Pi bootstrap becomes a no-op

## Costs

- Can't pin project-specific extension versions (all projects share global version)
- Extension dev/testing slightly harder (need explicit local override)
- Migration from current per-project installs

## Origin

Discovered during specialists repo hgpu implementation (worktree isolation feature). Pi-core symlink broke repeatedly between specialist runs, causing 10s RPC timeouts. The fragility is the direct cause of the Pi bootstrap requirement in the hgpu worktree design.
close_reason: Implemented: global extensions with repo symlinks. Renamed .xtrm/extensions/ → .xtrm/ext-src/ to avoid Pi auto-discovery conflicts. Extensions symlinked from ~/.pi/agent/extensions/ → .xtrm/ext-src/. Edit in repo works globally.

title: [epic] Project utils system: typed utility scripts, manifest, and process manager
description:
## Overview

Introduce a first-class `utils/` system to xtrm-tools — a set of typed, manifested utility scripts that specialists and orchestrators can invoke declaratively, plus an abstract process manager module for long-lived/background processes.

## Architecture

Xtreme is the execution substrate (worktrees, process lifecycle, toolchain, hooks). This epic formalizes that role with concrete tooling.

### Layer boundary (to document formally)

- **Xtreme** = provisioning, worktrees, process lifecycle, session management, toolchain, shared scripts, pre/post hooks
- **Specialist** = role logic, task execution, output, handoff — consumes Xtreme primitives

## Planned sub-epics / bundles

### 1. Utils folder + typed manifest (foundation)
- `utils/manifest.json` schema: id, description, runtime, command, input, output, timeout, phase (pre/post/on-demand), failure_policy (blocking/advisory)
- Every utility declares its contract; no ad-hoc scripts

### 2. Utility script bundles (implement manifest contract)
- **Core** — health-check, lint, type-check, format-check, test-smoke
- **Validators** — schema-validator (JSON/YAML/specialist-output), config-validator (env, project config), policy-validator (naming, structure, ownership)
- **Security** — secret-scan, dependency-vulnerability-check, unsafe-pattern-scan
- **Git/change intelligence** — changed-files-analyzer (classifies by type), diff-risk-estimator (coupling + missing tests), branch-consistency-check
- **Testing** — targeted-test-selector (runs tests covering changed files only), coverage-delta-check, flaky-test-detector
- **Observability** — log-follow-helper, error-summarizer, incident-snapshot (processes + ports + logs + repo state bundle)
- **Docker** — docker-health, docker-compose-validate, image-policy-check

### 3. Specialist integration
- Expose utils manifest to specialist YAML via `capabilities.utils[]`
- Specialists declare which utils to run at which phase (pre/in/post)

### 4. Abstract process manager module
- Interface: start / stop / restart / status / logs / follow / cleanup
- PNPM-backed as first implementation; interface-abstracted for future runtimes
- Named processes, PID + log tracking, follow streaming, reattach to existing
- Process policies: timeout, restart policy, blocking vs background classification
- Automatic cleanup at job end
- Enables specialists to launch dev servers, log tails, event streams, watchers — and human/agent operators to follow with `--follow`

## Sequencing

1. Architecture doc (formal Xtreme vs Specialist boundary)
2. Utils manifest schema
3. Core + Validator bundles (highest utility for specialists)
4. Process manager (unlocks background process UX)
5. Remaining bundles + specialist integration

## Notes

This epic is intentionally coarse-grained. Each sub-item above becomes its own issue when the time comes to implement it. File this as a planning anchor — break it down before starting.

title: Eval: consolidate beads hook files vs extract shared utils
description:
## Context

This project is **xtrm-tools** — a collection of Claude Code agent skills, hooks, and tooling for a multi-agent development workflow. Hooks are shell scripts (mostly .mjs) that fire at lifecycle events in Claude Code sessions (PreToolUse, PostToolUse, Stop, etc.) and enforce workflow rules.

## The Hooks in Question

Four beads hooks live in `~/.claude/hooks/` (installed globally, not tracked in this repo):

| File | Event | Purpose |
|------|-------|---------|
| `beads-edit-gate.mjs` | PreToolUse (Write/Edit) | Blocks file edits if this session has no claimed issue |
| `beads-stop-gate.mjs` | Stop | Blocks agent stop if this session has an unclaimed issue |
| `beads-commit-gate.mjs` | PreToolUse (Bash/git commit) | Blocks git commit if this session has an unclaimed issue |
| `beads-close-memory-prompt.mjs` | PostToolUse (Bash/bd close) | Clears kv claim + injects reminder after bd close |

## How They Work (Recent Refactor)

All three gate hooks now use **session-scoped claiming via `bd kv`** instead of global in_progress checks:

```js
// Shared pattern in all three gate hooks (currently duplicated):
function getSessionClaim(sessionId) {
  try {
    return execSync(`bd kv get "claimed:${sessionId}"`, { ... }).trim();
  } catch (err) {
    if (err.status === 1) return '';  // key not found
    return null;                      // bd kv unavailable — fail open
  }
}
```

Each hook also duplicates: exec options boilerplate, `.beads` dir check, cwd resolution, and the fallback path (no session_id → old global in_progress check).

## The Question for Evaluation

Two options were proposed:

### Option A — Single dispatcher script
One `beads-gate.mjs` file handles all events, routes internally by inspecting `input.hook_type` or similar.

**Key constraint**: Claude Code does NOT pass the hook event type in the hook input JSON. So `settings.json` still needs separate entries per event — each pointing to the same file. The file would need another mechanism to know which path to take (e.g. a CLI flag, or env var set per-entry in settings.json, e.g. `BEADS_HOOK_MODE=edit node beads-gate.mjs`).

### Option B — Shared utils module
Keep four separate hook files. Extract duplicated logic into `beads-gate-utils.mjs`:
- `getSessionClaim(sessionId, cwd)`
- `execBd(cmd, cwd)`
- `hasTotalWork(cwd)`
- `checkBeadsProject(cwd)`

Each hook imports from utils. Files stay small and independently testable.

## What We Want You to Evaluate

1. Is Option A actually viable given the Claude Code hook input constraint (no event type in JSON)? Is there a clean way to pass routing context per-entry in settings.json?
2. Is Option B the pragmatic choice, or does it add complexity for modest gain?
3. Is there an Option C we haven't considered?
4. What's the blast radius / maintenance risk of each approach over time, as more hooks get added?

Please post your recommendation as a comment or note on this issue. The author will implement based on your answer.

comments.text:
Recommendation: choose Option B now (separate hook entrypoints + shared utils module), with a narrow Option C fallback if/when complexity grows.

1) Option A viability
- Technically viable only if you pass explicit mode per settings entry (CLI arg or env var), since hook JSON does not include event type.
- That means you still keep multiple settings entries, and now add a dispatch contract that can drift (mode string mismatch, missing arg/env).
- Net: centralization gain is smaller than it appears, while routing fragility increases.

2) Option B pragmatism
- Best current tradeoff. Keep event-specific scripts for clarity and independent behavior, extract only duplicated primitives:
  - resolveCwd/input parsing
  - checkBeadsProject
  - execBd/getSessionClaim
  - fallback global in_progress path
- This removes repetition without coupling unrelated policy decisions into one dispatcher.

3) Option C (recommended guardrail)
- Hybrid: Option B + one tiny shared guard wrapper for uniform error/timeout/fail-open policy (e.g., withSafeBdContext(fn)).
- Keep policy logic in each hook, infra logic in utils. Avoid full dispatcher until >~8 hooks or heavy shared branching emerges.

4) Blast radius / maintenance risk
- Option A: high blast radius. A dispatcher bug or routing regression can break all hook events at once.
- Option B: low-to-medium blast radius. Utils bugs affect many hooks, but event logic stays isolated and easier to test.
- Option C hybrid: medium, but controlled if shared wrapper is very small and stable.

Decision rule going forward
- Stay on Option B while hooks remain mostly independent.
- Reconsider dispatcher only when duplication is primarily in policy branching (not just shell/bd plumbing) and you can enforce strict mode validation + tests per event mode.

title: Investigate: bd create may auto-set in_progress, triggering stop gate
description: After claiming an issue (bd update --status=in_progress + bd kv set), the stop gate showed in_progress on a freshly-created issue before any explicit status change. Possible causes: bd create defaults to in_progress status, or beads-edit-gate's bd kv claiming logic has a side effect on issue state. Reproduce: create a fresh issue, check status immediately, observe if stop gate fires. Compare behavior with and without the new session-scoped kv claiming code.
notes: ROOT CAUSE FOUND: Not bd create defaulting to in_progress (confirmed: new issues are always created as OPEN). The stop gate false-positive is a Dolt read inconsistency: bd list --status=in_progress reads the Dolt *working set* while bd show reads the *committed* state. With dolt.auto-commit=off (default), bd update writes to the working set immediately but bd close may only commit after the fact. Result: bd list sees stale in_progress from the working set even though bd show reports CLOSED from HEAD. The new session-scoped stop gate (kv claim check) sidesteps this entirely — it won't fire for a session with no kv claim, regardless of what bd list shows. Mitigation: ensure bd close always flushes the working set, OR document that dolt.auto-commit=on is required for gate consistency.
close_reason: Diagnosed: Dolt working-set vs committed-state read inconsistency, not bd create behavior

title: Add PreCompact/SessionStart hooks to restore in_progress beads state after compaction
description:
After /compact, beads issue statuses persist in Dolt but the agent resumes without knowing which issues were in_progress. The gate fires on the first write and the agent must manually re-mark issues before continuing.

Fix: ship two hooks as part of xtrm-tools (installed via xtrm install into ~/.claude/hooks/):

1. PreCompact hook (new): hooks/beads-compact-save.py (or .cjs)
   - Runs bd list --status=in_progress
   - Writes issue IDs to .beads/.last_active (one ID per line)
   - Fires before context is compacted so the list is accurate

2. SessionStart hook addition: extend existing hooks or add hooks/beads-compact-restore.cjs
   - On session start, checks for .beads/.last_active
   - If found, runs bd update <id> --status=in_progress for each ID
   - Deletes .beads/.last_active after restore
   - Injects a brief context message: 'Restored N in_progress issues from last session'

Both hooks wired in config/settings.json and synced by xtrm install.

Note: beads-edit-gate.mjs is owned by the beads npm package and should not be modified directly. Our hooks complement it without patching upstream. If the beads package ever ships its own compaction support, our hooks can be retired.

Acceptance criteria:
- /compact followed by new session → first write is NOT blocked by the gate
- Issues that were in_progress before compact are still in_progress after
- .beads/.last_active is cleaned up after restore (idempotent)

Anti-spin pattern for a Stop-hook reminder (bead xtrm-wiy5n.4.24, core#525 + xtmux#87). The write-first ordering is the part that is easy to get wrong: PERSIST the already-reminded key BEFORE emitting the reminder, and ABORT the reminder if the write fails. Reminder-then-write is the natural order and it silently voids the bounded-work guarantee, because a failed write means the same message re-surfaces on every later Stop forever. Also: Claude's Stop hook contract reads STDOUT on exit 0 and stderr only on a non-zero exit, so a reminder must be emitted as {"systemMessage": "..."} on stdout. Both points were found by Codex, not by the author.

beads stop/commit gates in a multi-lane repo: both shipped versions counted EVERY in_progress issue in the repo, which makes them unsatisfiable for whoever finishes second — the blocking issue belongs to another agent and the only way through is to falsely close their active work. Three defects found 2026-08-07, first two fixed locally in ~/.claude/hooks/. (1) beads-commit-gate.mjs resolved the beads DB from the SESSION cwd, so committing in a sibling checkout via a cd-prefixed or -C-prefixed invocation gated repo A against repo B's open work; it now parses the target path out of the command, falling back to session cwd. (2) beads-stop-gate.mjs now ATTRIBUTES work: session start comes from statSync(input.transcript_path).birthtime, and an issue whose started_at predates it cannot be this session's to close — those are reported via a systemMessage on stdout with exit 0 instead of blocking. Fail-safe both ways: no transcript, no timestamp, or only the legacy bd text count means attribution is impossible, so the issue counts as MINE and the gate still blocks. Epic exemption retained. (3) NOT FIXED: the commit gate matches the bare substring for a commit invocation anywhere in the command, so even a bd remember whose TEXT quotes that phrase is blocked as if it were a real commit — it needs to detect an actual invocation, not a substring. All local-only; overwritten by specialists install, so the durable fix belongs upstream and is not yet raised as a PR.

Bun caches process.ppid at process startup. A long-lived Bun child that checks process.ppid to detect an orphaned parent will NEVER notice reparenting — /proc/self/status can report PPid: 1 while process.ppid still returns the original. Read the live parent from the kernel each tick instead: /proc/self/status on Linux, 'ps -o ppid=' elsewhere. Found on xtrm-wiy5n.4.40, fixed in Jaggerxtrm/xtmux#86.

CI dist-verify + git-worktree gotcha: building cli/dist inside a git WORKTREE (e.g. .xtrm/worktrees/* or a detached sibling like xtrm-sv2) bakes worktree-relative node_modules paths into esbuild's embedded source-file comments (e.g. '// ../../xtrm-tools/cli/node_modules/conf/...' instead of CI's '// node_modules/conf/...'). The bundle is functionally identical but the 'Verify dist is up to date' CI gate does a strict git diff against a build from the canonical repo root and FAILS. Fix: always rebuild cli/dist from the canonical repo root (/home/dawid/dev/xtrm-tools), not from a worktree, before pushing a PR. Symptom: dist-verify fails in ~25s with diffs that are ONLY '// ...node_modules/...' comment-path lines. Complements xt-end-must-rebuild-cli-dist (which says to rebuild) — this says WHERE.

cli/dist CAN be rebuilt safely from an xt worktree despite cli/package.json's prebuild guard ('Do not run npm run build from a worktree'). The guard's premise (commit b86d9d68) is that tsup/esbuild embeds deep relative paths to node_modules when the worktree lacks its own deps. Run 'npm ci' at the worktree root AND in cli/, then 'npx tsup' (bypassing the prebuild guard): the node_modules layout matches the main repo exactly, and dist/index.cjs.map sources stay '../../node_modules/...' with zero absolute or worktree paths. Verify before committing: grep -c '/home/' cli/dist/index.cjs cli/dist/index.cjs.map must be 0. Without the npm ci step the guard is right and dist WILL be contaminated.

When writing a delegated bead contract, do NOT paste a literal command for the worker to execute unless you have just verified it yourself against --help. A worker handed an exact command will run it and will NOT go read help for it — you have suppressed its judgement, and any staleness in your command becomes its failure. On 2026-07-26 this turned a stale plan snippet into a false P1 product bug: the chain-coordinator correctly loaded /using-specialists first, then ran the broken command it was given. Prefer stating the GOAL plus constraints and letting the worker resolve the invocation, or verify the exact command first. Corollary: mandatory pre-flight steps in CLAUDE.md (sp --help, sp list) apply to the ORCHESTRATOR too, not just to workers.

scan_drift in drift_detector.py compares source file mtime against service.last_sync ISO TIMESTAMP, NOT last_sync_ref SHA. The SHA is metadata only. drift_detector OOM footgun fixed (xtrm-08i0b, target 0.8.4). Tre difetti che si sommavano nel service-skills drift scan + fix: (1) i territory glob matchano il FILESYSTEM (Path.glob), non git → alberi gitignored build/vendor/cache (rust target/, __pycache__, node_modules) finiscono nel candidate set → filtra i candidati ai file git-tracked via "git ls-files -z" (_git_tracked_files) PRIMA di qualsiasi enrichment. (2) per-item gitnexus fan-out illimitato: un subprocess "npx gitnexus" per file driftato, ognuno carica il grafo del repo → OOM (incidente reale: market-data 4991 candidati su VPS 32GB). Fix: cap hard MAX_ENRICH_CANDIDATES (env DRIFT_MAX_ENRICH, default 200) → oltre il cap, fallback a mtime + warning rumoroso su stderr. (3) PROCESS LEAK: npx spawna un figlio node che SOPRAVVIVE a un kill plain di subprocess.run (viene segnalato solo il pid di npx) — il node orfano tiene il grafo residente. Fix: subprocess.Popen(start_new_session=True) + su timeout/finally os.killpg(os.getpgid(pid), SIGKILL) (_kill_process_tree in bootstrap.run_gitnexus_json). INOLTRE: post_merge_drift_sweep.py ora chiama scan_drift(use_gitnexus=False) — il sweep solo RILEVA+flagga drift; il tiering semantico e compito del librarian, cosi un merge sul default branch non puo mai scatenare il fan-out gitnexus. Lezioni generali: qualsiasi scanner basato su glob filesystem deve intersecare con git-tracked; qualsiasi codice che spawna tool npx/node deve killare il process GROUP non il pid. Related: drift-detector-sync-never-stamped-last-sync-ref-lg9km, service-skills-post-merge-drift-sweep-jcmub.

drift_detector.py pyright pattern (xtrm-2oho): bootstrap module imported via runtime sys.path.insert returns Unknown; project_root args after the 'if None: try get_project_root()' resolution dance are typed Unknown | str | None. Pyright can't narrow Unknown. Fix: 'project_root = cast(str, project_root)' after the resolution block in every function that has the pattern (check_drift, _print_missing_registry_hint, scan_drift). Also add 'type: ignore[import-not-found]' on the dynamic bootstrap import line.

drift_detector.py sync never stamped last_sync_ref — the mechanical ROOT of the whole mtime-fallback saga (xtrm-lg9km, 2026-06-01). update_sync_time(service_id, project_root=None) on the CLI path (drift_detector.py sync <id>) passed project_root=None straight to _git_head -> subprocess git -C None rev-parse HEAD raises (None not str) -> caught -> last_sync_ref = "". So sync stamped last_sync (timestamp) but last_sync_ref was ALWAYS "" via the CLI. Because scan_drift needs last_sync_ref for the committed-range gitnexus compare (last_sync_ref..HEAD), an empty ref forces gitnexus_status=no_ref -> tier_source=mtime for EVERY service permanently — so even a correctly-wired drift hook (post xtrm-0p7bp) could never tier semantically, which is what pushed librarians to grep-only (q7436). FIX: resolve project_root via get_project_root() (same as load_registry/check_drift do with the `if project_root is None` pattern) BEFORE calling _git_head; keep the ""-fallback only for genuine git failure (detached/no-commits). skills/service-skills/scripts/drift_detector.py:46-62 + mirror. Test: skills/service-skills/tests/test_drift_detector_sync_ref.py (subprocess CLI sync in tmp git repo asserts last_sync_ref==HEAD). Proven on darth-feedor: 11/11 services had empty refs, manually stamped (py_backend-0ndo commit 3d4755e). This unblocks semantic tiering for ALL service repos. Related: [[service-skills-hooks-dormant-in-consumers-0p7bp-root-cause]] [[service-skills-gitnexus-mandatory-verdicts-q7436]].

Fresh '.beads/config.yaml' files created by 'bd init' contain only commented-out defaults. yaml.parse() of a comments-only file returns null (not an empty object). Any xt code that reads/parses '.beads/config.yaml' MUST coerce the parse result before property access — typical guard: 'const cfg = (rawParsed && typeof rawParsed === "object" && !Array.isArray(rawParsed)) ? rawParsed : {}'. Without this guard, accessing 'parsed.dolt' (or any other field) throws 'Cannot read properties of null'. Discovered 2026-05-12 via 'xt update --root ~/projects/mercury' which crashed on 6 repos with bare default configs. scripts/gen-registry.mjs walks the filesystem via fs.readdir, NOT the git index. Any operator-WIP file/dir physically present under .xtrm/skills/default/ in your local clone — even if untracked — gets hashed into .xtrm/registry.json on regen, then fails CI's check:registry-pack-parity because npm pack respects the git tracking + 'files' field and excludes them. Symptom: local 'Registry/pack parity ok: N files' but CI 'N files missing from npm pack'. Reproduced on xtrm-5bnfk PR #319 (commit 76296aa7 fixed it). Mitigation: before 'npm run gen-registry', sidecar any untracked dirs under .xtrm/skills/default/ aside (mv to /tmp), regen, commit, restore. Or never run gen-registry from a clone that carries operator-WIP untracked content. Permanent fix candidate (out of scope here): change gen-registry.mjs to filter via 'git ls-files' so it never indexes untracked content.

git-cliff cliff.toml Tera templates: the per-commit timestamp field is commit.author.timestamp (unix epoch), NOT commit.timestamp (that's undefined in the 'body' render context — only set on release-level context). Git exports GIT_DIR/GIT_WORK_TREE/GIT_INDEX_FILE into hook environments. Any hook-invoked tool that chdirs into a different checkout and runs git there (semgrep --baseline-commit materializes the baseline in a temp git worktree and runs 'git checkout' inside it) will have those calls retarget the INVOKING worktree instead: HEAD detaches at the baseline, the commit unwinds into unstaged changes, and the temp worktree leaks as prunable. Untracked files are NOT the cause - they only steer semgrep away from its safe 'git reset --hard' fast path onto the worktree path. Fix: strip the inherited git env before invoking the scanner. Verified in xtrm-bjbdf.

File modes do not travel through git — only the executable bit does. A tracked file's read/write mode is set by the umask of the shell that CHECKS IT OUT, so chmod at authoring time is theatre for anything crossing a git boundary. Under umask 077 this hits only files NEW to a given checkout: files already present keep the mode they have, so a tree looks correct (siblings 0664) while every newly-pulled file lands 0600. That is why the fault presents as intermittent and gets attributed to whatever change happened to trigger the pull. Per-file chmod cannot fix it; only a post-checkout normalisation target in the repo can, and that target must cover the whole asset tree, not the subset that failed first. Verified 2026-08-05 on xtrm-gvek4: capacity-reclaim/SKILL.md was chmod 644 before commit and git stored it 100644 exactly like sre-triage and deploy-monitor, yet it still landed 0600 in the orchestrator's checkout — the file documenting this fault was hit by it. In this worktree all three skills read 0600, confirming the mode is a property of the checkout, not the repo.

github-actions shell-injection fix pattern: any ${{ inputs.* }}, ${{ github.event.client_payload.* }}, ${{ github.event_name }}, ${{ steps.X.outputs.Y }} reference inside a run: block triggers semgrep yaml.github-actions.security.run-shell-injection. GitHub PR review-event semantics for CI gates (non-obvious): (1) issue_comment fires on top-level PR conversation comments only — inline diff comments fire the SEPARATE pull_request_review_comment event (types: created/edited/deleted). Miss it and a bot posting inline comments outside a review submission never re-triggers the gate. (2) A CHANGES_REQUESTED review stays active in GitHub's native branch-protection until the same author submits APPROVED or DISMISSED — a later COMMENTED review does NOT clear it. Track the latest verdict-carrying review (APPROVED/CHANGES_REQUESTED/DISMISSED) per bot, ignore COMMENTED entirely. Discovered via Codex adversarial review of the pr-review-gate fanout (xtrm-54zwl.7).

gitignore patterns with trailing slash (e.g., '.pi/npm/') match only directories, NOT symlinks pointing to directories. Symlinks are treated as regular files by git. To ignore something that may appear as either symlink or directory, list BOTH forms ('.pi/npm' and '.pi/npm/'). This was the root cause of .pi/npm getting re-committed weekly in xtrm-tools (PR #224 fix in xtrm-5kn1).

gitnexus detect_changes --scope unstaged only sees the DIRTY worktree, not committed history. gitnexus has two CLI verbs with very different cost/effect profiles: 'augment <pattern>' is the read-only fast-path designed for hot hooks (cold-start <500ms, queries existing index, writes only to stderr, never touches AGENTS.md/CLAUDE.md/DB) — used by xtrm-tools' PostToolUse hook (.xtrm/hooks/gitnexus/gitnexus-hook.cjs). 'analyze' is the heavy full-index path (memory-intensive, parser + graph + optional embeddings) and is the ONLY verb that writes AGENTS.md / CLAUDE.md unless --skip-agents-md --no-stats are both passed. Specialists supervisor (src/specialist/supervisor.ts:399) passes both since commit fd60db04 (2026-05-09). xtrm-tools CLI does not invoke analyze. Implication: in projects WITHOUT specialists running, the gitnexus index goes stale unless an operator runs 'npx gitnexus analyze' manually — augment hot-path enrichment continues but its results are based on the last analyzed snapshot. If a workflow needs auto-refresh, that's a managed git post-commit hook (tracked at xtrm-kye9), NOT additional augment calls.

Global-only registration pattern (bead xtrm-xnymw, core#527): when a resource must live in ONE place, 'delete it from the wrong place' is only half the rule. Do ENSURE-THEN-REMOVE: guarantee the correct location declares it, and only then remove the duplicate. If the ensure fails — unreadable file, write error — leave the duplicate ALONE and say so on stderr. Codex caught that unconditional removal would leave npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions registered NOWHERE when ~/.pi/agent/settings.json lacked the entry, which is worse than the duplicate it was fixing. ENOENT is different from a read error: absent means create, unreadable means refuse.

Installer safe-delete pattern, now used in two repos: an installer may remove ONLY what it can prove it wrote. xtmux uses a per-entry _source tag (xtmux#82); core uses a per-root manifest of the previous install, .installer-manifest.json (core#520). Three traps found while building the core one: (1) derive the manifest from the SOURCE walk, never from a post-copy walk of the target, or the first install adopts pre-existing user files and the SECOND install deletes them; (2) an absent manifest must mean OWN NOTHING, so the upgrade run deletes nothing; (3) refuse a manifest entry whose ancestor chain crosses a symlink, or a directory swapped for a symlink between installs lets the remover delete outside the managed root.

Migrating a project from 'npm-linked xtrm-tools + manual dev symlink' to a real npm consumer is NOT automatic. Steps: (1) 'npm install -g xtrm-tools' replaces the npm link with real files at the global path, breaking the dev-tree coupling — but the project's <repo>/.xtrm/skills/default symlink still exists, just now points at the real npm dir; (2) scaffoldSkillsDefaultFromPackage's 'symlink whose realpath==package realpath → noop' branch will keep preserving it on every xt update; (3) to fully cut over: 'rm <repo>/.xtrm/skills/default' then 'xt init -y' to copy real files in, then 'git rm --cached' + 'git add' + commit to flip the tracked symlink to a tracked directory. Without #3, the symlink stays forever — functional but invisibly coupled to whatever npm version is installed globally.

Modern bd 1.0.3 stores core.hooksPath as an ABSOLUTE parent path at bd init time. Worktrees inherit this via shared git config, so bd hooks fire from the parent location for all worktree git ops without needing per-worktree core.hooksPath overrides. bd hooks do NOT re-scaffold a worktree-local .beads/ when invoked from worktree cwd — the .beads/hooks/* shell scripts are pure 'bd hooks run <name>' delegators (no mkdir/scaffold logic). This means: rm -rf <worktree>/.beads + git update-index --skip-worktree -- $(git ls-files .beads) is sufficient to provision a clean worktree without a symlink. The previous dir->symlink approach (xtrm-as7d / xtrm-nsca / unitAI-u08e8) is now obsolete and caused a critical merge hazard: a squash-merge of any branch carrying the .beads symlink (mode 120000) wipes the parent .beads/ on main (real incident: projects/infra PR #39, 2026-05-12). Defense-in-depth pre-push guards (xt end findBeadsSymlinkIntroductions, xtrm-w1ip) stay valuable for older worktrees / non-CLI push paths. Open risk: older bd installs that stored core.hooksPath as relative — needs an audit pass across all repos before retiring the symlink approach in field installations.

MSG-05 parent notification fires ONLY when a specialist job reaches terminal status (done|error) — supervisor.ts:203 returns early otherwise. A job that dies at startup is left at status=running/is_dead=true and silently produces NO notification. The second precondition is spawn_origin.runtime_origin.verified=true (supervisor.ts:204-207); bead_id is optional (supervisor.ts:257), so a beadless sp run is a valid MSG-05 path.

Pi extension loop guard: never call pi.sendUserMessage() from agent_end/session_shutdown for reminders; it always triggers a new turn and can create stop-loop recursion. Use ctx.ui.notify (or pi.sendMessage without triggerTurn) and dedupe notices by session claim/worktree.

pi extension reload guard: prototype patches stamped with EXTERNAL_TOOL_FRAME_PATCH_VERSION survive /reload because the ToolExecutionComponent module stays cached in-process; any change to patched render behavior must bump the version constant or live sessions keep the old render.

Pi ExtensionRunner emit() catches session_start handler exceptions and continues. Security-sensitive extension startup cannot rely on throw to abort. For an isolated Pi child, first clear the active tool set; if that reset fails, terminate the child with process.exit(1) and verify the parent observes the nonzero exit.

Pi extensions (config/pi/extensions/*.ts) are separate from Claude hooks (hooks/*.mjs). Both systems need their own autocommit logic. Pi uses SubprocessRunner.run() for async git operations, Claude hooks use spawnSync().

Pi extensions in config/pi/extensions/ need package.json with 'exports' field for Pi to load them. Install locally with 'pi install ./path -l' which adds to .pi/settings.json. Without package.json, extensions won't load even if code exists.

Pi extensions package is published as @jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions (not @xtrm/pi-extensions). The npm scope is @jaggerxtrm matching the GitHub org Jaggerxtrm. All CLI references use npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions for pi install.

Pi extension tool_call handlers (pi.on('tool_call', ...)) are awaited BEFORE the tool executes and may return {block} or undefined; awaiting an async init there defers the tool until ready. Use this for lazy daemon startup: resolve cheap context at session_start, then ensure the daemon on first relevant tool_call via ONE memoized promise (concurrency-safe within the process; clear the promise on failure so the next call retries, never throw -> fail open). The Serena tool gate set is exactly the 11 semantic tools in docs/pi-extensions.md 'Serena tool ownership boundary' (find_symbol, find_referencing_symbols, get_symbols_overview, insert_after/before_symbol, replace_symbol_body, rename_symbol, jet_brains_* x4) — NOT pi-serena-compact's broader COMPACT_TOOLS, which also lists GitNexus/shell/file/memory tools that do not use SERENA_MCP_PORT. event.toolName carries the tool name.

pi-mcp-adapter (v2.2.1) works via Pi RPC mode. Key: use npm package install (not local extension), args param is JSON string not object. Pi MCP config uses npx -y pi-mcp-adapter for deepwiki/github-grep, but xt init/update active runtime sync installs only MANAGED_PACKAGES from cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts. Pi npm packages are per-project by design (~/.pi/agent/settings.json lists them, but they install to .pi/npm/node_modules/). Worktrees share main repo's .pi/npm via symlink to avoid reinstalls. True global packages would require Pi core changes.

Pi-only releases must run the root build before bumping packages/pi-extensions: the root prebuild sync resets workspace versions to the root version. Set the Pi workspace version after build, then pack/publish the workspace without rerunning root build.

Pi package deduplication is source-identity based: a local /path/pi-extensions registration and npm:@jaggerxtrm/pi-extensions are distinct and both load. Keep only one when it overrides built-in tools.

Pi package freshness helper design: getManagedPiPackageFreshness in cli/src/core/pi-runtime.ts is intentionally provider-injected and network-free; command beads should supply installed/expected version providers and consume states missing/current/outdated/version-unknown.

Pi resolves settings.json packages by SCOPE-FREE identity: getPackageIdentity() returns 'npm:<name>' with no scope for npm sources, so a package declared in BOTH ~/.pi/agent/settings.json and <project>/.pi/settings.json collides in dedupePackages() and the PROJECT entry wins. The global entry is dropped. Consequence: a per-project package entry silently shadows the global install and pins the repo to whatever copy sits in <project>/.pi/npm, which drifts. Never add a package entry per-project when the global settings already declare it.

pi per-call latency: pi-gitnexus autoAugment defaults ON and runs up to 3 'gitnexus augment' subprocesses after every grep/read/bash tool_result (dominant cost on nav-heavy sessions). It reads ~/.pi/pi-gitnexus.json only (NO env override). Set {"autoAugment": false} to disable the hook while keeping on-demand MCP tools (query/context/impact/detect_changes). xt now seeds this file in runPiInstall (xtrm-e2vkn). Separately: quality-gates pi-extension is inert-by-bug — it looks for .claude/hooks/quality-check.{cjs,py} but plugin-era cleanup migrated scripts to .xtrm/hooks/ and never re-wired the extension, so it never fires. pi-processes-pnpm-prereq: @aliou/pi-processes added to all Pi package lists (install-schema.json, settings.json.template, package.json pi.packages). install-pi.ts now checks/installs pnpm as a prerequisite via ensurePnpm() — pi-processes encourages pnpm dev/build/test commands so pnpm must be available.

Pi project package reinstalls in worktrees are triggered by missing <worktree>/.pi/npm/node_modules for npm: sources; preventing reinstallation requires sharing .pi/npm (symlink) even when .pi itself exists as a tracked directory.
